explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. a3
explanations.text:
__NOTOC__

1. a3 · Anderssen's Opening

This opening move does little for development or control of the center. In some cases, White can transpose the game to an opening where 1. a3 might have been useful, but using a tempo on such a move already on move one seems premature. In fact, this opening is based on the idea that White is playing with the black pieces, but he has the move 1. a3 already played. If a game starts 1. a3 e5 2. e4 Nf6 3. Nc3, Black cannot proceed in Ruy Lopez-fashion, and if Black plays 3... Bc5, then 4. Nf3 puts Black into the Two Knights' Defence and White's a3 precludes many possibilities.

Named after the German chess player Adolf Anderssen, who played this opening a few times against Morphy, this is a prophylactic waiting move that allows Black to choose an opening down a tempo, should a3 be useful in such cases.

Black's responses

There are a variety of ways for Black to respond to this move, including:

1...e5 may transpose into an English (1. c4 e5 2. a3), where a3 is a useful move for White. It covers and prepares b4, and allows White to set up a structure similar to that in the Najdorf or Kan for Black.

1...d5 makes transpositions into the Polish Opening or a reversed Pirc highly likely, should White eventually play b4 or d3/g3.

1...g6 may thwart White's plans if they planned to play b4 and Bb2 as the a1-h8 diagonal would be first occupied by a black Bg7 in that case, provided that Black fianchettos their bishop immediately.

1...c5 may transpose into an a3 Sicilian, or White may play b4 and attack c5.

1...Nf6 will likely transpose into other aforementioned lines.

explanations.textZh:
__NOTOC__

1. a3·安徒生的开局

这一开放举措对于中心的发展或控制作用不大。在某些情况下，白棋可以将棋局转移到 1.a3 可能有用的开局，但在第一步已经进行的这样的棋步上使用节奏似乎为时过早。事实上，这个开局是基于白棋正在下黑棋的想法，但他已经下了棋1.a3。如果比赛开始 1. a3 e5 2. e4 Nf6 3. Nc3，黑方无法按照 Ruy Lopez 的方式进行，如果黑方下 3...Bc5，则 4. Nf3 将黑方置于两马防守中，而白方的 a3 排除了许多可能性。

以德国国际象棋棋手阿道夫·安德森 (Adolf Anderssen) 的名字命名，他在与莫菲 (Morphy) 的比赛中多次使用此开局，这是一种预防性等待棋，允许黑方选择放慢节奏的开局，如果 a3 在这种情况下有用的话。

黑方的回应

黑棋应对这一着棋的方式有很多种，包括：

1...e5 可以转换成英语（1. c4 e5 2. a3），其中 a3 对于白方来说是一个有用的棋步。它覆盖并准备b4，并允许白棋建立类似于黑棋Najdorf或Kan的结构。

如果白方最终下 b4 或 d3/g3，那么 1...d5 很可能会转入波兰开局或反转的 Pirc。

1...g6 可能会阻碍白方的计划，如果他们计划下 b4 和 Bb2，因为在这种情况下 a1-h8 对角线将首先被黑方 Bg7 占据，前提是黑方立即消灭他们的主教。

1...c5 可以转换成 a3 西西里棋，或者白棋可以下 b4 并攻击 c5。

1...Nf6 可能会转入其他上述线路。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. a3/1...a6
explanations.text:
1...a6

Most analytical engines consider 1. a3? to be at most a wasted move, with it losing around 0.4 points on average. In lieu of this, Black should capitalise on this error, which 1...a6 most certainly does not do. There isn't very much to say regarding this move, just that it is not good. Better replies are 1...e5, 1...d5, 1...Nf6, 1...g6, and 1...c5.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. a4
explanations.text:
1. a4?! · Ware opening

1. a4?! is an unorthodox opening. It does not help White to develop their pieces or stake a claim to the centre. It is almost like White has passed their first turn: functionally, they are playing a tempo down.

It is most common with beginners who think that their rooks are powerful pieces, and wouldn't it be good to develop them first? Unfortunately, rook lifting (a4, Ra3, Rd3 etc) is too slow and gives Black plenty of time to develop all their minor pieces. Rooks come alive later in the game, when files begin to open.

After 1. a4, Black gets to decide which pawn to put in the centre. 1...e5 is the main line (as much as there is a "main line"), taking space and opening the a3-f8 diagonal for Black's bishop. As long as White responds with something like 2. e4 then they do not fall too far behind and the game is even. A classic beginner blunder (called sometimes the meadow hay trap) marries the plan of an early rook lift with a lack of board vision: 2. Ra3?? Bxa3.

1...d5 is also very sound.

1...a5?!, which might be called the "symmetrical variation", at worst fails to capitalise on White's irregular play.

History

1. a4 is named for Preston Ware who played it in 1880 during the 5th American Chess Congress. With the black pieces he played 1...a5. Contemporaries of Ware called 1. a4 the meadow hay opening.

Magnus Carlsen played it against Teimour Radjabov in the 2012 World Blitz Championship, apparently as an in-joke referencing Radjabov's comment, "Everyone is getting tired. You might as well start with 1. a4 and you can still beat them."

In May 2024, the opening gained notoriety after Grandmaster Brandon Jacobson, under the pseudonym Viih_Sou, won a sixty-nine game blitz match against Daniel Naroditsky by playing 1. a4 and 2. Ra3? with White and 1...a5 & 2...Ra6? with Black every game, voluntarily sacrificing the exchange. Chess.com banned Viih_Sou for fair play violations and the line became known as the "banned gambit" or "Viih_Sou gambit". Jacobson took to Reddit to reveal their identity and deny allegations of cheating.

Brandon Jacobson went on to win with 1. a4 (though not 2. Ra3?) against Hikaru Nakamura in the 2024 World Rapid Championship.

explanations.textZh:
1.a4？！ · 开仓

1.a4？！是一个非正统的开口。它无助于白棋发展棋子或占据中心。这几乎就像白方已经通过了他们的第一轮：从功能上讲，他们正在放慢节奏。

最常见的是初学者，他们认为自己的车是强大的棋子，首先开发它们不是很好吗？不幸的是，车举起（a4、Ra3、Rd3 等）太慢，给了黑方足够的时间来发展他们所有的小子。当文件开始打开时，车会在游戏后期复活。

1. a4 之后，黑方可以决定将哪个棋子放在中心。 1...e5 是主线（只要有“主线”），为黑方象占据空间并打开 a3-f8 对角线。只要白棋以 2.e4 之类的方式回应，那么他们就不会落后太远，比赛就很平了。一个典型的初学者错误（有时称为草地干草陷阱）将早期的车举升计划与缺乏董事会视野结合在一起：2.Ra3?? Bxa3。

1...d5 也很健全。

1...a5？！，这可能被称为“对称变化”，最坏的情况是无法利用白棋的不规则玩法。

历史

1. a4 是以 Preston Ware 的名字命名的，他在 1880 年第五届美国国际象棋大会上玩过它。他用黑子下棋 1...a5。韦尔的同时代人将 1.a4 称为草地干草开口。

Magnus Carlsen 在 2012 年世界闪电战锦标赛中对阵 Teimour Ra​​djabov，显然是一个笑话，引用了 Radjabov 的评论：“每个人都累了。你不妨从 1.a4 开始，你仍然可以击败他们。”

2024 年 5 月，大师 Brandon Jacobson 以笔名 Viih_Sou 通过 1.a4 和 2.Ra3？赢得了与 Daniel Naroditsky 的 69 局闪电战比赛后，这一开局就声名狼藉。白色和 1...a5 & 2...Ra6？每局都与黑棋，自愿牺牲交换。 Chess.com 以违反公平竞赛为由禁止 Viih_Sou，该路线被称为“禁止开局”或“Viih_Sou 开局”。雅各布森在 Reddit 上透露了他们的身份，并否认了作弊指控。

布兰登·雅各布森 (Brandon Jacobson) 在 2024 年世界快棋锦标赛中以 1.a4（尽管不是 2.Ra3？）战胜了中村光 (Hikaru Nakamura)。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. a4/1...a5
explanations.text:
Ware Opening - Symmetric Variation

1...a5

This move is an unusual response to 1. a4, but it is not without merit. If an informed player is playing White, he will not try to develop the rook from a1 to a3 (as ...e5 will prevent it), but will instead wait for a chance to play a5 followed by Ra4. An early 1...a5 by Black prevents this tactic and helps to negate any value of playing 1. a4.

All possible White's moves after 1. a4 a5

器皿开口 - 对称变化

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. a4/1...b5/2. axb5
explanations.text:
Ware Opening, Wing Gambit Accepted

2. axb5

White accepts Black's dubious gambit. Black players usually continue with c6 or a6 to contest the opponent pawn or Bb7 to fianchetto the bishop. White's rook now has the semi-open file to exploit later on in the game, and Black will find it hard to prove compensation for the lost b5 pawn.
explanations.textEn:
Ware Opening, Wing Gambit Accepted

2. axb5

White accepts Black's dubious gambit. Black players usually continue with c6 or a6 to contest the opponent pawn or Bb7 to fianchetto the bishop. White's rook now has the semi-open file to exploit later on in the game, and Black will find it hard to prove compensation for the lost b5 pawn.
explanations.textZh:
开局，翼开局已接受

2.axb5

白棋接受了黑棋可疑的棋局。黑方玩家通常会继续用 c6 或 a6 与对手棋子竞争，或用 Bb7 与主教对抗。白方的车现在拥有半开文件，可以在游戏后期利用，而黑方将发现很难证明对丢失的 b5 棋子的补偿。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. a4/1...d5
explanations.text: Black does what White has not, by controlling the center. This may be used in an attempt to close in the freed White rook rather than an attempt to prevent its development outright.
explanations.textEn: Black does what White has not, by controlling the center. This may be used in an attempt to close in the freed White rook rather than an attempt to prevent its development outright.
explanations.textZh: 黑棋通过控制中心做了白棋没有做的事情。这可以用来试图关闭被释放的白车，而不是试图彻底阻止其发展。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. a4/1...d5/2. e4
explanations.text: 2. e4 is erroneous move, as it allows /2...dxe4/ with advantage for Black. White is not lost, but must play for a quick win rather than a long battle.
explanations.textEn: 2. e4 is erroneous move, as it allows /2...dxe4/ with advantage for Black. White is not lost, but must play for a quick win rather than a long battle.
explanations.textZh: 2. e4 是错误的棋步，因为它允许 /2...dxe4/ 为黑方带来优势。白棋并没有失败，但必须着眼于速胜而不是持久战。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. a4/1...e5
explanations.text:
Ware Opening

1...e5

Black punishes White's lack of center control, and does what white has not by controlling the center. This move also prevents 2. Ra3.
explanations.textEn:
Ware Opening

1...e5

Black punishes White's lack of center control, and does what white has not by controlling the center. This move also prevents 2. Ra3.
explanations.textZh:
开仓

1...e5

黑棋惩罚白棋缺乏中心控制，并通过控制中心来完成白棋没有做的事情。这一举动也阻止了2.Ra3。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. a4/1...e5/2. Ra3
explanations.text:
2. Ra3??

2. Ra3 is a blunder as it allows 2...Bxa3!, when Black is up an exchange with good chances for the advantage after 3. bxa3, weakening White's pawns, or 3. Nxa3, when the knight is sidelined from the center, and after d5 White is in a losing position. The move 2. Ra3 is known as the Banned Gambit or Meadow Hay Trap among chess players.
explanations.textEn:
2. Ra3??

2. Ra3 is a blunder as it allows 2...Bxa3!, when Black is up an exchange with good chances for the advantage after 3. bxa3, weakening White's pawns, or 3. Nxa3, when the knight is sidelined from the center, and after d5 White is in a losing position. The move 2. Ra3 is known as the Banned Gambit or Meadow Hay Trap among chess players.
explanations.textZh:
2.Ra3??

2. Ra3 是一个错误，因为它允许 2...Bxa3！，当黑方在 3. bxa3 之后有很好的机会获得优势时，削弱白方的棋子，或 3. Nxa3，当马从中心靠边时，并且在 d5 之后白方处于失败位置。 2.Ra3 着法在国际象棋棋手中被称为“禁止开局”或“草地干草陷阱”。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. a4/1...e5/2. a5
explanations.text:
2. a5

White continues marching down the board with the a-pawn. This opening is considered dubious. Black has two options:

2...a6, stopping White from advancing their pawn any further, or

2...d5, taking the full center, unfazed by White's pawn push.
explanations.textEn:
2. a5

White continues marching down the board with the a-pawn. This opening is considered dubious. Black has two options:

2...a6, stopping White from advancing their pawn any further, or

2...d5, taking the full center, unfazed by White's pawn push.
explanations.textZh:
2.a5

白棋继续带着a兵沿着棋盘前进。这个开口被认为是可疑的。黑方有两种选择：

2...a6，阻止白棋进一步推进棋子，或者

2...d5，占据中心位置，不受白方兵推的影响。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. a4/1...e5/2. h4
explanations.text:
Crab Variation

This variation does nothing to aid White's development and weakens their position, and thus is not recommended for serious play. It is named due to its crab-like appearance, with the a and h pawns presumably representing claws.

It does have one upside, however, preventing 2...Qh4.
explanations.textEn:
Crab Variation

This variation does nothing to aid White's development and weakens their position, and thus is not recommended for serious play. It is named due to its crab-like appearance, with the a and h pawns presumably representing claws.

It does have one upside, however, preventing 2...Qh4.
explanations.textZh:
螃蟹变种

这种变化对白棋的发展没有任何帮助，并且削弱了他们的地位，因此不推荐用于严肃的游戏。它因其像螃蟹的外观而得名，其中的 a 和 h 棋子可能代表爪子。

然而，它确实有一个好处，可以防止 2...Qh4。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Na3
explanations.text:
1. Na3?! · Durkin Opening

White develops their knight to the edge of the board, where it has little influence on the board. This is a poor move that does little to develop White's position, at best passing the turn for Black to decide how to play. Black doesn't have to be as polite as White in eschewing the centre and can play 1...e5 or 1...d5.

After 1...e5, White may choose 2. Nc4 to put pressure on the e5-pawn.

History

The Oxford Companion to Chess says of 1. Na3, "played in over-the-board and correspondence games by Robert Durkin (1923- ) of New Jersey, but rarely by anyone else."

Eric Schiller gave 1. Na3 the name Sodium Attack, as "Na" is the chemical symbol for sodium.

explanations.textZh:
1.Na3？！ · 杜尔金开幕

白棋将马发展到棋盘的边缘，对棋盘的影响很小。这是一个糟糕的举动，对发展白方的位置没有什么帮助，最多是让黑方决定如何下棋。黑棋不必像白棋那样有礼貌地避开中间，并且可以下 1...e5 或 1...d5。

1...e5 之后，白方可以选择 2. Nc4 对 e5 兵施加压力。

Eric Sc​​hiller 将 1. Na3 命名为 Sodium Attack，因为“Na”是钠的化学符号。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nc3
explanations.text:
1. Nc3 · van Geet opening

1. Nc3 is an unusual opening that allows for a variety of transpositions, along with some independent lines.

Though it is a sensible move, developing a knight to a good square to control the centre, it is much less common than 1. Nf3. One reason is that the knight prevents White from playing c4, which they may be sad of if this transposes into a d4 opening. The other reason is that while 1. Nf3 prevents 1...e5, 1. Nc3 doesn't prevent 1...d5 (because after Black plays 1...d5, the d5 pawn is already defended by their queen).

In fact 1...d5 is the main response. 1...d5 threatens 2...d4 to take space and force White's knight to move again. There are some ways to prevent 2...d4: 2. d4 (transposing into a closed game); 2. Nf3 (transposing into a reversed Mexican defence); or 2. e3. However, it is most common to allow it with 2. e4, intending 2...d4 3. Nce2 e5 4. Ng3.

Several other moves allow White to play 2. e4 and transpose to a more common king's pawn opening, although there are ways of keeping the game in original territory.

1...c5 can transpose into the closed Sicilian defence if White plays 2. e4. Another line is 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4, playing in the manner of a Sicilian defence but delaying actually committing the pawn to e4.

1...e5 invites a transposition to the Vienna game with 2. e4. If White wishes to avoid this, the main continuation is 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4, called the Napoleon attack.

1...Nf6 and 1...Nc6 are patient moves that pass the decision to play a pawn in the centre back to White. These may transpose into a line in the Vienna game if e4 & ...e5 are eventually played, or into a queen's pawn opening if d4 & ...d5.

History

This opening has a range of names, commonly Dunst for Ted Dunst (1907―1985) and van Geet for Dirk van Geet (1932―2012), and descriptive names queen's knight opening and Linkspringer (German: knight on the left). Its most poetic name is the Sleipnir opening, for Odin's eight-legged horse.

A historic game in this opening is attributed to chess amateur and Emperor of France, Napoleon Bonaparte, 1804.

Schiller & Benjamin cite FM Asa Hoffman as having "built most of his successful chess career on 1. Nc3", which they describe as "the best of the non-standard opening moves."

It is most often seen in blitz events where White is equally happy to play an e4 or d4 opening by transposition, and is letting Black choose.

1. Nc3 · van Geet opening

1. Nc3 is an unusual opening that allows for a variety of transpositions, along with some independent lines.

Though it is a sensible move, developing a knight to a good square to control the centre, it is much less common than 1. Nf3. One reason is that the knight prevents White from playing c4, which they may be sad of if this transposes into a d4 opening. The other reason is that while 1. Nf3 prevents 1...e5, 1. Nc3 doesn't prevent 1...d5 (because after Black plays 1...d5, the d5 pawn is already defended by their queen).

In fact 1...d5 is the main response. 1...d5 threatens 2...d4 to take space and force White's knight to move again. There are some ways to prevent 2...d4: 2. d4 (transposing into a closed game); 2. Nf3 (transposing into a reversed Mexican defence); or 2. e3. However, it is most common to allow it with 2. e4, intending 2...d4 3. Nce2 e5 4. Ng3.

explanations.textZh:
1.NC3·范吉特开场

1. Nc3 是一个不寻常的开局，允许进行各种换位以及一些独立的台词。

虽然这是一个明智的举动，将骑士发展成一个好的方阵来控制中心，但它比 1. Nf3 少见得多。原因之一是马阻止白方下 c4，如果这转换成 d4 开局，他们可能会感到难过。另一个原因是，虽然 1. Nf3 可以防止 1...e5，但 1. Nc3 不能防止 1...d5（因为黑方下 1...d5 后，d5 棋子已经被其后所防守）。

事实上 1...d5 是主要响应。 1...d5 威胁 2...d4 占据空间并迫使白方的马再次移动。有一些方法可以防止 2...d4： 2. d4（转入封闭游戏）； 2. Nf3（转换为反向墨西哥防守）；或 2. e3。但是，最常见的是允许使用 2. e4，即 2...d4 3. Nce2 e5 4. Ng3。

其他一些走法允许白方下 2. e4 并转换为更常见的王棋开局，尽管有一些方法可以将游戏保持在原始范围内。

如果白方下2. e4，1...c5 可以转换为封闭的西西里防御。另一条线是 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4，以西西里防御的方式进行游戏，但延迟了实际将棋子交给 e4。

1...e5 邀请与 2. e4 换位到维也纳游戏。如果白方希望避免这种情况，主要的延续是 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4，称为拿破仑攻击。

1...Nf6 和 1...Nc6 是耐心的走法，将在中间下棋的决定传递给白棋。如果最终玩了 e4 & ...e5，这些可能会转变成维也纳游戏中的一行，或者如果最终玩 d4 & ...d5，则转变成皇后的棋子开局。

历史

这个开局有一系列的名称，通常是 Dunst 代表 Ted Dunst (1907―1985)，van Geet 代表 Dirk van Geet (1932―2012)，以及描述性名称 queen's Knight 开局和 Linkspringer（德语：左边的骑士）。它最富有诗意的名字是斯莱普尼尔（Sleipnir）开头，代表奥丁的八足马。

这一开局中的一场历史性比赛归功于国际象棋业余爱好者和法国皇帝拿破仑·波拿巴 (Napoleon Bonaparte)，1804 年。

Schiller 和 Benjamin 引用 FM Asa Hoffman 的话说“他成功的国际象棋生涯大部分建立在 1.Nc3 之上”，他们将其描述为“最好的非标准开局动作”。

这种情况最常出现在闪电战中，白方同样乐意通过换位下 e4 或 d4 开局，并让黑方选择。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nc3/1...Nc6
explanations.text:
1...Nc6

A funny sideline, Black passes the decision to play a pawn in the centre back to White. This is flexible and affords White a wide range of plausible continuations, the most ambitious being 2. d4 or 2. e4.

2. d4 d5 enters a closed opening. In closed openings one usually wants to have the option of c4 and ...c5, which here the knights prevent. However, since it is blocked for both White and Black, the game is equal. 3. e4 transposes into the Bogoljubow variation of the Nimzowitsch defence (1. e4 Nc6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3).

2. e4 e5 transposes to the Max Lange defence in the Vienna game.

2. d4 d5 进入一个封闭的开口。在封闭的空缺中，人们通常希望有 c4 和 ...c5 的选择，而这里的骑士会阻止这一选择。然而，由于白棋和黑棋都被阻挡，所以比赛是平等的。 3. e4 转置为 Nimzowitsch 防御的 Bogoljubow 变体（1. e4 Nc6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3）。

2. e4 e5 换位到维也纳比赛中的 Max Lange 防守。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nc3/1...c5
explanations.text:
1...c5

Black invites a transposition into the closed Sicilian, 2. e4.

If White wishes to avoid (or, at least, delay) the transposition they can try 2. Nf3?!, where 2...Nc6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 is a line Schiller christened the "Sicilian two knights," though White has the accept the possibility of 2...d5.

2. d4!? cxd4 3. Qxd4 Nc6 4. Qh4?! is the Novosibirsk variation, as Schiller calls it.

2.d4！？ cxd4 3.Qxd4 Nc6 4.Qh4？！是席勒所说的新西伯利亚变体。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nc3/1...d5
explanations.text:
1...d5

Black stakes a claim to the centre. Their d-pawn threatens to come to d4 and unseat White's knight.

If 2. d4, that danger is prevented. The game transposes into a version of the closed game where White's knight obstructs the usual move c4. No matter: White can try a Jobava-London system (Bf4) or Richter-Veresov attack (Bg5) instead.

2. e4 is more common, allowing 2...d5, which White answers with the manoeuvre Ne2 & Ng3.

黑棋占据中心。他们的 d 兵威胁要来到 d4 并推翻白方的马。

如果是 2. d4，则可以避免该危险。游戏转换为封闭游戏的版本，其中白棋的骑士阻碍了通常的棋步 c4。无论如何：白方可以尝试 Jobava-London 系统（Bf4）或 Richter-Veresov 攻击（Bg5）。

2. e4 更常见，允许 2...d5，白方用 Ne2 和 Ng3 策略来回答。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nc3/1...d5/2. e4
explanations.text:
2. e4

This move puts White in danger of 2...d4, which will unseat the knight. White usually reroutes it to g3: 2...d4 3. Nce2 e5 4. Ng3.

Defending d5, 2...Nf6, 2...c6, or 2...e6 transposes to the Alekhine, Caro-Kann, or French defences respectively.

Otherwise, 2...dxe4 avoids losing the pawn. 3. Nxe4 completes the trade, or White may gambit it:

3...f3, the Dougherty gambit;

3...d3, the Dunst-Perrenet gambit;

3...Bc4, the Hector gambit.

History

This is the main continuation of the van Geet opening, but may also occur in the Scandinavian defence if 2. Nc3. Chess.com's opening book, but not really anyone else, refers to this as the closed Scandinavian.

此步棋使白方面临 2...d4 的危险，这将使马下台。白棋通常将其重新路由到 g3： 2...d4 3. Nce2 e5 4. Ng3。

防守 d5、2...Nf6、2...c6 或 2...e6 分别转换为阿廖欣、卡罗-卡恩或法国防守。

否则，2...dxe4 可以避免丢失棋子。 3. Nxe4 完成交易，否则白方可能会下注：

3...f3，多尔蒂策略；

3...d3，邓斯特-佩雷内策略；

3...Bc4，赫克托策略。

历史

这是范吉特开局的主要延续，但也可能发生在斯堪的纳维亚防守中，如果2. Nc3。 Chess.com 的开本书（但实际上没有其他人）将其称为封闭的斯堪的纳维亚。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nc3/1...e5
explanations.text:
1...e5 · Reversed Nimzowitsch

This position resembles a Nimzowitsch defence, 1. e4 Nc6, but colours reversed and it's White to move. Given White has an extra tempo compared to Black in the Nimzowitsch, this should be very playable.

2. d4 exd4 3. Qxd4 plays this most like a Nimzowitsch. Because Black hasn't played ...d5 yet (contrast 1. e4 Nc6 2. d4 d5 3. exd5 Qxd5, where White's d-pawn is hanging) they can reply 3...Nc6 immediately.

2. e4 transposes into the Vienna game.

2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 is the Napoleon attack, something like the Scotch game.

1...e5 · 逆尼姆佐维奇

这个位置类似于尼姆佐维奇防御，1. e4 Nc6，但颜色相反，移动的是白色。鉴于尼姆佐维奇棋中白棋比黑棋有额外的节奏，这应该是非常可玩的。

2. d4 exd4 3. Qxd4 演奏起来最像尼姆佐维奇。因为黑方还没有下...d5（对比 1. e4 Nc6 2. d4 d5 3. exd5 Qxd5，白方的 d-pawn 挂在那里），他们可以立即回复 3...Nc6。

2. e4 转置为维也纳游戏。

2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 是拿破仑攻击，有点像苏格兰游戏。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nc3/1...f5
explanations.text:
Van Geet Opening

1...f5

Black plays in similar fashion to the Dutch Defence, controlling e4 with the f-pawn and is likely to double down on it with Nf6 or try a Stonewall-like or Leningrad-like setup with e6 or g6. However, since the knight on c3 already controls e4, this move is not as effective as 1...f5 against 1. d4 or 1. Nf3.

2. e4 immediately contests the f5 pawn and is the most accurate move. 2...fxe4 3. d3 is the aggressive Klüver Gambit.

2. d4 transposes to the Raphael Variation of the Dutch Defence (1. d4 f5 2. Nc3).

2. e3 opens up the f1 bishop.

2. d3 opens up the c1 bishop and controls e4.

范吉特开幕

1...f5

黑棋的玩法与荷兰防御类似，用f兵控制e4，并且可能用Nf6加倍下注，或者尝试用e6或g6进行类似石墙或列宁格勒的设置。然而，由于 c3 上的骑士已经控制了 e4，因此这一举动不如 1...f5 对抗 1.d4 或 1.Nf3 有效。

2. e4 立即与 f5 兵竞争，是最准确的走法。 2...fxe4 3. d3 是激进的 Klüver 策略。

2. d4 转置为荷兰防御的拉斐尔变奏 (1. d4 f5 2. Nc3)。

2、e3开f1主教。

2. d3打开c1主教并控制e4。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nc3/1...Nf6
explanations.text:
1...Nf6

A flexible continuation where Black passes the decision on making a pawn move in the centre back to White. There is little independent character and the game usually transposes shortly to another opening.

Whether 2. e4 or 2. d4, Black can move order into a classical French defence (2...e6, then either 3. d4 d5 or 3. e4 d5, respectively) or the Pirc (2...d6 3. d4 or 3. e4).

Otherwise, 2. e4 and Black's transpositional options include the Vienna game, 2...e5; and an Alekhine defence, 2...d5. 2. d4 may lead to a Chigorin closed game.

2. g4? is called the Tübingen gambit with a similar character to the Bronstein aka the Gibbins-Weidenhagen gambit, 1. d4 Nf3 2. g4, to which this may transpose. After 2...Nxg4 3. e4 discovers an attack on the knight.

Otherwise, 2. e4 and Black's transpositional options include the Vienna game, 2...e5; and an Alekhine defence, 2...d5. 2. d4 may lead to a Chigorin closed game.

explanations.textZh:
1...NF6

这是一种灵活的延续，黑方将在中间走棋的决定传递给白方。几乎没有独立的角色，游戏通常会很快转移到另一个空缺。

无论是 2. e4 还是 2. d4，黑方都可以将顺序转移到经典的法式防御（2...e6，然后分别是 3. d4 d5 或 3. e4 d5）或 Pirc（2...d6 3. d4 或 3. e4）。

否则，2. e4 和黑棋的换位选项包括维也纳对局，2...e5；和阿廖欣防御，2...d5。 2. d4可能会导致Chigorin封闭比赛。

2.g4？被称为 Tübingen 弃兵，其特征与 Bronstein 又名 Gibbins-Weidenhagen 弃兵 1. d4 Nf3 2. g4 相似，这可以转置为后者。 2...Nxg4 3. e4 发现骑士受到攻击。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. b3
explanations.text:
1. b3 · Nimzowitsch–Larsen attack

1. b3 prepares to fianchetto the queen's bishop to b2, where it will fight for the central squares and point towards Black's kingside. This is a hypermodern opening, preparing to control the centre from afar with a bishop rather than a central pawn (the classical style). This allows Black to seize the centre with a pawn themselves, which they usually choose to do with either 1...e5 or 1...d5. 1...Nf6 is also common.

1...e5, the modern variation, is Black's most ambitious and common response to 1. b3, occurring in about 45% of games. Black usually limits the scope of White's bishop and gets a big centre with both d and e pawns after 2. Bb2 Nc6 3. e3 d5.

1...d5, the classical variation, is a common sideline (27%). It preserves the option to fianchetto the black bishop to g7 to oppose the white one. White can play 2. Bb2 or 2. Nf3.

1...Nf6, the Indian variation, prepares to fianchetto the bishop to g7 immediately to oppose the white bishop on b2. However, if Black does play g6 after 2. Bb2, White can play 3. e4!, threatening to kick the knight on f6. 3...Nxe4?? loses to 4. Bxh8. It is an interesting second sideline (15%).

Minor sidelines

1...c5, English variation: Retains option of 1...d5 while also being a good transpositional tool. 2. e4 transposes into the Sicilian defence, and 2. c4 transposes into the symmetrical English. 2. Nf3 is also playable. Occurs about 5% of games.

1...b6, Symmetrical variation: Black copies White's idea. This is perfectly fine for Black. Occurs about 2% of games.

1...g6: Accounts for another 2% of games. Black prepares to fianchetto to g7, though after 2. Bb2 Black must play 2...Nf6 first and this transposes to the Indian variation.

There are a number of other "also-ran" sidelines possible that together make up about 5% of competitive level games, including:

1...f5, Dutch variation: This is a rather unexplored alternative. 2. d4 and 2. Nf3 are most commonly played after this, though 2. e3 and even 2. e4!? (borrowing ideas from the Staunton gambit) are both possible.

1...e6: Sets up a variation of the French defence. 2. e4 d5 3. Bb2 is the most common and recommended line.

1...c6: Sets up a variation of the Caro-Kann. 2. e4 d5 3. Bb2 is the most common and recommended line.

1...Nc6: Supports the advance of the e-pawn but allows 2. d4, pressuring the knight.

1...b5!?, Polish variation: A fun alternative to the other moves. Transpositions are now impossible.

1...a5?!: Somewhat playable, trying to ruin White's fianchetto, but seeing that White will likely castle on the kingside, this is not that useful.

History

Also known as Nimzowitsch-Larsen attack or just queen's fianchetto opening, it is named after its pioneers Aron Nimzowitsch and Bent Larsen. Nimzowitsch preferred an alternate move order, 1. Nf3, and only after 1...d5 committing to 2. b3. This has the advantage of preventing 1...e5 thereby avoiding that line.

This is a hypermodern opening, preparing to control the centre from afar with a bishop rather than a central pawn (the classical style). This allows Black to seize the centre with a pawn themselves, which they usually choose to do with either 1...e5 or 1...d5. 1...Nf6 is also common.

1...e5, the modern variation, is Black's most ambitious and common response to 1. b3, occurring in about 45% of games. Black usually limits the scope of White's bishop and gets a big centre with both d and e pawns after 2. Bb2 Nc6 3. e3 d5.

1...d5, the classical variation, is a common sideline (27%). It preserves the option to fianchetto the black bishop to g7 to oppose the white one. White can play 2. Bb2 or 2. Nf3.

1...Nf6, the Indian variation, prepares to fianchetto the bishop to g7 immediately to oppose the white bishop on b2. However, if Black does play g6 after 2. Bb2, White can play 3. e4!, threatening to kick the knight on f6. 3...Nxe4?? loses to 4. Bxh8. It is an interesting second sideline (15%).

Minor sidelines

1...c5, English variation: Retains option of 1...d5 while also being a good transpositional tool. 2. e4 transposes into the Sicilian defence, and 2. c4 transposes into the symmetrical English. 2. Nf3 is also playable. Occurs about 5% of games.

1...b6, Symmetrical variation: Black copies White's idea. This is perfectly fine for Black. Occurs about 2% of games.

1...g6: Accounts for another 2% of games. Black prepares to fianchetto to g7, though after 2. Bb2 Black must play 2...Nf6 first and this transposes to the Indian variation.

There are a number of other "also-ran" sidelines possible that together make up about 5% of competitive level games, including:

1...f5, Dutch variation: This is a rather unexplored alternative. 2. d4 and 2. Nf3 are most commonly played after this, though 2. e3 and even 2. e4!? (borrowing ideas from the Staunton gambit) are both possible.

1...e6: Sets up a variation of the French defence. 2. e4 d5 3. Bb2 is the most common and recommended line.

1...c6: Sets up a variation of the Caro-Kann. 2. e4 d5 3. Bb2 is the most common and recommended line.

1...Nc6: Supports the advance of the e-pawn but allows 2. d4, pressuring the knight.

1...b5!?, Polish variation: A fun alternative to the other moves. Transpositions are now impossible.

1...a5?!: Somewhat playable, trying to ruin White's fianchetto, but seeing that White will likely castle on the kingside, this is not that useful.

History

Also known as Nimzowitsch-Larsen attack or just queen's fianchetto opening, it is named after its pioneers Aron Nimzowitsch and Bent Larsen. Nimzowitsch preferred an alternate move order, 1. Nf3, and only after 1...d5 committing to 2. b3. This has the advantage of preventing 1...e5 thereby avoiding that line.
explanations.textZh:
1. b3·尼姆佐维奇-拉森攻击

1. b3 准备将后王的象切向 b2，争夺中心格并指向黑方王翼。这是一个超现代的开局，准备用主教而不是中央棋子（古典风格）从远处控制中心。这使得黑方可以用棋子自己夺取中心，他们通常选择使用 1...e5 或 1...d5。 1...Nf6 也很常见。

1...e5，现代变体，是黑方对 1.b3 最雄心勃勃和最常见的反应，出现在大约 45% 的棋局中。黑方通常会限制白方主教的范围，并在 2. Bb2 Nc6 3. e3 d5 之后获得一个带有 d 和 e 兵的大中心。

1...d5，经典变体，是常见的副线（27%）。它保留了将黑人主教交给七国集团以反对白人主教的选择。白方可以下 2. Bb2 或 2. Nf3。

1...Nf6，印度版本，准备立即将主教送到g7，以对抗b2上的白主教。然而，如果黑方在 2.Bb2 之后确实下 g6，白方可以下 3.e4!，威胁在 f6 上踢马。 3...Nxe4？？输给4.Bxh8。这是一个有趣的第二副业（15%）。

次要的旁观

1...c5，英文变体：保留 1...d5 的选项，同时也是一个很好的换位工具。 2. e4 转置为西西里防御，2. c4 转置为对称英语。 2.NF3也可以玩。大约有 5% 的游戏发生。

1...b6，对称变化：黑方复制白方的想法。这对于黑方来说是完美的。大约有 2% 的游戏发生。

1...g6：占游戏的另外 2%。黑方准备fianchetto到g7，尽管在2.Bb2之后黑方必须首先下2...Nf6，这转移到印度变体。

还有许多其他可能的“落选”副业，合计约占竞技级别游戏的 5%，包括：

1...f5，荷兰语变体：这是一个尚未探索的替代方案。此后最常玩的是 2. d4 和 2. Nf3，尽管 2. e3 甚至 2. e4！？ （借用斯汤顿策略的想法）两者都是可能的。

1...e6：设置法国防御的变体。 2. e4 d5 3. Bb2 是最常见和推荐的线路。

1...c6：设置 Caro-Kann 的变体。 2. e4 d5 3. Bb2 是最常见和推荐的线路。

1...Nc6：支持e-pawn的前进，但允许2.d4，对马施加压力。

1...b5!?，波兰变体：其他动作的有趣替代品。现在换位是不可能的。

1...a5?!: 有点可玩，试图破坏白棋的花式，但看到白棋很可能会在王翼筑垒，这并不是那么有用。

历史

它也被称为 Nimzowitsch-Larsen 攻击或皇后 fianchetto 开局，以其先驱 Aron Nimzowitsch 和 Bent Larsen 的名字命名。 Nimzowitsch 更喜欢替代移动顺序 1. Nf3，并且仅在 1...d5 后才执行 2. b3。这样做的优点是可以防止 1...e5 从而避免该行。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. b3/1...c5
explanations.text:
__NOTOC__

1...c5 · English variation

1...c5 is a sideline pursued by Black when they assume White will be more booked up with the theory following 1...e5 or 1...d5.

Having commited to b3 already, White's continuation is invariably 2. Bb2, but, since 1...c5 does not control e4 or c4, Black invites White to later play e4 themselves, transposing into a b3 Sicillian, or c4, transposing into a Symmetrical English, which Black hopes to be more comfortable playing.

Most commonly, White declines this invitiation and keeps things in Nimzo-Larsen territory with 3. e3. Then, Black can choose to play e5 or d5 with the additional central control afforded by having already played c5.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. b3/1...d5
explanations.text:
1...d5 · Classical variation

Black's controls the centre and opens up the queenside bishop. This prevents White from playing e4 or Nc3, as the pawn will be taken or the knight kicked respectively.

2. Bb2 is the main move: developing the bishop to control the long diagonal and prevent Black from taking more space in the centre with ...e5. White often plans a set-up involving e3 and Nf3, though move orders are flexible. One idea is to challenge the d5-pawn with e3 & c4, supported by the king's bishop. In 1. b3 move order, compared to the 1. Nf3 move order, White has retained the option of set-ups involving f4. If White can't or doesn't wish to play e3, then g3 allows them to develop their king's bishop to the other flank.

explanations.textZh:
1...d5 · 古典变奏

黑方控制中路并打开后翼主教。这可以防止白方下 e4 或 Nc3，因为棋子将被吃掉，马将被踢出。

2. Bb2 是主要棋步：开发象来控制长对角线并防止黑方用 ...e5 占用更多中心空间。白棋经常计划涉及 e3 和 Nf3 的布局，尽管移动顺序很灵活。一种想法是在国王主教的支持下用 e3 和 c4 挑战 d5 兵。在1.b3走棋顺序中，与1.Nf3走棋顺序相比，白方保留了涉及f4的走棋选择。如果白方不能或不想下 e3，那么 g3 可以让他们将国王的主教发展到另一侧。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. b3/1...d5/2. Bb2
explanations.text:
2. Bb2

White's bishop controls a swathe across the middle of the board, including the e5 square, preventing Black from building the ideal two-pawn centre.

As ...e5 is harder to achieve now, Black may consider playing with ...e6 in order to develop the king's side bishop. This would inhibit development of the queen's bishop, so Black may wish to decide on its future first.

2...Bg4 is a common plan, which pins White's e-pawn and so makes it harder for them to play e3 and free their bishop. If 3. h3 Bh5 4. g4 Bg6 5. e3, then Black has extracted the concession of a weakened kingside.

2...Bf5 is an alternative destination (or in the order 2...Nf6 & 3...Bf5). Black can adopt a reversed London system set-up with ...e6, ...c6, ...Nd7 etc.

The other plan for the king's bishop is to fianchetto it, and directly oppose White's bishop on the long diagonal. Of course Black cannot play 2...g6?? yet or blunder their rook: first they must play 2...Nf6 to prepare 3...g6.

2...c5, the more maximalist approach, is a natural move and takes more space on the flank. 3. e3 preparing Bb5 resembles Nimzo-Indian or Bogo-Indian defence in reverse

2. BB2

由于现在...e5 更难实现，黑方可以考虑下...e6 来发展王方象。这会抑制后主教的发展，因此黑方可能希望首先决定其未来。

2...Bg4 是一个常见的计划，它固定了白方的 e 兵，因此使他们更难玩 e3 并释放他们的主教。如果 3. h3 Bh5 4. g4 Bg6 5. e3，则黑方获得了弱势王翼的让步。

2...c5，更极端的方法，是一个自然的举动，并且在侧翼占据更多空间。 3. e3 准备 Bb5 类似于 Nimzo-Indian 或 Bogo-Indian 的反向防御

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. b3/1...e5
explanations.text:
1...e5 · Modern variation

By beginning with 1. b3, White allowed Black to take the centre with 1...e5. This is the most popular and ambitious continuation for Black.

Some are dismissive of the 1. b3 move order because of this reply: White is left playing an Owen's Defence with colours reversed, "and not even an extra tempo can make that fully respectable." For this reason, Nimzowitsch preferred the move order 1. Nf3 (preventing e5) d5 2. b3. On the other hand, by not playing Nf3 yet, White retains the option of f4 to contest e5 later.

Having already prepared to fianchetto with 1. b3, White's continuation is invariably 2. Bb2. 2...Nc6, to defend the e5 pawn, follows, though the timid 2...d6 is occasionally tried.

White may then play 3. c4 to prevent 3...d5, but normally, White is happy to allow Black to take over the centre with both e5 and d5, planning to later attack it with the flank c and f pawns. Instead, the typical Nimzo-Larsen plan is to continue with the more patient 3. e3, opening up their other bishop.

1...e5 · 现代变体

从 1.b3 开始，白方允许黑方以 1...e5 占据中心。这是布莱克最受欢迎和最雄心勃勃的延续。

有些人对 1.b3 移动顺序不屑一顾，因为这样的答复：白棋留下了欧文防御，颜色颠倒，“甚至没有额外的节奏可以使之完全受人尊敬。”因此，尼姆佐维奇更喜欢移动顺序 1. Nf3（防止 e5）d5 2. b3。另一方面，由于尚未下Nf3，白方保留了f4稍后对抗e5的选择。

已经准备好用 1. b3 进行 fianchetto，白方的继续总是 2. Bb2。 2...Nc6，用于防守 e5 棋子，尽管偶尔会尝试胆小的 2...d6。

然后白方可能会下 3.c4 来阻止 3...d5，但通常情况下，白方很乐意让黑方用 e5 和 d5 接管中心，并计划稍后用侧翼 c 和 f 棋子攻击它。相反，典型的 Nimzo-Larsen 计划是继续更有耐心的 3.e3，开放他们的另一位主教。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. b3/1...e5/2. Bb2/2...Nc6/3. d4
explanations.text:
3. d4?

A mistake. Rather than spending their time continuing development of their pieces, White initiates trades in the centre. After 3...exd4 4. Bxd4 Nxd4 5. Qxd4, White has given up central control and the bishop they had spent time developing to the powerful long diagonal. 5...Nf6 6. e4?! d5 7. e5 Ne4! with the threat of ...Bc5!.

3.d4？

一个错误。白方并没有花时间继续开发自己的棋子，而是在中心发起交易。在3...exd4 4. Bxd4 Nxd4 5. Qxd4之后，白棋放弃了中央控制权，并放弃了他们花时间发展到强大的长对角线的主教。 5...NF6 6.e4？！ d5 7.e5 Ne4！并以...Bc5! 为威胁。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. b3/1...Nf6
explanations.text:
Nimzovich-Larsen Attack

1...Nf6

In this response, black develops a piece without committing to a pawn opening.

White normally completes the fianchetto through 2. Bb2, and black sets up the same pattern by attempting 2...g6 (where the knight shields the pawn.) White may then send out the kings knight with 3.Nf3, or claim the center with 3.e4 (with the knight being pinned).

Less common is 2.Nf3, which lets black setup a fianchetto of his own.

Statistics

FICS Games Database shows the most common responses for white are Bb2 (64%), Nf3 (23%) and e3 (8%).

尼姆佐维奇-拉森攻击

1...NF6

在这种反应中，黑方在不承担兵开局的情况下发展出一颗棋子。

白棋通常通过2.Bb2完成fianchetto，而黑棋则通过尝试2...g6（马保护棋子）来建立相同的模式。然后白棋可以用3.Nf3派出国王的马，或者用3.e4占领中心（马被钉住）。

不太常见的是 2.Nf3，它可以让黑棋设置他自己的 fianchetto。

统计数据

FICS 游戏数据库显示，白色最常见的反应是 Bb2 (64%)、Nf3 (23%) 和 e3 (8%)。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. b4
explanations.text:
__NOTOC__

1. b4 · Polish Opening

The Polish Opening (or Orangutan Opening) is a flank and rather uncommon opening starting with the move 1. b4. The purpose of this move is to fight for a spatial advantage on the queenside instead of immediately taking control of the centre. White will claim their share of the centre after getting the queen’s bishop fianchettoed and an eventual pawn advance in the centre. The move b4 can always be played later in the game which is the reason why this opening is seldom seen nowadays, however, Tartakower and Magnus Carlsen have tried it in tournaments and won successfully. The Polish opening is classified under the code (A00) as an irregular opening.

Fianchettoing is often a good idea. Why not grab a little space?

At some point a quick b4-b5 might dislodge a knight on c6.

Trading the b-pawn for the c-pawn may give white central power.

If Black responds with 1...e5 or 1...e6, usual play either continues with 2. a3, defending the pawn, or 2. Bb2, fianchettoing the bishop on the powerful a1-h8 diagonal. The idea after Bb2 is that the black can't play Bxb4 right away. For example, after 1. b4 e6 2. Bb2 Bxb4??, White responds with 3. Bxg7, at which point Black loses a rook. However, 1. b4 e5 2. Bb2 Bxb4!? 3. Bxe5 is actually viable for Black, in spite of the fact that Black cedes White a central pawn majority. Black will usually obtain some form of compensation with a slight lead in development. Chances for both sides in these lines are around equal, with perhaps a very slight edge for White.

Another possibility is for White to advance their b-pawn with b5, so as to evade attack. This has been shown to be a good option in several lines, and White now has a clear spatial advantage on the queenside. On the other hand, White’s pawn is now overextended and difficult to protect. Once again, the positions resulting from these lines are generally equal.

1. b4·波兰开局

波兰开局（或猩猩开局）是从第 1. b4 步开始的侧翼且相当罕见的开局。此举的目的是争取后翼的空间优势，而不是立即控制中路。在让后主教先手并最终将棋子推进到中心后，白棋将占据中心的份额。 b4总是可以在比赛后期下出，这就是为什么现在很少看到这种开局的原因，然而，Tartakower和Magnus Carlsen已经在比赛中尝试过并成功获胜。波兰开口在代码 (A00) 下归类为不规则开口。

Fianchettoing 通常是个好主意。为什么不抢一点空间呢？

在某些时候，快速的 b4-b5 可能会驱逐 c6 上的骑士。

将 b 棋子换成 c 棋子可能会赋予白方中央权力。

如果黑方回应 1...e5 或 1...e6，则通常的玩法要么继续 2.a3，保卫棋子，要么继续 2.Bb2，在强大的 a1-h8 对角线上攻击主教。 Bb2 之后的想法是黑棋不能立即下 Bxb4。例如，在1.b4 e6 2.Bb2 Bxb4??之后，白方回应3.Bxg7，此时黑方失去车。然而，1.b4 e5 2.Bb2 Bxb4！？ 3. Bxe5 实际上对黑方来说是可行的，尽管黑方放弃了白方的中央兵多数。黑色通常会获得某种形式的补偿，并在发展中略微领先。在这几条线上双方的机会大致相等，白方可能稍有优势。

另一种可能是白方用b5推进b兵，从而躲避攻击。这在几条防线中都被证明是一个不错的选择，现在白棋在后翼拥有明显的空间优势。另一方面，白棋的棋子现在已经过度延伸并且难以保护。再一次，这些线产生的位置通常是相等的。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. b4/1...c6
explanations.text:
1...c6 · Outflank Variation

The Outflank Variation in the Polish Opening refers to a specific move sequence that Black can play after the initial move 1. b4. Here's how it goes:

b4 c6. (Main Line - 2. Bb2 Qb6)

In this line, White fianchettos their queen's bishop with 2. Bb2, while Black develops their queen to b6. The Outflank Variation is characterized by both sides trying to control the queenside and create imbalances. The queen on b6 exerts pressure on White's queenside pawns and can lead to tactical opportunities.

It's worth noting that the Polish Opening is flexible, and there are various move orders and plans that can be employed by both sides. The Outflank Variation is just one of the possible ways to play against the Polish Opening.

explanations.textZh:
1...c6 · 包抄变化

波兰开局中的包抄变化是指黑棋在初始棋步 1. b4 之后可以下的特定棋步顺序。事情是这样的：

b4 c6。 （主线 - 2.Bb2 Qb6）

在这一行中，白棋用 2.Bb2 击败了他们的后主教，而黑棋则将他们的后发展到了 b6。包抄变式的特点是双方都试图控制后侧并造成不平衡。 b6 上的后对白方后侧兵施加压力，可以带来战术机会。

值得注意的是，波兰开局非常灵活，有多种走位顺序和计划可供双方使用。包抄变式只是对抗波兰开局的可能方法之一。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. b4/1...e5
explanations.text:
Polish Opening

1. b4 e5

Black plays the most common reply. This pawn move gives Black a share of the centre slightly larger than in standard openings, while freeing the bishop on f8 to take White's b4 pawn. Now both 2. a3 and 2. Bb2 are good responses.
explanations.textEn:
Polish Opening

1. b4 e5

Black plays the most common reply. This pawn move gives Black a share of the centre slightly larger than in standard openings, while freeing the bishop on f8 to take White's b4 pawn. Now both 2. a3 and 2. Bb2 are good responses.
explanations.textZh:
波兰开局

1.b4e5

黑色是最常见的答复。这一棋子移动使黑方占据了比标准开局稍大的中心份额，同时释放了 f8 上的主教来吃掉白方的 b4 棋子。现在 2.a3 和 2.Bb2 都是很好的响应。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. b4/1...e5/2. Bb2
explanations.text:
Polish Opening

2. Bb2

White fianchettoes their queen’s bishop right away, attacking e5 (and Black’s kingside) but leaving their own b4-pawn unguarded. White reckons that Black’s central pawn will be worth more than a flank pawn, which generally is the case. This is a relatively uncharted opening. Black can try:

2...Bxb4 which practically forces White to play 3. Bxe5 with an unclear position in practice, though computer analysis has shown this position to very slightly favour White.

2...d6 which protects black's pawn on e5, but removes the attack on b4.

2...d5 which takes full control of the center, but Black must be careful not to fall into the trap 3. Bxe5 Bxb4?? allowing 4. Bxg7 with a winning position for White (Black’s rook will meet its demise next move, with no compensation).

2...Nc6? is a bad move. After 3. b5!, White wins a pawn after the knight moves, with 4. Bxe5.

explanations.textZh:
波兰开局

2. BB2

白棋立即攻击其后的主教，攻击 e5（以及黑棋的王翼），但让自己的 b4 兵无人防守。白方认为黑方的中央棋子将比侧翼棋子更有价值，通常情况都是如此。这是一个相对未知的开局。黑色可以尝试：

2...Bxb4 实际上迫使白棋下 3. Bxe5，在实践中位置不明确，尽管计算机分析表明该位置非常有利于白棋。

2...d6 保护黑方在 e5 上的棋子，但消除了对 b4 的攻击。

2...d5 完全控制中心，但黑方必须小心，不要落入陷阱 3. Bxe5 Bxb4??允许 4. Bxg7，白方有胜势（黑方的车将在下一步走向灭亡，没有补偿）。

2...NC6？这是一个糟糕的举动。 3. b5！之后，白方在马移动后赢得了一个棋子，4. Bxe5。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. b4/1...e5/2. Bb2/2...Bxb4
explanations.text:
Polish Opening, Main Line

2...Bxb4

Black takes the undefended pawn which will most likely result in White recapturing with 3. Bxe5. Not only has Black now ceded White a central pawn majority for the b-pawn, but Black also has to worry about white's threat on g7. Also, a sharper but very risky option for White is 3. f4?!. At this point, Black can safely gain some form of advantage with 3...d6 4. fxe5 dxe5 5. Bxe5, due to white's weakened kingside and missing f-pawn. Black has, on the other hand, traded two central pawns for two flank pawns. Black can also accept the gambit with 3...exf4?!, leading to wild play and an unclear position after 4. Bxg7 Qh4+! 5. g3 fxg3 6. Bg2! gxh2+ 7. Kf1 hxg1=Q+ 8. Kxg1 Qg3 9. Bxh8, where White has a rook and a pawn for a knight and three pawns. The board is wide open and both sides have possibilities, though computers evaluate the position as objectively better for White. Nevertheless, computer evaluation has suggested that 3...Nh6! gives Black a large, if not winning advantage.

2...Bxb4

Bxe5 安全地获得某种形式的优势。另一方面，黑方用两个中央棋子换成了两个侧翼棋子。黑方也可以接受 3...exf4?! 的策略，导致 4.Bxg7 Qh4+! 后的疯狂发挥和位置不明确。 5.g3 fxg3 6.Bg2！ gxh2+ 7. Kf1 hxg1=Q+ 8. Kxg1 Qg3 9. Bxh8，其中白方有一个车和一个棋子，一个马和三个棋子。棋盘的开放性很大，双方都有可能性，尽管计算机客观上认为白棋的位置更好。然而，计算机评估建议 3...Nh6！给黑方带来了很大的优势，即使不是获胜。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. b4/1...e6
explanations.text:
1...e6

Black pushes the e-pawn so they can gain control over the center. This move also allows the pawn to move without getting attacked by a bishop on b2. Secondly, this move attacks the pawn on b4. However, White can play 2. Bb2 anyway, as Black cannot capture with 2...Bxb4??, as it hangs a rook with 3. Bxg7!.
explanations.textEn:
1...e6

However, White can play 2. Bb2 anyway, as Black cannot capture with 2...Bxb4??, as it hangs a rook with 3. Bxg7!.
explanations.textZh:
1...e6

黑方推动电子兵，以便他们能够控制中心。这一举动还允许棋子移动而不会受到 b2 上主教的攻击。其次，这一步棋攻击 b4 上的棋子。然而，白棋无论如何都可以下2.Bb2，因为黑棋无法用2...Bxb4?? 捕获，因为它用3.Bxg7! 挂了车。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. c3
explanations.text:
1. c3 · Saragossa opening

This is a rarely played move, as it takes away the knight's developing square c3, doesn't take space in the centre, and doesn't prepare to develop a minor piece.

1...Nf6 is a common reply, and White may play as in a London system, Torre attack, or Colle system, where White's pawn structure is generally c3, d4, e3.

1...e5 is a natural move where Black takes space in the centre and prepares to develop their pieces. The pawn on e5 contests White's control of d4. If 2. d4 anyway, resembling some sort of Englund gambit declined, Black can push the pawn, 2...e4, or trade and form a Carlsbad structure.

1...c5 2. e4 transposes into the Alapin Sicilian.

1. c3·萨拉戈萨开局

这是一个很少使用的举动，因为它带走了马正在发展的方格c3，不占用中心空间，并且不准备发展小棋子。

1...Nf6 是常见的回复，白方可能会在伦敦体系、托雷攻击或科莱体系中下棋，其中白方的棋子结构通常是 c3、d4、e3。

1...e5 是黑棋在中间占据空间并准备展开棋子的自然走法。 e5 上的棋子争夺白方对 d4 的控制权。如果 2. d4 无论如何，类似于某种英格伦德弃兵，黑方可以推兵，2...e4，或者交易并形成卡尔斯巴德结构。

1...c5 2. e4 转置为阿拉宾西西里语。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. c3/1...c5
explanations.text:
Saragossa Opening

If white plays 2.e4 it is a transposition to the Alapin. You can keep this as unique Saragossa theory by playing 2.d4, but this is also likely to transpose into a London System with c5 and cxd4. This is considered as a bad opening as it hinders white's immediate piece development and is rarely seen in master games. In the Lichess Masters Database this line (1.c3 c5) has only appeared 27 times.

萨拉戈萨开幕

如果白棋下 2.e4，则它是到阿拉宾的变位。您可以通过玩 2.d4 将其保留为独特的萨拉戈萨理论，但这也可能转变成具有 c5 和 cxd4 的伦敦系统。这被认为是一个糟糕的开局，因为它阻碍了白棋的直接发展，并且在大师游戏中很少见。在巫妖大师数据库中，这一行（1.c3 c5）只出现了 27 次。

explanations.text:
Double Saragossa (c6?!)

Black creates double Saragossa opening on the board. This may be used to taunt opponent or later to be transposed into Caro-Kann Defense.

双萨拉戈萨 (c6?!)

黑棋在棋盘上创造了双萨拉戈萨开局。这可以用来嘲讽对手或稍后转换为卡罗-卡恩防御。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. c4
explanations.text:
__NOTOC__

1. c4 · English Opening

1. c4 is the English Opening. It is the fourth most commonly played opening move in chess. By playing this move, White allows the queen to move freely and also discourages Black from responding with 1...d5. Additionally, White ensures that the c-pawn will not be blocked behind a knight on c3. The resulting positions often resemble those that arise from 1. d4 openings rather than 1. e4 openings, and the move d4 is frequently played later on.

While this opening is not as sharp as 1. e4 or 1. d4, it is still effective in controlling the d5 square and is highly flexible, allowing for easy transpositions into other openings, and is often used when White desires to avoid certain responses to 1. d4 by Black. For example, transposition to Queen's Gambit and Indian Defence positions are very frequently seen.

Black's responses

/1...Nf6/ is likely to transpose into an Indian Defence or one of the alternative lines below.

/1...e5/ is a reversed Sicilian Defence, but the extra tempo for White changes the patterns noticeably.

/1...e6/ prepares 2...d5 and is known as the Agincourt Defense. It often ends up transposing to a Queen's Gambit Declined or Indian Defence. An independent alternative line is the Mikėnas-Carls Variation, continuing 2. Nc3 Nf6 3. e4.

/1...c5/ is the Symmetrical Variation, which has many unique lines. Often a d4 or d5 pawn break will occur later in the game.

/1...c6/ will usually either transpose into the Caro-Kann Defence or the Slav Defence.

/1...f5/, the Anglo-Dutch Defence, leads to sharp tactical lines for Black, but can open a powerful kingside attack. This is likely to transpose into the regular Dutch Defense after 2.d4.

/1...g6/ is likely to transpose into a King's Indian Defence, Reversed Sicilian, or Symmetrical Variation.

/1...b6/ will in all likelihood transpose into the English Defence.

/1...d5/ is seldom played but may transpose into the Queen's Gambit or the Réti Opening.

/1...b5/, the Jaenisch or Halibut Gambit, can give good practical chances for Black, but is considered unsound at the professional level.

/1...g5/, the Myers Defence, gives White a small advantage.

1...Nc6, the Anglo-Lithuanian Variation, is relatively rare, with 2. Nc3 or 2. g3 staying in the realm of English openings and 2. d4 transposing into a line in the Mikenas Defence.

Statistics

explanations.textZh:
__NOTOC__

1. c4 · 英语开头

1. c4 是英语开局。这是国际象棋中第四常见的开局动作。通过下这一步棋，白棋允许皇后自由移动，同时也阻止黑棋以 1...d5 回应。此外，白方确保 c-pawn 不会被挡在 c3 上的马后面。由此产生的局面通常类似于 1. d4 开局而不是 1. e4 开局产生的局面，并且 d4 棋步经常在稍后进行。

虽然这个开局不像 1. e4 或 1. d4 那样锐利，但它仍然可以有效地控制 d5 方格，并且高度灵活，可以轻松换位到其他开局，并且通常在白方希望避免黑方对 1. d4 做出某些反应时使用。例如，后翼弃兵和印度防御阵地的转换是很常见的。

黑方的回应

/1...Nf6/ 可能会转换为印度防御或下面的替代行之一。

/1...e5/ 是反向的西西里防御，但白棋的额外节奏明显改变了模式。

/1...e6/ 准备 2...d5，被称为阿金库尔防御。它通常最终会转变为后弃弃兵或印度防御。一条独立的替代线是 Mikėnas-Carls 变奏，继续 2. Nc3 Nf6 3. e4。

/1...c5/ 是对称变体，有许多独特的线条。 d4 或 d5 典当通常会在游戏后期发生。

/1...c6/ 通常会转换为卡罗-卡恩防御或斯拉夫防御。

/1...f5/，英荷防守，为黑方带来了尖锐的战术路线，但可以发起强大的王翼进攻。这很可能会在 2.d4 后转化为常规的荷兰防守。

/1...g6/ 可能会转换为国王印第安防御、反转西西里或对称变例。

/1...b6/ 很可能会转换为英国防守。

/1...d5/ 很少使用，但可能会转换为后弃兵或雷蒂开局。

/1...b5/，Jaenisch 或大比目鱼弃兵，可以为黑棋提供良好的实际机会，但在专业水平上被认为是不健全的。

/1...g5/，迈尔斯防御，给白方带来了一点优势。

1...Nc6，盎格鲁-立陶宛变体，相对罕见，2. Nc3 或 2. g3 停留在英语开局领域，2. d4 转入米克纳斯防守中的一条线。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. c4/1...a5
explanations.text:
English Opening

1...a5

Instead of developing a piece or contesting the center, Black plays in similar fashion to the Ware Defence. This move is a rare response to 1. c4 and hasn't been seen much. Black may want to develop their rook to a6 or march their a-pawn down the board to ruin White's queenside.

White can choose from a variety of responses, such as:

explanations.text:
English Opening: Halibut Gambit

The Halibut gambit is a wing gambit. Black sacrifices a pawn on b5 to move white's central pawn to the outermost flank, while also helping black develop his pieces after 3.bxa6 with either then 3...Bxa6, 3...Nxa6, or even 3...e5 ignoring the pawn like in the Benko Gambit and grabbing space in the center.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. c4/1...Nc6
explanations.text:
English Opening, Anglo-Lithuanian Variation

With the Anglo-Lithuanian Variation, Black develops their queenside knight and aims to control the central squares. This is a relatively rare move in the English Opening and could be transpositional.

2. d4 transposes into a line in the Mikenas Defence (1. d4 Nc6 2. c4) and grabs space in the center. This is the most accurate move.

However, White can stay in the realm of English openings by playing 2. Nc3 or 2. g3. This is the most popular approach.

然而，白棋可以通过下2. Nc3 或2. g3 留在英式开局的范围内。这是最流行的方法。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. c4/1...c5
explanations.text:
English Opening - Symmetrical Variation

1...c5

The Symmetrical Variation. Play varies greatly depending on how White chooses to develop. For instance, 2. Nf3 signals that White will try to achieve a favourable break with the d-pawn immediately and Black can then try to impede this break and achieve his own immediate d-pawn break.

2. Nc3 on the other hand makes it harder for Black to achieve that pawn break and signals White's intention to develop first and then break the symmetry. For instance, common moves for White in this variation include g3, Bg2, e4, Nge2, d3, and O-O (the arising white pawn structure is called the Botvinnik system) with the idea of a pawn break on f4, b4, or even d4. White may also play e3 instead of e4 and once the knight gets to e2 the pawn break on d4 becomes a very attractive possibility.

1...c5

2. Nc3 on the other hand makes it harder for Black to achieve that pawn break and signals White's intention to develop first and then break the symmetry. For instance, common moves for White in this variation include g3, Bg2, e4, Nge2, d3, and O-O (the arising white pawn structure is called the Botvinnik system) with the idea of a pawn break on f4, b4, or even d4. White may also play e3 instead of e4 and once the knight gets to e2 the pawn break on d4 becomes a very attractive possibility.
explanations.textZh:
英语开头 - 对称变化

1...c5

对称变化。根据白棋选择的发展方式，玩法会有很大差异。例如，2. Nf3 表示白方将尝试立即对 d 兵实现有利的突破，然后黑方可以尝试阻止这种突破并实现他自己的直接 d 兵突破。

2. 另一方面，Nc3 使黑方更难实现兵破，并表明白方打算先发展，然后打破对称性。例如，白方在此变体中的常见走法包括 g3、Bg2、e4、Nge2、d3 和 O-O（所出现的白棋结构称为博特维尼克系统），并在 f4、b4 甚至 d4 上突破棋子。白方也可以下 e3 而不是 e4，一旦马下到 e2，d4 上的兵突破就成为一种非常有吸引力的可能性。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. c4/1...c5/2. b4
explanations.text:
English Opening - Symmetrical Variation - Queen's Wing Gambit

Alternatively referred to as the "English Wing Gambit" or just the "Wing Gambit". Not to be confused with other wing gambits.

2. b4 is the characterising move of the Queen's Wing Gambit. White sacrifices b4 to Black's c5 pawn to bring it away from the centre planning to play a later d4, and to fianchetto the queenside bishop. Similar to the Queen's Gambit in the classical sense of drawing a central pawn away from the centre, thee Queen's Wing Gambit draws a centre-influencing pawn farther away from the centre to a place where it has essentially no effect.

The Queen's Wing Gambit is considered unsound by most masters and is uncommon in high-level play, but remains unrefuted and is playable. It is a Romantic-era opening.

Responses

Black usually responds in three main ways:

2. ... b6

Black declines the gambit, as well as providing fianchetto space to the black queenside bishop. White may exchange b-pawns (3. bxc5) or may continue developing (3. e3 / 3. Nf3).

2. ... d6

Black declines the gambit with a central pawn as opposed to a flank pawn. White may exchange (3. bxc5), and Black would have to recapture with a central pawn (3. ... dxc5) to maintain equal material, in essentiality exchanging control of the centre for the flank. Such a move is suboptimal but is not unplayable; this is similar to the Polish Opening's main exchange line between a central and flank pawn.

2. ... cxb4

Black accepts the gambit. White usually proceeds in these main ways:

3. d4

White may get straight to the point of why they got c5 out of the way: to get to controlling and occupying the centre with pawns. Similar to the Saduleto Variation of the Queen's Gambit Accepted (where White plays e4 as soon as possible, White chooses to play d4 before Black can play anything that hinders it e.g. e5 and the like.

3. Bb2

White fianchettoes their queenside bishop, controlling the centre from a distance as well as preventing Black e5. This is more of a hypermodern approach to the QWG. By this point, Black usually responds with 3. ... Nf6, 3. ... e6, or, more rarely, the Anglo-Scandinavian Defence-like d5.

3. a3

White offers to trade pawns, attempting to either gain initiative or space through Black's attempts to defend it, or to free up the queenside knight. This is similar to the pawn trade offer in the Benko Gambit of the Benoni Defence to the Indian Game. If Black were to accept (3. ... bxa3), White should develop the queenside bishop far through recapturing (4. Bxa3).

explanations.textZh:
英式开局 - 对称变式 - 皇后翼开局

或者称为“英式边翼开局”或简称为“边翼开局”。不要与其他翼策略混淆。

2. b4 是后翼弃兵的特征着法。白方将 b4 牺牲给黑方的 c5 棋子，使其远离中心，计划稍后下 d4，并向后翼主教出手。与经典意义上的将中央棋子拉离中心的后弃兵相似，后翼弃兵将影响中心的棋子从中心拉到远离中心的地方，使其基本上没有影响。

后翼开局被大多数大师认为是不健全的，并且在高水平游戏中并不常见，但仍然没有被驳倒并且可以玩。这是一个浪漫主义时代的开场。

回应

黑方通常以三种主要方式应对：

2....b6

黑方拒绝了这一策略，并为黑方后翼主教提供了前插空间。白棋可以交换 b-棋子 (3. bxc5) 或者可以继续发展 (3. e3 / 3. Nf3)。

2....d6

黑方用中央棋子而不是侧翼棋子拒绝这一策略。白棋可以交换（3. bxc5），黑棋必须用中央棋子（3. ... dxc5）重新夺回，以保持同等的材料，本质上是将中心的控制权交换为侧翼。这样的举动虽然不是最理想的，但也不是不可以玩的。这类似于波兰开局中中央棋子和侧翼棋子之间的主要交换线。

2. ...cxb4

黑棋接受了这个策略。白方通常以以下主要方式下棋：

3.d4

白棋可能会直截了当地解释他们为什么让出c5：用兵控制并占领中心。类似于接受后弃兵的 Saduleto 变例（其中白棋尽快下 e4，白棋选择在黑棋下任何阻碍它的东西之前下 d4，例如 e5 等）。

3. BB2

白方前卫是他们的后侧主教，从远处控制中心并阻止黑方 e5。这更像是 QWG 的超现代方法。此时，黑方通常会回应 3. ... Nf6、3. ... e6，或者更罕见的是类似盎格鲁-斯堪的纳维亚防御的 d5。

3.a3

白棋提出交换棋子，试图通过黑棋的防守来获得主动权或空间，或者释放后翼骑士。这类似于伯诺尼防御对印度游戏的 Benko Gambit 中的典当交易报价。如果黑方接受（3. ... bxa3），白方应该通过夺回（4. Bxa3）来发展后翼主教。

Black on the other hand might calmly accept the pawn exchange and develop comfortably, with the ideal of pinning and destroying the white knight on c3. This can also lead to Catalan type of positions where white plays g3 and Bg2.

1...e5

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. c4/1...e5/2. Nc3
explanations.text:
English Opening

2.Nc3

An instant way of reinforcing the attack on d5, Nc3 is the standard second move of the independent lines of the English opening. This move is also useful because it allows 3.Nf3, although some players prefer to play the Bremen System with 3.g3 preparing for 4.Bg2, and thus increasing control over d5 and keeping two good options for the development of the king's knight (a standard Nf3 or Ne2, which keeps the long diagonal open and offers some protection against the pinning and possible exchange of the other knight).

The flexibility of the English opening also applies for the black side which must choose how to develop after this move. While 2...Nf6 is flexible and provides some control over d5, 2...Nc6 is also possible, leading to sharp variations where white will have the initiative on the q-side with moves such as e3, Nge2, d4, Rb1 and b4, while black will have some counterplay on the opposite wing by advancing his k-side pawns, threatening to put the white king in some serious jeopardy.

Another black option is 2... Bb4, which allows Nd5 chasing the bishop, but the resulting position is unclear, so most players choose to play a more passive move such as 3. e3 or 3. Nf3, which allows black to take and try to place pawns on dark squares to create an imbalanced and double-edged position.

2.NC3

Nc3 是加强 d5 进攻的即时方式，是英式开局独立线的标准第二步。这个动作也很有用，因为它允许3.Nf3，尽管有些玩家更喜欢用3.g3来玩不莱梅系统，为4.Bg2做准备，从而增加对d5的控制，并为国王的骑士的发展保留两个好的选择（标准的Nf3或Ne2，它保持长对角线开放，并提供一些保护，防止其他骑士的钉住和可能的交换）。

英式开局的灵活性也适用于黑方，黑方必须选择此步棋后如何发展。虽然 2...Nf6 很灵活，可以对 d5 提供一定的控制，但 2...Nc6 也是可能的，这会导致急剧的变化，其中白方将通过 e3、Nge2、d4、Rb1 和 b4 等走法在 q 方占据主动，而黑方将通过推进其 k 方棋子在对面翼上进行一些反击，从而威胁到白王处于某种严重的危险之中。

黑棋的另一个选择是2...Bb4，它允许Nd5追象，但最终的位置并不清楚，因此大多数玩家选择下更被动的棋子，例如3.e3或3.Nf3，这使得黑棋可以采取并尝试将棋子放置在黑暗的方块上，从而形成不平衡和双刃剑的位置。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. c4/1...e5/2. Nc3/2...Nc6
explanations.text:
English Opening

2...Nc6

A good second move for black, 2...Nc6 keeps most options open for black including the possibility of transposition into the English four knights variation after 3.Nf3. Black must choose how to develop after this move; for instance more often than not white will fianchetto his light-squared bishop and pursue a q-side attack; in those cases it may be desirable to play f5, since the pawn duo on f5 and e5 along with a knight on f6 more often than not will present a formidable front with good counterplay possibilities vs a q-side attack by white. However as in most k-side pawn attacks black should be careful not to overextend these pawns as doing so might get them restrained and then destroyed by white, effectively putting black on the defensive.

Aside from the English four knights the main option for white is to prepare a q-side attack by playing the bishop to g2, the king´s knight to e2 and the rook to b1; different move orders are possible but the idea is the same: to achieve a beneficial pawn break on d4 (ideally exchanging black's e pawn, for example: e3, Ne2, d4 and after black takes the d pawn white recaptures with his e pawn effectively increasing his power on the center and q-side while at the same time weakening black's counterplay) and/or to support a pawn advance to b4 (a3 and Rb1 are good moves for this purpose). Using the subsequent spatial advantage on the q-side while neutralizing black's counterplay on the opposite wing does require some skill however and white is best advised not to neglect his k-side in favor of an all out q-side attack and to seek the restraint and destruction of black's f and e pawns, for example after 3.g3 f5 4.e3 Nf6 5.Nge2 Bb4 6.Bg2 0-0 7.0-0 d6 8.d4 +/=, and should black push his e pawn to e4 white can undermine it with f3 and get an open file for the rook on f1 in the process.

2...NC6

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. c4/1...e5/2. Nc3/2...Nf6
explanations.text:
English Opening

2...Nf6

This position, also reachable through the move orders 1...e5/2.Nc3 Nf6, can lead to two important variations of the English opening depending on how white chooses to develop. 3.Nf3 is the natural developing move and more often than not it leads to the English four knights variation simply because black must defend their pawn and the most practical way to do it is with 3...Nc6. After this white will usually develop their bishop to g2 and castle kingside. Black has a variety of options against this variation including the pinning of the knight on c3 with the dual idea of advancing the pawn on e5 and inflicting doubled pawns.

The other option for white is to get the bishop to g2 first and then choosing how to develop the knight, this idea is known as the Bremen system. The Bremen System has the advantage of maintaining flexibility in the development of the knight while also increasing control of the d5 square and putting extra pressure on black´s q-side. Black on the other hand might choose to counter this pressure by advancing their pawn to c6, the Keres variation, with the idea of creating a sturdy pawn formation which white must either undermine with their own pawns or fall to.

2...NF6

这个位置也可以通过移动指令 1...e5/2.Nc3 Nf6 到达，可以导致英式开局的两个重要变化，具体取决于白棋如何选择发展。 3.Nf3 是自然发展的走法，通常它会导致英国四骑士变体，仅仅是因为黑方必须保卫他们的棋子，而最实用的方法是使用 3...Nc6。在此之后，白方通常会将其主教发展到g2和城堡王侧。黑方对于这种变化有多种选择，包括将马钉在 c3 上，同时将棋子推进到 e5 上并造成双棋。

白方的另一个选择是先让主教进入g2，然后再选择如何发展骑士，这个想法被称为不来梅系统。不莱梅系统的优点是保持了马发展的灵活性，同时也增强了对 d5 方格的控制，并对黑方的 q 方施加了额外的压力。另一方面，黑方可能会选择通过将其棋子推进到 c6（Keres 变体）来应对这种压力，其想法是创建一个坚固的棋子阵型，白棋必须用自己的棋子破坏该阵型，否则就会落入其中。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. c4/1...e5/2. Nc3/2...Nf6/3. Nf3/3...e4/4. Ng5/4...c6
explanations.text:
Adhiban Gambit

The Adhiban Gambit rose to prominence in 2021, when Neural Network Leela Zero inspired strong GM Adhiban Baskaran to play this for the first time in the Meltwater Rapid Indian Qualifier, which is the qualifier for the prestigious Meltwater rapid. This has overtaken the popular Bellon Gambit (4..b5!?) which was refuted in the pre-computer era. As this opening is relatively new, theory is still developing.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. c4/1...e5/2. Nc3/2...Nf6/3. g3
explanations.text:
English Opening

3. g3

White plans to develop their bishop into the long diagonal. By doing this, the bishop will exert some serious pressure into the central light squares (especially d5) and into the enemy queenside. This does not come without issues however, as a king castled behind a fianchettoed bishop becomes very vulnerable should the bishop be removed.

Black now has two acceptable options, one is to play d5 immediately as delaying this move will allow white to achieve overprotection of this important central square by 4.Bg2.

Another choice for black, perhaps the sharpest, is to play 3...c6, the knight will be blocked from its best square but black regains control over the d5 square and closes the long diagonal for a bishop on g2. Once d5 has been played by black, his mighty center may cause some problems for white, although (as always) the more developed player can undermine it in hypermodern fashion through the use of his c- pawn, knights and fianchettoed bishop.

explanations.textZh:
英语开场

3.g3

白棋计划将他们的象发展成长对角线。通过这样做，主教将对中央光格（尤其是 d5）和敌方后翼施加一些严重的压力。然而，这并不是没有问题的，因为如果主教被罢免，被困在尖头主教后面的国王就会变得非常脆弱。

黑方现在有两个可接受的选择，一是立即下d5，因为延迟这一步将使白方通过4.Bg2实现对这个重要中心方格的过度保护。

黑方的另一个选择，也许是最敏锐的，是下3...c6，马将被阻挡在其最佳方格之外，但黑方重新控制了d5方格，并为g2上的主教关闭了长对角线。一旦黑方下出d5，他强大的中锋可能会给白方带来一些问题，尽管（一如既往）更发达的棋手可以通过使用他的c兵、马和fianchettoed主教以超现代的方式破坏它。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. c4/1...e5/2. g3
explanations.text:
English Opening

2.g3

White prepares to fianchetto the king's bishop on the long diagonal with 3. Bg2, putting more pressure on the d5-square and discouraging black from moving a pawn to d5. If black is determined to put a pawn d5, they can play 2...c6, leading to the Reversed Alapin, that is, the main line of the Alapin Variation with colours reversed: 1. c4 e5 2. g3 c6 3. Nf3 e4 4. Nd4.

Instead of playing 2...c6 black might also immediately play 2...d5, which a good move that (after 3. cxd5 Qxd5) forces white to protect its rook by blocking with 4. Nf3. Unfortunately, a tempting mistake is to play 4...e4? which loses a pawn if 5. Nc3 Qe6 6. Qa4+ Bd7 7. Qxe4. Black can keep material parity with 5...Qc6, but must take care to defend against the pin of 7. Bb5 if white opens the diagonal with 6. e3. If black instead greedily takes with 6...exf3??, white trades the two minor pieces for black's queen.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. c4/1...e6
explanations.text:
English Opening: Agincourt Defence

1...e6

1.c4 e6 is the Agincourt Defence (named for the Battle of Agincourt, fought between the English and the French). Black fights for control of d5 and plans to put a pawn there. Common replies to this opening are 2.Nf3, 2.Nc3, and 2.g3.

1...e6

1.c4 e6 是阿金库尔防御（以英国和法国之间的阿金库尔战役命名）。黑方争夺 d5 的控制权并计划在那里放一颗棋子。此开场白的常见回复是 2.Nf3、2.Nc3 和 2.g3。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. c4/1...f5
explanations.text:
English Opening: Anglo-Dutch Defence

1...f5

Black plays in similar fashion to the Dutch Defence, controlling the e4 pawn with the f-pawn. Named the Anglo-Dutch Defence, this offbeat response to the English Opening mimics 1. d4 f5 and can transpose to it regularly.

White can choose from a variety of responses, such as:

2. d4, transposing to the Dutch Defence

2. Nc3, developing the queenside knight

2. Nf3, developing the kingside knight

2. g3, preparing to fianchetto the f1 bishop

2. b3, preparing to fianchetto the c1 bishop

2. Qc2, attacking the pawn on f5 with the queen

2. e4!?, the Hickmann Gambit

2. g4!?, the Wade Gambit

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. c4/1...f6
explanations.text:
English Opening

1...f6?!

A rare and less conventional response to the English Opening. Black plays in similar fashion to the Barnes Defence, weakening the king and stripping the kingside knight of its most natural developing square, though not quite as weak as 1. e4 f6 or 1. d4 f6 as White doesn't have an immediate way of exploiting the weakness and prepares e5 without any tactical pitfalls (e.g. 1. e4 f6? 2. d4 e5 3. dxe5 fxe5?? 4. White can choose from a variety of responses, such as:

2. Nc3, developing the queenside knight

2. Nf3, developing the kingside knight

2. g3, preparing to fianchetto the f1 bishop

2. b3, preparing to fianchetto the c1 bishop

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. c4/1...g5
explanations.text:
English Opening: Myers Defence

After playing 1. c4, White can no longer support the centre with c3. By playing a version of Grob's Attack, Black intends to put pressure on d4. Nevertheless, White obtains a significant advantage but must play carefully because Black puts a lot of pressure on White's queenside.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. c4/1...Nf6
explanations.text:
English Opening: Anglo-Indian Defence

Black keeps their options open with this move. After a d4 advance by white, the game may transpose into an Indian defence.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. c4/1...Nf6/2. Nc3
explanations.text:
English Opening

2. Nc3

White reinforces the attack on the d5 square and keeps his options open. Black has a variety of answers here, aiming for a King's Indian setup with 2...g6 is an interesting option, 2...e6 is also possible although white can choose to disrupt black's plan of reaching a Nimzo-Indian or QID setup by playing 3. e4 leading to the very sharp and tactical variations known collectively as the Mikenas Carls variation, which black is best advised to avoid if not prepared to face them.

2...e5 is also possible leading to the English four knights and the Bremen system

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. c4/1...Nf6/2. Nc3/2...e6
explanations.text:
English Opening

2...e6

A flexible second move by black reaching a Nimzo-Indian or Queen's Indian defence setup is a possibility for black with good prospects as pinning the white knight at c3 weakens white's grip over the d5 square and threatens doubled pawns, not to mention that since white has not yet moved his d-pawn black might as well get a lead in development.

Black should be careful about this move however as white has the option of playing 3.e4 a move that leads to the ultra sharp Mikenas Carls variation where black will require very accurate play in order to stay alive.

And last but not least 3.Nf3 will lead to the more tactical lines of the symmetrical English after 3...c5 and a fight over the d4 and d5 squares will develop.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. c4/1...Nf6/2. Nc3/2...g6
explanations.text:
English Opening

2...g6

Black signals his intention to reach a KID setup. White can choose to seize central space and transpose into a standard KID by playing 3. d4 or to stay in the English opening by playing 3. g3. This refusal to seize central space by white does give white some flexibility and tactical subtleties in return. As the usual idea in the KID is to undermine the white center the apparently dimmer 3. g3 signals that white will develop first and get some strong control over the center before actually advancing his central pawns, which will make it much harder for black to destroy them through a conventional KID strategy.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. c4/1...Nh6
explanations.text:
English Opening

1...Nh6?!

The rarest response to the English Opening in amateur play, playing in similar fashion to the Adams/Hippopotamus Defence. Instead of contesting the center or developing the knight to f6, Black moves the knight to the rim for not much reason.

White can choose from a variety of responses, such as:

2. d4, pushing a central pawn to take control of the center

2. Nc3, developing the queenside knight normally

2. Nf3, developing the kingside knight normally

2. g3, preparing to fianchetto the kingside bishop.

2. b3, preparing to fianchetto the queenside bishop.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d3/1...e5
explanations.text:
Mieses Opening: Reversed Rat

1...e5

With 1...e5, named the Reversed Rat, Black takes the center as White didn't so it themselves with their timid starting move. The Mieses Opening is usually flexible for White as they haven't made a big commitment yet.

Responses

The most common amateur move, 2. e4, transposes to the Leonardis Variation of the King's Pawn Opening. Although it controls the center, it doesn't fully help White's development as their f1 bishop is blocked by the pawn on d3.

2. c4, Stockfish's most preferred move, transposes to a line more commonly seen in the English Opening (1. c4 e5 2. d3). It controls a central square, d5, and helps the b1 white knight to develop to c3 without blocking the c-pawn which would usually be on c2.

2. Nf3 is a good move, attacking the pawn on e5 while developing the knight on g1. Black cannot kick the knight away with 2...e4 as the pawn on d3 controls e4.

2. g3 has the simple idea of fianchettoing the kingside bishop to g2, as on the f1-a6 diagonal, the pawn on d3 blocks it from reaching anywhere past e2.

2. Nd2, the Valencia Opening, is a less orthodox response to 1...e5 as it blocks in the queenside bishop and cramps White's development a bit. However, it is fully playable as it develops the knight towards the center and the c1 bishop still has options of fianchettoing to b2 after the b-pawn moves to b3.

2. d4!? reaches a position which is identical to the Scandinavian Defence, but with colours reversed. Any position that can be reached from the normal Scandinavian can be reached from 2. d4!?, just with colours flipped.

explanations.textZh:
米塞斯开局：逆转的老鼠

1...e5

1...e5，被称为反向老鼠，黑方占据了中心，而白方则没有因此而采取了他们胆怯的开局。米塞斯开局对于白棋来说通常很灵活，因为他们还没有做出重大承诺。

回应

最常见的业余走法 2. e4，转换为国王兵开局的莱昂纳迪变化。虽然它控制了中心，但并不能完全帮助白方发展，因为他们的f1主教被d3上的棋子挡住了。

2. c4，Stockfish 最喜欢的走法，转置为英语开局中更常见的行（1. c4 e5 2. d3）。它控制一个中心方格d5，并帮助b1白骑士发展到c3，而不阻挡通常在c2上的c兵。

2. Nf3是个好棋，攻击e5上的兵，同时发展g1上的马。黑方无法用 2...e4 踢走马，因为 d3 上的棋子控制着 e4。

2. g3 的简单想法是将王翼主教向 g2 移动，因为在 f1-a6 对角线上，d3 上的棋子阻止它到达 e2 之外的任何位置。

2. Nd2，瓦伦西亚开局，是对 1...e5 的不太正统的反应，因为它阻挡了后翼主教并限制了怀特的发展。然而，它是完全可玩的，因为它将马向中心发展，并且在b兵移动到b3后，c1主教仍然可以选择fianchettoing到b2。

2.d4！？到达的位置与斯堪的纳维亚防御相同，但颜色相反。从普通斯堪的纳维亚可以到达的任何位置都可以从 2.d4!? 到达，只需翻转颜色即可。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4
explanations.text:
1. d4 · Queen's Pawn opening

1. d4 is the Queen's pawn opening. With 1. d4 White looks to take over control of the centre. The pawn directly controls the c5 and e5 squares, and White's queen now 'sees' the d4 square. 1. d4 is also a developing move in that it opens a diagonal for the queen's bishop to venture into the game later.

1. d4 is the second most common first move, after 1. e4. As the d4 pawn is already supported by the queen, the opening moves of Queen's Pawn games tend to be less forcing than King's Pawn games. This leads, in general, to games that are more closed and positional than open and tactical. 1. d4 is aimed at slowing down Black's development rather than accelerating White's.

If allowed, White could play 2. e4 next and achieve a big, two-pawn centre, and develop comfortably in all the space that affords them. Therefore a priority for Black is to prevent this.

Control e4

The chief approach to preventing 2. e4 is to control the e4 square.

1...d5, the Closed game, is the classical approach. It controls the c4 and e4 squares, and so if White does play 2. e4, they at least cannot keep the pawn there. 1...d5 also prevents White from pushing their d4 pawn to d5, and so secures some space for Black to develop. Additionally, like 1. d4 for White, 1...d5 helps Black to develop by releasing their queenside bishop. The most common continuation is 2. c4, the Queen's gambit, the champagne and caviar of White openings. 1...d5 is the most common at the club level and the second most common reply in tournament games.

1...Nf6, the Indian defence, controls e4 while developing a knight. This is a more flexible response: Black may yet commit a pawn to the centre, like ...d5 to transpose into classical lines, or they may play in a hypermodern style where they control the centre from afar with their pieces. 1...Nf6 is the mainline today.

1...f5, the Dutch defence, controls e4 with a flank pawn. Black acts on the principle that trading an important central pawn for one of their more peripheral pawns would be good for them. Black can develop their g8 knight behind f pawn, and can create a robust pawn structure with e6 and d5 (the Stonewall set-up) or d6 and g6 (fianchettoing the bishop, the Leningrad). The Dutch is a minor sideline. Advancing one's f-pawn while one's king is still in the centre isn't for the faint of heart: an example trap that exploits the weak e8-to-h5 diagonal is: 2. e4 fxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 (to hold onto the pawn) 4. Bg5 d5?? 5. Bxf6 exf6 6. Qh5+ g6 7. Qxd5 Qxd5 8. Nxd5 (forking the f6 and c7 pawns).

Attack d4

Another approach to preventing White from attaining the two-pawn centre is to attack d4.

1...e5?! is the Englund gambit. It offers White a pawn to deflect their pawn away from d4. This gambit is considered unsound, but it conceals many traps and has some success as a club-level line. If White prioritises their development over holding onto the pawn, they will enjoy a comfortable edge.

1...c5 is the Old Benoni. It offers White a less valuable flank pawn for their central d4 pawn. If they accept it, Black can easily recover it and enjoy having two central pawns to White's one. However, White is not compelled to accept the pawn: the mainline is 2. d5. It results in closed positions where White has more space.

Allow 2. e4

Alternatively, Black can allow White to play 2. e4 for now and look to undermine it later. Essentially Black gives White the option of transposing into an e4 opening (that Black hopes to be more familiar with than White). It's a curious fact that in practice White usually declines to play e4 right away even if allowed to do so, instead choosing to keep things in conventional Queen's pawn opening territory.

1...e6, the Horwitz defence, is the chief alternative to 1...d5 or 1...Nf6. This is essentially a transpositional trick: it invites White to play 2. e4 and transposes into the French defence after 2...d5, which happens about one in ten games. If Black plays the French against 1. e4, then this is a way to move to more familiar territory. If White chooses to stay in 1. d4 territory with 2. c4 instead, Black can transpose into a Queen's gambit declined (with 2...d5), a Dutch (2...f5), or a Nimzo-Indian/Bogo-Indian with 2...Nf6.

Similar approaches offering transposition into an e4 opening include:

1...c6: after 2. e4 d5, the game transposes to a Caro-Kann. Otherwise, White can play 2. c4 and the game becomes a Slav after 2...d5.

1...Na6?! is a vanishingly rare move that nonetheless has a name, the Australian defence, which can transpose into the De Bruycker variation of the Caro-Kann after 2. e4 c6.

1...Nc6, the eccentric Mikenas defence, invites 2. e4 and transposition into a Nimzowitsch defence, but 2. Nf3, 2. c4, or 2. d5 chasing the knight away are all more popular.

1...b6, the English defence, prepares a queenside fianchetto. After 2. e4 it transposes to an Owen's defence, otherwise after 2.
