explanations.textZh:
1. d4 · 后兵开局

1. d4 是后兵开局。 1. d4 白方看起来要接管中心的控制权。棋子直接控制 c5 和 e5 方格，而白方后现在“看到”d4 方格。 1. d4也是一个发展着的棋步，因为它为后王的主教随后冒险进入游戏打开了一条对角线。

1. d4 是第二常见的第一步，仅次于 1. e4。由于 d4 棋子已经得到了皇后的支持，因此皇后棋子游戏的开局动作往往不如国王棋子游戏那么强制。一般来说，这会导致比赛更加封闭和定位，而不是开放和战术性。 1. d4 的目的是减缓黑方的发展而不是加速白方的发展。

如果允许的话，白方接下来可以下2.e4，并实现一个大的、两个兵的中心，并在所有提供给他们的空间中舒适地发展。因此，黑棋的首要任务是防止这种情况发生。

控制e4

预防2. e4的主要方法是控制e4方块。

1...d5（封闭式游戏）是经典方法。它控制 c4 和 e4 方格，因此如果白方确实下 2. e4，他们至少不能将棋子保留在那里。 1...d5 还可以防止白方将 d4 兵推至 d5，从而为黑方提供了一些发展空间。此外，就像白棋的 1.d4 一样，1...d5 通过释放后翼主教来帮助黑棋发展。最常见的延续是2.c4，后弃兵，白方开局的香槟和鱼子酱。 1...d5 是俱乐部级别最常见的回复，也是锦标赛游戏中第二常见的回复。

1...Nf6，印度防守，控制e4，同时发展骑士。这是一个更灵活的反应：黑方可能会将棋子放到中心，就像...d5 转换成古典线，或者他们可能会以超现代的风格下棋，用棋子从远处控制中心。 1...Nf6是今天的主线。

1...f5，荷兰防守，用侧翼棋子控制 e4。黑棋遵循的原则是，用一个重要的中心棋子换取一个较外围的棋子对他们来说是有好处的。黑方可以在f兵后面发展他们的g8马，并且可以用e6和d5（石墙设置）或d6和g6（fianchettoing主教，列宁格勒）创建一个强大的兵结构。荷兰队是一个次要的副业。当一个人的国王仍然在中心时推进一个人的 f-pawn 不适合胆小的人：利用弱 e8-to-h5 对角线的一个示例陷阱是： 2. e4 fxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 （抓住棋子） 4. Bg5 d5?? 5. Bxf6 exf6 6. Qh5+ g6 7. Qxd5 Qxd5 8. Nxd5（分叉 f6 和 c7 棋子）。

攻击d4

阻止白方到达两兵中心的另一种方法是攻击 d4。

1...e5？！这是英格兰的策略。它为白方提供了一个棋子，使他们的棋子偏离 d4。这种策略被认为是不明智的，但它隐藏着许多陷阱，并且作为俱乐部级别的路线取得了一些成功。如果白棋优先考虑发展而不是守住棋子，他们将享有舒适的优势。

1...c5 是老伯诺尼。它为白方的中央 d4 棋子提供了一个价值较低的侧翼棋子。如果他们接受它，黑方可以轻松地收回它，并享受拥有两个中心棋子而白棋的一个棋子。然而，白棋并不被迫接受棋子：主线是 2. d5。这会导致白方有更多空间的封闭局面。

允许 2.e4

或者，黑方可以暂时让白方下2.e4，然后再考虑破坏它。本质上黑棋给了白棋转入 e4 开局的选择（黑棋希望比白棋更熟悉）。一个奇怪的事实是，在实践中，即使允许，白方通常也会拒绝立即下 e4，而是选择将事情保留在传统的后后兵开局区域。

1...e6，霍维茨防御，是 1...d5 或 1...Nf6 的主要替代方案。这本质上是一种换位技巧：它邀请白方下2.e4，并在2...d5之后转入法国防守，这种情况大约发生在十分之一的比赛中。如果黑棋对法国棋 1.e4，那么这是进入更熟悉领域的一种方式。如果白方选择留在 1.d4 区域并使用 2.c4，则黑方可以将其转换为后弃策略（使用 2...d5）、荷兰策略（2...f5）或使用 2...Nf6 的尼姆佐-印度/博戈-印度。

提供转入 e4 开头的类似方法包括：

1...c6：2.e4 d5 之后，游戏转换为 Caro-Kann。否则，白棋可以下 2.c4，并且在 2...d5 后游戏变成斯拉夫棋。

1...Na6？！这是一个极其罕见的举动，但有一个名字，澳大利亚防御，它可以在 2. e4 c6. 之后转换为 Caro-Kann 的 De Bruycker 变体。

1...NC6，古怪的米克纳斯防守，邀请2. e4并换位为尼姆佐维奇防守，但2. Nf3、2. c4或2. d5追赶骑士都更受欢迎。

1...b6，英国后卫，准备后翼前卫。在 2. e4 之后，它转换为欧文的防守，否则在 2. e4 之后。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...a5
explanations.text:
Queen's Pawn Opening

1...a5?!

Black plays in a fashion similar to the Ware Defence. Instead of contesting the center or developing a piece, Black pushes a flank pawn. This rare response to 1. d4 is dubious.

White can choose from a variety of moves, such as:

2. e4, taking the full center

2. c4, playing in the fashion of Queen's Pawn openings

2. Bf4, playing in the fashion of the London

2. Nf3, developing the kingside knight

2. Nc3, developing the queenside knight

皇后典当开局

1...a5？！

黑方的下法与威尔防御类似。黑方没有与中心争夺或发展棋子，而是推侧翼棋子。这种对 1.d4 的罕见回应是值得怀疑的。

白方可以选择多种走法，例如：

2. e4，取全中心

2. c4，以皇后兵开局的方式进行游戏

2. Bf4，玩转伦敦时尚

2. Nf3，开发王翼骑士

2. NC3，开发后翼骑士

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...a6
explanations.text:
Queen's Pawn Opening

1...a6

This less conventional response to 1. d4 plays in a similar fashion to the St. George Defence, where Black aims to expand on the queenside. Instead of developing a piece or central pawn, Black pushes a flank pawn, but as long as played seriously, this is playable.

White can choose from a variety of moves, such as:

2. c4, playing in a normal Queen's Pawn fashion

2. Bf4, playing in a London fashion

2. e4, transposing to the St. George Defence

2. Nf3, developing the kingside knight

2. Nc3, developing the queenside knight

皇后典当开局

1...a6

这种对 1.d4 的不太传统的反应与圣乔治防守类似，黑方的目标是在后翼扩大。黑棋不是发展棋子或中央棋，而是推侧棋，但只要认真下棋，这是可以下的。

白方可以选择多种走法，例如：

2. c4，以正常的后卒方式进行游戏

2. Bf4，以伦敦时尚的方式演奏

2. e4，移至圣乔治防御

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...b5
explanations.text:
1...b5 · Polish defence

Black prepares their queen's side bishop to be fianchettoed, and Black's pawn on b5 prevents White from playing c4.

However, this allows 2. e4 and White is able to occupy the centre with both pawns.
explanations.textEn:
1...b5 · Polish defence

Black prepares their queen's side bishop to be fianchettoed, and Black's pawn on b5 prevents White from playing c4.

However, this allows 2. e4 and White is able to occupy the centre with both pawns.
explanations.textZh:
1...b5 · 波兰防守

黑方准备好他们的后侧主教被双翼攻击，而黑方在 b5 上的棋子阻止了白方下 c4。

然而，这允许 2. e4 并且白方能够用两个棋子占据中心。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...b6
explanations.text:
__NOTOC__

1... b6 - English Defence

With the move 1.... b6 Black prepares to develop the Queenside Bishop. It's also a flexible option when played with the e6 development as Black has various ideas involving the e6, Nf6, Bb4, Bb7 moves.

White's responses

White likely to respond with one of the following:

2. c4 A standard reply, White continues in Queen Gambit formation ready to play e4.

2. Nf3 May transpose into a Queen's Indian Defence.

2. e4 This move order arrives at an Owen's Defence.

__NOTOC__

1... b6 - 英格兰防守

随着棋步 1.... b6 黑方准备发展后侧主教。当使用 e6 发展时，这也是一个灵活的选择，因为黑方有各种涉及 e6、Nf6、Bb4、Bb7 走法的想法。

白的回应

白方可能会做出以下反应之一：

2. c4 标准答复，白方继续后弃兵阵型，准备下 e4。

2. Nf3 可以转换为女王印第安防御。

2. e4 此移动指令到达欧文防御。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Na6
explanations.text:
1...Na6?! · Australian defence

1...Na6?! is a rare and dubious reply to 1. d4.

This is not a good developing move, as knights are not so effective on the rim of the board, however it keeps the c6 square available so that 2. e4 can be met with 2...c6, transposing into the De Bruycker sideline of the Caro-Kann. In this variation the knight routes from a6 to c7.

Although, after 2. c4 c6, Black can't exactly play a Caro-Kann, so they might wish they have played the move order 1. d4 c6, where 2. e4 can still be met with 2...Na6 (if they really want to) but against 2. c4 Black retains the option of a Slav defence 2...d5.

History

The earliest Australian connection with this move appears to be a game in the 1993-4 Australian Championship, Kagan v Wohl, which continued 2. Nf3 d6 3. e4 c6. Alexander Wohl played this line frequently in the '90s.

Magnus Carlsen played 1...Na6 against Aleksander Indjic in a Titled Tuesday blitz game in 2025. He continued in the manner of an Englund gambit with 2. c4 e5 3. dxe5 d6.

explanations.textZh:
1...Na6？！ · 澳大利亚国防

1...Na6？！这是对 1. d4 的罕见且可疑的答复。

这不是一个好的发展动作，因为骑士在棋盘边缘的效率不高，但是它保留了 c6 方格，以便 2. e4 可以与 2...c6 相遇，转移到 Caro-Kann 的 De Bruycker 边线。在这个变体中，马从 a6 路线到 c7。

虽然，在 2. c4 c6 之后，黑方无法完全发挥卡罗-卡恩的作用，所以他们可能希望自己已经发挥了移动顺序 1. d4 c6，其中 2. e4 仍然可以遇到 2...Na6（如果他们真的愿意），但对抗 2. c4 黑方保留了斯拉夫防御 2...d5 的选项。

历史

澳大利亚与这一举动最早的联系似乎是 1993-4 澳大利亚锦标赛中的一场比赛，Kagan v Wohl，比赛继续 2. Nf3 d6 3. e4 c6。亚历山大·沃尔 (Alexander Wohl) 在 20 世纪 90 年代经常使用这句台词。

马格努斯·卡尔森 (Magnus Carlsen) 在 2025 年的周二闪电战比赛中对阵亚历山大·因吉奇 (Aleksander Indjic)，打出 1...Na6。他继续采用英格兰策略，打出 2. c4 e5 3. dxe5 d6。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nc6
explanations.text:
1...Nc6 · Mikenas defence

A rare move. 1...Nc6 develops a knight and prepares ...e5. Part of the idea is, like a reflection of the Alekhine defence, 1. e4 Nf6, to encourage White to overextend in the centre before counter-attacking.

Original positions can arise if White plays d5, kicking the knight, either immediately, 2. d5, or after a sequence like 2. c4 e5 3. d5. Otherwise the often game transposes into positions more commonly reached by other move orders.

2. Nf3 is most common move, developing and controlling e5. This allows Black to play 2...d5 and the game resumes some sense of normality, although it is unusual in 1. d4 d5 games for Black to play Nc6 so early and deprive themselves of the option to move their c-pawn.

2. c4 d5 transposes into the Chigorin defence to the Queen's gambit, normally seen in the order 1. d4 d5 2. c4 Nc6.

2. e4 transposes into the Nimzowitsch defence, usually seen after 1. e4 Nc6 2. d4.

1...NC6 · 米凯纳斯防守

一个罕见的举动。 1...Nc6 培养骑士并准备 ...e5。这个想法的一部分是，就像阿廖欣防守的反映一样，1. e4 Nf6，鼓励白方在反击之前在中路过度伸展。

如果白方下 d5，踢马，则可能会出现原始位置，要么立即 2. d5，要么在 2. c4 e5 3. d5 等序列之后。否则，游戏通常会转移到其他移动指令更常见的位置。

2. Nf3是最常见的走法，发展并控制e5。这使得黑方可以下 2...d5 并且游戏恢复了某种正常感，尽管在 1. d4 d5 游戏中黑方这么早就下 Nc6 并剥夺了自己移动 c 兵的选择权是不寻常的。

2. c4 d5 转置为后弃兵的齐戈林防御，通常按顺序 1. d4 d5 2. c4 Nc6。

2. e4 转置为尼姆佐维奇防御，通常出现在 1. e4 Nc6 2. d4 之后。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nc6/2. d5
explanations.text:
2. d5

White attacks the knight. While /2...Ne5/ is the most common reply, /2...Nb8/ is slightly preferred by Stockfish on depth 55, even though it puts Black back into starting position.

2.d5

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...c5
explanations.text:
__NOTOC__

1...c5 - Old Benoni Defence/ Benoni Defense

The Old Benoni Defense is quite rare and uncommon nowadays but can actually lead to a tactical and sharp game. Black takes a swipe with c5 and gambits a pawn for the exchange, develops, and gets pieces into the game. White normally responds with d5; taking the pawn is not recommended because of 2...e6, and if White tries defending, then a5 and White has no solutions to hold on to pawns while Black gains a tempo. This opening is quite rare nowadays.

One idea for Black is to transpose to a Modern Benoni while avoiding the Four Pawn Attack (that is, variations with an early f2-f4 for White). Black can fianchetto his King's Bishop, and only after White plays Nf3 blocking an f-pawn, continue with ... e6 and ... exd5.

Another idea for Black is to keep the h8-a1 diagonal of Black's bishop open by delaying ... Nf6. Black could then play ... Ne7 instead of ... Nf6, or possibly, if White plays an early Nc3, give up his bishop by ... Bc3 to double the pawns.

explanations.textZh:
__NOTOC__

1...c5 - 旧伯诺尼防御/伯诺尼防御

老伯诺尼防御如今相当罕见，但实际上可以带来战术性和犀利的比赛。黑方用 c5 横扫并下棋以交换棋子，发展并获得棋子进入游戏。白方通常响应 d5；不建议拿走棋子，因为 2...e6，如果白方尝试防守，那么 a5 和白方没有解决办法来保住棋子，而黑方则获得节奏。如今，这种开放是非常罕见的。

黑方的一个想法是转换为现代贝诺尼，同时避免四兵攻击（即白方早期 f2-f4 的变体）。黑方可以先手攻击他的国王主教，并且只有在白方下出 Nf3 阻挡 f 兵后，才能继续... e6 和 ... exd5。

黑方的另一个想法是通过延迟... Nf6 来保持黑方象的 h8-a1 对角线打开。然后黑方可以下... Ne7 而不是... Nf6，或者可能，如果白方下早期的Nc3，则通过... Bc3 放弃他的主教以使兵加倍。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...c6
explanations.text:
1...c6

1...c6 is a transpositional tool. Black gives White the option of changing their mind and playing an e4 opening instead.

After 2. c4, Black can play 2...d5 and transpose into a Slav defence, as if they had played 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6.

With this move order, White has the option of 2. e4, where 2...d4 will transpose into a Caro-Kann, as if they had played 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5.

However, if White plays something else, like 2. Bf4, going for a Accelerated London-style set-up where Black might like to play ...c5 at some point, they may regret having given up a tempo on ...c6 now.
explanations.textEn:
1...c6

1...c6 is a transpositional tool. Black gives White the option of changing their mind and playing an e4 opening instead.

After 2. c4, Black can play 2...d5 and transpose into a Slav defence, as if they had played 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6.

With this move order, White has the option of 2. e4, where 2...d4 will transpose into a Caro-Kann, as if they had played 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5.

However, if White plays something else, like 2. Bf4, going for a Accelerated London-style set-up where Black might like to play ...c5 at some point, they may regret having given up a tempo on ...c6 now.
explanations.textZh:
1...c6

1...c6 是一个换位工具。黑方让白方可以选择改变主意并下 e4 开局。

2. c4 之后，黑方可以下 2...d5 并转入斯拉夫防御，就好像他们下过 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 一样。

通过这个走棋顺序，白方可以选择 2. e4，其中 2...d4 将转换为 Caro-Kann，就好像他们已经玩了 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 一样。

然而，如果白棋走其他棋子，比如 2. Bf4，采用加速伦敦风格的布局，而黑棋可能会在某个时刻下棋 ...c5，他们可能会后悔现在放弃了 ...c6 的节奏。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5
explanations.text:
1...d5 · Closed game

1...d5 is the classical approach to fighting for the centre: occupying it with pawns. 1...d4 takes some space for Black and opens a line of development for Black's queenside bishop.

Contest the centre with pawns

1...d5 controls the e4 square, so preventing White from securing an ideal two-pawn centre and all the space it would control. White can play 2. e4?! anyway, if they like, but the important thing is they can't keep the pawn there. 2. e4?! is the Blackmar-Diemer gambit, which is considered dubious against best play. After 2...dxe4, White hopes to get a lead in development as compensation for the lost pawn.

2. c4, the Queen's gambit, is the mainline. This is a much better try for getting a big centre. White offers the flanking c pawn to Black. Its threat is positional: if Black takes the free pawn, their d-pawn is deflected from its duty controlling the centre. White can then secure a bigger share of the centre for themselves, and should have no trouble recovering the gambitted pawn down the road. Therefore usually Black declines the gambit in one of a number of ways.

Develop a piece

Because both colours' d-pawns are already defended by their queens, there is less potential for immediate threats and forcing moves in the Closed game compared to after 1. e4 e5. Therefore, there are a wider range of reasonable turn two options and games have many transpositional possibilities by different move orders.

It is usually good to develop a piece when possible, so White may wish to start there.

2. Nf3 is the Zukertort variation. This is a flexible move: the knight was almost always going to go to f3, so White plays that move first. White retains the option of playing 3. c4 later (and 2...Nc6 3. c4 is the most common continuation), transposing into a Queen's gambit. Other lines include 3. Bf4, the London system, or 3. e3, the Colle system. 2. Nf3 is the main sideline in tournament play.

2. Bf4 is the Accelerated London system. This is the main club-level sideline. It is popular for its straight-forward plans that can be played against a variety of Black move orders. White prioritises developing the bishop so that they can play e3 to support the d-pawn without trapping the bishop behind the pawn chain. White must be conscious of their b2 pawn however, which is now weakened and a source of Black counterplay.

2. Nc3 is the Chigorin variation. This is an uncommon move because it prevents White from playing c4. Unlike 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3, here the knight gains no initiative on d5 because the pawn is already protected by Black's queen. After 2...Nf6, the main reply, this can lead to 3. Bg5, the Richter-Veresov attack, or 2. Bf4, the Rapport-Jobava London.

Other sidelines

2. f4!? is the Mason Attack and is dubious. It controls e5 once more, with the f-pawn. This weakens the kingside and creates a permanent hole on e4. White then usually doubles down with 3. Nf3 and although this is not fully sound, it could be playable.

2. g4? is the Zürich Gambit. It gives up a free pawn to 2...Bxg4 and is very unsound. White usually follows up with Bg2 and Nf3, but the kingside is weakened and the gambit is mostly good with surprise value.

explanations.textZh:
1...d5 · 封闭游戏

1...d5 是争夺中心的经典方法：用棋子占领它。 1...d4 为黑方占据了一些空间，并为黑方后翼主教打开了一条发展线。

用棋子争夺中心

1...d5 控制 e4 方格，从而阻止白方获得理想的两兵中心及其控制的所有空间。白棋可以下2.e4？！不管怎样，如果他们愿意的话，但重要的是他们不能把棋子留在那里。 2.e4？！是 Blackmar-Diemer 策略，它被认为对于最佳游戏来说是可疑的。 2...dxe4 之后，白方希望获得领先优势，作为对失去棋子的补偿。

2.c4，皇后的策略，是主线。这是建立一个大型中心的更好尝试。白方将侧翼 c 棋子提供给黑方。它的威胁是位置性的：如果黑方拿走自由棋子，他们的 D 棋子就会偏离其控制中心的职责。然后白棋就可以为自己争取到更大的中心份额，并且应该毫无困难地在路上收回已下棋的棋子。因此，黑方通常会以多种方式之一拒绝这一策略。

开发一块

因为两种颜色的 d-pawn 都已经受到其皇后的防守，所以与 1. e4 e5 之后相比，在封闭游戏中直接威胁和强制移动的可能性较小。因此，合理的第二回合选择范围更广，游戏通过不同的走法有多种换位的可能性。

在可能的情况下开发一个棋子通常是好的，所以白棋可能希望从那里开始。

2. Nf3 是 Zukertort 的变体。这是一个灵活的棋步：马几乎总是要下 f3，所以白方首先下棋。白方保留稍后下 3. c4 的选择（2...Nc6 3. c4 是最常见的延续），转换为后弃兵策略。其他线路包括 3. Bf4（伦敦系统）或 3. e3（Colle 系统）。 2. Nf3是锦标赛的主要边线。

2. Bf4是加速伦敦系统。这是俱乐部级别的主要副业。它因其直接的计划而广受欢迎，可以对抗各种黑棋棋子。白方优先发展主教，这样他们就可以下 e3 来支持 d 兵，而不会将主教困在兵链后面。然而，白棋必须意识到他们的 b2 棋子，该棋子现在已被削弱，并且是黑棋反击的一个来源。

2. Nc3是Chigorin的变体。这是一个不常见的棋步，因为它阻止白方下 c4。与 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 不同，这里马在 d5 上没有获得主动权，因为兵已经受到黑后的保护。在 2...Nf6（主要答复）之后，这可能会导致 3.Bg5（Richter-Veresov 攻击）或 2.Bf4（Rapport-Jobava London）。

其他副业

2.f4！？是梅森攻击并且值得怀疑。它用 f-pawn 再次控制 e5。这会削弱王翼并在 e4 上形成一个永久性的洞。然后白棋通常会用 3.Nf3 双倍下注，虽然这并不完全合理，但它是可以玩的。

2.g4？是苏黎世策略。它放弃了一个自由棋子给 2...Bxg4 并且非常不健全。白方通常会跟进Bg2和Nf3，但王翼被削弱，开局大多良好，具有惊喜价值。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. Nc3
explanations.text:
2. Nc3 · Chigorin Variation

The Chigorin Variation (Named after Mikhail Chigorin) is an opening that may often transpose to other lines. It is rarely played by masters and tournament players, as the c-pawn is blocked, disallowing it from contesting the d5-pawn. Nonetheless, this line is considered sound and leads to closed positions involving much slow, strategic maneuvering.

The main lines after this are the /2...Nf6/ 3. Bf4, the Jobava London System, and 2...Nf6 3. Bg5, the Richter–Veresov Attack (which transposes into the French Defense after 3...e6 or remains in independent lines after 3...Nbd7).

Black can also reasonably play 2...e6 (which likely leads to the aforementioned lines), 2...c6 (likely transposing to the Caro–Kann after 3. e4), 2...g6, 2...Bf5, or even 2...f5!? (the Dutch Variation), 2...c5!? (the Irish Gambit, which is a fairly unexplored option), or the unclear 2...e5!? (the Shaviliuk Gambit).

/2...Nc6/ transposes to the Nimzowitsch Defence after 3. e4, normally reached by 1. e4 Nc6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3.

explanations.textZh:
2. Nc3·齐戈林变奏

齐戈林变奏曲（以米哈伊尔·齐戈林的名字命名）是一个经常可以移植到其他诗句的开场白。大师和锦标赛玩家很少玩它，因为 c-pawn 被阻挡，不允许它与 d5-pawn 竞争。尽管如此，这条路线被认为是合理的，并且会导致平仓，涉及非常缓慢的战略机动。

此后的主线是 /2...Nf6/ 3. Bf4，Jobava 伦敦系统，以及 2...Nf6 3. Bg5，里希特-维列索夫攻击（在 3...e6 后转入法国防御，或在 3...Nbd7 后保持独立线路）。

黑方还可以合理地下 2...e6（这可能导致上述行）、2...c6（可能在 3.e4 后转为卡罗-卡恩）、2...g6、2...Bf5，甚至 2...f5！？ （荷兰变体），2...c5！？ （爱尔兰开局，这是一个相当未经探索的选项），还是不清楚的 2...e5！？ （沙维柳克策略）。

/2...Nc6/ 在 3. e4 之后转置为尼姆佐维奇防御，通常通过 1. e4 Nc6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 达到。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. Bf4
explanations.text:
2. Bf4 · Accelerated London system

White develops the dark-square bishop. Developing the bishop first allows White to support their d4-pawn with e3, without trapping this bishop behind the pawn chain.

This is the beginning of the London system. The appeal of this system is that White can go for the same general set-up in response to most of Black's replies (see diagram). General plans for White include planting their kingside knight on e5, controlled by d4 and the dark-square bishop. Often White's light-square bishop is sacrificed on h7 to open up a castled king, followed by Qh5+.

Formally, the Accelerated London follows 1...d5, but the London set up can be played against 1...Nf6 just as well and may transpose if Black plays d5.

At higher levels, the move order 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. Bf4 to reach the London system is more common.

The main alternative for White is the Rapport-Jobava London system, with Nc3 (in either order, 2. Nc3 & 3. Bf4 or 2. Bf4 & 3. Nc3) where plans include the knight coordinating with the f4 bishop to attack c7, and an early e4.

Responses

Because White can play the same system in response to most of Black's replies, White usually continues 3. e3, 4. c3, 5. Nd2 etc regardless. Most move orders are interchangeable.

Black's most common reply is 2...Nf6, then they have two main approaches: 3...c5 or 3...e6.

The idea behind the 3...e6 line is to play 4...Bd6, getting ready to castle quickly and threatening to trade off White's London bishop. White can drop their bishop back to g3, inviting Black to trade but after hxg3 White gets the semi-open h-file in return. In the e6 lines, Black's light square bishop often has difficulty developing. This approach resembles a Semi-Slav defence with colours reversed.

The ...c5 line (either 3...c5, or in the order 2...c5 3. e6 Nf6) is called the Steinitz countergambit. Black's idea is to prioritise ...Bf5 and ...Qb6 before they finish developing the kingside and castling. Black seeks counterplay by pressuring b2, which White left undefended when they moved their bishop early on. (White does not want to take the offered c5 pawn of course: they'd rather play c3 and let Black trade into them, so that they can keep two pawns in the centre).

Having committed to d5 already, the King's Indian-style approach with 3...g6 is less common but still playable. Black continues 4...Bg7, and 5...O-O. White usually includes h3, so there is a retreat square for their bishop on h2, and Be2.

Black can also play the uncommon 2...h5!?, a sideline setting up a trap if 3. e3? is played.

History

Possibly the earliest example of 1. d4 d5 2. Bf4 was given by Jacob Sarratt in his 1808 book A Treatise on the Game of Chess. This continued 2...Bf5 3. Nc3 Nc6 4. f3.

James Mason pioneered the London system continuation (i.e. where White plays e3, places a knight on d2 and their light square bishop on d3 or e2) in the 1882 Vienna tournament. It became known as the London after the 1922 London tournament, where it was played by Capablanca and others.

The London system is popular with amateurs. It is often recommended to beginners as White can develop in the same way irrespective of how Black chooses to respond. It is occasionally seen at the highest levels of chess, e.g. in Ding v Nepomniachtchi in their 2023 World Championship match.

A recent innovation is to combine Bf4 and Nc3, the Rapport-Jobava London, developed by Richárd Rapport and Baduur Jobava.

explanations.textZh:
2. Bf4·加速伦敦系统

白棋发展出暗方象。首先开发主教可以让白方用 e3 支持他们的 d4 兵，而不会将主教困在兵链后面。

这是伦敦体系的开始。该系统的吸引力在于，白方可以采用相同的一般设置来响应黑方的大多数答复（见图）。白方的总体计划包括在 e5 上安置王翼骑士，由 d4 和暗方主教控制。通常，白方的浅方主教会在 h7 上被牺牲，以打开城堡国王，然后是 Qh5+。

形式上，加速伦敦遵循 1...d5，但伦敦设置也可以对抗 1...Nf6，并且如果黑方下 d5，则可能会调换。

在较高级别，移动顺序 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. Bf4 到达伦敦系统更为常见。

白方的主要替代方案是 Rapport-Jobava London 系统，其中 Nc3（顺序为 2. Nc3 & 3. Bf4 或 2. Bf4 & 3. Nc3），其中计划包括骑士与 f4 主教协调攻击 c7，以及早期的 e4。

回应

由于白方可以使用相同的系统来响应黑方的大多数答复，因此白方通常会继续 3. e3、4. c3、5. Nd2 等。大多数移动命令是可以互换的。

黑方最常见的答复是2...Nf6，那么他们有两种主要方法：3...c5 或3...e6。

3...e6 线背后的想法是玩 4...Bd6，准备快速城堡并威胁要交易怀特的伦敦主教。白方可以将其象放回到 g3，邀请黑方进行交易，但在 hxg3 之后，白方得到半开放的 h 文件作为回报。在e6线中，黑方的轻方象常常难以展开。这种方法类似于颜色相反的半斯拉夫防御。

...c5 线（3...c5，或顺序为 2...c5 3. e6 Nf6）称为斯坦尼茨反策略。黑方的想法是在...Bf5 和...Qb6 完成王翼和王位的开发之前优先考虑。黑方通过向 b2 施压来寻求反击，而白方在早期移动了象时，就让 b2 处于不设防的状态。 （白棋当然不想接受所提供的 c5 棋子：他们宁愿下 c3 并让黑棋交易到它们，这样他们就可以在中间保留两个棋子）。

由于已经致力于 d5，国王的印度式 3...g6 方法不太常见，但仍然可以玩。黑方继续 4...Bg7 和 5...O-O。白方通常包括h3，因此他们的主教在h2和Be2上有一个撤退方格。

黑棋还可以发挥不常见的2...h5!?，如果3.e3?，边线设置陷阱？已播放。

历史

1. d4 d5 2. Bf4 的最早例子可能是 Jacob Sarratt 在他 1808 年的著作《国际象棋游戏论文》中给出的。继续 2...Bf5 3. Nc3 Nc6 4. f3。

詹姆斯·梅森 (James Mason) 在 1882 年维也纳锦标赛中开创了伦敦系统的延续（即白方下 e3，在 d2 上放置马，在 d3 或 e2 上放置轻方主教）。 1922 年伦敦锦标赛由卡帕布兰卡等人参加，此后它被称为“伦敦”。

伦敦系统深受业余爱好者的欢迎。通常推荐给初学者，因为无论黑棋选择如何应对，白棋都可以以相同的方式发展。它偶尔会出现在最高水平的国际象棋比赛中，例如：在 Ding 对阵 Nepomniachtchi 的 2023 年世界锦标赛比赛中。

最近的一项创新是将 Bf4 和 Nc3 结合起来，即由 Richard Rapport 和 Baduur Jobava 开发的 Rapport-Jobava London。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. Bf4/2...c5
explanations.text:
2...c5 · Steinitz countergambit

Black challenges the centre with c5, the Steinitz countergambit, offering White their c-pawn.

Decline the gambit

As the pawn is already defended by the Queen, White does not actually need to defend it further: if 3. Nc3 cxd4 4. Qxd4 and White is threatening to win Black's d-pawn: 4...Nc6? 5. Qxd5 Qxd5 6. Nxd5 (if 4...e6 5. Bxb8! Rxb8 and White's centralised queen is unassailable).

Usually however White does end up over-defending the d-pawn, because most of the moves they'd like to play next happen to do so anyway. White usually plays 3. e3, which defends d4 but is also essential for opening up White's kings-side bishop. After 3...Nf6, Black has transposed back into the main line against the Accelerated London.

Other London system-moves 3. c3 or 3. Nf3 may be played and usually transpose.

Accept the gambit

Accepting the gambit, 3. dxc5?!, is unwise. By taking the pawn, White reduces their control over the centre and Black can easily recover the pawn. Mason, pioneer of the London system, fell into this in his game against Steinitz in 1883. It continued like this: 3. dxc5?! Nc6 4. Nf3 f6 5. e3 e5 6. Bg3 Bxc5 (see diagram).

Countergambit

A rare sideline here is the Morris countergambit, 3. e4. White gives up their e-pawn in order to push d5 and cramp Black's position. This resembles an Albin Countergambit with colours reversed.

2...c5 · 斯坦尼茨对策

黑方用 c5（斯坦尼茨对策）向中心发起挑战，为白方提供了他们的 c 兵。

拒绝策略

由于棋子已经被后棋防守，白棋实际上不需要进一步防守：如果 3. Nc3 cxd4 4. Qxd4 并且白棋威胁要赢得黑棋的 d 棋子： 4...Nc6？ 5. Qxd5 Qxd5 6. Nxd5 （如果 4...e6 5. Bxb8！Rxb8 并且白方的集中后王是无懈可击的）。

然而通常情况下，白棋最终会过度防守d兵，因为他们接下来想要采取的大多数动作无论如何都会发生。白方通常下3. e3，它防守d4，但对于打开白方的王边象也是至关重要的。 3...Nf6 后，黑方转回主线对抗加速伦敦。

可以使用其他伦敦系统走法 3. c3 或 3. Nf3，并且通常可以进行移调。

接受这个策略，3.dxc5？！，是不明智的。通过吃掉棋子，白方减少了对中心的控制，黑方可以轻松地收回棋子。伦敦体系的先驱梅森在1883年与斯坦尼茨的比赛中陷入了这样的境地。 事情是这样继续的：3. dxc5？！ Nc6 4. Nf3 f6 5. e3 e5 6. Bg3 Bxc5（见图）。

反策略

这里一个罕见的副线是莫里斯的反击策略，3. e4。白方放弃 e 兵以推动 d5 并限制黑方的位置。这类似于阿尔宾反棋，但颜色相反。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. Bf4/2...h5
explanations.text:
2...h5!?

This sneaky and uncommon sideline sets up a trap to win White's bishop.

At first glance, this move appears strange, developing a flank pawn instead of a piece or central pawn. However, 3. e3? lets Black win the bishop for three pawns after 3...e5! 4. Bxe5 (4. dxe5?! g5 5. Bxg5 Qxg5 6. Qxd5) 4... f6 5. Be2 fxe5 6. Bxh5+ Ke7 7. dxe5, and thus White will have to change their usual e3 move and choose one of two responses instead.

3. Nf3 develops the kingside knight and doesn't block the c1-h6 diagonal for the bishop unlike 3. e3. It is quite solid and questions Black's premature h5 pawn push.

3. c4 challenges Black's center and is White's best move, ignoring Black's flank attack and instead focusing on the most important region of the board: the center. This can lead to aggressive play from both sides.

2...h5！？

这种狡猾且不常见的副线设置了一个陷阱，以赢得白棋的主教。

explanations.text:
Levitsky Attack or Queen's Bishop Attack

2. Bg5

Bg5 is an immediate attack by white, in hopes of slowing black's development via pinning the pawn on e7. This position can be negated by black developing Nf6, or a pawn move f6. usually, the bishop cannot remain in its position for long, necessitating a loss of tempo.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4
explanations.text:
2. c4 · Queen's gambit

The Queen's gambit is one of the oldest openings in chess. White offers a pawn in order to gain control of the centre. This opening is very popular among modern players and is one of the best openings for 1. d4.

Accept the gambit

2...dxc4, accepting the gambit, is playable. Black is up a pawn but only temporarily, as it turns out it's impractical for Black to hold onto it. By accepting the gambit Black loses control of e4. White can reclaim the gambitted pawn and take a bigger share of the centre with 3. e4, discovering an attack on c4. The main line however is 3. Nf3, seeking to prevent ...e5 and recovering the pawn later after 3...Nf6 4. e3 e6 5. Bxc4.

Decline the gambit

Most Black players choose to decline the gambit.

If Black allows White to play 3. cxd5, they would like, ideally, to retake with a pawn so as to keep a pawn on d5, controlling e4. Therefore the most common ways of declining are 2...e6, the Queen's gambit declined, or 2...c6, the Slav defence.

2...Nf6, the Marshall defence, prepares to retake on d5 with the knight, however Black loses time after 3. cxd5 Nxd5 4. e4! Nf6. Instead, 3...c6?!, the tricky Tan gambit, may offer more practical success.

Alternatively, Black may rely on the fact that the d5 pawn is already defended by the queen and prioritise developing their other pieces instead:

The exotic 2...Nc6, the Chigorin defence, develops a knight and intends to answer cxd5 with ...Qxd5 with added pressure on d4.

The eccentric 2...Bf5?, the Baltic defence, is thought worse for Black. If 3. cxd5 Qxd5 White can gain time on the queen and bishop: 4. Nc3 Qd7 5. e4 Bg6. The main line is to first give up one's bishop for a knight, so that one's queen can come out more safely: 3. cxd5 Bxb1! 4. Rxb1 Qxd5.

Countergambit

Finally Black may choose to derail White's plans with a gambit of their own, the most practical of which are:

The Albin countergambit, 2...e5: after 3. dxe5 d4 Black's pawn is an advanced wedge in White's territory and they get some attacking chances.

The Austrian defence, 2...c5. After 3. cxd5, 3...Qxd5 or 3...Nf6 may be played.

Dubious is 2...b5?!, the Zilbermints gambit.

explanations.textZh:
2. c4 · 后弃兵

后弃兵是国际象棋中最古老的开局之一。白方提供一个棋子以控制中心。这个开局在现代玩家中非常流行，也是 1.d4 的最佳开局之一。

接受策略

2...dxc4，接受策略，可以玩。黑棋是一颗棋子，但只是暂时的，因为事实证明黑棋要保留它是不切实际的。通过接受这个策略，黑方失去了对 e4 的控制。白棋可以夺回已出局的棋子，并用 3. e4 占据中心的更大份额，发现对 c4 的攻击。然而，主线是 3. Nf3，试图阻止 ...e5 并在 3...Nf6 4. e3 e6 5. Bxc4 之后恢复棋子。

拒绝策略

大多数黑人玩家选择拒绝这一策略。

如果黑方允许白方下 3.cxd5，那么理想情况下，他们会希望用棋子重夺棋子，以便将棋子保留在 d5 上，从而控制 e4。因此，最常见的衰落方式是 2...e6，后退策略，或 2...c6，斯拉夫防御。

2...Nf6，马歇尔防御，准备与马重夺 d5，但是黑方在 3. cxd5 Nxd5 4. e4 之后失去了时间！ NF6。相反，3...c6?!，这个棘手的 Tan 策略，可能会带来更多实际的成功。

或者，黑方可能会依赖 d5 兵已被后卫防守的事实，并优先发展其他棋子：

异国情调的 2...Nc6，Chigorin 防守，发展了一个骑士，并打算用 ...Qxd5 回答 cxd5，并对 d4 增加压力。

古怪的 2...Bf5？，即波罗的海防御，被认为对黑方来说更糟糕。如果 3. cxd5 Qxd5 白方可以在后和主教上赢得时间： 4. Nc3 Qd7 5. e4 Bg6。主线是先放弃自己的主教换马，这样自己的后才能更安全地出来：3.cxd5 Bxb1！ 4.Rxb1 Qxd5。

反策略

最后，黑方可能会选择用自己的策略来破坏白方的计划，其中最实用的是：

阿尔宾反棋，2...e5：在3.dxe5 d4之后，黑方的棋子是白方领土上的先进楔子，他们获得了一些攻击机会。

奥地利防守，2...c5。 3.cxd5 之后，可以播放 3...Qxd5 或 3...Nf6。

可疑的是 2...b5？！，Zilbermints 的策略。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...Nc6
explanations.text:
2...Nc6 · Chigorin defence

With 2...Nc6 Black does not support the central d5 pawn but develops a piece for an uneven game.

Theory in this defence has been extended in recent years in part due to the attempt to create playable lines in the Black Knights' Tango which can transpose into a Chigorin Defence.

Unlike most Queen's pawn openings, White's d-pawn gets put under a lot of pressure. White will have to either counter-attack or defend the pawn to keep the advantage.

/3. Nc3/ is the most popular response, putting pressure on Black's d-pawn. Black usually responds by capturing on c4.

/3. Nf3/ is more passive than 3. Nc3. Black will be able to build up the pressure, and White will be on the defensive for a while.

/3. cxd5/ is White's third most popular option. This is the Chigorin's Exchange variation. Just like in 3. Nf3, Black will be able to quickly build pressure on White's position.

History

The opening is named after Mikhail Chigorin, who first played the opening in 1889 against Steinitz. Early appearances of the Chigorin usually turned into a Queen's gambit declined with a knight on c6, which is far from optimal, since Black usually wants to play either c5 or c6 in those positions.

The first five moves of what is considered to be the main line were played already in 1895 by Chigorin in a consultation game against Blackburne and Pillsbury with Schiffers as his teammate.

explanations.textZh:
2...NC6·齐戈林防守

有了 2...Nc6 黑方不支持中央 d5 兵，但为不平衡的游戏开发了一块棋子。

近年来，这种防守的理论得到了扩展，部分原因是试图在黑骑士探戈中创造可玩的路线，可以将其转换为齐戈林防守。

与大多数后棋开局不同，白棋的 d 棋子承受着很大的压力。白棋必须反击或防守棋子才能保持优势。

/3。 Nc3/ 是最受欢迎的反应，对黑方的 d 兵施加压力。黑棋通常通过吃子来回应 c4。

/3。 Nf3/ 比 3. Nc3 更被动。黑方将能够形成压力，而白方将处于防守一段时间。

/3。 cxd5/ 是白方第三受欢迎的选择。这是 Chigorin 的交换变体。就像在 3.Nf3 中一样，黑方将能够快速对白方的位置施加压力。

历史

该开局以米哈伊尔·奇戈林 (Mikhail Chigorin) 的名字命名，他于 1889 年首次对战斯坦尼茨 (Steinitz) 打出开局。齐戈林的早期出现通常会变成后弃兵策略，马在 c6 上，这远非最佳，因为黑方通常想在这些位置下 c5 或 c6。

被认为是主线的前五步棋已经由 Chigorin 在 1895 年对阵 Blackburne 和 Pillsbury 的一场咨询赛中用 Schiffers 作为队友下出了。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...Nc6/3. Nc3
explanations.text:
3. Nc3

This is White's most popular and ambitious response. White decides to counter-attack Black instead of defending their d-pawn. Black has many options:

/3...dxc4/ is the main line. This gives up some control of the centre, but opens up an attack on White's d4-pawn. White will have to either defend the pawn with 4. Nf3, or push it with 4. d5.

/3...Nf6/ defends the d5-pawn with another piece. Depending on the following moves, the position can resemble a Queen's gambit declined (4. Nf3 e6), a Queen's gambit accepted (4. Nf3 dxc4) or a Grünfeld Defence (4. cxd5 Nxd5 5. e4).

/3...e5/ is the unorthodox Tartakower gambit, similar in spirit to the Albin countergambit. Contrary to the Albin, White should not take the e5-pawn in this position. Instead, 4. cxd5 leads to White being able to extract a few extra tempi from Black's knight.

3...e6 leads to more Queen's gambit declined-like positions, but with the knight on c6. This is not a great place for the knight in the QGD, since Black usually has the plan of protecting d5 with c6, or to play c5 in order to attack White's centre.

3.NC3

这是怀特最受欢迎、最雄心勃勃的回应。白棋决定反击黑棋而不是防守他们的 D 棋子。黑色有多种选择：

/3...dxc4/为主线。这放弃了对中心的一些控制，但开启了对白方 d4 兵的攻击。白方必须要么用 4. Nf3 防守棋子，要么用 4. d5 推动棋子。

/3...Nf6/ 用另一颗棋子保卫 d5 兵。根据接下来的走法，该位置可能类似于拒绝后弃兵 (4. Nf3 e6)、接受后弃兵 (4. Nf3 dxc4) 或格林菲尔德防御 (4. cxd5 Nxd5 5. e4)。

/3...e5/ 是非正统的 Tartakower 策略，其本质与 Albin 策略相似。与阿尔宾相反，白棋不应该在这个位置吃 e5 兵。相反，4.cxd5 导致白棋能够从黑棋的马身上获得一些额外的节奏。

3...e6 导致更多后退策略类似的位置，但马在 c6 上。这对 QGD 中的马来说不是一个好位置，因为黑方通常有用 c6 保护 d5 的计划，或者下 c5 来攻击白方的中心。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...Nc6/3. Nf3
explanations.text:
3. Nf3

White opts to defend the d-pawn. Black should respond by developing actively and posing practical problems for White.

/3...Bg4/ is the main line from this position. Usually this move wouldn't be very effective with White's e-pawn still on e2, but White can't respond with the usual Ne5 because Black controls that square with their own knight. White should therefore respond with either 4. Nc3 or 4. cxd5 instead.

/3...e5/ is the slightly more esoteric Lazard gambit. Ideas in this line are very similar to the Albin countergambit, with slight differences due to the knights on f3 and c6.

3. Nf3

White opts to defend the d-pawn. Black should respond by developing actively and posing practical problems for White.

/3...Bg4/ is the main line from this position. Usually this move wouldn't be very effective with White's e-pawn still on e2, but White can't respond with the usual Ne5 because Black controls that square with their own knight. White should therefore respond with either 4. Nc3 or 4. cxd5 instead.

explanations.textZh:
3.NF3

白棋选择防守 d 兵。黑方应该通过积极发展并为白方提出实际问题来做出回应。

/3...Bg4/是从这个位置开始的主线。通常，当白方的 e 兵仍在 e2 上时，这一举动不会非常有效，但白方无法用通常的 Ne5 做出回应，因为黑方用自己的马控制了该方格。因此，白棋应该用 4.Nc3 或 4.cxd5 来回应。

/3...e5/ 是稍微深奥的 Lazard 策略。这一行的想法与阿尔宾对策非常相似，但由于 f3 和 c6 上的骑士而略有不同。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...c5
explanations.text:
Austrian Defence

The Austrian chess players Hans Haberditz (c. 1901–57), Hans Müller (1896–1971), and GM Ernst Grünfeld studied this defense, which was initially introduced by Italian chess player Alessandro Salvio in 1604. Black creates a lot of tension and aims to disrupt White's center and prevent white from seizing the initiative by mirroring White's moves, adding a little complexity to the position. This defence is prone to complete equality, but current theory suggests that white should gain a practical (although still equal when analyzed with engines) advantage with the appropriate moves.

White's responses

White will probably reply with one of the following options:

3. cxd5 - The classical main line in the Austrian Defence.

3. dxc5 - Exchanging a central pawn for a flank pawn.

3. Nf3 - Inviting a transposition to the Tarrasch Defence.

explanations.textZh:
奥地利国防

奥地利国际象棋棋手汉斯·哈伯迪茨（Hans Haberditz，约 1901-57 年）、汉斯·穆勒（Hans Müller，1896-1971 年）和 GM Ernst Grünfeld 研究了这种防御，该防御最初由意大利国际象棋棋手亚历山德罗·萨尔维奥 (Alessandro Salvio) 在 1604 年提出。黑棋制造了很大的紧张局势，旨在通过模仿白棋的走法来扰乱白棋的中心并阻止白棋夺取主动权，从而增加了一点复杂性。的位置。这种防御倾向于完全平等，但当前的理论表明，白方应该通过适当的走法获得实际的（尽管用引擎分析时仍然平等）优势。

白的回应

白方可能会回复以下选项之一：

3. cxd5 - 奥地利防御中的经典主线。

3. dxc5 - 将中央棋子替换为侧翼棋子。

3. Nf3 - 邀请换位至塔拉什防御。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...c5/3. cxd5
explanations.text:
Austrian Defense

3. cxd5

The a logical and principled way of dealing with this central tension, using a flank pawn to exchange a center pawn. Black usually replies with 3...Qxd5, although 3...Nf6, the so called Gusev Countergambit, tries to complicate the position

奥地利国防

3.cxd5

处理这种中央紧张局势的逻辑和原则性方法是使用侧翼棋子交换中心棋子。黑方通常会回复 3...Qxd5，尽管 3...Nf6（所谓的古谢夫反策略）试图使局势复杂化

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...c5/3. cxd5/3...Nf6
explanations.text:
Gusev Countergambit (3...Nf6!?)

Arising from the Austrian Defense, the Gusev Countergambit, named after the Soviet Master of Sports Nikolai Nikolaevich Gusev, is represented by the gambit of a pawn on c5 with 3...Nf6. In distinction to traditional openings that prioritize immediate control, Black elects to relinquish central pawns for active piece play. By offering the pawn on c5 as a gambit, Black aims to swiftly develop their pieces and pinch the action from White. The position's dynamic nature places emphasis on sharpness and quick development.

White's responses

White will probably reply with one of the following options:

/4. e4/ - The critical approach for White.

/4. dxc5/ - Accepting the gambit and the further complications.

/4. Nf3/ - Inviting a transposition to one of the main Austrian Defense lines.

/4. Nc3/ - Trying to consolidate the position while keeping the central tension.

explanations.textZh:
古谢夫反击 (3...Nf6!?)

古谢夫反棋源自奥地利防御，以苏联体育大师尼古拉·尼古拉耶维奇·古谢夫命名，其代表方式是 c5 上的棋子带有 3...Nf6。与优先考虑立即控制的传统开局不同，黑方选择放弃中央棋子以进行主动棋子游戏。通过提供 c5 上的棋子作为策略，黑棋的目的是迅速发展自己的棋子并掐住白棋的行动。该职位的动态性质强调敏锐性和快速发展。

白的回应

白方可能会回复以下选项之一：

/4。 e4/ - 白棋的关键方法。

/4。 dxc5/ - 接受这个策略和进一步的并发症。

/4。 Nf3/ - 邀请转移到奥地利主要防线之一。

/4。 Nc3/ - 试图巩固阵地，同时保持中路的张力。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...c6
explanations.text:
2...c6 · Slav Defence

Originally considered a less-orthodox defence in the Queen's Gambit, this opening has stood as an entire opening system in its own right for decades.

The idea behind this defence is straightforward: instead of locking in the light squared bishop on c8, why not support the center with the c-pawn instead? Black tends to be more active in this variation than the QGD.

White's main lines:

/3. Nf3/ - The main line. As with the QGD, White makes a useful developing move while maintaining some flexibility: will they play for e4, play cxd5, or play for the minority attack?

/3. Nc3/ - Sometimes provocative, this move may lead to variations where Black overextends by trying to hold on to the pawn on c4.

/3. cxd5/ - The exchange variation. This relieves the central tension perhaps too early on and tends to allow Black equality. One of the main drawbacks of having the Slav as a main opening repertoire is that it is hard for Black (or White) to win in the exchange variation. According to chess365, 83% of Masters games ended in a draw after this move. Even so, it is important for both sides to know that there are still attacking options to sharpen up the game.

explanations.textZh:
2...c6 · 斯拉夫防御

最初被认为是后弃兵中不太正统的防御，几十年来，这种开局一直作为一个完整的开局系统存在。

这种防御背后的想法很简单：为什么不用 c-pawn 来支持中心，而不是锁定 c8 上的光方主教呢？黑棋在这种变化中往往比 QGD 更活跃。

白的主线：

/3。 Nf3/ - 主线。与 QGD 一样，白方在保持一定灵活性的同时做出了有用的发展举动：他们会玩 e4、玩 cxd5 还是玩少数进攻？

/3。 Nc3/ - 有时具有挑衅性，此步可能会导致黑方试图抓住 c4 上的棋子而过度延伸。

/3。 cxd5/ - 交换变化。这也许过早地缓解了中央的紧张局势，并倾向于允许黑人平等。以斯拉夫人作为主要开局曲目的主要缺点之一是黑方（或白方）很难在交换变化中获胜。据chess365统计，在这一举动之后，83%的大师赛比赛都以平局告终。即便如此，对于双方来说，重要的是要知道仍然有进攻选择来提高比赛质量。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...c6/3. Nc3
explanations.text:
3. Nc3

This move develops a piece and bears more pressure on d5. Due to this, it also makes 3...Bf5 a grave mistake due to 4. cxd5 cxd5 5. Qb3, winning a pawn. If then 5...Qb6, 6. Nxd5! Qxb3 7. axb3 wins the d pawn. If instead 5...Nf6 to protect the d-pawn, 6. Qxb7 Nbd7 7. Nf3 Rb8 8. Qxa7 wins two. In general, if Black can safely play Bf5 and e6 in the Slav, Black equalizes. The c3-knight also bears pressure on e4, allowing for a potential e4 pawn-push in the future.

/3...Nf6/ is Black's most common reply by far. White's play typically transposes into a semi-slav with 4. Nf3, although some unique lines exist where Nf3 is delayed or not played at all.

/3...dxc4/ followed by 4...b5 is also frequently played, as the c3 knight is vulnerable to a b7-b5-b4 advance allowing Black good queenside counter-play after White's gambited c-pawn is captured.

/3...e5/, the Winawer Countergambit, is rarely seen from Black in high-level games. Black gambits their e-pawn for faster development, but usually falls behind in development after recapturing the pawn.

explanations.textZh:
3.NC3

这一招发展了棋子，对d5承受了更大的压力。因此，它也使 3...Bf5 成为一个严重错误，因为 4.cxd5 cxd5 5.Qb3，赢得了一个棋子。如果那么 5...Qb6，6.Nxd5！ Qxb3 7. axb3 赢得 d 棋子。如果改为 5...Nf6 保护 d-pawn，则 6. Qxb7 Nbd7 7. Nf3 Rb8 8. Qxa7 赢得两场。一般来说，如果黑棋能够安全地下斯拉夫棋中的 Bf5 和 e6，黑棋就可以扳平。 c3-knight 还对 e4 施加压力，从而允许未来潜在的 e4 兵推。

/3...Nf6/ 是迄今为止黑方最常见的答复。白棋通常会用 4.Nf3 转为半斯拉夫，尽管存在一些独特的线路，其中 Nf3 被延迟或根本不播放。

/3...dxc4/ 后跟 4...b5 也经常被使用，因为 c3 骑士很容易受到 b7-b5-b4 推进的影响，从而在白棋的 c-pawn 被捕获后，黑方可以进行良好的后翼反击。

/3...e5/，Winawer 反棋，在高级对局中很少见到黑棋。黑方出局他们的电子棋子以获得更快的发展，但在夺回棋子后通常会落后于发展。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...c6/3. Nc3/3...dxc4
explanations.text:
3...dxc4

This move captures the gambit pawn. Since White's knight on c3 is exposed to attacks by Black's b-pawn, Black can often safely over-extend with moves like a6 and b5 to keep a hold of the c-pawn in this line. This move is lesser seen than the main line 3...Nf6. From here, White has several replies:

/4. e4/ - The most common reply, White gains a significant space advantage in the center but White's c3 knight loses access to e4 as a retreating square.

/4. e3/ - Slightly less common, White still advances in the center, but keeps the e4 square open for the c3 knight to retreat to.

/4. a4/ - Uncommon, White prevents Black's ...b5, but allows Black to fight in the center with e5. Black tends to do well in this variation.

/4. Nf3/ - Uncommon, White focuses on development with their g1 knight.

There is a trap following 4. e3 b5, where the move 5. Nxb5?, trying to exploit the h1-a8 diagonal is a mistake which gives Black the advantage after 5...cxb5 6. Qf3 Qc7! 7. Qxa8 Bb7 as White has to sacrifice material in order to avoid Black winning the Queen.

explanations.textZh:
3...DXC4

此步棋吃掉了弃兵。由于白方在 c3 上的马容易受到黑方 b 兵的攻击，因此黑方通常可以通过 a6 和 b5 等走法安全地过度延伸，以控制这条线上的 c 兵。与主线 3...Nf6 相比，此举动较少出现。从这里，怀特有几个答复：

/4。 e4/ - 最常见的答复，白方在中心获得了显着的空间优势，但白方的 c3 骑士失去了进入 e4 作为撤退方的机会。

/4。 e3/ - 稍微不太常见，白方仍然在中心推进，但保持 e4 方格开放，以便 c3 马撤退。

/4。 a4/ - 不常见，白方阻止黑方 ...b5，但允许黑方使用 e5 在中心战斗。黑色在这种变化中往往表现良好。

/4。 Nf3/ - 不常见，白方专注于他们的 g1 骑士的发展。

4. e3 b5 之后有一个陷阱，其中 5. Nxb5? 着法，试图利用 h1-a8 对角线是一个错误，这给了黑方在 5...cxb5 后的优势 6. Qf3 Qc7！ 7. Qxa8 Bb7 因为白棋必须牺牲材料以避免黑棋赢得后棋。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...c6/3. Nc3/3...dxc4/4. e3
explanations.text:
4. e3

This is considered to be the best move for White:

Keeps the e4-square free for the c3-knight to retreat to in case of a b7-b5-b4 advance.

Gains control of the centre with pawns on e3 and d4.

Prepares to capture the c4 pawn with Bxc4.

Black should prevent the capture of the c-pawn with /4...b5/. This usually leads to very complicated variations on the queenside where White attempts to undermine Black's defence of the c-pawn with moves like a4. If White can successfully recapture the pawn, White should be better.
explanations.textEn:
4. e3

This is considered to be the best move for White:

Gains control of the centre with pawns on e3 and d4.

Prepares to capture the c4 pawn with Bxc4.

Black should prevent the capture of the c-pawn with /4...b5/. This usually leads to very complicated variations on the queenside where White attempts to undermine Black's defence of the c-pawn with moves like a4. If White can successfully recapture the pawn, White should be better.
explanations.textZh:
4.e3

这被认为是白棋的最佳棋步：

保持 e4 方格空闲，以便 c3 骑士在 b7-b5-b4 推进时撤退。

通过 e3 和 d4 上的棋子控制中心。

准备用 Bxc4 捕获 c4 棋子。

黑方应该用 /4...b5/ 阻止吃掉 c 兵。这通常会导致后侧出现非常复杂的变化，白方试图通过 a4 等走法破坏黑方对 c 兵的防守。如果白棋能够成功夺回棋子，那么白棋应该会更好。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...c6/3. Nc3/3...dxc4/4. e3/4...b5
explanations.text:
4...b5

This guards c4 and is the best move. The queenside weaknesses are not a problem, as the knight on c3 is vulnerable to b-pawn attacks with ...b4. Note that 5. Nxb5?, trying to exploit the long diagonal to destroy Black's queenside, is a mistake, and gives up the advantage to Black. A common motif in these positions is for Black to play b5 in order to boot the knight, often giving up the c4-pawn in the process.

When your opponent has a space advantage, you want to use pawn breaks to break up their pawn chains. /5. a4/ is the most effective way to do that. The alternative 5. b3?! Qa5 results in Black being able to put a lot of pressure on White's queenside.

4...b5

这防守c4，是最好的棋步。后翼的弱点不是问题，因为 c3 上的骑士很容易受到 ...b4 的 b-pawn 攻击。请注意，5.Nxb5？试图利用长对角线来摧毁黑方的后翼，这是一个错误，并且将优势让给了黑方。这些位置的一个常见主题是黑方下 b5 来引导马，通常在此过程中放弃 c4 兵。

当你的对手拥有空间优势时，你需要使用兵断来打破他们的兵链。 /5。 a4/ 是最有效的方法。替代5.b3？！ Qa5 使得黑方能够对白方后翼施加很大压力。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...c6/3. Nc3/3...dxc4/4. e3/4...b5/5. a4
explanations.text:
5.a4

This move tries to attack Black's queenside and lure it to it's doom. b4 is almost universally played after this, as if Qa5, the queen is exposed. b4 tries to boot the knight into oblivion and disrupt White's queenside.
explanations.textEn:
5.a4

This move tries to attack Black's queenside and lure it to it's doom. b4 is almost universally played after this, as if Qa5, the queen is exposed. b4 tries to boot the knight into oblivion and disrupt White's queenside.
explanations.textZh:
5.a4

这一步棋试图攻击黑方的后侧并引诱其走向灭亡。此后b4几乎普遍被玩，就像Qa5一样，女王暴露了。 b4 试图将马带入遗忘状态并扰乱白方的后翼。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...c6/3. Nc3/3...dxc4/4. e3/4...b5/5. Nxb5
explanations.text:
5. Nxb5?

This clever attempt to win material is a huge mistake, providing Black with a huge advantage.

Black should undoubtedly continue with 5...cxb5, taking the offered piece. Now 6. Qf3 is White's only way to try to capitalise on their sacrifice, threatening to take the rook on a8. Black does have a few ways out.

6...Qc7 is the most principled. Black will try to trap the white queen if the rook is taken. White should continue with their plan, since backing out now would leave Black up a clean piece. 7. Qxa8 Bb7 8. Qxa7 e5! White's queen is trapped and 9...Nc6 is threatened. White has to give up another piece to save the queen: 9. Bxc4 bxc4 and the queen can escape to a4. White ends up with two pawns and a rook for two pieces, but White is also severely behind in development.

Alternatively, 6...Nc6 can be played, giving back the piece but gaining a ton of initiative: 7. Qxc6+ Bd7 8. Qa6 e5!. Material is equal, but Black has way more active pieces and a queenside space advantage.

6...Na6 is another interesting idea, temporarily giving up the rook for a vicious attack on White. The idea is 7. Qxa8 Nb4, threatening to fork the white king and rook. White's king can't go on the light squares, since that would allow a check with Black's light-squared bishop, revealing an attack on the white queen. While equal according to computer analysis, the position requires Black to play very accurately if they wish to keep their advantage.

5.Nxb5？

这种巧妙的赢得材料的尝试是一个巨大的错误，为黑方提供了巨大的优势。

毫无疑问，黑方应该继续下 5...cxb5，拿走所提供的棋子。现在是6。Qf3是白方试图利用他们的牺牲的唯一方法，威胁要在a8上拿下车。黑棋确实有一些出路。

6...Qc7是最有原则的。如果车被拿下，黑方将尝试诱捕白方皇后。白棋应该继续他们的计划，因为现在退出将使黑棋干净利落。 7.Qxa8 Bb7 8.Qxa7 e5！白后被困，9...Nc6 受到威胁。白棋必须放弃另一子才能拯救皇后：9。Bxc4 bxc4，皇后可以逃到a4。白棋最终拥有两个棋子和一个车两子，但白棋的发展也严重落后。

或者，可以演奏 6...Nc6，回馈作品但获得大量主动权：7. Qxc6+ Bd7 8. Qa6 e5!。物质是平等的，但黑棋有更多的活跃棋子和后侧空间优势。

6...Na6 是另一个有趣的想法，暂时放弃车来对白棋进行恶毒攻击。这个想法是7.Qxa8 Nb4，威胁要叉白王和车。白方的国王不能走在浅色方块上，因为这将允许与黑方的浅色方块主教进行检查，从而揭示对白后的攻击。虽然根据计算机分析，棋局是相等的，但如果黑方想保持优势，就需要非常准确地下棋。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...c6/3. Nc3/3...dxc4/4. e3/4...b5/5. Nxb5/5...cxb5
explanations.text:
5...cxb5

This move bravely accepts White's bold sacrifice. Conventional chess wisdom says "The best way to refute a gambit is to accept it". Therefore, if black would have declined the gambit, white would successfully rip black's queenside apart and Black would just be worse. Now, white's queen will get trapped on a8.

Of course, the only way to try to regain the material is with 6.Qf3.

5...cxb5

这一棋勇敢地接受了白棋的大胆牺牲。传统的国际象棋智慧说“反驳策略的最好方法就是接受它”。因此，如果黑棋拒绝这一策略，白棋将成功撕开黑棋的后侧，而黑棋的情况只会更糟。现在，白后将被困在a8上。

当然，尝试重新获得材料的唯一方法是使用 6.Qf3。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...c6/3. Nc3/3...dxc4/4. e3/4...b5/5. Nxb5/5...cxb5/6. Qf3
explanations.text:
6.Qf3

This move tries to regain the material, hopefully with interest. Now, we come to a cross, where two moves lead to a clear black advantage. The first idea is to cut Black's losses to a piece while maintaining the queenside. This can be achieved simply by Nc6, when after Qxc6+ Bd7 Black's queenside holds. The other, more dramatic plan is to imprison white's queen on a7 at the cost of a rook. This is achieved by Qc7! Qxa8 (Now, cut off the long diagonal so the Queen can't escape with her capture) Bb7! Qxa7 (Now, cut off c5 and a3 and the queen will get trapped) e5! (e6 is also good). Now, the center is opening, and Nc6 is threatened. White will have to lose material in order to save his queen.

Black can also play the extremely interesting Na6 Qxa8 Nb4, with an attack for the lost exchange. However, it is not clearly better for Black, and computer analysis proved that it is only a draw after Rb1 Nc2+ Kd2 Nf6 Qxa7 (Avoiding Kxc2?? Bf5+) a3! (Stopping Bb4+) Bf5 Qc6+ Qd7 Qa8+! (If Qxd7+?! Kxd7, black has the better ending since the rook will be won back due to the Bf5/Nc2 discovery for example: Let's say that white passed this move Nxd4 Ra1?? (White had to give back the material) Nb3+, 0-1) Qd8 Qc6+ Qd7, =.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...c6/3. Nc3/3...dxc4/4. e4
explanations.text:
4. e4 · Alekhine attack

White uses the fact that the capture has left the e4-square undefended and expends their centre, revealing an attack from the light-squared bishop on the c4 pawn.

Black generally holds onto their pawn with /4...b5/, preparing to push b5-b4 if White challenges their pawn with a2-a4.

/4...e5/ was the first main line, but players with White have shown that it is not to be feared, scoring very well against it.

History

This move was popularised after being played in round 6 of the world championship rematch between Alexander Alekhine and Max Euwe, which proceeded 4...e5 5. Bxc4 exd4 6. Nf6!? (if 6...dxc3 7. Bxf7+ Ke7 with the possible continuation of 8. Qb3 Qb6? 9. Bxg8 Rxg8 10. Qxg8 Sarapu - Anthony Garbett 1976) 6...b5 7. Nxb5 Ba6 8. Qb3 Qe7 9. O-O Bxb5 10. Bxb5 . Alekhine went on to win the game.

It wasn't until 1939 that players started holding onto the c4 pawn with 4...b5.

explanations.textZh:
4. e4·阿廖欣攻击

白方利用这一事实，即吃子使 e4 方格处于不设防状态，并扩大了其中心，揭示了光方主教对 c4 兵的攻击。

黑方通常会用 /4...b5/ 控制他们的棋子，准备在白方用 a2-a4 挑战他们的棋子时推动 b5-b4。

/4...e5/ 是第一条主线，但白方棋手已经表明它并不可怕，对抗它得分非常好。

历史

这一招在亚历山大·阿廖欣 (Alexander Alekhine) 和马克斯·尤威 (Max Euwe) 之间的世界冠军复赛第 6 轮比赛中流行起来，比赛结果为 4...e5 5. Bxc4 exd4 6. Nf6!? （如果 6...dxc3 7. Bxf7+ Ke7 可能延续 8. Qb3 Qb6？ 9. Bxg8 Rxg8 10. Qxg8 Sarapu - Anthony Garbett 1976） 6...b5 7. Nxb5 Ba6 8. Qb3 Qe7 9. O-O Bxb5 10. Bxb5 。阿廖欣最终赢得了比赛。

直到 1939 年，玩家才开始用 4...b5 持有 c4 棋子。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...c6/3. Nc3/3...e5
explanations.text:
Winawer Countergambit

3...e5

Black offers a gambit pawn in order to develop more quickly, as well as displacing White's knight. If the gambit is accepted, Black usually regains the pawn but more than returns the time: after 4. dxe5 d4 5. Ne4 Qa5+ 6. Bd2 Qxe5 7. Ng3, Black has his pawn back, but Nf3 is coming with tempo, and it is white who has the greater development. An alternative is 6. Nd2, after which Black is best not capturing on e5 immediately, but instead playing 6...Nd7, preparing something like 7. Ngf3 Nxe5 8. Nxe5 Qxe5. The old line 6. Nd2 f6!?, making the gambit sincere, has been analyzed by Schiller, building on work by Silman and Donaldson, but has never been played at the highest level.

Of course, White can also capture on d5 before considering the gambit: 4. cxd5 cxd5 and now any of 5. dxe5, 5. Nf3, 5. e3, and even 5. e4 are playable. 5. dxe5 gives Black an isolated queen's pawn, but after 5...d4 6. Ne4 Qa5+ 7. Nd2 Nc6 8. Nf3 Bg4 he will regain his gambit pawn at the cost of the bishop pair, with the d pawn potentially becoming passed after e.g. 9. g3 Bxf3 10. exf3 Qxe5 11. Qe2 Qxe2. 5. Nf3 gets kicked around twice by 5...e4 6. Ne5 f6 7. Qa4+ Nd7, with complex, unclear positions after either 8. Nxd7 Bxd7 9. Qb3 Bc6 or 8. Ng4 Kf7. 5. e3 allows Black to equalize with either the space-gaining 5...e4 or simply 5...exd4. 5. e4 is perhaps the strongest of White's fifth-move choices, and is always followed with 5...dxe4. Then the main continuation is 6. Bb4+ Bd7 7. dxe5 Bb4 8. Bd2 Bxc3 9. Bxd7+ (9. Bxc3 would be a losing mistake) Nxd7 10. Bxc3 Nc5, offering a queen trade while threatening ...Nd3+. 6. d5 bears mention mainly for the historic game Marshall-Winawer, 1901 rather than any great strength.

Finally, White can decline the gambit immediately with either 4. Nf3 or 4. e3. After 4. Nf3, Black equalizes with 4...exd4, or can try for more with 4...e4, where after 5. Nd2 Nf6 6. e3 a reversed French results. 4. e3 is best met with 4...exd4 5. exd4 Nf6. 4. e3 e4 results in a reversed French, but unlike the previous example, White can put the extra tempo to immediate use with 5. Qb3 etc.

explanations.textZh:
温纳维尔反击策略

3...e5

黑方提供了一个开局棋子，以便更快地发展，并取代白方的马。如果该策略被接受，黑方通常会夺回棋子，但不仅仅是返回时间：在4. dxe5 d4 5. Ne4 Qa5+ 6. Bd2 Qxe5 7. Ng3之后，黑方拿回了棋子，但Nf3来了节奏，白方发展更大。另一种选择是 6. Nd2，之后黑方最好不要立即吃 e5，而是下 6...Nd7，准备类似 7. Ngf3 Nxe5 8. Nxe5 Qxe5 之类的东西。席勒在西尔曼和唐纳森工作的基础上对老线 6. Nd2 f6!? 进行了分析，使策略变得真诚，但从未在最高水平上发挥过。

当然，白棋也可以在考虑策略之前吃掉 d5：4.cxd5 cxd5，现在 5.dxe5、5.Nf3、5.e3 甚至 5.e4 中的任何一个都可以玩。 5. dxe5 给黑方一个孤立的后棋棋子，但在 5...d4 6. Ne4 Qa5+ 7. Nd2 Nc6 8. Nf3 Bg4 之后，他将以主教对为代价重新获得开局棋子，例如 d 棋子可能会被通过。 9. g3 Bxf3 10. exf3 Qxe5 11. Qe2 Qxe2。 5. Nf3 被 5...e4 6. Ne5 f6 7. Qa4+ Nd7 踢了两次，在 8. Nxd7 Bxd7 9. Qb3 Bc6 或 8. Ng4 Kf7 之后位置复杂且不清楚。 5. e3 允许黑方用扩大空间的 5...e4 或简单的 5...exd4 来扳平比分。 5. e4 也许是白方第五手棋中最强的选择，并且总是紧随其后的是 5...dxe4。然后主要延续是 6. Bb4+ Bd7 7. dxe5 Bb4 8. Bd2 Bxc3 9. Bxd7+ （9. Bxc3 将是一个失败的错误） Nxd7 10. Bxc3 Nc5，在威胁 ...Nd3+ 的同时提供皇后交易。 6. d5熊提到的主要是1901年的历史性比赛Marshall-Winawer，而不是任何伟大的力量。

最后，白方可以使用 4. Nf3 或 4. e3 立即拒绝该策略。 4. Nf3 之后，黑方用 4...exd4 扳平比分，或者可以尝试用 4...e4 争取更多，其中 5. Nd2 Nf6 6. e3 之后是相反的法式结果。 4. e3 最好与 4...exd4 5. exd4 Nf6 配合。 4. e3 e4 导致相反的法语，但与前面的示例不同，白方可以将额外的节奏立即用于 5. Qb3 等。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...c6/3. Nc3/3...Nf6
explanations.text:
3...Nf6

Black develops a knight to f6, and puts pressure on the e4-square. From here White has multiple good responses, although 4. Bf4 and 4. Bg5 should be avoided as Black can play 4...dxc4 and retain the pawn without giving White any compensation.

/4. Nf3/ develops the White's knight to f3, increasing control over the d4 and e5 squares. This is considered the mainline and it gives Black many responses to choose from.

/4. e3/ is similar to the Quiet variation, which occurs after 3. Nf3 instead. It disallows the Slav accepted with 4...dxc4 and forces Black into a different variation like the Semi-Slav or the Chebanenko Slav. It is however possible for Black to play 4...Bf5 and sacrifice a pawn. This move is usually followed up by 5. Nf3, although occasionally Nf3 is delayed in favour of other developing moves such as Qc2.

/4. cxd5/ is occasionally played, relieving tension in the center, and play transposes to exchange Slav variations.

explanations.textZh:
3...NF6

黑棋将马发展到f6，并向e4方格施加压力。从这里开始，白棋有多个好的反应，尽管应该避免 4. Bf4 和 4. Bg5，因为黑棋可以下 4...dxc4 并保留棋子而不给白棋任何补偿。

/4。 Nf3/ 将白方骑士发展为 f3，增加对 d4 和 e5 方格的控制。这被认为是主线，它为黑方提供了多种反应可供选择。

/4。 e3/ 与 Quiet 变体类似，后者发生在 3. Nf3 之后。它不允许接受 4...dxc4 的斯拉夫，并迫使黑方采用不同的变体，如半斯拉夫或切巴年科斯拉夫。然而，黑棋有可能下 4...Bf5 并牺牲一个棋子。此步棋通常紧随其后的是 5.Nf3，尽管有时 Nf3 会因其他发展中的步法（例如 Qc2）而被延迟。

/4。 cxd5/ 偶尔会演奏，以缓解中间的紧张，并且演奏会转调以交换斯拉夫变奏。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...c6/3. Nc3/3...Nf6/4. Nf3/4...e6
explanations.text:
4...e6 · Semi-Slav defence

A highly theoretical opening. Black willingly keeps the light-squared bishop behind the pawn-chain, intending to free it later with either the e5 or c5 pawn breaks. In response, White has two main options with very different playstyles.

/5. Bg5/ leads to sharp, tactical positions, where Black can choose to play the Botvinnik variation 5...dxc4 or the Moscow or Anti-Moscow.

/5. e3/ leads to calmer, more positional variations. White will generally decide whether to go into the mainline Meran with 6. Bd3 or avoid it with one of the many Anti-Meran variations.

Some less popular options include /5. cxd5/, leading to either an exchange Slav or exchange Queens gambit declined. /5. g3/ is also a viable alternative, dodging theoretical lines of the Semi-Slav and potentially resulting in Catalan-esque positions.

This opening can also be reached through the queen's gambit declined by the move order 2...e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Nf3 c6.
explanations.textEn:
4...e6 · Semi-Slav defence

A highly theoretical opening. Black willingly keeps the light-squared bishop behind the pawn-chain, intending to free it later with either the e5 or c5 pawn breaks. In response, White has two main options with very different playstyles.

/5. Bg5/ leads to sharp, tactical positions, where Black can choose to play the Botvinnik variation 5...dxc4 or the Moscow or Anti-Moscow.

/5. e3/ leads to calmer, more positional variations. White will generally decide whether to go into the mainline Meran with 6. Bd3 or avoid it with one of the many Anti-Meran variations.

Some less popular options include /5. cxd5/, leading to either an exchange Slav or exchange Queens gambit declined. /5. g3/ is also a viable alternative, dodging theoretical lines of the Semi-Slav and potentially resulting in Catalan-esque positions.

This opening can also be reached through the queen's gambit declined by the move order 2...e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Nf3 c6.
explanations.textZh:
4...e6 · 半斯拉夫防御

一个高度理论化的开场白。黑方自愿将浅方象保留在典当链后面，打算稍后用 e5 或 c5 典当将其释放。作为回应，白棋有两种主要选择，两种玩法风格截然不同。

/5。 Bg5/ 导致尖锐的战术位置，黑方可以选择使用博特维尼克变体 5...dxc4 或莫斯科或反莫斯科。

/5。 e3/ 导致更平静、更多的位置变化。白方通常会决定是否使用 6.Bd3 进入主线 Meran，或者使用众多 Anti-Meran 变体之一来避免它。

一些不太受欢迎的选项包括 /5。 cxd5/，导致交换斯拉夫或交换皇后策略下降。 /5。 g3/也是一个可行的替代方案，避开半斯拉夫人的理论路线，并可能导致加泰罗尼亚式的立场。

这个开局也可以通过后弃兵策略来达到，移动顺序为 2...e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Nf3 c6。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...c6/3. Nc3/3...Nf6/4. Nf3/4...e6/5. Bg5
explanations.text:
5. Bg5

This super-sharp move is often today a true gambit. White intends to offer the c-pawn as a real sacrifice. Here Black can try the solid 5...Nbd7, which leads into the Queen's Gambit Declined (Cambridge Springs Variation), the sharp Botvinnik Variation (5...dxc4 6. e4 b5 7. e5 h6 8. Bh4 g5 9. Nxg5! hxg5 10. Bxg5 with tremendous complications), or the even sharper Anti-Moscow variation, 5...h6 6. Bh4 dxc4 7. e4 g5 8. Bg3 b5.

5. 背景5

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...c6/3. Nc3/3...Nf6/4. Nf3/4...e6/5. Bg5/5...dxc4
explanations.text:
5...dxc4 · Botvinnik variation

Welcome to the Botvinnik Slav, the highway of wild variations, where crazy tactical complications fill the board.

Black boldly accepts the gambit pawn, but their material advantage is only temporary. White's main response is /6. e4/, establishing a large center and planning to continue with e5. The resulting positions will be very chaotic and theoretical, making it very dangerous for an unprepared player.
explanations.textEn:
5...dxc4 · Botvinnik variation

Welcome to the Botvinnik Slav, the highway of wild variations, where crazy tactical complications fill the board.

Black boldly accepts the gambit pawn, but their material advantage is only temporary. White's main response is /6. e4/, establishing a large center and planning to continue with e5. The resulting positions will be very chaotic and theoretical, making it very dangerous for an unprepared player.
explanations.textZh:
5...dxc4 · 鲍特维尼克变体

欢迎来到博特维尼克斯拉夫，这是狂野变化的高速公路，这里充满了疯狂的战术复杂性。

黑方大胆接受弃兵，但他们的物质优势只是暂时的。白棋的主要反应是/6。 e4/，建立一个大型中心并计划继续e5。由此产生的局面将非常混乱且理论上，对于没有准备的玩家来说非常危险。

explanations.text:
7. e5

White pushes forward the e pawn, attacking the pinned knight. Black can still save the knight by playing /7...h6/, kicking away the bishop.
explanations.textEn:
7. e5

White pushes forward the e pawn, attacking the pinned knight. Black can still save the knight by playing /7...h6/, kicking away the bishop.
explanations.textZh:
7.e5

白棋向前推 e 兵，攻击被压制的马。黑棋仍然可以通过下/7...h6/来拯救马，踢掉主教。

explanations.text:
7...h6

This is the only move for Black to not lose a piece. White's main response is /8. Bh4/, retreating the bishop and retaining the pin.

The alternatives to 8. Bh4 give Black relatively little problems. If White tries 8. exf6? Black gets a comfortable position up a pawn after 8...hxg5 9. fxg7 Bxg7.

8. Bxf6?! is also dubious at best and allows Black to quickly equalize. Since White has given up the dark-squared bishop, Black can combat White's remaining bishop by putting the majority of their pawns on light squares.
explanations.textEn:
7...h6

This is the only move for Black to not lose a piece. White's main response is /8. Bh4/, retreating the bishop and retaining the pin.

The alternatives to 8. Bh4 give Black relatively little problems. If White tries 8. exf6? Black gets a comfortable position up a pawn after 8...hxg5 9. fxg7 Bxg7.

8. Bxf6?! is also dubious at best and allows Black to quickly equalize. Since White has given up the dark-squared bishop, Black can combat White's remaining bishop by putting the majority of their pawns on light squares.
explanations.textZh:
7...h6

这是黑方不失子的唯一一步。白棋的主要反应是/8。 Bh4/，撤退主教并保留销钉。

8.Bh4 的替代方案给黑方带来的问题相对较少。如果白方尝试 8.exf6？黑棋在 8...hxg5 9. fxg7 Bxg7 之后获得了一个舒适的棋子位置。

8.Bxf6？！充其量也是可疑的，并允许黑方迅速扳平。由于白棋已经放弃了暗方象，黑方可以通过将大部分棋子放在浅方格上来对抗白方剩余的象。

explanations.text:
8. Bh4

White retains the pin on Black's knight, threatening to take it with the pawn. Black must respond adequately with /8...g5/, removing the bishop from the diagonal.
explanations.textEn:
8. Bh4

White retains the pin on Black's knight, threatening to take it with the pawn. Black must respond adequately with /8...g5/, removing the bishop from the diagonal.
explanations.textZh:
8.Bh4

白棋保留了黑棋马上的别针，并威胁要用棋子夺走它。黑棋必须用 /8...g5/ 做出充分的反应，将象从对角线上移除。

explanations.text:
8...g5

Black blocks the vision of White's dark-squared bishop in order to save the knight. It seems that White's attack is finally over but /9. Nxg5/ continues the attack, temporarily sacrificing the knight for two pawns to win it back later.
explanations.textEn:
8...g5

Black blocks the vision of White's dark-squared bishop in order to save the knight. It seems that White's attack is finally over but /9. Nxg5/ continues the attack, temporarily sacrificing the knight for two pawns to win it back later.
explanations.textZh:
8...g5

黑棋挡住了白方黑方主教的视野，以拯救马。看起来白棋的攻击终于结束了，但是/9。 Nxg5/继续进攻，暂时牺牲骑士换取两个棋子，以便稍后赢回。

explanations.text:
9. Nxg5

White sacrifices their knight temporarily. Black should simply recapture with /9...hxg5/.

/9...Nd5/? doesn't work because of White's response 10. Nxf7! and Black can't avoid losing material.
explanations.textEn:
9. Nxg5

White sacrifices their knight temporarily. Black should simply recapture with /9...hxg5/.

/9...Nd5/? doesn't work because of White's response 10. Nxf7! and Black can't avoid losing material.
explanations.textZh:
9.NXG5

白棋暂时牺牲了他们的马。黑棋只需用/9...hxg5/ 重新夺回。

/9...Nd5/？由于白棋的反应而不起作用 10. Nxf7！黑方无法避免损失材料。

explanations.text:
10. Bxg5

White recaptures the pawn, reestablishing the pin on the knight. Black can't avoid White gaining his piece back and should continue development. /10...Nbd7/ is the usual reply, representing the starting point of the Botvinnik variation.

/10...Be7/ is another option, although it leads to many trades resulting in a very simplified position, which usually isn't the goal of players going into the Botvinnik.
explanations.textEn:
10. Bxg5

White recaptures the pawn, reestablishing the pin on the knight. Black can't avoid White gaining his piece back and should continue development. /10...Nbd7/ is the usual reply, representing the starting point of the Botvinnik variation.

/10...Be7/ is another option, although it leads to many trades resulting in a very simplified position, which usually isn't the goal of players going into the Botvinnik.
explanations.textZh:
10.Bxg5

白棋夺回棋子，重新锁定马。黑方无法避免白方夺回自己的棋子，因此应该继续发展。 /10...Nbd7/ 是通常的回复，代表鲍特维尼克变体的起点。

/10...Be7/ 是另一种选择，尽管它会导致许多交易，从而导致非常简化的位置，这通常不是进入 Botvinnik 的玩家的目标。

explanations.text:
10...Nbd7

Black defends the knight on f6 again to prevent 11. Bxf6 forking the queen and the rook.

This is the first big branching point in the Botvinnik variation. White has two main options.

/11. g3/, the Lilienthal variation, delays capturing the knight on f6 and prepares to fianchetto White's light-squared bishop.

/11. exf6/ takes the hanging knight immediately. While it often transposes back into the Lilienthal, it gives Black more options to deviate from the Lilienthal.
explanations.textEn:
10...Nbd7

This is the first big branching point in the Botvinnik variation. White has two main options.

/11. g3/, the Lilienthal variation, delays capturing the knight on f6 and prepares to fianchetto White's light-squared bishop.

/11. exf6/ takes the hanging knight immediately. While it often transposes back into the Lilienthal, it gives Black more options to deviate from the Lilienthal.
explanations.textZh:
10...NBD7

黑方再次防守f6马，阻止11.Bxf6分叉后车。

这是鲍特维尼克变体中的第一个大分支点。白棋有两个主要选择。

/11. g3/，李林塔尔的变体，延迟在 f6 上捕获骑士并准备先攻击白方的光方主教。

/11. exf6/ 立即拿下悬挂的骑士。虽然它经常变回李林塔尔，但它为黑方提供了更多偏离李林塔尔的选择。

explanations.text:
11. g3 · Lilienthal variation

White prepares to fianchetto the light-squared bishop.

Blacks main response is /11...Bb7/, fighting for the a8-h1 diagonal.

/11...Rg8/ is a sideline, preparing to exchange the rook for White's powerful dark-squared bishop. White ends up having a rook, a pawn and open lines on the kingside for the two pieces.

History

This move made its debut in 1944, in a game between Andre Lilienthal (whom the opening is named after) and Mikhail Botvinnik.

explanations.textZh:
11. g3·李林塔尔变奏

白棋准备向浅方主教下棋。

黑方主要反应是/11...Bb7/，争夺a8-h1对角线。

/11...Rg8/ 是副线，准备用车换白方强大的暗方象。白方最终拥有一车、一卒，王侧有两子的空位。

历史

这一招首次亮相是在 1944 年，安德烈·李林塔尔（Andre Lilienthal）（开局以他的名字命名）和米哈伊尔·鲍特维尼克（Mikhail Botvinnik）之间的一场比赛中。

explanations.text:
6. Bh4 · Anti-Moscow

White has decided to enter the Anti-Moscow variation of the Semi-Slav, a tactically rich and theoretically heavy opening.

Black's main move is /6...dxc4/, taking the pawn that White has declined to defend.
explanations.textEn:
6. Bh4 · Anti-Moscow

White has decided to enter the Anti-Moscow variation of the Semi-Slav, a tactically rich and theoretically heavy opening.

Black's main move is /6...dxc4/, taking the pawn that White has declined to defend.
explanations.textZh:
6. Bh4·反莫斯科

白棋决定进入半斯拉夫的反莫斯科变体，这是一个战术丰富、理论上沉重的开局。

黑方的主要棋步是/6...dxc4/，吃掉白方拒绝防守的棋子。

explanations.text:
7. e4

White takes control of the center, opening up the light-squared bishop to recapture the c pawn.

The immediate /7...b5/ allows White to play 8. e5, transposing into the Botvinnik variation.

Black's main response is to first play the in-between move /7...g5/, forcing White to drop back the dark-squared bishop to g3.
explanations.textEn:
7. e4

The immediate /7...b5/ allows White to play 8. e5, transposing into the Botvinnik variation.

Black's main response is to first play the in-between move /7...g5/, forcing White to drop back the dark-squared bishop to g3.
explanations.textZh:
7.e4

白棋控制了中心，打开了光方象，重新夺回了c兵。

立即的 /7...b5/ 允许白方下 8. e5，转换为鲍特维尼克变体。

黑棋的主要反应是首先下中间棋/7...g5/，迫使白棋将暗方象回落到g3。

explanations.text:
7...g5

Black attacks White's bishop again, forcing it to retreat to g3.

Unlike the Botvinnik variation, /8. Nxg5/? is a blunder in this position. After the sequence 8. Nxg5 hxg5 9. Bxg5 Black can defend the knight and break the pin with 9...Be7 and simply move the knight after e5.
explanations.textEn:
7...g5

Black attacks White's bishop again, forcing it to retreat to g3.

Unlike the Botvinnik variation, /8. Nxg5/? is a blunder in this position. After the sequence 8. Nxg5 hxg5 9. Bxg5 Black can defend the knight and break the pin with 9...Be7 and simply move the knight after e5.
explanations.textZh:
7...g5

黑方再次攻击白方的象，迫使其撤退至g3。

与鲍特维尼克变体不同，/8。 NXG5/？在这个位置上是一个错误。在序列之后 8. Nxg5 hxg5 9. Bxg5 黑方可以防守马并用 9...Be7 打破销钉，并在 e5 之后简单地移动马。

explanations.text:
8...b5

Black defends the c pawn. This is the starting point of the Anti-Moscow variation.

White's main move is /9. Be2/, preparing to castle short and start an attack on Black's king, which is still stuck in the center.
explanations.textEn:
8...b5

explanations.textZh:
8...b5

黑方防守 c 兵。这是反莫斯科变奏的起点。

白棋的主要棋步是/9。 Be2/，准备短兵相接并向仍卡在中间的黑方王发起攻击。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...c6/3. Nc3/3...Nf6/4. Nf3/4...e6/5. e3
explanations.text:
5. e3

This move protects the c4-pawn with the light-squared bishop, but keeps the dark-squared bishop behind the pawn-chain. Play is usually very positional compared to the 5. Bg5 lines.

Black's main idea is to take the c4-pawn once White develops their bishop to d3, gaining important tempi while expanding on the queenside. Since White has yet to place the bishop on d3, Black's main response is /5...Nbd7/, waiting for White to develop the bishop.
explanations.textEn:
5. e3

This move protects the c4-pawn with the light-squared bishop, but keeps the dark-squared bishop behind the pawn-chain. Play is usually very positional compared to the 5. Bg5 lines.

Black's main idea is to take the c4-pawn once White develops their bishop to d3, gaining important tempi while expanding on the queenside. Since White has yet to place the bishop on d3, Black's main response is /5...Nbd7/, waiting for White to develop the bishop.
explanations.textZh:
5.e3

这一举动用浅色方块的象保护了 c4 兵，但将深色方块的象保留在棋子链后面。与 5.Bg5 线相比，比赛通常非常注重位置。

黑方的主要想法是一旦白方将象发展到 d3，就拿走 c4 兵，在扩大后翼的同时获得重要的节奏。由于白方尚未将象放在d3上，黑方的主要反应是/5...Nbd7/，等待白方发展象。

explanations.text:
5...Nbd7

This is a waiting move: Black is waiting for White to develop the light-squared bishop with /6. Bd3/. Black does so in order to win some important tempi on White's bishop to make space for Black's light-squared bishop on b7. This is called the Meran variation.

White doesn't have to follow this plan however. White can play /6. Qc2/, the Anti-Meran, to avoid this line and make Black's development of the light-squared bishop more difficult.
explanations.textEn:
5...Nbd7

This is a waiting move: Black is waiting for White to develop the light-squared bishop with /6. Bd3/. Black does so in order to win some important tempi on White's bishop to make space for Black's light-squared bishop on b7. This is called the Meran variation.

White doesn't have to follow this plan however. White can play /6. Qc2/, the Anti-Meran, to avoid this line and make Black's development of the light-squared bishop more difficult.
explanations.textZh:
5...NBD7

这是一个等待着棋：黑方正在等待白方用/6 发展出光方象。 BD3/。黑方这样做是为了在白方的象上赢得一些重要的节奏，为黑方在 b7 上的浅方象腾出空间。这称为梅拉诺变体。

然而，白棋不必遵循这个计划。白棋可以下/6。 Qc2/，反梅拉诺，以避免这条线，并使黑方发展光方象变得更加困难。

explanations.text:
6. Qc2 · Anti-Meran variation

With this move, White decides to avoid the theory-heavy Meran. After Black's usual response /6...Bd6/ White will have a wide range of choices.
explanations.textEn:
6. Qc2 · Anti-Meran variation

With this move, White decides to avoid the theory-heavy Meran. After Black's usual response /6...Bd6/ White will have a wide range of choices.
explanations.textZh:
6. Qc2·反梅拉诺变异

通过这一举动，怀特决定避开理论重的梅兰。在黑方通常的反应/6...Bd6/之后，白方将有多种选择。

explanations.text:
6. Bd3

White intends to enter the Meran variation. However, Black gets the final say in this matter.

After /6...dxc4/ Black has officially entered the Meran variation, forcing White to move the bishop again to recapture the pawn.

If Black doesn't want to play the theoretical Meran, they can avoid it with /6...Bd6/.
explanations.textEn:
6. Bd3

If Black doesn't want to play the theoretical Meran, they can avoid it with /6...Bd6/.
explanations.textZh:
6.Bd3

白棋打算进入梅拉诺变体。不过，这件事最终的决定权还是由黑方决定。

/6...dxc4/之后，黑方正式进入梅兰变体，迫使白方再次移动象以夺回棋子。

如果黑方不想下理论上的 Meran，他们可以用 /6...Bd6/ 来避免它。

explanations.text:
6...dxc4 · Meran variation

Black captures the c4 pawn with a tempo on White's bishop, forcing White to move it again.

/7. Bxc4/ is the only sensible move.
explanations.textEn:
6...dxc4 · Meran variation

Black captures the c4 pawn with a tempo on White's bishop, forcing White to move it again.

/7. Bxc4/ is the only sensible move.
explanations.textZh:
6...dxc4 · 梅拉诺变体

黑棋以白棋象的节奏吃掉了 c4 棋子，迫使白棋再次移动它。

/7。 Bxc4/ 是唯一明智的举动。

explanations.text:
7. Bxc4

White recaptures the pawn.

/7...b5/ is the most proper response, justifying the loss of control over the center by making the b7-square available for the light-squared bishop while gaining a tempo.
explanations.textEn:
7. Bxc4

White recaptures the pawn.

/7...b5/ is the most proper response, justifying the loss of control over the center by making the b7-square available for the light-squared bishop while gaining a tempo.
explanations.textZh:
7.Bxc4

白棋夺回棋子。

/7...b5/ 是最正确的反应，通过使 b7 方格可供光方主教使用，同时获得节奏，从而证明对中心失去控制是合理的。

explanations.text:
7...b5

Black expands on the queenside and makes the b7-square available for their bishop while gaining a tempo on White's bishop.

White should retreat the bishop, there are three viable options:

/8. Bd3/ is the main line, returning the bishop to the square it was originally positioned on. From this square, it supports the e4 pawn-push and glances at Black's kingside.

/8. Be2/ is a more passive option. It can't be attacked as easily on e2 as on d3, but its also not as active in the attack.

/8. Bb3/ is the most aggressive option, keeping the bishop on the a2-g8 diagonal. White can generate a lot of pressure on the e6 and f7 pawns, possibly sacrificing a knight for the initiative. This option is not guaranteed if Black knows the theory well, so Black can come out with a slight edge if they are well prepared.
explanations.textEn:
7...b5

Black expands on the queenside and makes the b7-square available for their bishop while gaining a tempo on White's bishop.

White should retreat the bishop, there are three viable options:

/8. Bd3/ is the main line, returning the bishop to the square it was originally positioned on. From this square, it supports the e4 pawn-push and glances at Black's kingside.

/8. Be2/ is a more passive option. It can't be attacked as easily on e2 as on d3, but its also not as active in the attack.

/8. Bb3/ is the most aggressive option, keeping the bishop on the a2-g8 diagonal. White can generate a lot of pressure on the e6 and f7 pawns, possibly sacrificing a knight for the initiative. This option is not guaranteed if Black knows the theory well, so Black can come out with a slight edge if they are well prepared.
explanations.textZh:
7...b5

黑方向后侧扩张，为他们的主教提供了b7方格，同时获得了对白方主教的节奏。

白棋应该撤退象，有三种可行的选择：

/8。 Bd3/ 是主线，将主教返回到原来所在的方格。从这个方格开始，它支持 e4 兵推并扫视黑方的王翼。

/8。 Be2/ 是一个更被动的选择。它在 e2 上不像在 d3 上那样容易受到攻击，但它的攻击也不那么活跃。

/8。 Bb3/ 是最激进的选择，将主教保持在 a2-g8 对角线上。白棋可以对 e6 和 f7 兵产生很大的压力，可能会牺牲一个马来获得主动权。如果黑方熟悉该理论，则不能保证此选项，因此如果黑方准备充分，则可以取得轻微优势。

explanations.text:
8. Bd3

White returns the bishop to its original position, from where it supports the e4 pawn push. This is considered to be the main line.

The classical response by Black is /8...a6/, protecting the b4-pawn in order to be able to free the light-squared bishop with c5 later. This does allow White to take control of the center with the immediate 9. e4, after which some very complicated positions can arise.

A slightly more modern and nowadays more popular response is /8...Bb7/, the Wade variation. This makes the immediate 9. e4 less desirable for White, who usually responds by castling kingside immediately.

explanations.textZh:
8.Bd3

白方将象返回到原来的位置，从那里支持 e4 兵推。这被认为是主线。

黑方的经典反应是/8...a6/，保护b4兵，以便稍后能够用c5解放光方象。这确实允许白方通过立即的 9. e4 控制中心，之后可能会出现一些非常复杂的局面。

稍微更现代、现在更流行的响应是 /8...Bb7/，韦德变体。这使得立即的 9. e4 对白方来说不太理想，白方通常会立即通过王翼易位来做出反应。

explanations.text:
8...a6

Black protects the b-pawn so they can play 9...c5 without blundering a pawn.

Foreseeing this plan, White should play actively and take over the center with /9. e4/, preparing to open up the center with either 10. d5 or 10. e5 and opening up the dark-squared bishop.

Less provocative setups have been tried as well. At the amateur level /9. O-O/ is very popular, but this poses no problems for players with the black pieces at all, since they score quite well in this line.

Another move that is played often is /9. a4/. White does better than after 9. O-O, but has lost quite a bit of initiative.

8...a6

黑方保护 b 兵，这样他们就可以下 9...c5，而不会犯下一个兵错误。

预见到这个计划，白棋应该积极发挥并用/9接管中路。 e4/，准备用 10. d5 或 10. e5 打开中心并打开暗方象。

还尝试了较少挑衅性的设置。业余水平/9。 O-O/ 非常受欢迎，但这对于黑子棋手来说完全没有问题，因为他们在这条线上得分相当高。

另一个经常下的棋是/9。 a4/.白方比 9.O-O 后表现更好，但失去了相当多的主动性。

explanations.text:
9. e4

White strikes in the center, opening up the dark-squared bishop in the process.

Black's main move is /9...c5/, looking to break up White's center immediately. This move is played in the vast majority of games, and is Black's best option to open up the light-squared bishop and fight for an advantage.

A very rare sideline is /9...b4/, the Pirc variation. This is the only other move (according to chess engines) that doesn't give White a winning advantage, since it gains a tempo on White's knight.

explanations.textZh:
9.e4

白棋击中中心，在此过程中打开了暗方象。

黑棋的主要棋步是/9...c5/，希望立即破坏白棋的中心。这一步棋在绝大多数棋局中都会出现，是黑方打开光方象、争取优势的最佳选择。

一个非常罕见的副线是 /9...b4/，Pirc 变体。这是唯一一个不给白方带来获胜优势的走法（根据国际象棋引擎），因为它获得了白方马的节奏。

explanations.text:
9...c5

Black strikes back at White's center, opening up the light-squared bishop.

This is the main branching point of the mainline Meran, since White has to choose between one of two pawn breaks: e5 and d5.

/10. e5/ is the Old variation.

/10. d5/ is Reynold's variation.

9...c5

黑棋向白棋中心发起反击，打开了浅色方块的象。

这是主线 Meran 的主要分支点，因为白方必须在两个兵损之一之间进行选择：e5 和 d5。

/10. e5/ 是旧版本。

/10. d5/ 是雷诺变体。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...c6/3. cxd5
explanations.text:
3. cxd5 · Exchange Variation

After this move, the tension in the center is relieved often allowing Black equality due to the symmetrical position. Because of this, this variation often ends in a draw.

Black's only good move is to complete the exchange of pawns with /3...cxd5/, and accept a symmetrical position. However, Nf6!? might be interesting as the position transposes to QGD, Marshall defence, Tan Gambit although this is rarely seen in high-level games. 3...Qxd5?! should be avoided as 4. Nc3 gains a lot of tempo, and allows White a crushing spacial advantage in the center.

After 3...cxd5, either side will find it difficult to win unless the other is over-ambitious.

explanations.textZh:
3.cxd5·兑换变体

此举之后，中心的紧张局势得到缓解，由于对称的位置，黑方往往能够平等。正因为如此，这种变化常常以平局告终。

黑方唯一的好棋是用/3...cxd5/完成棋子交换，并接受对称位置。然而，Nf6！？可能会很有趣，因为位置转移到 QGD、马歇尔防守、谭甘比特，尽管这在高水平比赛中很少见。 3...Qxd5？！应避免使用 4。NC3 获得了很多节奏，并让白方在中路获得了压倒性的空间优势。

3...cxd5 之后，任何一方都会发现很难获胜，除非对方过于雄心勃勃。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...c6/3. cxd5/3...cxd5
explanations.text:
3...cxd5

This is Black's best option, accepting a symmetrical position.

While normal development moves will suffice, White can try to make it harder for Black to get the light-squared bishop out by delaying the combination of Nf3 and e3, which would allow Black to pin the knight to the queen with Bg4.

The most popular continuation for White is the combination of Nc3, Bf4 and e3. Usually White starts with /4. Nc3/ which is more flexible than the immediate, but totally viable, /4. Bf4/.
