3...c6 · 三角系统

在这个位置上，通过延迟 Nf6，黑方保留了许多机会。他们可以继续以正常的拒绝后弃兵 (QGD) 方式玩 4...Nf6（无论白棋下 e3 还是 Nf3），或者可以尝试其他选择。

/4。 Nf3/ 可以导致常规 QGD 游戏或 Noteboom 变体：4...dxc4。在这里，黑棋的目标是用侧翼的两个传棋来换取白棋的大中锋。中局很关键，但如果黑方能活下来，残局将对他们有利。

另一方面/4。 e3/ 可以导致 4...f5 的石墙防御位置，其中黑方通常的计划是对王方进行快速攻击，并且通常可以涉及将车提升到 f6。

白方的另一个选择是半斯拉夫的马歇尔弃兵，虽然不太受欢迎，但为 /4。 e4/.此举旨在利用黑方对 e4 方格缺乏控制、未下 Nf6 的优势。主线继续4...dxe4 5. Nxe4 Bb4+ 6. Bd2 Qxd4 7. Bxb4 Qxe4+ 比赛犀利。通常白方会用 Be2 格挡，并让 g2 棋子悬空。黑可以吃掉它，但不能吃车（Bf3 赢得后）。作为回报，白方可以拥有持久的压力和涉及 d6 弱点的战术。此系列游戏的一个示例是 Bacrot - Morozevich, Biel Rd2, 2012。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nc3/3...c6/4. e4
explanations.text:
4. e4 · Marshall gambit

This move controls the center and creates a huge pawn roller. Black's c8-bishop will be blocked and inactive for some time. However, White will have to sacrifice a pawn in a few moves if they want to fight for the edge. Black hasn't moved a single piece yet and put all their central pawns on light squares. White quickly got e4 in.
explanations.textEn:
4. e4 · Marshall gambit

This move controls the center and creates a huge pawn roller. Black's c8-bishop will be blocked and inactive for some time. However, White will have to sacrifice a pawn in a few moves if they want to fight for the edge. Black hasn't moved a single piece yet and put all their central pawns on light squares. White quickly got e4 in.
explanations.textZh:
4. e4·马歇尔策略

这一举动控制了中心并创造了一个巨大的典当滚轮。黑方的 c8 主教将被封锁并在一段时间内处于非活动状态。然而，如果白棋想要争夺优势，就必须在几步之内牺牲一个棋子。黑棋还没有移动任何棋子，并将所有中央棋子放在浅色方格上。白棋很快就下e4。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nc3/3...c6/4. e4/4...dxe4/5. Nxe4/5...Bb4
explanations.text:
5...Bb4+

This move is Black's best option to fight for an advantage. It forces White to either gambit the d4 pawn for activity, or to retreat the knight back to c3, "losing" a tempo in the process.

/6. Bd2/ is the main move, blocking the check and attacking Black's bishop at the same time. This does however block the white queen from defending the d4 pawn, allowing 6...Qxd4, which gambits the pawn in exchange for quick development and active pieces.

/6. Nc3/ is the Forgotten variation, a sideline where White holds onto the d4 pawn, keeping material equal.

6. Nd2? is a mistake, since it contains all the drawbacks of 6. Bd2 (losing d4) and none of the advantages (getting a very active dark-squared bishop). To add insult to injury, it also hampers the development of White's queenside by locking up the c1 bishop.
explanations.textEn:
5...Bb4+

This move is Black's best option to fight for an advantage. It forces White to either gambit the d4 pawn for activity, or to retreat the knight back to c3, "losing" a tempo in the process.

/6. Bd2/ is the main move, blocking the check and attacking Black's bishop at the same time. This does however block the white queen from defending the d4 pawn, allowing 6...Qxd4, which gambits the pawn in exchange for quick development and active pieces.

/6. Nc3/ is the Forgotten variation, a sideline where White holds onto the d4 pawn, keeping material equal.

6. Nd2? is a mistake, since it contains all the drawbacks of 6. Bd2 (losing d4) and none of the advantages (getting a very active dark-squared bishop). To add insult to injury, it also hampers the development of White's queenside by locking up the c1 bishop.
explanations.textZh:
5...Bb4+

此步棋是黑方争取优势的最佳选择。它迫使白方要么放弃 d4 兵以进行活动，要么将马撤退到 c3，在此过程中“失去”节奏。

/6。 Bd2/是主招，阻挡阻击，同时攻击黑方的象。然而，这确实阻止了白后保卫 d4 棋子，允许 6...Qxd4，这会用棋子换取快速发展和活跃棋子。

/6。 Nc3/ 是被遗忘的变体，白方持有 d4 棋子的一条边线，保持材料相等。

6. ND2？这是一个错误，因为它包含了 6. Bd2 的所有缺点（失去 d4），并且没有任何优点（得到一个非常活跃的暗方主教）。雪上加霜的是，它还锁住了c1主教，阻碍了白方后翼的发展。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nc3/3...c6/4. e4/4...dxe4/5. Nxe4/5...Bb4/6. Bd2
explanations.text:
6. Bd2

This move blocks the check and attacks Black's bishop, but loses sight of the d4-pawn. /6...Qxd4/ picks up the gambitted pawn and threatens the knight on e4.
explanations.textEn:
6. Bd2

This move blocks the check and attacks Black's bishop, but loses sight of the d4-pawn. /6...Qxd4/ picks up the gambitted pawn and threatens the knight on e4.
explanations.textZh:
6.BD2

这一举动阻止了检查并攻击黑方的主教，但失去了 d4 兵的视野。 /6...Qxd4/ 拿起已出局的棋子并威胁 e4 上的马。

explanations.text:
6...Qxd4

Black takes the gambitted pawn and will be up material for the time being. This opening doesn't come without compensation for White. After /7. Bxb4/ White will have dominance over Black's weakened dark squares.
explanations.textEn:
6...Qxd4

Black takes the gambitted pawn and will be up material for the time being. This opening doesn't come without compensation for White. After /7. Bxb4/ White will have dominance over Black's weakened dark squares.
explanations.textZh:
6...Qxd4

黑方拿下已下棋的棋子，暂时成为优势。这个空缺对于怀特来说并不是没有补偿的。 /7之后。 Bxb4/白方将对黑方被削弱的暗方占据主导地位。

explanations.text:
7. Bxb4

White takes Black's dark-squared bishop. White's dark-squared bishop is now placed on a very active diagonal, cutting through d6, e7 and f8. Black should play 7...Qxe4+ to not be down a piece.
explanations.textEn:
7. Bxb4

White takes Black's dark-squared bishop. White's dark-squared bishop is now placed on a very active diagonal, cutting through d6, e7 and f8. Black should play 7...Qxe4+ to not be down a piece.
explanations.textZh:
7.Bxb4

白方拿走黑方的黑方象。白方的暗方象现在被放置在一条非常活跃的对角线上，穿过 d6、e7 和 f8。黑棋应该下 7...Qxe4+ 才不会落下棋子。

explanations.text:
7...Qxe4+

Black recaptures the piece. This is the starting point of the Marshall gambit. White has two main ways of blocking the check, both leading to complex positions where White has to find a way to convert their lead in development into a tangible advantage. White should generally avoid trading pieces, especially queens, as any endgame will favour Black.

/8. Be2/ is the main line, blocking the check with the bishop. This leaves the g2-pawn undefended, but taking it would be unwise, since it allows White to develop even more quickly with Bf3, Ne2 and then Rg2 comes with tempo.

/8 Ne2/ is less popular, but still very often played. This leaves the c4-pawn undefended, but taking it is once again way too dangerous for Black because of Qd6!, infiltrating on the weakened dark squares. The main continuation in this line ends up restoring material equality.
explanations.textEn:
7...Qxe4+

Black recaptures the piece. This is the starting point of the Marshall gambit. White has two main ways of blocking the check, both leading to complex positions where White has to find a way to convert their lead in development into a tangible advantage. White should generally avoid trading pieces, especially queens, as any endgame will favour Black.

/8. Be2/ is the main line, blocking the check with the bishop. This leaves the g2-pawn undefended, but taking it would be unwise, since it allows White to develop even more quickly with Bf3, Ne2 and then Rg2 comes with tempo.

/8 Ne2/ is less popular, but still very often played. This leaves the c4-pawn undefended, but taking it is once again way too dangerous for Black because of Qd6!, infiltrating on the weakened dark squares. The main continuation in this line ends up restoring material equality.
explanations.textZh:
7...Qxe4+

黑棋夺回棋子。这就是马歇尔策略的起点。白棋有两种主要的方式来阻止检查，这两种方式都会导致复杂的局面，白棋必须找到一种方法将他们在发展中的领先优势转化为有形的优势。白方通常应避免交易棋子，尤其是皇后，因为任何残局都会有利于黑方。

/8。 Be2/为主线，阻挡与主教的检查。这使得g2兵不设防，但采取它是不明智的，因为它允许白方用Bf3、Ne2更快地发展，然后Rg2带有节奏。

/8 Ne2/ 不太受欢迎，但仍然经常播放。这使得 c4 兵处于不设防的状态，但是对于黑方来说，占据它又太危险了，因为 Qd6! 会渗透到被削弱的黑暗方格中。这条路线的主要延续最终是恢复物质平等。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nc3/3...c6/4. Nf3
explanations.text:
4. Nf3

White develops the knight and leaves the opening choice to Black. The move /4...Nf6/ transposes into the Semi-Slav defence, while /4...dxc4/ enters the sharp Noteboom variation.
explanations.textEn:
4. Nf3

White develops the knight and leaves the opening choice to Black. The move /4...Nf6/ transposes into the Semi-Slav defence, while /4...dxc4/ enters the sharp Noteboom variation.
explanations.textZh:
4.NF3

白方发展马并将开局选择留给黑方。招式 /4...Nf6/ 转入半斯拉夫防御，而 /4...dxc4/ 则进入尖锐的 Noteboom 变体。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nc3/3...c6/4. Nf3/4...dxc4
explanations.text:
4...dxc4 · Noteboom variation

With this move Black enters the aggressive Noteboom variation.

White can attempt to win back the pawn like in the Alapin Slav with /5. a4/ but Black can take advantage of that move with 5...Bb4. After 6. e3, attacking the pawn, Black can defend it with 6...b5, making use of the fact that after 7. axb5 cxb5 White's knight on c3 is still pinned and can't capture the pawn on b5.

White's other option is to try to win back the pawn with the immediate /5. e3/ but Black will respond with 5...b5, defending the pawn. After 6. a4 Black has successfully provoked White into weakening the b4-square, where Black will once again place the dark-squared bishop, transposing into the previous line.

White can also choose to avoid the Noteboom with either /5. Bg5/ the anti-Noteboom variation or with /5. g3/ the anti-Noteboom gambit.

History

This opening was named after the player Daniël Noteboom, who played it in the 1930 Chess Olympiad.

explanations.textZh:
4...dxc4 · Noteboom 变体

通过此步黑棋进入激进的 Noteboom 变体。

白方可以尝试像阿拉宾斯拉夫棋中那样用/5 赢回棋子。 a4/ 但黑方可以利用 5...Bb4 的优势。 6. e3 之后，攻击棋子，黑方可以用 6...b5 防守它，利用 7. axb5 cxb5 之后，白方 c3 上的马仍然被牵制，无法吃掉 b5 上的棋子。

白方的另一个选择是尝试用立即/5 赢回棋子。 e3/，但黑方会回应 5...b5，保卫棋子。 6. a4 黑方成功激怒白方削弱 b4 方格后，黑方将再次放置暗方象，移至前一行。

白方也可以选择使用 /5 来避免 Noteboom。 Bg5/ 反 Noteboom 变体或与 /5。 g3/ 反 Noteboom 策略。

历史

这一开局以 1930 年国际象棋奥林匹克比赛中的选手丹尼尔·诺特布姆 (Daniël Noteboom) 的名字命名。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nc3/3...f5
explanations.text:
1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 2.Nc3 f5

The Dutch Stonewall, contrived through a transpositional trick! This variation avoids the 2. Nc3 and 3. Bg5 lines against the Dutch. Black wants to play f5 only after White plays c4 and Nc3 to have an iron grip on e4.

The downside of playing Dutch Stonewall is that there will be a hole on e5, but White can play f3 to guard e4 while black does not have similar option to protect e5. White will try to blast open the position by arranging to play e4 or g4 (to open up the g file and try to weaken the structure of black) at an appropriate time. Black will try to build up against White's King with a kingside pawn roller. Qh5, Rf6, g5 etc. on White's King is always on cards. White also has play on the queenside.

Weakness pieces of Black

Bishop on c8 - This piece is stuck behind the pawns, but modern day analysis show that it can be maneuvered via d7,e8 and to h5/g6,

Pawn on e6 - It is a backward pawn that is hard to remove.

explanations.textZh:
1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 2.NC3 f5

荷兰石墙，通过换位技巧设计而成！这种变化避免了针对荷兰队的 2. Nc3 和 3. Bg5 线。只有在白方下c4和Nc3之后，黑方才想下f5，以牢牢掌握e4。

玩荷兰石墙的缺点是e5上会有一个洞，但白棋可以下f3来防守e4，而黑棋没有类似的选项来保护e5。白棋会在适当的时候安排下e4或g4（打开g档，试图削弱黑棋的结构）来尝试炸开局面。黑方将尝试用王侧滚兵来对抗白方的国王。白王上的 Qh5、Rf6、g5 等总是在牌上。白棋也在后翼发挥作用。

黑棋的弱点

c8 上的主教 - 这颗棋子卡在棋子后面，但现代分析表明它可以通过 d7、e8 和 h5/g6 进行操作，

e6 上的棋子 - 这是一个难以移除的向后棋子。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nc3/3...Be7
explanations.text:
3...Be7 · Charousek variation

Black stops White from playing the immediate 4. Bg5, practically forcing White into one of three options:

/4. Nf3/, simply developing the knight. This is the most common and flexible response, since White doesn't reveal anything about their setup yet. If Black plays 4...Nf6 then 5. Bg5 transposes back into the main lines.

/4. Bf4/ develops the bishop to f4 instead. White intends to enter the Harrwitz attack.

/4. cxd5/ transposes into an exchange variation where Black has already played Be7, preventing White from usefully developing the bishop to g5.
explanations.textEn:

/4. Nf3/, simply developing the knight. This is the most common and flexible response, since White doesn't reveal anything about their setup yet. If Black plays 4...Nf6 then 5. Bg5 transposes back into the main lines.

/4. Bf4/ develops the bishop to f4 instead. White intends to enter the Harrwitz attack.

/4. cxd5/ transposes into an exchange variation where Black has already played Be7, preventing White from usefully developing the bishop to g5.
explanations.textZh:
3...Be7·查鲁塞克变体

黑方阻止白方下4.Bg5，实际上迫使白方做出以下三种选择之一：

/4。 Nf3/，只是发展骑士。这是最常见和灵活的回应，因为怀特还没有透露任何有关他们的设置的信息。如果黑方下 4...Nf6，则下 5。Bg5 移回主线。

/4。 Bf4/ 将主教改为 f4。白棋打算进入哈维茨进攻。

/4。 cxd5/ 转置为黑方已下 Be7 的交换变体，阻止白方有效地将象发展为 g5。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nc3/3...Nf6
explanations.text:
3...Nf6

With 3...Nf6, Black begins developing the minor pieces, gets closer to castling, and exerts control over the center.

This is the classical main line of the Queen's Gambit Declined. White has several options, though some of these may transpose into each other at some point.

/4. cxd5/ is the exchange variation. Unlike other exchange variations notorious for yielding a quiet game (e.g. French, Slav), this exchange results in what is known as the Carlsbad pawn structure, which has several aggressive plans, such as a "minority attack" on the queenside. Although it was once relatively uncommon, as Black's usual response 4...exd5 unblocks the queen's bishop from development, it has become the main line after 3...Nf6.

/4. Bg5/ is a classical continuation that leads to a wide variety of positions. White gets the dark-squared bishop outside of the pawn chain in order to be able to release the light-squared bishop with e2-e3. Black usually unpins the knight with 4...Be7 and tries to castle quickly. After the usual 5. e3 O-O 6. Nf3, Black has a major choice between 6...Nbd7 (the classical variation) and 6...h6. 4...Nbd7 is a notable alternative, often leading to the Cambridge Springs defense (5.e3 c6 6.Nf3 Qa5).

/4. Nf3/ is the three knights variation. White gives Black many choices on how to continue development, including some of the most aggressive variations of the Queen's Gambit, such as the Semi-Slav (4...c6) and Vienna (4...dxc4) variations, as well as the Ragozin (4...Bb4) and Semi-Tarrasch (4...c5). Transposition to the 4. Bg5 line after 4...Be7 5. Bg5 is also possible, but White has the major alternative of 5. Bf4, the Harrwitz Attack.

3...NF6

有了 3...Nf6，黑棋开始发展小棋子，更接近易位，并控制中心。

这是《后弃兵》的经典主线。白棋有多种选择，尽管其中一些可能在某些时候相互转换。

/4。 cxd5/ 是交换变体。与其他因产生安静游戏而臭名昭著的交换变体（例如法语、斯拉夫语）不同，这种交换导致了所谓的卡尔斯巴德典当结构，该结构有几个激进的计划，例如对后翼的“少数派攻击”。虽然曾经比较少见，但由于黑方惯常的应对4...exd5解除了后主教的发展，因此在3...Nf6之后成为了主线。

/4。 Bg5/ 是一个经典的延续，导致了各种各样的位置。白方将暗方象置于典当链之外，以便能够用 e2-e3 释放亮方象。黑方通常用 4...Be7 解开马并尝试快速占领城堡。在通常的 5. e3 O-O 6. Nf3 之后，黑方在 6...Nbd7（经典变体）和 6...h6 之间有一个主要选择。 4...Nbd7 是一个值得注意的替代方案，通常会导致剑桥泉防御 (5.e3 c6 6.Nf3 Qa5)。

/4。 Nf3/是三骑士的变体。白方在如何继续发展方面为黑方提供了多种选择，包括后弃兵的一些最具攻击性的变体，例如半斯拉夫（4...c6）和维也纳（4...dxc4）变体，以及拉戈津（4...Bb4）和半塔拉什（4...c5）变体。 4...Be7 5. Bg5 之后换位到 4. Bg5 线也是可能的，但白方有 5. Bf4 的主要替代方案，哈维茨攻击。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nc3/3...Nf6/4. Bg5/4...Nbd7
explanations.text:
Queen's Gambit Declined

4...Nbd7

With 4...Nbd7, black intends to play the Cambridge Springs Defense, which continues 5. Nf3 c6 6. e3 Qa5. The Cambridge Springs Defense is a solid line of the QGD and is often played both in the amateur level (because of the easier to understand theme) and the grandmaster level. This move also sets a trap that has ensnared quite a few players. White can continue 5. cxd5 exd5, resulting in a position that resembles the QGD Exchange variation (which is fine for both camps), as long as he/she doesn't play 6. Nxd5??. While it superficially appears to win a pawn (because the black knight is pinned), black can capture with his knight with 6... Nxd5!. Then after 7. Bxd8, white has not won black's queen because of 7... Bb4+!, where the only legal move is 8. Qd2, and black gets his/her queen back and emerges a minor piece ahead.

explanations.textZh:
后弃兵策略

4...NBD7

有了 4...Nbd7，黑方打算进行剑桥泉防御，继续 5. Nf3 c6 6. e3 Qa5。剑桥泉防御赛是 QGD 的一条坚实的路线，经常在业余级别（因为主题更容易理解）和特级大师级别中进行。这一举动还设置了一个陷阱，让不少玩家陷入了陷阱。白棋可以继续 5.cxd5 exd5，从而形成类似于 QGD 交换变体的位置（这对两个阵营都很好），只要他/她不玩 6.Nxd5??。虽然它表面上看起来赢得了一个棋子（因为黑棋被钉住了），但黑棋可以用 6...Nxd5! 吃掉他的棋子。然后在 7.Bxd8 之后，白棋没有赢得黑棋的后棋，因为 7...Bb4+!，其中唯一合法的棋步是 8.Qd2，黑棋拿回了他/她的后棋，并在前面出现了一个小棋子。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nc3/3...Nf6/4. Bg5/4...Be7
explanations.text:
4...Be7 · Orthodox variation

Black unpins the knight and prepares to castle short.

White's two main responses /5. e3/ and /5. Nf3/ are very likely to transpose, so the order doesn't particularly matter.
explanations.textEn:
4...Be7 · Orthodox variation

Black unpins the knight and prepares to castle short.

White's two main responses /5. e3/ and /5. Nf3/ are very likely to transpose, so the order doesn't particularly matter.
explanations.textZh:
4...Be7 · 正统变体

黑棋解开了马并准备短兵相接。

白棋的两个主要反应/5。 e3/和/5。 Nf3/ 很可能会转置，因此顺序并不特别重要。

explanations.text:
6. Nf3

White proceeds with normal development. Black now has two options.

Go into the classical variation with /6...Nbd7/.

Go for either Lasker's defense or the Tartakower variation with /6...h6/.
explanations.textEn:
6. Nf3

White proceeds with normal development. Black now has two options.

Go into the classical variation with /6...Nbd7/.

Go for either Lasker's defense or the Tartakower variation with /6...h6/.
explanations.textZh:
6.NF3

白色继续正常发育。黑棋现在有两个选择。

进入经典变体 /6...Nbd7/。

选择拉斯克防御或 Tartakower 变体 /6...h6/。

explanations.text:
6...Nbd7 · Classical variation

With this move Black enters the Classical variation. This is an older and well-studied variation that has stood the test of time, as it is still played to this day. Due to its age, White has developed many responses to it over time.

/7. Rc1/ is the main line, developing the rook to the to-be-opened c-file.

/7. Qc2/ is the Rubinstein attack. White develops the queen to watch over the b1-h7 diagonal.

/7. cxd5/ releases the tension from the center and transposes into an exchange variation.

/7. Bd3/ is the Botvinnik variation, in which Black gains a few tempi on White's bishop with 7...cxd5 and, later on, Nb6.

History

The classical variation has been played all the way back in the late 1800's and has been deployed by and against the likes of Capablanca, Lasker, Alekhine, Kasparov and many more.

explanations.textZh:
6...Nbd7 · 古典变奏

通过这一步黑棋进入了经典变化。这是一种古老且经过充分研究的变奏，经受住了时间的考验，至今仍在演奏。由于它的年龄，随着时间的推移，怀特对其产生了许多反应。

/7。 rc1/ 是主线，将 rook 开发为要打开的 c 文件。

/7。 Qc2/ 是鲁宾斯坦攻击。白方派出皇后来监视 b1-h7 对角线。

/7。 cxd5/ 释放中心的张力并转变成交换变化。

/7。 Bd3/ 是博特维尼克变体，其中黑方以 7...cxd5 以及后来的 Nb6 在白方主教上获得了一些节奏。

历史

这一经典变体早在 1800 年代末就已被演奏，并被卡帕布兰卡、拉斯克、阿廖欣、卡斯帕罗夫等人使用或对抗。

explanations.text:
6...h6

Black pushes the bishop away, likely intending to go for either the Tartakower or Lasker's defence.

Apart from White's main option /7. Bh4/ they can also avoid these theoretical lines by playing /7. Bxf6/.
explanations.textEn:
6...h6

Black pushes the bishop away, likely intending to go for either the Tartakower or Lasker's defence.

Apart from White's main option /7. Bh4/ they can also avoid these theoretical lines by playing /7. Bxf6/.
explanations.textZh:
6...h6

布莱克将主教推开，可能是打算为塔塔科尔或拉斯克辩护。

除了白方的主要选项/7。 Bh4/ 他们还可以通过播放 /7 来避免这些理论台词。 Bxf6/.

explanations.text:
7...b6 · Tartakower defence

7...b6 enters the Tartakower defence, where Black hopes to develop the light-squared bishop. While it looks like Black intends to fianchetto the bishop, this isn't necessarily true. If White tries to blunt the a8-h1 diagonal immediately with 8. cxd5, Black will nonetheless be able to develop the bishop: 8. cxd5 Nxd5 9. Bxe7 Qxe7 10. Nxd5 exd5 and Black can now put the bishop somewhere on the c8-h3 diagonal instead (usually going to e6).

If White tries to blunt the a8-h1 diagonal immediately with 8. cxd5, Black will nonetheless be able to develop the bishop: 8. cxd5 Nxd5 9. Bxe7 Qxe7 10. Nxd5 exd5 and Black can now put the bishop somewhere on the c8-h3 diagonal instead (usually going to e6).
explanations.textZh:
7...b6 · 塔塔科韦尔防御

7...b6 进入 Tartakower 防御，黑方希望在此发展光方主教。虽然看起来布莱克打算与主教较量，但事实并非如此。如果白方试图立即用 8.cxd5 钝化 a8-h1 对角线，黑方仍然能够发展象：8.cxd5 Nxd5 9.Bxe7 Qxe7 10.Nxd5 exd5 并且黑方现在可以将象放在 c8-h3 对角线上的某个位置（通常是 e6）。

explanations.text:
7...Ne4 · Lasker defence

Black centralizes the knight, opening up an attack on White's dark-squared bishop.

The mainline continues by trading the dark-squared bishops and later the knights as well.
explanations.textEn:
7...Ne4 · Lasker defence

The mainline continues by trading the dark-squared bishops and later the knights as well.
explanations.textZh:
7...Ne4·拉斯克防御

黑棋集中了马，向白棋的黑方主教发起攻击。

主线继续交易暗方主教，后来也交易骑士。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nc3/3...Nf6/4. cxd5
explanations.text:
Queen's Gambit Declined - Exchange Variation

4. cxd5

With 4. cxd5, White enters into the Exchange Variation of the Queen's Gambit Declined. White aims to enter a Carlsbad pawn structure position, and has a variety of plans, including the queenside "minority attack", or a big pawn center duo with an eventual ...f3 and ...e4.

Black usually responds with 4...exd5, which frees up the c8-bishop, and officially enters the thematical Carlsbad pawn structure, though he can alternatively recapture with 4...Nxd5, which usually transposes into the Semi-Tarrasch.
explanations.textEn:
Queen's Gambit Declined - Exchange Variation

4. cxd5

With 4. cxd5, White enters into the Exchange Variation of the Queen's Gambit Declined. White aims to enter a Carlsbad pawn structure position, and has a variety of plans, including the queenside "minority attack", or a big pawn center duo with an eventual ...f3 and ...e4.

Black usually responds with 4...exd5, which frees up the c8-bishop, and officially enters the thematical Carlsbad pawn structure, though he can alternatively recapture with 4...Nxd5, which usually transposes into the Semi-Tarrasch.
explanations.textZh:
后弃兵 - 交换变化

4.cxd5

凭借 4.cxd5，白方进入后弃兵的交换变体。白方的目标是进入卡尔斯巴德棋子结构位置，并有多种计划，包括后翼“少数派攻击”，或最终形成 ...f3 和 ...e4 的大棋子中心二人组。

黑方通常用 4...exd5 回应，这释放了 c8 主教，并正式进入主题卡尔斯巴德棋子结构，尽管他也可以用 4...Nxd5 夺回，这通常会转入半塔拉什。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nc3/3...Nf6/4. cxd5/4...exd5
explanations.text:
Queen's Gambit Declined - Exchange Variation

4...exd5

With this move, Black frees up his light squared bishop, which was originally blocked with the move 2...e6. In addition, the classic Carlsbad pawn structure is entered, in which White has a pawn majority in the centre, and Black has a pawn majority on the queenside.

White wants flexibility on where to place the knight on g1 in this position. In the cases in which White goes for the minority attack, a knight on f3 is usually preferred, and in cases in which he prefers a central expansion with f3 and e4, a knight on e2 is preferred. As a result, White usually prefers to develop the light squared bishop first (almost always to d3), so ...e3 is played before deciding on a placement for the knight. However, playing 5. e3 immediately would block in the dark squared bishop, so White almost always continues with 5. Bg5, pinning the knight on f6 and adding pressure to the pawn on d5, whilst also getting the bishop outside the pawn chain. With this move, White threatens to double Black's pawns with 6. Bxf6, as 6...Qxf6 would lose a pawn to 7. Nxd5.
explanations.textEn:
Queen's Gambit Declined - Exchange Variation

4...exd5

With this move, Black frees up his light squared bishop, which was originally blocked with the move 2...e6. In addition, the classic Carlsbad pawn structure is entered, in which White has a pawn majority in the centre, and Black has a pawn majority on the queenside.

White wants flexibility on where to place the knight on g1 in this position. In the cases in which White goes for the minority attack, a knight on f3 is usually preferred, and in cases in which he prefers a central expansion with f3 and e4, a knight on e2 is preferred. As a result, White usually prefers to develop the light squared bishop first (almost always to d3), so ...e3 is played before deciding on a placement for the knight. However, playing 5. e3 immediately would block in the dark squared bishop, so White almost always continues with 5. Bg5, pinning the knight on f6 and adding pressure to the pawn on d5, whilst also getting the bishop outside the pawn chain. With this move, White threatens to double Black's pawns with 6. Bxf6, as 6...Qxf6 would lose a pawn to 7. Nxd5.
explanations.textZh:
后弃兵 - 交换变化

4...exd5

通过这一步棋，黑方释放了最初被 2...e6 棋阻挡的光方象。此外，还采用了经典的卡尔斯巴德棋子结构，其中白方的棋子多数位于中间，而黑方的棋子多数位于后侧。

白棋希望灵活地将马放置在 g1 的这个位置上。在白棋进行少数攻击的情况下，通常会首选 f3 上的马，而在他更喜欢使用 f3 和 e4 进行中央扩张的情况下，则优选 e2 上的马。因此，白方通常更喜欢先发展光方主教（几乎总是发展到 d3），因此在决定马的位置之前先下...e3。然而，立即下5.e3会阻止暗方象，因此白方几乎总是继续5.Bg5，将马​​固定在f6上，并给d5上的棋子增加压力，同时也将象置于棋子链之外。通过这一举动，白棋威胁将黑棋的棋子加倍为 6.Bxf6，因为 6...Qxf6 将失去一个棋子到 7.Nxd5。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nc3/3...Nf6/4. Nf3/4...c5
explanations.text:
Semi-Tarrasch Defense

General concepts

Unlike the regular Tarrasch, in the Semi-Tarrasch Defense Black does not accept an isolated pawn, since he intends to recapture on d5 with the knight (as after 5.cxd5, 5...exd5 has long been known to be dubious after 6.Bg5), but he cedes a spatial advantage to White.

After 4...c5, White usually plays 5.cxd5 Nxd5 6.e3 or 6.e4, which leads to different types of middlegame play and has attracted the interest of strong players with both colors since the early twentieth century.
explanations.textEn:
Semi-Tarrasch Defense

General concepts

Unlike the regular Tarrasch, in the Semi-Tarrasch Defense Black does not accept an isolated pawn, since he intends to recapture on d5 with the knight (as after 5.cxd5, 5...exd5 has long been known to be dubious after 6.Bg5), but he cedes a spatial advantage to White.

After 4...c5, White usually plays 5.cxd5 Nxd5 6.e3 or 6.e4, which leads to different types of middlegame play and has attracted the interest of strong players with both colors since the early twentieth century.
explanations.textZh:
半塔拉什防御

一般概念

与常规的塔拉什不同，在半塔拉什防御中，黑方不接受孤立的棋子，因为他打算在 d5 上与马一起夺回棋子（因为在 5.cxd5 之后，5...exd5 在 6.Bg5 之后长期以来一直被认为是可疑的），但他将空间优势让给了白方。

4...c5之后，白方通常会下5.cxd5 Nxd5 6.e3或6.e4，这导致了不同类型的中局玩法，并自二十世纪初以来吸引了两种颜色的强手的兴趣。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nc3/3...Nf6/4. Nf3/4...dxc4
explanations.text:
4...dxc4 · Vienna variation

4...dxc4 is a very aggressive response by Black leading to very double-edged positions. Black gives up some central control, allowing for White to build up a big center that Black tries to tear down later.

5. e4 is White's main response, taking up the entire center and preparing to recapture the pawn with the bishop.

5. e3 is the quiet variation. Positions often resemble those of the Queens Gambit accepted with 3. Nf3.

5. Qa4+ is a sideline with positions similar to the Semi Slav defence.
explanations.textEn:
4...dxc4 · Vienna variation

4...dxc4 is a very aggressive response by Black leading to very double-edged positions. Black gives up some central control, allowing for White to build up a big center that Black tries to tear down later.

5. e4 is White's main response, taking up the entire center and preparing to recapture the pawn with the bishop.

5. e3 is the quiet variation. Positions often resemble those of the Queens Gambit accepted with 3. Nf3.

5. Qa4+ is a sideline with positions similar to the Semi Slav defence.
explanations.textZh:
4...dxc4 · 维也纳变奏

4...dxc4 是黑方非常激进的应对，导致非常双刃剑的局面。黑棋放弃了一些中央控制权，让白棋建立了一个大中锋，然后黑棋试图拆除这个大中锋。

5. e4是白方的主要应对，占据整个中心，准备与象夺回棋子。

5. e3 是安静的变体。位置通常类似于 3.Nf3 所接受的后弃兵策略。

5. Qa4+是一个边线，其位置类似于半斯拉夫防守。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nc3/3...Nf6/4. Nf3/4...dxc4/5. e4
explanations.text:
5. e4

White takes up the center and opens up the light-squared bishop to recapture the pawn on c4.

Black can choose to go into the sharp mainline with 5...Bb4 or to hang onto the pawn a little longer with 5...b5.
explanations.textEn:
5. e4

White takes up the center and opens up the light-squared bishop to recapture the pawn on c4.

Black can choose to go into the sharp mainline with 5...Bb4 or to hang onto the pawn a little longer with 5...b5.
explanations.textZh:
5.e4

白方占据中心并打开浅方象以夺回c4上的棋子。

黑方可以选择用 5...Bb4 进入锋利的主线，或者用 5...b5 延长棋子的停留时间。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nc3/3...Nf6/4. Nf3/4...dxc4/5. e4/5...Bb4
explanations.text:
5...Bb4

Black pins the c3 knight, removing the only defender of the e4 pawn.

6. Bg5 is White's main response, pinning the f6 knight to the queen which indirectly defends the e4 pawn.

6. Bxc4 is a sideline, letting Black take the e4 pawn for faster development.
explanations.textEn:
5...Bb4

Black pins the c3 knight, removing the only defender of the e4 pawn.

6. Bg5 is White's main response, pinning the f6 knight to the queen which indirectly defends the e4 pawn.

6. Bxc4 is a sideline, letting Black take the e4 pawn for faster development.
explanations.textZh:
5...Bb4

黑方钉住了 c3 马，移除了 e4 兵的唯一防守者。

6. Bg5是白方的主要应对，将f6马固定在后，从而间接保护e4兵。

6. Bxc4 是副线，让黑方拿走 e4 棋子，以加快发展速度。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nc3/3...Nf6/4. Nf3/4...Be7
explanations.text:
Queen's Gambit Declined

Three Knights Variation 4...Be7

This position is often reached from the Indian defence after white tries to avoid the Nimzo-Indian through 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 d5 4. Nc3 Be7
explanations.textEn:
Queen's Gambit Declined

Three Knights Variation 4...Be7

This position is often reached from the Indian defence after white tries to avoid the Nimzo-Indian through 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 d5 4. Nc3 Be7
explanations.textZh:
后弃兵策略

三骑士变奏 4...Be7

白棋试图通过 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 d5 4. Nc3 Be7 避开尼姆佐-印度棋后，通常会从印度防御到达此位置

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nc3/3...Nf6/4. Nf3/4...Be7/5. Bf4
explanations.text:
5. Bf4 · Harrwitz Attack

White develops the bishop to f4. This just looks like a standard developing move, but it is extremely aggressive. With the bishop on f4 instead of g5, White avoids piece exchanges, and often castles queenside while Black castles kingside, leading to sharp opposite-side castling positions.

Black has nothing better to do than castle.
explanations.textEn:
5. Bf4 · Harrwitz Attack

White develops the bishop to f4. This just looks like a standard developing move, but it is extremely aggressive. With the bishop on f4 instead of g5, White avoids piece exchanges, and often castles queenside while Black castles kingside, leading to sharp opposite-side castling positions.

Black has nothing better to do than castle.
explanations.textZh:
5. Bf4·哈维茨攻击

白方将象发展到f4。这看起来只是一个标准的发展动作，但它却极具侵略性。当主教位于 f4 而不是 g5 时，白方避免了棋子交换，并且经常在后侧城堡，而黑方在王侧城堡，导致尖锐的对面易位位置。

黑棋除了城堡之外没有什么更好的事情可做。

explanations.text:
Queen’s Gambit Declined

Blackburne Variation

After the developing move 6. e3, Black has 3 choices:

-She can take advantage of the Bishop being on f4 instead of g5, which doesn’t pressure the d5 pawn, and play 6...c5 without fear of being forced into an IQP structure. However, this line is entry to the rabbit hole and leads to very complicated positions.

-6...Nbd7 is a more solid choice and avoids the complications of the main line. However, it allows 7. c5 resulting in white having a pleasant space advantage.

-6...b6 is the most solid way for Black to play, resulting in positions resembling the Tartokower Defense.
explanations.textEn:
Queen’s Gambit Declined

Blackburne Variation

After the developing move 6. e3, Black has 3 choices:

-She can take advantage of the Bishop being on f4 instead of g5, which doesn’t pressure the d5 pawn, and play 6...c5 without fear of being forced into an IQP structure. However, this line is entry to the rabbit hole and leads to very complicated positions.

-6...Nbd7 is a more solid choice and avoids the complications of the main line. However, it allows 7. c5 resulting in white having a pleasant space advantage.

-6...b6 is the most solid way for Black to play, resulting in positions resembling the Tartokower Defense.
explanations.textZh:
后弃兵策略

布莱克本变例

在展开6.e3之后，黑棋有3个选择：

-她可以利用主教位于 f4 而不是 g5 的优势，这不会给 d5 棋子带来压力，并且可以玩 6...c5，而不必担心被迫进入 IQP 结构。然而，这条线是兔子洞的入口，会导致非常复杂的局面。

-6...Nbd7是一个更可靠的选择，避免了主线的复杂性。然而，它允许 7.c5 导致白色具有令人愉快的空间优势。

-6...b6 是黑方最可靠的下法，导致类似塔托科防御的局面。

explanations.text:
Queen’s Gambit Declined, Blackburne Variation, Main Line

6...c5

Black immediately strikes the White centre with ...c7-c5. This takes advantage of the Bishop being on f4 instead of g5, which applies less pressure on d5. To demonstrate, after 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Nf3 Be7 5. Bg5 O-O 6. e3 h6 7. Bh4, 7...c5 can be met with 8. Bxf6 Bxf6 9. cxd5 exd5 10. dxc5, and Black is left with a suboptimal isolated queen’s pawn structure.

White’s only move is the Botvinnik exchange: 7. dxc5, forcing the black bishop on e7 to waste a tempo. 7. cxd5 can be met with ...Nxd5, and 7. Bd3 or 7. Be2 can be met with ...dxc4, which all allow black to equalise comfortably.
explanations.textEn:
Queen’s Gambit Declined, Blackburne Variation, Main Line

6...c5

Black immediately strikes the White centre with ...c7-c5. This takes advantage of the Bishop being on f4 instead of g5, which applies less pressure on d5. To demonstrate, after 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Nf3 Be7 5. Bg5 O-O 6. e3 h6 7. Bh4, 7...c5 can be met with 8. Bxf6 Bxf6 9. cxd5 exd5 10. dxc5, and Black is left with a suboptimal isolated queen’s pawn structure.

White’s only move is the Botvinnik exchange: 7. dxc5, forcing the black bishop on e7 to waste a tempo. 7. cxd5 can be met with ...Nxd5, and 7. Bd3 or 7. Be2 can be met with ...dxc4, which all allow black to equalise comfortably.
explanations.textZh:
后弃兵、布莱克本变例、主线

6...c5

黑棋立即用...c7-c5 攻击白棋中心。这利用了主教在 f4 而不是 g5 上的优势，这对 d5 施加的压力较小。为了证明，在 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Nf3 Be7 5. Bg5 O-O 6. e3 h6 7. Bh4, 7...c5 之后可以遇到 8. Bxf6 Bxf6 9. cxd5 exd5 10. dxc5，黑方留下了次优的孤立后棋结构。

白方唯一的棋步是鲍特维尼克交换：7.dxc5，迫使e7上的黑主教浪费节奏。 7. cxd5 可以与...Nxd5 配合，7. Bd3 或7. Be2 可以与...dxc4 配合，这些都可以让黑色轻松均衡。

explanations.text:
Queen’s Gambit Declined, Blackburne Variation, Main Line

7. dxc5

White captures the c-pawn with 7. dxc5, forcing the black bishop on e7 to waste a tempo with 7...Bxc5. Note that 7...dxc4 leads to a favorable endgame for white after 8. Bxc4 Qxd1+ 9. Rxd1, where white enjoys more active pieces.
explanations.textEn:
Queen’s Gambit Declined, Blackburne Variation, Main Line

7. dxc5

White captures the c-pawn with 7. dxc5, forcing the black bishop on e7 to waste a tempo with 7...Bxc5. Note that 7...dxc4 leads to a favorable endgame for white after 8. Bxc4 Qxd1+ 9. Rxd1, where white enjoys more active pieces.
explanations.textZh:
后弃兵、布莱克本变例、主线

7. DXC5

白方用 7.dxc5 吃掉了 c 兵，迫使 e7 上的黑主教用 7...Bxc5 浪费了节奏。请注意，7...dxc4 在 8.Bxc4 Qxd1+ 9.Rxd1 之后为白棋带来了有利的结局，其中白棋享有更多活跃棋子。

explanations.text:
Queen’s Gambit Declined, Blackburne Variation, Main Line

7...Bxc5

Black recaptures the pawn. Now White can play the unambitious 8. cxd5 and saddle black with an isolani, or continue going down the rabbit hole with the mainline 8. Qc2, where the queen points towards the black kingside. It should be noted that 8. a3 transposes into the mainline.
explanations.textEn:
Queen’s Gambit Declined, Blackburne Variation, Main Line

7...Bxc5

Black recaptures the pawn. Now White can play the unambitious 8. cxd5 and saddle black with an isolani, or continue going down the rabbit hole with the mainline 8. Qc2, where the queen points towards the black kingside. It should be noted that 8. a3 transposes into the mainline.
explanations.textZh:
后弃兵、布莱克本变例、主线

7...Bxc5

黑方夺回棋子。现在，白方可以使用毫无野心的 8.cxd5 并用 isolani 骑上黑棋，或者继续使用主线 8.Qc2 进入兔子洞，其中皇后指向黑色的王侧。需要注意的是，8.a3 转置到了主线中。

explanations.text:
Queen’s Gambit Declined, Blackburne Variation, Main Line

8. Qc2

White activates the queen, who points towards the black kingside. Black develops with 8...Nc6
explanations.textEn:
Queen’s Gambit Declined, Blackburne Variation, Main Line

8. Qc2

White activates the queen, who points towards the black kingside. Black develops with 8...Nc6
explanations.textZh:
后弃兵、布莱克本变例、主线

8. 质量控制2

白棋激活后棋，后棋指向黑棋王翼。黑棋发展成 8...Nc6

explanations.text:
Queen’s Gambit Declined, Blackburne Variation, Main Line

9. a3

This move is important to control the b4 square and support b2-b4. Black is forced to play 9...Qa5, which prevents b4 by pinning the a3 pawn to the rook and pins the c3 knight to the king. This also supports ...Nb4.
explanations.textEn:
Queen’s Gambit Declined, Blackburne Variation, Main Line

9. a3

This move is important to control the b4 square and support b2-b4. Black is forced to play 9...Qa5, which prevents b4 by pinning the a3 pawn to the rook and pins the c3 knight to the king. This also supports ...Nb4.
explanations.textZh:
后弃兵、布莱克本变例、主线

9.a3

这一招对于控制b4方位和支撑b2-b4很重要。黑方被迫下9...Qa5，这通过将a3兵钉在车上来阻止b4，并将c3马钉在王上。这也支持...Nb4。

explanations.text:
Queen’s Gambit Declined, Blackburne Variation, Main Line

9...Qa5

This move is forced, pinning the a3 pawn to the rook, preventing b2-b4 and supporting ...Nb4 ideas. White has a sideline and 2 mainline moves.

10. Nd2 is the sideline, avoiding the complications of the mainlines. As Nb3 is threatened, black responds with ...Be7.

The mainlines 10. Rd1 and 10. O-O-O are not for the faint of heart, as they lead to wild, extremely complicated positions.
explanations.textEn:
Queen’s Gambit Declined, Blackburne Variation, Main Line

9...Qa5

This move is forced, pinning the a3 pawn to the rook, preventing b2-b4 and supporting ...Nb4 ideas. White has a sideline and 2 mainline moves.

10. Nd2 is the sideline, avoiding the complications of the mainlines. As Nb3 is threatened, black responds with ...Be7.

The mainlines 10. Rd1 and 10. O-O-O are not for the faint of heart, as they lead to wild, extremely complicated positions.
explanations.textZh:
后弃兵、布莱克本变例、主线

9...Qa5

这一举动是被迫的，将 a3 棋子钉在车上，阻止 b2-b4 并支持 ...Nb4 想法。白棋有一条边线和两条主线走法。

10. Nd2是副线，避免了主线的复杂性。当 Nb3 受到威胁时，黑棋以 ...Be7 回应。

主线 10. Rd1 和 10. O-O-O 不适合胆小的人，因为它们会导致狂野、极其复杂的局面。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nf3
explanations.text:
Queen's Gambit Declined

With 3.Nf3, White begins the development of his minor pieces after establishing a pawn center on the first two moves. 3.Nf3 controls important central squares, but unlike 3.Nc3, it does not immediately help to prepare the e4 pawn break. However, it does bring White close to castling kingside, something 3.Nc3 does not. In most QGD lines, White will play both Nc3 and Nf3 anyway; the order is important only if White desires to avoid specific variations.

White's dark-squared bishop will likely go to g5 after Black plays Nf6, but of course this is not possible immediately because of 3...Qxg5. Moving the bishop to a different square on move 3 would simply lose a tempo if it later went on to g5, so it is best to develop a knight here instead. There are sound systems involving Bf4, but it is not wise to commit to a Bf4 system so early. Thus 3.Nc3 and 3.Nf3 are the most sensible options.
explanations.textEn:
Queen's Gambit Declined

With 3.Nf3, White begins the development of his minor pieces after establishing a pawn center on the first two moves. 3.Nf3 controls important central squares, but unlike 3.Nc3, it does not immediately help to prepare the e4 pawn break. However, it does bring White close to castling kingside, something 3.Nc3 does not. In most QGD lines, White will play both Nc3 and Nf3 anyway; the order is important only if White desires to avoid specific variations.

White's dark-squared bishop will likely go to g5 after Black plays Nf6, but of course this is not possible immediately because of 3...Qxg5. Moving the bishop to a different square on move 3 would simply lose a tempo if it later went on to g5, so it is best to develop a knight here instead. There are sound systems involving Bf4, but it is not wise to commit to a Bf4 system so early. Thus 3.Nc3 and 3.Nf3 are the most sensible options.
explanations.textZh:
后弃兵策略

在 3.Nf3 中，白方在前两步棋中建立了典当中心后，开始发展他的小子。 3.Nf3控制重要的中心方格，但与3.Nc3不同的是，它并不能立即帮助准备e4兵破。然而，它确实使白方接近王翼易位，而 3.Nc3 则不然。在大多数 QGD 线路中，白方无论如何都会下 Nc3 和 Nf3；仅当白方希望避免特定变化时，顺序才重要。

在黑方下 Nf6 后，白方的暗方主教可能会进入 g5，但当然这不可能立即发生，因为 3...Qxg5。如果在第 3 步中将主教移动到另一个方格，如果随后进入 g5，只会失去节奏，因此最好在这里发展一个马。有涉及 Bf4 的健全系统，但过早致力于 Bf4 系统并不明智。因此 3.Nc3 和 3.Nf3 是最明智的选择。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nf3/3...Nf6
explanations.text:
Queen's Gambit Declined

3...Nf6

Here white can take an interesting departure from the typical QGD lines by playing 4. g3, transposing into a main line of the Catalan Opening. This colorful opening can be very aggressive, especially if black opens the long diagonal with ...dxc4 at some point. The piece play white obtains from such an opening of lines is often dangerous for black.

At this point, white's other main continuations are 4. Nc3 and 4. Bg5, though 4. cxd5 is certainly possible.
explanations.textEn:
Queen's Gambit Declined

3...Nf6

Here white can take an interesting departure from the typical QGD lines by playing 4. g3, transposing into a main line of the Catalan Opening. This colorful opening can be very aggressive, especially if black opens the long diagonal with ...dxc4 at some point. The piece play white obtains from such an opening of lines is often dangerous for black.

At this point, white's other main continuations are 4. Nc3 and 4. Bg5, though 4. cxd5 is certainly possible.
explanations.textZh:
后弃兵策略

3...NF6

在这里，白棋可以通过玩 4.g3 来有趣地偏离典型的 QGD 线，转换成加泰罗尼亚开局的主线。这种彩色的开局可能非常具有侵略性，特别是如果黑棋在某个时刻用 ...dxc4 打开长对角线。白棋从这样的开局中获得的棋子对于黑棋来说通常是危险的。

此时，白棋的其他主要延续是4.NC3和4.Bg5，尽管4.cxd5当然是可能的。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...e6/3. g3
explanations.text:
3. g3

White prepares to fianchetto their bishop. White chooses a Catalan-style set up, an approach that combines c4 and d4 with a king's side fianchetto.

This is a less common move order. Black usually develops their knight next, 3...Nf6, and the same Catalan position is reached as if the game had played out in the order 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. g3 d5.
explanations.textEn:
3. g3

White prepares to fianchetto their bishop. White chooses a Catalan-style set up, an approach that combines c4 and d4 with a king's side fianchetto.

This is a less common move order. Black usually develops their knight next, 3...Nf6, and the same Catalan position is reached as if the game had played out in the order 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. g3 d5.
explanations.textZh:
3.g3

白方准备向他们的主教发起攻击。白方选择了加泰罗尼亚风格的布局，这种方法将 c4 和 d4 与国王的侧翼切托结合起来。

这是一种不太常见的移动顺序。黑方通常接下来会发展他们的马，3...Nf6，并且达到相同的加泰罗尼亚位置，就好像游戏按照 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. g3 d5 的顺序进行一样。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...Nf6
explanations.text:
Marshall Defence

A rarely seen opening at the higher levels of chess. Instead of playing e6, black can play Nf6. Black's knight defends the d5 square, but if white exchanges pawns, it is not too difficult to later gain a tempo by attacking the piece on d5.

However, this defense may not be as bad as it seems. After 3. cxd5, black can play 3...c6?!, the Tan gambit. In this case, it is best for white to accept the gambit and now, black has a lead in development after 4. dxc6 Nxc6, giving at least partial compensation for the pawn. Usually, in the middlegame that follows, white gets a small advantage, but black usually holds out just fine. Even into the endgame, black may have chances for a draw, despite being a pawn down.

Marshall Defence

However, this defense may not be as bad as it seems. After 3. cxd5, black can play 3...c6?!, the Tan gambit. In this case, it is best for white to accept the gambit and now, black has a lead in development after 4. dxc6 Nxc6, giving at least partial compensation for the pawn. Usually, in the middlegame that follows, white gets a small advantage, but black usually holds out just fine. Even into the endgame, black may have chances for a draw, despite being a pawn down.
explanations.textZh:
马歇尔防御

在高级国际象棋中很少见的开局。黑棋可以下Nf6，而不是e6。黑方的马防守d5方格，但如果白方交换兵，稍后通过攻击d5方的棋子来获得节奏并不是太困难。

然而，这种防守可能并不像看起来那么糟糕。 3.cxd5 后，黑方可以下 3...c6？！，即 Tan 策略。在这种情况下，白棋最好接受这一策略，现在黑棋在 4. dxc6 Nxc6 之后处于领先地位，至少为棋子提供了部分补偿。通常，在接下来的中局中，白方会获得一点优势，但黑方通常会坚持得很好。即使到了残局，尽管黑棋已被棋子落下，但仍可能有平局的机会。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. c4/2...Nf6/3. cxd5
explanations.text:
3. cxd5

White takes the pawn. Black almost has to recover the pawn because of the control d5 exerts over his moves, but neither variation is very appealing:

3...Nxd5 allows 4. e4 when White has gained a tempo, the centre, and opened up lines for his pieces.

3...Qxd5 prevents white from obtaining a full pawn centre but results in 4. Nc3, winning a tempo anyway.

Because white is given a comfortable position regardless of what path black chooses, this opening is not seen very often at the professional level.

Black has also the option to play a gambit and aim at the center, with for instance 3...c6 4.dxc6 Nxc6 5.Nf3 e5!
explanations.textEn:
3. cxd5

White takes the pawn. Black almost has to recover the pawn because of the control d5 exerts over his moves, but neither variation is very appealing:

3...Nxd5 allows 4. e4 when White has gained a tempo, the centre, and opened up lines for his pieces.

3...Qxd5 prevents white from obtaining a full pawn centre but results in 4. Nc3, winning a tempo anyway.

Because white is given a comfortable position regardless of what path black chooses, this opening is not seen very often at the professional level.

Black has also the option to play a gambit and aim at the center, with for instance 3...c6 4.dxc6 Nxc6 5.Nf3 e5!
explanations.textZh:
3.cxd5

白棋拿走棋子。由于 d5 对他的走法施加了控制，黑方几乎必须收回棋子，但这两种变化都不是很有吸引力：

3...Nxd5 允许 4. e4 当白方获得节奏、中心并为他的棋子打开线路时。

3...Qxd5 阻止白棋获得完整的棋子中心，但结果是 4. Nc3，无论如何都赢得了节奏。

因为无论黑棋选择什么路径，白棋都会得到一个舒适的位置，因此这种空缺在职业级别中并不常见。

黑方还可以选择出局并瞄准中心，例如 3...c6 4.dxc6 Nxc6 5.Nf3 e5！

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. Qd3
explanations.text:
Amazon Attack

1. d4 d5 2. Qd3!?

A rarely played move. The name is presumed to derive from the Amazon tribe of fearsome female warriors in Greek mythology, as well as the powerful fairy chess piece used in some variants of the game, which combines the abilities of a queen and a knight

Against white's most common replies 2...Nc6 leads to an even position, with 2...Nf6 and 2...e6 giving black a very slight edge, while 2...c5 is generally engine favourite.

A similar idea is the sunshine (1. d4 d5 2. Nc3 Nf6 3. Qd3) Played by William Pollock against Max Weiss in 1889. White lost.

explanations.textZh:
亚马逊攻击

1.d4d5 2.Qd3！？

很少有人玩的动作。这个名字据推测源自希腊神话中可怕的亚马逊女战士部落，以及游戏某些变体中使用的强大的仙女棋子，它结合了女王和骑士的能力

针对白棋最常见的回复，2...Nc6 会导致平局，2...Nf6 和 2...e6 给黑棋带来非常轻微的优势，而 2...c5 通常是引擎最喜欢的。

类似的想法是阳光 (1. d4 d5 2. Nc3 Nf6 3. Qd3)，由威廉·波洛克 (William Pollock) 在 1889 年对阵马克斯·韦斯 (Max Weiss)。怀特输了。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. Kd2
explanations.text:
Queen's Bongcloud

2. Kd2?

2. Kd2? is thought to be the second worst following move to 1. d4 d5 (the worst move is 2. Bh6??) The problems with 2. Kd2? are that the King move prevents castling to protect the King, endangers the King, and ignores development. Like the normal Bongcloud Attack, this move may be played to gain a psychological advantage, or as a handicap.

女王的云雾

2.Kd2？

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. Kd2/2...Kd7
explanations.text:
Double Queen's Bongcloud

2. Kd7??

2.Kd7... What is this? Are you even playing chess at this point? When you play this move, you lose an opportunity to develop or attack, and it's probably the most shameful response. However this move is surely trolling, so most of games end in draw by repetition.

explanations.textZh:
双皇后的蓬云

2.Kd7??

2.Kd7...这是什么？你现在还在下棋吗？当你打出这个招式时，你就失去了发育或攻击的机会，这可能是最可耻的反应。但这一招无疑是恶搞，所以大多数比赛都是以重复的平局告终。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. e3/2...Nf6/3. c4/3...dxc4/4. Bxc4/4...Nc6
explanations.text:
Unofficial Kurtz Opening

4...Nc6

This move is the main move and where is diverged most of the lines of the Kurtz opening, some like the main line, the Benz Variation, the Silent Game, etc.

It is a door for a big center attack, and White does everything to stop 5... e5.

explanations.textZh:
非官方库尔茨开幕

4...NC6

这一招是主要招式，与库尔茨开局的大部分台词有分歧，有些像主线、奔驰变奏、无声游戏等。

这是一个大中锋攻击的大门，白棋尽一切努力阻止 5...e5。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. e4
explanations.text:
2. e4 · Blackmar-Diemer gambit

White offers their e4 pawn in exchange for quick development and open lines. At the professional level this move is considered somewhat suspect, but Black must be careful if they choose to take the pawn as there are many traps in this opening.

2...dxe4 accepts the gambit.

Black has three ways to decline the gambit.

2...e6 transposes to the French Defence

2...c6 transposes to the Caro-Kann Defence

2...Nc6 transposes to the Nimzowitsch Defence

2...c5 is a largely unexplored countergambit.

explanations.textZh:
2. e4·布莱克马尔-迪默策略

白方提供他们的 e4 棋子，以换取快速发展和开放线路。在专业层面上，这一步棋被认为有些可疑，但如果黑方选择吃兵，则必须小心，因为这个空缺中有很多陷阱。

2...dxe4 接受这个策略。

黑棋有三种方法来拒绝这一策略。

2...e6 转置为法国防御

2...c6 转置为卡罗-卡恩防御

2...Nc6 转换为尼姆佐维奇防御

2...c5 是一种很大程度上未被探索的对策。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. e4/2...c5
explanations.text:
2...c5?

An unusual countergambit to the Blackmar-Diemer or Smith-Morra gambits. It superficially resembles a reversed Albin countergambit, but with White to move.

White can capture either of the pawns and come out ahead.

If 3. dxc5 dxe4 leads to a queen trade. Most common in amateur games is 3...d4?, which seems to take space but just leaves the pawn stranded after 4. Nf3 (preventing ...e5) Nc6 5. c3. 3...Nf6 is an improvement.

If 3. exd5 Qxd5 then 4. Ne2 is best to defend the d-pawn (if 4. Nf3 then ...Bg4, pinning the knight, cannot be met with f3) 4...Nf6 5. Nbc3 Qd7 6. d5. Otherwise this probably leads to a queen trade too, e.g. 4. Nc3 Qxd4 5. Qxd4 cxd4 6. Nb5 Na6.

2...c5？

这是 Blackmar-Diemer 或 Smith-Morra 策略的不寻常的反策略。它表面上类似于相反的阿尔宾反棋，但由白棋移动。

白方可以吃掉任何一个棋子并取得领先。

如果3. dxc5 dxe4 导致皇后交易。业余游戏中最常见的是 3...d4？，这似乎占用空间，但只是让棋子在 4. Nf3（防止 ...e5）Nc6 5. c3 之后陷入困境。 3...Nf6 是一种改进。

如果 3. exd5 Qxd5 那么 4. Ne2 最好防守 d-pawn（如果 4. Nf3 那么...Bg4，钉住马，不能与 f3 相遇） 4...Nf6 5. Nbc3 Qd7 6. d5。否则这也可能导致皇后交易，例如4. Nc3 Qxd4 5. Qxd4 cxd4 6. Nb5 Na6。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. e4/2...dxe4
explanations.text:
Blackmar-Diemer Gambit (BDG) Accepted

2...dxe4

White has given up his king's pawn, in hopes of an aggressive game. Since there is no way White can win a pawn back immediately, he can expect this set-up most times he plays the Blackmar-Diemar Gambit. The best move for White would be Nc3, putting pressure on the e4-pawn and preparing the move f3, as 3. f3 is well met by 3...e5!, with an edge for Black. One example: 4. dxe5 (other moves are even worse, for example 4. fxe4 Qh4+ and Qxe4 with an extra pawn and an attack, or d5 Nf6 c4 c6 when d5 will soon fall) Qxd1+ Kxd1 Nc6 fxe4 (f4 Bg4+ Ne2 O-O-O+ with a winning attack) Nxe5 with an obvious advantage. Black normally plays 3...Nf6, though 3...f5 and 3...Bf5 are interesting ways to avoid mainline theory. Now, if f3 e5?, dxe5 gains a tempo on the knight. Sometimes Bc4 is played, to hopefully trap Black quickly with a variation of Scholar's Mate.

explanations.textZh:
Blackmar-Diemer 策略 (BDG) 已接受

2...dxe4

白棋已经放弃了王的棋子，希望能进行一场侵略性的比赛。由于白方不可能立即赢回棋子，因此他在玩布莱克马尔-迪马尔弃兵时大多数时候都可以预期这种布局。白方的最佳走法是 Nc3，对 e4 兵施加压力并准备走法 f3，因为 3.f3 很好地满足了 3...e5!，黑方有优势。举个例子：4. dxe5（其他走法更差，例如4. fxe4 Qh4+和Qxe4有一个额外的棋子和一次攻击，或者d5即将倒下时的d5 Nf6 c4 c6）Qxd1+ Kxd1 Nc6 fxe4（f4 Bg4+ Ne2 O-O-O+具有获胜的攻击）Nxe5优势明显。黑棋通常下 3...Nf6，尽管 3...f5 和 3...Bf5 是避免主线理论的有趣方法。现在，如果f3 e5？，dxe5 获得骑士的节奏。有时会下 Bc4，希望通过学者之副的变体快速困住黑方。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. e4/2...dxe4/3. Nc3
explanations.text:
Blackmar-Diemer Gambit (BDG)

3. Nc3

White has brought his minor piece into action and taken control of the middle. Simultaneously, he has put pressure on Black's e4-pawn, which Black must now try and defend. Nf6 or Bf5 would most commonly be used to defend the lone pawn, while e5 gives the option of a pawn transfer. f5 defends the pawn using Black's f-pawn, a less optimal response. Rarer responses include Nc6 transposing to the Nimzowitsch Defense and adding an attacker to the d4 pawn, and c5, a rather unexplored countergambit.
explanations.textEn:
Blackmar-Diemer Gambit (BDG)

3. Nc3

White has brought his minor piece into action and taken control of the middle. Simultaneously, he has put pressure on Black's e4-pawn, which Black must now try and defend. Nf6 or Bf5 would most commonly be used to defend the lone pawn, while e5 gives the option of a pawn transfer. f5 defends the pawn using Black's f-pawn, a less optimal response. Rarer responses include Nc6 transposing to the Nimzowitsch Defense and adding an attacker to the d4 pawn, and c5, a rather unexplored countergambit.
explanations.textZh:
布莱克马尔-迪默策略 (BDG)

3.NC3

白棋将他的小棋子付诸行动并控制了中间棋子。同时，他对黑方的 e4 兵施加了压力，黑方现在必须尝试防守。 Nf6 或 Bf5 最常用于防御单独的棋子，而 e5 则提供棋子转移的选项。 f5 使用黑方的 f 棋子来保卫棋子，这是一个不太理想的响应。较罕见的反应包括 Nc6 转换为尼姆佐维奇防御并向 d4 棋子添加攻击者，以及 c5，这是一种尚未探索的反策略。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. e4/2...dxe4/3. Nc3/3...c5
explanations.text:
3...c5 - Reversed Albin Countergambit

This rare and rather unknown countergambit adds pressure to White's d-pawn. The name of this opening is the Reversed Albin Countergambit as it resembles an accepted Albin Countergambit with colors reversed and an extra knight on c3. This is sometimes considered slightly dubious or bizarre, but it is nonetheless playable.

Responses

White may try to regain the lost e4 pawn immediately with 3. dxc5?!, but this is too greedy and gives up White's central control and the White pawn on c5 would be quite weak and attacked easily with e6 or e5 as well as the idea of 3...Qxd1+ trading queens and is thus not the best move.

3. d5 is White's best and most popular move, pushing their pawn like in the standard Albin Countergambit. 3...Nf6 is the best and most popular move, but 3...e6? may lead to Black falling for a deadly trap (see Traps section below). It steps out of Black's c5 pawn attack.

3. Nxe4 aims to trade pawns. After 3...cxd4, White will see the reason why this is not preferred over 3. d5. It diminishes White's trap potential and after 4. Nf3 Nc6, White may not be able to prove sufficient compensation for the e4 pawn.

Traps

Because this is a mirrored Albin Countergambit Accepted, White may try to do a Reversed Lasker Trap if after 3. d5, 3...e6 is played. The trap is 4. Bb5+ Bd7 5. dxe6!, and if Black decides to trade bishops with 5...Bxb5??, they will get a nasty surprise after 6. exf7+ Ke7 7. fxg8=N+!! and 7...Rxg8?! isn't possible as 8. Bg5+! would skewer the Black king and queen, so after 7...Ke8 8. Qh5+! White has a crushing attack on Black's king and will probably overwhelm Black with attacking moves.

explanations.textZh:
3...c5 - 逆向阿尔宾对策

这种罕见且相当未知的反策略给白方的d兵增加了压力。这个开局的名称是反向阿尔宾反棋，因为它类似于公认的阿尔宾反棋，但颜色相反，并且 c3 上有一个额外的马。这有时被认为有点可疑或奇怪，但它仍然是可以玩的。

回应

白棋可能会尝试立即用 3.dxc5 夺回失去的 e4 棋子？！，但这太贪婪了，放弃了白棋的中央控制，而 c5 上的白棋棋子会很弱，很容易用 e6 或 e5 以及 3...Qxd1+ 交易皇后的想法进行攻击，因此不是最好的棋步。

3. d5 是白方最好也是最受欢迎的走法，像标准的阿尔宾反策略一样推动他们的棋子。 3...Nf6 是最好、最受欢迎的棋步，但是 3...e6 呢？可能会导致黑棋落入致命陷阱（参见下面的陷阱部分）。它走出了黑方的 c5 兵攻击。

3. Nxe4旨在交易典当。 3...cxd4 之后，白方将明白为什么这不优于 3.d5 的原因。它削弱了白方陷阱的潜力，并且在 4.Nf3 Nc6 之后，白方可能无法证明对 e4 棋子有足够的补偿。

陷阱

因为这是一个已接受的镜像阿尔宾反策略，如果在 3.d5、3...e6 之后下棋，白方可能会尝试做一个反向拉斯克陷阱。陷阱是 4. Bb5+ Bd7 5. dxe6!，如果黑方决定用 5...Bxb5?? 交易主教，他们将在 6. exf7+ Ke7 7. fxg8=N+!! 后得到一个令人讨厌的惊喜。和 7...Rxg8？！不可能，因为 8.Bg5+！会刺穿黑王和王后，所以在 7...Ke8 8. Qh5+！白棋对黑棋的国王进行了毁灭性的攻击，并且很可能会用攻击动作压倒黑棋。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. e4/2...dxe4/3. Nc3/3...Bf5
explanations.text:
Blackmar-Diemer Gambit (BDG): Zeller Defense

3. Bf5

Bf5 defends the pawn on e4 and develops the queenside bishop, with intentions of keeping the pawn as it is a thorn to White who can't play Nf3 or Bd3, otherwise the knight/bishop will be taken by the pawn.

Responses

White usually responds with 3. f3?!, which attacks the e4 pawn albeit blocking the development of the knight to f3, which can be rectified after exd3. A rare option that is preferred by computers is g4, kicking the bishop away with the intention of creating a pawn storm with h4 and h5, forcing Black to play defensively.

Other than that, other options can block pieces from developing, get kicked away by pawns, or just do nothing.

Blackmar-Diemer Gambit (BDG): Zeller Defense

3. Bf5

Bf5 defends the pawn on e4 and develops the queenside bishop, with intentions of keeping the pawn as it is a thorn to White who can't play Nf3 or Bd3, otherwise the knight/bishop will be taken by the pawn.

Responses

White usually responds with 3. f3?!, which attacks the e4 pawn albeit blocking the development of the knight to f3, which can be rectified after exd3. A rare option that is preferred by computers is g4, kicking the bishop away with the intention of creating a pawn storm with h4 and h5, forcing Black to play defensively.

Other than that, other options can block pieces from developing, get kicked away by pawns, or just do nothing.
explanations.textZh:
Blackmar-Diemer Gambit (BDG)：泽勒防御

3.Bf5

Bf5在e4上防守棋子并发展了后侧主教，目的是保留该棋子，因为它对不能下Nf3或Bd3的白方来说是一个眼中钉，否则马/主教将被棋子拿走。

回应

白方通常会回应 3. f3?!，它会攻击 e4 兵，尽管会阻止马向 f3 的发展，这可以在 exd3 后纠正。计算机偏爱的一个罕见选项是 g4，将象踢开，意图用 h4 和 h5 制造兵风暴，迫使黑方采取防守策略。

除此之外，其他选项可能会阻止棋子发展，被棋子踢走，或者什么也不做。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. e4/2...dxe4/3. Nc3/3...e5
explanations.text:
Blackmar-Diemer Gambit (BDG): Lemberger Countergambit

3... e5

Black has advanced their pawn to e5 and offers a pawn transfer. If White takes the e5 pawn, then Qxd1 forces White to either give up the right to castle with Kxd1 or undevelop the knight with Nxd1. However, there are better options such as Nxe4, encouraging Black to take d4 with the queen and make a queen trade, or Nge2, declining the countergambit and protecting the d4 pawn.

Traps

The Sneiders attack with Qh5 can lead to a winning position on the 6th move with Nd5?!, with most opponents going Qd7? and blundering Qe5+! and Nxc7!. However, there are players who refute this with a counterattack of their own with Nf6, leading to a queen exchange with both knights capturing the opposing queens.

However, there are better options such as Nxe4, encouraging Black to take d4 with the queen and make a queen trade, or Nge2, declining the countergambit and protecting the d4 pawn.

Traps

The Sneiders attack with Qh5 can lead to a winning position on the 6th move with Nd5?!, with most opponents going Qd7? and blundering Qe5+! and Nxc7!. However, there are players who refute this with a counterattack of their own with Nf6, leading to a queen exchange with both knights capturing the opposing queens.
explanations.textZh:
Blackmar-Diemer 策略 (BDG)：伦伯格反策略

3...e5

黑方已将棋子提升至 e5 并提供棋子转移。如果白方拿走 e5 兵，那么 Qxd1 会迫使白方要么放弃 Kxd1 的城堡权利，要么用 Nxd1 取消马的发育。然而，还有更好的选择，例如 Nxe4，鼓励黑方与皇后一起拿 d4 并进行皇后交易，或 Nge2，拒绝反棋并保护 d4 兵。

陷阱

斯奈德的 Qh5 攻击可以在第 6 手 Nd5 上取得胜利？！，而大多数对手会选择 Qd7？和笨手笨脚的Qe5+！和 Nxc7！。然而，也有玩家用自己的 Nf6 反击反驳了这一点，导致双方骑士都捕获了对方的皇后，从而发生了皇后交换。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. e4/2...dxe4/3. Nc3/3...f5
explanations.text:
3...f5 - Netherlands Variation

Instead of opting for the standard 3...Nf6 or even 3...Bf5, Black chooses to defend their e4 pawn with their f-pawn, an opening named the Netherlands Variation. This is inferior to other ways of defending the pawn as it weakens the kingside and creates a hole on e5.

Responses

White has many possible responses to 3...f5.

4. f3 is the standard Blackmar-Diemer way to continue, attacking the e4 pawn once more and usually looking for 4...exf3 5. Nxf3 where White develops yet another piece, but can be declined by 4...Nf6 defending the e4 pawn once more, this time by the knight. This is White's most popular continuation.

4. Bc4 and 4. Bf4 both develop the bishops, however they do nothing to take advantage of the weakened kingside or put pressure on the e4 pawn. They can both be met easily by the solid 4...Nf6.

4. Bg5 is the best and most aggressive move. It tries to discourage 4...Nf6, and springs a potentially deadly trap to exploit the weakened kingside if Black plays incorrectly. 4...Nf6 would be Black's best move, but 4...h6?? is way more common and falls into the trap: 5. Qh5+!, and 5...g6? isn't possible as the pawn on h7 that would usually guard it is now on h6, so 5...Kd7 is forced, and 6. Bc4+- rolls an attack on Black's king which Black simply can't defend safely.

Traps

The Netherlands Variation with 3...f5 can lead to many traps where White can get a crushing attack after 4. Bg5. The most popular example is 4...h6??, where after 5. Qh5+ Kd7 6. Bc4+- White has a crushing attack on Black's exposed king with the h6 pawn not being able to take the g5 bishop because it is pinned to the h8 rook by the queen on h5. 4...Nf6 is Black's best move after 4. Bg5 but can still fall for a trap after 5. f3 exf3 6. Nxf3. If Black thinks 6...h6? is safe now, 7. Bxf6! exf6 8. Nh4! will prove them wrong, usually leading to 8...Qe7+ 9. Be2+- as Ng6 forking the queen on e7 and the rook on h8 is threatened and 9...Qf7??, the most popular move, loses to 10. Bh5! pinning the lost queen to the king and the White queen on d1 defending the bishop.

explanations.textZh:
3...f5 - 荷兰变体

黑方没有选择标准的 3...Nf6 甚至 3...Bf5，而是选择用 f 棋来保卫 e4 棋子，这种开局称为荷兰变例。这比其他防御兵的方法要差，因为它削弱了王翼并在 e5 上造成了一个洞。

回应

白方对 3...f5 有多种可能的反应。

4. f3 是标准的 Blackmar-Diemer 继续方式，再次攻击 e4 棋子，通常寻找 4...exf3 5. Nxf3，其中白方又发展出另一子，但可以通过 4...Nf6 再次防守 e4 棋子，这次是由骑士拒绝。这是怀特最受欢迎的延续。

4. Bc4和4. Bf4都发展了象，但是他们没有采取任何措施来利用王翼的削弱或对e4兵施加压力。固体 4...Nf6 可以轻松满足它们。

4. Bg5 是最好、最具攻击性的棋步。它试图阻止 4...Nf6，并且如果黑方下棋不正确，就会形成一个潜在的致命陷阱，以利用被削弱的王翼。 4...Nf6 将是黑方的最佳棋步，但是 4...h6？更常见并陷入陷阱：5. Qh5+! 和 5...g6？不可能，因为通常在 h7 上防守的棋子现在在 h6 上，所以 5...Kd7 被迫，并且 6. Bc4+- 对黑方的国王发起攻击，而黑方根本无法安全防御。

陷阱

荷兰变例 3...f5 可能会导致许多陷阱，白方可以在 4.Bg5 之后获得毁灭性的攻击。最流行的例子是 4...h6??，在 5.Qh5+ Kd7 6.Bc4+- 白棋对黑方暴露的王进行毁灭性攻击时，h6 兵无法吃掉 g5 主教，因为它被 h5 上的后被固定在 h8 车上。 4...Nf6 是黑方在 4. Bg5 之后的最佳棋步，但在 5. f3 exf3 6. Nxf3 之后仍然可能落入陷阱。如果黑方认为 6...h6？现在安全了，7.Bxf6！ exf6 8.NH4！将证明他们是错误的，通常会导致 8...Qe7+ 9. Be2+-，因为 Ng6 在 e7 上分叉皇后，而 h8 上的车受到威胁，而 9...Qf7??，最流行的举动，输给了 10. Bh5！将丢失的王后钉在国王身上，白王后则在 d1 上保卫主教。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. e4/2...dxe4/3. Bc4/3...Nc6/4. Qh5
explanations.text:
Blackmar-Diemer Gambit (BDG)

4. Qh5

White threatens to win a queen by checking on f7. Black should play g6 to stop the threat. However, if he, in his hotheaded desire plays Nf6??, Black faces doom with Qxf7+ Kd7 Be6+ Kd6 Bf4+ Ne5 Bxe5+ Kc6 Nc3 Bxe6 Qxe6+ Qd6 Bxd6.

Blackmar-Diemer Gambit (BDG)

explanations.textZh:
布莱克马尔-迪默策略 (BDG)

4.Qh5

白棋威胁要通过检查 f7 来赢得皇后。黑棋应该下g6来阻止威胁。然而，如果他在急躁的欲望中下Nf6??，黑方将面临Qxf7+ Kd7 Be6+ Kd6 Bf4+ Ne5 Bxe5+ Kc6 Nc3 Bxe6 Qxe6+ Qd6 Bxd6 的厄运。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. f4
explanations.text:
2. f4!? - Mason Attack

This dubious attack controls e5 once more, with the f-pawn. The name of the opening is the Mason Attack. Although it is not fully sound, it is playable and White scores quite well after the main line, 2...Nc6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. e3, and White controls lots of the dark squares. However, this slightly weakens the kingside and creates a permanent hole on e5.

Responses

2...Nc6 is the most common move, controlling e5 themselves. However, after 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. e3=, White has good central control and is focused on the critical e5 square.

2...Nf6 is similar to 2...Nc6, but doesn't control e5 unlike 2...Nc6. It is principled and develops a piece which controls the new hole on e4 to try and exploit it.

2...Bf5 is the most accurate move, leading to a slightly better position for Black as it develops the bishop and takes advantage of White's slightly weakened kingside and light squares, looking to exploit the new hole on e4.

Overall, the Mason Attack is a dubious but nonetheless playable attack aggressively looking to control e5 and the dark squares in general.

explanations.textZh:
2.f4！？ - 梅森攻击

这种可疑的攻击再次用 f-pawn 控制了 e5。开局的名称是梅森攻击。虽然它并不完全健全，但它是可玩的，并且白方在主线之后得分相当好，2...Nc6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4. e3，并且白方控制了很多黑暗方块。然而，这稍微削弱了王翼并在 e5 上造成了一个永久性的洞。

回应

2...Nc6 是最常见的动作，控制 e5 本身。然而，在3. Nf3 Nf6 4. e3=之后，白方具有良好的中央控制力，并且专注于关键的e5方格。

2...Nf6 与 2...Nc6 类似，但与 2...Nc6 不同，它不控制 e5。它是有原则的，并开发了一个控制 e4 上新漏洞的组件来尝试利用它。

2...Bf5 是最准确的棋步，为黑方带来了稍微更好的位置，因为黑方发展了象，并利用了白方稍微削弱的王翼和浅方，希望利用 e4 上的新洞。

总的来说，梅森攻击是一种可疑但仍然可以玩的攻击，它积极地寻求控制 e5 和一般的黑暗方格。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. Nf3
explanations.text:
2. Nf3

A flexible developing move. While this move usually leads to a Queen's Gambit, it is also used to go into a Colle System—a solid line that prepares e2-e4 earlier and can be more aggressive than the usual lines.

Black can develop a number of ways, though /2...Nf6/ is most common due to its flexibility.

2.NF3

灵活的发展举措。虽然这一着法通常会导致后弃兵，但它也可用于进入科莱系统（Colle System）——一条更早准备 e2-e4 的实线，并且比通常的线更具攻击性。

黑色可​​以发展多种方式，但 /2...Nf6/ 由于其灵活性而最为常见。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. Nf3/2...Nf6/3. Bf4
explanations.text:
3. Bf4

White is playing the London system, where they plan to support d4 with their e3 pawn and eventually plant their knight on e5, controlled by the e pawn and the dark square bishop. Now that they have developed their bishop, they can play e3 without trapping it behind the pawn chain.

The London system is a system opening, where White has the same general ideas to many Black responses and the specific orders are very flexible. This position can also arise from the Accelerated London 1. d4 d5 2. Bf4 Nf6 where 3. Nf3 transposes.

Black has several approaches to the position, including ...c5 and ...Qb6 to pressure White's b2 pawn, weakened by moving the bishop away.

explanations.textZh:
3、Bf4

白棋正在玩伦敦系统，他们计划用 e3 棋子支持 d4，并最终将他们的马放在 e5 上，由 e 棋子和暗方主教控制。现在他们已经开发出了主教，他们可以玩 e3，而无需将其困在典当链后面。

伦敦体系是一个开放体系，白棋对黑棋的反应大体思路相同，具体的下单非常灵活。这个位置也可以由加速伦敦 1. d4 d5 2. Bf4 Nf6 其中 3. Nf3 转置产生。

黑方有多种方法可以接近该位置，包括 ...c5 和 ...Qb6 来向白方的 b2 棋子施加压力，通过将象移走而削弱白棋的 b2 棋子。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d5/2. g4
explanations.text:
2. g4? · Zürich gambit

Called the Zürich gambit, this very unsound and dubious move gambits the g4 pawn. Moving the g-pawn so early weakens White's kingside and is generally not advised.

Black should take with 2...Bxg4 as it is simply a free pawn. Black simply wins a pawn and White doesn't have much compensation except the hope that the semi-open g-file will one day be useful for attacking Black's kingside. White may continue with 3. Bg2, then Nf3 or h3.

Declining the gambit, e.g. 2...Nc6?!, gives White the chance to defend the pawn with 3. h3 (not 3. f3?? allowing 3...Qh4+!) or they could play 3. Bg2 to insist on gambitting the pawn.

2...c5, as if playing a Queen's gambit with colours reversed, is a natural move. White doesn't want to take 3. dxc5? and give up their space in the centre, but their d- and g-pawns are now both under attack.

History

This move is vanishingly rare in master-level chess and it's unclear to what we owe the name "Zürich gambit", which appears in several online opening books.

This resembles the Grob gambit, 1. g4 d5 where White leaves the g-pawn undefended with 2. Bg2.

In 2018, the Free Internet Chess and Go Server (FICGS) held a thematic tournament where all games began from this position.

explanations.textZh:
2.g4？ · 苏黎世策略

这种非常不合理且可疑的举动被称为“苏黎世策略”，是 g4 棋子的策略。过早移动 g 兵会削弱白方的王翼，一般不建议这样做。

黑方应该拿 2...Bxg4，因为它只是一个自由兵。黑方只是赢得了一颗棋子，而白方没有太多补偿，除了希望半开放的 G 锉有一天能够用于攻击黑方的王翼。白棋可以继续 3.Bg2，然后是 Nf3 或 h3。

拒绝策略，例如2...Nc6？！，让白方有机会用 3.h3（不是 3.f3？？允许 3...Qh4+！）来保卫棋子，或者他们可以玩 3.Bg2 来坚持让棋子下注。

2...c5，就像玩反转颜色的皇后策略一样，是一个自然的举动。白棋不想拿3.dxc5？并放弃中间的空间，但他们的 d 和 g 棋子现在都受到攻击。

历史

这种走法在大师级国际象棋中极为罕见，而且我们还不清楚“苏黎世弃兵”这个名字的由来，这个名字出现在几本在线开局书籍中。

这类似于 Grob 策略，1. g4 d5，其中白方用 2. Bg2 让 g 兵不设防。

2018年，免费互联网国际象棋围棋服务器（FICGS）举办了一场主题锦标赛，所有比赛都从这个位置开始。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...d6
explanations.text:
1...d6

As with many of Black's off-beat 1st move alternatives, this move does not hold independent status as it usually transposes into other mainstream openings. It is certainly not a bad move on Black's part, but it does allow White to transpose into the Pirc or Modern defence by playing 2. e4, so Black must enjoy playing these defences or should shy from this move.

White's options are many. Here are the three most popular:

2. e4, Pirc or Modern transposition.

2. c4, allowing 2... e5! Otherwise, heading for various queen's pawn games (e.g. King's Indian defence).

2. Nf3, keeping the options open while controlling the e5 square.

1...d6

与黑方许多另类的第一手棋替代方案一样，这一手棋并不具有独立地位，因为它通常会转移到其他主流开局中。对于黑棋而言，这当然不是一个坏棋，但它确实允许白棋通过下2.e4转入Pirc或现代防御，因此黑棋必须喜欢玩这些防御，否则应该回避这一棋。

白棋的选择有很多。以下是最受欢迎的三个：

2. e4、Pirc 或现代转调。

2. c4，允许2...e5！否则，前往各种后的典当游戏（例如国王的印度防御）。

2. Nf3，保持选项打开，同时控制e5方块。

The Rat Defence is a solid option for black in the Old Indian. It mainly challenges white’s center and fights for development. White may take the pawn with 3. dxe5.

explanations.text:
Rat Defence

Nc6 is the key move to the Lisbon Gambit. White can greedily capture another pawn with /4. exd6/, but must play accurately.

Rat Defence

Nc6 is the key move to the Lisbon Gambit. White can greedily capture another pawn with /4. exd6/, but must play accurately.

老鼠防御

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...e5
explanations.text:
1...e5?! · Englund gambit

Black offers their e-pawn. The Englund gambit is considered unsound: against best play, Black will not get enough compensation for the pawn. It is therefore rare in tournament chess, but it is not uncommon in amateur games where Black wants an open, tactical game with sharp traps and practical chances.

2. dxe5 to accept the gambit capitalises on Black's dubious move. White challenges Black to find compensation. The main line continues with 2...Nc6 3. Nf3 Qe7 4. Bf4, and Black invites White to blunder with the manoeuvre ...Qb4+ &...Qxb2, but if White plays carefully this is toothless. 2...d6, letting the pawn go in return for an open centre and development, is the main side line.

Declining the gambit gives an even game. White can allow Black to take on d4―2. e3!? exd4 (the reversed French), 2. c4?! exd4, etc.―and open the position, or push the pawn 2. d5!? to keep the position closed.

2. Nf3!?, the reversed Alekhine, allows 2...e5 to kick the knight. 2. e4 transposes into the centre game (1. e4 e5 2. d4).

explanations.textZh:
1...e5？！ · 英格兰策略

黑方提供了电子棋子。英格兰的策略被认为是不合理的：相对于最佳策略，黑棋将无法获得足够的棋子补偿。因此，这种情况在锦标赛国际象棋中很少见，但在业余比赛中并不罕见，黑方希望进行一场开放的、具有尖锐陷阱和实际机会的战术比赛。

2. dxe5 接受了黑方可疑棋步的策略。白方挑战黑方寻求补偿。主线以 2...Nc6 3. Nf3 Qe7 4. Bf4 继续，黑方邀请白方因 ...Qb4+ &...Qxb2 策略而犯错误，但如果白方谨慎行事，这将是无牙的。 2...d6，放走棋子以换取开放的中心和发展，是主要的边线。

拒绝策略会带来一场势均力敌的比赛。白棋可以让黑棋吃 d4―2。 e3！？ exd4（反向法语），2.c4？！ exd4等——然后开仓，或者推兵2.d5！？保持平仓。

2. Nf3!?，反转的阿廖欣，允许 2...e5 踢骑士。 2. e4 转置到中心游戏（1. e4 e5 2. d4）。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...e5/2. d5
explanations.text:
2. d5? · Englund gambit declined

White avoids ...exd4 by pushing their pawn to d5. This is a mistake only in that it does not punish Black for their mistake. The Englund gambit is bad for Black, but if White does not know the refutation they may choose this line to avoid complications.
explanations.textEn:

explanations.textZh:
2.d5？ · 英格兰的策略被拒绝

白方通过将棋子推至 d5 来避免 ...exd4。这是一个错误，只是因为它没有惩罚黑方的错误。英格兰的策略对黑方不利，但如果白方不知道反驳，他们可能会选择这条路线以避免复杂化。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...e5/2. dxe5
explanations.text:
2. dxe5 · Englund gambit accepted

White captures the free pawn. This is theoretically the best variation for White. Black can try several approaches to entrap White:

2...Nc6 is the main line. Black starts efforts to recover the pawn. After 3. Nf3 Qe7 White can let Black have it back (4. Nc3 Nxe5 5. Bf4 Nxf3+ 6. gxf3 d6 7. e4) for a lead in development and space. More common is 3. Bf4 and Black swings over to take the b-pawn: 4...Qb4+ 5. Bd2 Qxb2. So long as White avoids a couple of traps (6. Bc3?? is fatal, as is 6. Nc3 Nb4 7. Rb1??) White comes out ahead in position.

2...d6, the Hartlaub-Charlick gambit, is the main alternative. Rather than recover the pawn, Black lets White keep it in exchange for development, e.g. 3. exd6 Bxd6 4. Nf3 Nc6 5. Nc3 Bg4: White should be ahead, but shouldn't take their eye off the ball (e.g. 6. e4 Qe7 7. Be2? O-O-O 8. O-O? Bxf3 9. Bxf3 Bxh2+! 10. Kxh2 Rxd1.

2...Bc5 goes into the Derek Wu trap: a trap for online blitz or bullet where Black pretends to blunder a premove.

explanations.textZh:
2. dxe5·接受英格兰策略

白棋吃掉了自由棋子。理论上这是白棋的最佳变体。黑方可以尝试多种方法来诱捕白方：

2...Nc6为主线。黑方开始努力收回棋子。 3. Nf3 Qe7 之后，白棋可以让黑棋夺回（4. Nc3 Nxe5 5. Bf4 Nxf3+ 6. gxf3 d6 7. e4），以获得领先的发展和空间。更常见的是 3. Bf4 和黑方挥动以获取 b-兵：4...Qb4+ 5. Bd2 Qxb2。只要白棋避开了几个陷阱（6. Bc3?? 是致命的，6. Nc3 Nb4 7. Rb1?? 也是致命的），白棋就处于领先位置。

2...d6，Hartlaub-Charlick 策略，是主要的选择。黑方没有收回棋子，而是让白方保留它以换取发展，例如3. exd6 Bxd6 4. Nf3 Nc6 5. Nc3 Bg4：白方应该领先，但不应将注意力从球上移开（例如 6. e4 Qe7 7. Be2？ O-O-O 8. O-O？ Bxf3 9. Bxf3 Bxh2+！ 10. Kxh2 Rxd1。

2...Bc5 进入 Derek Wu 陷阱：在线闪电战或子弹的陷阱，黑方假装在前步中犯了错误。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...e5/2. dxe5/2...d6
explanations.text:
2...d6 · Blackburne-Hartlaub gambit

Black argues that by play 2...d6 and gambiting the pawn, they will have enough compensation because of their earlier kingside development and open centre. However, if White plays carefully, they will be ahead throughout the game because of their central pawn on e2. This doesn't mean, though, that Black shouldn't play this gambit. If White isn't careful, Black can gain an extraordinary kingside attack because of Black's extra tempo in development.

Main Ideas

Black hopes to play a systematic move order ...Nf6, ...Nc6, ...Bg4, ...Qe7, ...O-O-O, and ...Rhe8. These moves maximize the potential of each piece in this gambit. If White isn't careful, Black can have chances for a Greek gift sacrifice. ...O-O can also be played at any time, especially in early Bg5 lines.

History

The first recorded case of the Blackburne-Hartlaub gambit being played was in the early 1890's by Henry Charlick. Charlick's idea was to meet 2. dxe5 with the gambit 2...d6 "with the object of preventing White from playing a close game. In 1998, Claude F. Bloodgood published the book Blackburne-Hartlaub Gambit. Within it, Bloodgood presents opening theory for the Blackburne-Hartlaub gambit he compiled throughout his prison sentence. It is one of the main openings he used to become the second-highest rated US Chess player in history by 1997.

explanations.textZh:
2...d6 · 布莱克本-哈特劳布策略

黑方认为，通过走 2...d6 并下棋，他们将获得足够的补偿，因为他们早期的王翼发展和开放中心。然而，如果白棋谨慎行事，他们将在整个游戏中领先，因为他们的中心棋子在 e2 上。但这并不意味着黑棋不应该玩这种策略。如果白棋不小心，黑棋可以因为黑棋的额外节奏而获得非凡的王侧攻击。

主要思想

黑方希望下一个系统的走棋顺序...Nf6、...Nc6、...Bg4、...Qe7、...O-O-O 和...Rhe8。这些动作最大限度地发挥了这一策略中每个棋子的潜力。如果白方不小心，黑方可能有机会牺牲希腊礼物。 ...O-O 也可以随时播放，尤其是在早期的 Bg5 线路中。

历史

第一个有记录的布莱克本-哈特劳布策略是在 1890 年代初由亨利·查理克 (Henry Charlick) 进行的。查理克的想法是用开局 2...d6 与 2.dxe5 会面，目的是阻止白方打出势均力敌的棋局。1998 年，克劳德·F·布拉德古德 (Claude F. Bloodgood) 出版了《布莱克本-哈特劳布弃兵》一书。在书中，布拉德古德提出了他在服刑期间编写的布莱克本-哈特劳布弃兵策略的开局理论。这是他用来成为美国排名第二的主要开局之一。 1997年成为历史上的国际象棋棋手。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...e5/2. dxe5/2...f6
explanations.text:
Soller Gambit

Black offers a second pawn with 2...f6. Although it looks like a weakening move, White must be careful to avoid falling into potential traps.

White can capture the pawn with 3. exf6, but Black gains a lead in development in exchange after re-capturing with the knight.

Alternatively, White can give back the pawn by playing 3. e4. Note that Black cannot immediately capture the e5 pawn as 3...fxe5?? loses to 4. Qh5+.
explanations.textEn:
Soller Gambit

Black offers a second pawn with 2...f6. Although it looks like a weakening move, White must be careful to avoid falling into potential traps.

White can capture the pawn with 3. exf6, but Black gains a lead in development in exchange after re-capturing with the knight.

explanations.textZh:
索勒策略

黑方提供第二个棋子 2...f6。虽然这看起来像是一个削弱棋子，但白棋必须小心，以免落入潜在的陷阱。

白棋可以用 3. exf6 吃掉棋子，但黑棋在重新吃掉马后，获得了发展领先优势。

或者，白方可以通过下 3. e4 归还棋子。请注意，黑方无法立即吃掉 e5 兵，因为 3...fxe5??输给4.Qh5+。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...e5/2. dxe5/2...f6/3. exf6
explanations.text:
Soller Gambit Accepted

Taking the pawn is a slight inaccuracy and not recommended, as it plays into Black's gameplan and allows them to easily develop their knight. White still has the advantage, though they must be careful not to fall for any of Black's traps. Black could continue by developing their bishop to c5, threatening the f7 pawn and laying down a nasty trap. After 4. Bg5 Bc5 5. Nf3 Ne4!!, it looks like Black blundered their queen, but 6. Bxd8?? results in White getting checkmated by Bxf2#

接受索勒策略

拿走棋子有点不准确，不推荐，因为它符合黑方的游戏计划，让他们可以轻松地发展他们的马。白方仍然具有优势，但他们必须小心不要落入黑方的任何陷阱。黑方可以继续将象发展到 c5，威胁 f7 兵并设置一个令人讨厌的陷阱。在4. Bg5 Bc5 5. Nf3 Ne4!!之后，看起来黑方犯了大错，但是6. Bxd8??结果白方被 Bxf2 将死#

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...e5/2. dxe5/2...Bc5
explanations.text:
2...Bc5 · (towards the) Derek Wu trap

Black develops the bishop to pressure f2.

This usually leads to the Derek Wu trap, where Black pretends to blunder a pre-move (it therefore is best kept for online blitz or bullet), where, after 3. Nf3 Black plays 3...d6 and premoves 4. Ne7: so after 3...d6 4. exd6 Ne7? White is lulled into a false sense of security. However the obvious move 5. dxe7?? blunders 5...Bxf2+! deflecting White's king from defence of the queen.

Otherwise, the game can continue 3. Nf3 Nc6 and transpose into the Felbecker Gambit (usually reached after 2...Nc6 3. Nf3 Bc5).

3. Nc3, another natural developing move, also acts to defang the trap by adding another defender to the queen.

History

The trap was developed by Derek Wu. The Chess.com opening book refers to the trap from 6...Qxd1 as the Rosen trap, after IM Eric Rosen who popularised it.

explanations.textZh:
2...Bc5·（朝向）Derek Wu 陷阱

黑方发展象向f2施压。

这通常会导致德里克·吴陷阱，其中黑方假装犯了一个预走棋（因此最好保留在线闪电战或子弹），其中，在 3. Nf3 之后，黑方下 3...d6 并预走 4. Ne7：那么在 3...d6 4. exd6 Ne7 之后？怀特陷入了一种虚假的安全感。然而明显的举动5.dxe7??失误 5...Bxf2+！使白棋国王不再保护王后。

否则，游戏可以继续 3. Nf3 Nc6 并转入 Felbecker Gambit（通常在 2...Nc6 3. Nf3 Bc5 之后到达）。

3. Nc3，另一个自然发展的动作，也可以通过在皇后后添加另一名防守者来解除陷阱。

历史

该陷阱是由德里克·吴（Derek Wu）开发的。 Chess.com 的开篇书籍将 6...Qxd1 中的陷阱称为罗森陷阱，以推广该陷阱的 IM Eric Rosen 命名。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...e5/2. e3
explanations.text:
Englund Gambit Declined: Reversed French

White declines the gambit by supporting the pawn. This position looks similar to the French defense, as the name suggests. The winrate according to the lichess database is: 50% win rate to 47% loss rate, and a 3% draw rate.

英格伦德策略被拒绝：相反的法语

白方通过支持棋子来拒绝这一策略。顾名思义，这个位置看起来与法国防守相似。根据lichess数据库的胜率是：胜率为50%，败率为47%，平局率为3%。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...e5/2. Nf3
explanations.text:
2. Nf3 - Reversed Alekhine

This move may seem like a good response, and also is similar to Alekhine defense but from white side. However black can just push the pawn further and force the knight to move (if you don't want to lose it of course).

Black's responses:

2... e4 - 45%; winrate 47% (w) - 50% (b)

2...exd4 - 35%; winrate 50% (w) - 47% (b)

2. Nf3 - 逆阿廖欣

这一举动似乎是一个很好的回应，也类似于阿廖欣的防守，但来自白方。然而，黑色可以将棋子推得更远并迫使马移动（当然如果你不想失去它）。

黑方的回应：

2...e4 - 45%；胜率 47% (w) - 50% (b)

2...exd4 - 35%；胜率 50% (w) - 47% (b)

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...e4
explanations.text:
2... e4 - Reversed Krebs

Of course black pushes further, forcing white to lose tempo and move the knight. White has a few responses to this:

White's responses:

Nfd2 - 61%; winrate 48% (w) - 49% (b)

Ne5 - 16%; winrate 45% - 53% - Reversed Mokele Mbembe

Ng1 - 16%; winrate 49% - 48% - Reversed Brooklyn

2... e4 - 反向克雷布斯
