白的回应：

Nfd2 - 61%；胜率 48% (w) - 49% (b)

Ne5 - 16%；胜率 45% - 53% - 逆转摩克拉·姆贝贝

NG1 - 16%；胜率 49% - 48% - 逆转布鲁克林

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...e4/3. Nfd2
explanations.text: This is the only move that makes sense. You seem to retreat the knight to a safe place and also attack undefended pawn in hope to develop normally. But black has an interesting response - e3 (!?) - they sacrifice their semi-isolated pawn for good. It's forced to either take it or move the knight once again. But every one of them is bad - if you take it you think you just got a free material (even chess engines don't like it), but in exchange you ruin your kingside, your pawn structure,open your king for attacks and block your center pawn. If you move your knight, black just takes pawn on f2 and then you're unable to castle anymore.

explanations.textZh: 这是唯一有意义的举动。你似乎将马撤退到安全的地方，并攻击不设防的棋子，希望能够正常发展。但黑棋有一个有趣的反应 - e3（！？） - 他们永远牺牲了半孤立的棋子。它被迫要么接受它，要么再次移动骑士。但它们中的每一个都很糟糕 - 如果你接受它，你会认为你只是得到了一个免费的材料（即使是国际象棋引擎也不喜欢它），但作为交换，你破坏了你的王翼，你的棋子结构，打开你的国王进行攻击并阻止你的中心棋子。如果你移动你的马，黑方只会在 f2 上吃兵，然后你就无法再城堡了。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...e4/3. Ne5
explanations.text:
3. Ne5 (?!) - Reversed Mokele Mbembe

White hops the knight into opponent's territory, which is not a good move, of course. It is easily kickable, which only helps black to develop pieces and makes position worse for white because they lose more and more tempo.

explanations.textZh:
3. Ne5 (?!) - 逆转摩克拉·姆贝贝

白棋将马跳入对手的领土，这当然不是一个好棋。它很容易被踢，这只会帮助黑棋发展棋子，并使白棋的位置变得更糟，因为他们失去越来越多的节奏。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...e4/3. Ng1
explanations.text:
3. Ng1

Due to the lack of good options, White decides to retreat the knight, losing tempo. This shows that playing Nf3 earlier was a mistake. Black will play /4...d5/ to solidify their control of the center.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...e6
explanations.text:
1...e6 · Horwitz defence

1...e6 is the Horwitz defence. Black plays something less committal without showing their hand, and waits to see how White wants to approach the game. This can transpose into a myriad of different openings.

Uniquely, this is an invitation for White to transpose into a French defence with 2. e4.

2. c4 is the most common reply, where White keeps the game in Queen's pawn territory. Black can then transpose into a Dutch defence with 2...f5, an Indian defence with 2...Nf6, or a Queen's gambit declined with 2...d5. 2...Bb4+ is known as the Keres or Kangaroo defence.

Otherwise, White can play almost anything at this point: 2. Nf3 and 3. e3 if White is a Colle system player, 2. Bf4 should they happen to be a London player, 2. Nc3 and 3. Bf4 if they are a Jobava London player, etc, then Black transposes into their preferred line against these moves.

History

The Horwitz defence is named for Bernhard Horwitz, a "star" chess player of the group known as the Berlin Pleiades, who played it several times against Daniel Harrwitz in their 15-game match in Brighton, 1849.

1...e6 had earlier been tried by Howard Staunton in his 1843 match series against the strongest French player of the time Saint-Amant, though presumably the world collectively decided that enough things had been named after Staunton by that point. Staunton played it five times, and each game transposed into a Queen's gambit declined with 2. c4 d5. Though 1...e6 didn't bring Staunton much success, he won the match overall and became something of an unofficial World Champion.

1...e6 is also called the Franco-Indian Defence.

explanations.textZh:
1...e6 · 霍维茨防守

1...e6 是霍维茨防守。黑方在不亮牌的情况下采取了一些不那么坚定的做法，并等待着看白方想如何处理比赛。这可以转换成无数不同的空缺。

独特的是，这是对白方的邀请，用 2. e4 转入法国防守。

2. c4 是最常见的答复，白方将棋局保持在后方兵的领土上。然后黑方可以将其转换为荷兰防御 2...f5、印度防御 2...Nf6 或后弃兵策略 2...d5。 2...Bb4+ 被称为 Keres 或袋鼠防御。

否则，白棋此时几乎可以下任何棋：如果白棋是科莱系统棋手，则 2. Nf3 和 3. e3；如果他们碰巧是伦敦棋手，则 2. Bf4；如果他们是 Jobava 伦敦棋手，则 2. Nc3 和 3. Bf4，等等，然后黑棋转入他们针对这些棋步的首选路线。

历史

霍维茨防御以伯恩哈德·霍维茨 (Bernhard Horwitz) 的名字命名，他是柏林昴宿星队的“明星”国际象棋棋手，1849 年在布莱顿举行的 15 场比赛中，他与丹尼尔·哈维茨 (Daniel Harrwitz) 多次使用这种防守。

1...e6 早些时候曾由霍华德·斯汤顿 (Howard Staunton) 在 1843 年的系列赛中尝试过，对手是当时最强的法国选手圣阿芒 (Saint-Amant)，尽管当时全世界都一致认为，当时已经有足够多的东西以斯汤顿的名字命名了。斯汤顿玩了五次，每局都转换成皇后弃兵，以 2. c4 d5 下降。尽管 1...e6 并没有给斯汤顿带来太大的成功，但他赢得了整场比赛并成为了一位非官方的世界冠军。

1...e6 也称为法印防御。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...e6/2. c4
explanations.text:
Queen's Pawn Opening

2. c4

White keeps the game in the realm of Queen pawn openings with this move. Most responses (like 2...Nf6 or 2...f5) transpose to other openings.

A unique opening order is 2...Bb4+, the Keres Defense. This is usually also a transpositional tool, usually transposing into the Bogo-Indian Defense after 3.Bd2. However, even 3. Nc3 (then transposing into the Nimzo-Indian Defense) or 3. Nd2 (a unique order, but can transpose into the Bogo-Indian Defense) are both playable.

皇后典当开局

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...e6/2. c4/2...b6
explanations.text:
English Defence

The system of having b6 and e6 was developed by English player P.N. Wallis, and was taken up by several leading English players including Tony Miles and Jon Speelman.
explanations.textEn:
English Defence

explanations.textZh:
英语防守

有b6和e6的系统是由英国选手P.N.开发的。沃利斯（Wallis），并被托尼·迈尔斯（Tony Miles）和乔恩·斯皮尔曼（Jon Speelman）等几位领先的英国球员所采用。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...e6/2. c4/2...Bb4
explanations.text:
Keres Defence

The Keres Defence is a chess opening that begins with the moves 1. d4 e6 2. c4 Bb4+. It is also known as the Kangaroo Defence or Franco-Indian Defence. The opening is named after Estonian grandmaster Paul Keres.

After the opening moves, White has several options to respond, including 3. Bd2, 3. Nd2, and 3. Nc3. If white plays 3. Nc3, the game might transpose into a Nimzo-Indian Defence or a Bogo-Indian Defence.

The standard reply today is 3. Bd2. Black can continue with 3...Bxd2+ into a line of the Bogo-Indian, and 3...a5 will also usually transpose to a Bogo-Indian when White plays Nf3. Alternatively, Black can allow White to play e4: 3...Qe7 4.e4 d5.

1. d4 e6 2. c4 Bb4+

explanations.textZh:
凯雷斯防御

凯雷斯防御是一种国际象棋开局，以 1. d4 e6 2. c4 Bb4+ 动作开始。它也被称为袋鼠防御或法印防御。开幕式以爱沙尼亚大师保罗·凯雷斯（Paul Keres）的名字命名。

开局后，白方有多种应对选择，包括 3. Bd2、3. Nd2 和 3. Nc3。如果白方下 3.Nc3，游戏可能会转变为尼姆佐-印度防御或博戈-印度防御。

今天的标准回复是3.Bd2。黑棋可以继续用 3...Bxd2+ 进入 Bogo-Indian 线，并且当白方下 Nf3 时，3...a5 通常也会转换为 Bogo-Indian。或者，黑方可以允许白方下 e4: 3...Qe7 4.e4 d5。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...f5
explanations.text:
1...f5 · Dutch defence

This is the Dutch defence, the fourth most common way to meet 1. d4. Black controls the central e4 square with their flank f-pawn.

Because it does not develop or prepare to develop a piece (cf. 1...Nf6 and 1...d5 respectively), 1...f5 is less popular than Black's other options to control e4. In addition, moving the f-pawn so early, before Black has castled, is not for the faint of heart because it weakens Black's kingside. An illustration of this is the classic beginner's trap in the Hopton attack: 2. Bg5 h6 3. Bh4 g5 3. Bg3 f4 (thinking to trap the bishop) 4. e3 fxg3?? 5. Qh5#.

However, the Dutch is very combative, with an original character compared to other 1. d4 openings. Black intends to get maximum value out of a kingside attack.

White's main approach against the Dutch is a set-up with Bg2, Nf3, short castling, and c4 by one of a number of move orders. 2. g3 is the main move, though 2. c4 or 2. Nf3 are also common and usually transpose.

Black chooses between two plans for their kingside bishop: either to fianchetto it with ...g6 and ...Bg7, called the called the Leningrad Dutch, e.g. 2. c4 Nf6 3. g3 g6 4. Bg2 Bg7; or ...e6 and ...Be7, where they may then choose either ...d6, the classical variation, or an early ...d5 to clamp down on e4, called the stonewall variation, e.g. in the move order 2. c4 Nf6 3. g3 e6 4. Bg2 Be7 5. Nf3 O-O 6. O-O d5.

If 2. e4?! anyway, the Staunton gambit, Black should be very happy to trade their flank pawn for the more valuable central pawn, 2...fxe5. The Staunton gambit makes sense conceptually―Black has weakened their kingside and slowed down their development, therefore White should open the centre and attack―but while there are many traps available to White involving the weakened e8-h5 diagonal, against best play White is no better than equal.

Other sidelines include:

2. Bg5, the Hopton attack. If White can't play e4, then they want to ensure the bishop is developed before playing e3. If Black plays 2...Nf6 then White is happy to trade their bishop for it and double Black's pawns. Black can expand on the kingside with tempo against White's bishop, 2...h6 3. Bh4 g5 4. Bg3, so long as they avoid the famous trap (above), or leave the bishop there for now and play 2...g6, ...Bg7 etc.

2. Nc3, the Raphael variation. From c3 the knight may help support playing e4 and opening the centre, (e.g. 2...Nf6 (controls e4) 3. Bg5 e6?! 4. e4 fxe4 5. Nxe4, where 5...h6?? is a rookie error) but usually they games involve Bg5 and e3 as in the Hopton attack, e.g. 2...Nf6 3. Bg5 d5 (to control e4) 4. Bxf6 exf6 5. e3 intending Bd3.

2. g4?!, the Krejcik gambit, looks to deflect the f5 pawn from control of e4. However, after 2...fxg4 and ...d5 (defending g4 with the queen's bishop), White will have trouble recapturing the bothersome pawn and find they can't make much of e4 anyway.

2. f3 is an uncommon sideline aiming for a central push with e4. Sometimes, White gambits a pawn on e4 for quick development and lines. The position is relatively equal after 2...d5 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5=.

/2. Nh3/ is a rare yet sound sideline where White develops the knight to the rim, usually with the intention of the Blackburne variation, after 2...Nf6 3. g3 e6 4. Bg2.

/2. Qd3/, the Alapin variation, aggressively develops the queen and attacks the pawn on f5.

History

Dutch chess master Elias Stein recommended the move 1...f5 in his 1789 Nouvel essai sur le jeu des échecs (French: New essay on the game of chess) as an alternative to avoid the queen's gambit, 1. d4 d5 2. c4.

In the 19th and early 20th centuries, 2. e4?!, the Staunton gambit, was considered critical. In 1931, Tarrasch gave the line 2. e4 fxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 c6 5. f3! exf3, with White being better.

Though it was never the main line, the Dutch received renewed interest in the 20th century, especially with reappraisal of 2. e4?!. Its most significant outing was in the 1951 World Chess Championship, where it was adopted by Mikhail Botvinnik

explanations.textZh:
1...f5 · 荷兰防守

这是荷兰队防守中第四种最常见的应对方式 1. d4。黑方用侧翼 f 兵控制中央 e4 方格。

因为它不发展或准备发展棋子（分别参见 1...Nf6 和 1...d5），1...f5 不如黑方控制 e4 的其他选项受欢迎。此外，在黑方尚未出局之前过早移动f兵并不适合胆小的人，因为这会削弱黑方的王翼。霍普顿攻击中经典的初学者陷阱就是一个例子： 2. Bg5 h6 3. Bh4 g5 3. Bg3 f4（想陷阱主教） 4. e3 fxg3?? 5.Qh5#。

然而，荷兰人非常好斗，与其他 1.d4 空位相比，具有原创性。黑方打算从王翼进攻中获得最大价值。

白棋对抗荷兰人的主要方法是通过一系列移动指令之一使用 Bg2、Nf3、短易位和 c4 进行设置。 2. g3 是主要动作，但 2. c4 或 2. Nf3 也很常见并且通常是转置。

黑棋在王翼主教的两个计划之间进行选择：要么用...g6和...Bg7进行fianchetto，称为列宁格勒荷兰人，例如2. c4 Nf6 3. g3 g6 4. Bg2 Bg7;或者 ...e6 和 ...Be7，然后他们可以选择 ...d6（经典变体）或早期 ...d5 来压制 e4，称为石墙变体，例如移动顺序为 2. c4 Nf6 3. g3 e6 4. Bg2 Be7 5. Nf3 O-O 6. O-O d5。

如果2.e4？！无论如何，在斯汤顿策略中，黑方应该很乐意将侧翼棋子换成更有价值的中央棋子 2...fxe5。斯汤顿策略在概念上是有道理的——黑棋削弱了他们的王翼并减慢了他们的发展，因此白棋应该打开中心并进攻——但是，尽管白棋有很多陷阱可以利用，涉及削弱的e8-h5对角线，但在对抗最好的比赛时，白棋并不比对手更好。

其他副业包括：

2. Bg5，霍普顿攻击。如果白方不能打 e4，那么他们想确保在打 e3 之前已经开发出象。如果黑棋下 2...Nf6，那么白棋很乐意用他们的象来换取它，并将黑棋的棋子加倍。黑方可以在王翼扩大对抗白方主教的节奏，2...h6 3. Bh4 g5 4. Bg3，只要他们避免著名的陷阱（上图），或者暂时将主教留在那里并玩 2...g6，...Bg7 等。

2. Nc3，拉斐尔变奏。从c3开始，骑士可能会帮助支持玩e4并打开中心，（例如2...Nf6（控制e4）3.Bg5 e6？！4.e4 fxe4 5.Nxe4，其中5...h6??是菜鸟错误），但通常他们的游戏涉及Bg5和e3，如Hopton攻击中，例如2...Nf6 3. Bg5 d5（控制 e4） 4. Bxf6 exf6 5. e3 意为 Bd3。

2. g4?!，Krejcik 策略，旨在使 f5 棋子脱离 e4 的控制。然而，在 2...fxg4 和 ...d5（用后王的主教保卫 g4）之后，白方将很难重新捕获麻烦的棋子，并发现他们无论如何也无法充分利用 e4。

2. f3是一种不常见的边线，旨在与e4进行中推。有时，白方会在 e4 上下棋以实现快速发展和线路。 2...d5 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5= 之后位置相对相等。

/2。 Nh3/ 是一种罕见但健全的边线，白方将骑士发展到篮筐，通常是出于布莱克本变体的意图，在 2...Nf6 3. g3 e6 4. Bg2 之后。

/2。 Qd3/，Alapin 变体，积极发展皇后并攻击 f5 上的棋子。

历史

荷兰国际象棋大师 Elias Stein 在其 1789 年的 Nouvel essai sur le jeu des échecs（法语：关于国际象棋游戏的新论文）中推荐了 1...f5 棋法，作为避免后棋的替代方法，1. d4 d5 2. c4。

在 19 世纪和 20 世纪初，斯汤顿策略 2. e4?! 被认为是至关重要的。 1931 年，Tarrasch 给出了这行代码 2. e4 fxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5 c6 5. f3！ exf3，白棋更好。

尽管它从来都不是主线，但荷兰人对 20 世纪重新产生了兴趣，尤其是对 2. e4?! 的重新评价。它最重要的亮相是 1951 年世界国际象棋锦标赛，并被米哈伊尔·鲍特维尼克 (Mikhail Botvinnik) 采用

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...f5/2. Nc3
explanations.text:
2. Nc3 - Raphael Variation

The Raphael Variation, characterized by 2. Nc3, aims to control e4, the square Dutch players want to control. Although this is a sideline, it is principled as it develops a piece and controls a key central square.

Responses

2...Nf6 is the best and most popular move, reinforcing e4 with the knight. It generally leads to 3. Bg5, usually followed by e3 as in the Hopton Attack. However, Black still has to be careful of White's aggressive setup as traps can arise (see Traps section below).

2...e6 and 2...g6 give up trying to defend e4 and instead choose to go for a standard Dutch Stonewall or Leningrad setup, sometimes delaying Nf6.

2...d5 greedily reinforces e4 with a pawn. It is the third most common move but creates a permanent hole on e5 that can be exploited with the simple 3. Bf4. However, Black especially has to be careful of the Kingfisher Gambit with 3. e4!?, setting up deadly traps (see Traps section below).

Traps

The Raphael is home to many traps. One such "trap" comes after 2...Nf6 3. Bg5, where 3...h6? is played kicking the bishop away, but after 4. Bxf6! exf6 5. e4± White has a great center attacking the f5 pawn and Black has a demolished and awful pawn structure. An even more poisonous trap comes out of the greedy 2...d5. White can then play 3. e4!?, the dubious Kingfisher Gambit. 3...dxe4 transposes to the Netherlands Variation of the Blackmar-Diemer Gambit (BDG) and Black has to avoid a minefield of traps after 4. Bg5 (e.g. 4...h6?? 5. Qh5+! Kd7 6. Bc4+- with a crushing attack on Black's king) and 4...fxe4?, the more common capture, leads to 5. Qh5+! g6 6. Qxd5! where White wins back the pawn with a way better position. Then Black should play 6...Nf6 kicking the White queen away leading to a better position for white after 7. Qb3±, but more popular is 6...Qxd5? leading to 7. Nxd5+- with Nxc7+ forking king and rook is threatened, forcing 7...Kd8 or 7...Kd7 (7...Na6? 8. Bxa6! wins the knight as the defender of c7 is removed, and 8...bxa6 would allow 9. Nxc7+).

explanations.textZh:
2. Nc3 - 拉斐尔变奏

拉斐尔变例，特点是2.Nc3，目标是控制荷兰玩家想要控制的e4。虽然这是副线，但也是有原则的，因为它发展了一块，控制了一个关键的中心方格。

回应

2...Nf6 是最好、最受欢迎的招式，用马加强 e4。它通常导致 3. Bg5，通常后面是 e3，如霍普顿攻击中那样。然而，黑方仍然必须小心白方的激进布局，因为陷阱可能会出现（参见下面的陷阱部分）。

2...e6 和 2...g6 放弃尝试防守 e4，转而选择标准的荷兰石墙或列宁格勒设置，有时会延迟 Nf6。

2...d5 用棋子贪婪地强化 e4。这是第三个最常见的举动，但在 e5 上造成了一个永久性的漏洞，可以通过简单的 3. Bf4 来利用。然而，黑方必须特别小心 3. e4!? 的翠鸟弃兵，设置致命的陷阱（参见下面的陷阱部分）。

陷阱

拉斐尔河上有许多陷阱。一个这样的“陷阱”出现在 2...Nf6 3. Bg5 之后，哪里是 3...h6？是踢掉主教，但在 4. Bxf6！ exf6 5. e4± 白方有一个出色的中锋攻击 f5 兵，而黑方则有一个被破坏且糟糕的兵结构。贪婪的 2...d5 中出现了一个更有毒的陷阱。然后白棋可以下 3. e4!?，可疑的翠鸟弃兵。 3...dxe4 转换为 Blackmar-Diemer 开局 (BDG) 的荷兰变体，黑方必须在 4. Bg5 之后避开陷阱雷区（例如 4...h6?? 5. Qh5+! Kd7 6. Bc4+- 对黑方国王进行毁灭性攻击）和 4...fxe4?（更常见的捕获）导致 5. Qh5+！ g6 6.Qxd5！白方以更好的位置赢回棋子。那么黑棋应该下6...Nf6，将白后踢开，从而在7.Qb3±之后为白棋带来更好的位置，但更受欢迎的是6...Qxd5？导致 7. Nxd5+- 与 Nxc7+ 分叉国王和车受到威胁，迫使 7...Kd8 或 7...Kd7 （7...Na6？8. Bxa6！赢得骑士，因为 c7 的防守者被移除，并且 8...bxa6 将允许 9. Nxc7+）。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...f5/2. Bg5
explanations.text:
2. Bg5 · Hopton attack

White develops the Bishop so as to hinder Black's development. The bishop pins Black's e-pawn, and in the event of ...Nf6 White will be happy to trade the bishop for the knight and upset Black's pawn structure.

Therefore Black usually postpones the development of their knight and chooses whether they wish to fianchetto or to drive the bishop off first.

2...h6 kicks the bishop. 3. Bh4 g5, and though it may appear that Black will trap White's bishop with ...f4, in fact White lays a sly trap of their own: 4. Bg3 f4? 5. e3! fxg3?? 6. Qh5#. The main move is 4. e3 (where 4...gxh4?? 5. Qh5# also) Nf6 (now guarding h5) 5. Bg3 Bg7. Black has been able to develop their knight and bishop successfully and avoided doubled f-pawns, but the expansion of their kingside pawns is weakening. h4 is a plan for White, eliciting ...g5 and playing on the dark squares.

2...g6 is a straightforward alternative: Black wishes to avoid doubled f-pawns by playing ...Bg7 before ...Nf6, so they may recapture with the bishop instead. Unlike after 2. c4 g6, even though Black has postponed developing their knight they need not worry about the sharp h4 & h5 manoeuvre as 3. h4? h6! comes with tempo on the bishop.

If 2...Nf6 3. Bxf6 and Black must take back with the e-pawn else weaken the e8-h5 diagonal further. 3...gxf6? (following the "rule" to take back towards the centre) 4. e4! fxe4?? 5. Qh5# occurs more often in amateur games than you might imagine.

History

An 1860 game in this line is attributed to an "R. Hopton", which continued 2...h6 3. Bh4 c5 4. e3 Qb6 5. b3 Nf6 6. dxc5? Qb4+ (winning the bishop by a fork), White resigns. Otherwise, this line has been known simply as the "queen bishop attack".

Garry Kasparov favoured this line against the Dutch defence.

explanations.textZh:
2. Bg5·霍普顿攻击

白方发展象，以阻碍黑方发展。主教钉住了黑方的电子棋子，如果出现...Nf6，白方将很乐意用主教换取马，并扰乱黑方的棋子结构。

因此，黑方通常会推迟马的发展，并选择是要先杀还是先把主教赶走。

2...h6 踢了主教。 3. Bh4 g5，虽然看起来黑方会用...f4困住白方的象，但实际上白方自己设下了一个狡猾的陷阱： 4. Bg3 f4？ 5.e3！ FXG3？？ 6.Qh5#。主要动作是4. e3（其中4...gxh4?? 5. Qh5#也）Nf6（现在守卫h5）5. Bg3 Bg7。黑方已经能够成功地发展他们的马和象，并避免了双F兵，但他们的王侧兵的扩张正在减弱。 h4 是白方的计划，引出...g5 并在暗方下棋。

2...g6 是一个简单的替代方案：黑方希望通过在 ...Nf6 之前下 ...Bg7 来避免双 f 兵，因此他们可能会用主教重新夺回。与2.c4 g6之后不同，即使黑方推迟了他们的马的发展，他们也不必像3.h4那样担心尖锐的h4和h5机动？哈6！带有主教的节奏。

如果 2...Nf6 3. Bxf6 和黑方必须用 e 兵收回，否则会进一步削弱 e8-h5 对角线。 3...gxf6？ （遵循“规则”回到中心） 4. e4！ FXE4？？ 5. Qh5# 在业余游戏中出现的频率比你想象的要高。

历史

1860 年的这一行游戏归因于“R. Hopton”，该游戏继续 2...h6 3. Bh4 c5 4. e3 Qb6 5. b3 Nf6 6. dxc5？ Qb4+（用叉子赢得主教），白棋辞职。否则，这条路线就被简单地称为“女王主教攻击”。

加里·卡斯帕罗夫（Garry Kasparov）倾向于这条路线来对抗荷兰的防守。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...f5/2. Bg5/2...Nc6
explanations.text:
2...Nc6!?

A rare sideline in Hopton attack. Black did not wish to develop their king's knight, 2...Nf6, because White would be happy to trade it off, so instead they developed their other knight. Usually in the Hopton attack, Black doesn't play ...Nc6 because they want to support d5 with c6 (the main line is 1. d4 f5 2. Bg5 g6 3. Nc3 Bg7 4. e3 d5 5. h4 c6). Though White is better by engine, the inaccuracy is not immediately punishable by White.

3. e3 unleashes the bishop and queen, and Black has missed their chance to play ...h6, as 3...h6?? loses to 4. Qh5+! g6 5. Qxg6#. Black can continue with 3...g6 & 4...Bg7 and adopt a Leningrad-style system. Black delays playing ...Nf6 until they may retake with the bishop, so as to avoid Bxf6 exf6 and doubled pawns. For White, the maximalist approach is c4 and Nc3.

3. Nf3 may be followed by 3...h6, and White's bishop really is in danger of being trapped this time because after 3...h6 4. Bh4?? g5 5. Bg3 f4, 6. e3? no longer gives the queen access to h4. White must retreat the bishop, 4. Bd2, and Black has relieved its pressure on their position.

History

The earliest recorded game of 2...Nf6 is Vesely vs Florian, 1961. It is a very uncommon sideline. Its highest level adopter is Soviet-born English grandmaster Alexander Cherniaev (1969-).

explanations.textZh:
2...NC6！？

霍普顿进攻中罕见的边线。黑方不希望发展他们的国王的骑士2...Nf6，因为白方很乐意将其进行交易，所以他们反而发展了他们的另一个马。通常在Hopton进攻中，黑棋不下...Nc6，因为他们想用c6来支持d5（主线是1.d4 f5 2.Bg5 g6 3.Nc3 Bg7 4.e3 d5 5.h4 c6）。尽管白棋的引擎更好，但白棋的不准确并不会立即受到惩罚。

3. e3 释放象和后，黑方错过了下...h6 的机会，因为 3...h6？输给4.Qh5+！ g6 5.Qxg6#。黑棋可以继续 3...g6 和 4...Bg7 并采用列宁格勒风格的系统。黑方推迟下...Nf6，直到他们可以重新夺回象，以避免Bxf6 exf6 和双兵。对于白方来说，最大化方法是 c4 和 Nc3。

3. Nf3 后面可能会出现 3...h6，白棋这次的象确实有被困的危险，因为 3...h6 之后 4. Bh4?? g5 5.Bg3 f4，6.e3？不再允许女王访问 h4。白棋必须撤退象，4. Bd2，黑棋已经减轻了对他们位置的压力。

历史

最早有记录的 2...Nf6 比赛是 1961 年 Vesely 对阵 Florian。这是一种非常罕见的边线比赛。其最高水平采用者是出生于苏联的英国特级大师亚历山大·切尔尼亚耶夫（Alexander Cherniaev，1969-）。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...f5/2. Bg5/2...g6
explanations.text:
2...g6

Black prepares to fianchetto their bishop. This will allow them to develop their knight and, if White captures it, recapture with the bishop instead of doubling their pawns.

One way for White to play this is to keep the position closed with ideas of e3, h4, and Nf3. Typically both sides castle short.

This leads for more positional grinds.

After 2. Nc3 Bg7, White can open the position with 3. e4 fxe4 5. Nxe4 or keep the position closed with with 3. e3. Black may adopt a move order with 2...d5 followed by 3...Bg7 to discourage White from playing e4.

2...g6

One way for White to play this is to keep the position closed with ideas of e3, h4, and Nf3. Typically both sides castle short.

This leads for more positional grinds.

explanations.textZh:
2...g6

黑方准备向他们的主教发起攻击。这将使他们能够发展他们的马，并且如果白方捕获它，则用主教重新捕获而不是加倍他们的棋子。

白棋的一种方法是用 e3、h4 和 Nf3 的想法来保持封闭位置。通常双方的城堡都很短。

这会导致更多的位置磨练。

2. Nc3 Bg7 之后，白方可以用 3. e4 fxe4 5. Nxe4 开仓，或者用 3. e3 保持平仓。黑棋可能会采用 2...d5 后跟 3...Bg7 的走棋顺序，以阻止白棋下 e4。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...f5/2. Bg5/2...h6
explanations.text:
Dutch Defence with 2.Bg5

2. ... h6

Black drives back the white bishop. White can now play either Bf4 or Bh4, the latter maintaining the pin on the pawn. Because 2... h6 weakens black's kingside squares, some players prefer to avoid it, although there is no obvious refutation for white.
explanations.textEn:
Dutch Defence with 2.Bg5

2. ... h6

Black drives back the white bishop. White can now play either Bf4 or Bh4, the latter maintaining the pin on the pawn. Because 2... h6 weakens black's kingside squares, some players prefer to avoid it, although there is no obvious refutation for white.
explanations.textZh:
荷兰防守2.Bg5

2. ... h6

黑方击退白方主教。白方现在可以下 Bf4 或 Bh4，后者保持对棋子的控制。由于2...h6 削弱了黑棋的王翼方格，因此一些棋手宁愿避开它，尽管对于白棋没有明显的反驳。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...f5/2. c4
explanations.text:
Dutch Defence

Towards this move black has basically two typical set ups and one theory based opening.

One is a fortress like position with pawn structure f5-e6-d5. This is called the Stonewall defence. This type of position is considered solid, but perhaps too static.

A dynamic choice is a Leningrad setup. The pawn structure is practically always g6-f5-d6. Black plays in this system, with only a few rare exceptions, his bishop to g7, knight to f6, and castles quickly.

The more theoretical approach is the Bladel variation with 2...g6 3. Nc3 Nh6 which allows white to play e4 and transforms the Dutch into an semi open game. Black delays to castle and instead fights for the center with c6 ... followed by d5. White trades off a center pawn for side pawn. White seeks to deliver an early checkmate in the middle game. Black has an additional center pawn which has proven to be a significant advantage in the end game.

explanations.textZh:
荷兰国防

对于这一棋，黑棋基本上有两种典型的布局和一种基于理论的开局。

一种是类似堡垒的位置，棋子结构为f5-e6-d5。这就是所谓的石墙防御。这种类型的立场被认为是稳固的，但可能过于静态。

一个动态的选择是列宁格勒的设置。棋子结构实际上总是 g6-f5-d6。黑方在这个系统中下棋，除了少数罕见的例外，他的主教为g7，马为f6，并且城堡很快。

更理论化的方法是 Bladel 变体，其中 2...g6 3. Nc3 Nh6，它允许白棋下 e4，并将荷兰棋转变为半开放游戏。黑方延迟到城堡，转而用 c6 争夺中心……随后是 d5。白方将中心棋子换成边棋。白棋寻求在中局尽早将死。黑棋有一个额外的中心棋子，这已被证明在最后的游戏中具有显着的优势。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...f5/2. c4/2...g6
explanations.text:
Dutch Defence

With g6

A dynamic choice, the Dutch with g6 is a Leningrad setup. The pawn structure is practically always g6-f5-d6. Black plays in this system, with only a few rare exceptions, his bishop to g7, knight to f6, and castles quickly.

Leningrad Dutch main line is, with possible changes in move order: 1. d4 f5 2. c4 Nf6 3. g3 g6 4. Nf3 Bg7 5. Bg2 d6 6. 0-0 0-0 7. Nc3 Qe8 (Diagram).

With 7...Qe8 black plans e5. White usually either plays a pawn advance on queenside with b4-b5 etc., which is helped by the strong bishop on g2 or/and plays for center with e4 and d5. In fact the space advancing move 8 d5 is main line . The main alternatives to 7..Qe8 for black are 7...c6 and 7..Nc6. 7..c6 is considered quite solid and played by former world champion M Botvinnik in the end of his career. 7... Nc6 is an ultra sharp alternative where black usually plays for kingside attack.

On absolute top level Leningrad Dutch is today rarely played. But it is used occasionally and former world champion Vladimir Kramnik played it several times in his youth. Its considered an excellent way for black to play for win, especially below grandmaster level, but the slight weakening of kingside with pawn f5 makes it not the taste of every strong

chessplayer.

与g6

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...f5/2. c4/2...g6/3. Nc3
explanations.text:
3. Nc3

A natural move, White develops a their queen's knight to control the centre. At the moment White's options are still open and they may choose whether to play in the modern way with g3 and Bg2, or in the traditional way with e3 and Be2.

3...Nf6 is the main move here, usually followed by 4...Bg7, or in the order 3...Bg7 followed by 4...Nf3. White may continue with Nf3, g3, etc, or with the aggressive 4. h4! intending h5 and h6 if possible, though this attack doesn't work as well as if White had tried it on turn turn.

An unusual option, which Black enabled by having played 2...g6 before developing their knight, is 3...Nh6!?, the Bladel variation.

explanations.textZh:
3.NC3

怀特自然而然地派出了一名后骑士来控制中路。目前白方的选择仍然是开放的，他们可以选择是否以现代方式玩 g3 和 Bg2，或者以传统方式玩 e3 和 Be2。

3...Nf6 是这里的主要动作，通常随后是 4...Bg7，或者按照 3...Bg7 后跟 4...Nf3 的顺序。白方可能会继续使用 Nf3、g3 等，或者使用激进的 4.h4！如果可能的话，打算使用 h5 和 h6，尽管这种攻击不如白方在转牌圈尝试过那样有效。

一个不寻常的选择是黑方在发展他们的马之前通过下2...g6启用的，是3...Nh6!?，即Bladel变体。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...f5/2. c4/2...g6/3. Nc3/3...Nh6
explanations.text:
3...Nh6!? · Bladel variation

3...Nh6!? is an offbeat continuation in the Dutch defence. Black develops their knight to the edge of the board. 3...Nf6 would be more active, but ...Nh6 is just about getting the knight out of the way. It at least helps Black get ready to castle, and keeping the f6 square clear of pieces means both ...Bg7 will exert immediate pressure and (so long as Black can castle and open the f-file) so will Black's rook on f8. Black may later reroute their knight to f7 or f5.

White may choose to continue with their typical development plans, e.g. 4. Nf3 with g3 and Bg2 or e3 and Be2.

4. e4 is testing. White seizes more space in the centre. If 4...fxe4 5. Nxe4 White is happy to see the position open, where they aim to punish Black's passive play and weakened kingside with an attack. Black may leave the pawn tension, hoping that White will take into them so they may recapture and activate their knight, 4...d6 5. exf5 Nxf5, or otherwise play 4...d6 and 5...Nf7.

History

The Bladel variation was first played by Max Euwe in Flohr v Euwe, 1969, during a small tournament in Bladel, the Netherlands, held in memoriam of Richard Réti. The four competitors in the tournament had all faced Reti before his death forty years prior. A contemporary account from USCF's Chess Life read:

One would hardly have expected opening novelties to be produced in such a tournament, but Euwe uncorked one in his game against Flohr. Playing Black, Euwe chose the Dutch Defense, introducing the following line: 1. P-Q4, P-KB4; 2. P-QB4, P-KN3; 3. N-QB3, N-KR3!?; 4. P-K4, P-Q3; 5. P-QN3, B-N2; 6. B-N2, 0-0; 7. N-B3, N·B3; 8. B-K2, P-K4; 9. QPxP, NxP; 10. PXP, NxP; 11.0-0, B-Q2; 12. Q-Q2, and a draw was agreed. Hardly an auspicious launching, but perhaps the "Bladel Variation" will find a home in some future anthology of openings.

At time of writing it still has yet to find a "home": the line has hardly ever been played since and there is little established theory.

explanations.textZh:
3...NH6！？ · 布拉德尔变体

3...NH6！？这是荷兰后防线另类的延续。黑棋将他们的马发展到棋盘的边缘。 3...Nf6 会更活跃，但是...Nh6 只是让骑士走开。它至少可以帮助黑方准备好城堡，并且保持f6方格没有棋子意味着……Bg7将立即施加压力并且（只要黑方可以城堡并打开f档）黑方的f8车也会如此。黑方稍后可能会将其马重新安排到 f7 或 f5。

白方可能会选择继续他们典型的发展计划，例如4. Nf3与g3和Bg2或e3和Be2。

4. e4正在测试。白棋在中路占据了更多空间。如果 4...fxe4 5. Nxe4 白方很高兴看到位置空缺，他们的目标是通过进攻来惩罚黑方的被动玩法和削弱王翼。黑方可能会留下兵紧张，希望白方能够接纳他们，这样他们就可以重新捕获并激活他们的马，4...d6 5. exf5 Nxf5，或者以其他方式玩 4...d6 和 5...Nf7。

历史

1969 年，Max Euwe 在 Flohr v Euwe 比赛中首次使用 Bladel 变体，当时是在荷兰 Bladel 为纪念 Richard Réti 举办的小型锦标赛中。比赛中的四名参赛者在四十年前都曾与雷蒂死前交过手。 USCF 国际象棋生活的当代报道如下：

人们很难想象在这样一场比赛中会产生开局新奇的东西，但尤威在对阵弗洛尔的比赛中打开了一个新局面。下黑棋时，尤威选择了荷兰防守，推出以下路线： 1. P-Q4，P-KB4； 2. P-QB4、P-KN3； 3.N-QB3，N-KR3！？； 4. P-K4，P-Q3； 5. P-QN3、B-N2； 6.B-N2，0-0； 7. N-B3，N·B3； 8、B-K2、P-K4； 9.QPxP、NxP； 10.PXP、NxP； 11.0-0，B-Q2； 12.Q-Q2，双方同意平局。这并不是一个吉祥的推出，但也许“Blade Variation”会在未来的一些开场选集中找到一个家。

在撰写本文时，它仍然尚未找到“家”：此后该线路几乎没有被演奏过，也几乎没有既定的理论。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...f5/2. c4/2...Nf6
explanations.text:
2...Nf6 · Normal variation

2...Nf6 is the normal variation of the Dutch Defence. It is a natural developing move. As well as helping to control the centre, the knight is valuable in controlling h5. Black weakened the e8-h5 diagonal when they moved their f-pawn.

White has several ways to continue:

3. Nc3 is the queen's knight variation. White develops the knight to its most active square to control e4.

3. g3 is the fianchetto variation, where White prepares to control the long diagonal with their king's bishop.

2...Nf6 · Normal variation

2...Nf6 is the normal variation of the Dutch Defence. It is a natural developing move. As well as helping to control the centre, the knight is valuable in controlling h5. Black weakened the e8-h5 diagonal when they moved their f-pawn.

White has several ways to continue:

3. Nc3 is the queen's knight variation. White develops the knight to its most active square to control e4.

3. g3 is the fianchetto variation, where White prepares to control the long diagonal with their king's bishop.
explanations.textZh:
2...Nf6 · 正常变化

2...Nf6 是荷兰防御的正常变化。这是自然发展的举动。除了帮助控制中路之外，骑士对于控制h5也很有价值。当黑方移动 f 兵时，他们削弱了 e8-h5 对角线。

白棋有几种继续的方法：

3. NC3是女王的骑士变体。白棋将马发展到最活跃的方格来控制e4。

3. g3 是 fianchetto 变体，其中白方准备用其国王的主教控制长对角线。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...f5/2. c4/2...Nf6/3. Nc3
explanations.text:
3. Nc3 · Queen's knight variation

3. Nc3 develops a piece and increases White's control over the e4 and d5 squares.

3...e6 leads to the Classical or Stonewall systems.

3...d6 prepares to develop the king's bishop to b4, pinning White's knight.

3...g6: prepares to fianchetto the king's bishop instead.

Preparing to fianchetto the queen's bishop, 3...b6, is uncommon.
explanations.textEn:
3. Nc3 · Queen's knight variation

3. Nc3 develops a piece and increases White's control over the e4 and d5 squares.

3...e6 leads to the Classical or Stonewall systems.

3...d6 prepares to develop the king's bishop to b4, pinning White's knight.

3...g6: prepares to fianchetto the king's bishop instead.

Preparing to fianchetto the queen's bishop, 3...b6, is uncommon.
explanations.textZh:
3.NC3·女王骑士变种

3. Nc3 发展一颗棋子并增强白方对 e4 和 d5 方格的控制。

3...e6 通向古典或石墙系统。

3...d6准备将国王的主教发展到b4，钉住白方的马。

3...g6：准备向国王的主教发起攻击。

准备向女王的主教 3...b6 发起攻击的情况并不常见。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...f5/2. c4/2...Nf6/3. Nc3/3...b6
explanations.text:
3...b6

Black prepares ...Bb7, to exert long term pressure on the long light square diagonal and further control e4.

This move order makes it harder for White to play g3 and Bg2, as Black's bishop gets to contest the diagonal first. A continuation is 4. Nf3 to prepare g2, and 4...e6 5. g3 Bb7 6. Bg2 Bb4.

History

The earliest recorded game played in this line was played between Remo Calapso and Ernesto Hellmann at the 1924 Italian national tournament (see sample game).

Another early game was played between Carlos Portela and Alexander Alekhine, 1926.

Sample game

Remo Calapso vs Ernesto Hellmann, Foligno 1924: 1. d4 f5 2. c4 Nf6 3. Nc3 b6 4. Bg5 e6 5. a3 Be7 6. e3 Bb7 7. Nf3 O-O 8. Bxf6 Rxf6 9. Bd3 Qf8 10. Qe2 Nc6 11. d5 Nd8 12. Ne5 Qe8 13. e4 Nf7 14. Nxf7 Qxf7 15. O-O f4 16. e5 f3 17. gxf3 Rh6 18. Kg2 Qh5 19. Rh1 Qh3+ 20. Kg1 exd5 21. Nxd5 Bxd5 22. cxd5 Rh5 23. f4 Rh4 24. Qe3 Rg4+ 25. Qg3 Bc5 0-1

Nxf7 Qxf7 15. O-O f4 16. e5 f3 17. gxf3 Rh6 18. Kg2 Qh5 19. Rh1 Qh3+ 20. Kg1 exd5 21. Nxd5 Bxd5 22. cxd5 Rh5 23. f4 Rh4 24. Qe3 Rg4+ 25. Qg3 Bc5 0-1
explanations.textZh:
3...b6

黑方准备...Bb7，对长光方对角线施加长期压力，进一步控制e4。

这种走法使得白方更难下 g3 和 Bg2，因为黑方的象首先要争夺对角线。延续是4.Nf3制备g2，以及4...e6 5.g3Bb7 6.Bg2Bb4。

历史

最早记录的该线比赛是 1924 年意大利国家锦标赛上雷莫·卡拉普索 (Remo Calapso) 和埃内斯托·赫尔曼 (Ernesto Hellmann) 之间的比赛（参见比赛示例）。

1926 年，卡洛斯·波特拉 (Carlos Portela) 和亚历山大·阿廖欣 (Alexander Alekhine) 进行了另一场早期比赛。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...f5/2. Qd3
explanations.text:
2. Qd3 · Alapin variation

A rarer line. White develops their queen aggressively to an active square and attacks the vulnerable f5 pawn.

2...e6 is the most common way of defending the pawn and the second most common move. Black goes into a Stonewall setup and makes the queen seem misplaced. However, the unique line that can arise from 2. Qd3 is 3. g4!?, the tricky Manhattan gambit.

2...Nf6!? is the most popular move, the so-called Pretzel gambit. Black ignores that their pawn is hanging and hopes that kicking the queen around after 3. Qxf5 d5 is sufficient compensation.
explanations.textEn:
2. Qd3 · Alapin variation

A rarer line. White develops their queen aggressively to an active square and attacks the vulnerable f5 pawn.

2...e6 is the most common way of defending the pawn and the second most common move. Black goes into a Stonewall setup and makes the queen seem misplaced. However, the unique line that can arise from 2. Qd3 is 3. g4!?, the tricky Manhattan gambit.

2...Nf6!? is the most popular move, the so-called Pretzel gambit. Black ignores that their pawn is hanging and hopes that kicking the queen around after 3. Qxf5 d5 is sufficient compensation.
explanations.textZh:
2. Qd3·阿拉平变体

比较少见的线路。白棋将他们的皇后积极地发展成一个活跃的方格并攻击脆弱的 f5 兵。

2...e6 是最常见的防御棋子的方式，也是第二常见的走法。黑棋进入石墙阵势，让后棋看起来错位了。然而，从 2.Qd3 中产生的唯一路线是 3.g4!?，这是棘手的曼哈顿策略。

2...NF6！？这是最受欢迎的举动，即所谓的椒盐卷饼策略。黑方忽略了他们的棋子悬空，并希望在 3.Qxf5 d5 后将后踢走就足够了。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...f5/2. e4
explanations.text:
Staunton Gambit

2. e4

The type of approach one might expect to be successful against the Dutch in view of the weak h5-e8 diagonal. Practice has shown that Black has adequate resources; it is difficult for white to show much after a skirmish to recover the pawn sacrifice.
explanations.textEn:
Staunton Gambit

2. e4

The type of approach one might expect to be successful against the Dutch in view of the weak h5-e8 diagonal. Practice has shown that Black has adequate resources; it is difficult for white to show much after a skirmish to recover the pawn sacrifice.
explanations.textZh:
斯汤顿开局

2.e4

鉴于 h5-e8 对角线较弱，人们可能期望这种方法能够在对阵荷兰队时取得成功。实践证明，黑方资源充足；在一场小冲突之后，白棋很难表现出太多的行动来追回棋子牺牲。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...f5/2. f3
explanations.text:
2. f3

A rare and abnormal sideline in the Dutch Defence. The main idea is quite straightforward: push e4 to control the center and challenge Black's f5 pawn. However, it blocks the natural developing square for the g1 knight and opens the e1-h4 diagonal. Sometimes, White can gambit a pawn on e4 for quick development and lines.

Responses

2...Nf6 is Black's most common move, controlling d5 once more with the knight. White can gambit their e-pawn with 3. e4 fxe4 4. fxe4 Nxe4 5. Nc3 Nxc3 6. bxc3, and White is prepared to develop with Nf3, Bf4 and Bc4.

2...e6 goes for a standard Stonewall system, but allows White to fight for the center with 3. e4. However, after 3...fxe4, 4. fxe4? is not advised because of 4...Qh4+! and Black regains the pawn with compensation after 5. Ke2 (5. g3?? Qxe4+! 6. Qe2 Qxh1-+) Qxe4+ 6. Kf2. So instead White can try to sacrifice the pawn for development with 4. Nc3 exf3 5. Nxf3 where White has two knights developed an ready to develop the bishops.

2...d5 is the most accurate move, reinforcing d5 with the pawn. This leads to an equal, slightly normal position after 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Bg5=, where both sides want to attempt to challenge the center and develop their pieces quickly.

2.f3

荷兰后防线中罕见且不正常的边线。主要思想非常简单：推动e4控制中心并挑战黑方的f5兵。然而，它阻挡了g1骑士的自然发展方格并打开了e1-h4对角线。有时，白棋可以在 e4 上下棋以实现快速发展和线路。

2...Nf6 是黑方最常见的走法，用马再次控制 d5。白方可以用 3. e4 fxe4 4. fxe4 Nxe4 5. Nc3 Nxc3 6. bxc3 下注他们的电子兵，白方准备用 Nf3、Bf4 和 Bc4 发展。

2...e6 适用于标准石墙系统，但允许白方用 3. e4 争夺中心。然而，3...fxe4之后，4.fxe4？不建议，因为 4...Qh4+！ 5. Ke2 (5. g3?? Qxe4+! 6. Qe2 Qxh1-+) Qxe4+ 6. Kf2 后，黑方以补偿夺回棋子。因此，白方可以尝试牺牲棋子来发展4. Nc3 exf3 5. Nxf3，其中白方有两个马发展了一个准备发展主教的地方。

explanations.text:
2. Nh3

A rare but respectable sideline where White chooses to develop their knight to the edge of the board. Despite going against common opening principles, this move is sound.

2...Nf6 is the most common move, continuing with the plan of controlling e4 alongside the f-pawn. The game can progress many ways, but the most common is the Blackburne variation, 3. g3 e6 4. Bg2, where the knight doesn't block the kingside bishop's sight, and is essentially similar to a Bladel but from the White side.

2...e6 usually leads to the same line, just from a different move order, through 3. g3 Nf6 4. Bg2.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...f5/2. g4
explanations.text:
2. g4?! · Krejcik gambit

The idea of 2. g4?! is straight forward enough: deflect Black's f-pawn from control of e4, and perhaps White can get in the move e4 themselves soon, so building a strong, spacious centre with both d and e pawns. Against best play the gambit doesn't work out that way and White doesn't get complete compensation for the pawn.

2...fxg4 accepts the gambit. Though this loses control of the e4 square, it transpires that White can't make much of 3. e4?! anyway. (If 3. e4 (discovering an attack on g4 with the queen) d5 both discovers a defender of g4 in the form of the bishop and attacks e4. Black is up a pawn and better. If 4. exd5? Qxd5 comes with an attack on White's rook.)

The more usual move is 3. h3.

If 3...gxh3?! 4. Nxh3, White is happy to recapture while developing their pieces and an idea is to attack on the kingside with Ng5 and Qd3, e.g. 4...Nf6 5. Qd3 d5 6. Ng5 and White threatens to take three times on h7:

6...h6?? 7. Qg6+ Kd7 8. Nf7 forks the rook and queen, and after 8...Qe8 White has this neat manoeuvre 9. Nxh8 Qxg6 10. Nxg6)

6...g6? 7. Rxh7! and White threatens Qxg6+.

7...Bf5?? and White can sacrifice their queen: 8. Rxh8! Bxd3 9. Ne6 Qd6 10. Rxf8+ (rook is defended by knight) Kd7 11. Rd8+ Kxe6 12. Rxd6+ Kxd6 13. cxd3 (retakes bishop) and White is up a piece.

7. Rg8 and White can sacrifice their rook: 8. Rh8! Rxh8 9. Qxg6+ (drives king from defence of f7) Kd7 10. Nf7 Qe8, and White has the same manoeuvre 11. Nxh8 Qxg6 12. Nxg6

6...e6 is the best reply, but Black gives back the pawn and loses castling rights 7. Nxh7 Nxh7 8. Rxh7 Rxh7 9. Qg6+ Kd7 10. Qxh7.

Instead, Black is better advised to play 3...d5 and allow 4. hxg4 Bxg4.

2....d5 declines the gambit and is also fine for Black. This allows Black's bishop to see f5, meaning that if 3. gxf5?! Black can recapture while developing their bishop, 3...Bxf5. Black may still take the free pawn later, if say 3. Bg2 fxg4. 3. Qd3, threatening to take twice on f5, transposes into something called the Manhattan gambit, otherwise seen in the move order 1. d4 f5 2. Qd3 (the Alapin variation) e5 4. g4.

Other ways of defending the f-pawn are bad, e.g. 2...g6? 3. gxf5, and Black cannot take back, else 3...gxf5? 4. e4! Nf6? (thinking to prevent Qh5+; 4...fxe4?? 5. Qh5#) 5. e5! Ng4 6. h3 Nh6?! (so that Qh5+ Nf7 is possible) 7. Bxh6 Bxh6 8. Qh5+ Kf8 9. Qxh6+ etc.

2...e5?!, the Hevendehl gambit, is a surprise within a surprise.

History

Josef Krejcik (1885–1957) was an Austrian chess player and publisher of Wiener Schachzeitung (German: Viennese Chess Magazine).

In one of the earliest recorded games featuring the line, it was played successfully by Brian Moore against Jonathan Penrose, who would go on to become ten time British champion, in the 1955 British Chess Championship.

explanations.textZh:
2.g4？！ · 克雷吉克策略

2.g4的想法？！足够简单：使黑方的 f 棋子偏离 e4 的控制，也许白棋很快就能进入 e4 棋，因此用 d 和 e 棋子建立一个强大、宽敞的中心。对抗最佳策略时，这种策略不会奏效，白方也无法从棋子中得到完全的补偿。

2...fxg4 接受这个策略。虽然这样失去了对 e4 方格的控制，但白棋却不能充分利用 3. e4？！反正。 （如果 3. e4（发现与后对 g4 的攻击）d5 都发现了 g4 的象象形式的防御者并攻击 e4。黑棋是棋子并且更好。如果 4. exd5？Qxd5 对白棋的车进行攻击。）

更常见的走法是 3. h3。

如果3...gxh3？！ 4. Nxh3，白方很高兴在发展自己的棋子时重新夺回，并且一个想法是用 Ng5 和 Qd3 攻击王翼，例如4...Nf6 5. Qd3 d5 6. Ng5 和白方威胁在 h7 上拿下 3 次：

6...h6？？ 7. Qg6+ Kd7 8. Nf7 分叉车和后，8...Qe8 白棋有这个巧妙的策略 9. Nxh8 Qxg6 10. Nxg6)

6...g6？ 7. Rxh7！白棋威胁 Qxg6+。

7...Bf5？？白棋可以牺牲他们的皇后：8.Rxh8！ Bxd3 9. Ne6 Qd6 10. Rxf8+（车被马防守） Kd7 11. Rd8+ Kxe6 12. Rxd6+ Kxd6 13. cxd3（夺回主教），白方领先一子。

7. Rg8 和白方可以牺牲他们的车： 8. Rh8！ Rxh8 9. Qxg6+（将王从 f7 的防守中赶走） Kd7 10. Nf7 Qe8，白棋有相同的策略 11. Nxh8 Qxg6 12. Nxg6

6...e6 是最好的答复，但黑方归还棋子并失去易位权 7. Nxh7 Nxh7 8. Rxh7 Rxh7 9. Qg6+ Kd7 10. Qxh7。

相反，建议黑棋下 3...d5 并允许 4. hxg4 Bxg4。

2....d5 拒绝这个策略，对黑棋来说也很好。这使得黑棋的象可以看到f5，也就是说如果3.gxf5？！黑方可以在发展其主教 3...Bxf5 的同时夺回胜利。如果说 3. Bg2 fxg4，黑方稍后仍可能拿走空闲兵。 3. Qd3，威胁要对 f5 采取两次行动，转置为所谓的曼哈顿策略，否则可以在移动顺序 1. d4 f5 2. Qd3（阿拉平变体） e5 4. g4 中看到。

其他防御 f-pawn 的方法都不好，例如2...g6？ 3. gxf5，黑方无法收回，否则3...gxf5？ 4.e4！ NF6？ （想阻止Qh5+；4...fxe4?? 5.Qh5#）5.e5！ NG4 6.h3 Nh6？！ （因此 Qh5+ Nf7 是可能的） 7. Bxh6 Bxh6 8. Qh5+ Kf8 9. Qxh6+ 等

2...e5?!，赫文德尔的策略，是惊喜中的惊喜。

历史

约瑟夫·克雷西克（Josef Krejcik，1885-1957 年）是一位奥地利国际象棋棋手，也是《Wiener Schachzeitung》（德语：维也纳国际象棋杂志）的出版人。

在最早记录的以这句台词为特色的比赛之一中，布莱恩·摩尔 (Brian Moore) 在 1955 年英国国际象棋锦标赛中对阵乔纳森·彭罗斯 (Jonathan Penrose)，后者后来成为十次英国冠军。

2.h3 - Dutch Defence, Korchnoi Attack

The Korchnoi attack is a theory based, sound, aggressive way to play against the Dutch. This Attack has been named after the Russian Grandmaster, Viktor Lvovich Korchnoi.

Viktor Lvovich Korchnoi (Russian: Виктор Львович Корчной, IPA: [vʲiktər lʲvovʲɪtɕ kɐrtɕˈnoj]; 23 March 1931 – 6 June 2016) was a Soviet (before 1976) and Swiss (after 1980) chess grandmaster (GM) and chess writer. He is considered one of the strongest players never to have become World Chess Champion.

Black has to respond differently right from the start. Black strongest responses are:

for the open variations with 2...d6 3...e5 4...Nc6,

for the closed variations with 2...d5 3...c5 4...e6,

In both variation in the spirit of the Dutch Defence, black will fight in most sound and aggressive way possible. In the event of the open variations white can go for

for the classic variation with 3.g6... 4.Bg5... 5.e5...

for the normal variation with 3.Nf3... 4.c4... 5.Nc3...

for the modern variation with 3.Nc3... 4.e5 fxe5 5.Nxe5...

In the case of the Dutch Defence, Korchnoi Attack, open Variations there is high probability to castle on opposing sites, which can lead to very exciting positions.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...f5/2. h3/2...Nf6
explanations.text:
== 2...Nf6 ==

The most common and best response to the Korchnoi Attack, however White can spring a trap with a surprising gambit.

3. g4 is the Janzen-Korchnoi Gambit, which can set up a trap if accepted with 3...fxg4: 4. hxg4 Nxg4 5. Qd3! Nf6?? 6. Rxh7!! Rxh7?? 7. Qg6#. However, if Black knows the correct responses, it can be neutralized.

A sounder response is 3. Nf3, however it doesn't lead to the fun Janzen-Korchnoi positions, instead developing the kingside knight and aiming for a relatively normal game.

1...f6?

A weak response to 1. d4. Playing in similar fashion to the Barnes Defence, Black weakens their king and the e8-h5 diagonal while blocking the kingside knight's most natural square but prepares e5 This is one of the worst responses to 1. d4, only beaten by 1. d4 g5?.

White can choose from a variety of responses, such as:

2. e4, taking the full center and poisoning 2...e5

2. Nf3, developing the kingside knight and controlling e5.

2. c4, playing in the fashion of Queen's Pawn openings.

2. Bf4, playing in the fashion of the London and controlling e5

2. Nc3, developing the queenside knight

2. e4, taking the full center and poisoning 2...e5

2. Nf3, developing the kingside knight and controlling e5.

2. c4, playing in the fashion of Queen's Pawn openings.

2. Bf4, playing in the fashion of the London and controlling e5

2. Nc3, developing the queenside knight

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...g5
explanations.text:
1...g5?? · Borg gambit

Perhaps the worst possible reply to 1. d4 is 1...g5??. Against 1. e4, 1...g5? is bad because it fails to contest White's centre and weakens Black's kingside. Against 1. d4 it has the added disadvantage of sacrificing the pawn immediately.

2. Bxg5, accepts the gambit while developing a piece. A common mistake is 2...f6?, thinking to kick White's "overextended" bishop: unfortunately this weakens Black's kingside too much and the bishop is unassailable: 3. e4 fxg5?? 4. Qh5#. Instead, ideas for Black include increasing pressure on d4 with ...Bg7, making use of the square opened by playing 1...g5, and ...c5. Black can try for counter-play using the semi-open g-file with ...Rg8. Overall, Black does not have sufficient compensation for the pawn.

2. e4 is an alternative. White prioritises taking space in the centre and opens more lines for their queen and king's bishop to develop. This transposes to the Borg defence 1. e4 g5?? 2. d4. In this line Black can play ...Bg7 and ...c5, but also has the sly idea of 2...g4?! 3. Qxg4, where Black hopes to gain time on White's queen while attacking the centre.

History

The name "Borg" comes from the reverse of "Grob". The Grob, considered to be one of the worst starting moves, is 1. g4, therefore when Black begins with the g-pawn, 1. e4 g5?, they have played the "reverse Grob" i.e. the "Borg". When ...g5 is played after 1. d4, it is a gambit as it immediately offers the pawn to 2. Bxg5.

It is rare in tournament chess. An early recorded outing was in 1987, where the gambit was declined with 2. Nc3. It is most often seen as a surprise weapon in blitz chess.

explanations.textZh:
1...g5？？ · 博格策略

也许对 1.d4 最糟糕的答复是 1...g5??。反对 1.e4、1...g5？不好是因为它无法对抗白方的中锋并削弱了黑方的王翼。相对于 1.d4，它还有一个额外的缺点，即立即牺牲棋子。

2. Bxg5，在开发棋子时接受策略。一个常见的错误是2...f6？，想踢白方“过度扩张”的主教：不幸的是，这削弱了黑方的王翼太多，而主教是无懈可击的：3. e4 fxg5？ 4.Qh5#。相反，黑棋的想法包括用...Bg7增加对d4的压力，利用通过下棋1...g5和...c5打开的方块。黑棋可以尝试使用半开放的 g 锉与 ...Rg8 进行反击。总体而言，黑方对棋子没有足够的补偿。

2. e4是一个替代方案。白棋优先考虑在中间占据空间，并为他们的后和国王的主教打开更多的路线来发展。这转换为博格防御 1. e4 g5?? 2.d4。在此行中，黑方可以下...Bg7 和...c5，但也有2...g4 的狡猾想法？！ 3. Qxg4，黑棋希望在攻击中心的同时赢得白棋后的时间。

历史

“Borg”这个名字来自“Grob”的反面。 Grob 被认为是最差的起始棋之一，它是 1. g4，因此当黑方以 g 兵开始 1. e4 g5？时，他们就下了“反向 Grob”，即“Borg”。当在 1.d4 之后玩 ...g5 时，这是一种策略，因为它立即将棋子提供给 2.Bxg5。

这在国际象棋锦标赛中是罕见的。早期有记录的一次出局是在 1987 年，当时的策略被 2. Nc3 拒绝。它最常被视为闪电战棋中的奇兵武器。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...g5/2. Bxg5
explanations.text:
2. Bxg5: Borg Gambit Accepted

First Impressions

After accepting the Borg Gambit with Bxg5, White has gained a pawn as well as developed the queenside bishop. Obviously, this puts Black at a disadvantage, as White is now leading in development. Black has three main options here: Play the better move Bg7 and commit to a pseudo-Indian defense, c5 to try to destabilize the center and let the queen out, or try to kick the bishop out with f6.

2... c6

c6 has an interesting idea. While seeming to do nothing, White sometimes responds with 3. e3??, a mistake, since black has the strong double attack Qa5+, checking the king and attacking the bishop. Normally the bishop could come back to d2 but since white played e3, they will continue the game without a bishop.

2... Bg7

Bg7 prioritizes development over central control, and is considered better by masters and computers alike. This move aims to get quick development up in exchange for gambiting the g pawn. White can fight back by expanding in the center and developing their own pieces, leading to a rather quick race for who can develop their pieces the fastest. This gambit is usually considered not justified.

2... c5

The intent of c5 has two reasons. First, it is to destabilize White's center pawns and force them to respond lest they lose space by a center pawn being taken by a flank pawn. Secondly, it is to let the queen out, which can help destabilize the center or hunt the b2 pawn. This also develops a piece, getting a bit of advantage back for Black.

2... f6?

f6 attempts to kick away the bishop and expand in the center with an eventual e5, but this can be refuted with 3. e4!, saving the bishop for 1 turn and making some center space. If Black tries to take the bishop, the White queen can go to h5 for a quick checkmate. Overall, this line is considered inferior to Bg7 by masters and computers.

Other options

Black can also play Nf6 to develop the kingside knight, however after Bxf6, there are doubled pawns on the f file and there is a clear line of sight to the king which can be exploited since the kingside pawns are weak.

explanations.textZh:
2. Bxg5：接受博格弃兵

第一印象

在用 Bxg5 接受博格弃兵后，白方获得了棋子并发展了后侧主教。显然，这使黑方处于劣势，因为白方现在处于领先地位。黑棋在这里有三个主要选择：下更好的棋Bg7并致力于伪印度防御，c5试图破坏中心稳定并让后出局，或者尝试用f6将象踢出局。

2...c6

c6 有一个有趣的想法。虽然看似什么也没做，但白棋有时会回应 3. e3??，这是一个错误，因为黑棋具有强大的双攻 Qa5+，检查国王并攻击主教。通常主教可以回到 d2，但由于白棋下 e3，他们将在没有主教的情况下继续比赛。

2... 背景7

Bg7 优先考虑开发而不是中央控制，并且被主机和计算机都认为更好。此举的目的是为了获得快速发展，以换取g棋子。白方可以通过向中心扩张并发展自己的棋子来进行反击，从而导致一场相当快的竞赛，看谁能最快地发展自己的棋子。这种策略通常被认为是不合理的。

2...c5

c5 的意图有两个原因。首先，它是为了破坏白方中心棋子的稳定性，迫使他们做出反应，以免中间棋子被侧翼棋子吃掉而失去空间。其次，就是把后放出去，这样可以帮助动摇中心或者猎杀b2兵。这也形成了棋子，为黑棋赢得了一些优势。

2...f6？

f6 试图踢开主教并用最终的 e5 向中心扩张，但这可以用 3. e4! 反驳，节省主教 1 回合并腾出一些中心空间。如果黑棋试图吃掉主教，白后可以去 h5 快速将死。总体而言，这条线被大师和计算机认为不如Bg7。

其他选项

黑方也可以下Nf6来发展王翼骑士，但是在Bxf6之后，f档上有双兵，并且王翼的视线很清晰，可以利用，因为王翼兵很弱。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...g5/2. Bxg5/2...f6
explanations.text:
2. f6?

f6 seems like a relatively decent, if strange move by Black at first, kicking out the bishop and preparing for an advance to e5. However, this move weakens the king, as well as blocks development of the knight and the queen to f6. This can be abused by White with the move e4!, which makes the bishop poisoned, takes control of the center, and threatens to attack with the queen.

White always goes Qh5 after a few moves to either checkmate the king or force it to move away. This is not a good situation for Black to be in at all, with little development chances, being attacked, and a weak kingside.

There is a trap which comes after 3.e4! by white, and if Black greedily captures the Bg5, White plays 4. Qh5# and Black gets checkmated in four moves.

2.f6？

f6 看起来是一个相对不错的棋，虽然黑棋一开始有点奇怪，踢出了主教并准备晋级到 e5。然而，这一举动削弱了国王，并阻碍了马和王后向 f6 的发展。白棋可以用 e4! 来滥用这一点，使主教中毒，控制中心，并威胁与后攻击。

3.e4之后有一个陷阱！白方，如果黑方贪婪地吃掉 Bg5，白方下 4.Qh5#，黑方四步就将死。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...g6
explanations.text:
Queen's Pawn Opening: Modern Defence

1...g6

The Modern Defence is a solid, if not offbeat, response to White's 1. d4. Black gives up the centre in exchange for slower development on the kingside. White's most common reply is 2. e4, and Black usually responds with 3...Bg7 attacking the pawn and aiming at the d4-square.

White's options are many. Here are the 2 most popular:

2. e4 - Pirc (Robatsch) or Modern transposition

2. c4 - Heading for various queen's pawn games (e.g. KID, OID, QGD)

后兵开局：现代防御

1...g6

现代防御即使不是另类，也是对怀特 1.d4 的可靠回应。黑棋放弃了中路，以换取王翼发展缓慢。白方最常见的回应是 2. e4，黑方通常回应 3...Bg7 攻击棋子并瞄准 d4 方格。

白棋的选择有很多。以下是最受欢迎的 2 个：

2. e4 - Pirc (Robatsch) 或现代转置

2. c4 - 前往各种皇后典当游戏（例如 KID、OID、QGD）

explanations.text:
Queen's Pawn: Modern

2. c4

Playing the standard Queen's pawn formation controlling the center.

Black's options are still many, but likely to be a King's Indian or Grunfeld Defence, but possible is a transposition into the Dutch Defense.

2.c4

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6
explanations.text:
1...Nf6 · Indian defence

Black controls e4 while developing a knight. This is the most flexible response to 1. d4. Black doesn't commit a pawn to the centre yet. They may yet do so, or they can fight for the centre in the hypermodern way: controlling it from afar with pieces, allowing White to construct their pawn centre but undermining it later with timely pawn advances.

This move gives White lots of leeway to either develop pieces or take more space in the centre. Openings tend to be flexible with lots of potential for transpositions.

Take space in the centre

White would like two pawns in the centre if possible.

2. c4 is the main line: White takes more space and controls the important d5 square. After 2. c4, White can develop their knight behind their pawn line and perhaps play e4. Black can still choose to contest this centre with pawns with 2...d5, 2...c5 (Benoni), or 2...e5 (Budapest), but more typically they move their pawns only as necessary to develop their bishops: 2...e6, 2...g6, 2...d6 or 2...b6.

White can't play e4 and keep the pawn there (2. e4?! is called the Omega gambit and loses a pawn to 2...Nxe4). White can prepare 3. e4 with 2. Nc3 or 2. f3, which usually compels Black to play 2...d5 to keep control of e4.

Develop a piece

Alternatively, White can prioritise piece development.

2. Nf3, the Knights variation is the chief sideline. It's a flexible move: White may still play c4 afterwards but first gets more information on how Black intends to play.

2. Nc3, prevents c4 but, as noted above, prepares e4. After 2...d5 (controlling e4) the main continuations are 3. Bg5, the Richter-Veresov attack, or 3. Bf4, the Jobava-Rapport London.

The bishop has two main candidate squares to develop to.

2. Bg5, the Trompowsky attack, pressures Black's knight. White has hopes of trading it to double Black's pawns.

2. Bf4 plays the Accelerated London system into Black's Indian defence. Play may transpose with 2...d5, but the Indian defence has original ways to meet it without ...d5.

Uncommon moves

2. e3 plays in Colle system-style against the Indian defence. Transposes if Black plays ...d5.

2. g3, the Tartakower attack, prepares to fianchetto the bishop.

Strange moves

2. d5?!, the Pawn push variation. Since Black didn't play d5, White can advance their pawn, guarded by their queen. After 2...e6 3. dxe6 fxe6, White loses their central pawn.

2. f4?!, the Canard opening.

2. Nd2?!, hoping to support e4 without preventing c4, should be met with 2...d4, but 2...e4?! is the unsound Lazard gambit.

2. g4?!, the Bronstein gambit, hopes to tempt Black's knight away from controlling e4 by offering a free flank pawn.

explanations.textZh:
1...Nf6·印度国防

黑方在发展马的同时控制了e4。这是对 1. d4 的最灵活的响应。黑棋还没有将棋子放到中心。他们可能会这样做，或者他们可以以超现代的方式争夺中心：用棋子从远处控制它，允许白方构建他们的棋子中心，但随后通过及时的棋子推进来破坏它。

这一举动为白方提供了很大的余地，可以发展棋子或在中路占据更多空间。空缺往往很灵活，具有很大的换位潜力。

在中心占据空间

如果可能的话，白棋希望有两个棋子在中间。

2. c4为主线：白方占据更多空间，控制重要的d5方格。 2. c4之后，白方可以在兵线后面发展他们的马，也许可以下e4。黑方仍然可以选择用 2...d5、2...c5（贝诺尼）或 2...e5（布达佩斯）棋子来争夺该中心，但更常见的是，他们仅在发展主教所需时才移动棋子：2...e6、2...g6、2...d6 或 2...b6。

白方不能下 e4 并将棋子保留在那里（2. e4？！被称为 Omega 策略，并失去一个棋子到 2...Nxe4）。白方可以准备 3. e4 和 2. Nc3 或 2. f3，这通常迫使黑方下 2...d5 以保持对 e4 的控制。

开发一块

或者，白方可以优先考虑棋子的开发。

2. Nf3，骑士变体是主要副线。这是一个灵活的棋步：白棋之后可能仍然下 c4，但首先获得有关黑棋打算如何下棋的更多信息。

2. Nc3，阻止c4，但如上所述，准备e4。 2...d5（控制 e4）之后，主要延续是 3. Bg5，Richter-Veresov 攻击，或 3. Bf4，Jobava-Rapport London。

主教有两个主要的候选方格可供发展。

2. Bg5，Trompowsky 进攻，对黑方马施压。白方希望将其交易为黑方棋子的两倍。

2. Bf4 将加速伦敦系统运用到黑方的印度防御中。比赛可能会用 2...d5 进行调换，但印度的防守有独特的方法来应对它而不需要 ...d5。

不常见的动作

2. e3以科莱系统风格对抗印度防守。如果黑棋下...d5，则转置。

2. g3，Tartakower进攻，准备向主教发起攻击。

奇怪的举动

2. d5?!，Pawn 推变体。由于黑方没有下 d5，白方可以推进其棋子，并由其皇后守卫。 2...e6 3.dxe6 fxe6 之后，白方失去了中央棋子。

2. f4？！，鸭式开局。

2. nd2？！，希望支持e4而不妨碍c4，应该会遇到2...d4，但是2...e4？！这是拉扎德不明智的策略。

2. g4?!，布朗斯坦策略，希望通过提供一个自由的侧翼兵来引诱黑方的马放弃对 e4 的控制。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Nc3
explanations.text:
2.Nc3

White develops his Queen's Knight to support 3.e4, sometimes called the Veresov Opening. After Black's usual reply 2...d5, White may respond with 3.Bg5, leading to the Richter-Veresov Attack. Often transposes into the Chigorin Defence, the French Defence, or less commonly the Pirc Defence.

This position may also be reached via the move order 1.Nc3 Nf6 2.d4
explanations.textEn:
2.Nc3

White develops his Queen's Knight to support 3.e4, sometimes called the Veresov Opening. After Black's usual reply 2...d5, White may respond with 3.Bg5, leading to the Richter-Veresov Attack. Often transposes into the Chigorin Defence, the French Defence, or less commonly the Pirc Defence.

This position may also be reached via the move order 1.Nc3 Nf6 2.d4
explanations.textZh:
2.NC3

白方开发了他的皇后骑士来支持 3.e4，有时称为维列索夫开局。在黑方通常回复 2...d5 之后，白方可能会回复 3.Bg5，从而导致 Richter-Veresov 攻击。经常转换为齐戈林防御、法国防御，或者不太常见的皮尔奇防御。

也可以通过移动命令 1.Nc3 Nf6 2.d4 到达该位置

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Nc3/2...d5/3. Bf4
explanations.text:
3. Bf4 · Jobava London

Sometimes referred to as the Rapport-Jobava System. This opening serves as a good surprise weapon against unprepared opponents, and in the worst case, equalizes. White often plans to threaten a knight fork on the c7 square after Nb5, usually played on the fourth or fifth move. Black typically challenges the center immediately with /3...c5/ and trades their c-pawn for White's e-pawn. Alternatively, Black often plays the /3...a6/ Anti-Jobava to control the b5 square or the natural /3...e6/ development move. Black may also attempt /3...Bf5/, developing the light-squared bishop before playing 4...e6, but it gives White an opportunity to launch a pawn storm with a tempo on the bishop through a well-timed g4 push (usually after White plays f3 or Ne5, protecting the g4 square).

explanations.textZh:
3. Bf4·乔巴瓦·伦敦

有时称为融洽-乔巴瓦系统。这个开局对于毫无准备的对手来说是一个很好的奇袭武器，在最坏的情况下，甚至可以扳平比分。白棋经常计划在 Nb5 之后威胁 c7 方格上的马叉，通常在第四步或第五步棋时下棋。黑方通常会立即用 /3...c5/ 挑战中心，并将其 c 棋子换成白棋的 e 棋子。或者，黑方经常下 /3...a6/ 反乔巴瓦来控制 b5 方格或自然的 /3...e6/ 发展棋。黑方也可能会尝试/3...Bf5/，在下4...e6之前开发光方象，但这给了白方一个机会，通过适时的g4推动（通常在白方下f3或Ne5之后，保护g4方格），对象发起兵风暴。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Nc3/2...d5/3. Bf4/3...e6
explanations.text:
3...e6

This is Black's most popular response. This move reinforces the centre and opens up the dark-squared bishop. It does, however, pacify Black's light-squared bishop. The next couple of moves will likely happen on the queenside, since neither side has many attacking opportunities on the kingside.

The thematic 4. Nb5 is White's main response, threatening a fork on the c7-square. Black has two ways to defend against this: 4...Na6 is the most popular response. Black defends c7 with their knight and will soon kick out White's knight with c6 and reposition their a6-knight to c7 and subsequently e8, protecting the kingside. Alternatively, Black can opt for 4...Bb4+, which leads to a forcing line 5. c3 (5. Bd2? Bxd2 6. Qxd2 ) Ba5 and the bishop is now protecting c7. If White continues chasing the bishop with 6. a4 a6 7. b4 Bxb4 8. cxb4 axb5 9. axb5 Rxa1 10. Qxa1 the players have entered an endgame where White has a worse pawn structure, but more advanced pawns on the queenside.

Alternatively, White can play 4. e3, simply continuing development. This gives Black the opportunity of playing 4...Bb4, pinning the knight and possibly doubling White's queenside pawns, similar to the Winawer French. Alternatively, Black can continue 4...Bd6, preparing to trade dark-squared bishops.

explanations.textZh:
3...e6

这是布莱克最受欢迎的回应。这一举动加固了中心并打开了暗方象。然而，它确实安抚了黑方的浅方象。接下来的几个动作很可能发生在后翼，因为双方在王翼都没有太多的进攻机会。

主题 4. Nb5 是白方的主要回应，威胁在 c7 方格上形成叉子。黑方有两种方法来防御这种情况： 4...Na6 是最流行的反应。黑方用他们的马防守c7，很快就会用c6踢出白方的马，并将他们的a6马重新定位到c7，随后是e8，保护王翼。或者，黑方可以选择 4...Bb4+，这会导致一条强行线 5.c3 (5.Bd2? Bxd2 6.Qxd2 ) Ba5 并且主教现在正在保护 c7。如果白方继续用 6. a4 a6 7. b4 Bxb4 8. cxb4 axb5 9. axb5 Rxa1 10. Qxa1 追赶主教，那么玩家就进入了残局，其中白方的棋子结构更差，但后侧的棋子更先进。

或者，白方可以下 4. e3，只需继续开发即可。这给黑方提供了下 4...Bb4 的机会，压制马并可能加倍白方后侧兵，类似于 Winawer French。或者，黑方可以继续 4...Bd6，准备交易暗方象。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Nc3/2...d5/3. Bg5
explanations.text:
3...Bg5?! · Richter-Veresov Attack

The Richter-Veresov Attack or Mirrored Ruy Lopez is not the common attack we see, White plays early Bg5 while aiming at the knight on f6, preparing to damage Black’s pawn structure. Black’s most common response is e6 but other moves are seen as well, the attack can lead to a sharp attack and Black has to play carefully.
explanations.textEn:
3...Bg5?! · Richter-Veresov Attack

The Richter-Veresov Attack or Mirrored Ruy Lopez is not the common attack we see, White plays early Bg5 while aiming at the knight on f6, preparing to damage Black’s pawn structure. Black’s most common response is e6 but other moves are seen as well, the attack can lead to a sharp attack and Black has to play carefully.
explanations.textZh:
3...BG5？！ · Richter-Veresov 攻击

Richter-Veresov 攻击或镜像 Ruy Lopez 并不是我们所看到的常见攻击，白方在早期下 Bg5，同时瞄准 f6 上的马，准备破坏黑方的兵结构。黑方最常见的应对是e6，但也可以看到其他走法，攻击可能会导致猛攻，黑方必须谨慎下棋。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Nc3/2...d5/3. e4
explanations.text:
3. e4

White breaks open the centre with a pawn sacrifice.

3...dxe4 is a transposition into the Blackmar-Diemer gambit.

3. Nxe4 Nxe4 4. dxe4 is the alternative way to accept the gambit.

2...e6 transposes into the classical French.

History

Hübsch or Huebsch was a chess amateur who surprised Savielly Tartakower with this gambit in 1922. Emil Diemer used this opening to transpose into his favourite Blackmar-Diemer gambit from the Indian defence.
explanations.textEn:
3. e4

White breaks open the centre with a pawn sacrifice.

3...dxe4 is a transposition into the Blackmar-Diemer gambit.

3. Nxe4 Nxe4 4. dxe4 is the alternative way to accept the gambit.

2...e6 transposes into the classical French.

History

Hübsch or Huebsch was a chess amateur who surprised Savielly Tartakower with this gambit in 1922. Emil Diemer used this opening to transpose into his favourite Blackmar-Diemer gambit from the Indian defence.
explanations.textZh:
3.e4

白棋用牺牲兵打开了中心。

3...dxe4 是 Blackmar-Diemer 策略的转置。

3. Nxe4 Nxe4 4. dxe4 是接受该策略的另一种方式。

2...e6 转置为古典法语。

历史

Hübsch 或 Huebsch 是一位国际象棋业余爱好者，他在 1922 年用这一策略让萨维利·塔塔科维尔 (Savielly Tartakower) 感到惊讶。埃米尔·迪默 (Emil Diemer) 利用这个开局，将印度防守中的布莱克马尔-迪默 (Blackmar-Diemer) 策略转变为他最喜欢的策略。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Nd2
explanations.text:
Nd2 is a weak move by White where Black can play /2...e5/, the dubious Lazard Gambit, hoping that White falls into the trap 3. dxe5 Ng4 4. h3?? Ne3.

The most principled response by Black is /2...d5/.
explanations.textEn:
Nd2 is a weak move by White where Black can play /2...e5/, the dubious Lazard Gambit, hoping that White falls into the trap 3. dxe5 Ng4 4. h3?? Ne3.

The most principled response by Black is /2...d5/.
explanations.textZh:
Nd2 是白方的弱棋，黑方可以下 /2...e5/，即可疑的拉扎德弃兵，希望白方落入陷阱 3. dxe5 Ng4 4. h3?? Ne3。

黑方最有原则的回应是/2...d5/。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Nd2/2...e5
explanations.text:
2...e5?! · Lazard Gambit

In a similar fashion to the Englund Gambit, Black sacrifices their e-pawn in the hopes of playing a trap after the pawn is taken, but is considered an unsound move in perfect play. Therefore, it is a rare occurrence in a real tournament game, but is not uncommon in amateur levels of play.

3. dxe5 accepts the gambit, and capitalizes on Black's dubious move, while gaining a tempo by attacking the knight on f6.
explanations.textEn:
2...e5?! · Lazard Gambit

In a similar fashion to the Englund Gambit, Black sacrifices their e-pawn in the hopes of playing a trap after the pawn is taken, but is considered an unsound move in perfect play. Therefore, it is a rare occurrence in a real tournament game, but is not uncommon in amateur levels of play.

3. dxe5 accepts the gambit, and capitalizes on Black's dubious move, while gaining a tempo by attacking the knight on f6.
explanations.textZh:
2...e5？！ · 拉扎德策略

与英格伦开局类似，黑棋牺牲电子棋子，希望在棋子被拿走后下一个陷阱，但在完美的游戏中被认为是不健全的棋步。因此，这种情况在真正的锦标赛游戏中很少见，但在业余水平的比赛中并不罕见。

3. dxe5接受这个策略，并利用黑方可疑的棋步，同时通过攻击f6上的马来获得节奏。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. b4
explanations.text: The Neo-Polish Variation is an variation of the Indian Defense in which White commits to a push of a flank pawn instead of a center pawn. This move is not seen much in the top level because it does not benefit White in most ways. As, Black will try to play e6 and attack the pawn or play g6 into a King's Indian type of setup, it is recommended that White plays very carefully and tries to play moves like Bb2 and a3, just like if they had played b4 on the first move.
explanations.textEn: The Neo-Polish Variation is an variation of the Indian Defense in which White commits to a push of a flank pawn instead of a center pawn. This move is not seen much in the top level because it does not benefit White in most ways. As, Black will try to play e6 and attack the pawn or play g6 into a King's Indian type of setup, it is recommended that White plays very carefully and tries to play moves like Bb2 and a3, just like if they had played b4 on the first move.
explanations.textZh: 新波兰变例是印度防御的一种变体，其中白方致力于推动侧翼棋子而不是中心棋子。这一举动在高层中并不多见，因为它在大多数方面都没有给白方带来好处。由于黑方会尝试下 e6 并攻击兵，或者下 g6 进入国王的印度类型设置，建议白方非常小心地下棋，尝试下 Bb2 和 a3 之类的棋步，就像他们在第一步下 b4 一样。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Bf4
explanations.text:
2. Bf4 · Accelerated London system (Indian defence)

White develops their dark-squared bishop, so that they may play e3 to support the d4 pawn without leaving the bishop stuck behind the pawn chain.

This is the London system, a general set of moves for White that can be played against a variety of moves by Black (it is Accelerated insofar as White has played Bf4 before Nf3). Thus, 2. Bf4 can be played against both 1. d4 d5 and 1. d4 Nf6. For an introduction to the Accelerated London system, see the move order 1. d4 d5 2. Bf4.

After 2...d5, the most common reply, the two move orders (1. d4 d5 2. Bf4 Nf6 and 1. d4 Nf6 2.Bf4 d5) merge. Then, Black's main approaches are 3...c5 or 3...e6.

By virtue of having not committed a pawn to d5 yet, however, in this move order Black has a number of other approaches:

2...g6, playing King's Indian-style with ...Bg7, ...d6 and ...c5.

2...b6, to play Queen's Indian-style with ...Bb7, ...e6, ...Be7 and ...d6.

Playing both ...g6 and ...b6 to play in a Double fianchetto-style.

2...c5: after 3. e3 Qb6 Black wishes to target White's weak b2 pawn as soon as possible.

In any case, White generally plans to play e3 and c3 to support the d4 pawn, Bd3, and Nf3 then Ne5. An alternative set-up involves Nc3 instead of c3, the Jobava-Rapport London system.

explanations.textZh:
2. Bf4·加速伦敦系统（印度防御）

白方开发了他们的暗方象，这样他们就可以下 e3 来支持 d4 兵，而不会让象卡在兵链后面。

这是伦敦系统，白棋的一套通用棋步，可以对抗黑棋的各种棋步（由于白棋在 Nf3 之前下过 Bf4，所以它是加速的）。因此，2.Bf4 可以与 1.d4 d5 和 1.d4 Nf6 对抗。有关 Accelerated London 系统的介绍，请参阅移动顺序 1. d4 d5 2. Bf4。

在最常见的回复 2...d5 之后，两个移动顺序（1. d4 d5 2. Bf4 Nf6 和 1. d4 Nf6 2.Bf4 d5）合并。那么，黑方的主要走法是3...c5 或3...e6。

然而，由于尚未将棋子下到 d5，因此在此走法中黑方还有许多其他方法：

2...g6，用 ...Bg7、...d6 和 ...c5 演奏 King's Indian 风格。

2...b6，与 ...Bb7、...e6、...Be7 和 ...d6 一起演奏 Queen's Indian 风格。

同时演奏 ...g6 和 ...b6 以双 fianchetto 风格演奏。

2...c5：在3.e3 Qb6 之后，黑方希望尽快瞄准白方较弱的b2 兵。

无论如何，白方通常计划下e3和c3来支持d4兵，Bd3和Nf3，然后Ne5。另一种设置涉及 Nc3 而不是 c3，即 Jobava-Rapport London 系统。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Bf4/2...d5
explanations.text:
2...d5

Black's most common approach to combating the Accelerated London is with both Nf6 and d5, whether they began with the Indian defence 1...Nf6 or the Closed game 1...d5.

White's plans in the London system are generally to to play e3, c3, Nd2, Bd3 in some order, and plant their kingside knight on e5 via Nf3.

3. e3 is the most common move order. This defends d4 and prepares to develop Bd3. Once Nf3 is played, e.g. 3. Nf3, the opening has converged with the regular, non-accelerated London. 3. Nc3, instead of playing c3, transposes to the Rapport-Jobava London.

Black's two main approaches involve 3...c5 or 3...e6.

The idea behind the 3...e6 line is to play 4...Bd6, getting ready to castle quickly and threatening to trade off White's London bishop. White can drop their bishop back to g2, inviting Black to trade but after hxg2 White gets the semi-open h-file in return. In the e6 lines, Black's light square bishop often has difficulty developing. This approach resembles a Semi-Slav defence with colours reversed.

The ...c5 line has the idea to to prioritise ...Bf5 and ...Qb6 before finishing developing the kingside and castling. Black seeks counterplay by pressuring b2, which White left undefended when they moved their bishop early on. (White does not want to take the offered c5 pawn of course: they'd rather play c3 and let Black trade into them, so that they can keep two pawns in the centre).

Having committed to d5 already, the King's Indian-style approach with 3...g6 is less common but still playable. Black continues 4...Bg7, and 5...O-O. White usually includes h3, so there is a retreat square for their bishop on h2, and Be2.

explanations.textZh:
2...d5

黑方对抗加速伦敦最常见的方法是使用 Nf6 和 d5，无论它们是从印度防御 1...Nf6 还是封闭游戏 1...d5 开始。

白棋在伦敦体系中的计划通常是按某种顺序玩e3、c3、Nd2、Bd3，并通过Nf3将王翼骑士放置在e5上。

3. e3是最常见的走棋顺序。这捍卫了d4并准备开发Bd3。一旦播放 Nf3，例如3. Nf3，开局已与常规、非加速伦敦会合。 3. Nc3 不再播放 c3，而是移至 Rapport-Jobava London。

黑棋的两种主要方法涉及 3...c5 或 3...e6。

3...e6 线背后的想法是玩 4...Bd6，准备快速城堡并威胁要交易怀特的伦敦主教。白方可以将其象放回到 g2，邀请黑方进行交易，但在 hxg2 之后，白方得到半开放的 h 文件作为回报。在e6线中，黑方的轻方象常常难以展开。这种方法类似于颜色相反的半斯拉夫防御。

...c5 系列的想法是在完成王侧和王位的开发之前优先考虑 ...Bf5 和 ...Qb6。黑方通过向 b2 施压来寻求反击，而白方在早期移动了象时，就让 b2 处于不设防的状态。 （白棋当然不想接受所提供的 c5 棋子：他们宁愿下 c3 并让黑棋交易到它们，这样他们就可以在中间保留两个棋子）。

由于已经致力于 d5，国王的印度式 3...g6 方法不太常见，但仍然可以玩。黑方继续 4...Bg7 和 5...O-O。白方通常包括h3，因此他们的主教在h2和Be2上有一个撤退方格。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Bf4/2...d5/3. e3
explanations.text:
London System Main Line with ...d5

The London System is a solid and flexible opening system for white that can be played against various setups by black. After the moves:

1. d4 d5 2. Bf4 Nf6 3. e3 or

1. d4 Nf6 2. Bf4 d5 3. e3

The main ideas for both sides in the London System's main line are:

For White:

Development and Structure: Nf3, Be2, c3, and often Nbd2 followed by a potential e4 break or the more restrained h3 and O-O. The pawn on d4 and the pawn on e3 provide a solid central structure.

Queenside Expansion: With moves like a4-a5 or a queenside pawn storm with b4, aiming for a potential minority attack.

King Safety: Usually achieved with O-O. The rook on f1 might later swing over to the c-file or e-file.

Central Break: Depending on Black's setup, White can aim for e4 at some point.

For Black:

Challenge the Bishop: ...c5 or ...Nh5 can be played to challenge White's strong Bf4.

Development: e6 followed by Be7, O-O, and Nbd7 or Nc6. Depending on the situation, the light-squared bishop can be developed to d7, f5, or g4.

Central Control: Black usually maintains a pawn on d5 and can consider playing ...e5 under the right conditions.

Queenside Counterplay: Black can look for counterplay with moves like ...a6 and ...b5, depending on White's play.

For a general introduction to the London System, take a closer look at 1. d4 d5 2. Bf4

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Bf4/2...e6
explanations.text:
2...e6

2...e6 is a sideline. Black refrains from advancing in the centre yet and opens a line for their bishop. This position may also arise by transposition if White plays the London into Black's Horwitz defence: 1. d4 e6 2. Bf4 Nf6.

White usually continues 3. e3, though London system move orders are flexible and other moves like 3. Nf3 can be played and later transpose.

2...e6 is a move order variation that usually commits Black to playing against the London with ...d5 ...e6 and ...Nf6. This is because the pawn on e6 restricts the queen side bishop and prevents Bf5, as in the Steinitz Countergambit lines, and after e6 Black surely doesn't wish to reverse-course and play ...g6 and ...Bg7 for a King's Indian approach, leaving their d6 square weakened. Once Black plays ...d5 then play transposes. Black plans ...Bd6 to contest White's London bishop's control of e5. One move order is 3. e3 c5 4. c3 Nc6 5. Nd2 d5 6. Ngf3 Bd6 7. Bg3 O-O.

An alternative for Black is to play in a Queen's Indian defence fashion, with ...b6 and ...Bb7.

explanations.textZh:
2...e6

2...e6 是副线。黑方尚未在中间推进，而是为他们的主教打开了一条线。如果白棋将伦敦棋打入黑棋的霍维茨防御，则这种位置也可能通过换位出现： 1. d4 e6 2. Bf4 Nf6。

白棋通常会继续 3. e3，尽管伦敦系统走棋顺序很灵活，并且可以使用 3. Nf3 等其他走棋，然后进行转置。

2...e6 是一种走法顺序变化，通常要求黑棋用 ...d5 ...e6 和 ...Nf6 对抗伦敦棋。这是因为 e6 上的棋子限制了后侧主教并阻止了 Bf5，如斯坦尼茨反策略线中那样，并且在 e6 之后，黑方肯定不希望逆转方向并为国王的印度方法使用 ...g6 和 ...Bg7，从而使他们的 d6 方格被削弱。一旦黑方下...d5，则进行转置。黑方计划...Bd6 争夺白方伦敦主教对 e5 的控制权。一步顺序是 3. e3 c5 4. c3 Nc6 5. Nd2 d5 6. Ngf3 Bd6 7. Bg3 O-O。

黑方的另一种选择是采用后印度防御方式，即 ...b6 和 ...Bb7。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Bf4/2...e6/3. e3
explanations.text:
London System Indian Setup with 2. Bf4 e6

After 3. e3, White aims for a solid, unbreakable center and potential queenside expansion, while Black seeks to challenge the center and develop harmoniously, keeping multiple pawn breaks and piece maneuvers in mind. After the moves 1. d4 Nf6 2. Bf4 e6 3. e3, both sides have committed to certain pawn structures and plans:

White's Position and Plans:

Pawn Structure & Central Control:

White's pawn chain (d4-e3) is solid and tough to break. This setup supports the dark-squared bishop on f4 and restricts Black's pawn breaks.

Piece Activity:

The Bf4 targets the d6 square and is also out of the pawn chain, ensuring its active participation in the game.

Plans:

Development and King Safety: Nf3 and Bd3 are natural moves, followed by O-O.

Queenside Play: With the center secure, White can consider a queenside expansion with c4 (often after Nbd2), possibly followed by Qb3, Rc1, and a3-b4.

Center Control: Maintaining the pawn on d4 and preventing ...e5 or ...c5 breaks.

King's Side Attack: If Black fianchettoes the king's side, h2-h3 followed by g2-g4 can be a pawn storm plan.

Black's Position and Plans:

Pawn Structure & Central Control:

Black's ...e6 provides support for a potential ...d5 pawn break, directly challenging White's center.

Piece Activity:

The Nf6 is well placed, pressurizing the e4 square.

Plans:

Central Breaks: ...d5 is the most straightforward plan to challenge White's central structure.

Bishop Development: The dark-squared bishop can be developed to d6, challenging White's Bf4, or to e7. An alternative plan involves a fianchetto setup with ...b6 and ...Bb7.

Queenside Play: ...c5 can be an effective pawn break to challenge the center and open lines for the rooks and queen.

King's Side Play: If White overextends on the kingside, counterplay with ...Nh5 can challenge the Bf4 or ...f5 can be considered in some setups.

Knight Maneuvers: The knight on b8 can be developed to d7 or c6 based on the requirements of the position.

explanations.textZh:
伦敦系统印度设置 2. Bf4 e6

3. e3之后，白棋的目标是建立一个稳固的、牢不可破的中锋和潜在的后翼扩张，而黑棋则寻求挑战中锋并和谐发展，同时牢记多种棋子突破和棋子机动。在走棋 1. d4 Nf6 2. Bf4 e6 3. e3 之后，双方都承诺了某些棋子结构和计划：

白方的立场和计划：

典当结构和中央控制：

白方的棋子链（d4-e3）坚固且难以打破。此设置支持 f4 上的暗方象并限制黑方的兵断。

作品活动：

Bf4 的目标是 d6 方格，并且也处于典当链之外，确保其积极参与游戏。

计划：

发育和King Safety：Nf3和Bd3是自然走法，其次是O-O。

后翼玩法：在中锋安全的情况下，白方可以考虑使用 c4（通常在 Nbd2 之后）进行后翼扩张，随后可能是 Qb3、Rc1 和 a3-b4。

中心控制：将棋子维持在 d4 上并防止 ...e5 或 ...c5 中断。

王方攻击：如果黑方先攻王方，则 h2-h3 紧随其后的 g2-g4 可以是典当风暴计划。

黑方的立场和计划：

典当结构和中央控制：

黑方的 ...e6 为潜在的 ...d5 兵突破提供了支持，直接挑战白方的中锋。

作品活动：

Nf6 位置很好，给 e4 方块加压。

计划：

中路突破：...d5是挑战白方中路结构的最直接的方案。

主教发展：暗方主教可以发展到d6，挑战白方的Bf4，或发展到e7。另一种计划涉及使用 ...b6 和 ...Bb7 进行 fianchetto 设置。

后侧打法： ...c5 可以成为挑战中路的有效典当，并为车和后提供开放路线。

王侧打法：如果白方在王侧过度延伸，则在某些设置中可以考虑用 ...Nh5 反击 Bf4 或 ...f5。

骑士演习：b8上的骑士可以根据位置的要求发展到d7或c6。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Bf4/2...e6/3. e3/3...b6
explanations.text:
3...b6

3...b6 prepares to fianchetto the queenside bishop. From b7, the bishop will help control the centre from afar.

Black is playing in a Queen's Indian defence style, an opening that usually arises after 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 b6.

As usual in the London system, White's plans are to play Nf3, Bd3, and Nd2 in any order.

Black will fianchetto their queenside bishop and develop their kingside bishop to e7. As they have not committed to ...d5 yet, Black is able to later play ...d6 to control the e5 square and end White's ambition of planting their knight on e5.

3...b6

3...b6 准备向后翼主教发起攻击。从b7开始，主教将帮助远程控制中心。

黑棋采用后印度防御风格，这种开局通常出现在 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 b6 之后。

与伦敦体系中的惯例一样，怀特的计划是以任何顺序玩 Nf3、Bd3 和 Nd2。

黑棋将击败他们的后翼主教并将他们的王翼主教发展到e7。由于他们还没有承诺 ...d5，黑方可以稍后下 ...d6 来控制 e5 方格并结束白方将马种植在 e5 上的野心。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Bf4/2...e6/3. e3/3...d5
explanations.text:
London System Main Line with 3. ...e6

In the London System, White aims for a solid, flexible pawn structure and develops their dark-squared bishop early to f4.

When Black responds with 1. d4 Nf6 2. Bf4 d5 3. e3 e6, they aim for:

A solid pawn chain in the center while also developing their pieces.

A straightforward setup that avoids complex theory, making it suitable for amateur players and those familiar with Queen's Gambit Declined structures.

Achieving a comfortable position and, rather than going for an immediate pawn break, they plan for one in the midgame, allowing for a more positional and strategic battle.

This setup can result in a closed game, and Black might look to expand on the queenside or prepare a central break with ...e5 or ...c5 later in the game. Overall, the setup is about achieving a solid position without entering into deep theoretical battles and also keeping options open for different plans based on how White proceeds.

伦敦系统主线 3. ...e6

在伦敦体系中，白棋的目标是建立一个坚实、灵活的棋子结构，并将他们的暗方象早期发展到 f4。

当黑方回应 1. d4 Nf6 2. Bf4 d5 3. e3 e6 时，他们的目标是：

他们获得一个舒适的位置，而不是立即休息，而是在游戏中期计划休息，以便进行更具位置性和战略性的战斗。

这种设置可能会导致一场封闭的比赛，黑方可能会寻求在后翼扩张，或者在比赛后期用 ...e5 或 ...c5 准备中央突破。总体而言，该设置是为了在不进入深入的理论斗争的情况下获得稳固的地位，并根据怀特的进展情况为不同的计划保留选择余地。

explanations.text:
London System Main Line with Black ...e6 and ...c5

In the London System, following the moves 1. d4 Nf6 2. Bf4 e6 3. e3 d5 4. Nd2, White's strategy emphasizes proactive queenside development for defensive purposes and capitalizes on the activity of the dark-squared bishop to press for an advantage. White's strategy is based on the following core principles:

Queenside Development for Defense: By proactively developing pieces on the queenside, White ensures a robust defense of the b2 pawn. This pawn often becomes vulnerable to attacks, especially when Black aims for ...Qb6, putting direct pressure on it.

Leveraging the Active Bishop: The placement of the dark-squared bishop on f4 grants White a dynamic piece that can exert influence across the board. Its active positioning enhances White's prospects in both the middlegame and the endgame.

Counteracting the Queen’s Gambit Declined Approach: While Black can attempt to adopt the structure and plans of the Queen's Gambit Declined, this often turns favorable for White. With the dark-squared bishop already actively placed outside the pawn chain, White generally retains a minor advantage, especially as the game transitions into endgame scenarios.
