explanations.textZh:
6.bxc3

椒盐卷饼开局（非官方名称，国际象棋开局百科全书未承认）是一种有点可疑和半晦涩的开局，它允许白棋玩 2 种不同类型的位置游戏，否则这些游戏不会出现在 6.Qxc3 之后的主线中。虽然主教采取后更好的行动是 Qxc3，但中等深度的 Stockfish 18 将其评估为完全相等 (0.0 – -0.1)。

6…dxc4？！

虽然 6…dxc4?!，采取自由棋子，看起来是这个位置上的最佳走法，但引擎将其评估为该位置上的第四个最佳走法，放弃了黑色所拥有的任何一点优势。这是因为白棋在这个位置的下一步棋是e4！获得中央空间的黑色将不会获得回报，并计划去e5攻击骑士。

这个立场有点类似于所接受的后弃兵策略，但有一些关键的区别。

出局的棋子不会被赢回来，因为它可以用 b5 防御。

c 棋子（以前是 take 之前的 b 棋子）保护 d 棋子并阻止黑色 c 棋子前进。

女王代替骑士支持e4推

有趣的是，与公认的皇后开局中的基本理论相反，主线是用 7...b5 来防守弱兵，因为在 8.a4（白棋的最佳棋步）之后，保持黑棋平局的唯一棋步是 8...Bb7！对 e-pawn 施加压力，但更好的是对长对角线施加永久压力。如果/当白色城堡时，由于后侧的弱点，他们（100次中有99次）必须在王侧城堡，并且将来如果e兵移动，浅色方形主教将始终将目光投向国王。

6…O-O

O-O 是引擎最喜欢的举动（在云深度上），许多对此策略的良好回复。 7.cxd5？对于白棋来说，不立即失败是一个非常可疑和危险的举动。这是因为：7...exd5之后，e4不再是白棋的棋步，而且无论你下什么棋，c5！是立即反应；后侧非常弱，白色不发达。

6...O-O 之后，引擎会选择两种简单的走法：7. e3，支持弱兵或 7. Nf3！？重新邀请这个策略并开发一个作品。如果黑方拿走“自由”棋子，他们的情况会更糟，因为 8. e4!带有之前没有的毒液。现在白方可以主动进攻。

e3 和 Nf3 之后的最佳走法是 c5，这是一种非常不可思议的 Tarrasch 类型的位置，其中白棋在 c2 上有一个皇后，在 c3 和 c4 上有双兵。

在播放 e3 和 Nf3 后（例如 6... O-O 7. e3 7... c5 8. Nf3），计算机推荐 b6，接下来的台词本质上是深不可测的卡夫卡风格，其中： 8... b6 9. dxc5！？ 9...Ba6！？ 10.cxd5！？ 10...Bxf1 11.Kxf1！？ 11...Qxd5 12.cxb6！ 12... axb6。

6...c5

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nc3/3...Bb4/4. e3
explanations.text:
Nimzo-Indian Defence, Rubinstein Variation

4. e3

White assesses that an immediate 4...Bxc3 is not a threat, but also that 4. a3, provoking the capture, is not necessary (yet). Instead, 4. e3 simply clears the way for White's light-squared bishop to develop, usually to d3, where it helps control the all-important e4 square. Black has three main responses:

4...O-O is the most common. Since Black will never castle queenside in a Nimzo-Indian, castling kingside now is a useful but still highly flexible move.

4...c5 puts pressure on White's center immediately. Taking on c5 and accepting tripled isolated pawns (after ...Bxc3 bxc3) is right out of the question, and pushing d5 now simply creates a target, so White instead continues his development and leaves the tension.

4...b6 is the St. Petersburg Variation (not to be confused with the Leningrad Variation). This move prepares to strengthen Black's control of e4 yet further by fianchettoing a bishop to b7, though ...Ba6 is not yet out of the question.

In all three cases White has a choice between 5. Nge2 and 5. Bd3.

explanations.textZh:
尼姆佐-印度防御，鲁宾斯坦变例

4.e3

白方评估认为，立即的 4...Bxc3 不是威胁，但引发捕获的 4.a3 也没有必要（目前）。相反，4. e3 只是为白方的光方象发展扫清了道路，通常是发展到 d3，它有助于控制最重要的 e4 方格。黑方主要有以下三种应对方式：

4...O-O 是最常见的。由于黑方永远不会在尼姆佐-印度棋中对王侧进行易位，因此现在对王侧易位是一个有用但仍然高度灵活的着法。

4...c5 立即对白方中锋施加压力。拿下c5并接受三重孤立兵（在...Bxc3 bxc3之后）是不可能的，而推动d5现在只是创建一个目标，所以怀特继续他的发展并留下紧张局势。

4...b6 是圣彼得堡变奏曲（不要与列宁格勒变奏曲混淆）。此举准备通过将主教击至 b7 来进一步加强黑方对 e4 的控制，尽管……Ba6 还不是不可能。

在所有三种情况下，白方都可以在 5.Nge2 和 5.Bd3 之间进行选择。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nc3/3...Bb4/4. f3
explanations.text:
4. f3 · Kmoch Variation

4. f3 enters the aggressive, and increasingly common, Kmoch variation of the Nimzo-Indian Defence. White moves their pawn to f3 with a very clear idea; to advance with e4 and gain a massive pawn center, suffocating Black's army. This is one of the most aggressive and dangerous weapons for Black to face, and Black needs to abandon some of their key plans in order to combat the serious threat behind the f3 move.

With the plan of f3, e4, and eventually e5 to scare away Black's king knight, White gains a colossal pawn center. However, the Kmoch variation carries several risks. f3 is not a developing move; in fact, it's move that weakens White's kingside shelter and risks creating holes near White's king which Black could exploit later on. Furthermore, White's colossal center can be struck at by Black's pawn breaks, potentially leaving White's center flimsy and vulnerable to attack. Black has several ways of countering the Kmoch variation.

4...d5, in similar fashion to the Queen's Gambit Declined, clamps down on the e4-square. With this approach, Black looks to stop White's e4 move at all costs, hindering White's central expansion.

4...c5, in similar fashion to the Benoni Defence, strikes at White's center with a flank pawn. With this approach, Black forces White's center to overextend with 5. d5 and can even undermine the center further with b5 at some point. Note how this approach allows White to play the move 6. e4; Black looks to demonstrate that White's overextended center will become a huge target for Black's superior piece development.

4. f3·克莫赫变例

4. f3 进入进攻性且日益常见的尼姆佐-印度防御的克莫赫变体。白方以非常清晰的思路将棋子移至f3；以e4推进并获得一个巨大的兵中心，窒息黑方的军队。这是黑方要面对的最具侵略性和危险性的武器之一，黑方需要放弃一些关键计划才能对抗f3棋背后的严重威胁。

通过f3、e4和最终e5的计划吓跑黑方的王马，白方获得了一个巨大的兵中心。然而，Kmoch 变体存在一些风险。 f3 不是发展棋；事实上，这一举动削弱了白棋王翼的庇护，并有可能在白棋国王附近造成漏洞，而黑棋稍后可以利用这些漏洞。此外，白方巨大的中心可能会被黑方的兵断击中，从而可能使白方的中心变得脆弱且容易受到攻击。黑棋有几种对抗克莫赫变异的方法。

4...d5，与后弃兵类似，压制 e4 方格。通过这种方法，黑方希望不惜一切代价阻止白方的 e4 棋步，从而阻碍白方的中央扩张。

4...c5，与伯诺尼防御类似，用侧翼棋子攻击白方的中心。通过这种方法，黑方用 5.d5 迫使白方中心过度延伸，甚至可以在某些时候用 b5 进一步破坏中心。注意这种方法如何让白方下棋 6. e4;黑棋希望证明白棋过度延伸的中心将成为黑棋高级棋子发展的巨大目标。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nf3
explanations.text:
Indian Defence with e6, Nf3

3. Nf3 develops a piece and contributes to White's fight for the center of the board. This move strengthens the d4 and e5 squares and brings White a move closer to castling kingside. Nf3 blocks the f-pawn, which can be a powerful lever for White in some lines, but White has many other options as well. This continuation is often chosen by White players who are trying to avoid the Nimzo-Indian Defence, 3. Nc3 Bb4. 3...Bb4+ is still possible after 3. Nf3, but this usually leads to the Bogo-Indian Defence, which has a much poorer theoretical reputation for Black than the Nimzo-Indian.

Because it blocks the f-pawn, does not support the e4 pawn break, and does not fight for the d5 square, 3. Nf3 is a little more passive on White's part than 3. Nc3. Nevertheless, it is solid, and there are many ways for White to get a quiet, positional advantage. Apart from the Bogo-Indian, Black can aim for the Queen's Indian or Benoni as well as the usual transpositions:

3...b6 - The Queen's Indian (QID). This move is quiet and aims at equality via active piece play, trades in the center, and freeing pawn breaks such as ...c5, ...d5 or even ...e5 (usually utilizing ...d6 as preparation for this)

3...d5 - as always, the Queen's Gambit Declined (QGD) transposition is in the air.

3...c5 - is the Benoni... This is one of the more appealing paths to the Benoni as it avoids the dangerous f2-f4 lines.

explanations.textZh:
印度的 e6、Nf3 防御

3. Nf3发展出一颗棋子，为白棋争夺棋盘中心做出贡献。这一棋强化了 d4 和 e5 方格，使白方更接近王翼易位。 Nf3 阻挡了 f 兵，这在某些行中可以成为白方的强大杠杆，但白方还有许多其他选择。这种延续经常被试图避开尼姆佐-印度防御的白人玩家选择，3. Nc3 Bb4。 3...Bb4+ 在 3. Nf3 之后仍然是可能的，但这通常会导致 Bogo-Indian 防御，对于 Black 来说，Bogo-Indian 防御的理论声誉比 Nimzo-Indian 防御要差得多。

因为它阻挡了 f 兵，不支持 e4 兵突破，并且不争夺 d5 方格，所以 3. Nf3 对白方来说比 3. Nc3 更被动一些。尽管如此，它还是很稳固的，而且白方有很多方法可以获得安静的位置优势。除了波戈印第安人之外，黑棋还可以瞄准后印第安人或贝诺尼以及通常的换位：

3...b6 - 女王印第安人 (QID)。此步棋是安静的，旨在通过积极的棋子游戏、中心交易以及释放典当来实现平等，例如 ...c5、...d5 甚至 ...e5（通常利用 ...d6 作为准备）

3...d5 - 一如既往，后弃兵（QGD）换位悬而未决。

3...c5 - 是伯诺尼...这是通往伯诺尼更有吸引力的路径之一，因为它避免了危险的 f2-f4 线。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nf3/3...b6
explanations.text:
Queen's Indian Defence

The Queen's Indian Defence is a popular and fairly modern opening whereby black quickly develops his queenside bishop, either by fianchettoing it on b7 to contest the long diagonal, or on a6 to put pressure on white's c-pawn.

It has been employed regularly by a number of top players including former world champions like Anatoly Karpov and Viswanathan Anand.
explanations.textEn:
Queen's Indian Defence

It has been employed regularly by a number of top players including former world champions like Anatoly Karpov and Viswanathan Anand.
explanations.textZh:
女王的印第安人防御

后印式防御是一种流行且相当现代的开局，黑棋可以通过在 b7 上用剑来对抗长对角线，或者在 a6 上对白棋的 c 兵施加压力，从而快速发展他的后侧主教。

它已被许多顶级选手定期使用，包括前世界冠军阿纳托利·卡尔波夫和维斯瓦纳坦·阿南德。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nf3/3...b6/4. Bf4
explanations.text:
Queen's Indian Defence - London System (Miles Variation)

In essence, in this variation, White seeks central control and space, with potential kingside attacking ideas, while Black adopts a hypermodern defense, allowing White's central occupation but preparing to challenge and undermine it later.

White's Strategy:

Central Control: With 1. d4 and 2. c4, White immediately asserts control over the center. The aim is to gain space and restrict Black's central pawn breaks.

Piece Development: The knight on f3 and the bishop on f4 represent optimal development. The Nf3 knight supports the d4 pawn and prepares for e2-e3, while the Bf4 bishop is developed outside the pawn chain, exerting pressure on the c7 pawn.

Flexibility: White's setup allows for various pawn structures and middle game plans, ranging from the traditional d4-c4 pawn duo, a potential d5 push, or even transitioning into other Queen's Pawn openings.

Kingside Potential: With the bishop developed to f4 early, White can consider ideas like e2-e3 followed by Bd3, potentially supporting a later kingside pawn storm with moves like g2-g4, especially if Black has already castled kingside.

Black's Strategy:

Hypermodern Approach: With ...Nf6, ...e6, and ...b6, Black takes a hypermodern approach, allowing White to occupy the center initially with the aim of counter-attacking and undermining White's center later.

Flexible Pawn Structure: Black's setup, especially with ...b6, hints at the idea of fianchettoing the queen's bishop with ...Bb7. This places pressure on the e4 square and supports potential central pawn breaks like ...d5 or ...c5.

Central Counterplay: Despite allowing White to occupy the center, Black aims for counterplay with moves like ...d5 or ...c5. The knight on f6 and the potential bishop on b7 work in tandem to challenge White's center.

King Safety: Black often aims for a short castle, ensuring the king's safety while also connecting the rooks. Depending on the course of the game, Black might even consider a queenside castle if the situation allows.

Active Piece Play: Black will look to develop the remaining minor pieces (e.g., ...Bb4+ or ...Bd6, and ...Nc6 or ...Nd7) to maximize their activity and coordinate potential counter-attacks.

Piece Development: The knight on f3 and the bishop on f4 represent optimal development. The Nf3 knight supports the d4 pawn and prepares for e2-e3, while the Bf4 bishop is developed outside the pawn chain, exerting pressure on the c7 pawn.

Flexibility: White's setup allows for various pawn structures and middle game plans, ranging from the traditional d4-c4 pawn duo, a potential d5 push, or even transitioning into other Queen's Pawn openings.

Kingside Potential: With the bishop developed to f4 early, White can consider ideas like e2-e3 followed by Bd3, potentially supporting a later kingside pawn storm with moves like g2-g4, especially if Black has already castled kingside.

Black's Strategy:

Hypermodern Approach: With ...Nf6, ...e6, and ...b6, Black takes a hypermodern approach, allowing White to occupy the center initially with the aim of counter-attacking and undermining White's center later.

Flexible Pawn Structure: Black's setup, especially with ...b6, hints at the idea of fianchettoing the queen's bishop with ...Bb7. This places pressure on the e4 square and supports potential central pawn breaks like ...d5 or ...c5.

Central Counterplay: Despite allowing White to occupy the center, Black aims for counterplay with moves like ...d5 or ...c5. The knight on f6 and the potential bishop on b7 work in tandem to challenge White's center.

King Safety: Black often aims for a short castle, ensuring the king's safety while also connecting the rooks. Depending on the course of the game, Black might even consider a queenside castle if the situation allows.

Active Piece Play: Black will look to develop the remaining minor pieces (e.g., ...Bb4+ or ...Bd6, and ...Nc6 or ...Nd7) to maximize their activity and coordinate potential counter-attacks.
explanations.textZh:
女王印度防御 - 伦敦系统（英里变体）

本质上，在这种变化中，白棋寻求中央控制和空间，具有潜在的王翼进攻想法，而黑棋则采用超现代的防守，允许白棋占据中央位置，但准备稍后挑战和破坏它。

白方策略：

中央控制：通过 1. d4 和 2. c4，白方立即控制了中央。目的是获得空间并限制黑方的中央棋子突破。

棋子发展：f3上的马和f4上的主教代表最佳发展。 Nf3骑士支援d4棋子，为e2-e3做好准备，而Bf4主教则在棋子链外发展，对c7棋子施加压力。

灵活性：白方的设置允许各种棋子结构和中间游戏计划，从传统的 d4-c4 棋子二人组，潜在的 d5 推，甚至过渡到其他后棋开局。

王边潜力：随着象早早发展到f4，白方可以考虑诸如e2-e3，然后是Bd3之类的想法，可能会通过g2-g4等走法支持后来的王边兵风暴，特别是如果黑方已经占领了王边。

黑棋策略：

超现代方法：通过...Nf6、...e6 和...b6，黑方采取超现代方法，让白方首先占据中心，目的是随后反击并削弱白方的中心。

灵活的兵结构：黑方的布局，尤其是...b6，暗示了用...Bb7 击败后王主教的想法。这对 e4 方格施加了压力，并支持潜在的中央棋子突破，例如 ...d5 或 ...c5。

中央反击：尽管允许白棋占据中心，但黑棋的目标是通过 ...d5 或 ...c5 等棋子进行反击。 f6 上的马和 b7 上的潜在主教联手挑战白方中锋。

王安全：黑方经常瞄准一座矮堡，确保王的安全，同时也连接车。根据棋局的进程，如果情况允许，黑方甚至可能考虑建立后侧城堡。

活跃棋子玩法：黑方将寻求开发剩余的小棋子（例如，...Bb4+ 或 ...Bd6，以及 ...Nc6 或 ...Nd7），以最大化其活动并协调潜在的反击。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nf3/3...b6/4. g3
explanations.text:
Queen's Indian Defense

4. g3

With this move, White decides to challenge the h1-a8 diagonal immediately and fianchetto his own light-squared bishop to counter black's.

Black can now play:

4...Bb7 (Old Main Line), a standard developing move. White can then respond with Bg2 and Nc3. The line continues: 5. Bg2 Be7 6. 0-0 0-0 7. Nc3 Ne4 8. Qc2 Nxc3 9. Qxc3. White now has a spacial advantage, but black's position is solid. Black can choose many ways for counterplay, including 9...c5 (the most common), 9...f5, or 9...Be4. These lines are known for their drawish tendencies and are currently used as drawing weapons. However, there have been developed a few ways to unbalance the play in the Old Main Line:

6. Nc3, which postpones castling for the e2-e4 and d4-d5 thrusts.

7. d5!?, which gives up a pawn. However, white can play 8. Nh4, threatening to regain the pawn or play Nf5. If black keeps the pawn, white gets plenty of compensation for it.

8. Bd2, which defends the knight on c3 and threatens a d4-d5 push.

That was, until, the Modern Main Line came by:

4...Ba6, attacking the c-pawn. This is a bit of a nuisance for white, who cannot comfortably defend the pawn with the natural e2-e3 because the bishop is already committed to g2.

Also possible is:

4...Bb4+, echoing the Bogo-Indian and Nimzo-Indian defences. White can interpose with the bishop or knight. However, this leaves black with a slightly passive position. Nevertheless, this is solid as well.

There are other options available, though these are less likely to be encountered:

4...c5, immediately challenging the (central) d-pawn. This leads to pawn structures specific to the Benoni or to variations with a late c5 of the Queen's Indian, if both sides choose to neglect this central challenge and continue to develop

4...c6, leads to a Closed Catalan variation after Black's immediate 5...d5 follow-up

女王的印第安人防御

4.g3

通过这一步棋，白方决定立即挑战 h1-a8 对角线，并用自己的浅方象来对抗黑棋。

黑方现在可以下棋：

4...Bb7（旧主线），标准发展动作。然后白方可以用 Bg2 和 Nc3 做出回应。该行继续： 5. Bg2 Be7 6. 0-0 0-0 7. Nc3 Ne4 8. Qc2 Nxc3 9. Qxc3。白棋现在拥有空间优势，但黑棋的地位稳固。黑方可以选择多种反击方式，包括 9...c5（最常见）、9...f5 或 9...Be4。这些线条以其吸引人的倾向而闻名，目前被用作吸引武器。然而，已经开发了几种方法来平衡旧主线的游戏：

6. Nc3，推迟 e2-e4 和 d4-d5 推力的易位。

7. d5!?，放弃一个棋子。然而，白棋可以下8.Nh4，威胁夺回棋子或下Nf5。如果黑方保留棋子，白方将获得大量补偿。

8. Bd2，防守c3上的骑士并威胁进行d4-d5推击。

直到现代主线到来：

4...Ba6，攻击c兵。这对白棋来说有点麻烦，因为白棋已经下注了 g2，所以白棋无法轻松地用自然 e2-e3 防守棋子。

还可能的是：

4...Bb4+，与博戈-印度和尼姆佐-印度防御相呼应。白棋可以介入主教或马。然而，这使得黑棋处于稍微被动的位置。尽管如此，这也是可靠的。

还有其他可用选项，尽管这些选项不太可能遇到：

4...c5，立即挑战（中央）d-pawn。如果双方选择忽视这一核心挑战并继续发展，这将导致伯诺尼特有的典当结构或与女王印第安人的后期 c5 的变化

4...c6，在黑方立即跟进 5...d5 后导致封闭式加泰罗尼亚变体

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...e6/3. Nf3/3...Bb4
explanations.text:
Bogo-Indian Defence

Black plays Bb4+ and White must block against the check. If White plays Nc3, the opening transposes into a Nimzo-Indian Defence. If instead White decides to block the check with Bd2, the resulting complications are likely to cause an exchange of pieces. Positions tend to be roughly equal, with trades (and, consequently, draws) being very common.
explanations.textEn:
Bogo-Indian Defence

explanations.textZh:
博戈-印度防御

黑方下 Bb4+，白方必须阻止过让。如果白方下 Nc3，开局就会转变为尼姆佐-印度防御。相反，如果白方决定用 Bd2 阻止过牌，那么由此产生的复杂情况很可能会导致棋子交换。头寸往往大致相等，交易（因此平局）也很常见。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...e6/3. g3
explanations.text:
3. g3 · Catalan Opening

This is the Catalan Opening, named after the Spanish region of Catalonia, when Grandmaster Savielly Tartakower was asked, at the Barcelona tournament of 1929, to invent an opening system in honor of the region's chess history. Usually, the game continues 3...d5 4. Nf3. The Catalan then has two main branches, the Open Variation and the Closed Variation. In the Open Variation, Black takes the pawn on c4. This gives White strong pressure on Black's queenside, thanks to the fianchettoed bishop on g2. In the Closed Variation, Black retains their strong-point on d5, attempting to block out the bishop on g2, but stays passive.

Usually, the game continues 3...d5 4. Nf3. The Catalan then has two main branches, the Open Variation and the Closed Variation. In the Open Variation, Black takes the pawn on c4. This gives White strong pressure on Black's queenside, thanks to the fianchettoed bishop on g2. In the Closed Variation, Black retains their strong-point on d5, attempting to block out the bishop on g2, but stays passive.
explanations.textZh:
3. g3·加泰罗尼亚开赛

这就是加泰罗尼亚公开赛，以西班牙加泰罗尼亚地区命名，当时大师萨维利·塔塔科维尔 (Savielly Tartakower) 在 1929 年巴塞罗那锦标赛上被要求发明一种开局系统，以纪念该地区的国际象棋历史。通常，游戏继续 3...d5 4. Nf3。加泰罗尼亚语有两个主要分支：开放变体和封闭变体。在开放变例中，黑方拿走 c4 上的棋子。这给了白方对黑方后翼的强大压力，这要归功于 g2 上的双足主教。在封闭变例中，黑方保留了 d5 上的强点，试图在 g2 上阻挡象，但仍处于被动。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...e6/3. g3/3...Bb4
explanations.text:
Bogo-Catalan Defense

Black plays Bb4+, the same move as the Bogo-Indian Defense, and White must block the check. If White plays Nc3, the opening transposes into a Nimzo-Indian Defense, Romanishin Variation. The Bogo-Catalan Defense is the same move order as the Bogo-Indian, but against the Catalan move of 3. g3 instead of 3. Nf3.

Much like the Bogo-Indian, the Bogo-Catalan's mainlines are infamous for leading to several draws. However, unlike the regular Bogo-Indian, the Bogo-Catalan Defense has a couple of interesting sidelines which lead to imbalanced, fighting games against the Catalan Opening.

Bogo-Catalan Defense

The Bogo-Catalan Defense is the same move order as the Bogo-Indian, but against the Catalan move of 3. g3 instead of 3. Nf3.

Much like the Bogo-Indian, the Bogo-Catalan's mainlines are infamous for leading to several draws. However, unlike the regular Bogo-Indian, the Bogo-Catalan Defense has a couple of interesting sidelines which lead to imbalanced, fighting games against the Catalan Opening.
explanations.textZh:
博戈-加泰罗尼亚防御

黑棋下 Bb4+，与 Bogo-Indian 防御相同，白棋必须阻止检查。如果白棋下 Nc3，开局就会转入尼姆佐-印度防御、罗马尼辛变例。 Bogo-Catalan 防御与 Bogo-Indian 的移动顺序相同​​，但针对的是 Catalan 移动 3.g3 而不是 3.Nf3。

与博戈-印度赛很相似，博戈-加泰罗尼亚赛的主线因导致多次平局而臭名昭著。然而，与常规的博戈-印度防守不同，博戈-加泰罗尼亚防守有一些有趣的边线，这些边线会导致加泰罗尼亚开局时的不平衡、战斗性比赛。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...e6/3. g4
explanations.text:
3. g4? · Devin gambit

This unorthodox gambit involves White offering the g-pawn early to disrupt Black's development and seize central control. After 3...Nxg4, White aims to play e4, establishing a strong pawn center and opening lines for rapid piece activity.

Though rarely seen at high levels, the Devin gambit has been employed in classical play by GM Shakhriyar Mamedyarov, notably against Andrey Esipenko in the 2022 Tata Steel Masters tournament. Its surprise value and aggressive nature make it a compelling choice for players looking to catch opponents off guard and steer the game into sharp, tactical waters.

Compare 2. g4, the Bronstein gambit.

explanations.textZh:
3.g4？ ·德文的策略

这种非正统的策略涉及白方尽早提供 g 兵来扰乱黑方的发展并夺取中央控制权。 3...Nxg4 之后，白方的目标是下 e4，建立强大的兵中心并为快速棋子活动打开线。

尽管在高水平比赛中很少见到，但德文策略已被 GM Shakhriyar Mamedyarov 在经典比赛中使用，特别是在 2022 年塔塔钢铁大师赛中对阵安德烈·埃西彭科 (Andrey Esipenko)。其令人惊讶的价值和侵略性使其成为那些希望让对手措手不及并引导游戏进入尖锐的战术水域的玩家的一个令人信服的选择。

比较 2. g4，布朗斯坦策略。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...g6
explanations.text:
2...g6 · King's Indian Defence

With 2...g6, Black commits to a hypermodern development strategy. They will fianchetto their dark-squared bishop with ...Bg7 and attempt to exert pressure on White's center with pieces and timely pawn breaks. After 2...g6 certain themes are already evident. Preservation of the dark-square bishop will be vital for Black's safety after castling kingside. 2...g6 weakens the dark squares around Black's king; without the dark-square bishop to control squares like f6 and h6, these weaknesses can be fatal. The g7 bishop is not purely a defensive piece, however. White must be aware that opening the center by pawn exchanges may very well unleash the bishop's power by giving it a clear diagonal towards White's queenside.

2...g6 will almost certainly lead to either a King's Indian Defence or a Grunfeld Defence.

In the King's Indian Defence, Black castles kingside as quickly as possible with a fianchettoed structure, in doing so it will allow White to have pawn presence in the centre. Black will then do their best to claim as much as they can back with their own pawns, often chipping away at the residual White presence. A strategist's playground.

While in the Grunfeld, Black uses 2...g6 to wait for Nc3 by White where he will follow with ...d5. Black's play will be the dark diagonal, usually with the help of the move ...c5, while White's advantage will be his broad centre - Hypermodernism exemplified.

explanations.textZh:
2...g6 · 国王的印度防御

通过 2...g6，Black 致力于超现代的发展战略。他们将用...Bg7 攻击他们的暗方主教，并尝试通过棋子和及时的兵突破对白方的中心施加压力。 2...g6 之后，某些主题已经很明显。保护暗方主教对于黑方在王翼易位后的安全至关重要。 2...g6 削弱黑王周围的暗方；如果没有暗方主教来控制像 f6 和 h6 这样的方格，这些弱点可能是致命的。然而，g7 主教并不是纯粹的防御性棋子。白方必须意识到，通过棋子交换打开中心很可能会释放主教的力量，因为它给了白方后翼一条清晰的对角线。

2...g6 几乎肯定会导致国王印第安防御或格伦菲尔德防御。

在国王的印第安防御中，黑棋以剑齿形结构尽快在王侧建立城堡，这样做将使白棋在中心拥有兵位。然后，黑棋将尽最大努力用自己的棋子反击尽可能多的棋子，通常会削弱白棋剩余的存在。战略家的游乐场。

在格伦菲尔德时，黑方使用 2...g6 等待白方的 Nc3，然后他将使用 ...d5。黑方的玩法将是黑暗对角线，通常借助 ...c5 棋子，而白方的优势将是他的宽中锋 - 超现代主义的例证。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...g6/3. Nc3
explanations.text:
3. Nc3

White intends to play e4 with this move. Developing this knight first also keeps options open for being able to play multiple lines against the King's Indian.

One of Black's most powerful weapon here is the Grünfeld Defence with /3...d5/. The main variation, 4. cxd5 Nxd5 5. e4 Nxc3 6. bxc3 Bg7 leads to a typical hypermodern situation where White has a powerful center that Black will have to attack from a distance with their dark-squared bishop and a ...c5 pawn break.

/3...Bg7/ and /3...d6/ stick to the classical ideas behind the King's Indian, another venerable and popular opening.
explanations.textEn:
3. Nc3

White intends to play e4 with this move. Developing this knight first also keeps options open for being able to play multiple lines against the King's Indian.

One of Black's most powerful weapon here is the Grünfeld Defence with /3...d5/. The main variation, 4. cxd5 Nxd5 5. e4 Nxc3 6. bxc3 Bg7 leads to a typical hypermodern situation where White has a powerful center that Black will have to attack from a distance with their dark-squared bishop and a ...c5 pawn break.

/3...Bg7/ and /3...d6/ stick to the classical ideas behind the King's Indian, another venerable and popular opening.
explanations.textZh:
3.NC3

白棋打算用这步棋下e4。首先开发这位骑士也为能够与国王的印第安人打多线比赛保留了选择余地。

黑方最强大的武器之一是带有 /3...d5/ 的格林菲尔德防御。主要的变体，4.cxd5 Nxd5 5.e4 Nxc3 6.bxc3 Bg7 导致了一种典型的超现代局面，其中白棋拥有强大的中锋，而黑棋必须使用暗方主教和 ...c5 兵突破从远处进行攻击。

/3...Bg7/ 和 /3...d6/ 坚持 King's Indian 背后的经典思想，这是另一个受人尊敬且受欢迎的开局。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...g6/3. Nc3/3...d5
explanations.text:
3...d5 · Grünfeld Defence

This is the classic, and most common, starting position of the Grünfeld Defence, although d5 can be delayed if White has delayed e4 which typically happens if Nf3 is played at some stage. Most notably, the famous Game of the Century by Bobby Fischer originated from the Grünfeld Defence.

The Grünfeld Defence often becomes incredibly sharp and tactical due to Black quickly striking at White's vulnerable center. Unlike the King's Indian Defence, where Black immediately fianchettoes the king bishop, here Black immediately plays 3...d5 to stop e4 (at least temporarily) and challenge White's occupation of the center. White has a range of choices, the main one is to exchange the pawns on d5 and follow up with e4 in order to displace Black's pieces.

During the 1920s, European chess was in revolution, with the entry of the Nimzo-Indian Defence into mainstream opening theory. The masters of the day termed this the "Modern style". Then, in 1922, a well-known master named Ernst Grünfeld came up with a new system that started bashing the great masters of the day, including Kostic, Sämisch, Colle, and Alekhine (who famously threw his king across the room in frustration after losing to it). This came to be known as the new "hypermodern" style, and Grünfeld, true to hypermodern tastes, showed in pure form how the previously accepted classical dogma could be wrong, and that a pawn center could be an object of attack as well as a boon.

The main battleground of philosophies is the Exchange Variation, 4. cxd5 Nxd5 5. e4 Nxc3 6. bxc3. White's pawn center gains space, but Black has excellent play along the long, dark diagonal from a1 to h8, and can eventually target d4 with moves like ...Bg7, ...Rd8, ...c5, ...Nc6, and occasionally ...Qa5. Eventually he may also bring a bishop to fianchetto on the other diagonal, targeting e4.

The more classical moves are /4. Nf3/, /4. Bf4/, and /4. Qb3/, which are more conservative ways to fight Black's system. The pawn center still remains, but Black's counterplay is still adequate. The most positional move is /4. Bg5/.

3...d5 · Grünfeld Defence

This is the classic, and most common, starting position of the Grünfeld Defence, although d5 can be delayed if White has delayed e4 which typically happens if Nf3 is played at some stage. Most notably, the famous Game of the Century by Bobby Fischer originated from the Grünfeld Defence.

The Grünfeld Defence often becomes incredibly sharp and tactical due to Black quickly striking at White's vulnerable center. Unlike the King's Indian Defence, where Black immediately fianchettoes the king bishop, here Black immediately plays 3...d5 to stop e4 (at least temporarily) and challenge White's occupation of the center. White has a range of choices, the main one is to exchange the pawns on d5 and follow up with e4 in order to displace Black's pieces.

explanations.textZh:
3...d5 · 格林菲尔德防御

这是格林菲尔德防御的经典且最常见的起始位置，尽管如果白方延迟了 e4，则 d5 可能会被延迟，而如果在某个阶段进行 Nf3，则通常会发生这种情况。最值得注意的是，鲍比·费舍尔（Bobby Fischer）著名的世纪之战源自格伦菲尔德防守。

由于黑方迅速攻击白方脆弱的中心，格伦菲尔德防守往往变得异常敏锐和战术性。与国王的印第安防御不同，黑方立即对王主教进行前击，这里黑方立即下 3...d5 来阻止 e4（至少暂时）并挑战白方对中心的占领。白棋有多种选择，主要是在d5上交换棋子，然后用e4来取代黑棋。

20 年代，随着尼姆佐-印度防御进入主流开放理论，欧洲国际象棋正在发生革命。当今的大师将其称为“现代风格”。然后，在 1922 年，一位名叫恩斯特·格伦菲尔德 (Ernst Grünfeld) 的著名大师提出了一个新系统，开始猛烈抨击当时的伟大大师，包括科斯蒂克 (Kostic)、萨米施 (Sämisch)、科勒 (Colle) 和阿廖欣 (Alekhine)（众所周知，他在输给它后沮丧地将国王扔到了房间的另一边）。这后来被称为新的“超现代”风格，而格林菲尔德忠于超现代的品味，以纯粹的形式展示了以前接受的古典教条如何可能是错误的，典当中心既可以成为攻击的对象，也可以成为福音。

哲学的主要战场是交换变体，4.cxd5 Nxd5 5.e4 Nxc3 6.bxc3。白棋的棋子中心获得了空间，但黑棋沿着从 a1 到 h8 的长而暗的对角线具有出色的发挥，并且最终可以通过诸如 ...Bg7、...Rd8、...c5、...Nc6 以及偶尔 ...Qa5 等动作瞄准 d4。最终他也可能会在另一对角线上给fianchetto带来一个主教，目标是e4。

比较经典的动作是/4。 Nf3/，/4。 Bf4/和/4。 Qb3/，这是对抗黑方系统的更保守的方法。当子中心仍然存在，但黑棋的反击仍然足够。最大幅度的移动是/4。 Bg5/.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...g6/3. Nc3/3...d5/4. cxd5/4...Nxd5/5. Na4
explanations.text:
Grünfeld Defence - Nadanian Variation

5. Na4!?

This strange looking move was first employed by Ashot Nadanian in 1996. Usually it is not recommended to put Knights on the edge of the board, but here it is meaningful. White takes the important c5-square under control and going to force black's Knight from the center with е4. Eventually, the a4-Knight can occupy the c5-square and attack the pawn on b7.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...g6/3. Nc3/3...d5/4. cxd5/4...Nxd5/5. e4
explanations.text:
5.e4

This move greedily grabs central space. Since Nf6 or Nb6 would leave black without enough pressure in the center, Nb4 misplaces the knight only to create the obvious threat of Qxd4 followed by Nc2, Nxc3 is forced. Although d4 is strengthened, the queenside weakens, and the a1-h8 diagonal loosens up. That is why g6 and Bg7 is played in the Gruenfeld Defence. Black will now play to dismantle white's central ambitions. Usually, Black advances the c-pawn, and then he uses his e-pawn to dismantle white's center. Also, Nb4?? loses to Qa4+ Nc6 d5.

After e4, White has a dangerous center. Black must pressure it or risk a cramped, passive game. The only good move is Nxc3, else play resembles the dubious Marshall defence.

Since Nf6 or Nb6 would leave black without enough pressure in the center, Nb4 misplaces the knight only to create the obvious threat of Qxd4 followed by Nc2, Nxc3 is forced. Although d4 is strengthened, the queenside weakens, and the a1-h8 diagonal loosens up. That is why g6 and Bg7 is played in the Gruenfeld Defence. Black will now play to dismantle white's central ambitions. Usually, Black advances the c-pawn, and then he uses his e-pawn to dismantle white's center. Also, Nb4?? loses to Qa4+ Nc6 d5.

After e4, White has a dangerous center. Black must pressure it or risk a cramped, passive game. The only good move is Nxc3, else play resembles the dubious Marshall defence.
explanations.textZh:
5.e4

这一举动贪婪地抢夺了中心空间。由于Nf6或Nb6会在中心没有足够压力的情况下留下黑色，Nb4错位马只会造成Qxd4随后是Nc2的明显威胁，Nxc3被迫。虽然d4得到加强，但后侧减弱，a1-h8对角线放松。这就是为什么 g6 和 Bg7 在 Gruenfeld 防守中进行。黑棋现在将致力于摧毁白棋的核心野心。通常，黑方推进 c 兵，然后用 e 兵拆除白方的中心。还有，Nb4??输给 Qa4+ Nc6 d5。

e4之后，白棋有了一个危险的中锋。黑棋必须施加压力，否则就会面临局局局促、被动的风险。唯一好的举动是 Nxc3，否则打法类似于可疑的马歇尔防守。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...g6/3. Nc3/3...d5/4. cxd5/4...Nxd5/5. e4/5...Nxc3
explanations.text:
5...Nxc3

This is forced, as Nb6 and Nf6 lost time, and Nb4 lost to Qa4+ Nc6 d5. Now, Black appears to have improved White's center, but weakened the long diagonal when Black plays Bg7. Black will play ...Bg7 and ...c5 soon after.
explanations.textEn:
5...Nxc3

explanations.textZh:
5...Nxc3

这是被迫的，因为Nb6和Nf6输了时间，Nb4输给了Qa4+ Nc6 d5。现在，黑方似乎改善了白方的中线，但在黑方下Bg7时削弱了长对角线。不久之后黑棋将下...Bg7 和...c5。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...g6/3. Nc3/3...d5/4. cxd5/4...Nxd5/5. e4/5...Nxc3/6. bxc3/6...Bg7/7. Bc4
explanations.text:
7. Bc4

This move places the bishop on a good, active post. However, the drawback is that Nf3 will become unplayable, since Bg4! will put unbearable pressure on d4. It's either Be2/Nf3, Bc4/Ne2 or Bc4/Nf3/h3. In this setup, the bishop will be more active, while in the other setup, the knight will be so. That other setup has increasingly popular since the 1980's.

explanations.textZh:
7.BC4

这一举动使主教处于一个积极活跃的位置。然而，缺点是从Bg4开始，Nf3将变得无法玩！会给d4带来难以承受的压力。它是 Be2/Nf3、Bc4/Ne2 或 Bc4/Nf3/h3。在这种设置中，主教会更加活跃，而在另一种设置中，马会更加活跃。自 20 世纪 80 年代以来，另一种设置越来越流行。

explanations.text:
7...c5

This pawn lever also tries to attack the center. Since the center is potentially opening, white is well advised to move his king out of danger with 8.Ne2 followed by O-O.
explanations.textEn:
7...c5

explanations.textZh:
7...c5

该典当杆也试图攻击中心。由于中心可能会打开，白方最好先用 8.Ne2 移动他的王，然后用 O-O。

This move starts a piece setup that has become increasingly popular since the 1980's. White moves their knight to an active place. The drawback is that the bishop will have to settle for the passive e2-square, else Bg4 would be strong.

explanations.textZh:

这一举动开启了自 20 世纪 80 年代以来越来越流行的棋子设置。白棋将他们的马移动到一个活跃的位置。缺点是主教必须满足于被动的 e2 方阵，否则 Bg4 会很强。

explanations.text:
7...c5

This move is the key pawn lever, taking advantage of the diagonal. Note that the long diagonal is weak. Without this lever, d4 would be indestructible and the Grünfeld defence would be unsound. White has four main moves, the most theoretical being /8. Rb1/.
explanations.textEn:

explanations.textZh:
7...c5

此步是关键的兵杆，利用对角线的优势。请注意，长对角线很弱。如果没有这个杠杆，d4将坚不可摧，格林菲尔德的防守也将不健全。白棋有四个主要棋步，其中最理论的是/8。铷1/。

explanations.text:
This check is an attempt to provoke concessions by Black who has three options now. Clearly the main move is 8...Nc6, which develops the knight on its best square but allows complications after 9.d5.

8...Bd7 9.Be2 leads to a slightly better position for White who profits from the fact that the pressure on d4 has been reduced for the moment.

8...Nd7 places the knight on a passive square. There will be no serious pressure against d4 now, and White should have the better chances thanks to his pawn centre.

8.Bb5+

This check is fine since Black cannot block with ...c6, and thus should play Nd7. If Black wants a dull, equal position with no dynamic energy, he can play Bd7. Black is fine here.

explanations.textZh:
这一检查是为了让黑方做出让步，黑方现在有三种选择。显然，主要动作是 8...Nc6，它使马在其最佳方格上发展，但在 9.d5 之后允许复杂化。

8...Bd7 9.Be2 为白方带来了稍微好一点的位置，白方从 d4 的压力暂时减轻这一事实中获利。

8...Nd7 将骑士置于被动方格上。现在对 d4 不会有太大的压力，而且由于他的典当中心，白方应该有更好的机会。

8.Bb5+

这个检查没问题，因为黑方无法用 ...c6 阻挡，因此应该下 Nd7。如果黑方想要一个平淡、平等、没有动态能量的局面，他可以下 Bd7。黑色在这里很好。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...g6/3. Nc3/3...Bg7
explanations.text:
King's Indian Defence

3...Bg7 is the King's Indian Defence, one of the most heavily analysed openings in chess. Black's idea is to concede the centre to white and to then put pressure on it using the bishop on g7, often in conjunction with moves like c5 and Nc6. One of the common themes of the King's Indian Defence is for black to launch a kingside attack, typically beginning with the move f5. In reply, White will often launch their own attack on the queenside where they often have a large space advantage.

The King's Indian Defence is a very dynamic opening which can be highly risky but can also give excellent counterplay for black. As such it is often employed by players who wish for a more tactical game than is normal in Queen's pawn openings. In the late 80s and early 90s, Garry Kasparov used it regularly to devastating effect and as a result, it became very popular with players at all levels. In recent years it has been less used at the top level although Teimour Radjabov's excellent results with it helped him to win the strong Corus tournament in 2007 and possibly signalled a comeback for the dangerous defence.

explanations.textZh:
国王的印第安防御

3...Bg7 是国王印度防御，是国际象棋中分析最多的开局之一。黑方的想法是让白方占据中路，然后利用 g7 上的主教向其施加压力，通常与 c5 和 Nc6 等动作结合起来。国王印度防御的共同主题之一是黑棋发起王侧进攻，通常从 f5 棋开始。作为回应，白棋经常会在后侧发起攻击，在那里他们通常拥有很大的空间优势。

国王的印度防御是一个非常有活力的开局，可能具有很高的风险，但也可以为黑方提供出色的反击。因此，它经常被那些希望比皇后棋子开局中的正常情况更具战术性的玩家所使用。在 80 年代末和 90 年代初，加里·卡斯帕罗夫（Garry Kasparov）经常使用它，产生了毁灭性的效果，因此它在各个级别的玩家中都非常受欢迎。近年来，尽管 Teimour Ra​​djabov 凭借此技术取得了出色成绩，帮助他赢得了 2007 年强大的 Corus 锦标赛，并可能预示着危险防守的卷土重来，但它在顶级赛事中的使用较少。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...g6/3. Nc3/3...Bg7/4. e4
explanations.text:
4. e4

The most principled move, with 4. e4, White takes over the centre that Black has conceded.

Black's main move is 4...d6. The d-pawn prevents White from playing 5. e5 and kicking Black's knight, opens a line for the queen's bishop, and will be a springboard for later attacks on the centre, ...e5 or ...c5. White has a variety of responses: the mainline is 5. Nf3 O-O 6. Be2 e5 7. O-O.

4...O-O is also playable as, if 5. e5, Black can save the knight on the newly-available e8 square (5...Nh5?? 6. g4 traps the knight) and the game may continue 5...Ne8 6. f4 d6 7. Nf3. More commonly however White plays 5. Nf3 and after 5...d6 the game transposes.

4...d5? now loses a pawn, as White's c and e pawns clamp down on d5. If Black had been planning to play a Grünfeld, then they have missed their chance.
explanations.textEn:
4. e4

The most principled move, with 4. e4, White takes over the centre that Black has conceded.

Black's main move is 4...d6. The d-pawn prevents White from playing 5. e5 and kicking Black's knight, opens a line for the queen's bishop, and will be a springboard for later attacks on the centre, ...e5 or ...c5. White has a variety of responses: the mainline is 5. Nf3 O-O 6. Be2 e5 7. O-O.

4...O-O is also playable as, if 5. e5, Black can save the knight on the newly-available e8 square (5...Nh5?? 6. g4 traps the knight) and the game may continue 5...Ne8 6. f4 d6 7. Nf3. More commonly however White plays 5. Nf3 and after 5...d6 the game transposes.

4...d5? now loses a pawn, as White's c and e pawns clamp down on d5. If Black had been planning to play a Grünfeld, then they have missed their chance.
explanations.textZh:
4.e4

最原则的一步棋是 4. e4，白棋占据了黑棋已经让出的中心位置。

黑棋的主要棋步是 4...d6。 d-兵阻止白方下5.e5并踢黑方的马，为后方的主教打开一条线，并且将成为以后攻击中心，...e5或...c5的跳板。白棋有多种应对：主线是5. Nf3 O-O 6. Be2 e5 7. O-O。

4...O-O 也可以玩，因为如果 5. e5，黑方可以在新可用的 e8 方格上拯救马（5...Nh5?? 6. g4 困住马），并且游戏可以继续 5...Ne8 6. f4 d6 7. Nf3。然而更常见的是，白棋下 5.Nf3，在 5...d6 之后，游戏会转换。

4...d5？现在失去了一个棋子，因为白方的 c 和 e 棋子压制了 d5。如果布莱克一直计划下格伦菲尔德，那么他们就错过了机会。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...g6/3. Nc3/3...Bg7/4. e4/4...d6
explanations.text:
4...d6

The move d6 ensures that White can't kick the Black Knight with e5. It also prepares to play e5 or c5 at some point. White has a variety of sharp choices:

5. Nf3, the Classical or Orthodox variation, results in a race on opposite sides: White tries to break through on the queenside before Black's forces get to the White king. Having taken the lion's share of the centre, White must now develop their minor pieces and castle. After 5...O-O 6. Be2, Black tries for the 6...e5 pawn break, and how White responds leads to the next major branching point of the theory. 5. Nf3 is by far the most popular line. This is commonly also played in the mover order 5. Be2 O-O 5. Nf3.

5. f3, the aggressive Sämisch variation, is the chief sideline. White will normally castle queenside (although castling kingside can also occur) and attack along the h-file. After 5...O-O 6. Be3, Black chooses between the 6...e5 pawn break, as in the classical variation, or 6...c5, the tactical Sämisch gambit.

5. f4, the Four Pawns attack, is the most megalomaniacal variation. White gains even more space with a fourth pawn in on the fourth rank. Black must react quickly to avoid getting crushed by White's centre, but in the long term they can exploit the weak squares the advancing pawns has left behind. This is the most popular sideline at the amateur level.

5. h3 is the quirky Makogonov variation, which stops a knight or bishop from getting into g4 while retaining the option of Nf3.

5. g3, the Deferred fianchetto, is the most positional variation. Normally the position is fluid. Black usually exchanges his e-pawn for White's d-pawn, Black tries to play on the queenside dark squares and against e4, while White lines his forces up against d6 and the kingside.

5. Nge2 is the Kramer variation. 5. Nge2 intends Ng3, keeping the option of f3, similar to the Sämisch.

4...d6

Be2, Black tries for the 6...e5 pawn break, and how White responds leads to the next major branching point of the theory. 5. Nf3 is by far the most popular line. explanations.textZh:
4...d6

d6 棋确保白棋无法用 e5 踢黑棋。它还准备在某个时候播放 e5 或 c5。白方有多种锐利选择：

5. Nf3，古典或正统的变体，导致对立双方的比赛：白方试图在黑方部队到达白方国王之前从后侧突破。在占据了中心的最大份额之后，白方现在必须发展他们的小棋子和城堡。在 5...O-O 6. Be2 之后，黑方尝试 6...e5 兵破，而白方的反应则引出了该理论的下一个主要分支点。 5. Nf3 是迄今为止最受欢迎的系列。这通常也按照移动顺序 5. Be2 O-O 5. Nf3 进行。

5. f3，激进的萨米施变体，是主要的边线。白棋通常会在后侧城堡（尽管也可能发生王侧易位）并沿 h 线攻击。在 5...O-O 6. Be3 之后，黑方在 6...e5 兵突破（如经典变体）或 6...c5（战术萨米施策略）之间进行选择。

5. f4，四兵攻击，是最狂妄的变体。白方在第四排有第四个棋子时获得了更多的空间。黑棋必须迅速做出反应，以避免被白棋的中心压垮，但从长远来看，他们可以利用前进的棋子留下的弱方格。这是业余水平上最受欢迎的副业。

5. h3 是古怪的 Makogonov 变体，它阻止骑士或主教进入 g4，同时保留 Nf3 的选项。

5. g3，Deferred fiianchetto，是位置变化最多的。通常情况下，位置是流动的。黑棋通常用他的 e 棋子交换白棋的 d 棋子，黑棋试图在后侧黑暗方格上对抗 e4，而白棋则将他的兵力排列在 d6 和王翼上。

5. Nge2 是 Kramer 变体。 5. Nge2意向Ng3，保留f3的选项，与Sämisch类似。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...g6/3. Nc3/3...Bg7/4. e4/4...d6/5. f3
explanations.text:
5. f3 · Sämisch Variation

5. f3 is the Sämisch Variation, a well-known and popular line in the King's Indian. With this solid move white bolsters his centre. He remains noncommittal with regards to his king, with castling both queenside or kingside possible depending on what black does. This can be a tough nut to crack for black, who usually wants white to overextend when playing the King's Indian.

However, the Sämisch does have some drawbacks for white. Most obviously, kingside development is impeded because the king's knight cannot go to its usual square, f3. Secondly, the g1-a7 diagonal is open and on a direct line to white's king, should white castle short. The Sämisch has fallen somewhat out of favour at the highest levels of chess for the more natural-looking 5. Nf3, but it's still sometimes seen in grandmaster play. At the amateur level, this variation remains perfectly viable and gives both sides good chances.

explanations.textZh:
5. f3 · 萨米施变奏

5. f3 是萨米施变奏曲 (Sämisch Variation)，是 King's Indian 中著名且流行的诗句。通过这一坚实的举动，白棋支撑了他的中心。他对他的王仍然不置可否，后侧或王侧的易位都可能取决于黑棋的行动。对于黑棋来说，这可能是一个棘手的难题，因为黑棋通常希望白棋在玩国王印第安人时过度伸展。

然而，萨米施对于白色来说确实有一些缺点。最明显的是，王侧发展受到阻碍，因为王的骑士无法前往其通常的方格f3。其次，g1-a7对角线是开放的，并且与白方的国王成一条直线，如果白方城堡短的话。萨米施棋在最高水平的国际象棋比赛中因看起来更自然的 5.Nf3 而有些失宠，但有时在特级大师比赛中仍然会看到它。在业余水平上，这种变化仍然完全可行，并为双方提供了很好的机会。

explanations.text:
6. Be3

White defends the d4 pawn, which is usually the weakest in the Sämisch formation. Black now has a variety of options - usually they want to strike in the centre with /6...e5/ or even the gambit line /6...c5/. The latter, although it gives up a pawn, gives Black a lead in development with plenty of open lines and White's extra pawn is doubled, limiting its usefulness. In practice, Black scores very well in the gambit line and it is partially due to it that the Sämisch is not quite as popular as it once was.

explanations.textZh:
6.Be3

白方防守 d4 棋子，该棋子通常是萨米施阵型中最弱的。黑棋现在有多种选择 - 通常他们想用 /6...e5/ 甚至开局线 /6...c5/ 下棋。后者虽然放弃了一个棋子，但却让黑方在发展中处于领先地位，有大量的开放线，而白方的额外棋子加倍，限制了它的用处。实际上，黑棋在开局路线上得分非常高，部分原因是萨米施棋不再像以前那样受欢迎。

explanations.text:
King's Indian Defense, Sämisch Gambit

6...c5

This surprising move is one of the biggest questions posed to white's choice of moving the pawn to f3. One of the most interesting and studied gambits in all of chess, the Sämisch Gambit offers a free pawn on c5 to create wild tactical chaos against white's underdeveloped position. White has three main options, according to the masters and the lichess database:

Ignore the pawn break entirely, by developing another piece (Usually Nge2),

Immediately close the center, King's Indian style, with d5,

Or accept the gambit with dxc5 dxc5 Bxc5

The first and second options are probably the best for people who don't want to get into an absolute wilderness of a position. While you miss out on a "free pawn", you can still go ahead with your regular knowledge of the Sämisch, with minimal danger to follow, and as such, they won't be discussed here.

The third option is possibly the most dangerous for both sides. After the pawn is accepted, black immediately brings both knights (Nc6, Ne5, ...) to attack the white king. White tries to either simplify the position or force black's attack to lose its initiative. Lines get extremely complicated after Bxc5, with the engine giving mixed opinions about the gambit.

explanations.textZh:
国王的印度防御，萨米施策略

6...c5

这一令人惊讶的举动是白棋选择将棋子移至 f3 所面临的最大问题之一。萨米施开局是所有国际象棋中最有趣、最受研究的开局之一，它在 c5 上提供了一个免费棋子，以针对白棋不发达的位置制造疯狂的战术混乱。根据大师和巫师数据库，白棋有三个主要选择：

完全忽略典当，通过开发另一个棋子（通常是 Nge2），

立即关闭中心，国王的印度风格，用d5，

或者接受 dxc5 dxc5 Bxc5 的策略

对于那些不想陷入绝对困境的人来说，第一个和第二个选择可能是最好的选择。虽然您错过了“自由棋子”，但您仍然可以继续使用您对萨米施的常规知识，而遵循的危险很小，因此，这里不会讨论它们。

第三种选择对双方来说可能都是最危险的。棋子被接受后，黑方立即带两个马（Nc6，Ne5，...）攻击白王。白方要么试图简化局面，要么迫使黑方失去进攻主动权。 Bxc5 之后的线路变得极其复杂，引擎对这一策略给出了不同的意见。

explanations.text:
6...e5 · Orthodox variation

This used to be the main line of the Sämisch. Its use has been in steady decline for a while due to 6...c5 becoming the most ambitious way to play the Sämisch variation.

White has the choice to either leave the central tension, or to release it.

/7. d5/ advances the pawn further into Black's territory. It's presence, however, is only temporary, as Black will be able to get rid of it with 7...c6. This is the main continuation.

/7. Nge2/ leaves the central tension and prioritizes development instead. While Black has the option of taking the pawn, they often choose to play moves that transpose back into 7. d5 instead.

/7. dxe5/ releases the tension in the centre and initiates a trade of queens after 7...dxe5 8. Qxd8 Rxd8.

6...e5 · 正统变体

这曾经是萨米施人的主线。由于 6...c5 成为演奏萨米施变体最雄心勃勃的方式，它的使用量在一段时间内一直在稳步下降。

白方可以选择要么离开中心紧张局势，要么释放它。

/7。 Nge2/ 摆脱了核心压力并优先考虑发展。虽然黑方可以选择拿走棋子，但他们通常会选择转回 7.d5 走棋。

explanations.text:
King's Indian Defence

5. f4

The Four Pawns Attack is the most aggressive line for White in the King's Indian. White creates a massive pawn centre and has full control over the middle of the board ... for now. This is a dangerous line for Black, and if they don't play correctly, they will be knocked off the board by White's advancing army. However, if Black can survive the initial onslaught, they will have the better game since White will have many weak squares in their camp that their pawns can't defend. For this reason, the Four Pawns Attack isn't seen frequently at the highest levels of chess, although it's still very viable at the amateur level.

explanations.textZh:
国王的印第安防御

5.f4

四兵攻击是王印中白棋最具侵略性的路线。白方创造了一个巨大的兵中心，并完全控制了棋盘的中间……目前。这对黑方来说是一条危险的路线，如果他们下棋不正确，他们就会被白方前进的军队击落到棋盘上。然而，如果黑方能够在最初的猛攻中幸存下来，他们将会有更好的比赛，因为白方的阵营中有许多弱方，他们的棋子无法防守。因此，四兵攻击在最高水平的国际象棋比赛中并不常见，尽管它在业余水平上仍然非常可行。

此后，白方似乎对中路有着铁一般的掌控，所有棋子都得到了防守，毫无弱点。然而，在黑方城堡之后，他可以用 ...c5 和 ...e5 对白方的兵结构发起攻击。

explanations.text:
King's Indian Defence

Classical

This position is part of the Classical King's Indian Defence. White has an expansive pawn trio which Black is planning on attacking. White must brace himself because Black's counteroffensive in the centre of the board is about to start with ...e5.

6.Be2 is simply allowing White the opportunity to allow his King to get to safety (and stop the ...Bg4 pin on the knight) before Black begins his counteroffensive in the middle of the board. This move is played the vast majority of the time.

6.h3 is more passive move that stops ...Bg4 from happening but without allowing a kingside castle. This leaves the King slightly more vulnerable.

explanations.textZh:
国王的印第安防御

古典

这个位置是古典国王印第安防御的一部分。白棋有一个广阔的棋子三人组，黑棋正计划攻击它。白棋必须做好准备，因为黑棋在棋盘中央的反攻即将从...e5开始。

6.Be2 只是让白方有机会让他的国王在黑方开始在棋盘中间进行反攻之前到达安全地带（并阻止...Bg4 钉在马身上）。绝大多数时候都会使用这个动作。

6.h3 是更被动的举动，可以阻止...Bg4 的发生，但不允许出现王侧城堡。这让国王变得更加脆弱。

explanations.text: The main line of the King's Indian Defense. The main line continues 6...e5, attacking the center. White usually castles kingside, and the main line continues 7...Nc6 8. d5 Ne7. White has a space advantage in the center and will try to attack on the queenside and prepare a pawn break, c5. Black will attack on the kingside, by advancing his pawns to f5 and g4.

explanations.text:
King's Indian Defence: Orthodox Variation, 6...e5

The move e5 from Black attacks the center and gains space. The main line continues by White castling kingside to get the king away from the center, then Black plays Nc6 to gain space and develop a piece, which White immediately kicks with d5, forcing it to e7. From there, the game can branch off in several different ways.

b4 makes a pawn storm on the queenside, with the rooks developing to support in the attack. In some games, Black's kingside knight goes to h5 then back to f6 on its own volition to push the f-pawn to f5 to destabilize the center and prepare g4.

Ne1 eventually rotates the knight to the center after Nd3 where it can defend better against Black's counterattack, be protected from g4as well as attack in the future. Black's kingside knight also moves to allow f5.

d5 immediately locks the center, reaching a thematic position from the King's Indian Defense mainlines, with black trying to continue with the pawn storm using f5, h6, g5, and so on, whereas white tries to go for a similar pawn storm on the queenside, seeking to dislodge Black's attack.

Castling is not a bad move, preserving the tension in the center, however black can later equalize with exd4, so white will have to show their cards soon.

国王的印第安防御：正统变例，6...e5

黑棋 e5 攻击中心并获得空间。主线继续由白方王侧易车，使王远离中心，然后黑方下 Nc6 以获得空间并发展棋子，白方立即用 d5 踢出，迫使其到 e7。从这里开始，游戏可以以几种不同的方式分支。

b4 在后翼发起典当风暴，同时车队也开始支援进攻。在某些对局中，黑方的王翼骑士会自行下h5然后返回f6，将f兵推至f5以破坏中心的稳定并准备g4。

Ne1最终在Nd3之后将马轮换到中心，这样可以更好地防御黑方的反击，免受g4的攻击以及未来的攻击。黑棋的王翼骑士也允许f5。

d5立即锁定中心，从国王的印度防御主线到达主题位置，黑方试图使用f5、h6、g5等继续兵风暴，而白方则试图在后侧进行类似的兵风暴，试图驱逐黑方的攻击。

易车位并不是一个坏棋，可以保持中间的张力，但黑棋随后可以用 exd4 扳平比分，因此白棋很快就要亮出底牌了。

explanations.text:
King's Indian Defense, Fischer Transposition

This is true hypermodernism. Usually the game transposes after moves like 5.Nf3 d6, but sometimes White plays 5.e5 Ne8 6.f4 d6, when 7.Nf3 c5! 8.dxc5 Nc6! leads to a sharp but equal game.

国王的印第安防御，费舍尔换位

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...g6/3. Nc3/3...Bg7/4. Nf3
explanations.text:
Indian Defence

4. Nf3

This Knight development is solid but leaves the options open for Black to either play The King's Indian or the Grunfeld Defence.

If Black wishes to play the Grunfeld then responding immediately with d5 is required as white next move is likely to be 5. e4 which prevents d5 from being played.

印度国防

4.NF3

这种骑士的发展是坚实的，但为黑方留下了选择，可以选择国王的印第安人或格伦菲尔德防御。

如果黑方希望下格伦菲尔德，则需要立即用 d5 做出响应，因为白方下一步可能是 5。e4，这会阻止 d5 被下。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...g6/3. f3
explanations.text:
3. f3 · Anti-Grünfeld

3. f3 is an Anti-Grünfeld move that was popularized by Alekhine.

It prepares e4 with a pawn to secure a big center. However, it weakens White's kingside and allows Black a larger lead in development. White usually castles queenside and starts a pawn storm on the kingside, similar to the Sämisch variation.

Black can choose to go into the mainline with /3...d5/, playing in more of a Grünfeld fashion. Black is however free to go for one of the transpositional moves:

/3...c5/ transposes into a variation of the Benoni defence where White has already played f3, eliminating some of White's usual options.

/3...Bg7/ and /3...d6/ transpose into the Sämisch variation of the King's Indian.

Therefore, it is important for White to be comfortable in these openings as well if they want to avoid the Grünfeld with this move.

explanations.textZh:
3. f3·反格林菲尔德

3. f3 是由阿廖欣推广的反格伦菲尔德动作。

它为 e4 准备了一个棋子来确保一个大中心。然而，它削弱了白棋的王翼，并使黑棋在发展中取得更大的领先优势。白棋通常在后侧筑垒，并在王侧发起兵风暴，类似于萨米什变体。

黑棋可以选择以 /3...d5/ 进入主线，以更多的格伦菲尔德风格进行游戏。然而，黑棋可以自由地进行换位动作之一：

/3...c5/ 转换为伯诺尼防御的变体，其中白棋已经打出了 f3，从而消除了白棋的一些常用选项。

/3...Bg7/ 和 /3...d6/ 转置为 King's Indian 的萨米什语变体。

因此，如果白方想通过这一步棋避开格伦菲尔德，那么在这些空缺中保持舒适也很重要。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...g6/3. f3/3...d5
explanations.text:
3...d5 · Goglidze attack

Black continues playing in a Grünfeld style. The immediate 4. e4? prepared by f3 would simply blunder the pawn, so White should either remove one of Black's attackers or prepare it with another piece.

White's main move is /4. cxd5/, exchanging in the centre. This is different from the usual Grünfeld since after 4...Nxd5 5. e4 Black's knight doesn't have the option of taking on c3, so it must move to b6 or f6 (b6 being the better option). Play usually continues with Black castling short and White developing the queenside pieces and castling long.

Alternatively, White can play /4. Nc3/ transposing into the Lutikov variation of the Grünfeld.

3...d5 · 戈格利泽攻击

黑方继续以格林菲尔德风格下棋。立即4.e4？由 f3 准备的棋子只会使棋子失误，因此白棋应该移除黑棋的一名攻击者，或者准备另一子。

白棋的主要棋步是/4。 cxd5/，在中心交换。这与通常的格林菲尔德不同，因为在 4...Nxd5 5 之后。e4 黑方的骑士没有选择 c3，因此它必须移动到 b6 或 f6（b6 是更好的选择）。比赛通常继续进行，黑方易位短棋，白方发展后侧棋子，易位长方。

或者，白方可以下/4。 Nc3/ 转换为 Grünfeld 的 Lutikov 变体。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...g6/3. Nf3
explanations.text:
Indian Defence

3. Nf3

White develops a piece and continues their fight for the central dark squares.

This Knight's development, while solid, prevents White's option of playing f3 or f4 and thus gives up options of the aggressive Four Pawns Attack by requiring f4 and the Samisch, which requires f3.

explanations.textZh:
印度国防

3.NF3

白方发展出一颗棋子并继续争夺中央暗方。

该马的发展虽然稳固，但阻止了白方选择f3或f4，从而放弃了需要f4和萨米施（需要f3）的激进四兵攻击的选择。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. c4/2...g6/3. Nf3/3...Bg7
explanations.text:
Indian Defence

3...Bg7

The Bishop moves to its ideal square, bearing down on the central dark squares. Black has so far kept the options open by not committing a central pawn move.

White can now take control of e4 ready for occupation or develop in a more passive way, the most common is to play g3 and fianchetto the kingside Bishop.

印度国防

3...背景7

主教移动到其理想的方格，压向中央的黑色方格。到目前为止，黑方没有采取中央兵行动，从而保留了选择余地。

白棋现在可以控制e4准备占领或者以更被动的方式发展，最常见的是下棋g3和fianchetto王翼主教。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. e4
explanations.text:
2. e4?! · Omega gambit

An unconventional move, White offers Black their e4 pawn.

After 2...Nxe4, taking the free pawn, White has two continuations.

3. Bd3 kicks the knight back while developing a piece. White hopes a developmental edge and a half-open e-file is compensation for the pawn.

3. Nc3, offering a trade of knights and recapturing with the b pawn. The gambit's pioneer, Clyde Nakamura, characterised the chief compensation of this line being that Black's kingside was without the knight to defend it.

This gambit is considered unsound, as neither of these continuations offers sufficient compensation for the loss of White's central pawn. If Black is feeling generous however, they can decline the gambit with 2...d6 and transpose into a Pirc.

History

The earliest appearance of the gambit was in a 1906 game between George Hutton and Alfred Axtell.

Clyde Nakamura, who pioneered the gambit in 1985, said he christened it Omega after The Omega Man, a Charlton Heston movie. Nakamura refers to the 3. Nc3 continuation as the "mainline" Omega gambit, and the 3. Bd3 variation as the Arafat gambit after Abdel Arafat who played it a few times in the 80s.

explanations.textZh:
2.e4？！ · 欧米茄的策略

一个非常规的举动，白方将他们的 e4 棋子提供给黑方。

2...Nxe4 后，白方拿走空闲棋子，有两次延续。

3. Bd3一边发展棋子，一边踢回马。怀特希望发展优势和半开放的电子文件是对棋子的补偿。

3. Nc3，提供骑士交易并用b兵夺回。该策略的先驱克莱德·中村（Clyde Nakamura）描述了这条路线的主要补偿是黑方的王翼没有骑士来防守。

这种策略被认为是不合理的，因为这些延续都没有为白方中央棋子的损失提供足够的补偿。然而，如果黑方感觉慷慨，他们可以用 2...d6 拒绝这一策略并转入 Pirc。

历史

这种策略最早出现在 1906 年乔治·赫顿 (George Hutton) 和阿尔弗雷德·阿克斯特尔 (Alfred Axtell) 之间的一场比赛中。

克莱德·中村 (Clyde Nakamura) 是 1985 年这一策略的先驱者，他表示，他以查尔顿·赫斯顿 (Charlton Heston) 的电影《欧米茄人》(The Omega Man) 的名字将其命名为欧米茄 (Omega)。中村将 3.NC3 延续称为“主线”Omega 策略，将 3.Bd3 变体称为阿拉法特策略，继阿卜杜勒·阿拉法特在 80 年代玩过几次之后。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. f3
explanations.text:
2. f3!? · Paleface attack

White's pawn on f3 prepares to play 3. e4. However, this breaks the principle of not pushing one's f-pawn early in the opening. It weakens White's kingside and takes away the natural development square of the king's knight. This is usually played with the idea of transposing into the Blackmar-Diemer gambit.

This move usually compels Black to play 2...d5 in order to increase Black's control of e4. If 3. e4 anyway, White doesn't have enough support to defend the pawn. 3...dxe4 4. fxe4 Nxe4 , Black is up a pawn. 4. Nc3 is the usual idea: White transposes into the Blackmar-Diemer gambit, a line otherwise seen after 1. d4 d5.

Otherwise, say 3. c4 e6 and White has ended up playing a queen's gambit declined, and the incorporated of the unusual move f3 proves to be weakening and a waste of time.

History

"Paleface" is a supposed Native American term for white Europeans. The name "paleface attack" for this line against the Indian defence then seems to be intended to evoke a European offensive against the American Indians (the Indian defence is not named for Native Americans, but for Indian chess masters like Moheschunder Bannerjee whose games against John Cochrane introduced the defence to the West).

The name goes back to at least 1986, where it was used in Eric Schiller's book on the Blackmar-Diemer gambit. He may have coined it.

One of the earliest appearances of 2. f3!? was in 1931 at the Buenos Aires Copa Geniol.

explanations.textZh:
2.f3！？ · 白脸攻击

白棋在f3上的棋子准备下3. e4。然而，这打破了开局时不早出f兵的原则。它削弱了白棋的王翼，并剥夺了王马的自然发展方格。这通常是通过转换为 Blackmar-Diemer 策略来实现的。

这步棋通常迫使黑方下 2...d5，以增强黑方对 e4 的控制。无论如何，如果 3. e4，白棋没有足够的支持来防守棋子。 3...dxe4 4. fxe4 Nxe4 ，黑棋是棋子。 4. Nc3 是通常的想法：白棋转入 Blackmar-Diemer 策略，这条线在 1. d4 d5 之后会出现。

否则，比如 3.c4 e6，白方最终会采取后退策略，而事实证明，结合不寻常的走法 f3 会削弱并浪费时间。

历史

“白脸”是美洲原住民对欧洲白人的称呼。这条针对印第安人防守的路线被称为“白脸攻击”，似乎是为了唤起欧洲人对美洲印第安人的进攻（印第安人防守不是以美洲原住民命名的，而是以印度象棋大师莫赫施德·班纳吉（Moheschunder Bannerjee）命名的，他与约翰·科克伦（John Cochrane）的比赛将这种防守引入了西方）。

这个名字至少可以追溯到 1986 年，埃里克·席勒 (Eric Sc​​hiller) 在其关于 Blackmar-Diemer 策略的书中使用了该名称。这可能是他创造的。

2.f3!? 最早出现之一1931 年，在布宜诺斯艾利斯的 Copa Geniol 比赛中。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Nf3
explanations.text:
2. Nf3 · Knights variation

This move keeps White's options open: they can first see how Black intends to play before deciding on a response. If, for example, White likes to play against the King's Indian defence with c4, but wants to avoid lines involving c4 and ...e6, they can lead with 2. Nf3 and answer 2...g6 with 3. c4 but 2...e6 with (e.g.) 3. Bg5.

This position is also often reached via the move order 1.Nf3 Nf6 2.d4.

Prepare to develop a bishop

Black now makes a decision as to which way they intend to develop their bishop(s). Then, White chooses which line they would like to play, generally from the options 3. c4, 3. g3 (preparing to fianchetto), 3. Bg5 or 3. Bf4, or 3. e3.

2...g6 is the most common move. Black prepares to fianchetto their kingside bishop and play in a King's Indian or Grünfeld style. White can transpose into a King's Indian with 3. c4, but other plans include 3. g3, the Przepiorka variation, 3. Bg5, the Torre attack, or 3. Bf4, the London system.

2...e6 and Black prepares to deploy their bishop on the a3-f8 diagonal. White has the usual options of 3. c4, 3. g3, 3. Bg5 or 3. Bf4. 3. e3, like the Colle, is called the Yusupov-Rubinstein system.

2...b6, the Pseudo-Queens Indian defence, and 2...d6, the Wade-Tartakower defence, make a decision about Black's queenside bishop instead.

Play a pawn to the centre

Alternatively, Black can still play a pawn in the centre.

If Black plays 2...d5 after all, the third most common move, White has the option to transpose into a Queen's gambit.

2...c5, the Spielmann-Indian, resembles the Benoni defence (1. d4 c5). White usually pushes the d pawn to d5 save it or defends it with c3 or e3.

Other moves

2...c6, the Czech-Indian, usually reaches a Slav-style set-up. 3. c4 d5.

2...b5!?, the Polish variation, looks to prevent c4 while preparing ...Bb7.

2...Ne4!? is called the Döry defence.

explanations.textZh:
2. Nf3·骑士变种

此举使白棋的选择保持开放：他们可以先看看黑棋打算如何下棋，然后再决定如何应对。例如，如果白棋喜欢用 c4 对抗国王的印度防御，但想避免涉及 c4 和 ...e6 的线路，他们可以用 2. Nf3 领先，并用 3. c4 回答 2...g6，但用（例如）3. Bg5 回答 2...e6。

该位置也经常通过移动指令 1.Nf3 Nf6 2.d4 到达。

准备培养主教

布莱克现在决定他们打算以何种方式发展他们的主教。然后，白方选择他们想要下的线，通常从选项3.c4、3.g3（准备fianchetto）、3.Bg5或3.Bf4或3.e3中选择。

2...g6 是最常见的走法。黑方准备向王翼主教发起进攻，并以国王的印第安人或格伦菲尔德风格下棋。白方可以使用 3. c4 转变成国王印第安人，但其他计划包括 3. g3（Przepiorka 变体）、3. Bg5（托雷攻击）或 3. Bf4（伦敦系统）。

2...e6 和黑方准备将象部署在 a3-f8 对角线上。白方通常有3.c4、3.g3、3.Bg5或3.Bf4的选择。 3. e3 和 Colle 一样，被称为 Yusupov-Rubinstein 系统。

2...b6，伪皇后印地安防御，以及 2...d6，韦德-塔塔考尔防御，对黑方后翼主教做出决定。

将棋子下到中心

或者，黑方仍然可以在中间下一个棋子。

如果黑方毕竟下的是 2...d5，这是第三种最常见的走法，那么白方可以选择转入后弃兵策略。

2...c5，斯皮尔曼-印第安人，类似于伯诺尼防御（1. d4 c5）。白棋通常将d兵推到d5保存它或用c3或e3防御它。

其他动作

2...c6，捷克-印度，通常达到斯拉夫风格的设置。 3.c4d5。

2...b5!?，波兰语变体，在准备 ...Bb7 的同时，旨在阻止 c4。

2...Ne4！？称为“多里防御”。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Nf3/2...c5
explanations.text:
Spielmann-Indian Defense

In this opening, named after Austrian grandmaster Rudolf Spielmann, Black strikes at White's center with their bishop pawn, in similar fashion to the Benoni.

The main response is 3. d5, amassing space in the center similar to the Benoni. Black can continue down the Benoni with 3...e6; or, they can take advantage of White's c-pawn not being on c4 yet by playing 3...b5!, the Benko Defense (sometimes referred to as the Pseudo-Benko).

3. c4 transposes into an English Opening, Symmetrical Variation.

Some 1. d4 players may try to play the Catalan setup with 3. g3?; this is considered a mistake due to 3...cxd4 4. Bg2 e5!, defending their extra pawn tactically; 5. Nxe5?? runs into 5...Qa5+ with a fork, winning the knight.

Some 1. d4 players as White may try to stay consistent to the London with 3. c3 or 3. e3, which are the most common responses.

斯皮尔曼-印度国防

在这个以奥地利大师鲁道夫·斯皮尔曼命名的开局中，黑棋用主教棋子攻击白棋的中心，其方式与伯诺尼棋类似。

主要反应是3.d5，在中心聚集空间，类似于贝诺尼。黑棋可以继续下贝诺尼 3...e6；或者，他们可以利用白方的c兵尚未在c4上的优势，下出3...b5！，即Benko防御（有时称为伪Benko）。

3. c4 转置为英语开头对称变奏。

一些 1. d4 玩家可能会尝试用 3. g3? 玩加泰罗尼亚设置；这被认为是一个错误，因为 3...cxd4 4. Bg2 e5!，在战术上保卫他们的额外棋子； 5.Nxe5??用叉子碰到 5...Qa5+，赢得骑士。

一些 1. d4 棋手（如白方）可能会尝试用 3. c3 或 3. e3 与伦敦保持一致，这是最常见的反应。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Nf3/2...d5
explanations.text:
2...d5

The position has turned symmetrical again. White has many options to choose from, each one leading to very different opening systems.

/3. c4/ is the most popular, transposing into a Queen's Gambit. White may choose this move order to avoid certain openings, like the Budapest defence, which would have been playable had White not placed their knight on f3 in advance.

/3. Bf4/ is the second-most popular, turning the game into a London System.

/3. e3/ sees White going for the Colle System. This is the main move-order used by practitioners of this system.

/3. g3/ turns the game into a Catalan-like position, but through a less accurate move-order. Black gets to place their light-squared bishop outside of the pawn-chain without any troubles.

/3. Bg5/ is the relatively rare Torre Attack. Unless White tries to double Black's pawns by exchanging the bishop for the f6 knight, this is an independent line. Otherwise it will likely transpose into typical Queen's Gambit declined lines.

A move like 3. Nc3 is certainly not bad, but it doesn't put much pressure on Black. White's c-pawn plays a key role in control of the centre, and moving the knight to c3 earlier usually allows Black easy equality.

2...d5

位置再次变得对称。白棋有多种选择，每一种都会导致截然不同的开局系统。

/3。 c4/ 是最受欢迎的，转换成后弃兵。白棋可能会选择此走法以避免某些空缺，例如布达佩斯防御，如果白棋没有提前将马放在f3上，那么布达佩斯防御是可以玩的。

/3。 Bf4/ 是第二受欢迎的游戏，将游戏变成了伦敦系统。

/3。 e3/ 认为怀特将进入科莱系统。这是该系统的实践者使用的主要移动顺序。

/3。 g3/ 将游戏变成类似加泰罗尼亚语的局面，但移动顺序不太准确。黑方可以毫无困难地将他们的浅方象放在典当链之外。

/3。 Bg5/是相对罕见的托雷攻击。除非白棋试图通过将象换成 f6 马来使黑棋的棋子加倍，否则这是一条独立的路线。否则它可能会转化为典型的后弃兵策略。

像3.Nc3这样的棋步当然还不错，但它并没有给黑棋带来太大的压力。白棋的c兵在控制中心方面发挥着关键作用，提前将马移动到c3通常可以让黑棋轻松扳平。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Nf3/2...d5/3. Bg5
explanations.text:
Torre Attack

The Torre Attack is not often seen at top level, as statistically doesn't give white much more than equality. However, if black does not play accurately, white can get a dangerous kingside attack.

e6 is most common, although statistically gives white the better chances, and plays into whites goals for the Torre. Perhaps best for black is the dynamic c5.

托雷攻击

托雷攻击在高层并不常见，因为统计数据并没有给予白人更多的平等。然而，如果黑棋不准确，白棋可能会受到危险的王翼攻击。

e6 是最常见的，尽管从统计数据来看，白人有更好的机会，并且有助于托雷的白人进球。也许最适合黑色的是动态 c5。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Nf3/2...d5/3. Bg5/3...c5
explanations.text:
Torre Attack

c5 is rarely played so early, though it does ask questions of white, and in master play black has a far superior record after this move.

c5 is rarely played so early, though it does ask questions of white, and in master play black has a far superior record after this move.

c5很少这么早下棋，尽管它确实会向白棋提出问题，并且在大师棋中，黑棋在这步棋之后拥有远为优越的记录。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Nf3/2...d5/3. Bg5/3...e6
explanations.text:
Torre Attack

e6 is the most common response, and a solid, though perhaps insipid move. It does leave the knight pinned, and play into white's plans, leaving e5 as a prime destination for white's knight. Black's will almost certainly have to play Be7 at some point too.

explanations.textZh:
托雷攻击

e6 是最常见的反应，也是一个可靠但可能平淡的举动。它确实让马陷入困境，并参与了白方的计划，使 e5 成为白方马的主要目的地。几乎可以肯定，黑棋在某个时候也必须下 Be7。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Nf3/2...d5/3. Bg5/3...e6/4. e3
explanations.text:
Torre Attack

e3 continues white's plan for a kingside assault, with the bishop on d3 and knight on e5 as targets. Black has failed to disrupt white, and needs to play carefully now.

At this point, perhaps c5 is the best response, although white already has a solid advantage.

Torre Attack

explanations.textZh:
托雷攻击

e3继续白方王翼进攻的计划，以d3上的主教和e5上的骑士为目标。黑方未能扰乱白方，现在需要谨慎行事。

在这一点上，也许c5是最好的应对，尽管白棋已经拥有稳固的优势。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Nf3/2...d5/3. e3
explanations.text:
3. e3 · Colle System

White opts for the Colle System, a system opening where their main idea is to prepare an eventual e4 pawn-break. The system knows two set-ups: the traditional Colle, and the Colle-Zukertort system.

Traditional Colle

The traditional Colle is characterized by the upcoming moves Bd3, c3 and Nbd2. This is the way the Edgard Colle, whom the opening is named after, played the system.

Colle-Zukertort system

The Colle-Zukertort system is slightly different from the traditional Colle. The dark-squared bishop is quite passive in the Colle system, so instead of playing c3, White can play b3, preparing to fianchetto the bishop. The b3-pawn also supports the potential c2-c4 in the future.

Black's responses

Since White's next few moves are fairly predictable, Black can choose their own set-up quite freely.

/3...e6/ is played most frequently. Black will usually go for their own set-up with ...Bd6, either ...Nc6 or ...Nbd7, ...c5 and ...b6.

/3...c5/ postpones ...e6 in order to possibly develop the light-squared bishop outside of the pawn-chain (generally to g4, pinning White's knight to the queen).

/3...Bf5/ is the anti-Colle. White can't continue with their system since Black will simply trade light-squared bishops. Therefore, White's usual response is 4. c4, transposing into the Slav defence. A similar transposition occurs after /3...c6/.

explanations.textZh:
3. e3·科莱系统

白棋选择了 Colle 系统，这是一个系统，他们的主要想法是准备最终的 e4 典当。该系统有两种设置：传统的 Colle 系统和 Colle-Zukertort 系统。

传统学院

传统的 Colle 的特点是即将推出的动作 Bd3、c3 和 Nbd2。这就是埃德加·科尔（Edgard Colle）（该开局以他的名字命名）玩这个系统的方式。

Colle-Zukert系统

Colle-Zukertort 系统与传统的 Colle 略有不同。暗方象在科莱体系中相当被动，因此白棋可以下b3，而不是下c3，准备先杀象。 b3-pawn 还支持未来潜在的 c2-c4。

黑方的回应

由于白棋接下来的几步棋是相当可预测的，黑棋可以相当自由地选择自己的布局。

/3...e6/ 最常播放。黑方通常会选择自己的布局...Bd6、...Nc6 或...Nbd7、...c5 和...b6。

/3...c5/ 推迟 ...e6，以便可能在典当链之外发展光方主教（通常到 g4，将白方的马固定到后）。

/3...Bf5/是反Colle。白方无法继续他们的系统，因为黑方将简单地交易浅方象。因此，白棋通常的反应是4.c4，转入斯拉夫防御。类似的换位发生在 /3...c6/ 之后。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. Nf3/2...e6/3. Bf4
explanations.text:
London System Indian Setup with a Early 2. Nf3

The London System has evolved significantly since its showcase in the 1922 London tournament. A prominent shift in modern play is the preference for 2.Bf4 instead of the traditional 2.Nf3. Both sides have seen strategic advancements in the London System.

The move order with 2. Nf3 before 3. Bf4 in the London System can be seen as a more flexible way to reach the London System and has its specific advantages and drawbacks.

For a general introduction to the London System, take a closer look at 1. d4 d5 2. Bf4

Advantages:

Flexibility: By playing 2. Nf3 first, White keeps more options open. This can be particularly useful if Black opts for setups that may not be best met with the traditional London System. For instance, White can divert into other openings or setups based on Black's moves.

Control over e5: Central control, particularly over the e5 and e4 squares, is vital in the London System. The move 2. Nf3 immediately prevents any potential pawn break with ...e5 by Black.

Avoiding Immediate Pressure: Certain move orders by Black might put immediate pressure on the d4 pawn (like ...c5 and ...Qb6 setups). The knight on f3 provides additional support to the d4 pawn.

Drawbacks:

Delaying the London System's Set-up: The very essence of the London System is rapid and harmonious development, particularly the dark-squared bishop. By playing 2. Nf3 first, White is essentially delaying the typical London setup. By shifting the knight from f3 to d4, White diminishes their hold on the e5 square.

When White plays 2.Nf3, it can prompt Black to opt for 2...c5 because the subsequent 3.Bf4 can be met by 3...cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nd7.

Allowing Black's Equalizing Attempts: Black might employ certain systems that challenge White's center more directly before White can establish the typical London System setup.

Potential Transpositions: The move 2. Nf3 allows various transpositions into other openings, which could be a disadvantage if the White player is specifically aiming to play the London System and avoid other lines.

explanations.textZh:
伦敦系统印度设置与早期 2. Nf3

自 1922 年伦敦锦标赛首次亮相以来，伦敦体系已经发生了显着的演变。现代游戏的一个显着转变是对 2.Bf4 的偏好，而不是传统的 2.Nf3。双方都看到了伦敦体系的战略进步。

伦敦系统中 2.Nf3 先于 3.Bf4 的移动顺序可以被视为到达伦敦系统的更灵活的方式，并且有其特定的优点和缺点。

有关伦敦体系的一般介绍，请仔细查看 1. d4 d5 2. Bf4

优点：

灵活性：通过首先下2.Nf3，白方保留了更多的选择余地。如果黑棋选择了可能不适合传统伦敦系统的设置，这可能特别有用。例如，白棋可以根据黑棋的走法转移到其他空位或布局。

对 e5 的控制：中央控制，特别是对 e5 和 e4 广场的控制，在伦敦体系中至关重要。走棋 2. Nf3 立即阻止黑方用 ...e5 进行任何潜在的兵破。

避免立即压力：黑方的某些走棋指令可能会对 d4 兵施加直接压力（如 ​​...c5 和 ...Qb6 设置）。 f3 上的骑士为 d4 棋子提供额外的支持。

缺点：

推迟伦敦体系的建立：伦敦体系的本质是快速和谐的发展，尤其是暗方主教。通过首先下2.Nf3，怀特实质上推迟了典型的伦敦设置。通过将马从 f3 转移到 d4，白方削弱了他们对 e5 方格的掌控。

当白方下2.Nf3时，它可以提示黑方选择2...c5，因为后续的3.Bf4可以通过3...cxd4 4.Nxd4 Nd7来满足。

允许黑方的扳平尝试：在白方建立典型的伦敦体系设置之前，黑方可能会采用某些系统来更直接地挑战白方的中心。

潜在的换位：第 2 步。Nf3 允许各种换位到其他空位，如果白方玩家专门致力于玩伦敦系统并避开其他线路，这可能是一个缺点。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nf6/2. g4
explanations.text:
2. g4!? · Bronstein gambit

2. g4!? is an uncommon gambit line against the Indian defence. White offers the g pawn to deflect Black's knight from controlling the centre.

If Black accepts, 2...Nxg4, White can play 3. e4, achieving a two-pawn centre and scoring tempo on the knight (discovered attack from White's queen). If Black retreats, 3...Nf6, White can continue to expand their centre while scoring tempo on the knight 4. e5 Nd5 5. c4 Nb6 =. Alternatively, Black can try try 3...d6 or 3...d5 (bishop defends knight). After 4. Be2 Black must retreat their knight anyway. In exchange for the pawn, White can often get a two pawn centre and a development lead.

Declining the gambit with 2...d5 allows 3. g5 to kick the knight. If White wants, they can eventually get their two pawn centre after 3...Ne4 4. f3 (c4 is engine continuation) Nd6 5. Nc3 Nc6 6. e4 dxe4 7. fxe4.

Alternatively, 2...h6 declines the gambit and prevents 3. g5. This allows Black to play d5 without getting kicked by 3. g5, e.g. 3. Nf3 d5 (to control e4, renewing threat of Nxg4) 4. h3 (defending g4).

2. g4!? is known as the Bronstein gambit or the Gibbins-Weidenhagen gambit. It is very rare in tournament games. The engine considers White's development lead to not quite compensate for the pawn and weakened kingside but its evaluation only gives Black a slight edge and it scores well enough for White in club level games, so may be worthy of further exploration.

explanations.textZh:
2.g4！？ · 布朗斯坦的策略

2.g4！？这是针对印度防守的罕见策略。白棋提供 g 棋子来转移黑棋的马对中心的控制。

如果黑方接受 2...Nxg4，白方可以下 3.e4，实现两兵中心并对马得分（发现白方后的攻击）。如果黑方撤退，3...Nf6，白方可以继续扩大其中心，同时对马得分 4. e5 Nd5 5. c4 Nb6 =。或者，黑方可以尝试 3...d6 或 3...d5（主教保卫马）。 4. Be2 之后，黑方无论如何都必须撤退他们的马。作为棋子的交换，白棋通常可以获得两个棋子中心和发展领先优势。

用 2...d5 拒绝策略允许 3.g5 踢马。如果白方愿意，他们最终可以在 3...Ne4 4. f3（c4 是引擎延续） Nd6 5. Nc3 Nc6 6. e4 dxe4 7. fxe4 之后获得两个棋子中心。

或者，2...h6 拒绝该策略并阻止 3. g5。这使得黑方可以下 d5 而不会被 3. g5 踢，例如3. Nf3 d5（控制e4，延续Nxg4的威胁） 4. h3（防守g4）。

2.g4！？被称为布朗斯坦策略或吉宾斯-魏登哈根策略。这在锦标赛比赛中是非常罕见的。引擎认为白方的发展导致并不能完全补偿兵和弱化的王翼，但其评估只给黑方带来了轻微的优势，并且在俱乐部级别的比赛中对白方来说得分足够好，因此可能值得进一步探索。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...Nh6
explanations.text:
Queen's Pawn Opening

1...Nh6?!

This rarer response to 1. d4 plays in a similar fashion to the Adams/Hippopotamus Defence. Black develops the knight to the rim instead of contesting the center. White can take the center for free or try to ruin Black's pawn structure with Bxh6.

White can choose from a variety of moves, such as:

2. c4, playing in the fashion of Queen's Pawn openings

2. e4, taking the full center

2. Nf3, developing the kingside knight

2. Nc3, developing the queenside knight

2. Bf4, playing in the fashion of the London

2. Bxh6, trading bishop for knight to damage Black's kingside pawn structure.

皇后典当开局

1...NH6？！

这种对 1.d4 的罕见反应与亚当斯/河马防御类似。黑棋将骑士发展到边缘，而不是对抗中心。白棋可以免费占据中心，或者尝试用 Bxh6 破坏黑棋的兵结构。

白方可以选择多种走法，例如：

2. c4，以皇后兵开局的方式进行游戏

2. e4，取全中心

2. Nf3，开发王翼骑士

2. NC3，开发后翼骑士

2. Bf4，玩转伦敦时尚

2. Bxh6，用象换马，破坏黑方王翼兵结构。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...h5
explanations.text:
Queen's Pawn Opening

1...h5?!

Black plays in a similar fashion to the Goldsmith Defence, pushing a flank pawn on the kingside. Instead of contesting the center or developing a piece, Black may want to push their h-pawn to h3 to try and ruin White's kingside. However, this plan is unsound as White grabs the center.

White can choose from a variety of moves, such as:

2. e4, taking the full center

2. c4, playing in the fashion of Queen's Pawn openings

2. Nf3, developing the kingside knight

2. Nc3, developing the queenside knight

2. Bf4, playing in the fashion of the London

2. h4!?, halting the h-pawn's advance

1...h5？！

黑棋的玩法与金匠防御类似，将侧翼棋子推到王翼。黑棋可能不想与中心争夺或发展棋子，而是想将他们的h兵推到h3以尝试破坏白棋的王翼。然而，这个计划并不健全，因为白棋占据了中心。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. d4/1...h6
explanations.text:
Queen's Pawn Opening

1...h6?!

A less conventional response to 1. d4, playing in a similar fashion to the Carr Defence. Black wants to gain space on the kingside with g5 and Bg7, however, White can grab the center as Black hasn't contested the center themselves nor developed a piece.

White can choose from a variety of moves, such as:

2. e4, taking the full center

2. c4, playing in the fashion of Queen's Pawn openings

2. Nf3, developing the kingside knight

2. Nc3, developing the queenside knight

2. Bf4, playing in the fashion of the London, but the bishop can be kicked with 2...g5

2. h4!?, stopping g5.

1...h6？！

对 1.d4 的一种不太传统的反应，以与卡尔防御类似的方式进行。黑方想用g5和Bg7在王翼赢得空间，然而，白方可以抓住中路，因为黑方自己没有争夺中路，也没有发展出棋子。

白方可以选择多种走法，例如：

2. e4，取全中心

2. c4，以皇后兵开局的方式进行游戏

2. Nf3，开发王翼骑士

2. NC3，开发后翼骑士

2. Bf4，按照伦敦的方式打法，但是主教可以用2...g5踢掉

2. h4!?，停止g5。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e3
explanations.text:
1. e3 · Van 't Kruijs Opening

An irregular opening, considered somewhat passive, as although White opens lines for their bishop and queen to enter the game, Black is given the opportunity to take over the centre with ...e5 and ...d5.

Black may play any number of moves to stake a claim in the centre: 1...Nf6, 1...e5, 1...d5, 1...c5 are all reasonable. 1...g6, intending ...Bg7, or 1...Nf6 followed by 2...g6, is a typical approach to meet lots of transpositions equally.

Many openings for White feature e3 at some point, so play can transpose into lines of the English Opening if White plays c4, Queen's Pawn Opening with d4, Larsen's Opening with b3 and Bb2, and so on. A consideration is that the pawn on e3 prevents development of White's queenside bishop: White must concede a tempo with e4, passively develop it to d2, or fianchetto it to b2.

Uniquely, play can proceed with 1...e5 2. e4!?, which arrives at an Open Game (1. e4 e5) but with colours reversed, where it is Black's turn to move.

After 1...Nf6 2. Nf3 g6 3. b4 Bg7 4. Bb2 O-O 5. c4 d6 6. d4, the most common continuation, play reaches a King's Indian-type position.

explanations.textZh:
1. e3·范特克鲁伊斯开局

不规则的开局，被认为有些被动，因为虽然白方为他们的主教和后进入游戏打开了路线，但黑方有机会用 ...e5 和 ...d5 接管中心。

黑方可以下任意步棋以在中心占据一席之地：1...Nf6、1...e5、1...d5、1...c5 都是合理的。 1...g6，意为...Bg7，或1...Nf6 后跟2...g6，是同等满足大量换位的典型方法。

白方的许多开局在某些时候都具有 e3，因此，如果白方下 c4，则可以将棋法转换为英式开局的行，后兵开局为 d4，拉森开局为 b3 和 Bb2，等等。一个考虑因素是，e3 上的棋子阻止了白方后翼主教的发展：白方必须承认 e4 的节奏，被动地将其发展到 d2，或者先将其发展到 b2。

独特的是，游戏可以继续进行 1...e5 2. e4!?，这会到达开放游戏 (1. e4 e5)，但颜色相反，轮到黑棋走棋。

在 1...Nf6 2. Nf3 g6 3. b4 Bg7 4. Bb2 O-O 5. c4 d6 6. d4（最常见的延续）之后，比赛达到了 King 的印第安式位置。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e3/1...d5
explanations.text:
Van 't Kruijs Opening

1. e3 d5

The response 1...d5 by black to the opening 1.e3 can be a choice to move the game closer to a variation of the Queen`s pawn opening, especially if white responds with 2. d4

范特克鲁伊斯开场

1.e3d5

黑方对开局 1.e3 的反应 1...d5 可以是一种选择，使游戏更接近后棋开局的变体，特别是当白方回应 2.d4 时

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e3/1...e5
explanations.text:
1...e5

Black takes space in the centre.

If White responds 2. d4, a reversed French defence position is arrived at, more usually seen in the Englund gambit declined with e3.

2. e4?! appears to reach the usual position seen after 1. e4 e5, the Open game--except this time it's Black to move.

explanations.textZh:
1...e5

黑色占据了中间的空间。

如果白方回应 2. d4，法国队的防守位置就会逆转，这在英格兰队以 e3 拒绝的策略中更为常见。

2.e4？！似乎到达了公开赛 1. e4 e5 之后看到的通常位置 - 只不过这次是黑棋走棋。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e3/1...e5/2. e4
explanations.text:
2. e4!? · Reversed open game

Play reaches the same position as after 1.e4 e5, the Open game, but with Black to move. This is an irregular way to play where White concedes the first move advantage, perhaps because they really wanted to play the Black side.

From here any of the typical Open game positions can be reached, but with colours reversed.
