explanations.textZh:
西西里防御、龙、主线

白色城堡的皇后区。黑方接下来应该用 Rc8 或 Qa5 瞄准白方的王，但其他走法如 Ne5 也是可能的。双方经常使用a6和b6（黑）或g2和h2（白）上的棋子来打开他们攻击的一方的阵线。

explanations.text:
Sicilian Defense, Dragon, Old Line

Black takes advantage of the half-open c-file they received in the Open Sicilian, and aims at the hanging c4-bishop. As Nxd4 Qxd4 Ng4! takes advantage of the overworked White queen and Black is attacking both bishops at once, White typically moves the bishop to safety with Bb3, keeping an eye on the Black king.

黑方利用他们在西西里公开赛中收到的半开c线优势，瞄准了悬挂的c4主教。作为 Nxd4 Qxd4 Ng4！利用过度劳累的白后和黑同时攻击两个主教，白方通常用 Bb3 将主教移动到安全的地方，并密切关注黑王。

explanations.text:

White correctly moves their bishop out of the c8 rook's line of fire with Bb3, keeping watch over Black's kingside. Now pawn attacks begin on both sides, and speed and tempi are very important in these such attacks.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c5/2. Nf3/2...d6/3. d4/3...cxd4/4. Nxd4/4...Nf6/5. Nc3/5...g6/6. Bc4
explanations.text:
Sicilian Defense: Dragon Variation

6. Bc4 is an older sideline, very similar to the Fischer-Sozin attack in the Najdorf and the Scheveningen. White seeks to better control d5 and exert pressure on the black king, especially the f7 square. It also keeps options open for white, on whether to transpose into the mainline Yugoslav or play a more quiet, maneuvering game. Black almost always proceeds with Bg7, looking to castle fast.

If white doesn't transpose into the Yugoslav Attack, this variation is considered not sharp enough for black, which is why it has fallen out of favour. Black gets a fantastic middlegame with a very nice pawn structure and easy plans, whereas white has no immediate pressure and doesn't use the extra tempo effectively.

It is worth noting that formally this variation doesn't have a name or separate code in the ECO. Informally, some call it the Sozin or the Italian Attack.

explanations.textZh:
西西里防御：龙变式

6. Bc4 是一条较旧的边线，与 Najdorf 和 Scheveningen 的 Fischer-Sozin 进攻非常相似。白棋寻求更好地控制d5并向黑王施加压力，尤其是f7方格。它还为白方保留了选择余地，无论是转移到南斯拉夫主线还是玩更安静、机动的游戏。黑方几乎总是下 Bg7，希望快速占领城堡。

如果白棋没有转换成南斯拉夫进攻，那么这种变化对于黑棋来说就被认为不够尖锐，这就是它失宠的原因。黑方获得了精彩的中局，拥有非常好的棋子结构和简单的计划，而白方没有立即的压力，也没有有效地利用额外的节奏。

值得注意的是，从形式上来说，这种变体在 ECO 中没有名称或单独的代码。非正式地，一些人将其称为“索津”或“意大利进攻”。

explanations.text:
Sicilian Defense: Dragon Variation

Black continues with the regular plan of fianchettoing the dark squared bishop. Both sides will continue by castling and entering the middlegame. White will try to play actively in the center and try to eliminate the bishop on g7, whereas black will use that bishop to pressure the center and the queenside.

Alternatively, black can try to transpose into the Yugoslav attack with f3, Qd2, O-O-O and launching a pawn storm at black's king. However, black can prevent this since Bc4 is premature in this position and should be played later on.

Alternatively, black can try to transpose into the Yugoslav attack with f3, Qd2, O-O-O and launching a pawn storm at black's king. However, black can prevent this since Bc4 is premature in this position and should be played later on.
explanations.textZh:
西西里防御：龙变式

黑棋继续执行常规计划，先下暗方象。双方继续易位，进入中局。白棋将尝试在中路积极发挥并试图消除 g7 上的象，而黑棋将利用该象向中路和后翼施压。

或者，黑方可以尝试用 f3、Qd2、O-O-O 转入南斯拉夫进攻并向黑方国王发起兵风暴。然而，黑棋可以阻止这种情况，因为 Bc4 在这个位置上还为时过早，应该稍后下棋。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c5/2. Nf3/2...d6/3. d4/3...cxd4/4. Nxd4/4...Nf6/5. Nc3/5...g6/6. f4
explanations.text:
Levenfish Variation

This move has a few ideas connoted to it. The primary idea is to push e5, since this pawn idea gains central influence and is now prepared by f4. White can also look to put the knight back onto f3 and play the position like a Grand Prix attack, with future ideas of swinging the white queen onto the kingside through the e1-h4 diagonal. Against some sidelines, white can also consider castling long!

The point - 6...Bg7?! 7. e5!

The natural looking 6...Bg7 is actually theoretically inaccurate. This runs into White's primary idea of the Levenfish, to push e5. White does this immediately with 7. e5 and then can claim a slight, nagging edge in the upcoming variations because of the advanced e-pawn.

White should seek active play with Bb5+ and Qe2 to support the pawn before deciding which way to castle, both leading to viable positions

Main Line - 6...Nc6

The best move since it immediately covers the threat of e5. This idea effectively killed the Levenfish variation pre-2000. Black develops the queenside knight. Here, White has traditionally gone for the line 7. Nxc6!? bxc6 8. e5 which is somewhat favourable for black upon 8...Nd7! 9. exd6 exd6 leading to an interesting pawn structure. A sounder alternative several high profile games have included is the idea of 7. Nf3!? swinging the knight back to the kingside and looking to play a slower game on the kingside.

Other sidelines

6...Nbd7 is traditionally met by 7. Nf3, although in recent times engines have preferred queen developments such as 7. Qe2, the choice of Grandmaster Gevorg Harutjunyan.

6...a6 aims to stop a piece landing on b5 and constructs a sort of Dragondorf setup. Here White can choose between 7. e5 and 7. Nf3.

Statistics

351 games in Lichess Masters database.

White wins 32 percent of games. 29 percent are drawn. 38% have black emerge victorious.

explanations.textZh:
利文菲什变例

这一举措有一些隐含的想法。主要想法是推动e5，因为这个典当想法获得了核心影响力，现在由f4准备。白棋还可以考虑将马放回f3，并像大奖赛进攻一样发挥该位置，未来的想法是通过e1-h4对角线将白后摆到王侧。对抗一些旁观者，白棋也可以考虑易位长！

重点 - 6...Bg7？！ 7.e5！

看起来自然的 6...Bg7 实际上在理论上是不准确的。这与 White 的 Levenfish 的主要想法是一致的，即推动 e5。白棋立即用 7. e5 做到了这一点，然后由于先进的 e-pawn，可以在即将到来的变化中获得轻微的、令人烦恼的优势。

白方应该在决定走哪条路之前积极使用 Bb5+ 和 Qe2 来支持棋子，这两者都会导致可行的位置

主线 - 6...Nc6

这是最好的举动，因为它立即覆盖了 e5 的威胁。这个想法有效地扼杀了 2000 年之前的 Levenfish 变体。黑方发展了后翼骑士。在这里，白棋传统上走7行。Nxc6！？ bxc6 8. e5 对 8...Nd7 上的黑色有些有利！ 9. exd6 exd6 导致一个有趣的典当结构。几款备受瞩目的游戏中包含的更合理的替代方案是 7. Nf3!?将骑士摆回王翼，并希望在王翼进行较慢的游戏。

其他副业

6...Nbd7 传统上由 7. Nf3 满足，尽管最近引擎更喜欢皇后开发，例如 7. Qe2，大师 Gevorg Harutjunyan 的选择。

6...a6 旨在阻止棋子落在 b5 上并构建一种 Dragondorf 设置。这里白棋可以在 7. e5 和 7. Nf3 之间选择。

统计数据

Lichess Masters 数据库中有 351 场比赛。

白棋胜率为 32%。 29% 被抽取。 38% 的黑人获胜。

Nc3 is currently the preferred white move in the main line, however Bb5 or Bg5 are widely accepted but less played through openings.

dxc5 对于白棋来说似乎是一个诱人的棋步，可以进行皇后交换并取代黑棋的国王，但很容易在 Nxe4 的这条线上扩散。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c5/2. Nf3/2...d6/3. Bb5
explanations.text:
3. Bb5+ · Moscow variation

3. Bb5+ is the Moscow variation. White develops their bishop with a tempo. White's kingside is now developed, so they are ready to castle. One plan for White is to set up a Maróczy bind, where they control d5 with pawns on both e4 and c4, and not wishing to have the king's bishop stuck behind the c4 pawn, they exchanging it first. Alternatively, they may plan to play for the centre with c3 and d4, Ruy López-style.

Black must get out of the check. In order of popularity, their legal options are:

3...Bd7 is the main line. Black compels the exchange of bishops, after which Black can take back with either the knight or the queen. 4...Qxd7 is sharper, retaining the option of ...Nc6 to control d5.

3...Nd7 is an alternative. White doesn't usually elect to take the knight, which would allow Black the bishop pair. Instead, 4. d4 is popular: White can open the centre and recapture with the queen, who cannot be chased away now by Nc6.

3...Nc6 blocks the check by developing the knight to its natural square. The knight is pinned and cannot influence the centre yet, so Black usually intends 4...Bd7. White may trade bishop for knight and double Black's pawns (4. Bxc6 bxc6) but 4. O-O is more common. After 4...Bd7, Bxc6 would no longer lead to doubling Black's pawns, so if provoked to move the bishop, White will usually retreat it, e.g. 5. Re1 a6 6. Bf1.

Finally, 3...Qd7?? just blunders the queen, of course.

History

The Moscow variation is also known as the Canal-Sokolsky attack after Alexey Sokolsky and Esteban Canal who began playing it in the 1940s. It is a popular sideline where White wishes to avoid the mainline Open Sicilians involving d4 cxd4 Nxd4.

The name "Moscow variation" could come from several events in Moscow where the opening was played. One such is the 1947 Chigorin Memorial, where this line was played twice by Sokolsky, though earlier games are known.

It is a close "cousin" to 2...Nc6 3. Bb5, known as the Rossolimo variation. Nicolas Rossolimo also played 2...d6 3. Bb5+, and some databases give Rossolimo as an alternate name for the Moscow (e.g. Chess365.com list 2...d6 3. Bb5+ as "Canal-Sokolsky (Nimzovich-Rossolimo, Moscow) attack").

Garry Kasparov played this line in Kasparov versus the World, a consultation game where he played against moves chosen by online vote, which Kasparov described as the hardest-fought game of his career and "the greatest game in the history of chess."
explanations.textEn:
3. Bb5+ · Moscow variation

3. Bb5+ is the Moscow variation. White develops their bishop with a tempo. White's kingside is now developed, so they are ready to castle. One plan for White is to set up a Maróczy bind, where they control d5 with pawns on both e4 and c4, and not wishing to have the king's bishop stuck behind the c4 pawn, they exchanging it first. Alternatively, they may plan to play for the centre with c3 and d4, Ruy López-style.

Black must get out of the check. In order of popularity, their legal options are:

3...Bd7 is the main line. Black compels the exchange of bishops, after which Black can take back with either the knight or the queen. 4...Qxd7 is sharper, retaining the option of ...Nc6 to control d5.

3...Nd7 is an alternative. White doesn't usually elect to take the knight, which would allow Black the bishop pair. Instead, 4. d4 is popular: White can open the centre and recapture with the queen, who cannot be chased away now by Nc6.

3...Nc6 blocks the check by developing the knight to its natural square. The knight is pinned and cannot influence the centre yet, so Black usually intends 4...Bd7. White may trade bishop for knight and double Black's pawns (4. Bxc6 bxc6) but 4. O-O is more common. After 4...Bd7, Bxc6 would no longer lead to doubling Black's pawns, so if provoked to move the bishop, White will usually retreat it, e.g. 5. Re1 a6 6. Bf1.

Finally, 3...Qd7?? just blunders the queen, of course.

History

The Moscow variation is also known as the Canal-Sokolsky attack after Alexey Sokolsky and Esteban Canal who began playing it in the 1940s. It is a popular sideline where White wishes to avoid the mainline Open Sicilians involving d4 cxd4 Nxd4.

The name "Moscow variation" could come from several events in Moscow where the opening was played. One such is the 1947 Chigorin Memorial, where this line was played twice by Sokolsky, though earlier games are known.

It is a close "cousin" to 2...Nc6 3. Bb5, known as the Rossolimo variation. Nicolas Rossolimo also played 2...d6 3. Bb5+, and some databases give Rossolimo as an alternate name for the Moscow (e.g. Chess365.com list 2...d6 3. Bb5+ as "Canal-Sokolsky (Nimzovich-Rossolimo, Moscow) attack").

Garry Kasparov played this line in Kasparov versus the World, a consultation game where he played against moves chosen by online vote, which Kasparov described as the hardest-fought game of his career and "the greatest game in the history of chess."
explanations.textZh:
3. Bb5+·莫斯科变体

3. Bb5+ 是莫斯科变体。白棋有节奏地发展他们的象。白棋的王翼现在已经开发完毕，所以他们已经准备好城堡了。白方的一个计划是建立 Maróczy 绑定，他们用 e4 和 c4 上的棋子控制 d5，并且不希望国王的主教卡在 c4 棋子后面，他们首先交换它。或者，他们可能计划用 c3 和 d4 打中锋，鲁伊·洛佩斯风格。

黑棋必须出局。按照受欢迎程度排列，他们的合法选择是：

3...Bd7为主线。黑方强制交换主教，之后黑方可以用马或后夺回。 4...Qxd7 更锐利，保留...Nc6 控制d5 的选项。

3...Nd7 是一种替代品。白方通常不会选择吃马，这将允许黑方成为主教对。相反，4. d4 很受欢迎：白方可以打开中心并用后线夺回，而后线现在不能被 Nc6 赶走。

3...Nc6 通过将马展开到其自然方格来阻止检查。马被牵制，还不能影响中心，所以黑方通常打算 4...Bd7。白棋可以用象换马，并加黑棋的棋子 (4. Bxc6 bxc6)，但 4. O-O 更为常见。 4...Bd7 之后，Bxc6 将不再导致黑方棋子加倍，因此如果被激怒而移动主教，白方通常会撤退，例如5. Re1 a6 6. Bf1。

最后，3...Qd7??当然，这只是让女王犯了错误。

历史

莫斯科变种也被称为 Canal-Sokolsky 攻击，由 Alexey Sokolsky 和 Esteban Canal 在 20 世纪 40 年代开始玩。这是一个受欢迎的副线，白棋希望避开涉及 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 的主线西西里公开赛。

“莫斯科变奏”这个名字可能来自于开幕式在莫斯科举行的几场活动。其中之一就是 1947 年的齐戈林纪念馆，索科尔斯基曾在这里玩过两次这句台词，但更早的游戏是众所周知的。

它是 2...Nc6 3. Bb5 的近亲，被称为 Rossolimo 变体。 Nicolas Rossolimo 也玩过 2...d6 3. Bb5+，一些数据库将 Rossolimo 作为莫斯科的替代名称（例如 Chess365.com 列表 2...d6 3. Bb5+ 为“Canal-Sokolsky（尼姆佐维奇-Rossolimo，莫斯科）攻击”）。

加里·卡斯帕罗夫（Garry Kasparov）在《卡斯帕罗夫对抗世界》（Kasparov vs the World）中使用了这句台词，这是一款咨询游戏，他与在线投票选择的棋步进行对弈，卡斯帕罗夫将其描述为他职业生涯中最艰难的游戏，也是“国际象棋历史上最伟大的游戏”。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c5/2. Nf3/2...d6/3. Bc4
explanations.text:
Open Sicilian

3. Bc4, "Italian" variation

A trendy continuation, leading to structures resembling the Giuoco Pianissimo or the Ruy Lopez. White usually develops with d2-d3, c2-c3, O-O, Re1, and plays a2-a4 or Bb3 to prevent the bishop from being exchanged off, and prepares Nbd2-Nf1-Ng3 manoeuvres.

开放西西里岛

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c5/2. Nf3/2...e5
explanations.text:
2...e5? · Jalalabad variation

Sorry, but JalalaVeryBad.―Anish Giri

In the Jalalabad variation, Black responds to e4 with both e5 and c5 (in either the move order 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 c5? or 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 e5?). This gives up Black's central e-pawn. This is not considered sound.

After 3. Nxe5, Black can play 3...Nc6, offering to trade knights and take the game in a Stafford gambit-style direction, or 3...Qe7 looking to recover the pawn.

3...Nc6 offers to trade knights. 4. Nxc6 dxc6 and the position resembles a Stafford gambit where Black is down a tempo, having played c5 instead of Nf6. There is no immediately threat to e4 and the position is a lot less precarious for White.

3...Qe7 and Black looks to recover the pawn after 4. Nf3 Qxe4+ 5. Be2. Unfortunately White can hold onto the pawn with 4. d4 cxd4 5. Qxd4 (protecting knight and e pawn) Nc6 6. Nxc6 dxc6 +-.

3...d6?! to kick the knight seems very weakening while Black's king is still in the centre.

History

Sam Sloan explains he invented the opening while incarcerated for six weeks in Jalalabad prison in Afghanistan. He played it in a Marshall Chess Club tournament in 1978, where he defeated Jans Pamiljens with the 3...Qe7 continuation in a game that was published in Chess Life. Writing around 2002, Sloan recalled he had played it at other times in the late 70s, but that he thought his ex-wife had taken his score sheets. Of the opening, he said, "I still think that the Jalalabad Defense is playable."

It received some online revival as an unorthodox gambit line online in 2020.

explanations.textZh:
2...e5？ · 贾拉拉巴德变体

抱歉，贾拉拉非常糟糕。—安尼什·吉里 (Anish Giri)

在贾拉拉巴德变体中，黑棋用 e5 和 c5 响应 e4（走棋顺序为 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 c5？或 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 e5？）。这放弃了黑方的中央电子兵。这不被认为是健全的。

3. Nxe5 之后，黑方可以下 3...Nc6，提出交易马并将游戏推向斯塔福德弃兵风格的方向，或者 3...Qe7 寻求收回棋子。

3...Nc6 提出交易骑士。 4. Nxc6 dxc6，该位置类似于斯塔福德策略，其中黑方降低了节奏，下的是 c5 而不是 Nf6。 e4 没有立即受到威胁，白棋的地位也没有那么不稳定。

3...Qe7 和黑方希望在 4. Nf3 Qxe4+ 5. Be2 之后收回棋子。不幸的是，白方可以用 4. d4 cxd4 5. Qxd4（保护马和 e 兵）Nc6 6. Nxc6 dxc6 +- 来保住棋子。

3...d6？！当黑王仍在中间时，踢马似乎很弱。

历史

萨姆·斯隆解释说，他在阿富汗贾拉拉巴德监狱被监禁六周时发明了这个开口。 1978 年，他在马歇尔国际象棋俱乐部锦标赛上玩过这款游戏，并以 3...Qe7 延续击败了 Jans Pamiljens，该游戏发表在《Chess Life》上。斯隆在 2002 年左右写到，他在 70 年代末的其他时候也玩过这种游戏，但他认为他的前妻拿走了他的乐谱。谈到开局，他说：“我仍然认为贾拉拉巴德防御是可以玩的。”

2020 年，它作为一种非正统的在线策略在网上得到了一些复兴。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c5/2. Nf3/2...e6
explanations.text:
2...e6 · French Sicilian

Black opens up the a3-f8 diagonal for their dark squared bishop, while also controlling the d5 square for a second time. This prepares to play ...d5 and recapture with a pawn, gaining further central control.

Open the centre

3. d4 is the main move. This is the standard open Sicilian plan: 3...cxd4 4. Nxd4. The centre is open and both of White's bishops are ready to come into the game. Then Black has a choice of how to proceed: the main French Sicilians are the Kan, Paulsen, Taimanov, or four knights variations.

3. Nc3 is also possible. This postpones d4 while White waits for more information on which Sicilian Black will choose.

Anti-Sicilians

There is also a variety of "anti-Sicilians" (Sicilians that aren't the open Sicilian) available to White, avoiding the main line and aiming to exploit the fact that 2...e6 blocked Black's c8 bishop. Against 2...d6 or 2...Nc6, the main anti-Sicilian is 3. Bb5, but it is not so effective here following 2...e6. If White still wishes to avoid the open Sicilian, they might opt for one of the following instead.

3. c3 is the delayed Alapin Sicilian. The idea is to support playing d4 and keep the pawn there. While similar in character to the Alapin played on turn two (1. e4 c5 2. c3), playing c3 on the third move, after Black has committed a pawn to 2...e6, means Black has different options for how to proceed.

3. c4 is the Kramnik Sicilian, creating a "Maroczy bind" position where White contests the d5 square.

3. b3 is the Westerinen attack, preparing to fianchetto the bishop.

3. d3 may lead to a king's Indian-type position. White recognises that the position is a bit like a French defence (1. e4 e6), just where Black has already played ...c5 and hasn't gotten to ...d5 yet. White may start with 3. Qe2 or 3. g3 and reach the same set-up.

History

Carl Jaenisch (1813―1872) may have been the first one to give this the name "French". In his 19th century treatise on chess, he grouped together 1...c5 followed by 2...e6 (2...e6 was the main variation at the time) with 1...e6 as the "French Openings", writing, "Far from being 'irregular,' they afford a line of defence more secure than [1...e5], but the Kings being severally less exposed, the game becomes much more tedious."

explanations.textZh:
2...e6 · 法语西西里语

黑方为暗方象打开了a3-f8对角线，同时第二次控制了d5方格。这准备玩...d5并用棋子重新夺回，获得进一步的中央控制。

打开中心

3、d4为主招。这是标准的开放西西里计划：3...cxd4 4. Nxd4。中心已经开放，白方的两位主教都已准备好上场比赛。然后布莱克可以选择如何进行：主要的法国西西里棋是坎、保尔森、泰马诺夫或四骑士变体。

3.NC3也是可以的。这推迟了 d4，同时白方等待有关西西里黑方将选择哪一个的更多信息。

反西西里人

白方还可以使用各种“反西西里人”（不是开放西西里人的西西里人），避开主线并旨在利用 2...e6 阻挡黑方 c8 主教这一事实。对抗2...d6或2...Nc6，主要的反西西里岛是3.Bb5，但在2...e6之后在这里不太有效。如果白棋仍然希望避免开放的西西里棋，他们可能会选择以下其中一种。

3. c3 是延迟的阿拉平西西里语。这个想法是支持玩 d4 并将棋子保留在那里。虽然与第二回合下的阿拉宾（1. e4 c5 2. c3）的性格相似，但在黑方将棋子下到 2...e6 后，在第三步下棋 c3，意味着黑方对于如何进行有不同的选择。

3. c4 是克拉姆尼克西西里棋，创建了一个“Maroczy 束缚”位置，白棋在 d5 方格中争夺。

3. b3是Westerinen进攻，准备向主教发起进攻。

3. d3 可能会导致国王的印第安式位置。白方认识到该位置有点像法国防守（1. e4 e6），只是黑方已经下...c5但尚未到达...d5。白棋可以从 3.Qe2 或 3.g3 开始，并达到相同的设置。

历史

卡尔·耶尼施（Carl Jaenisch，1813—1872）可能是第一个将其命名为“French”的人。在他 19 世纪的国际象棋论文中，他将 1...c5 和 2...e6（2...e6 是当时的主要变体）组合在一起，其中 1...e6 作为“法国开局”，写道：“它们远非‘不规则’，它们提供了比 [1...e5] 更安全的防线，但国王队的暴露程度较低，比赛变得更加乏味。”

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c5/2. Nf3/2...e6/3. b3
explanations.text:
3. b3

This opening has some very interesting ideas. With this move White prepares to fianchetto the dark squared bishop to b2 but depending on what Black plays next White's ideas aren't really clear.

Black can continue with the usual Taimanov or Kan setup and Black can also play the /4...d5/ pawn break, but the most played move in the chess database right now is /4...b6/.

3.b3

黑方可以继续采用通常的 Taimanov 或 Kan 设置，黑方也可以走 /4...d5/ 走兵，但目前国际象棋数据库中最常用的着法是 /4...b6/。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c5/2. Nf3/2...e6/3. d4
explanations.text:
3. d4 · Open Sicilian with 2...e6

White plays 3. d4, inviting Black to trade a pawn and open the position.

3...cxd4 is the main move. Black captures towards the centre with a flank pawn, breaking up White's two pawn centre. Once White recaptures 4. Nxd4, Black has two central pawns to White's one, and a semi-open c-file to use. White meanwhile has opened attacking lines: both bishops have access to the game, and their queen has the semi-open d-file. After the trade of pawns is complete, Black then has a choice of ...e6 Sicilians, the most popular of which are the Kan (4...a6), Taimanov (4...Nc6), four knights (both ...Nc6 and ...Nf6), or Kveinis (4...Qb6) variations.

Very minor sidelines include:

3...d5!?, the Marshall counterattack.

3...a6!?, the Drazic variation.

explanations.textZh:
3. d4 · 用 2...e6 打开西西里岛

白方下 3.d4，邀请黑方交换棋子并开仓。

3...cxd4 是主要动作。黑棋用侧翼棋子向中心夺取，打破了白棋的两个棋子中心。一旦白方夺回 4.Nxd4，黑方就拥有了白方的两个中央棋子，以及一个半开的 c 档可供使用。与此同时，白棋打开了进攻线：两位主教都可以进入比赛，而他们的皇后拥有半开放的d线。棋子交易完成后，黑方可以选择 ...e6 西西里人，其中最受欢迎的是 Kan (4...a6)、Taimanov (4...Nc6)、四骑士（...Nc6 和 ...Nf6）或 Kveinis (4...Qb6) 变体。

非常小的副业包括：

3...d5!?，马歇尔反击。

3...a6!?，德拉奇变体。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c5/2. Nf3/2...e6/3. d4/3...cxd4
explanations.text:
Sicilian Defence

Black captures White's d-pawn with cxd4 to reduce White's control of the centre, expecting the pawn to be recaptured.

White usually plays 4. Nxd4 so that the knight may subsequently move to b3 to assist in the defence of their king following queenside castling. A knight on d4 also eyes the f5 square and once the king is safe on the queenside can support the advance of a barrage of pawns at Black's castled position.

Also in keeping with the position is the gambit 4. c3, usually transposing into the Morra Gambit. White obtains a lead in development and aims to fully open the c-file to counter Black's influence thereof.
explanations.textEn:
Sicilian Defence

Black captures White's d-pawn with cxd4 to reduce White's control of the centre, expecting the pawn to be recaptured.

White usually plays 4. Nxd4 so that the knight may subsequently move to b3 to assist in the defence of their king following queenside castling. A knight on d4 also eyes the f5 square and once the king is safe on the queenside can support the advance of a barrage of pawns at Black's castled position.

Also in keeping with the position is the gambit 4. c3, usually transposing into the Morra Gambit. White obtains a lead in development and aims to fully open the c-file to counter Black's influence thereof.

西西里防御

黑方用 cxd4 吃掉白方的 d 棋子，以减少白方对中心的控制，并期望棋子被重新吃掉。

白棋通常下4.Nxd4，这样马就可以在后侧易位后移动到b3以协助防守他们的国王。 d4 上的马也关注 f5 方格，一旦国王在后侧安全，就可以在黑方的城堡位置支援一连串兵的前进。

同样与该位置保持一致的是开局 4. c3，通常转换为莫拉开局。白方取得发展领先，旨在全面开放c档以对抗黑方的影响。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c5/2. Nf3/2...e6/3. d4/3...cxd4/4. Nxd4/4...Nc6
explanations.text:
4...Nc6 · Taimanov variation

4...Nc6 in the e6 Sicilian is the Taimanov, named for Russian GM Mark Taimanov who popularised the opening in the 1960s.

While Nc6 doesn't make a threat on e4, 5. Nc3 is White's usual response all the same. After, Black's principal options are 5...Nf6, the Four Knights Sicilian, or 5...Qc7, the Bastrikov variation.

With 5...Qc7, Black wants to focus on their queenside development first: a6, b5, Bb7 and Rc8, with the dark-square bishop developing to e7 or b4. White's plans include the English Attack (with Nc3, Be3, Qd2 and O-O-O), or Nc3, Be2 and O-O.

5. Nb5 is the chief sideline, where White moves to exploit the hole Black left on d6 when they played 2...e6. White has two attackers on d6 and Black only one defender, the bishop, so 5...a6? allows 6. Nd6+ Bxd6 7. Qxd6 ∓. Black gets the bishop pair and their Queen is all up in White's business. The only way for White to add a defender to d6 is 5...d6 (now the queen sees d6), after which 6. c4 or 6.Bf4 usually follow.

5. Nxc6?!, exchanging the knights, is a sideline only really seen at the amateur level. Unlike in the Four Knights Sicilian, where exchanging the knights lets White push e5 with tempo, it is of no real benefit to White here. After 5...bxc6, Black can easily play 6...d5 with extra support from the c pawn. 6. e5? is met with 6...Qa5+ forking the pawn.

5. c4 is a Maróczy bind- or Kramnik-style line where White looks to gain space. 5...Nf6 6. Nc3 Bb4 equalises.

History

The Taimanov Sicilian evolved out of the older Paulsen variation of the Sicilian (a Sicilian with with e6, a6, and Qc7). Curiously, in his book, Taimanov himself didn't consider 4...Nc6 to be the defining moving of his system, which he describes as just one of a number of possible move orders of the Paulsen. Rather, he considered the defining move of the Taimanov to be delaying Qc7 in favour of Nge7, describing "Black's basic opening plan in... the Taimanov system [is to remove] active White pieces from the d4 outpost... by an exchange of the knight in the centre [Nxd4 Qxd4] and the subsequent 'tempo' transfer of the 'knight understudy' to c6."

explanations.textZh:
4...Nc6·泰马诺夫变体

e6 Sicilian 中的 4...Nc6 是 Taimanov，以俄罗斯通用汽车总经理马克·泰马诺夫 (Mark Taimanov) 的名字命名，他在 20 世纪 60 年代推广了这种开口。

虽然Nc6对e4、5没有威胁。Nc3仍然是白方通常的反应。之后，黑方的主要选择是 5...Nf6（西西里四骑士）或 5...Qc7（巴斯特里科夫变体）。

对于 5...Qc7，黑方希望首先专注于他们的后翼发展：a6、b5、Bb7 和 Rc8，而暗方主教发展到 e7 或 b4。白棋的计划包括英式进攻（Nc3、Be3、Qd2 和 O-O-O），或 Nc3、Be2 和 O-O。

5. Nb5 是主要边线，白棋在 2...e6 下棋时利用黑棋在 d6 留下的洞。白方在 d6 上有两名攻击者，黑方只有一名防守者，即主教，所以 5...a6？允许 6. Nd6+ Bxd6 7. Qxd6 ∓。黑棋得到了主教对，而他们的王后则完全取决于白棋的事。白方在 d6 中添加防守者的唯一方法是 5...d6（现在后王看到 d6），之后通常是 6.c4 或 6.Bf4。

5. Nxc6？！，交换骑士，是只有在业余水平才能真正看到的副业。与西西里四骑士中交换骑士让白方按节奏推 e5 不同，这里对白方没有真正的好处。 5...bxc6 之后，黑方可以在 c 兵的额外支持下轻松下 6...d5。 6.e5？遇到 6...Qa5+ 分叉典当。

5. c4 是一条 Maróczy 绑线或 Kramnik 风格的线，白方希望获得空间。 5...Nf6 6. Nc3 Bb4 均衡。

历史

Taimanov 西西里语是从旧的 Paulsen 西西里语变体（带有 e6、a6 和 Qc7 的西西里语）演变而来。奇怪的是，在他的书中，泰马诺夫本人并不认为 4...Nc6 是他的系统的定义移动，他将其描述为只是 Paulsen 的许多可能的移动顺序之一。相反，他认为 Taimanov 的决定性举动是推迟 Qc7 以支持 Nge7，并描述“黑方的基本开局计划……Tamanov 系统[是从 d4 前哨移除]活跃的白方棋子……通过交换中心的骑士 [Nxd4 Qxd4] 以及随后将‘骑士替补’转移到 c6 的‘节奏’。”

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c5/2. Nf3/2...e6/3. d4/3...cxd4/4. Nxd4/4...Nc6/5. Nc3/5...Qc7
explanations.text:
5...Qc7 · Bastrikov variation

Black chooses to develop their queen to a safe square where it has good scope.

6. Be3 is the most common move. White develops their bishop to an active square where the knight on d4 is defended from any potential ...Nxd4 exchanges that may happen in the future. White may be preparing to castle long, 6...a6 7. Qd2 Nf6 8. O-O-O, or is overdefending their knight so that they may play 7. Bd3 and castle short.

6. Be2 develops the king's bishop without obstructing the queen's defence of d4, and prepares to castle short, 6...a6 7. O-O.

6. Nxc6 does not wait to exchange knights. White decides that it is finally time to settle the trade offer by accepting.

6. Ndb5 is the most aggressive move. White immediately goes on the offensive and attacks the newly placed queen on c7 with their knight.

explanations.textZh:
5...Qc7·巴斯特里科夫变体

黑棋选择将他们的皇后发展到一个安全的方格，那里有良好的范围。

6. Be3是最常见的走法。白方将他们的主教发展到一个活跃的方格，在该方格中，d4 上的马可以免受未来可能发生的任何潜在的 ...Nxd4 交换的影响。白方可能正准备长城堡，6...a6 7. Qd2 Nf6 8. O-O-O，或者过度防守他们的马，以便他们可以玩 7. Bd3 和短城堡。

6. Be2在不阻碍后防d4的情况下发展出国王的主教，准备短兵相接，6...a6 7. O-O。

6. Nxc6不等待交换骑士。白棋决定最终是时候通过接受来解决交易要约了。

6. Ndb5是最激进的举动。白方立即发起进攻，用马攻击 c7 上新放置的后。

explanations.text:
Sicilian - Four Knights Variation

Black deploys their knight to f6, where it puts pressure on the pawn on e4. One of Black's main idea in this position is to play Bb4, where it would pin the white knight and threaten to take it on e4.
explanations.textEn:

explanations.textZh:
西西里-四骑士变奏

黑方将马部署到 f6，对 e4 上的棋子施加压力。黑棋在这个位置上的主要想法之一是下Bb4，它会压制白马并威胁在e4上拿下它。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c5/2. Nf3/2...e6/3. d4/3...cxd4/4. Nxd4/4...Nc6/5. Nb5
explanations.text:
5. Nb5 · Szén variation

With 5. Nb5 White moves to exploit Black's dark square weaknesses. When Black played 2...e6, they left a hole on the d6 square.

White has two attackers on d6 and Black only one defender, the bishop, so 5...a6? allows 6. Nd6+ Bxd6 7. Qxd6 ∓. White gets the bishop pair and their Queen is all up in Black's business.

5...d6 is the only way for Black to add a defender, allowing the black queen to see d6. White can then follow with 6. c4 or 6. Bf4. White will have to spend some tempo retreating their knight to somewhere safer, before or after it is kicked by a6. White chooses either knights on a3 and c3, or c3 and d2.

5...d5? technically adds a defender to d6, but after 6. exd5 exd5 7. Bf4 takes control of the square again. (7. Qxd5 also works: 7...Qxd5? Nc7+ recovers the queen.)

5...Nf6 is an alternative: Black postpones White playing Nd6 by threatening their e4 pawn. After 6. Nc3 to defend it, Black can then choose to play 7...d6 after all, or 7...Bb4, pinning the knight, instead, then 7. a3 Bxc3+ 8. Nxc3 d5.

5. Nb5·Szén变体

5. Nb5 白方利用黑方的暗方弱点采取行动。当黑方下 2...e6 时，他们在 d6 方格上留下了一个洞。

白方在 d6 上有两名攻击者，黑方只有一名防守者，即主教，所以 5...a6？允许 6. Nd6+ Bxd6 7. Qxd6 ∓。白棋得到了主教对，而他们的王后则全神贯注于黑棋的事务。

5...d6是黑方加守的唯一方法，让黑后看到d6。白棋随后可以下 6.c4 或 6.Bf4。在被a6踢之前或之后，白方必须花一些节奏将他们的马撤退到更安全的地方。白方选择 a3 和 c3 上的马，或者 c3 和 d2 上的马。

5...d5？技术上在d6上增加了一名防守者，但在6. exd5 exd5 7. Bf4之后再次控制了方阵。 （7. Qxd5 也有效：7...Qxd5？NC7+ 恢复皇后。）

5...Nf6 是另一种选择：黑方通过威胁其 e4 棋子来推迟白方下 Nd6。 6. Nc3 防守后，黑方可以选择下 7...d6，或者 7...Bb4，压制马，然后 7. a3 Bxc3+ 8. Nxc3 d5。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c5/2. Nf3/2...e6/3. d4/3...cxd4/4. Nxd4/4...Nc6/5. Nb5/5...d6
explanations.text:
5...d6

Black prevents White's knight coming in to d6.

White can then follow with 6. c4 or 6. Bf4.

6. Bf4 acts to provoke 6...e5, weakening the d5 square and leading the game into a Kalashnikov-style Sicilian, with Black's pawns on e5 and d6. After 6...e5 the bishop falls back to 7. Be3. Then Black typically looks to kick White's misplaced knight, 7...a6, or develop while attacking White's e4 pawn, 7...Nf6.

6. c4 is more common: White sets up the Maroczy bind structure to control d5. Black can play 6...a6 to kick White's knight, or 6...Nf6 followed by 7...a6: the idea being to first induce N1c3, then White's other knight has no choice but to retreat to the passive a3 square when kicked. White will have moved the same knight four times in the opening: in exchange they hope that their pawns on e4 and c4 will restrict Black's space and so make their development harder.

White will have moved the same knight four times in the opening: in exchange they hope that their pawns on e4 and c4 will restrict Black's space and so make their development harder.
explanations.textZh:
5...d6

黑方阻止白方的马进入 d6。

白棋随后可以下 6.c4 或 6.Bf4。

6. Bf4 挑衅 6...e5，削弱 d5 方格，将棋局引入卡拉什尼科夫式的西西里式，黑方棋子在 e5 和 d6 上。 6...e5 之后，主教回落到 7.Be3。然后黑方通常会踢白方错位的马 7...a6，或者在攻击白方的 e4 兵 7...Nf6 时发展。

6. c4更常见：白方设置Maroczy绑定结构来控制d5。黑方可以下6...a6来踢白方的马，或者6...Nf6然后7...a6：这个想法是首先诱导N1c3，然后白方的另一个马在被踢时别无选择，只能撤退到被动的a3方格。白方将在开局中四次移动同一个马：作为交换，他们希望他们在 e4 和 c4 上的棋子将限制黑方的空间，从而使他们的发展更加困难。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c5/2. Nf3/2...e6/3. d4/3...cxd4/4. Nxd4/4...Nc6/5. Nb5/5...d6/6. c4
explanations.text:
6. c4

White sets up the Maroczy bind structure to control d5. Between their c and e pawns, and having induced Black to play d6 and restrict their own dark square bishop, they hope to keep Black's position cramped, hampering their development, and that this will make up for the loss of tempo White incurred in moving their knight multiple times in the opening.

If 6...a6 straight away, Black kicks White's knight and they are forced to move it again: usually to c3.

Black usually plays 6...Nf6 first, threatening Nxe4 with the idea of inducing 7. N1c3, followed by 7...a6 to kick the knight to 8. Na3 where it is on the rim and therefore grim, but from where it overprotect the c4 pawn and doesn't obstruct the White queen's support of d5.
explanations.textEn:

Between their c and e pawns, and having induced Black to play d6 and restrict their own dark square bishop, they hope to keep Black's position cramped, hampering their development, and that this will make up for the loss of tempo White incurred in moving their knight multiple times in the opening.

explanations.textZh:
6.c4

白方设置 Maroczy 绑定结构来控制 d5。在他们的c和e兵之间，并诱导黑方下d6并限制自己的暗方主教，他们希望使黑方的位置狭窄，阻碍他们的发展，并且这将弥补白方在开局中多次移动他们的马所造成的节奏损失。

如果直接出现 6...a6，黑方将踢白方的马，他们被迫再次移动它：通常是到 c3。

黑方通常首先下6...Nf6，以诱导7.N1c3的想法威胁Nxe4，然后用7...a6将马踢到8.Na3，它位于边缘，因此很严峻，但从那里它过度保护了c4兵并且不妨碍白后对d5的支持。

explanations.text:
6...Nf6

6...Nf6 develops while threatening White's e4 pawn.

White can defend with 7. N1c3, developing their second knight and intending their other knight to retreat to a3, or 7. N5c3, leaving their knight on b1 undeveloped for now.
explanations.textEn:
6...Nf6

6...Nf6 develops while threatening White's e4 pawn.

White can defend with 7. N1c3, developing their second knight and intending their other knight to retreat to a3, or 7. N5c3, leaving their knight on b1 undeveloped for now.
explanations.textZh:
6...NF6

6...Nf6 发展，同时威胁白方的 e4 棋子。

白棋可以用 7.N1c3 防守，发展他们的第二个马，并打算让他们的另一个马撤退到 a3，或者 7.N5c3，让他们的马在 b1 上暂时未发展。

explanations.text:
7. N1c3

7. N1c3 defends White's e4 pawn while developing their knight.

Black usually continues 7...a6, compelling White to retreat to the passive a6 square. However, at least from there White will overprotect the c4 pawn and keep d5 in sight of their queen.

Black can delay a6 until after they have castled: 7...Be7 8. Be2 9. O-O O-O 10. a6.

7.N1c3

7. N1c3 防守白方的 e4 兵，同时发展他们的马。

黑棋通常会继续7...a6，迫使白棋撤退到被动的a6方格。然而，至少从那时起，白方会过度保护 c4 兵，并让 d5 处于其后的视线范围内。

黑方可以延迟 a6 直到他们已出局： 7...Be7 8. Be2 9. O-O O-O 10. a6。

explanations.text:
7...a6

7...a6 kicks White's knight.

Its available squares are d4 or a3.

The most common move is 8. Na3. This places a knight on the rim, but at least it overdefends c4 in case Black hopes to make use of the half-open file and play ...Rc8 one day.

8. Nd4 reduces White's control of d5, and allows Black to untangle with 8...d5 9. cxd5 exd5 10. exd5 Nxd5 11. Nxc6 bxc6 (see diagram). The position is equal but now open, and White is no longer able to keep Black suffocating in their side of the board as they had hoped.

7...a6

7...a6 踢白方的马。

它的可用方格是 d4 或 a3。

最常见的走法是8.Na3。这将骑士置于边缘，但至少它对 c4 进行了过度防守，以防黑方希望有一天利用半开的文件并玩 ...Rc8。

8. Nd4 减少了白方对 d5 的控制，并允许黑方用 8...d5 9. cxd5 exd5 10. exd5 Nxd5 11. Nxc6 bxc6 解开（见图）。局面是平等的，但现在是开放的，白方不再能够像他们希望的那样让黑方在棋盘的一侧窒息。

explanations.text:
8. Na3

White saves their knight with 8. Na3.

The position is looking cramped for Black. Those pawns on c4 and e4 prevent them from playing d5 and gaining more space. Meanwhile, Black's pawns on d6 and e6 prevent Black from developing their bishops very actively.

They have three typical continuations.

Black still has their bishops to develop, so option one is to develop their light-square bishop, in which case first Black must play 8...b6 to make room to fianchetto it.

Option two is to develop their dark-square bishop. Fianchettoing it is inconceivable of course because of how weak f6 will become. Since White induced them to play 5...d6, there is only one place left for it, so Black may as well play 8...Be7 and get it over with, then at least they can castle.

Option three is to discard both these options as too timid, throw caution at the wind, and kick open the Maroczy bind with 8...d5 anyway. This is an especially good continuation if it is 1985 and you are Garry Kasparov, after whom the audacious play, the Garry gambit, is named.

8.Na3

白方用 8.Na3 拯救了他们的马。

黑棋的位置看起来很狭窄。 c4 和 e4 上的棋子阻止他们玩 d5 并获得更多空间。同时，黑方在 d6 和 e6 上的棋子阻止了黑方非常积极地发展他们的象。

explanations.text:
8...d5!? · Garry gambit

Black challenges White in the centre to open up the position.

White has four attackers to Black's three defenders. However, after 9. cxd5 exd5 10. exd5, Black intends to play 10...Nb4, bringing another attacker.

History

The Garry gambit was first played by Garry Kasparov in two games of the 1985 World Championship match with Anatoly Karpov (see sample game).

After the discovery of the continuation 12. Be3 Bxe3 13. Qa4+! (see below) this fell out of favour for Black.

Sample game

Karpov v Kasparov, 1985

The sixteenth game of the World Championship match.

1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 e6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nc6 5. Nb5 d6 6. c4 Nf6 7. N1c3 a6 8. Na3 d5

Kasparov plays the "Garry gambit".

9. cxd5 exd5 10. exd5 Nb4

This position had already been reached in their twelfth game of the match. In that game, Karpov (playing White) continued 11. Bc4, a natural move to defend the pawn, and continued cautiously before having to settle for a draw: 11...Bg4 (compelling White's bishop to retreat) 12. Be2 Bxe2 13. Qxe2+ Qe7 14. Be3 Nbxd5 (Black recovers the pawn) 15. Nc2 Nxe3 16. Nxe3 Qe6 17. O-O Bc5 18. Rfe1 O-O ½-½.

11. Be2

This time White intends to control d5 with a Be2-Bf3 manoeuvre.

11...Bc5

Rather than take back the pawn, Black leaves it and focuses on development instead. They can quickly capitalise on good, active squares for their pieces, while White's knight on a3 is passive.

Kasparov analysed 11...Nbxd5 12. O-O Be7 13. Nxd5 Nxd5 14. Bf3 (attacking knight) Be6 (defending knight) 15. Nc2! as better for White. The c2 knight threatens to come to d4, where it can take bishop on e6 that is tied down to protect the knight. Black therefore avoids taking the pawn because of the difficulty in defending the knight on the d5 square.

12. O-O

When Karpov faced this line again in 1986, he played the improvement 12. Be3 Bxe3 13. Qa4+! forking the now-undefended knight on b4.

12...O-O 13. Bf3 Bf5

Black locks out the a3 knight from play. It now cannot go to c2, and Nc4 allows Bd3, forking the knight and the rook. (In fact, modern engines are happy with the transformation 14. Nc4 Bd3 15. Ne3 Bxf1 16. Kxf1 for White: willing to sacrifice the exchange to eliminate Black's active bishop and revive the prospects of White's knight).

14. Bg5 Re8 15. Qd2 b5 16. Rad1 Nd3

Black's knight takes over a superb outpost and dominates White's position. Black threatens b3, forking the knights.

17. Nab1 h6 18. Bh4 b4 19. Na4 Bd6

White's position is close to paralysis: Black's monstrous knight is preventing White from bringing their rooks into the game, White's knights have been pushed to the rim with nowhere to go, and now Black threatens to trap White's queen with Rc8 and Bf4.

20. Bg3

Forced, to prevent White's queen becoming trapped.

20...Rc8

Black had to discard two alternatives:

20...Ne4 21. Bxe4 Bxe4, winning the bishop pair and weakening White's d5 pawn. Seirawan's analysis picks out the danger of 22. Qe3 as a continuation, allowing White to untangle their position by playing Qb6 to trade queens (though the engine likes this for Black. One continuation is 22...Bf5 23. Qb6 Bxg3 24. Qxd8 Bxh2+ 25. Kxh2 Raxd8).

20...Bxg3 21. hxg3 Qa5 22. b3 Rad8 23. Na3 (the b3 pawn is pinned to Black's queen) Nxd5 and Black wins the d5 pawn, then 24. Nc4 Qb5 25. Bxd5 Rxd5 26. Ne3 Rdd8 27. Nxf5 Qxf5. Kasparov believed he had more chance to play for advantage by avoiding the trades and "tightening the screws on the position [asking] White how he intends to solve his problems."

Black takes the open c-file and control of even more of White's space.

21. b3

To allow Nb2: White hopes to trade off Black's monstrous knight.

21...g5 22. Bxd6 Qxd6 23. g3 Nd7 24. Bg2 Qf6

White can't get in Nb2 now. Their a4 knight is so out of play that they are practically down a piece; their b1 knight is no better.

25. a3 a5 26. axb4 axb4 27. Qa2

White is desperate to untangle their position and get some piece activity. Unable to shift Black's b pawn, White moves the queen to make room for Nd2 instead.

27...Bg6

Black can meet Nd2 with Re2!, pinning the knight to White's queen. However, if say 27...h5 28. Nd2 Re2, White has the defensive resource Bf2. By moving their bishop back, Black allows their queen to control f2 and 28. Nd2 Re2 29. Bf3 Rxd2 30. Qxd2 Qxf3 wins two pieces for a rook.

28. d6 g4 29. Qd2 Kg7 30. f3 Qxd6 31. fxg4 Qd4+ 32. Kh1 Nf6 33. Rf4 Ne4 34. Qxd3 Nf2+ 35. Rxf2 Bxd3 36. Rfd2 Qe3 37. Rxd3 Rc1 38. Nb2 Qf2 39. Nd2 Rxd1+ 40. Nxd1 Re1+

Black has mate in 2 (41. Nf1 Rxf1+ 42. Bxf1 Qxf1#). White resigns.

explanations.textZh:
8...d5！？ · 加里·甘比特

黑棋向中间的白棋发起挑战，以打开局面。

白方有四名攻击者，而黑方则有三名防守者。然而，在 9.cxd5 exd5 10.exd5 之后，黑方打算下 10...Nb4，带来另一名攻击手。

历史

加里策略首次由加里·卡斯帕罗夫（Garry Kasparov）在 1985 年世界锦标赛与阿纳托利·卡尔波夫（Anatoly Karpov）的两场比赛中使用（参见示例比赛）。

发现后继续12.Be3 Bxe3 13.Qa4+！ （见下文）这对黑方失去了青睐。

示例游戏

卡尔波夫 v 卡斯帕罗夫，1985 年

世锦赛第十六场比赛。

1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 e6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Nc6 5. Nb5 d6 6. c4 Nf6 7. N1c3 a6 8. Na3 d5

卡斯帕罗夫玩“加里策略”。

9. cxd5 exd5 10. exd5 Nb4

这个位置在他们的第十二场比赛中就已经达到了。在那场比赛中，卡尔波夫（白方）继续走 11. Bc4，这是保护棋子的自然棋，并在不得不解决平局之前继续谨慎行事： 11...Bg4（迫使白方象撤退） 12. Be2 Bxe2 13. Qxe2+ Qe7 14. Be3 Nbxd5（黑方收回棋子） 15. Nc2 Nxe3 16. Nxe3 Qe6 17.O-O Bc5 18.Rfe1 O-O 1/2-1/2。

11. 贝2

这次白方打算用 Be2-Bf3 策略来控制 d5。

11...Bc5

黑方没有收回棋子，而是留下棋子并专注于发展。他们可以快速利用良好的、活跃的方格作为自己的棋子，而白棋在a3上的骑士是被动的。

卡斯帕罗夫分析 11...Nbxd5 12. O-O Be7 13. Nxd5 Nxd5 14. Bf3（进攻骑士） Be6（防守骑士） 15. Nc2！对白棋来说更好。 c2骑士威胁要来到d4，在那里它可以带走e6上的主教，而e6上的主教被束缚以保护骑士。因此，黑方避免吃兵，因为在 d5 方格上很难防守马。

12.O-O

当卡尔波夫在1986年再次面对这条线时，他打出了改进12.Be3 Bxe3 13.Qa4+！在 b4 上分叉现在不设防的骑士。

12...O-O 13. Bf3 Bf5

黑方将 a3 马排除在外。现在它不能去c2，并且Nc4允许Bd3，将马和车分叉。 （事实上​​，现代引擎对白棋的转变很满意 14. Nc4 Bd3 15. Ne3 Bxf1 16. Kxf1：愿意牺牲交换来消除黑棋的活跃主教并恢复白棋马的前景）。

14. Bg5 Re8 15. Qd2 b5 16. Rad1 Nd3

黑棋的骑士占据了一个绝佳的前哨基地并控制了白棋的位置。黑棋威胁b3，分叉马队。

17. Nab1 h6 18. Bh4 b4 19. Na4 Bd6

白棋的位置接近瘫痪：黑棋的怪物骑士阻止白棋将车带入游戏，白棋的骑士已被推到篮筐无处可去，现在黑棋威胁用Rc8和Bf4困住白棋的后。

20. 背景3

被迫，以防止白后被困。

20...Rc8

黑棋不得不放弃两种选择：

20...Ne4 21. Bxe4 Bxe4，赢得主教对并削弱白方的 d5 兵。 Seirawan的分析指出了22.Qe3作为延续的危险，允许白方通过下Qb6来交易皇后来理清自己的位置（尽管引擎喜欢黑方这样。一个延续是22...Bf5 23.Qb6 Bxg3 24.Qxd8 Bxh2+ 25.Kxh2 Raxd8）。

20...Bxg3 21. hxg3 Qa5 22. b3 Rad8 23. Na3（b3 棋子固定在黑方后）Nxd5 且黑方赢得 d5 棋子，然后 24. Nc4 Qb5 25. Bxd5 Rxd5 26. Ne3 Rdd8 27. Nxf5 Qxf5。卡斯帕罗夫相信，通过避免交易和“拧紧局面（询问）怀特他打算如何解决他的问题”，他有更多机会获得优势。

黑棋占据了开放的c线并控制了白棋更多的空间。

21.b3

为了允许Nb2：白方希望交易黑方的怪物骑士。

21...g5 22.Bxd6 Qxd6 23.g3 Nd7 24.Bg2 Qf6

现在白棋无法进入Nb2。他们的a4骑士太不发挥作用了，他们几乎落后了一步；他们的b1骑士也好不了多少。

25.a3 a5 26.axb4 axb4 27.Qa2

白方迫切希望理清他们的局面并获得一些棋子活动。由于无法移动黑方的 b 棋子，白方移动了皇后，为 Nd2 腾出空间。

27...Bg6

黑棋可以用 Re2! 与 Nd2 相遇，将马钉在白棋的后上。然而，如果说27...h5 28.Nd2 Re2，白方拥有防御资源Bf2。通过将象向后移动，黑方允许其后控制 f2 和 28. Nd2 Re2 29. Bf3 Rxd2 30. Qxd2 Qxf3 为车赢得两子。

28.d6 g4 29.Qd2 Kg7 30.f3 Qxd6 31.fxg4 Qd4+ 32.Kh1 Nf6 33.Rf4 Ne4 34.Qxd3 Nf2+ 35.Rxf2 Bxd3 36.Rfd2 Qe3 37.Rxd3 Rc1 38.Nb2 Qf2 39. Nd2 Rxd1+ 40. Nxd1 Re1+

黑棋有 2 局（41. Nf1 Rxf1+ 42. Bxf1 Qxf1#）。白辞职了

explanations.text:
Sicilian Defense: Kveinis Variation

The razor-sharp Kveinis Variation has often been considered inferior to other variations of the Sicilian French Variation, yet statistics show it scores better than any other at club level! It scores respectably well at grandmaster level, too.

By playing 4...Qb6, Black puts pressure on White's d4 knight and b2 pawn. With the dark-squared bishop ready to add more pressure from c5, Black also x-rays f2. White must be extremely careful not to make any false moves. The opening is especially efficacious in blitz and bullet games where White might not have time to spot the danger. For example: 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 e6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Qb6 5. Nc3 Bc5 6. Nce2 e5 7. Nb3 Bxf2+ 8. Kd2 Qe3#

Black must also be extremely careful about capturing White's poisoned pawn' on b2. It's a tactical mastermind between the two sides that can frequently give rise to tense, exciting middlegames.

explanations.textZh:
西西里防御：克维尼斯变例

锋利的克韦尼斯变奏经常被认为不如西西里法国变奏的其他变奏，但统计数据显示它的得分比俱乐部级别的任何其他变奏都要好！它在大师级别的得分也相当不错。

通过下 4...Qb6，黑方对白方的 d4 马和 b2 兵施加压力。随着暗方主教准备好从c5增加更多压力，黑方也X射线f2。白方必须极其小心，不要做出任何错误的举动。在白棋可能没有时间发现危险的闪电战和子弹棋中，这种开局尤其有效。例如： 1. e4 c5 2. Nf3 e6 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4 Qb6 5. Nc3 Bc5 6. Nce2 e5 7. Nb3 Bxf2+ 8. Kd2 Qe3#

黑方在b2 上吃掉白方的“有毒棋子”时也必须非常小心。这是双方之间的战术策划者，经常能引发紧张、刺激的中局。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c5/2. Nf3/2...e6/3. d4/3...cxd4/4. Nxd4/4...Nf6
explanations.text:
Sicilian 2...e6

This is the flexible move. The Knight comes out to f6 and threatens the e4 pawn. It's important that Black determines how White deals with the e4 pawn before moving pawns further if White plays Nc3 then he can no longer play c4 first. 5.e5? is a common mistake as ...Qa5+ picks up material.

西西里岛 2...e6

这就是灵活的动作。马出来到 f6 并威胁 e4 兵。重要的是，黑方在进一步移动棋子之前要确定白方如何处理 e4 棋子，如果白棋下 Nc3，那么他就不能再先下 c4。 5.e5？这是一个常见的错误，因为...Qa5+ 选取材料。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c5/2. Nf3/2...g6
explanations.text:
2...g6 · Hyperaccelerated Dragon

Black prepares to fianchetto their king's bishop, ...Bg7. This is the start of the Hyperaccelerated Dragon.

In the Accelerated Dragon, Black usually plays 2...Nc6 before preparing to fianchetto their bishop. This allows White the option of 3. Bb5, the Rossolimo attack. With the move order 2...g6, Black hopes to sidestep that line.

The main continuation is the usual Open Sicilian plan: 3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4, and 4...Nc6 transposes to the Accelerated Dragon, Rossolimo successfully avoided. White can continue with 5. Nc3, the conventional Open Sicilian move, or 5. c4, the tricky Maróczy bind, which clamps down on the d5 square with both e- and c-pawns.

However, the 2...g6 move order gives White some other options that steer the game away from transposing into an Accelerated dragon, which Black must be prepared for:

3. d4 cxd4 4. Qxd4!?, attacking Black's rook. The main continuation is 4...Nf6 5. e5 Nc6 6. Qa4 Nd5 7. Qe4.

3. c3, a sort of deferred Alapin, is also strong.

3. c4 transposes to the Maróczy bind line after 3...Nc6 4. d4 cxd4 5. Nxd4 Bg7.

explanations.textZh:
2...g6 · 超加速龙

黑方准备向他们国王的主教发起攻击，...Bg7。这是超加速龙的开始。

在加速龙中，黑方通常在准备向主教发起攻击之前先下 2...Nc6。这使得白方可以选择 3. Bb5，即罗索里莫进攻。通过走棋顺序 2...g6，黑方希望避开这条线。

主要延续的是通常的西西里公开赛计划：3. d4 cxd4 4. Nxd4，以及4...Nc6转置到加速龙，罗索里莫成功避开。白方可以继续使用 5.Nc3，传统的西西里公开棋，或者 5.c4，棘手的 Maróczy 绑定，它用 e 和 c 棋子压制 d5 方格。

然而，2...g6 的移动顺序为白方提供了一些其他选择，使游戏远离转变为加速龙，而黑方必须为此做好准备：

3. d4 cxd4 4. Qxd4!?，攻击黑方车。主要延续是 4...Nf6 5. e5 Nc6 6. Qa4 Nd5 7. Qe4。

3. c3，一种延迟的Alapin，也很强大。

3. c4 在 3...Nc6 后转置至 Maróczy 结合线 4. d4 cxd4 5. Nxd4 Bg7。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c5/2. Nf3/2...g6/3. c4
explanations.text:
Sicilian - Hyper-Accelerated Dragon, Maróczy Bind

The Maróczy Bind Variation of the Hyper-Accelerated Dragon is a variation where white advances the c4 before playing Nc3, this also helps controlling the d5 square, after black fianchettos the bishop on g7, white will play Nc3 and d4, build a big and stable center, Similar to the Staunton-Cochrane Sicilian where white play e4, c4, and aims for d4.

Possible moves for black

After the move c4, black can decide on many moves but the most popular ones include:

3... Bg7

Possibly the most common one, the whole idea of the move g6 is to play fianchetto the bishop in the g7 square, after that move, white has mainly two great options, d4, immediately striking at the center, or, a slower move, which is Nc3, white can alternatively play the move d3, guarding both pawns, but the pawn on d3 will be an weakness for white as well as giving play time to develop both knights and then play d6, which wont be a weakness since they didn't commit the e-pawn forward.

3... Nc6

This is a possible transportion to the accelerated dragon, since after 4. d4 cxd4 5. Nxd4 and Bg7, the position is the same as if had committed the c-pawn after the move Nc6 instead of Bg7,white can choose not to transpose with the move Nc3, but the position will not be as great, according to modern-day engines like Stockfish.

explanations.textZh:
西西里 - 超加速龙，Maróczy Bind

超加速龙的Maróczy Bind变体是白棋在下Nc3之前先推进c4的变体，这也有助于控制d5方块，在黑棋上g7上的主教后，白棋将下Nc3和d4，建立一个大而稳定的中心，类似于Staunton-Cochrane西西里白棋中的e4，c4，并瞄准d4。

黑方可能采取的行动

在 c4 棋步之后，黑棋可以决定许多棋步，但最受欢迎的棋步包括：

3... 背景7

可能是最常见的，g6棋的整体思路是在g7方格中对主教下棋，此棋之后，白棋主要有两个不错的选择，d4，立即攻击中心，或者是较慢的棋，即Nc3，白棋也可以下棋d3，保护两个棋子，但d3上的棋子将成为白棋的弱点，并给予发挥时间来发展两个马，然后棋d6，这不会成为弱点，因为他们没有将电子典当向前推进。

3...NC6

这是向加速龙的可能转移，因为在 4.d4 cxd4 5.Nxd4 和 Bg7 之后，位置与在 Nc6 而不是 Bg7 后投入 c 兵相同，白方可以选择不与 Nc3 移动进行换位，但根据像 Stockfish 这样的现代引擎，位置不会那么好。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c5/2. Nf3/2...g6/3. d4
explanations.text:
3. d4

White plays 3. d4, the classic Open Sicilian move, to open up the centre while opening lines for their bishop and queen to develop. White is playing to maximise their activity.

This gives White pawns on both d4 and e4 controlling great tracts in the middle of the board, so the main move is 3...cxd4 to break up White's powerful two-pawn centre, and after White recaptures, Black will have a central pawn majority and use of the half-open c-file. White can then retake the pawn with either 4. Nxd4, the conventional Open Sicilian move, or 4. Qxd4, which is an effective sideline against the Hyperaccelerated Dragon.

3...Bg7!? is a sideline for Black, which transposes into the Pterodactyl defence (usually reached by an early ...c5 in the Modern defence). 4. dxc5 Qa4+ lets Black recover the pawn.

3.d4

白棋下3.d4，这是经典的西西里公开棋，打开中心，同时为他们的主教和后发展打开路线。白棋正在最大化他们的活动。

这使得白方在 d4 和 e4 上的棋子控制了棋盘中间的大片区域，因此主要的动作是 3...cxd4 来打破白方强大的两棋中心，并且在白方夺回后，黑方将拥有中央棋子多数并使用半开的 c 线。然后，白方可以使用 4.Nxd4（传统的西西里公开棋）或 4.Qxd4（对抗超加速龙的有效边线）夺回棋子。

3...Bg7！？是黑方的一条边线，转入翼手龙防御（通常由现代防御中的早期 ...c5 达到）。 4. dxc5 Qa4+ 让黑方收回棋子。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c5/2. Nf3/2...g6/3. d4/3...cxd4
explanations.text:
3...cxd4

Black takes the d-pawn. This was the idea behind 1...c5: White can retake and Black has a central pawn majority (both d- and e-pawns). In exchange, White gets open lines for development.

There are two ways to retake the pawn.

4. Nxd4 is natural. 4...Nc6 transposes into the accelerated dragon Sicilian and Black has successfully avoided facing the Rossolimo variation through the hyperaccelerated move order.

From there, the main continuations Black faces are 5. c4 or 5. Nc3. 4...Bg7 5. c4 Nc3 transposes. 4...Nf6 first, attacking e4, encourages 5. Nc3 so as to avoid facing 5. c4, though White can always play 5. f3 to keep the option of c4. 4...Nf6 5. e5? loses the pawn to 5...Qa5+.

4. Qxd5 is an alternative that avoids a straight transposition into the accelerated dragon. This attacks h8, since Black has moved their g-pawn (4...Nc3?? 5. Qxh8! or 4...Bg7 5. Qxg7!).

4...Nf6 and White has the tricky line 5. e5!? Nc6 6. Qa4 Nd5 7. Qe4 Ndb4?! 8. Bb5 Qa5?! 9. Nc3 (diagram), where e.g. 9...d5 10. exd6 Bf5 11. Qe5 f6 12. Bxc6+ Nxc6 13. Qxa5 Nxa5 14. dxe7 Bxe7 15. Nd4 Bb4.

3...cxd4

黑方拿走 D 兵。这就是 1...c5 背后的想法：白棋可以夺回，黑棋拥有多数中央棋子（d-棋子和 e-棋子）。作为交换，怀特获得了开放的发展路线。

夺回棋子有两种方法。

4. Nxd4是天然的。 4...Nc6 转换为加速龙西西里，黑方通过超加速移动顺序成功避免了面对罗索里莫变体。

4...Nf6 和白棋有棘手的路线 5. e5!? NC6 6.Qa4 Nd5 7.Qe4 Ndb4？！ 8. Bb5 Qa5？！ 9. Nc3（图表），例如9...d5 10.exd6 Bf5 11.Qe5 f6 12.Bxc6+ Nxc6 13.Qxa5 Nxa5 14.dxe7 Bxe7 15.Nd4 Bb4。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c5/2. Nf3/2...g6/3. d4/3...cxd4/4. Nxd4
explanations.text:
4. Nxd4

White recaptures according to the standard open Sicilian plan.

Black can now transpose into the accelerated dragon with 4...Nc6. This is the main idea behind this move order: to reach the accelerated dragon while avoiding facing the Rossolimo sideline. White may play with 5. Nc3 or 5. c4, the Maróczy bind.

4...Nf6 attacks the e4 pawn so encourages 5. Nc3, though White may play 5. f3 to keep the option of c4. 5. e5? loses the pawn to 5...Qa5+. After 5. Nc3, ...Qa5 does not come with check, so White is then threatening e5 (5...Nc6? 6. Nxc6 bxc6 7. e5). Therefore Black usually answers 5. Nc3 with 5...d6, accepting they will not be playing ...d5 in one tempo and transposing into the regular dragon Sicilian.

4...Bg7 typically transposes to the accelerated dragon by a slightly different move order. 5. c4 Nf6 6. Nc3 O-O 7. Be3 Nc6.

4.Nxd4

怀特按照标准的开放式西西里岛计划夺回了自己的领土。

黑方现在可以用 4...Nc6 转入加速龙。这就是这个移动顺序背后的主要思想：到达加速龙的同时避免面对罗索里莫边线。白方可以使用 5. Nc3 或 5. c4（Maróczy 绑定）。

4...Nf6 攻击 e4 兵，因此鼓励 5.Nc3，尽管白方可能会下 5.f3 以保留 c4 的选择。 5.e5？将棋子输给 5...Qa5+。 5. Nc3 之后，...Qa5 没有过牌，因此白棋随后威胁 e5（5...Nc6？ 6. Nxc6 bxc6 7. e5）。因此，黑方通常会用 5...d6 回答 5.Nc3，接受他们不会以一种节奏下 ...d5 并转换成常规的西西里龙。

4...Bg7 通常通过稍微不同的移动顺序转换为加速龙。 5. c4 Nf6 6. Nc3 O-O 7. Be3 Nc6。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6
explanations.text:
1...c6 · Caro-Kann defence

1...c6 is the Caro-Kann. Black prepares to play 2...d5, with the c pawn ready to take back should White take it.

In the traditional Open Game (1. e4 e5), many of the major threats that Black faces target their weak f7-square with White's bishop positioned on c4. Black often can consider this threat resolved if they succeed in pushing their queen's pawn to d5, controlling c4. So, by achieving d5, Black makes their kingside safer.

Compared to the French defence, which prepares 2...d5 with 1...e6 instead, this avoids blocking in Black's own bishop, but at the cost of preventing Black from playing Nc6. Additionally, if Black later wishes to assault White's centre with c5, they will have lost a tempo on this move.

2. d4 is the main line. By not making a threat or controlling d4, Black allowed White to put two pawns in the centre. Black responds with 2...d5 and then the game can go in several directions depending on how White proceeds. Options include trading pawns, advancing the e-pawn to e5, or defending the e4 pawn with a piece or pawn.

A sideline is the Two Knights attack, where White plays 2. Nc3, defending e4, followed by 3. Nf3, or 2. Nf3 followed by 3. Nc3. It is played about once for every ten games in the mainline. Usually, White will wait a little bit before placing the d pawn on d4 and sometimes just places it on the d3 square.

2. c4, the Accelerated Panov attack, is an aggressive sideline. Recognising that Black is determined to play d5, White wishes to make it impossible for them to hold onto it. This usually results in White and Black exchanging two pawns: 2...d5 3. cxd5 cxd5 4. exd5 Nf6 5. Nc3 Nxd5. In this line, White hopes to weaken Black's c- and d-files. White ends up with an isolated queen's pawn which may be a liability in the long run.

Other moves

Some other rare moves:

2. d3 is the Breyer variation. This move is fine but unambitious. After 2...d5, White's plan is to allow Black to take on e4. White plays 3. Nd2 to prevent trading the queens after 3...dxe4 4. dxe4.

2. b3 is the Euwe attack, preparing to fianchetto. White intends to give up their centre to Black and plays in a hypermodern style instead. Why-for start with 1. e4 then, and not 1. b3? Unclear, but with this idea Max Euwe triumphed over Richard Reti in 1920.

2. Bc4?! is called the Hillbilly attack. White, seeing Black is indubitably planning 2...d5, kindly makes 2...d5 even more appealing by letting Black kick their bishop while they're at it. This is certainly bad but (at the amateur level at least) not as rare as you might assume.

History

The earliest recorded games beginning 1. e4 c6 are from 1845 and 1847. The first game that continued 2. d4 d5 was published in 1859.

By the 1880s it was attributed to Horatio Caro, who played it and introduced it into master games, and Marcus Kann, who analysed it. A 1888 issue of Chess Monthly annotated it as, "introduced by the late Herr Kann, of Pest, and adopted in practice by Herr Caro, of Berlin. It gives a safe but dull game."

Its reputation is largely the same today: a solid, defensive reply to e4, albeit one not as dynamic or combative as other approaches. It's popular with players trying to avoid learning reams of Sicilian theory. Today it is Black's fourth- or fifth-most common defence against 1. e4, much less common than 1...c5, 1...e5, or 1...e6, so makes a good surprise weapon.

2. Bc4?! is called the Hillbilly attack. White, seeing Black is indubitably planning 2...d5, kindly makes 2...d5 even more appealing by letting Black kick their bishop while they're at it. This is certainly bad but (at the amateur level at least) not as rare as you might assume.

History

The earliest recorded games beginning 1. e4 c6 are from 1845 and 1847. The first game that continued 2. d4 d5 was published in 1859.

By the 1880s it was attributed to Horatio Caro, who played it and introduced it into master games, and Marcus Kann, who analysed it. A 1888 issue of Chess Monthly annotated it as, "introduced by the late Herr Kann, of Pest, and adopted in practice by Herr Caro, of Berlin. It gives a safe but dull game."

Its reputation is largely the same today: a solid, defensive reply to e4, albeit one not as dynamic or combative as other approaches. It's popular with players trying to avoid learning reams of Sicilian theory. Today it is Black's fourth- or fifth-most common defence against 1. e4, much less common than 1...c5, 1...e5, or 1...e6, so makes a good surprise weapon.
explanations.textZh:
1...c6 · 卡罗-卡恩防守

1...c6 是卡罗-卡恩。黑方准备下 2...d5，c 兵准备好在白方拿走时收回。

在传统的开放游戏（1. e4 e5）中，黑方面临的许多主要威胁都针对其较弱的 f7 方格，而白方的象位于 c4 上。如果黑方成功地将其后的棋子推至 d5，控制 c4，则通常可以认为这种威胁已经解决。因此，通过实现 d5，黑方使他们的王翼更加安全。

与法式防守用 1...e6 准备 2...d5 相比，这避免了黑方自己的象的阻挡，但代价是阻止黑方下 Nc6。此外，如果黑方随后希望用c5攻击白方的中心，他们将在这一步棋中失去节奏。

2、d4为主线。通过不构成威胁或控制 d4，黑方允许白方将两个棋子放在中间。黑方回应 2...d5，然后根据白方的进展，棋局可以朝多个方向发展。选项包括交易棋子、将 e-棋子推进到 e5，或者用棋子或棋子保卫 e4 棋子。

边线是两骑士进攻，白方下2. Nc3，防守e4，然后是3. Nf3，或2. Nf3，然后是3. Nc3。主线中大约每十场比赛就会进行一次。通常，白棋会稍等一下，然后将 d 棋子放在 d4 上，有时只是将其放在 d3 方格上。

2. c4，加速帕诺夫攻击，是一种侵略性的边线。认识到黑棋决心下d5，白棋希望让他们无法坚持下去。这通常会导致白方和黑方交换两个棋子：2...d5 3. cxd5 cxd5 4. exd5 Nf6 5. Nc3 Nxd5。在这一点上，白棋希望削弱黑棋的c档和d档。白方最终得到了一个孤立的后棋棋子，从长远来看这可能是一种负担。

其他动作

其他一些罕见的动作：

2. d3 是布雷耶变体。此举很好，但缺乏野心。 2...d5 之后，白方的计划是让黑方对阵 e4。白方下 3. Nd2 以防止在 3...dxe4 4. dxe4 之后交易皇后。

2. b3是Euwe进攻，准备fianchetto。白棋打算将其中心让给黑棋，并以超现代的风格进行比赛。为什么从 1.e4 开始，而不是 1.b3？不清楚，但凭借这一想法，马克斯·尤威 (Max Euwe) 在 1920 年战胜了理查德·雷蒂 (Richard Reti)。

2.BC4？！被称为乡巴佬攻击。白棋看到黑棋毫无疑问正在计划 2...d5，善意地让黑棋在进行时踢掉他们的主教，从而使 2...d5 更具吸引力。这当然很糟糕，但（至少在业余水平上）并不像您想象的那么罕见。

历史

最早记录的从 1. e4 c6 开始的游戏是 1845 年和 1847 年。第一个以 2. d4 d5 开头的游戏于 1859 年发布。

到了 1880 年代，它被归功于霍雷肖·卡罗 (Horatio Caro) 和马库斯·卡恩 (Marcus Kann)，前者玩过它并将其引入到大师游戏中，后者分析过它。 1888 年的《国际象棋月刊》将其注释为“由已故佩斯的卡恩先生引入，并由柏林的卡罗先生在实践中采用。它提供了一种安全但乏味的游戏。”

今天，它的声誉基本上没有变化：对 e4 的可靠、防御性回应，尽管不像其他方法那样充满活力或好斗。它很受那些试图避免学习大量西西里理论的玩家的欢迎。今天，它是黑方针对 1. e4 的第四或第五常见防御，比 1...c5、1...e5 或 1...e6 少见得多，因此是一种很好的出其不意的武器。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. Nc3
explanations.text:
2. Nc3

This is a flexible alternative move order in the Caro-Kann, where White has not committed the pawn to d4 yet.

After 2...d5 (near enough the only move, contesting the centre as Black prepared to do on move one), White may still play 3. d4 and transpose into the more common 2. d4 & 3. Nc3 Caro-Kann. However, the plan usually is to play 3. Nf3, the two knights attack. 3. Qf3 is the unusual Goldman variation.

explanations.textZh:
2.NC3

这是 Caro-Kann 中灵活的替代走法，其中白方尚未将棋子交到 d4。

在 2...d5 后（几乎是唯一的一步，黑方准备在第一步中争夺中心），白方仍可下 3.d4 并转入更常见的 2.d4 和 3.Nc3 卡罗-卡恩。不过，通常的计划是打3.Nf3，两个骑士进攻。 3. Qf3 是高盛不寻常的变体。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. Nc3/2...d5/3. Nf3/3...Bg4
explanations.text:
3...Bg4 · Caro-Kann Defence: Two Knights Attack

3...Bg4 frees Black's problematic dark-squared bishop. White's most common response, 4. h3, leads either to sharp lines with a lot of theory, or to Black giving White the bishop pair.
explanations.textEn:
3...Bg4 · Caro-Kann Defence: Two Knights Attack

3...Bg4 frees Black's problematic dark-squared bishop. White's most common response, 4. h3, leads either to sharp lines with a lot of theory, or to Black giving White the bishop pair.
explanations.textZh:
3...Bg4 · 卡罗-卡恩防御：两名骑士进攻

3...Bg4 释放了黑方有问题的暗方象。白方最常见的反应是 4. h3，要么导致带有大量理论的尖锐线条，要么导致黑方给白方象对。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. Nc3/2...d5/3. Nf3/3...Nf6
explanations.text:
3...Nf6 · Caro-Kann Defence: Two Knights Attack

3...Nf6 adds pressure to the d pawn, and has the advantage for Black of being played far less often than the main line 3...Bg4, or 3...dxe4. White only has one good response, 4. e5.

Attempting to defend the pawn with 4. d3? is inaccurate, as after Black captures and the resulting exchanges, White either loses a pawn, or loses the right to castle.

Exchanging with 4. exd5 is playable, but is effectively an inferior version of the Exchange Variation for White.

Attempting to defend the pawn with 4. d3? is inaccurate, as after Black captures and the resulting exchanges, White either loses a pawn, or loses the right to castle.

explanations.textZh:
3...Nf6 · 卡罗-卡恩防御：两名骑士进攻

3...Nf6 给 d 兵增加了压力，并且黑方的优势是比主线 3...Bg4 或 3...dxe4 少得多。白棋只有一种好的反应，4. e5。

尝试用 4.d3 保卫棋子？是不准确的，因为在黑方吃子和由此产生的交换之后，白方要么失去棋子，要么失去城堡的权利。

与 4.exd5 进行交换是可以玩的，但实际上是白方交换变体的劣质版本。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. Nc3/2...d5/3. Nf3/3...Nf6/4. e5/4...Ne4
explanations.text:
4...Ne4 · Caro-Kann Defence: Two Knights Attack

The advanced knight appears threatening, but Black doesn't need to worry about the positions after White captures it with 5. Nxe4, although this move is quite common at amateur level. After the capture and exchange, the white knight on g5 is misplaced, and Black is comfortable. 5. Ne2 and 5. d4 are the main lines.
explanations.textEn:
4...Ne4 · Caro-Kann Defence: Two Knights Attack

The advanced knight appears threatening, but Black doesn't need to worry about the positions after White captures it with 5. Nxe4, although this move is quite common at amateur level. After the capture and exchange, the white knight on g5 is misplaced, and Black is comfortable. 5. Ne2 and 5. d4 are the main lines.
explanations.textZh:
4...Ne4 · 卡罗-卡恩防御：两名骑士进攻

高级马看起来很有威胁，但黑棋不需要担心白棋用 5.Nxe4 吃掉它后的位置，尽管这种走法在业余水平上很常见。吃掉交换后，g5白棋走位错位，黑棋舒服。 5. Ne2和5. d4是主线。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. b3
explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Defence, Euwe Attack

White's response to the Caro-Kann is a fianchetto of the dark-squared bishop. This move is rarely played today, but was used with success by World Champion Max Euwe, who won against Richard Reti in 1920.

Black will almost always continue with the usual 2...d5.
explanations.textEn:
Caro-Kann Defence, Euwe Attack

White's response to the Caro-Kann is a fianchetto of the dark-squared bishop. This move is rarely played today, but was used with success by World Champion Max Euwe, who won against Richard Reti in 1920.

Black will almost always continue with the usual 2...d5.
explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩防守，尤威进攻

白方对卡罗-卡恩的回应是暗方主教的 fianchetto。这一招如今很少有人使用，但世界冠军马克斯·尤威 (Max Euwe) 曾成功运用过这一招，他在 1920 年战胜了理查德·雷蒂 (Richard Reti)。

黑方几乎总是会继续通常的 2...d5。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. c4
explanations.text:
2. c4 · Accelerated Panov attack

With pawns on c4 and e4, White locks down d5 square. This is a rare, aggressive sideline against the Caro-Kann. It is "accelerated" over the regular Panov where White plays c4 only after 2. d4 d5 3. exd5 cxd5. This can lead to very different positions. A difference is that, in the accelerated Panov, White leaves their pawn on d2 until after they have castled, so they may place their knight on c3 without it becoming pinned.

2...d5, the main line, leads to a series of pawn trades: 3. cxd5 cxd5 4. exd5 Nf6 (4...Qxd5?! 5. Nc3! gains tempo on the queen). White is temporarily up a pawn but usually allows Black to take it back with 5. Nc3 Nxd5. In the resulting position, White is left with an isolated d-pawn. This is a weakness in an endgame, so it's important for White to capitalise on their middlegame chances, using the open lines created by the removal of their c- and e-pawns.

White can make a play to keep the extra material with the intermezzo 5. Bb5+, to force the knight or bishop to d7 and so obstruct Black's queen's defence of the pawn. However, this line usually results in a queen trade (5...Nbd7 6. Nc3 a6 7. Qa4 Rb8 8. Bxd7+ Qxd7 9. Qxd7+ Bxd7) and in an endgame with doubled isolated d-pawns White may not feel the advantage of the extra material.

2...e5 is a sideline called the open variation. It's a bit like playing an open game (1. e4 e5), except now after 3. Nf3 Black can't defend the pawn with ...Nc6 because their pawn is misplaced on c6.

explanations.textZh:
2. c4·加速帕诺夫攻击

白棋在 c4 和 e4 上有棋子，锁定 d5 方格。这是针对卡罗-卡恩的罕见的、侵略性的边路。它比常规帕诺夫棋“加速”，其中白方仅在 2. d4 d5 3. exd5 cxd5 之后才下 c4。这可能会导致截然不同的立场。不同之处在于，在加速的帕诺夫中，白方将棋子留在 d2 上，直到他们出城后，因此他们可以将马放在 c3 上，而不会被钉住。

2...d5，主线，导致一系列典当交易： 3. cxd5 cxd5 4. exd5 Nf6（4...Qxd5？！ 5. Nc3！在皇后上获得节奏）。白方暂时占据棋子，但通常允许黑方用 5. Nc3 Nxd5 将其收回。在最终的局面中，白方只剩下一个孤立的 d 兵。这是残局中的弱点，因此对于白方来说，利用他们的中局机会很重要，利用通过移除他们的 c 和 e 棋子而创造的开放线。

白方可以通过间奏5.Bb5+来保留额外的材料，迫使马或主教下d7，从而阻碍黑方后对兵的防守。然而，这条线通常会导致皇后交易（5...Nbd7 6. Nc3 a6 7. Qa4 Rb8 8. Bxd7+ Qxd7 9. Qxd7+ Bxd7），并且在残局中双孤立的d兵白棋可能不会感受到额外材料的优势。

2...e5 是一种称为开放变体的边线。这有点像玩开放游戏（1. e4 e5），除了现在在 3. Nf3 之后，黑方无法用 ...Nc6 防守棋子，因为他们的棋子错位在 c6 上。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. c4/2...d5/3. exd5/3...cxd5/4. cxd5
explanations.text:
4. cxd5

Black is down a pawn.

4...Qxd5!?, retaking immediately, has been played but concedes the initiative back to White. 5. Nc3 develops with tempo and the line continues 5...Qd8 6. d4 e6 7. Nf3 Nf6 8. Bd3 Be7 9. O-O O-O.

4...Nf6 is the main move. This prepares to recapture the d-pawn with the knight. White either concedes the pawn back straight away, 5. Nc3 Nxd5, or attempts to hold onto it with the intermezzo 5. Bb5+!?, intending 5...Bd7 6. Bc4. This brings a defender to the pawn while also cutting the number of attackers (Black's bishop on d7 prevents their queen from seeing d5). Better for Black is 5...Nbd7, which can answer 6. Bc4 with 6...Nb6!.

The line after 5...Nbd7 continues 6. Nc3 (defending the pawn) a6 7. Qa4 (x-rays the rook) Rb8 8. Bxd7+ Qxd7 9. Qxd7+ Bxd7: because the pawn is isolated and White cannot defend it with another pawn, Black can eventually pick it back up, e.g. ...Bf5 and ...Re1.
explanations.textEn:
4. cxd5

Black is down a pawn.

4...Qxd5!?, retaking immediately, has been played but concedes the initiative back to White. 5. Nc3 develops with tempo and the line continues 5...Qd8 6. d4 e6 7. Nf3 Nf6 8. Bd3 Be7 9. O-O O-O.

4...Nf6 is the main move. This prepares to recapture the d-pawn with the knight. White either concedes the pawn back straight away, 5. Nc3 Nxd5, or attempts to hold onto it with the intermezzo 5. Bb5+!?, intending 5...Bd7 6. Bc4. This brings a defender to the pawn while also cutting the number of attackers (Black's bishop on d7 prevents their queen from seeing d5). Better for Black is 5...Nbd7, which can answer 6. Bc4 with 6...Nb6!.

The line after 5...Nbd7 continues 6. Nc3 (defending the pawn) a6 7. Qa4 (x-rays the rook) Rb8 8. Bxd7+ Qxd7 9. Qxd7+ Bxd7: because the pawn is isolated and White cannot defend it with another pawn, Black can eventually pick it back up, e.g. ...Bf5 and ...Re1.
explanations.textZh:
4.cxd5

黑棋落下棋子。

4...Qxd5!?，立即重夺，已下，但将主动权交还给白棋。 5. Nc3 随着节奏发展，线路继续 5...Qd8 6. d4 e6 7. Nf3 Nf6 8. Bd3 Be7 9. O-O O-O。

4...Nf6是主招。这准备用马夺回d-pawn。白方要么立即让兵退后，5. Nc3 Nxd5，要么尝试用间奏曲 5. Bb5+!? 保住棋子，意图 5...Bd7 6. Bc4。这将防御者带到棋子上，同时也减少了攻击者的数量（黑方在 d7 上的主教阻止他们的后看到 d5）。黑棋更好的是 5...Nbd7，它可以用 6...Nb6! 回答 6. Bc4。

5...Nbd7 之后的线继续 6. Nc3（保卫棋子）a6 7. Qa4（对车进行 X 射线检查）Rb8 8. Bxd7+ Qxd7 9. Qxd7+ Bxd7：因为棋子是孤立的，并且白方无法用另一个棋子来防御它，所以黑方最终可以将其捡起，例如...Bf5 和 ...Re1。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. c4/2...d5/3. exd5/3...cxd5/4. cxd5/4...Nf6
explanations.text:
4...Nf6 · Caro-Kann Accelerated Panov Attack

4...Nf6 puts another attacker on the d5 pawn.

Here, the main line is 5. Nc3, but White can also play the tricky 5. Bb5+ or 5. Qa4+, which give the unprepared Black player a chance to go wrong quickly.
explanations.textEn:
4...Nf6 · Caro-Kann Accelerated Panov Attack

4...Nf6 puts another attacker on the d5 pawn.

Here, the main line is 5. Nc3, but White can also play the tricky 5. Bb5+ or 5. Qa4+, which give the unprepared Black player a chance to go wrong quickly.
explanations.textZh:
4...Nf6·卡罗-卡恩加速帕诺夫攻击

4...Nf6 将另一名攻击者放在 d5 棋子上。

这里，主线是5.NC3，但白棋也可以下棘手的5.Bb5+或5.Qa4+，这给了毫无准备的黑棋手快速出错的机会。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. c4/2...d5/3. exd5/3...cxd5/4. cxd5/4...Nf6/5. Qa4
explanations.text:
5. Qa4+ · Caro-Kann Accelerated Panov Attack

Here Black must respond carefully. 5...Qd7 immediately loses to 5. Bb5+. 5...Bd7 is fine, but allows White to retreat the queen to b3, and now the bishop is no longer defending the b7 pawn, and the knight has to take longer to develop. So, 5...Nd7 is the usual response.
explanations.textEn:
5. Qa4+ · Caro-Kann Accelerated Panov Attack

Here Black must respond carefully. 5...Qd7 immediately loses to 5. Bb5+. 5...Bd7 is fine, but allows White to retreat the queen to b3, and now the bishop is no longer defending the b7 pawn, and the knight has to take longer to develop. So, 5...Nd7 is the usual response.
explanations.textZh:
5. Qa4+·卡罗-卡恩加速帕诺夫攻击

这里黑棋必须谨慎应对。 5...Qd7 立即输给 5.Bb5+。 5...Bd7 还可以，但是让白方将后退到 b3，现在主教不再防守 b7 兵，马需要更长的时间来发展。因此，5...Nd7 是通常的响应。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. c4/2...d5/3. exd5/3...cxd5/4. cxd5/4...Nf6/5. Qa4/5...Bd7
explanations.text:
5...Bd7 · Caro-Kann Accelerated Panov Attack

5...Bd7 is a slightly inferior reply, but still perfectly playable. 6. Qb3 is the only response that leaves some initiative for White.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d3
explanations.text:
2. d3 · Breyer variation

The unambitious Breyer variation of the Caro-Kann. 2. d3 prepares to recapture the pawn on e4 and may lead to an early endgame, or, if White wants to keep queens on the board, a King's Indian Attack-style position (see diagram).

The usual 2...d5 is almost always the move. White plans to allow Black to take into them, and then recapture on e4 with the d-pawn. If 3. Nf3, then after 3...dxe4 4. dxe4 the queens see each other and are traded. To avoid the early endgame, the main reply is 3. Nd2: this unpins White's d-pawn from the queen and so prepares for 3...dxe4 4. dxe4. The mainline is to leave the tension with 3...e5. An alternative after 3. Nf3 dxe4 is to gambit the pawn with the sharp trap line 4. Ng5!?.

2...e5 is a move order difference. White usually still achieves a King's Indian Attack-style position; Black keeps the option of either ...d5 (transposing) or ...d6.

History

The line is named for Hungarian chess master Gyula Breyer (1893―1921) who played it in a 1920 game against Efim Bogoljubov (1889―1952). Originally this was played with Be2 rather than a King's Indian-style piece deployment. The Breyer v Bogoljubov game continued 2...d5 3. Nd2 Nf6 (3...e5 is the main line today) 4. Ngf3 Bg4 5. Be2. The approach with g3 and Bg2 was first played by Siegfried Wolf (1867―1951) against William Winter (1897―1955) in 1930.

2. d3·布雷耶变体

卡罗-卡恩的布雷耶变体毫无野心。 2. d3 准备夺回 e4 上的棋子，并可能导致提前结束游戏，或者，如果白方想将皇后保留在棋盘上，则可以采用国王的印第安攻击式位置（见图）。

通常的 2...d5 几乎总是移动。白方计划让黑方吃掉他们，然后在 e4 上用 d 兵重新夺回。如果是 3. Nf3，则在 3...dxe4 4. dxe4 之后，皇后会看到对方并进行交易。为了避免早期的残局，主要回复是 3. Nd2：这将白方的 d-pawn 从后上解开，从而为 3...dxe4 4. dxe4 做好准备。主线是用 3...e5 来消除紧张。 3. Nf3 dxe4 之后的另一种选择是使用锋利的陷阱线 4. Ng5!? 来下棋。

2...e5 是移动顺序差异。白棋通常仍然会达到国王的印度进攻式局面；黑方保留 ...d5（移调）或 ...d6 的选择。

该线以匈牙利国际象棋大师久拉·布雷耶（Gyula Breyer，1893—1921 年）的名字命名，他在 1920 年与埃菲姆·博戈尔朱博夫（Efim Bogoljubov，1889—1952 年）的比赛中使用了该线。最初这是用 Be2 演奏的，而不是 King 的印度风格的棋子部署。 Breyer v Bogoljubov 比赛继续 2...d5 3. Nd2 Nf6（3...e5 是今天的主线） 4. Ngf3 Bg4 5. Be2。 g3 和 Bg2 的方法首次由齐格弗里德·沃尔夫（Siegfried Wolf，1867—1951）于 1930 年对阵威廉·温特（William Winter，1897—1955）。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d3/2...d5
explanations.text:
2...d5

Black plays 2...d5, supported by the pawn on c6. The main choice White faces is whether to allow a queen trade or not.

Offer an endgame

When White played 2. d3, they prepared to allow Black to take on e4 and recapture it with the d-pawn, but presently the d-pawn becomes pinned to White's queen. If White allows this, e.g. 3. Nf3, then after 3...dxe4 4. dxe4 the queens see each other, and 4...Qxd1+ 5. Kxd1 for an even endgame.

After 3. Nf3 dxe4, White still has an opportunity to avoid the endgame by gambitting a pawn: 4. Ng5!? exd3 5. Bxd3 is a sharp line that affords White some practical success.

Avoid the queen trade

If White wishes to avoid the queen trade, they may play 3. Nd2 to prevent the d-pawn becoming pinned to the queen. After 3...dxe4 White can actually capture either way, 4. dxe4 or 4. Nxe4, though the former is more common.

Usually Black leaves the tension with 3...e5 and the game continues resembling a King's Indian Attack, where White plays Nf3, g3, Bg7 and O-O. This is the mainline Breyer variation.

Other moves

3. exd5?! would be strange: when White played 2. d3, they prepared to allow Black to take on e4 and recapture with the d-pawn if they did. After 3. exd5?! cxd5 White will eventually want to play d4 and so has lost a tempo compared to playing 2. d4.

3. Nc3 is interesting: after 3...dxe4 White can retake with the knight instead and avoid the queen trade that way. 3...d4 kicks the knight and Black can take more space in the centre, but is playable for White.

explanations.textZh:
2...d5

黑方下 2...d5，由 c6 上的棋子支持。白面的主要选择是是否允许皇后交易。

提供残局

当白方下 2.d3 时，他们准备让黑方吃 e4 并用 d 兵夺回它，但很快 d 兵就被固定到白方的后上。如果白方允许这样做，例如3. Nf3，然后在 3...dxe4 4. dxe4 之后，皇后们会看到对方，然后 4...Qxd1+ 5. Kxd1，以实现平局。

3. Nf3 dxe4之后，白方仍有机会通过下棋来避免残局：4. Ng5！？ exd3 5. Bxd3 是一条尖锐的线，为白方提供了一些实际的成功。

避免女王贸易

如果白方希望避免皇后交易，他们可以下 3. Nd2 以防止 d 兵被钉在皇后身上。在 3...dxe4 之后，白方实际上可以吃掉 4.dxe4 或 4.Nxe4 中的任何一种，尽管前者更为常见。

通常黑方会用 3...e5 来摆脱紧张局势，而比赛继续类似于国王的印第安进攻，其中白方下 Nf3、g3、Bg7 和 O-O。这是主线布雷耶变体。

其他动作

3.exd5？！会很奇怪：当白方下 2.d3 时，他们准备让黑方下 e4，如果他们这样做的话，可以用 d 兵夺回。 3.exd5之后？！ cxd5 白方最终会想下 d4，因此与下 2.d4 相比失去了节奏。

3. Nc3 很有趣：在 3...dxe4 之后，白棋可以用马重新夺取，从而避免后交易。 3...d4 踢马，黑棋可以在中间占据更多空间，但对于白棋来说是可以发挥的。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d3/2...d5/3. Nf3
explanations.text:
3. Nf3 · Endgame offer

This variation is called the Endgame offer because, more often than not, the players will now trade their pawns and queens.

3...dxe4, eliminating the tension, is the most common move. After 4. dxe4 Qxd1+ 5. Kxd1 the endgame is reached. White still has an opportunity to avoid the endgame with 4. Ng5!?, a trappy line similar to the Tennison gambit in the Scandinavian defence.

If Black wishes to keep the queens on the board, they may want to remove their queen from the d-file (3...Qc7) before taking or just leave the central tension: 3...Bg4 and 3...g6 (intending 4...Bg7) have both been played.

explanations.textZh:
3.NF3·残局优惠

这种变化被称为“残局提议”，因为玩家现在通常会交换他们的棋子和皇后。

3...dxe4，消除紧张，是最常见的动作。 4. dxe4 Qxd1+ 5. Kxd1 结束后，游戏结束。白方仍然有机会用 4. Ng5!? 避免残局，这是一条类似于斯堪的纳维亚防守中的网球策略的陷阱线。

如果黑方希望将皇后保留在棋盘上，他们可能需要在采取或保留中心张力之前将皇后从 d 线 (3...Qc7) 中移除：3...Bg4 和 3...g6（打算 4...Bg7）都已下出。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d3/2...d5/3. Nf3/3...dxe4
explanations.text:
3...dxe4

Black takes the pawn.

4. dxe4, the most common move, leads to a queen trade and an even position after 4...Qxd1+ 5. Kxd1.

White's other option is 4. Ng5!?. This is a sharp line where White sacrifices a pawn. After 4...exd3 5. Bd3 White gets compensation with a lead in development. White has the possibility of attacks on f7 or h7, and it is easy for Black to misstep.

3...dxe4

黑棋拿走棋子。

4. dxe4，最常见的走法，在 4...Qxd1+ 5. Kxd1 之后导致皇后交易和偶数位置。

白方的另一个选择是 4. Ng5!?。这是一条锐线，白方牺牲了棋子。 4...exd3 5 之后。Bd3 白方获得领先发展的补偿。白方有攻击f7或h7的可能性，黑方很容易失步。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d3/2...d5/3. Nf3/3...dxe4/4. Ng5
explanations.text:
4. Ng5!? · Dinic gambit

White gambits their d-pawn while targeting Black's weak f7-pawn.

The most critical line is to accept the gambit with 4...exd3 and Black is up material but must be careful not to fall into any traps. After 5. Bxd3, White threatens attacks on h7 and f7. If Black is not careful and plays a natural move like 5...Nf6?? they are soon lost: 6. Nxf7! (forking queen and rook) Kxf7!? 7. Bg6+ hxg6 8. Qxd8 wins Black's queen for two minor pieces.

Alternatively Black may find declining the gambit to be more straight-forward: e.g. 4...e5 5. Nxe4 or 4...Nf6 5. Nxe4 Nxe4 6. dxe4 Qxd1+ 7. Kxd1.

History

4. Ng5!? first appeared in a 1936 blindfolded simul, where the pawn was declined with 4...Nf6 (continuing 5. Nc3 Bf5 6. dxe4 Qxd1+ 7. Kxd1 Bg6...).

It was revived in the 1990s and 2000s by Serbian FM Dragan Dinic, after whom we may gave it the unofficial name, the Dinic gambit.

Sample game

Dragan Dinic vs Branko Komnenic, Serbian Championship. 26 February 2000.

1. e4 c6 2. Nf3 d5 3. d3 dxe4 4. Ng5

Dinic preferred to reach the position via 2. Nf3 and 3. d3, rather than 2. d3 (known as the the Breyer variation) and 3. Nf3.

4...exd3 5. Bxd3

Accepting the free material is most critical. White gets compensation in the form of development.

In this position White's threat is, firstly, to take on h7 and win a pawn. A second threat is created by both queens being on the d-file: White can choose when to move their bishop and allow the queens to see each other. If they can move their bishop with tempo they have a chance to gain material.

5...Nf6??

This looks to be a natural developing move and adds a defender to h7.

6. Nxf7!

However White can take on f7 and fork Black's queen and rook.

6...Qd5

If 6...Kxf7!? then White can move their bishop away with check. 7. Bg6+ is a discovered attack on the queen: 7...hxg6 8. Qxd8 and White is up a queen for two minor pieces.

The text move is the most resourceful. It saves Black's queen and counterattacks g2.

7. Nxh8 Qxg2 8. Rf1

White is up a rook for a pawn.

8...Bh3

Black isn't quite threatening to win the rook while White's bishop is on e3 guarding f1, but this serves to tie down White's bishop.

If 8...Qxh7, White could have extricated their knight with 9. Ng6, because 9...hxg6?? 10. Bg6#!.

If e.g. 8...Nd7, White had the idea of 9. Bxh7 and Black cannot retake because 9...Nxh7? 10. Qh4+ picking up the knight.

9. Bf4 Nbd7 10. Nd2

Black is prepared to castle queenside, though doing so will allow White's knight back into the game. White's other knight,

developed to d2 rather than c3, guards f1 and so frees up White's bishop and threatens Bxh7.

10...e5 11. Bg3 e4 12. Bc4 Bb4 13. c3 Nb6

Black threatens to take on c4 as White's knight on d2 is overloaded defending both c4 and f1.

14. Qb3 Nxc4 15. Qxc4

White brings an extra defender to c4, so that after the trade they keep f1 defended.

15...O-O-O 16. Nf7 e3 17. Nxd8 1-0

Black resigns.

explanations.textZh:
4.NG5！？ · 迪尼克策略

白方下注他们的 d 棋子，同时瞄准黑方较弱的 f7 棋子。

最关键的路线是接受 4...exd3 的策略，并且黑棋是上牌，但必须小心不要落入任何陷阱。 5.Bxd3后，白方威胁攻击h7和f7。如果黑方不小心下出了 5...Nf6 这样的自然棋？他们很快就迷失了：6. Nxf7！ （分叉后和车）Kxf7！？ 7. Bg6+ hxg6 8. Qxd8 以两个小子赢得黑方后。

或者，黑方可能会发现拒绝这一策略更为直接：例如4...e5 5.Nxe4 或 4...Nf6 5.Nxe4 Nxe4 6.dxe4 Qxd1+ 7.Kxd1。

历史

4.NG5！？首次出现在 1936 年的蒙眼模拟游戏中，棋子以 4...Nf6 被拒绝（继续 5. Nc3 Bf5 6. dxe4 Qxd1+ 7. Kxd1 Bg6...）。

塞尔维亚调频德拉甘·迪尼奇 (Dragan Dinic) 在 2000 年代和 20 世纪 90 年代复兴了这一策略，我们可以用他的名字给它起一个非官方的名字：迪尼克策略 (Dinic gambit)。

示例游戏

塞尔维亚锦标赛，德拉甘·迪尼奇 (Dragan Dinic) 对阵布兰科·科姆内尼奇 (Branko Komnenic)。 2000 年 2 月 26 日。

1. e4 c6 2. Nf3 d5 3. d3 dxe4 4. NG5

Dinic 更愿意通过 2. Nf3 和 3. d3 到达该位置，而不是 2. d3（称为 Breyer 变体）和 3. Nf3。

4...exd3 5.Bxd3

接受免费材料是最关键的。白色以发展的形式获得补偿。

在这个局面下，白方的威胁首先是吃 h7 并赢得棋子。第二个威胁是由两个皇后都在 d 线上造成的：白棋可以选择何时移动他们的主教并允许皇后看到对方。如果他们能按节奏移动主教，他们就有机会获得材料。

5...NF6??

这看起来是一个自然发展的举动，并为 h7 增加了一名防守者。

6.Nxf7！

然而，白棋可以对抗f7并分叉黑棋的后和车。

6...Qd5

如果6...Kxf7！？然后白方可以用过牌将他们的主教移开。 7. Bg6+ 是对皇后的发现攻击：7...hxg6 8. Qxd8 和怀特是两个小棋子的皇后。

文动最为足智多谋。救了黑后，反击g2。

7.Nxh8 Qxg2 8.Rf1

白棋摆出车作为棋子。

8...Bh3

当白棋的主教在 e3 上守卫 f1 时，黑棋并没有太大的威胁赢得车，但这有助于束缚白棋的主教。

如果 8...Qxh7，白方可以用 9.Ng6 解救他们的马，因为 9...hxg6？ 10. Bg6#!.

如果例如8...Nd7，白方有9的想法。Bxh7和黑方无法重夺，因为9...Nxh7？ 10.Qh4+捡起骑士。

9. Bf4 Nbd7 10. Nd2

黑方准备在后翼建立城堡，尽管这样做将使白方的马重新回到游戏中。白方的另一位骑士，

发展到d2而不是c3，守卫f1，从而释放白方的主教并威胁Bxh7。

10...e5 11.Bg3 e4 12.Bc4 Bb4 13.c3 Nb6

由于白方在 d2 上的马在防守 c4 和 f1 时负荷过重，因此黑方威胁要对 c4 进行进攻。

14.Qb3 Nxc4 15.Qxc4

白方为c4带来了一名额外的防守者，这样在交易之后他们就可以继续防守f1。

15...O-O-O 16.Nf7 e3 17.Nxd8 1-0

布莱克辞职。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d3/2...d5/3. Nf3/3...dxe4/4. Ng5/4...exd3/5. Bxd3
explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Defence, Endgame Offer

Here White double attacks Black's h-pawn. While it is natural to defend the pawn (with 5...h6 or Nf6), White is also threatening a knight sacrifice to win Black's queen, which Black must address. Thus, moving their queen out of the way with 5...Qa5+ or blocking it with 5...Nd7 are Black's best choices.

explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩防守，残局报价

此处，白方双重攻击黑方的 h 兵。虽然保卫棋子是很自然的事（用 5...h6 或 Nf6），但白棋也威胁要牺牲马来赢得黑棋的后，这是黑棋必须解决的问题。因此，用 5...Qa5+ 移动他们的皇后或用 5...Nd7 阻挡它是黑方的最佳选择。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d3/2...d5/3. Nf3/3...dxe4/4. Ng5/4...exd3/5. Bxd3/5...Nf6
explanations.text:
5...Nf6?? - Caro-Kann Defence, Endgame Offer

Black fails to consider that 6. Nf7! is a valid fork on the Black queen and rook. If the Black king captures back, 7. Bg6+ leaves the Black queen defenseless and White will be up 3 points in material with a clearly stronger position.
explanations.textEn:
5...Nf6?? - Caro-Kann Defence, Endgame Offer
