explanations.textZh:
5...NF6?? - 卡罗-卡恩防守，残局报价

黑方没有考虑到 6. Nf7！是黑后和车上的有效分叉。如果黑王夺回，则 7。Bg6+ 使黑后毫无防备，白棋将在材料上领先 3 分，位置明显更强。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d3/2...d5/3. Nf3/3...dxe4/4. Ng5/4...exd3/5. Bxd3/5...h6
explanations.text:
5...h6?? - Caro-Kann Defence, Endgame Offer

Black fails to consider that 6. Nf7! is a valid fork on the Black queen and rook. Furthermore, the g6 square is no longer protected and White gains checkmate threats with their bishop and queen.
explanations.textEn:
5...h6?? - Caro-Kann Defence, Endgame Offer

Black fails to consider that 6. Nf7! is a valid fork on the Black queen and rook. Furthermore, the g6 square is no longer protected and White gains checkmate threats with their bishop and queen.
explanations.textZh:
5...h6？？ - 卡罗-卡恩防守，残局报价

黑方没有考虑到 6. Nf7！是黑后和车上的有效分叉。此外，g6 方格不再受到保护，白方通过其主教和后获得了将死威胁。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d3/2...d5/3. Nf3/3...dxe4/4. Ng5/4...exd3/5. Bxd3/5...h6/6. Nxf7
explanations.text:
6. Nf7! - Caro-Kann Defence, Endgame Offer

Black's best move now is to lose their queen for a bishop and knight with 6...Qxd3 7. Qxd3 Kxf7 and White will be up 3 points in material. If Black captures White's knight with 6...Kxf7, White has a forced mate in 6 moves beginning with 7. Qh5+. In any other case, White will win Black's rook and have both bishops and queen lined up on the diagonals to potentially checkmate (such as 6...Qb6 7. Nxh8 Nf6 8. Bg6#).

6. Nf7! - Caro-Kann Defence, Endgame Offer

explanations.textZh:
6.NF7！ - 卡罗-卡恩防守，残局报价

黑方现在最好的棋步是用 6...Qxd3 7 失去后，换取主教和马。Qxd3 Kxf7，白方将在材料上领先 3 点。如果黑棋用 6...Kxf7 吃掉白棋的马，白棋在从 7.Qh5+ 开始的 6 步中就被迫交配。在任何其他情况下，白棋将赢得黑棋的车，并且象和后都排列在对角线上，有可能将死（例如 6...Qb6 7. Nxh8 Nf6 8. Bg6#）。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4
explanations.text:
2. d4

White plays the principled move: if your opponent allows you to put two pawns in the centre, then put two pawns in the centre.

Black responds 2...d5. Black threatens to take on e4 if White leaves their e-pawn where it is. As d5 is supported by Black's c-pawn, Black is very happy to answer 3. exd5 (the exchange variation) with 3...cxd5, functionally having traded White's central e-pawn for Black's peripheral c-pawn. Therefore, White's most common responses are 3. e5, protecting the pawn by moving it out of harms way, or 3. Nc3, preparing to recapture it.

2...d5, in accordance with the plan set in motion by 1...c6, is almost always the move here, chosen more than 95 times in 100 in serious games. On rare occasions a few other things have been tried (though often ...d5 follows soon after):

2...d6 transposes to the Czech Pirc Defense.

2...g6, preparing to fianchetto, has been played.

2...Na6!? is called the De Bruycker defence. The knight makes its way to c7 via a6.

2...Nf6!? is called the Masi variation. This invites 3. e5!, and the knight relocates to d5 and, if kicked again with 4. c4, to c7.

explanations.textZh:
2.d4

白棋走原则性棋：如果对手允许你将两个棋子放在中间，那么就将两个棋子放在中间。

黑方回应 2...d5。黑方威胁称，如果白方将其 e 兵留在原处，则黑方将采取 e4 行动。由于 d5 得到黑方 c 兵的支持，黑方很高兴用 3...cxd5 回答 3. exd5（交换变体），功能上已将白方的中央 e 兵换成了黑方的外围 c 兵。因此，白方最常见的反应是 3. e5，通过将棋子移出危险的方式来保护棋子，或 3. Nc3，准备夺回棋子。

2...d5，按照 1...c6 制定的计划，几乎总是这里的着法，在严肃的游戏中，在 100 场比赛中被选择了超过 95 次。在极少数情况下，会尝试其他一些方法（尽管通常...d5紧随其后）：

2...d6 转换为捷克皮尔克防御。

2...g6，准备fianchetto，已经演奏。

2...Na6！？称为德布鲁伊克防御。马通过a6到达c7。

2...NF6！？称为马西变体。这会邀请 3. e5!，并且骑士将移动到 d5，如果再次用 4. c4 踢，则移动到 c7。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...Na6
explanations.text:
2...Na6!? · De Bruycker defence

2...Na6!? is the De Bruycker defence. Black delays playing d5 to first develop their knight.

Having played c6, the usual square for Black's queenside knight is unavailable. Although a6 (being on the rim) is grim, via a6 the knight can reach c7, where it is more active.

Using two tempi to develop the knight this way is an unusual continuation: in the Caro-Kann, Black usually just develops the knight a bit later when they can do so in one move: either to c6 (if it becomes available again, as in the Exchange Caro-Kann) or d7.

White may be tempted to snap the knight off, 3. Bxa6?!, so that after Black recaptures 3...bxa6? they have doubled rook pawns. However this does not work in this instance: Black has the intermezzo 3...Qa5!+ followed by ...Qxa6. Their pawn structure is unaffected and then they are happy with the bishop pair.

Better is for White is to take advantage of the slow move to grab more space, 3. c4, or to develop their own knight more actively 3. Nf3.

explanations.textZh:
2...Na6！？ · 德布鲁伊克防守

2...Na6！？是德布鲁伊克防守。黑方延迟下 d5 来首先发展他们的马。

下完c6后，黑方后翼马的常用方格就无法使用了。虽然a6（在篮筐上）很严峻，但通过a6骑士可以到达c7，在那里它更活跃。

以这种方式使用两个节奏来发展马是一种不寻常的延续：在卡罗-卡恩中，黑方通常只是在他们可以一步完成时稍后发展马：要么是c6（如果它再次可用，如在交换卡罗-卡恩中）或d7。

白棋可能会想把马打掉，3. Bxa6？！，这样黑棋重新夺回3...bxa6？他们有双车兵。然而，这在这种情况下不起作用：黑方有间奏曲 3...Qa5!+ 后跟 ...Qxa6。他们的典当结构不受影响，然后他们对主教对感到满意。

对于白方来说更好的是利用缓慢的移动来抢占更多的空间，3.c4，或者更积极地发展自己的骑士3.Nf3。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...Na6/3. Bxa6
explanations.text:
3. Bxa6

White snap off Black's knight, thinking if 3...bxa6? they have ruined Black's pawn structure with doubled, isolated pawns on the a-file.

However, because Black has already opened up their queen with c6, they have the reply 3...Qa5+ 4. Nc3 Qxa6, and Black picks up the bishop pair without spoiling their pawns.
explanations.textEn:

However, because Black has already opened up their queen with c6, they have the reply 3...Qa5+ 4. Nc3 Qxa6, and Black picks up the bishop pair without spoiling their pawns.
explanations.textZh:
3.Bxa6

白棋击垮了黑棋的马，思考是否 3...bxa6？他们用a字形上的双重、孤立的棋子破坏了黑方的棋子结构。

然而，因为黑方已经用 c6 打开了他们的后，所以他们得到了答复 3...Qa5+ 4. Nc3 Qxa6，并且黑方拿起了主教对而不破坏他们的兵。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...Na6/3. Bxa6/3...Qa5
explanations.text:
3...Qa5+

Black gives a check and attacks the bishop, intending to capture it with the queen. White will most likely block the check using /4. Nc3/.
explanations.textEn:
3...Qa5+

Black gives a check and attacks the bishop, intending to capture it with the queen. White will most likely block the check using /4. Nc3/.
explanations.textZh:
3...Qa5+

黑方过让并攻击主教，意图与后一起吃掉主教。白方很可能会使用 /4 阻止检查。 NC3/。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5
explanations.text:
2...d5

This is the main line of the Caro-Kann defence, a semi-open game that tends to contain lines with minor piece play.

Black's threatens to capture ...dxe4. White has four main plans to deal with the central tension: close the centre, capture first, or prepare to recapture with knight or pawn.

3. e5 is the advance variation. White closes the centre and takes more space. This is the modern-day main line at all levels. The main line continues 3...Bf5 4. Nf3 e6 5. Be2, and Black either plays for an early ...c5 pawn break or contents themselves with developing in a cramped position. White has a choice of several sharp sidelines, including 3. Nc3 & 4. g4, sometimes called the Shirov attack.

3. exd5 is the exchange variation. Black retakes 3...cxd5 and frees the c6 for their knight again. Then White's main options are the Rubinstein variation, 4. Bd3 Nc6 5. c3 Nf6 6. Bf4, which leads to a Carlsbad pawn structure, or the sharp Panov attack, 4. c4, where White is willing to accept an isolated queen's pawn position for rapid development and attacking chances.

3. Nc3, the classical, and 3. Nd2, the modern variation, prepare to recapture with the knight. Usually, both moves reach the same position after 3...dxe4 4. Nxe4. The two move orders differ in how they may answer the sideline 3...g6.

3. f3, preparing to recapture with the pawn, is the Maróczy or fantasy variation. Black doesn't usually want to allow White to retake in the centre with a pawn (though 3...dxe4 4. fxe4 e5 is playable) and the main continuation is 3...e6 and a closed, manoeuvring game.

Other moves

Defending the pawn with 3. Bd3!? is irregular as 3...dxe4 4. Bxe4 Nf6 gives Black the initiative.

3. c4?! transposes into the Diemer gambit of the Slav defence, otherwise seen after 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. e4.

3. Be3?! is the Mieses gambit. The usual idea is 3...dxe4 4. f3 exf3 5. Nf3, a pawn sacrifice for a development lead similar to the Blackmar Diemer gambit, 1. d4 d5 2. e4.

explanations.textZh:
2...d5

这是卡罗-卡恩防守的主线，这是一种半开放的游戏，往往包含带有小块比赛的线路。

黑方威胁要夺取...dxe4。白方应对中心紧张局势有四个主要计划：关闭中心、先吃人、或准备用马或兵夺回。

3. e5 是高级变体。白色封闭了中心并占据了更多空间。这是现代各个层面的主线。主线继续 3...Bf5 4. Nf3 e6 5. Be2，黑棋要么争取早期 ...c5 兵破，要么满足于在狭窄的位置上发展。白棋可以选择几种锋利的边线，包括 3. Nc3 和 4. g4，有时称为 Shirov 进攻。

3. exd5 是交换变体。黑方重新夺回 3...cxd5 并再次为他们的马释放了 c6。那么白方的主要选择是鲁宾斯坦变体，4. Bd3 Nc6 5. c3 Nf6 6. Bf4，这会导致卡尔斯巴德棋子结构，或尖锐的帕诺夫攻击，4. c4，白方愿意接受孤立的皇后棋子位置以获得快速发展和攻击机会。

3. Nc3，古典，3. Nd2，现代变体，准备与骑士一起夺回。通常，两个动作在 3...dxe4 4. Nxe4 之后到达相同的位置。这两个移动指令的不同之处在于它们如何回答边线 3...g6。

3. f3，准备用棋子夺回，是 Maróczy 或幻想变体。黑方通常不想让白方用棋子重新占据中心（尽管 3...dxe4 4. fxe4 e5 是可以玩的），主要的延续是 3...e6 和一个封闭的、机动的游戏。

其他动作

用 3.Bd3!? 保卫棋子不规则为 3...dxe4 4。Bxe4 Nf6 给予黑方主动。

3.c4？！转置为斯拉夫防御的 Diemer 策略，否则在 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. e4 之后可见。

3.Be3？！是密塞斯策略。通常的想法是 3...dxe4 4. f3 exf3 5. Nf3，为发展领先而做出的典当牺牲，类似于 Blackmar Diemer 策略，1. d4 d5 2. e4。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3
explanations.text:
3. Nc3 · Classical variation

White develops a knight, ready to take back on e4.

3...dxe4, denying White their two-pawn centre, is the main move, after which White usually recaptures with 4. Nxe4, though some ways of gambitting the pawn may be played.

A few sidelines exist if Black wishes to avoid main line theory;

3...Nf6 is called the Campomanes attack. This induces White to play 4. e5, kicking the knight to d7. Black has induced White to play with a closed centre, resembling an advance variation Caro-Kann, perhaps not a line they were prepared to play.

3...g6 is the Gurgenidze system. It allows White to expand on the kingside, 4. e5 Bg7 5. f4 h5, where Black usually looks to trade off their light square bishop and plant their knight on f5 via h5. 4. h3 prevents Black from playing ...Bg4 and trading off the bishop and usually leads to an open centre.

3...b5?!, the Gurgenidze counterattack, where Black hopes to drive off White's knight with ...b4, which they imagine might be good for them. An unsound surprise attack that performs well enough at the club level.

3...e6?!, defending the d5 pawn again and combining the disadvantages of both the Caro-Kann and the French defence, must surely be the worse than either.

explanations.textZh:
3. Nc3·古典变奏

白方派出一名骑士，准备夺回 e4。

3...dxe4，阻止白方的两兵中心，是主要的走法，之后白方通常会用 4.Nxe4 重新夺回，尽管可能会采取一些下棋方式。

如果黑方希望避免主线理论，则存在一些副线；

3...Nf6 称为 Campomanes 攻击。这促使白棋下 4. e5，将马踢到 d7。黑方诱导白方使用封闭中锋，类似于卡罗-卡恩的高级变体，也许不是他们准备使用的路线。

3...g6 是古尔根尼泽系统。它允许白方在王翼展开，4. e5 Bg7 5. f4 h5，黑方通常会考虑权衡其轻方主教，并通过 h5 将马放在 f5 上。 4. h3 阻止黑棋下...Bg4 并交易主教，并且通常会导致开放中心。

3...b5？！，古尔根尼泽反击，黑方希望用...b4击退白方的马，他们认为这可能对他们有好处。一次不健全的突然袭击，在俱乐部层面表现得足够好。

3...e6？！，再次防守d5兵，结合卡罗-卡恩和法国防守的缺点，肯定比任何一个都更糟糕。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4
explanations.text:
3...dxe4

Black has taken White's e-pawn and denied them the classical two-pawn centre. By taking the pawn, Black frees up the space it controlled and creates new possibilities for their piece development.

4. Nxe4, recapturing the pawn is the natural and most common response, which usually leads to one of three main lines, 4...Bf5, the classical variation, 4...Nd7, the Karpov variation, or 4...Nf6 5. Nxf6+ exf6, the Tartakower variation.

White may choose to gambit the pawn with 4. f3 or 4. Bc4 for a development advantage. White doesn't receive full compensation for the pawn, but the lines can be sharp.

4. f3 is the Rasa-Studier gambit. White offers Black the f-pawn to remove the problematic e-pawn so that they can recapture it by developing a new piece, 4...exf3 5. Nxf3. This leads to positions resembling the Blackmar-Diemer gambit.

4. Bc4 is the Von Hennig gambit, though this comes with the same idea to play f3 and the two gambits usually converge after 4...Nf6 5. f3 exf3 6. Nxf3. If Black declines to take the f-pawn there are other original lines.

explanations.textZh:
3...dxe4

黑方占据了白方的 e 兵并剥夺了他们的经典两兵中心。通过拿走棋子，黑方释放了它所控制的空间，并为棋子的发展创造了新的可能性。

4. Nxe4，夺回棋子是自然且最常见的反应，通常会导致三个主线之一：4...Bf5，经典变体，4...Nd7，卡尔波夫变体，或 4...Nf6 5. Nxf6+ exf6，Tartakower 变体。

白方可能会选择用 4. f3 或 4. Bc4 下棋以获得发展优势。白棋并没有获得棋子的全部补偿，但线条可能很尖锐。

4. f3 是 Rasa-Studier 策略。白方向黑方提供 f 棋子以移除有问题的 e 棋子，以便他们可以通过开发新棋子 4...exf3 5. Nxf3 来夺回它。这导致了类似于布莱克马尔-迪默策略的立场。

4. Bc4 是 Von Hennig 策略，尽管这与玩 f3 具有相同的想法，并且这两种策略通常在 4...Nf6 5. f3 exf3 6. Nxf3 之后收敛。如果黑方拒绝吃 f 兵，则还有其他原始行。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4
explanations.text:
4. Nxe4

4. Nxe4 is an obvious recapture. This is the traditional treatment of the Caro-Kann and may arise from either the 3. Nc3 or 3. Nd2 variations.

Black has three main alternatives.

4...Bf5 is the classical variation. The bishop ends up controlling the long diagonal first from g6 via the manoeuvre 5. Ng3 Bg6, then from h7 after 6. h4 h6 7. Nf3 Nd7 8. h5 Bh7.

4...Nf6, developing the knight instead, leads to 5. Nxf6+ exf6, the Tartakower variation. This is perfectly playable but Black has to accept doubling their pawns.

4...Nd7 is the Smyslov or Karpov variation. This looks slower, as the knight will have to move again before the light-square bishop can enter the game. If Black ends up trading their knight on f6, they may recapture with another knight rather than double their pawns: 5. Nf3 Ngf6 6. Nxf6 Nxf6. Otherwise, the main move is 5. Ng5.

None of the other alternatives have seen significant use. 4...h6 is known as the Finnish variation.

explanations.textZh:
4.NXE4

4. Nxe4是明显的夺回。这是 Caro-Kann 的传统处理方法，可能源自 3. Nc3 或 3. Nd2 变体。

黑方有三种主要选择。

4...Bf5 是经典变体。象最终通过策略 5. Ng3 Bg6 首先从 g6 开始控制长对角线，然后在 6. h4 h6 7. Nf3 Nd7 8. h5 Bh7 之后从 h7 开始控制。

4...Nf6，改为发展骑士，导致 5. Nxf6+ exf6，Tartakower 变体。这是完全可以玩的，但黑方必须接受将棋子加倍。

4...Nd7 是 Smyslov 或 Karpov 变体。这看起来比较慢，因为在光方块主教进入游戏之前，骑士必须再次移动。如果黑方最终在 f6 上交易了他们的马，他们可能会用另一位马重新夺回，而不是加倍他们的棋子：5. Nf3 Ngf6 6. Nxf6 Nxf6。否则，主要动作是5。NG5。

其他替代方案都没有得到显着的使用。 4...h6 被称为芬兰变体。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...Nd7
explanations.text:
Smyslov/Karpov Variation

4...Nd7

By developing his Knight rather than the Bishop, Black aims to trade for White's central Knight, without compromising his pawn structure.

At one time named after the first world champion Wilhelm Steinitz, nowadays the variation is more often referred to as the Smyslov Variation after the seventh world champion Vasily Smyslov who played a number of notable games with it, or the Karpov Variation, after the twelfth World Champion Anatoly Karpov, in whose repertoire it appeared quite often. The short-term goal of 4...Nd7 is to ease development by the early exchange of a pair of Knights without compromising the structural integrity of his position. Play is similar to the Classical Variation except that Black has more freedom by delaying the development of his bishop, and is not forced to play it to the g6 square. However, this freedom comes at a cost as White enjoys added freedom in taking up space in the center, and often plays the aggressive 5.Ng5!? where Black's development is brought into question as well as the positional weakness of the f7-square. The famous last game of the Deep Blue-Garry Kasparov rematch where Kasparov committed a known blunder and lost was played in this very line.

explanations.textZh:
斯梅斯洛夫/卡尔波夫变例

4...ND7

通过发展他的马而不是象，黑方的目标是在不损害其棋子结构的情况下交换白方的中央马。

该变奏曾经以第一届世界冠军威廉·斯坦尼茨的名字命名，如今，该变奏更常被称为“斯梅斯洛夫变奏”，以第七届世界冠军瓦西里·斯梅斯洛夫的名字命名，他曾使用该变奏进行过许多著名的比赛；而“卡尔波夫变奏”则以第十二届世界冠军阿纳托利·卡尔波夫的名字命名，它经常出现在他的曲目中。 4...Nd7 的短期目标是通过早期交换一对骑士来缓解发展，同时不损害其位置的结构完整性。玩法与经典变例类似，只是黑方通过延迟其象的发展而拥有更多自由，并且不必被迫将其下到 g6 方格。然而，这种自由是有代价的，因为白棋在占据中心空间方面享有额外的自由，并且经常打出侵略性的 5.Ng5!?黑方的发展以及 f7 方格的位置弱点都受到质疑。著名的深蓝与加里·卡斯帕罗夫复赛的最后一场比赛就是在这条线路上进行的，卡斯帕罗夫犯了一个已知的错误并输掉了比赛。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...Nd7/5. Qe2
explanations.text:
5.Qe2?!

This is an unusual looking move, but it creates a subtle mate threat. Black can fall into it very easily in amateur play, and so this move is recommended.

Black can get mated in one move if he makes an error.

If black plays correctly, it is easier for him to equalize. Black can get mated on move 5.

explanations.textZh:
5.Qe2？！

这是一个看起来不寻常的举动，但却造成了微妙的配偶威胁。在业余棋中，黑棋很容易陷入困境，因此推荐此步棋。

如果黑棋走错了一步，他就可以一举落败。

如果黑方下法正确，他就更容易扳平比分。黑棋可以在第 5 步中交配。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...Nd7/5. Qe2/5...Ngf6
explanations.text:
5.Ngf6??

This move looks like simple development, yet black is now doomed to a mate in 1. Can you see it?. This trap has ensnared countless amateurs.

Much better is 5...Ndf6.
explanations.textEn:
5.Ngf6??

This move looks like simple development, yet black is now doomed to a mate in 1. Can you see it?. This trap has ensnared countless amateurs.

Much better is 5...Ndf6.
explanations.textZh:
5.NGF6??

这步棋看起来很简单，但黑棋现在注定是1中的搭档。你能看到吗？这个陷阱让无数业余爱好者陷入困境。

更好的是 5...Ndf6。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...Nd7/5. Ng5
explanations.text:
5.Ng5 !?

This is an interesting move, with chances to blow Black off the Board. Even Kasparov got blown with a crushing knight sacrifice.

For the interested people, the game followed:

1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4 Nd7 5.Ng5!? Ngf6 6.Bd3 e6 7.N1f3 h6? (this allows a crushing sacrifice) 8.Nxe6! Qe7?! 9.0-0 fxe6 10.Bg6+ Kd8 (White has a winning attack) 11.Bf4 b5 12.a4 Bb7 13.Re1 Nd5 14.Bg3 Kc8 15.axb5 cxb5 16.Qd3 Bc6 17.Bf5 exf5 18.Rxe7 Bxe7 19.c4 1–0

Theory

explanations.textZh:
5.NG5！？

这是一个有趣的举动，有机会将黑棋从棋盘上击落。就连卡斯帕罗夫也被压倒性的骑士牺牲所震惊。

对于感兴趣的人来说，游戏如下：

1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4 Nd7 5.Ng5！？ Ngf6 6.Bd3 e6 7.N1f3 h6？ （这允许压倒性的牺牲）8.Nxe6！ Qe7？！ 9.0-0 fxe6 10.Bg6+ Kd8（白方获胜进攻） 11.Bf4 b5 12.a4 Bb7 13.Re1 Nd5 14.Bg3 Kc8 15.axb5 cxb5 16.Qd3 Bc6 17.Bf5 exf5 18.Rxe7 Bxe7 19.c4 1–0

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...Nd7/5. Ng5/5...h6
explanations.text:
5...h6?!

This move seems logical, as Nxf7 doesn't work. However, White can get a slight edge with Ne6! and can win quickly if Black makes a blunder.

A grandmaster lost to this trap. The e8-h5 diagonal is slightly weakened, and so is f7. The main line is Ne6! Qb6 (Wisely avoiding fxe6?? Qh5+ g6 Qxg6#) Nxf8 Nxf8 with two Bishops and a slight edge.
explanations.textEn:
5...h6?!

This move seems logical, as Nxf7 doesn't work. However, White can get a slight edge with Ne6! and can win quickly if Black makes a blunder.

A grandmaster lost to this trap. The e8-h5 diagonal is slightly weakened, and so is f7. The main line is Ne6! Qb6 (Wisely avoiding fxe6?? Qh5+ g6 Qxg6#) Nxf8 Nxf8 with two Bishops and a slight edge.
explanations.textZh:
5...h6？！

这一举动似乎合乎逻辑，因为 Nxf7 不起作用。然而，白棋用 Ne6 可以取得轻微优势！如果黑方犯了错误，也能很快获胜。

一位宗师就落入了这个陷阱。 e8-h5对角线稍弱，f7也是如此。主线是Ne6！ Qb6（明智地避开fxe6？？Qh5+ g6 Qxg6#）Nxf8 Nxf8，有两个主教，稍有优势。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...Bf5
explanations.text:
4... Bf5 · Caro-Kann Defence: Classical Variation

The Classical Variation. Black develops their bishop and attacks White's knight on e4.

White often sticks to the main line with /5. Ng3/, forcing the Bf5 back. However, other options exist. The aggressive Burris Gambit, /5. Bd3/, has given White surprising success and the interesting /5. Ng5/ is an aggressive move, often aiming to play the Martian Gambit.

Other moves are generally not very good. 5. Nc3 retreats the knight to where it was before, while the ambitious 5. Nc5 is perhaps too aggressive and the knight can be kicked away easily, while 5. f3 defending the knight is playable but White will have to be careful to not weaken their kingside.
explanations.textEn:

White often sticks to the main line with /5. Ng3/, forcing the Bf5 back. However, other options exist. The aggressive Burris Gambit, /5. Bd3/, has given White surprising success and the interesting /5. Ng5/ is an aggressive move, often aiming to play the Martian Gambit.

Other moves are generally not very good. 5. Nc3 retreats the knight to where it was before, while the ambitious 5. Nc5 is perhaps too aggressive and the knight can be kicked away easily, while 5. f3 defending the knight is playable but White will have to be careful to not weaken their kingside.
explanations.textZh:
4... Bf5 · 卡罗-卡恩防御：经典变式

古典变奏。黑方在 e4 上发展了象并攻击白方的马。

白棋经常用/5 坚持主线。 Ng3/，迫使 Bf5 后退。然而，还存在其他选择。好斗的伯里斯甘比特，/5。 Bd3/，给白棋带来了令人惊讶的成功和有趣的/5。 Ng5/ 是一个激进的棋步，通常旨在玩火星开局。

其他动作一般都不太好。 5. Nc3将马撤回到原来的位置，而野心勃勃的5. Nc5可能过于激进，马很容易被踢开，而5. f3防守马是可以玩的，但白方必须小心不要削弱他们的王翼。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...Bf5/5. Ng3
explanations.text:
5. Ng3 · Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

Bg6 is almost always played as the only sensible place for the bishop to retreat to, although defending the bishop with g6 is a very rare alternative, leaving black with an inferior pawn structure.
explanations.textEn:
5. Ng3 · Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

Bg6 is almost always played as the only sensible place for the bishop to retreat to, although defending the bishop with g6 is a very rare alternative, leaving black with an inferior pawn structure.
explanations.textZh:
5. Ng3·卡罗-卡恩防御：经典变例

Bg6 几乎总是被视为象撤退的唯一明智位置，尽管用 g6 保卫象是一种非常罕见的选择，使黑棋的兵结构较差。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...Bf5/5. Ng3/5...Bg6/6. Nf3/6...Nd7
explanations.text:
6... Nd7 · Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

White again has a large list of options, some of which transpose to other lines. h4 will probably transpose to the most popular line (h4 is more commonly played on move 6).
explanations.textEn:
6... Nd7 · Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

White again has a large list of options, some of which transpose to other lines. h4 will probably transpose to the most popular line (h4 is more commonly played on move 6).
explanations.textZh:
6... Nd7 · 卡罗-卡恩防御：经典变例

白棋再次有一大堆选项，其中一些可以转换为其他行。 h4 可能会移调到最流行的台词（h4 更常见于第 6 步）。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...Bf5/5. Ng3/5...Bg6/6. h4
explanations.text:
6. h4 · Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

Black needs to defend the bishop, and h6 is almost universal, although the probably inferior h5 and Nd7 have been attempted.
explanations.textEn:
6. h4 · Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

Black needs to defend the bishop, and h6 is almost universal, although the probably inferior h5 and Nd7 have been attempted.
explanations.textZh:
6. h4·卡罗-卡恩防御：经典变式

黑方需要保卫主教，h6 几乎是通用的，尽管可能较差的 h5 和 Nd7 已被尝试过。

explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

While Nd7 seems inferior because of the weak bishop, this was never tested in the only instance this move was played at master level, between Rustam Kasimdzhanov and Mikhael Mchedlishvili in the European Clubs Cup (Men) in 2003. (That game quickly transposed back to a main line, continuing: 6...Nd7 7. Nf3 h6 8. h5 Bh7 9. Bd3 Bxd3 10. Qxd3 e6 11. Bf4 Ngf6 12. O-O-O Be7 13. Kb1 O-O 14. Ne4 Qa5 15. g4 Nxg4 16. Ne5 Ndxe5 17. dxe5 Rad8 18. Qh3 Qb4 19. Rdg1 Qxe4 20. Rxg4 Qh7 21. Rhg1 Kh8 22. Qg3 Rg8 23. Be3 a6 24. a3 Rd7 25. Qg2 Rd5 26. Qg3 Rd7 27. Qg2 Rd5 28. Qg3 1/2-1/2.)

It may appear at first that White can trap the bishop, but this is not the case after 7. h5 Bf5 8. Nxf5 Qa5+! +=. However, White can do this anyway and get the bishop pair and light-square control.

Ne5 Ndxe5 17. dxe5 Rad8 18. Qh3 Qb4 19. Rdg1 Qxe4 20. Rxg4 Qh7 21. Rhg1 Kh8 22. Qg3 Rg8 23. Be3 a6 24. a3 Rd7 25. Qg2 Rd5 26. Qg3 Rd7 27. Qg2 Rd5 28. Qg3 1/2-1/2.)

It may appear at first that White can trap the bishop, but this is not the case after 7. h5 Bf5 8. Nxf5 Qa5+! +=. However, White can do this anyway and get the bishop pair and light-square control.

乍一看，白方可能会困住象，但在 7. h5 Bf5 8. Nxf5 Qa5+ 之后情况并非如此！ +=。然而，白棋无论如何都可以做到这一点，并获得象对和光方控制。

explanations.text:
6. ...h5

Instead of the more traditional ...h6, here black opts to block the white pawn from advancing altogether. This is a rare move at the professional level, although not an inherently bad one (although castling kingside becomes more dangerous compared to ...h6 lines). White has a large variety of moves to play; 7. Nf3 develops a piece while 7. Nh3!?, aiming for an eventual Nf4, has also been attempted.

explanations.textZh:
6. ...h5

在这里，黑棋选择阻止白棋完全前进，而不是更传统的 ...h6。这是职业水平上罕见的走法，尽管本质上并不是一个糟糕的走法（尽管与...h6 线相比，王侧易车变得更加危险）。白棋有多种走法； 7. Nf3 正在开发一款作品，而 7. Nh3!? 也已尝试以最终的 Nf4 为目标。

explanations.text:
6... h6 · Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

7. Nf3 is almost always played, with white aiming to place the knight on e5. White's other options have rarely been seen in master play.
explanations.textEn:
6... h6 · Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

7. Nf3 is almost always played, with white aiming to place the knight on e5. White's other options have rarely been seen in master play.
explanations.textZh:
6... h6 · 卡罗-卡恩防御：经典变例

7. Nf3几乎总是被玩，白棋的目标是将马放在e5上。白棋的其他选择在大师棋中很少见到。

explanations.text:
7... Nd7 · Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

8. h5 is mostly played, aiming to tie up black's kingside pawns. The pawn on h5 is double-edged. It's powerfully positioned in black's territory, but it also requires protection from the knight on g3, making this potentially a bad piece.
explanations.textEn:
7... Nd7 · Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

8. h5 is mostly played, aiming to tie up black's kingside pawns. The pawn on h5 is double-edged. It's powerfully positioned in black's territory, but it also requires protection from the knight on g3, making this potentially a bad piece.
explanations.textZh:
7... Nd7 · 卡罗-卡恩防御：经典变例

8. 主要是用h5，目的是绑住黑方王翼兵。 h5 上的棋子是一把双刃剑。它在黑棋的地盘中处于强势地位，但它也需要 g3 上马的保护，这使得它可能是一个坏棋。

explanations.text:
8... Bh7 · Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

9. Bd3 is almost always played. Black has spent numerous tempos on this bishop, and since white usually aims to castle queenside, it makes sense to remove the light-squared bishop.
explanations.textEn:
8... Bh7 · Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

9. Bd3 is almost always played. Black has spent numerous tempos on this bishop, and since white usually aims to castle queenside, it makes sense to remove the light-squared bishop.
explanations.textZh:
8... Bh7 · 卡罗-卡恩防御：经典变例

9. Bd3几乎总是被播放。黑棋在这个象上花费了很多节奏，并且由于白棋通常的目标是在后翼建立城堡，所以移除浅色方块的象是有道理的。

explanations.text:
9. Bd3 · Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

Black's almost invariable response of 9...Bxd3 is almost forced, although 9...Ngf6 and even 9...e6 have both been attempted, without much success.
explanations.textEn:
9. Bd3 · Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

Black's almost invariable response of 9...Bxd3 is almost forced, although 9...Ngf6 and even 9...e6 have both been attempted, without much success.
explanations.textZh:
9. Bd3·卡罗-卡恩防御：经典变例

黑方几乎不变的 9...Bxd3 反应几乎是被迫的，尽管 9...Ngf6 甚至 9...e6 都被尝试过，但没有取得太大成功。

explanations.text:
10. Qxd3 · Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

Previously, all three main responses (...Ngf6, ...e6, ...Qc7) were thought to be equivalent, and often transposed to the same position with black castling queenside. Later development saw Black look at castling kingside, but for a while this fell out of favour as White found he could move his knight to e4 or e2, and advance g4, without needing to prepare Rg1. This extra tempo seems to threaten this line as a viable alternative for black, as white can win the race between the white kingside and black queenside attacks. More recent theory, however, has seen Black resurrect ...e6, quite often not castling at all, while the other alternatives remain out of favour.
explanations.textEn:
10. Qxd3 · Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

Later development saw Black look at castling kingside, but for a while this fell out of favour as White found he could move his knight to e4 or e2, and advance g4, without needing to prepare Rg1. This extra tempo seems to threaten this line as a viable alternative for black, as white can win the race between the white kingside and black queenside attacks. More recent theory, however, has seen Black resurrect ...e6, quite often not castling at all, while the other alternatives remain out of favour.
explanations.textZh:
10.Qxd3·卡罗-卡恩防御：经典变例

以前，所有三个主要响应（...Ngf6、...e6、...Qc7）被认为是等效的，并且经常与黑色易位后侧转移到相同的位置。后来的发展中，黑方开始考虑王翼易位，但有一段时间，这种做法失宠了，因为白方发现他可以将他的马移动到 e4 或 e2，并推进 g4，而无需准备 Rg1。这种额外的节奏似乎威胁到这条线作为黑棋的可行替代方案，因为白棋可以赢得白棋王翼和黑棋后翼攻击之间的比赛。然而，最近的理论已经看到黑方复活...e6，通常根本不进行王位易位，而其他选择仍然不受欢迎。

explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

With this move, black develops a piece, prepares possible queenside castling, and prevents the white bishop from coming to f4, which could be problematic for black's king should he castle long. White's two main options from here include:

11. Bd2 - The standard, main line move.

11. Rh4!? - A less common, aggressive move sometimes seen in professional play. White intends to swing the rook out to help pressure a black target.
explanations.textEn:

11. Rh4!? - A less common, aggressive move sometimes seen in professional play. White intends to swing the rook out to help pressure a black target.
explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩防御:经典变式

通过这一着棋，黑方发展出一颗棋子，准备可能的后侧易位，并阻止白方主教来到f4，如果黑方国王长期城堡，这可能会给他带来麻烦。白方的两个主要选择包括：

11. Bd2 - 标准的主线移动。

11.Rh4！？ - 职业比赛中有时会出现的不太常见的攻击性举动。白棋打算将车摆出以帮助向黑棋目标施压。

explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

11. Bf4 is the most challenging response when faced with modern Black theory where Black does not castle queenside. In earlier theory, when Black planned to castle queenside, Bd2 was almost equivalent. The other alternatives offer little for White.
explanations.textEn:
Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

11. Bf4 is the most challenging response when faced with modern Black theory where Black does not castle queenside. In earlier theory, when Black planned to castle queenside, Bd2 was almost equivalent. The other alternatives offer little for White.
explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩防御:经典变式

11. 当面对现代黑理论时，Bf4 是最具挑战性的反应，其中黑不占据后侧。在早期的理论中，当黑方计划在后翼筑垒时，Bd2 几乎是等价的。其他选择对白棋来说几乎没有什么帮助。

explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

Still the main line. White prepares for queenside castling. Since we have played h2-h4-h5 before, it makes sense to launch a pawn storm on the kingside.

Black should continue with his development with moves like 11...Ngf6 or 11...Be7. After that, kingside castling is the only option. This leads to an intense battle later, while both side try to push their pawns to the enemy king's territory.

To avoid this, Black can try to castle on queenside with 11...Qc7 to control the b8-h2 diagonal, follow with 12...O-O-O.
explanations.textEn:
Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

To avoid this, Black can try to castle on queenside with 11...Qc7 to control the b8-h2 diagonal, follow with 12...O-O-O.

卡罗-卡恩防御:经典变式

还是主线。白方准备后侧易位。由于我们之前玩过h2-h4-h5，所以在王翼发起典当风暴是有道理的。

黑棋应该继续他的发展，走 11...Ngf6 或 11...Be7。此后，王侧易位是唯一的选择。这导致了随后的激烈战斗，双方都试图将自己的棋子推向敌方国王的领土。

为了避免这种情况，黑方可以尝试用 11...Qc7 占据后侧以控制 b8-h2 对角线，然后用 12...O-O-O。

explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Defence:Classical Variation

This line aims to avoid the main one 11...Ngf6 12.O-O Be7 12.Kb1 O-O 13.Ne2, when White and Black castle on the opposite side. Black will likely queenside castle on the next move.

Nevertheless, White still can continue with the idea by playing 12.O-O.
explanations.textEn:

explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩防御:经典变式

这条线的目的是避免主要的11...Ngf6 12.O-O Be7 12.Kb1 O-O 13.Ne2，当白黑城堡在对面时。下一步黑棋很可能会在后侧城堡。

尽管如此，白棋仍然可以继续这个想法，下12.O-O。

explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Defence: Classical Variation

A flexible move, since there are chances for Black to castle on both sides. Most of the time, White will play 12. O-O-O.
explanations.textEn:

explanations.textZh:

这是一个灵活的走法，因为黑方都有机会在两边筑垒。大多数时候，白棋会下12.O-O-O。

explanations.text:

Black is able to castle in the next two moves, either with 12...Bd6 13...O-O (12...Be7 is the same, since White will play 13. Ne2 anyway), or 12...Qc7 13...O-O-O.

The main line involves kingside castling.

explanations.text:

Black prepares to castle on kingside with 13...O-O. White's most popular move is the prophylactic 13.Kb1, while other options include 13.Ne4 and 13.Qe2, continuing operations in the centre.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...Bf5/5. Ng5/5...Bg6/6. N1f3
explanations.text: White plays Nf3 and is about to counterattack. However, black rarely understands and notices it. There are a few popular replies to this, but black usually responds with h6, trying to kick out the knight, who's been a pain in the neck for a while.
explanations.textEn: White plays Nf3 and is about to counterattack. However, black rarely understands and notices it. There are a few popular replies to this, but black usually responds with h6, trying to kick out the knight, who's been a pain in the neck for a while.
explanations.textZh: 白棋下Nf3，即将反击。然而，黑色却很少理解和注意到这一点。对此有一些受欢迎的回复，但黑棋通常会用 h6 来回应，试图踢掉马，后者已经让马脖子痛了一段时间了。

explanations.text:
7. Ne6

Like the Alien Gambit, the Martian Gambit leads to an interesting and very exciting game. White plays Ne6, which is considered a blunder by Stockfish. However, in a real game, the move does pretty well. It ruins the kingside, doubles Black's pawns, and what is most important, helps the knight on f3 to deploy on e5 and control king's escape squares. But don't fret, Black has various responses to this gambit.
explanations.textEn:
7. Ne6

Like the Alien Gambit, the Martian Gambit leads to an interesting and very exciting game. White plays Ne6, which is considered a blunder by Stockfish. However, in a real game, the move does pretty well. It ruins the kingside, doubles Black's pawns, and what is most important, helps the knight on f3 to deploy on e5 and control king's escape squares. But don't fret, Black has various responses to this gambit.
explanations.textZh:
7.Ne6

与外星人开局一样，火星开局也带来了一场有趣且非常令人兴奋的游戏。白棋下Ne6，这被Stockfish认为是一个错误。然而，在真正的游戏中，这一举动表现得相当不错。它破坏了王翼，使黑方兵加倍，最重要的是，帮助f3上的马部署在e5上并控制国王的逃生方。但别担心，黑方对此策略有多种反应。

explanations.text: Knight lands on e5, controlling black king's escape squares. Because of doubled pawns, black side has turned into bipolar world - Queenside and Kingside, when the last one has been ruined. Best response as black would be Be4, but the most popular is Bf7?, which at the first sight helps to defend the king, but later causes only more problems. The main counterattack for white is usually either Bc4, but sometimes you can attack right after that with Qh5+.
explanations.textEn: Knight lands on e5, controlling black king's escape squares. Because of doubled pawns, black side has turned into bipolar world - Queenside and Kingside, when the last one has been ruined. Best response as black would be Be4, but the most popular is Bf7?, which at the first sight helps to defend the king, but later causes only more problems. The main counterattack for white is usually either Bc4, but sometimes you can attack right after that with Qh5+.
explanations.textZh: Knight 降落在 e5，控制黑王的逃生方格。由于双兵的缘故，黑方变成了两极世界——后侧和王侧，而最后一个已经被毁掉了。黑色的最佳反应是 Be4，但最受欢迎的是 Bf7？，乍一看有助于捍卫国王，但后来只会造成更多问题。白棋的主要反击通常是Bc4，但有时你可以在Bc4之后立即进攻Qh5+。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...e5
explanations.text:
Caro-Kann

A rarely seen move as it gives up a pawn for the idea of 5. dxe5 Qxd1+ 6. Kxd1 where White has lost castling rights. However, the simple 5. Nf3 gives white a lead in development and an advantage.
explanations.textEn:
Caro-Kann

A rarely seen move as it gives up a pawn for the idea of 5. dxe5 Qxd1+ 6. Kxd1 where White has lost castling rights. However, the simple 5. Nf3 gives white a lead in development and an advantage.
explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩

这是一个罕见的举动，因为它放弃了棋子，换取 5. dxe5 Qxd1+ 6. Kxd1 的想法，其中白方失去了易位权。然而，简单的 5.Nf3 使白色在发展上处于领先地位并具有优势。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...e6
explanations.text:
Caro-Kann

A rarely seen move as it blocks the Bc8 with the idea of letting the Bf8 and the Qd8 out. However, the simple 5. Nf3 gives White a development lead and an advantage.
explanations.textEn:
Caro-Kann

A rarely seen move as it blocks the Bc8 with the idea of letting the Bf8 and the Qd8 out. However, the simple 5. Nf3 gives White a development lead and an advantage.
explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩

这是一个罕见的举动，因为它阻挡了 Bc8，同时让 Bf8 和 Qd8 出局。然而，简单的 5.Nf3 给白方带来了发展领先和优势。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...f6
explanations.text:
Caro-Kann f6

This has been tried quite a few times, but chances of success are low.

Epilogue

The f6 Caro-Kann is a rare line that weakens the kingside and hinders the development of the king's knight, but prepares an e5 push.
explanations.textEn:
Caro-Kann f6

This has been tried quite a few times, but chances of success are low.

Epilogue

The f6 Caro-Kann is a rare line that weakens the kingside and hinders the development of the king's knight, but prepares an e5 push.
explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩 f6

这种方法已经尝试过很多次了，但成功的机会很小。

尾声

f6卡罗-卡恩是一条稀有的线路，削弱了王翼，阻碍了王骑士的发展，但准备了一个e5推。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...f6/5. Ng3
explanations.text:
Caro-Kann f6

This refutes the f6 line.

Epilogue

Ng3 is an interesting but important move that allows the e5 pawn push, but gains a huge lead in development after 5...e5 6. Nf3.
explanations.textEn:
Caro-Kann f6

This refutes the f6 line.

Epilogue

Ng3 is an interesting but important move that allows the e5 pawn push, but gains a huge lead in development after 5...e5 6. Nf3.
explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩 f6

这反驳了f6线。

尾声

Ng3 是一个有趣但重要的举动，它允许 e5 兵推，但在 5...e5 6. Nf3 之后在开发中获得巨大领先。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...g6
explanations.text:
Caro-Kann

A rarely seen move as it does not immediately confront the white knight on e4, with the idea of ...Bg7. However, the simple 5. Bc4 gives White a development lead and an advantage.
explanations.textEn:
Caro-Kann

A rarely seen move as it does not immediately confront the white knight on e4, with the idea of ...Bg7. However, the simple 5. Bc4 gives White a development lead and an advantage.
explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩

这是一个很少见的举动，因为它不会立即与 e4 上的白骑士对抗，并带有 ...Bg7 的想法。然而，简单的 5.Bc4 给白方带来了发展领先和优势。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...Nf6
explanations.text:
4...Nf6

The standard move in amateur play, offering a trade of knights.

This move challenges white's strong e4-knight but allows white to double black's pawns with the main move, 5. Nxf6+.

Other moves also exist. /5. Qd3/ defends the knight and sets up a trap, 5...Bf5?? 6. Nxf6+! exf6 7. Qxf5!.

/5. Bd3/ is the Alekhine Gambit. White gives up their d-pawn in exchange for development after 5...Qxd4 6. Nf3.

Some players have also tried /5. Ng5/, with the intention of entering the Alien Gambit, a dubious but scary knight sacrifice on f7, first played by Witty Alien, a streamer from Bulgaria.

/5. Ng3/ is not really a bad move, but allows Black to begin creating threats themselves with the move 5...h5.
explanations.textEn:

Other moves also exist. /5. Qd3/ defends the knight and sets up a trap, 5...Bf5?? 6. Nxf6+! exf6 7. Qxf5!.

/5. Bd3/ is the Alekhine Gambit. White gives up their d-pawn in exchange for development after 5...Qxd4 6. Nf3.

Some players have also tried /5. Ng5/, with the intention of entering the Alien Gambit, a dubious but scary knight sacrifice on f7, first played by Witty Alien, a streamer from Bulgaria.

/5. Ng3/ is not really a bad move, but allows Black to begin creating threats themselves with the move 5...h5.
explanations.textZh:
4...NF6

业余比赛中的标准动作，提供骑士交易。

这一步棋挑战了白棋强大的 e4-马，但允许白棋通过主要棋步 5.Nxf6+ 来加倍黑棋的棋子。

还存在其他动作。 /5。 Qd3/ 防守骑士并设置陷阱，5...Bf5？ 6.Nxf6+！ exf6 7.Qxf5！.

/5。 Bd3/ 是阿廖欣策略。白方放弃他们的 d 兵以换取 5...Qxd4 6. Nf3 后的发展。

也有玩家尝试过/5。 Ng5/，意图进入Alien Gambit，f7上的一个可疑但可怕的骑士牺牲，首先由来自保加利亚的主播Witty Alien扮演。

/5。 Ng3/ 实际上并不是一个糟糕的棋步，但允许黑方开始通过棋步 5...h5 制造威胁。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...Nf6/5. Qd3
explanations.text:
Caro–Kann Defence

5. Qd3

This move looks odd, but sets a trap and is an interesting way to avoid theory. It is a top engine choice and allows Black to blunder 5...Bf5??, which loses a piece after 6. Nxf6+.

The best continuation is 5...Nbd7 6. Nf3 Nxe4 7. Qxe4, which enters a position that is more commonly reached from the Two Knights Attack.

Richard Réti played this move against Savielly Tartakower in 1910. The game continued with 5...e5? 6. dxe5 Qa5+ 7. Bd2 Qxe5 8. O-O-O! Nxe4?? 9. Qd8+!! Kxd8 10. Bg5+ Kc7 11. Bd8#.
explanations.textEn:
Caro–Kann Defence

5. Qd3

This move looks odd, but sets a trap and is an interesting way to avoid theory. It is a top engine choice and allows Black to blunder 5...Bf5??, which loses a piece after 6. Nxf6+.

The best continuation is 5...Nbd7 6. Nf3 Nxe4 7. Qxe4, which enters a position that is more commonly reached from the Two Knights Attack.

Richard Réti played this move against Savielly Tartakower in 1910. The game continued with 5...e5? 6. dxe5 Qa5+ 7. Bd2 Qxe5 8. O-O-O! Nxe4?? 9. Qd8+!! Kxd8 10. Bg5+ Kc7 11. Bd8#.
explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩防御

5.Qd3

这一举动看起来很奇怪，但却设置了一个陷阱，并且是避免理论的有趣方式。这是一个顶级的引擎选择，让黑方犯下 5...Bf5?? 错误，在 6. Nxf6+ 后丢掉了一颗棋子。

最好的延续是 5...Nbd7 6. Nf3 Nxe4 7. Qxe4，它进入了两骑士攻击更常见的位置。

理查德·雷蒂 (Richard Réti) 在 1910 年对萨维利·塔塔科维尔 (Savielly Tartakower) 下过这手棋。比赛继续进行，出 5...e5？ 6. dxe5 Qa5+ 7. Bd2 Qxe5 8. O-O-O！恩克斯4？？ 9.Qd8+！！ Kxd8 10.Bg5+ Kc7 11.Bd8#。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...Nf6/5. Qd3/5...e5
explanations.text:
5...e5?

This move appears to completely free Black's position and equalize the game, but it really loses time in a wide open position and falls behind in development. This puts Black in a critical position. This also gives black an opportunity to fall for a brilliant mating attack that was played in the game Reti-Tartakower, 1910. It is rarely a good idea to open up the position if you are behind in development, and Black is doing just this here.

Better is to trade knights on e4 and then move the other knight to d7. He can then play for the freeing...c5, ...e5, or attack the queen with ...Nf6 After this mistake, black loses time and development.

Reti-Tartakower, 1910

The game continued: 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Nf6 5. Qd3 e5? 6. dxe5 Qa5+ 7. Bd2 Qxe5 8. 0-0-0! (Sacrificing a piece to get at the unprotected black king). 8...Nxe4?? (This gets mated. However, he was so far behind in development that he already had a poor position. 8...Qxe4 loses the queen to 10.Re1) 9. Qd8+!! Kxd8 10. Bg5+ Kc7 (10...Ke8 Rd8#) 11. Bd8# A remarkable finish!

The final position is given in the second diagram below. According to chessgames.com, the game Reti-Tartakower, 1910 was the "Game of the day" on Jan 16 2005 and the "Sucker Punch".

explanations.textZh:
5...e5？

这步棋看似完全解放了黑棋的位置，扳平了棋局，但实则在大空位置上浪费了时间，发展落后。这使黑方处于关键位置。这也给黑方提供了一个机会，让其陷入1910年Reti-Tartakower游戏中的精彩交配攻击。如果您在发展中落后，那么打开位置很少是一个好主意，而黑方在这里正是这样做的。

更好的办法是在 e4 上交易骑士，然后将另一个骑士移至 d7。然后他可以发挥自由...c5，...e5，或用...Nf6 攻击皇后。在这个错误之后，黑色失去了时间和发展。

雷蒂-塔塔科韦尔，1910

游戏继续： 1. e4 c6 2. d4 d5 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Nf6 5. Qd3 e5？ 6. dxe5 Qa5+ 7. Bd2 Qxe5 8. 0-0-0！ （牺牲一块棋子来攻击未受保护的黑王）。 8...Nxe4？？ （这会交配。但是，他在发展方面远远落后，以至于他的位置已经很差了。8...Qxe4将女王输给了10.Re1） 9. Qd8+！ Kxd8 10. Bg5+ Kc7 (10...Ke8 Rd8#) 11. Bd8# 出色的完成！

最终位置如下第二张图所示。据 chessgames.com 称，Reti-Tartakower, 1910 游戏是 2005 年 1 月 16 日的“今日游戏”和“Sucker Punch”。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...Nf6/5. Nxf6/5...exf6
explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Defence:Korchnoi Variation

Viktor Korchnoi has played 5...exf6 many times (including in a world championship match). 5...exf6 is sounder than 5...gxf6!? of the Bronstein-Larsen Variation and offers Black rapid development.
explanations.textEn:
Caro-Kann Defence:Korchnoi Variation

Viktor Korchnoi has played 5...exf6 many times (including in a world championship match). 5...exf6 is sounder than 5...gxf6!? of the Bronstein-Larsen Variation and offers Black rapid development.
explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩防御:科尔奇诺伊变例

Viktor Korchnoi 曾多次玩过 5...exf6（包括在世界冠军赛中）。 5...exf6 比 5...gxf6 更健全！？布朗斯坦-拉森变例并提供了黑色的快速发展。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...Nf6/5. Nxf6/5...gxf6
explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Defence:Bronstein-Larsen Variation

Black has voluntarily opted for an inferior kingside pawn structure, an isolated h-pawn, and a practical necessity of castling queenside, but also has some compensation in the form of the open g-file for the rook and unusually active play for the Caro-Kann. It is generally considered somewhat more unsound than 5...exf6, but former top-10 player Bent Larsen employed it with some success during the 1970s. Black has more control of the center and a possible ...Bh6 later on.
explanations.textEn:
Caro-Kann Defence:Bronstein-Larsen Variation

Black has voluntarily opted for an inferior kingside pawn structure, an isolated h-pawn, and a practical necessity of castling queenside, but also has some compensation in the form of the open g-file for the rook and unusually active play for the Caro-Kann. It is generally considered somewhat more unsound than 5...exf6, but former top-10 player Bent Larsen employed it with some success during the 1970s. Black has more control of the center and a possible ...Bh6 later on.
explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩防御:布朗斯坦-拉森变例

黑方自愿选择了较差的王翼兵结构、孤立的 h 兵以及后翼易位的实际需要，但也以车的开放 G 档和卡罗-卡恩异常活跃的方式进行了一些补偿。人们普遍认为它比 5...exf6 更不健全，但前 10 名选手 Bent Larsen 在 1970 年代使用它并取得了一些成功。黑方对中心有更多的控制权，并且稍后可能有...Bh6。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...Nf6/5. Ng5
explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Defense, Classical Variation: 5. Ng5?

This move is not good for White; moving an already-developed piece, the queen knight, for a third time. Black already has an advantage.

However, many players with White, especially followers of Witty Alien or even Eric Rosen, usually have a sneaky idea with this move; after the natural 5...h6 by Black, White intends to sacrifice the knight for the f7 pawn with 6. Nxf7??, entering the dubious but incredibly scary Alien Gambit.
explanations.textEn:
Caro-Kann Defense, Classical Variation: 5. Ng5?

This move is not good for White; moving an already-developed piece, the queen knight, for a third time. Black already has an advantage.

However, many players with White, especially followers of Witty Alien or even Eric Rosen, usually have a sneaky idea with this move; after the natural 5...h6 by Black, White intends to sacrifice the knight for the f7 pawn with 6. Nxf7??, entering the dubious but incredibly scary Alien Gambit.
explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩防御，经典变体：5. Ng5？

这步棋对白方不利；第三次移动已经开发的棋子——女王骑士。黑棋已经占据优势。

然而，许多白棋棋手，尤其是机智外星人甚至埃里克·罗森的追随者，通常对这手棋有一个偷偷摸摸的想法；在黑方天然 5...h6 之后，白方打算用 6.Nxf7?? 牺牲马来换取 f7 兵，进入可疑但令人难以置信的可怕外星人开局。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...Nf6/5. Ng5/5...h6
explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Defense, Classical Variation: 5...h6

Black naturally looks to kick the knight away with h6. Best in this position is 6. N5f3, retreating the knight to safety. However, this move of 5...h6 actually encourages many players, especially followers of chess content creator Witty Alien, to play 6. Nxf7??, the dubious but scary Alien Gambit.
explanations.textEn:
Caro-Kann Defense, Classical Variation: 5...h6

Black naturally looks to kick the knight away with h6. Best in this position is 6. N5f3, retreating the knight to safety. However, this move of 5...h6 actually encourages many players, especially followers of chess content creator Witty Alien, to play 6. Nxf7??, the dubious but scary Alien Gambit.
explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩防御，经典变体：5...h6

黑方自然会用 h6 踢走马。这个位置最好的是6.N5f3，将骑士撤退到安全的地方。然而，5...h6 的这一步实际上鼓励了许多玩家，尤其是国际象棋内容创作者 Witty Alien 的追随者，去玩 6.Nxf7??，即可疑但可怕的外星人开局。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...Nf6/5. Ng5/5...h6/6. Nxf7
explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Defense: Alien Gambit

White grabs the f7 pawn with 6. Nxf7?, entering the dubious but incredibly scary Alien Gambit, popularized by YouTuber Witty Alien! This gambit is losing for White and can be punished with careful play; as such, it is mostly used in Bullet and Blitz.

The purpose of this move is to ruin Black's kingside structure by creating several light-squared holes in Black's kingside; force the Black king to recapture, giving up castling rights; and take Black out of their comfort zone, since most Caro-Kann players are mostly used to slow, positional grinds rather than tactical skirmishes. The Alien Gambit is an attack on Black's weak light squares on the kingside. When the knight grabs the f7 pawn, Black has several light-squared holes on e6 and g6 which can quickly be pounced on by White's pieces, often leading to checkmate for White on these very squares.

Black has two approaches to send the aliens back to their desolate sector of the cosmos: one is to attack White's weak dark squares with c5, Nc6, and so on; another is to defend the light squares with Be6, develop the knight with Nbd7, and counterattack on the light squares. Both of these approaches can even be combined seamlessly, leading to the aliens' demise.

Black must respect White's attack on the light squares. After Nxf7? Kxf7 Nf3 Bg4?? (which is the most common response), White can play Ne5! and win the knight back with a monstrous attack on the light squares to follow.

explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩防御：外星人策略

白棋用 6. Nxf7? 抓住 f7 棋子，进入可疑但极其可怕的外星人开局，由 YouTuber Witty Alien 推广！这种策略对白方来说是失败的，谨慎行事可能会受到惩罚；因此，它主要用于《Bullet》和《Blitz》。

此举的目的是通过在黑方王翼上制造几个浅方形孔来破坏黑方王翼结构；迫使黑王夺回，放弃王位继承权；并将布莱克带出他们的舒适区，因为大多数卡罗-卡恩棋手大多习惯于缓慢的位置磨练，而不是战术小冲突。异形开局是对王侧黑方弱光方格的攻击。当马吃掉f7兵时，黑方在e6和g6上有几个浅方孔，白方的棋子可以迅速扑向这些孔，通常会导致白方在这些方格上将死。

黑方有两种方法可以将外星人送回他们在宇宙中的荒凉区域：一是用c5、Nc6等攻击白方的弱暗方格；二是用c5、Nc6等攻击白方的弱暗方格；二是用c5、Nc6等攻击白方的弱暗方格。另一种是Be6防守光格，Nbd7发育骑士，反攻光格。这两种方法甚至可以无缝结合，导致外星人的灭亡。

黑方必须尊重白方对浅色方格的攻击。 Nxf7之后？ Kxf7 Nf3 Bg4?? （这是最常见的反应），白棋可以下Ne5！并通过对随后的光方块进行可怕的攻击来赢回骑士。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Nxe4/4...h6
explanations.text:
4...h6 · Finnish variation

Black prepares an escape square for their c-bishop's later use. This is usually perceived as passive and is thus rarely seen at higher levels.

5. Nf3 is the main move. White develops their knight to its more natural square, ignoring Black's strange pawn move h6.

5. Bc4 is another good move, developing the bishop to an active square with good scope, and maybe even preparing Bxf7+ sacrifices to exploit the weakened kingside h6 caused.

5. Ng3 is playable. White stops the bishop from coming to f5 so it doesn't gain tempo on the knight nor does it get a chance to go to the newly opened h7.

explanations.textZh:
4...h6 · 芬兰变体

黑方准备了一个逃生方格供他们的c主教稍后使用。这通常被认为是被动的，因此很少在更高级别上看到。

5. Nf3是主招。白棋将他们的马发展到更自然的方格，忽略了黑棋奇怪的棋子h6。

5. Bc4是另一个好棋，将主教发展为具有良好范围的活跃方阵，甚至可能准备Bxf7+牺牲以利用王翼h6造成的削弱。

5.NG3可以玩。白方阻止主教来到f5，这样它就不会在马身上获得节奏，也没有机会去新开的h7。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nc3/3...dxe4/4. Bc4
explanations.text:
Von Hennig Gambit

4. Bc4

White is playing in a way reminiscent of the Blackmar-Diemer gambit, and indeed the popular lines fall into that trend. Common responses include 4...Nf6 and 4...Bf5, the latter of which transposes to the main line of the former after 5. f3 exf3 6. Nxf3 Nf6. The main line after 4...Nf6 is 5. f3 exf3 Nxf3 (5...Bf5 is another line, best responded to with 6. fxe4 Nxe4 7. Qf3). In this position the main moves are 6...Bf5, 6...Bg4, and 6...e6. 6...Bg4 falls into a trap after 7. Bxf7+ Kxf7 8. Ne5+ winning a piece or the slightly worse 7. Ne5, where Bxd1 hangs Bxf7# and all other moves besides Be6 and Qc8 nearly instantly lose, while those 2 moves still leave white with a nice advantage. 6...e6 is played the most like a Blackmar-Diemer with ideas of O-O, Qe1-h4, and Bd3. 6...Bf5 is the main line, which is followed up with 7. O-O e6 8. Ng5 Bg6 (preventing Rxf5 where recaptures leads to a fork), where White's options are the calm 9. Ne2 and 9. Bf4 or the wild 9. Bxe6 fxe6 10. Nxe6, which will force Black to either give up their queen or weather an incredibly dangerous attack. Another possible response is 4...b5, which often ends up following a similar line to the others after 5. Bb3.

explanations.textZh:
冯·亨尼格·甘比特

4.BC4

白方的下棋方式让人想起布莱克马尔-迪默策略，事实上，流行的台词也属于这种趋势。常见的响应包括 4...Nf6 和 4...Bf5，后者在 5. f3 exf3 6. Nxf3 Nf6 之后转置到前者的主线。 4...Nf6 之后的主线是 5.f3 exf3 Nxf3（5...Bf5 是另一条线，最好用 6.fxe4 Nxe4 7.Qf3 来回应）。在这个位置上，主要动作是 6...Bf5、6...Bg4 和 6...e6。 6...Bg4 在 7. Bxf7+ Kxf7 8. Ne5+ 赢得棋子或稍差的 7. Ne5 后陷入陷阱，其中 Bxd1 挂 Bxf7#，除了 Be6 和 Qc8 之外的所有其他棋步几乎立即失败，而这 2 个棋步仍然让白棋具有很大的优势。 6...e6 的演奏方式最像 Blackmar-Diemer，具有 O-O、Qe1-h4 和 Bd3 的想法。 6...Bf5 是主线，随后是 7. O-O e6 8. Ng5 Bg6（防止 Rxf5 夺回导致分叉），其中白方的选择是平静的 9. Ne2 和 9. Bf4 或狂野的 9. Bxe6 fxe6 10. Nxe6，这将迫使黑方要么放弃他们的皇后，要么经受极其危险的攻击。另一种可能的响应是 4...b5，它通常最终会遵循与 5.Bb3 之后的其他响应类似的路线。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nd2
explanations.text:
3. Nd2 · Modern variation

White prepares to recapture on e4 with their knight while keeping the option of c3.

This move is intended to avoid the Gurgenidze system, 3. Nc3 g6, where Black will fianchetto their king's side bishop.

Here, 3...g6 may be answered 4. c3, mitigating the pressure Black's bishop will be able to impose on the long diagonal.

This encourages the main move, 3...dxe4, and after 4. Nxe4 this transposes into the same line as if 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 had been played.

A minor sideline is /3...Qb6/, the Edinburgh Variation. Black develops their queen and attacks the undefended d4 pawn, though this can be answered with 4. c3.
explanations.textEn:
3. Nd2 · Modern variation

Here, 3...g6 may be answered 4. c3, mitigating the pressure Black's bishop will be able to impose on the long diagonal.

This encourages the main move, 3...dxe4, and after 4. Nxe4 this transposes into the same line as if 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 had been played.

explanations.textZh:
3. Nd2·现代变异

白方准备用马夺回 e4，同时保留 c3 的选择。

此举是为了避免古尔根尼泽系统，3. Nc3 g6，其中黑方将先手攻击他们的王方主教。

这里，3...g6 可能会被回答 4.c3，减轻黑方主教将能够施加在长对角线上的压力。

这鼓励了主要动作 3...dxe4，并且在 4. Nxe4 之后，这会转置到同一行，就像已经玩了 3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 一样。

一个次要的边线是/3...Qb6/，爱丁堡变奏曲。黑方展开后并攻击不设防的 d4 兵，尽管这可以用 4. c3 来回答。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. Nd2/3...Qb6
explanations.text:
3...Qb6 · Edinburgh variation

This is a minor sideline of 3. Nd2, where Black attacks the undefended d4 pawn.

4. c3 is the main and best move. White defends their pawn with another pawn, forming a solid b2-c3-d4 pawn chain.

4. Ngf3 is another good move. White develops their g-knight to its most active square and defends the d-pawn.
explanations.textEn:
3...Qb6 · Edinburgh variation

This is a minor sideline of 3. Nd2, where Black attacks the undefended d4 pawn.

4. c3 is the main and best move. White defends their pawn with another pawn, forming a solid b2-c3-d4 pawn chain.

4. Ngf3 is another good move. White develops their g-knight to its most active square and defends the d-pawn.
explanations.textZh:
3...Qb6 · 爱丁堡变奏

这是 3.Nd2 的次要边线，黑方攻击不设防的 d4 兵。

4. c3是主要也是最好的棋步。白棋用另一个棋子保卫自己的棋子，形成一条坚固的 b2-c3-d4 棋子链。

4. Ngf3 是另一个好举措。白方将 G 型马发展到最活跃的方格并防守 d 型兵。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. exd5
explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Defence: Exchange Variation

White exchanges on d5, and black almost always responds with cxd5. This forms opposite-wing majorities. This usually leads to either the Panov-Botvinnik Attack after 4.c4, or the main line Exchange after 4. Bd3.
explanations.textEn:
Caro-Kann Defence: Exchange Variation

White exchanges on d5, and black almost always responds with cxd5. This forms opposite-wing majorities. This usually leads to either the Panov-Botvinnik Attack after 4.c4, or the main line Exchange after 4. Bd3.
explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩防御：交换变化

白棋在 d5 上交换，黑棋几乎总是用 cxd5 响应。这形成了反对派的多数。这通常会导致 4.c4 之后的 Panov-Botvinnik Attack，或者 4.Bd3 之后的主线交换。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. exd5/3...cxd5
explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Defence: Exchange Variation

Main line: 4. Bd3

The main line begins with 4. Bd3 (to prevent ...Bf5 while still developing) 4...Nc6 5. c3 Nf6 6. Bf4 Bg4 7. Qb3. This line was once considered harmless before being used by Bobby Fischer to defeat Tigran Petrosian in 1970. The pawn structure resembles a Carlsbad structure with reversed colours, so some of the strategic ideas are analogous to the Queen's Gambit Declined, Exchange Variation (1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. cxd5 exd5).

c4. Panov-Botvinnik Attack

The Panov-Botvinnik attack is a sharp alternative for white, with white often accepting long-term weaknesses for a strong direct attack.

Note that 4. Nc3?! would be a poor move due to the fact that the knight doesn't do much. e4 is poison, while e6 will turn d5 into a rock. Therefore, c4 followed by Nc3 is far better since then, there would be pressure on d5.

explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩防御：交换变化

主线：4.Bd3

主线以 4. Bd3 开始（防止仍在发育中的 ...Bf5）4...Nc6 5. c3 Nf6 6. Bf4 Bg4 7. Qb3。这条线在1970年被鲍比·费舍尔（Bobby Fischer）用来击败蒂格兰·彼得罗相（Tigran Petrosian）之前曾被认为是无害的。棋子结构类似于带有相反颜色的卡尔斯巴德结构，因此一些战略思想类似于后弃兵，交换变化（1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. cxd5 exd5）。

c4.帕诺夫-鲍特维尼克攻击

帕诺夫-鲍特维尼克攻击是白棋的一个尖锐的替代方案，白棋经常接受长期的弱点，进行强有力的直接攻击。

注意4.NC3？！由于骑士没有做太多事情，因此这将是一个糟糕的举动。 e4是毒药，而e6会将d5变成石头。因此，c4之后的Nc3要好得多，之后d5就会有压力。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. exd5/3...cxd5/4. c4
explanations.text:
4. c4 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

4... Nf6 is almost always played, although 4... e6, previously regarded as having a very poor record, as well as 4... g6, among others, appear to be playable for Black.
explanations.textEn:
4. c4 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

4... Nf6 is almost always played, although 4... e6, previously regarded as having a very poor record, as well as 4... g6, among others, appear to be playable for Black.
explanations.textZh:
4. c4·卡罗-卡恩·帕诺夫-鲍特维尼克攻击

4... Nf6 几乎总是被使用，尽管 4... e6（以前被认为具有非常差的记录）以及 4... g6 等似乎可以用于黑方。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. exd5/3...cxd5/4. c4/4...Nf6
explanations.text:
4... Nf6 · Caro-Kann, Panov-Botvinnik Attack

The usual response will be 5. Nc3, to continue to place pressure on white's d5 pawn. White aims for direct pressure, often at the expense of long-term structural weaknesses.
explanations.textEn:
4... Nf6 · Caro-Kann, Panov-Botvinnik Attack

The usual response will be 5. Nc3, to continue to place pressure on white's d5 pawn. White aims for direct pressure, often at the expense of long-term structural weaknesses.
explanations.textZh:
4... Nf6 · 卡罗-卡恩、帕诺夫-鲍特维尼克攻击

通常的反应是5.NC3，继续对白方的d5兵施加压力。怀特的目标是直接施压，通常以牺牲长期的结构性弱点为代价。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. exd5/3...cxd5/4. c4/4...Nf6/5. Nc3
explanations.text:
5. Nc3 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

With white putting pressure on the d5 pawn, 5... e6 is a solid response. 5... Nc6 is more ambitious, but more risky. Black can also fianchetto the bishop with 5... g6.
explanations.textEn:
5. Nc3 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

With white putting pressure on the d5 pawn, 5... e6 is a solid response. 5... Nc6 is more ambitious, but more risky. Black can also fianchetto the bishop with 5... g6.
explanations.textZh:
5. Nc3·卡罗-卡恩·帕诺夫-博特维尼克攻击

白棋对 d5 兵施加压力，5...e6 是一个可靠的回应。 5...NC6 更加雄心勃勃，但风险也更大。黑方还可以用 5...g6 向主教发起攻击。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. exd5/3...cxd5/4. c4/4...Nf6/5. Nc3/5...Nc6
explanations.text:
5... Nc6 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

5... Nc6 is regarded as the most ambitious, but also risky, response for black. White usually responds with either 6. Nf3 or 6. Bg5 here. 6. cxd5 is also sometimes played, but black can prevent it transposing into the 6. Nf3 line by playing 6... Bf5 instead, which prevents white's later Qb3 with N5b4, exposing white's weakness on c2.
explanations.textEn:
5... Nc6 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

5... Nc6 is regarded as the most ambitious, but also risky, response for black. White usually responds with either 6. Nf3 or 6. Bg5 here. 6. cxd5 is also sometimes played, but black can prevent it transposing into the 6. Nf3 line by playing 6... Bf5 instead, which prevents white's later Qb3 with N5b4, exposing white's weakness on c2.
explanations.textZh:
5... Nc6 · 卡罗-卡恩·帕诺夫-博特维尼克攻击

5...NC6 被认为是对黑色来说最雄心勃勃但也有风险的应对措施。白棋通常会用 6.Nf3 或 6.Bg5 来回应。 6. cxd5 有时也会下，但黑棋可以通过下 6...Bf5 来阻止它转入 6. Nf3 线，这可以防止白棋后来用 N5b4 下 Qb3，暴露白棋在 c2 上的弱点。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. exd5/3...cxd5/4. c4/4...Nf6/5. Nc3/5...Nc6/6. Bg5
explanations.text:
6. Bg5 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

With this move, White immediately threatens the d5 pawn. Here, Black can simply capture the c pawn with 6...dxc4, or defend the d pawn with 6...e6 or even the strange-looking but perfectly sound 6...Be6, when Black usually fianchettos the dark-squared bishop.
explanations.textEn:
6. Bg5 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

With this move, White immediately threatens the d5 pawn. Here, Black can simply capture the c pawn with 6...dxc4, or defend the d pawn with 6...e6 or even the strange-looking but perfectly sound 6...Be6, when Black usually fianchettos the dark-squared bishop.
explanations.textZh:
6. Bg5·卡罗-卡恩·帕诺夫-鲍特维尼克攻击

通过这一步棋，白棋立即威胁到了 d5 兵。在这里，黑方可以简单地用 6...dxc4 吃掉 c 兵，或者用 6...e6 保卫 d 兵，甚至用看起来奇怪但听起来很完美的 6...Be6，此时黑方通常会先杀暗方象。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. exd5/3...cxd5/4. c4/4...Nf6/5. Nc3/5...Nc6/6. Bg5/6...dxc4
explanations.text:
6... dxc5 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

6... dxc5 results in the classic isolated queen's pawn position. White usually recaptures the pawn, offering up the d pawn for a healthy lead in development, but can also push to d5, or develop the knight to f3.
explanations.textEn:
6... dxc5 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

6... dxc5 results in the classic isolated queen's pawn position. White usually recaptures the pawn, offering up the d pawn for a healthy lead in development, but can also push to d5, or develop the knight to f3.
explanations.textZh:
6... dxc5 · 卡罗-卡恩·帕诺夫-博特维尼克攻击

6... dxc5 导致经典的孤立后的棋子位置。白方通常会夺回棋子，提供 d 棋子以获得健康的领先发展，但也可以推至 d5，或将马发展至 f3。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. exd5/3...cxd5/4. c4/4...Nf6/5. Nc3/5...Nc6/6. Bg5/6...dxc4/7. Bxc4
explanations.text:
7. Bxc4 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

Following the capture, Black most frequently challenges the bishop with 7...h6, sending it to a weaker square, or activating Black's dark-squared bishop if the knight is captured. Alternatively, Black can simply capture the pawn on d4 directly, or activate the bishop directly with 7...e6.
explanations.textEn:
7. Bxc4 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

Following the capture, Black most frequently challenges the bishop with 7...h6, sending it to a weaker square, or activating Black's dark-squared bishop if the knight is captured. Alternatively, Black can simply capture the pawn on d4 directly, or activate the bishop directly with 7...e6.
explanations.textZh:
7. Bxc4·卡罗-卡恩·帕诺夫-博特维尼克攻击

俘获后，黑方最常用 7...h6 挑战主教，将其发送到较弱的方格，或者在马被俘获时激活黑方的暗方主教。或者，黑方可以直接吃掉 d4 上的棋子，或者直接用 7...e6 激活象。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. exd5/3...cxd5/4. c4/4...Nf6/5. Nc3/5...Nc6/6. Nf3
explanations.text:
6. Nf3 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

6. Nf3 is the main line for white, and black has a number of alternatives here. The more solid 6... e6, fianchettoing the bishop with 6... g6, or the main line, 6... Bg4, which leads to somewhat crazy positions that black can safely navigate if they know what they're doing.
explanations.textEn:
6. Nf3 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

6. Nf3 is the main line for white, and black has a number of alternatives here. The more solid 6... e6, fianchettoing the bishop with 6... g6, or the main line, 6... Bg4, which leads to somewhat crazy positions that black can safely navigate if they know what they're doing.
explanations.textZh:
6. Nf3·卡罗-卡恩·帕诺夫-鲍特维尼克攻击

6. Nf3是白方的主线，黑方这里有多种选择。更扎实的 6...e6，用 6...g6 或主线 6...Bg4 来攻击主教，这会导致有点疯狂的位置，如果黑方知道自己在做什么，就可以安全地导航。

explanations.text:
6... Bg4 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

White has their eye on the weak points in black's position, b7 and d5, and most commonly takes on d5 with the pawn here. However, 7. Be3, 7. Bg5, and 7. Be2 are also perfectly playable.
explanations.textEn:
6... Bg4 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

White has their eye on the weak points in black's position, b7 and d5, and most commonly takes on d5 with the pawn here. However, 7. Be3, 7. Bg5, and 7. Be2 are also perfectly playable.
explanations.textZh:
6... Bg4 · 卡罗-卡恩·帕诺夫-鲍特维尼克攻击

白棋着眼于黑棋的弱点，b7 和 d5，并且最常见的是在这里用棋子对抗 d5。不过7.Be3、7.Bg5、7.Be2也是可以完美玩的。

explanations.text:
7... Nxd5 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

White should play aggressively here, with 8. Qb3 being the key test. A passive move like 8. Be2 allows black to consolidate with a move such as 8... e6, and with the bishop outside the pawn chain, this is a pleasant isolated queen's pawn position for black.
explanations.textEn:
7... Nxd5 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

White should play aggressively here, with 8. Qb3 being the key test. A passive move like 8. Be2 allows black to consolidate with a move such as 8... e6, and with the bishop outside the pawn chain, this is a pleasant isolated queen's pawn position for black.
explanations.textZh:
7... Nxd5 · 卡罗-卡恩·帕诺夫-博特维尼克攻击

白棋在这里应该发挥侵略性，8.Qb3 是关键的考验。像 8.Be2 这样的被动棋可以让黑棋通过 8...e6 这样的棋来巩固，而主教在兵链之外，这对于黑棋来说是一个令人愉快的孤立后后兵位置。

explanations.text:
8. Qb3 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

White is creating threats, but black can create long-term weaknesses with 8... Bxf3. However, they will come under sustained pressure from white's attack.
explanations.textEn:
8. Qb3 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

White is creating threats, but black can create long-term weaknesses with 8... Bxf3. However, they will come under sustained pressure from white's attack.
explanations.textZh:
8. Qb3·卡罗-卡恩·帕诺夫-博特维尼克攻击

白棋正在制造威胁，但黑棋可以用 8...Bxf3 制造长期弱点。然而，他们将受到白棋攻击的持续压力。

explanations.text:
9. gxf3 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

White is committed to the attack, and must accept the doubled, isolated pawns. Beware the tempting 9. Qxb7, which loses on the spot to 9... Ndb4, and white's queen is trapped.
explanations.textEn:
9. gxf3 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

White is committed to the attack, and must accept the doubled, isolated pawns. Beware the tempting 9. Qxb7, which loses on the spot to 9... Ndb4, and white's queen is trapped.
explanations.textZh:
9. gxf3·卡罗-卡恩·帕诺夫-博特维尼克攻击

白棋致力于进攻，并且必须接受双倍的孤立棋子。当心诱人的 9.Qxb7，它当场输给 9...Ndb4，白后被困。

explanations.text:
9. gxf3 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

White now has a poor pawn structure, but also has numerous threats. Best here is to allow white to take the b7 pawn by defending the knight with 9... e6. 9... Nb6 is also an option, but 10. d5 creates many challenges for Black. Note that 9... Nxc3 is a mistake allowing both 10. bxc3 or even 10. Qxb7 with advantage for white.
explanations.textEn:
9. gxf3 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

White now has a poor pawn structure, but also has numerous threats. Best here is to allow white to take the b7 pawn by defending the knight with 9... e6. 9... Nb6 is also an option, but 10. d5 creates many challenges for Black. Note that 9... Nxc3 is a mistake allowing both 10. bxc3 or even 10. Qxb7 with advantage for white.
explanations.textZh:
9. gxf3·卡罗-卡恩·帕诺夫-博特维尼克攻击

白棋现在的棋子结构很差，但也有很多威胁。这里最好的办法是让白棋通过用 9...e6 防守马来拿走 b7 棋子。 9...Nb6 也是一种选择，但是 10.d5 给黑棋带来了很多挑战。请注意，9...Nxc3 是一个错误，允许 10.bxc3 甚至 10.Qxb7 都具有白色优势。

explanations.text:
9... e6 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

White has a poor pawn structure but strong pressure, and needs to force the issue. 10. Qxb7 is almost always played here.
explanations.textEn:
9... e6 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

White has a poor pawn structure but strong pressure, and needs to force the issue. 10. Qxb7 is almost always played here.
explanations.textZh:
9... e6 · 卡罗-卡恩·帕诺夫-鲍特维尼克攻击

白方棋子结构较差，但压力较大，需要强行下棋。 10. Qxb7几乎总是在这里演奏。

explanations.text:
10. Qxb7 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

The position looks threatening for Black, but with careful play they can come out of it unscathed. Here 10... Nxd4 is almost always played.
explanations.textEn:
10. Qxb7 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

The position looks threatening for Black, but with careful play they can come out of it unscathed. Here 10... Nxd4 is almost always played.
explanations.textZh:
10.Qxb7·卡罗-卡恩·帕诺夫-博特维尼克攻击

这个局面对黑棋来说看起来很有威胁，但只要小心行事，他们就可以毫发无伤地摆脱困境。这里 10...Nxd4 几乎总是被玩。

explanations.text:
10... Nxd4 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

White's damaged pawn structure means they should continue to press quickly. 11. Bb5+ is almost always played. 11. Nxd5 is the only other viable move, but if Black responds with 11... Qxd5, white has lost any initiative.
explanations.textEn:
10... Nxd4 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

White's damaged pawn structure means they should continue to press quickly. 11. Bb5+ is almost always played. 11. Nxd5 is the only other viable move, but if Black responds with 11... Qxd5, white has lost any initiative.
explanations.textZh:
10... Nxd4 · 卡罗-卡恩·帕诺夫-博特维尼克攻击

白方受损的棋子结构意味着他们应该继续快速施压。 11. 几乎总是演奏 Bb5+。 11. Nxd5 是唯一可行的棋步，但如果黑棋回应 11...Qxd5，白棋就失去了主动权。

explanations.text:
11... Nxb5 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

Following the capture, Black has two responses. Either recapture the knight directly with 12. Qxb5, or the more commonly played intermediate check, with 12. Qc6+, forcing the black king into the open.
explanations.textEn:
11... Nxb5 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

Following the capture, Black has two responses. Either recapture the knight directly with 12. Qxb5, or the more commonly played intermediate check, with 12. Qc6+, forcing the black king into the open.
explanations.textZh:
11... Nxb5 · 卡罗-卡恩·帕诺夫-博特维尼克攻击

吃子后，黑方有两种反应。要么直接用12.Qxb5夺回骑士，要么用更常见的中间检查，用12.Qc6+，迫使黑王进入空位。

explanations.text:
12... Ke7 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

Black's king will now come under sustained attack. White most commonly recaptures the knight with Qxb5, but there also exists the dramatic but perfectly sound piece sacrifice, Qc5+. Nxb5 is also played on occasion.
explanations.textEn:
12... Ke7 · Caro-Kann Panov-Botvinnik Attack

Black's king will now come under sustained attack. White most commonly recaptures the knight with Qxb5, but there also exists the dramatic but perfectly sound piece sacrifice, Qc5+. Nxb5 is also played on occasion.
explanations.textZh:
12...Ke7·卡罗-卡恩·帕诺夫-鲍特维尼克攻击

黑方国王现在将受到持续的攻击。白棋最常见的是用 Qxb5 夺回马，但也存在戏剧性但完美的棋子牺牲，Qc5+。有时也会演奏 Nxb5。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. exd5/3...cxd5/4. Bd3/4...Nc6
explanations.text:
4. Nc6

Black attacks the d-pawn. 5. c3 is probably the most sound response, and the most-commonly played.

Black is fine after 5. Nf3 or 5. Be3, although 5. Nf3 has a poor record and allows Black to play 5...Bg4, freeing the weak light-squared bishop, and White has to play 6. c3 anyway. 5. Ne2 at least prevents it.
explanations.textEn:
4. Nc6

Black attacks the d-pawn. 5. c3 is probably the most sound response, and the most-commonly played.

Black is fine after 5. Nf3 or 5. Be3, although 5. Nf3 has a poor record and allows Black to play 5...Bg4, freeing the weak light-squared bishop, and White has to play 6. c3 anyway. 5. Ne2 at least prevents it.
explanations.textZh:
4.NC6

黑方攻击 D 兵。 5. c3 可能是最响亮的响应，也是最常演奏的。

黑方在 5.Nf3 或 5.Be3 之后就可以了，尽管 5.Nf3 战绩不佳，允许黑方下 5...Bg4，解放了弱光方象，而白方无论如何也必须下 6.c3。 5. Ne2至少可以阻止它。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. exd5/3...cxd5/4. Bd3/4...Nc6/5. c3
explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Exchange Variation

This move defends the d4-pawn, while still prohibiting the development of black's light squared bishop to either f5 or g4.

White's light-squared bishop is well-developed on f4, and can be placed there after the most common response, 5...Nf6. For this reason, 5...Qc7, preventing 6. Bf4, is also commonly played.
explanations.textEn:
Caro-Kann Exchange Variation

This move defends the d4-pawn, while still prohibiting the development of black's light squared bishop to either f5 or g4.

White's light-squared bishop is well-developed on f4, and can be placed there after the most common response, 5...Nf6. For this reason, 5...Qc7, preventing 6. Bf4, is also commonly played.
explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩交换变体

这一着棋保护了 d4 兵，同时仍然禁止黑方的轻方象发展为 f5 或 g4。

白方的光方主教在 f4 上得到了很好的发展，并且可以放置在最常见的响应 5...Nf6 之后。因此，5...Qc7 也常用于阻止 6. Bf4。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. exd5/3...cxd5/4. Bd3/4...Nc6/5. c3/5...Qc7
explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Exchange Variation

Black prevents the white bishop from moving to f4, and contests the vital e5 square. If white neglects to contest this, a later e5 by Black can be very strong.

White here can stop the black bishop from developing to g4 with 6. h3.

6. Nf3 is commonly played, but needlessly allows the white bishop to develop to g4.
explanations.textEn:
Caro-Kann Exchange Variation

Black prevents the white bishop from moving to f4, and contests the vital e5 square. If white neglects to contest this, a later e5 by Black can be very strong.

White here can stop the black bishop from developing to g4 with 6. h3.

6. Nf3 is commonly played, but needlessly allows the white bishop to develop to g4.
explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩交换变体

黑方阻止白方主教移至f4，并争夺重要的e5方格。如果白棋忽略了这一点，那么黑棋后来的 e5 可能会非常强大。

这里白可以用6.h3阻止黑主教发展到g4。

6. Nf3很常见，但不必要地让白主教发展到g4。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. exd5/3...cxd5/4. Bd3/4...Nc6/5. c3/5...Qc7/6. h3
explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Exchange Variation

White prevents the black bishop from developing to g4. This presents a problem, as Black has to decide what to do with their light-squared bishop. 6...g6 is one way to respond, developing the bishop to f4 anyway, and fianchettoing the dark-squared bishop.
explanations.textEn:
Caro-Kann Exchange Variation

White prevents the black bishop from developing to g4. This presents a problem, as Black has to decide what to do with their light-squared bishop. 6...g6 is one way to respond, developing the bishop to f4 anyway, and fianchettoing the dark-squared bishop.
explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩交换变体

白棋阻止黑象发展到g4。这就提出了一个问题，因为黑方必须决定如何处理他们的光方象。 6...g6 是一种应对方式，将主教发展到 f4，然后用 fianchettoing 暗方主教。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...c6/2. d4/2...d5/3. exd5/3...cxd5/4. Bd3/4...Nc6/5. c3/5...Nf6
explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Exchange Variation

This move develops the knight and threatens to develop the light-squared bishop to g4, attacking the queen. White usually continues with 6. Bf4, allowing 6...Bg4, where white plays 7. Qb3, putting pressure on black's b- and d-pawns. White may also play 6. h3, still not allowing the preferred development of the c8-bishop. 6. Nf3, also allowing Black's light-squared bishop to be freed, is also playable.
explanations.textEn:
Caro-Kann Exchange Variation

This move develops the knight and threatens to develop the light-squared bishop to g4, attacking the queen. White usually continues with 6. Bf4, allowing 6...Bg4, where white plays 7. Qb3, putting pressure on black's b- and d-pawns. White may also play 6. h3, still not allowing the preferred development of the c8-bishop. 6. Nf3, also allowing Black's light-squared bishop to be freed, is also playable.
explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩交换变体

这一招发展了马，并威胁将光方主教发展到g4，攻击皇后。白棋通常继续下 6. Bf4，允许 6...Bg4，而白棋则下 7. Qb3，对黑棋的 b-和 d-棋子施加压力。白棋也可以下6.h3，但仍然不允许c8主教的优先发展。 6. Nf3，同样可以释放黑方的光方象，也可以玩。

explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Exchange Variation

Allowing the option of queenside castling, as well as Rc8 after castling kingside.

Nd2 is almost always played, although in a 1939 game, Aitken vs Flohr, white tried h3, and lost.
explanations.textEn:
Caro-Kann Exchange Variation

Allowing the option of queenside castling, as well as Rc8 after castling kingside.

Nd2 is almost always played, although in a 1939 game, Aitken vs Flohr, white tried h3, and lost.
explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩交换变体

允许选择后侧易位，以及王侧易位后的 Rc8。

Nd2几乎总是被使用，尽管在1939年的一场比赛中，艾特肯对阵弗洛尔，怀特尝试了h3，但输了。

explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Exchange Variation

With the light bishop now trapped,(this is also a drawback of the French Defense) black would like to exchange the bishop.
explanations.textEn:
Caro-Kann Exchange Variation

With the light bishop now trapped,(this is also a drawback of the French Defense) black would like to exchange the bishop.
explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩交换变体

现在光明主教被困，（这也是法国防守的缺点）黑方想交换主教。

explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Exchange Variation

With the light bishop now trapped, black would like to exchange the bishop, so Bxf3 is most common, although this can be delayed.
explanations.textEn:
Caro-Kann Exchange Variation

With the light bishop now trapped, black would like to exchange the bishop, so Bxf3 is most common, although this can be delayed.
explanations.textZh:
卡罗-卡恩交换变体

由于光象现在被困，黑棋想交换象，所以 Bxf3 是最常见的，尽管这可以延迟。

explanations.text:
Caro-Kann Exchange Variation

White can either castle, the usual response, or prepare the queen for some shuffling around by accepting the gambit.
explanations.textEn:
Caro-Kann Exchange Variation

White can either castle, the usual response, or prepare the queen for some shuffling around by accepting the gambit.

白棋可以选择城堡（通常的反应），或者通过接受这一策略来为后的一些洗牌做好准备。
