黑方拿走白方的 D 兵。

3、Qxd4为主招。这是黑方用节奏开发 3...Nc6。

3. c3 是丹麦策略。白方提出让黑方保留棋子，以换取快速发展。

3. Nf3，Kieseritzky 变体，通常会导致多次换位。黑棋可以用 3...Nc6 或 3...Bb4+ 转换为苏格兰棋，用 3...d6 转换为 Philidor，用 3...Nf6 转换为彼得罗夫的斯坦尼茨变体，或者用 3...Bc5 转换为主教开局的刘易斯开局（随后是 4. Bc4 Nf6）。独立行是 3...Bc5 4. Nxd4 Nf6。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. d4/2...exd4/3. c3
explanations.text:
Danish Gambit

White chooses to play an aggressive game. By giving a two-pawn material advantage to his opponent, Black spends two moves to capture both of the pawns, and has to deal with a massive attack. Black has few choices here:

The most common move for Black to play here is to take the pawn, /3...dxc3/.

However, another common alternative is to safely decline the gambit and play /3...d5/, the Sörensen Defence or /3...d6/.

It's also possible to safely decline the gambit with /3...Nf6/ (intending to transpose to the Ponziani after 4. e5 Nd5 5. cxd4 d6 6. Nf3 Nc6) or /3...Nc6/ (leading to an independent line after 4. cxd4 d5 5. e5 f6! or the Göring Gambit of the Scotch Game after 4. Nf3, which can still be declined with 4... d5 or 4... Nf6)

Another way to "accept" the gambit is 3...Qe7, which has recently been suggested by computers.

explanations.textZh:
丹麦策略

白方选择采取激进的策略。通过给予对手双兵物质优势，黑方需要花费两步才能吃掉两个棋子，并且必须应对大规模的攻击。黑棋在这里几乎没有什么选择：

黑棋在这里最常见的走法是吃兵，/3...dxc3/。

然而，另一种常见的选择是安全地拒绝策略并玩/3...d5/、索伦森防御或/3...d6/。

也可以使用 /3...Nf6/（打算在 4. e5 Nd5 5. cxd4 d6 6. Nf3 Nc6 后转置为庞齐亚尼）或 /3...Nc6/（在 4. cxd4 d5 5. e5 f6！后形成独立行！或在 4. Nf3 后苏格兰游戏的戈林策略，其中仍然可以用 4...d5 或 4...Nf6 拒绝）

另一种“接受”策略的方法是 3...Qe7，这是计算机最近建议的。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. d4/2...exd4/3. c3/3...dxc3
explanations.text:
Danish Gambit Accepted

The Danish Gambit Accepted is popular among club players, but not so popular at the highest level. That is because, it is easy for black to fall into one of the many traps on this line, but if black knows what to do, white can get no more than equality out of the opening.

White has two main options from this position:

4. Bc4 - Double Danish Gambit

4. Nxc3 - Single Danish Gambit

Although it may have been known earlier, Danish player Severin From essayed the gambit in an 1867 Paris tournament and he is usually given credit for the opening. The Danish gambit was popular with masters of the attack including Alexander Alekhine, Frank Marshall, Joseph Henry Blackburne, and Jacques Mieses, but as Black's defenses improved it lost favor in the 1920s. Today it is rarely played in top-level chess.

White will sacrifice one or two pawns for the sake of rapid development and attack. With care, Black can accept one or both pawns safely, or simply decline the gambit altogether.

接受丹麦策略

接受的丹麦开局在俱乐部球员中很受欢迎，但在最高级别比赛中并不那么受欢迎。这是因为，黑棋很容易落入这条线上的众多陷阱之一，但如果黑棋知道该怎么做，白棋只能从开口中获得平等。

白棋在这个位置上有两个主要选择：

4. Bc4 - 双丹麦开局

4. Nxc3 - 单丹麦开局

尽管人们可能更早知道这一点，但丹麦选手塞维林·弗洛姆 (Severin From) 在 1867 年的巴黎锦标赛中尝试了这一策略，并且他通常因开局而受到赞誉。丹麦策略深受亚历山大·阿廖欣 (Alexander Alekhine)、弗兰克·马歇尔 (Frank Marshall)、约瑟夫·亨利·布莱克本 (Joseph Henry Blackburne) 和雅克·米塞斯 (Jacques Mieses) 等进攻大师的欢迎，但随着布莱克防守的改进，这种策略在 1920 年代失去了青睐。如今，它在顶级国际象棋中已经很少见了。

白棋为了快速发展和进攻，会牺牲一两个棋子。只要小心，黑方可以安全地接受一个或两个棋子，或者干脆完全拒绝这一策略。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. d4/2...exd4/3. c3/3...dxc3/4. Nxc3
explanations.text:
4.Nxc3

This move was Alekhine's choice. This move regains the one of the lost pawns, thus keeping White's material deficit to a minimum. White now has a huge lead in development and a central pawn.
explanations.textEn:
4.Nxc3

This move was Alekhine's choice. This move regains the one of the lost pawns, thus keeping White's material deficit to a minimum. White now has a huge lead in development and a central pawn.
explanations.textZh:
4.Nxc3

这一举动是阿廖欣的选择。此举重新获得了失去的棋子，从而将白方的物质赤字保持在最低限度。白棋现在在发展上拥有巨大的领先优势，并且是一个中心棋子。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. d4/2...exd4/3. c3/3...dxc3/4. bxc3
explanations.text:
4. bxc3?

An error. White forgets why the sacrifice was offered in the first place: by retaking with a pawn, White does not develop their pieces in compensation for the sacrifice, and is left with weak and isolated a- and c-pawns to boot.

Black should have an easy game.

4. bxc3?

4.bxc3？

一个错误。白棋忘记了为什么首先要做出牺牲：通过用棋子重新夺取棋子，白棋并没有发展自己的棋子来补偿牺牲，而是留下了弱小的和孤立的a棋子和c棋子。

黑方应该会轻松应对。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. d4/2...exd4/3. c3/3...dxc3/4. Bc4
explanations.text:
Danish Gambit Accepted - Double Danish

4. Bc4

4. Bc4 gambits a second pawn. It develops the light-squared bishop to a place attacking Black's weakest square f7.

Black almost always accepts the second pawn with 4...cxb2, rather than offering a transposition to the Göring Gambit with 4...Nc6.

In one rare line, Black advances the pawn to c2, not wanting to let White develop the dark squared bishop onto the long diagonal.

接受丹麦语开局 - 双丹麦语

4.BC4

4. Bc4 下第二个棋子。它将光方象发展到攻击黑方最弱的方f7的位置。

黑方几乎总是接受 4...cxb2 的第二个棋子，而不是用 4...Nc6 提供戈林弃兵的换位。

在一条罕见的行中，黑方将棋子推进到 c2，不想让白方将暗方象展开到长对角线上。

This time White has to recapture the pawn with 5. Bxb2 rather than give Black a second queen. (The sacrifice Bxf7 is an important idea in the Double Danish Accepted, just not yet.)

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. d4/2...exd4/3. c3/3...dxc3/4. Bc4/4...cxb2/5. Bxb2
explanations.text:
Danish Gambit Accepted

The pawn is recaptured. White has great attacking chances with her two open bishops and quick development, but Black is up two pawns. A player who is up two pawns can safely assume that they're going to win any endgame that arises, which means White's attack needs concrete results - either material, or checkmate.

Rather than accept those stakes, Black often gambits a pawn straight back with 5...d5 to get her queen and c8-bishop into the game. This is the Schlechter Defence, in which Black can either try to hold onto the second pawn, or return that one too to steer the game into a level, queenless middlegame.

A more ambitious approach is 5...Nf6, the Classical Defence. It looks like the knight is just walking into an e5 advance, but tactical considerations mean it's not that simple.

5...Bb4+ is the Copenhagen Defence. Committing the bishop to b4 invites a later Qb3, but who doesn't love developing a piece with check when you're behind in development?

5...d6 is not fatal, but abandons any hope of active defence in favour of Turtle Mode.

5...Nc6 offers a transposition to the Göring Gambit.

5...c6 hampers the b8-knight and doesn't actually help Black achieve ...d5. Likewise 5...Qe7 and 5...f6 are anti-developing moves, and the attempted Scholar's Mate with 5...Qh4 doesn't work.

explanations.textZh:
接受丹麦策略

棋子被夺回。白棋凭借两个空位象和快速发展有很大的进攻机会，但黑棋领先两个棋子。拥有两个棋子的玩家可以放心地假设他们将赢得任何出现的残局，这意味着白棋的攻击需要具体的结果 - 要么是材料，要么是将死。

黑棋并没有接受这些赌注，而是经常直接用 5...d5 下棋，让她的后和 c8-象进入游戏。这就是施莱希特防御，黑方可以尝试保住第二个棋子，也可以将第二个棋子也归还，从而将游戏带入一个水平的、无皇后的中局。

更雄心勃勃的方法是 5...Nf6，即经典防御。看起来骑士刚刚进入e5进阶，但战术上的考虑意味着事情并没有那么简单。

5...Bb4+ 是哥本哈根防御队。将主教提交给 b4 会邀请稍后的 Qb3，但是当您在开发中落后时，谁不喜欢开发带有检查的棋子呢？

5...d6 并不致命，但放弃了主动防御的任何希望，转而采用海龟模式。

5...Nc6 提供了戈林策略的转换。

5...c6 阻碍了 b8-马，并且实际上并没有帮助黑方实现 ...d5。同样，5...Qe7 和 5...f6 是反发展动作，并且尝试使用 5...Qh4 的学者伴侣不起作用。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. d4/2...exd4/3. c3/3...dxc3/4. Bc4/4...cxb2/5. Bxb2/5...d5
explanations.text:
Danish Gambit Accepted: Schlechter Defence

By playing 5...d5, Black aggressively strikes back at the center, releasing the bishop to catch up in development, returning a pawn in the process. White main move is 6. Bxd5, and the main continuation is 6...Nf6 7. Bxf7+ Kxf7 8. Qxd8 Bb4+ 9. Qd2 Bxd2+ 10. Nxd2 with an equal position.

Alternatively after 6. Bxd5 Nf6, 7. Nc3?! is tried, but after 7...Nxd5 8. Nxd5 Nd7! (8...c6?? 9. Nf6+ gxf6 10. Qxd8+ Kxd8 11. Bxf6+ and White wins an exchange) Black has an advantage as he is still up a pawn and has the bishop pair, but accurate play is needed.

Note that 6. exd5?! is inaccurate because the bishop on c4 is now blocked by its own pawn. After ...Nf6 and ...Bd6, Black's king is safe and White does not have compensation for Black's extra pawn.

explanations.textZh:
接受丹麦策略：施莱希特防御

通过下 5...d5，黑方积极反击中心，释放主教以追赶发展，并在此过程中返回棋子。白方主棋是6.Bxd5，主要延续是6...Nf6 7.Bxf7+ Kxf7 8.Qxd8 Bb4+ 9.Qd2 Bxd2+ 10.Nxd2，同等位置。

或者在 6. Bxd5 Nf6、7. Nc3 之后？！已尝试，但在 7...Nxd5 8. Nxd5 Nd7 之后！ (8...c6?? 9. Nf6+ gxf6 10. Qxd8+ Kxd8 11. Bxf6+ 和白棋赢得对局) 黑棋有优势，因为他仍然是棋子并且有象对，但需要准确的发挥。

注意6.exd5？！不准确，因为 c4 上的象现在被它自己的棋子挡住了。在...Nf6 和...Bd6 之后，黑方的王安全了，而白方对于黑方的额外棋子没有补偿。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. d4/2...exd4/3. c3/3...dxc3/4. Bc4/4...cxb2/5. Bxb2/5...Nf6
explanations.text:
Danish Gambit Accepted, Classical Defence

5...Nf6

Black's knight on f6 is targeting the undefended e-pawn. Turning the tables with 6. e5 is an obvious and strong choice.

Defending the pawn with 6. Nc3 or, if you don't want to block the bishop's diagonal, with 6. Nd2 are less popular. Although developing pieces can't be bad, if Black finds the accurate ...d5 in response then the pawn is getting blown up anyway.

6. Nf3 is just a bit too normal to be an optimal move in this crazy line. The moves Black needs to find in response are correspondingly quite normal ones, like castling kingside.

6. Qb3 is obviously devastating if Black were forced to capture on e4, which she isn't. The immediate tactical problem for White is that 6...d5! now can't be met with 7.e5, because the White queen would find herself badly placed after 7...dxc4 8.exf6.

The "forcing" 6. Bxf6 is a terrible, horrible, no good, very bad move. Apart from giving up the bishop pair, the Black queen that appears on f6 will target a1 (forcing the passive 7.Nd2) and also f2 in combination with a bishop on c5.

6.e5 is the most popular and strongest move for White.

接受丹麦开局，古典防御

5...NF6

黑方 f6 的马瞄准的是不设防的 e 兵。用 6.e5 扭转局面是一个明显且强有力的选择。

用 6. Nc3 防守兵，或者，如果你不想阻挡主教的对角线，用 6. Nd2 不太受欢迎。虽然发展中的棋子不会太差，但如果黑方找到准确的 ...d5 作为回应，那么棋子无论如何都会被炸毁。

6. Nf3 有点太正常了，无法成为这条疯狂路线中的最佳走法。黑方需要找到相应的应对棋步是相当正常的棋步，例如王侧易车。

6. 如果黑方被迫在 e4 上吃子，那么 Qb3 显然是毁灭性的，而她却没有。白方面临的直接战术问题是 6...d5！现在不能遇到 7.e5，因为白皇后会发现自己在 7...dxc4 8.exf6 之后处于不利地位。

“逼”6。Bxf6是一个可怕的、可怕的、没有好处、非常糟糕的举动。除了放弃主教对之外，出现在f6上的黑后还将瞄准a1（迫使被动7.Nd2）以及f2与c5上的主教组合。

6.e5 是白方最受欢迎、最强的棋步。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. d4/2...exd4/3. c3/3...dxc3/4. Bc4/4...cxb2/5. Bxb2/5...Nf6/6. e5
explanations.text:
Danish Gambit Accepted, Classical Defence

6. e5

Black's f6-knight is attacked by a pawn. How about moving it? 6...Ng8 is an abject retreat that only magnifies White's lead in development. 6...Ne4 and 6...Ng4 both allow the simplifying Bxf7+, leaving White with ongoing pressure for an investment of a single pawn, although 6...Ng4 does set a couple of dastardly traps.

Black would ideally like the single pawn without giving White the ongoing pressure, and so the highest scoring moves are those which take preventative measures against Bxf7+:

6...Bb4+ means White can't take on f7 because she's in check;

6...d5 means White can't take on f7 because there's a pawn in the way.

Inserting 6...Qe7 7.Qe2 before dealing with the threat only helps White, whose queen isn't blocking her bishop in.

Danish Gambit Accepted, Classical Defence

explanations.textZh:
接受丹麦开局，古典防御

6.e5

黑方的 f6 马被兵攻击。搬走怎么样？ 6...Ng8 是一次卑鄙的撤退，只会放大白方在发展中的领先优势。 6...Ne4 和 6...Ng4 都允许简化 Bxf7+，使白方面临着投资单个棋子的持续压力，尽管 6...Ng4 确实设置了一些卑鄙的陷阱。

理想情况下，黑棋会喜欢单个棋子，而不会给白棋带来持续的压力，因此得分最高的棋步是针对 Bxf7+ 采取预防措施的棋步：

6...Bb4+ 意味着白棋无法对抗 f7，因为她处于受制状态；

6...d5 意味着白方无法对抗 f7，因为有棋子挡道。

在处理威胁之前插入 6...Qe7 7.Qe2 只会对白棋有帮助，因为白棋的后并没有阻挡她的主教。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. d4/2...exd4/3. c3/3...dxc3/4. Bc4/4...cxb2/5. Bxb2/5...Nf6/6. e5/6...d5
explanations.text:
Danish Gambit Accepted, Classical Defence

6...d5

Capturing the piece with 7. exf6 is both positionally desirable (threatening to ruin Black's kingside pawns) and tactically forced. Most other moves are punished by a combination of ...Bb4+ and ...Ne4, threatening a second piece. After 7. exd6? Qxd6 Black has the same number of pieces out as White (and two extra pawns), nor does White have any way in after 7. Bb5+? Nd7 (8.Qxd5?? c6).
explanations.textEn:
Danish Gambit Accepted, Classical Defence

6...d5

Capturing the piece with 7. exf6 is both positionally desirable (threatening to ruin Black's kingside pawns) and tactically forced. Most other moves are punished by a combination of ...Bb4+ and ...Ne4, threatening a second piece. After 7. exd6? Qxd6 Black has the same number of pieces out as White (and two extra pawns), nor does White have any way in after 7. Bb5+? Nd7 (8.Qxd5?? c6).
explanations.textZh:
接受丹麦开局，古典防御

6...d5

用 7. exf6 吃掉棋子既是有利的位置（有可能毁掉黑棋的王翼兵），也是战术上的强制。大多数其他走法都会受到 ...Bb4+ 和 ...Ne4 组合的惩罚，威胁到第二个棋子。 7.exd6 之后？ Qxd6 黑方的棋子数量与白方相同（还有两个额外的棋子），白方在 7.Bb5+ 之后也没有任何办法进入？ Nd7 (8.Qxd5??c6)。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. d4/2...exd4/3. c3/3...dxc3/4. Bc4/4...cxb2/5. Bxb2/5...Nf6/6. e5/6...d5/7. exf6
explanations.text:
Danish Gambit Accepted, Classical Defence

7. exf6

Black will lose castling rights and have to play around a protected White pawn on g7 if she captures on c4 immediately.

So instead she throws in 7...Bb4+. In responding to the check, White must either give up the dark-squared bishop, block the dark-squared bishop's diagonal, block the d-file, or forfeit castling rights herself. All of those are good things for Black!
explanations.textEn:
Danish Gambit Accepted, Classical Defence

7. exf6

Black will lose castling rights and have to play around a protected White pawn on g7 if she captures on c4 immediately.

So instead she throws in 7...Bb4+. In responding to the check, White must either give up the dark-squared bishop, block the dark-squared bishop's diagonal, block the d-file, or forfeit castling rights herself. All of those are good things for Black!
explanations.textZh:
接受丹麦开局，古典防御

7. 前六

如果黑方立即在 c4 上吃子，她将失去易位权，并且必须在 g7 上围绕受保护的白方棋子进行游戏。

因此她投入了 7...Bb4+。为了回应检查，怀特必须要么放弃暗方象，阻挡暗方象的对角线，阻挡d线，要么放弃自己的易位权。这些对于黑来说都是好事！

explanations.text:
Danish Gambit Accepted, Classical Defence

7...Bb4

White has five legal moves to respond to the check. Ke2 is not the right one.

8. Kf1 is surprisingly popular, but the positive of keeping lines open is outweighed by the negative of losing castling rights, especially since the h1-rook can't get out via h3 while Black's unopposed light-squared bishop is watching it.

8. Nc3 looks natural, but 8...Qxf6! is a very cold shower. Far from stepping into a discovered attack, Black is setting up a devastating cross-pin on the knight that White must waste several moves wriggling out of.

8. Nd2 means it's White, not Black, who will lose castling rights after 8...dxc4. Thanks to the threatened pawn fork on c3, White won't have time to reinforce d2 with Ngf3.

So by a process of elimination we have 8. Bc3. This time there's a tactical flaw with 8...Qxf6, so Black must exchange bishops on c3 so as not to lose a piece.
explanations.textEn:
Danish Gambit Accepted, Classical Defence

7...Bb4

White has five legal moves to respond to the check. Ke2 is not the right one.

8. Kf1 is surprisingly popular, but the positive of keeping lines open is outweighed by the negative of losing castling rights, especially since the h1-rook can't get out via h3 while Black's unopposed light-squared bishop is watching it.

8. Nd2 means it's White, not Black, who will lose castling rights after 8...dxc4. Thanks to the threatened pawn fork on c3, White won't have time to reinforce d2 with Ngf3.

So by a process of elimination we have 8. Bc3. This time there's a tactical flaw with 8...Qxf6, so Black must exchange bishops on c3 so as not to lose a piece.
explanations.textZh:
接受丹麦开局，古典防御

7...Bb4

白棋有五种合法动作来回应检查。 Ke2 不是正确的。

8. Kf1 出人意料地受欢迎，但保持线路畅通的积极作用被失去易车权的消极作用所抵消，特别是因为 h1 车无法通过 h3 出局，而黑方无对手的光方主教正在观看。

8. NC3看起来很自然，但是8...Qxf6！是一个非常冷的淋浴。黑棋根本没有采取被发现的攻击，而是在马身上设置了一个毁灭性的十字钉，白棋必须浪费好几步才能摆脱。

8. Nd2 意味着在 8...dxc4 后将失去王位的是白方，而不是黑方。由于 c3 上受到威胁的兵叉，白方将没有时间用 Ngf3 来加固 d2。

因此，通过消除过程，我们得到 8. Bc3。这次 8...Qxf6 存在战术缺陷，因此黑方必须在 c3 上交换象，以免丢子。

explanations.text:
Danish Gambit Accepted, Classical Defence

9. Nxc3

Black recovers the piece with 9...dxc4. (9…Qxf6?? 10.Nxd5 saves both threatened pieces and Black has nothing.)
explanations.textEn:
Danish Gambit Accepted, Classical Defence

9. Nxc3

Black recovers the piece with 9...dxc4. (9…Qxf6?? 10.Nxd5 saves both threatened pieces and Black has nothing.)
explanations.textZh:
接受丹麦开局，古典防御

9.Nxc3

黑方用 9...dxc4 追回棋子。 (9…Qxf6?? 10.Nxd5 救了两个受威胁的棋子，而黑方什么也没有。)

explanations.text:
Danish Gambit Accepted, Classical Defence

9...dxc4

White has to play fxg7 sooner or later or be a full three pawns down. If she plays 10. fxg7 she can be confident that Black will reply with ...Rg8, as either …Qxd1+ or …Qe7+ would concede possession of the d-file and allow the devastating Nd5.
explanations.textEn:
Danish Gambit Accepted, Classical Defence

9...dxc4

White has to play fxg7 sooner or later or be a full three pawns down. If she plays 10. fxg7 she can be confident that Black will reply with ...Rg8, as either …Qxd1+ or …Qe7+ would concede possession of the d-file and allow the devastating Nd5.
explanations.textZh:
接受丹麦开局，古典防御

9...dxc4

白棋迟早必须下fxg7，否则就会落下整整三个棋子。如果她下 10.fxg7，她可以确信黑棋会回复 ...Rg8，因为 ...Qxd1+ 或 ...Qe7+ 都会承认对 d 线的占有，并允许毁灭性的 Nd5。

explanations.text:
Danish Gambit Accepted, Classical Defence

10. fxg7

Black's only move to save the rook is 10...Rg8. Both 10...Qxd1+ 11.Rxd1 Rg8 12.Nd5 and 10...Qe7+ 11.Nge2 Rg8 12.Nd5 are much worse for Black.
explanations.textEn:
Danish Gambit Accepted, Classical Defence

10. fxg7

Black's only move to save the rook is 10...Rg8. Both 10...Qxd1+ 11.Rxd1 Rg8 12.Nd5 and 10...Qe7+ 11.Nge2 Rg8 12.Nd5 are much worse for Black.
explanations.textZh:
接受丹麦开局，古典防御

10.fxg7

黑方拯救车的唯一棋步是 10...Rg8。 10...Qxd1+ 11.Rxd1 Rg8 12.Nd5 和 10...Qe7+ 11.Nge2 Rg8 12.Nd5 对于黑棋来说都差得多。

explanations.text:
Danish Gambit Accepted, Classical Defence

10...Rg8

Black is now threatening to trade queens on d1 with a winning advantage, as once the rook has captured on g7, White's Nd5 doesn't come with the threat of a fork on f6, so Black can simply defend c7 with ...Na6.

So to limit the damage, White's queen usually makes tracks, with either 11. Qf3 or 11. Qa4+.

Another possibility is for White to voluntarily get the queens off with 11. Qxd8+, followed by castling queenside, hoping that an all-out attack on Black's still underdeveloped forces will be enough compensation for the two pawns.
explanations.textEn:
Danish Gambit Accepted, Classical Defence

10...Rg8

Black is now threatening to trade queens on d1 with a winning advantage, as once the rook has captured on g7, White's Nd5 doesn't come with the threat of a fork on f6, so Black can simply defend c7 with ...Na6.

So to limit the damage, White's queen usually makes tracks, with either 11. Qf3 or 11. Qa4+.

Another possibility is for White to voluntarily get the queens off with 11. Qxd8+, followed by castling queenside, hoping that an all-out attack on Black's still underdeveloped forces will be enough compensation for the two pawns.
explanations.textZh:
接受丹麦开局，古典防御

10...Rg8

黑方现在威胁要以获胜优势在 d1 上交易后，因为一旦车在 g7 上吃掉，白方的 Nd5 就不会在 f6 上产生叉子威胁，因此黑方可以简单地用 ...Na6 防守 c7。

因此，为了限制伤害，白棋后通常会使用 11. Qf3 或 11. Qa4+ 进行追踪。

另一种可能性是白方主动以11.Qxd8+除掉皇后，然后易位后侧，希望对黑方仍不发达的力量进行全面攻击，足以补偿两个棋子。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. d4/2...exd4/3. c3/3...dxc3/4. Bc4/4...cxb2/5. Bxb2/5...Nf6/6. Nf3
explanations.text:
Danish Gambit Accepted, Classical Defence

6. Nf3

6…Nxe4? would be a great move to teach chess students about the value of development over pawn-grabbing. The simple 7. O-O sets in motion an overwhelming attack.

Part of the reason White wants to play 7. O-O is that it deprives Black of the bishop check on b4, which is otherwise a free developing move. So it makes sense that Black's most popular move is the immediate 6...Bb4+ followed by castling, and that a less popular but higher-scoring alternative is 6...d5 to distract White from castling by threatening a piece. After 6...d5 7.exd5 Black has the nice d6 square for the bishop, Open Ruy Lopez style.

Black can opt for passive defence with 6...Be7 or 6...d6, or for a transposition to the Göring Gambit with 6...Nc6.

Danish Gambit Accepted, Classical Defence

After 6...d5 7.exd5 Black has the nice d6 square for the bishop, Open Ruy Lopez style.

Black can opt for passive defence with 6...Be7 or 6...d6, or for a transposition to the Göring Gambit with 6...Nc6.
explanations.textZh:
接受丹麦开局，古典防御

6.NF3

6…Nxe4？这将是一个伟大的举措，可以让国际象棋学生了解发展而不是抢兵的价值。简单的 7.O-O 就可以发起压倒性的攻击。

白棋想要下 7.O-O 的部分原因是它剥夺了黑棋在 b4 上的主教过牌，否则这是一个自由发展的棋步。因此，黑方最受欢迎的棋步是立即走 6...Bb4+，然后是易位，而不太受欢迎但得分较高的替代方案是 6...d5，通过威胁棋子来分散白棋易位的注意力。 6...d5 7.exd5 后，黑棋有漂亮的 d6 象棋方格，Open Ruy Lopez 风格。

黑方可以选择使用 6...Be7 或 6...d6 进行被动防御，或者使用 6...Nc6 换位至戈林开局。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. d4/2...exd4/3. c3/3...dxc3/4. Nf3
explanations.text:
4. Nf3!?

This offers another pawn to Black. Black may take 4...cxb2, where White's idea is 5. Bxb2.

It is more typical for White to offer this gambit with 4. Bc4 instead, which develops the bishop to pressure f7. Delaying Bc4 with 4. Nf3 is less sharp. The difference can be illustrated in the lines

After 4. Nf3 cxb2 5. Bxb2 Nf6 6. e5, Black has 6...Ne4, and 7. Bc4 is a bit too late. 7...Bb4+ and Black's knight and bishop combine to control the dark squares around the king.

Compare the 4. Bc4 line, 4...cxb2 5. Bxb2 Nf6 6. e5, where 6...Ne4? allows 7. Bxf7+ Kxf7 8. Qf3+ Ke8 9. Qxe4 .

4.NF3！？

这为黑棋提供了另一个棋子。黑方可能走 4...cxb2，而白方的想法是 5.Bxb2。

白方更典型的做法是用 4. Bc4 来提供这种策略，从而使主教向 f7 施压。用 4 延迟 Bc4。Nf3 不太尖锐。差异可以用以下几行来说明

在4. Nf3 cxb2 5. Bxb2 Nf6 6. e5之后，黑棋有6...Ne4，而7. Bc4有点太晚了。 7...Bb4+ 和黑方的骑士和主教联合起来控制国王周围的黑暗方格。

比较 4. Bc4 行，4...cxb2 5. Bxb2 Nf6 6. e5，其中 6...Ne4？允许 7. Bxf7+ Kxf7 8. Qf3+ Ke8 9. Qxe4 。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. d4/2...exd4/3. c3/3...d5
explanations.text: This is the Sörensen Defense and is also sometimes called the Capablanca Defense. From this position, White almost always plays /4. exd5/. Black can safely respond with ...Qxd5, as White cannot immediately attack the Queen. A common continuation is 5. cxd4 Nc6 6. Nf3 Bg4 7. Be2.
explanations.textEn: This is the Sörensen Defense and is also sometimes called the Capablanca Defense. From this position, White almost always plays /4. exd5/. Black can safely respond with ...Qxd5, as White cannot immediately attack the Queen. A common continuation is 5. cxd4 Nc6 6. Nf3 Bg4 7. Be2.
explanations.textZh: 这就是索伦森防御，有时也称为卡帕布兰卡防御。从这个位置开始，白方几乎总是下/4。前5/。黑方可以安全地回应...Qxd5，因为白方无法立即攻击皇后。常见的延续是 5. cxd4 Nc6 6. Nf3 Bg4 7. Be2。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. d4/2...exd4/3. Qxd4
explanations.text:
__NOTOC__

Center Game Accepted

In the Center Game, White is happy with himself for knocking out Black's only foothold in the center square, e5. At the time, all four central squares are controlled by White. This may seem like a huge advantage for White, but if Black simply plays Nc6, the queen is forced to move. Conversely, it may seem like a bad idea to develop the queen before any other pieces; however, Black can get into trouble if careless.

Black's responses

Usually, Black responds to the center game by playing /3...Nc6/ forcing White's queen to leave its central outpost.

This may seem like a huge advantage for White, but if Black simply plays Nc6, the queen is forced to move. Conversely, it may seem like a bad idea to develop the queen before any other pieces; however, Black can get into trouble if careless.

Black's responses

Usually, Black responds to the center game by playing /3...Nc6/ forcing White's queen to leave its central outpost.
explanations.textZh:
__NOTOC__

接受中心游戏

在中心棋中，白方为自己击倒了黑方在中心方格 e5 的唯一立足点而感到高兴。当时，所有四个中心方格均由白方控制。这对白棋来说似乎是一个巨大的优势，但如果黑棋只是下 Nc6，那么后棋就被迫走棋。相反，在任何其他棋子之前开发皇后似乎是一个坏主意；然而，如果不小心，黑棋可能会遇到麻烦。

黑方的回应

通常，黑棋通过下/3...Nc6/ 迫使白棋后离开其中央前哨来应对中心游戏。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. d4/2...exd4/3. Qxd4/3...Nc6
explanations.text:
Center Game Accepted

White's responses

White's queen is forced to retreat. By far, the most popular move is 4. Qe3 – Paulsen's Attack – lining up the queen with Black's king.

Most of White's other possible queen retreats allow Black a quick d5 to at least equalize - though most disastrous would be 4. Qc3, allowing 4...Bb4 to win the queen with a pin.

The move 4. Qd1 allows d5 a few moves later in an even worse scenario than usual for White. Black then usually responds with 4...Nf6, deciding to focus on developing the other knight.

On occasion, White chooses 4. Qa4 (mimicking the Scandinavian Main Line) or 4. Qc4 (the Hall Variation).
explanations.textEn:
Center Game Accepted

White's responses

White's queen is forced to retreat. By far, the most popular move is 4. Qe3 – Paulsen's Attack – lining up the queen with Black's king.

Most of White's other possible queen retreats allow Black a quick d5 to at least equalize - though most disastrous would be 4. Qc3, allowing 4...Bb4 to win the queen with a pin.

The move 4. Qd1 allows d5 a few moves later in an even worse scenario than usual for White. Black then usually responds with 4...Nf6, deciding to focus on developing the other knight.

On occasion, White chooses 4. Qa4 (mimicking the Scandinavian Main Line) or 4. Qc4 (the Hall Variation).
explanations.textZh:
接受中心游戏

白的回应

白后被迫撤退。到目前为止，最受欢迎的着法是 4.Qe3 – 保尔森的进攻 – 将后与黑方的王排成一列。

大多数白方其他可能的后撤退都允许黑方快速 d5 至少扳平比分 - 尽管最灾难性的是 4. Qc3，允许 4...Bb4 用针赢得后。

4.Qd1 棋步允许 d5 晚走几步，这对白方来说是比平常更糟糕的情况。黑方通常会回应 4...Nf6，决定集中精力发展另一位马。

有时，白方会选择 4. Qa4（模仿斯堪的纳维亚主线）或 4. Qc4（霍尔变例）。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. d4/2...exd4/3. Bc4
explanations.text:
3. Bc4 · von der Lasa gambit

White gambits their d4 pawn. After either 3...Nf6 or 3...Nc6, this will transpose into other openings.

3...Nf6 is Black's most common move, transposing to the Urusov gambit which is more normally seen from the Bishop's opening with 1. e4 e5 2. Bc4 Nf6 3. d4 exd4.

3...Nc6 is another good move developing the queenside knight. This often transposes to the Scotch gambit after the normal and common developing move 4. Nf3.
explanations.textEn:
3. Bc4 · von der Lasa gambit

White gambits their d4 pawn. After either 3...Nf6 or 3...Nc6, this will transpose into other openings.

3...Nf6 is Black's most common move, transposing to the Urusov gambit which is more normally seen from the Bishop's opening with 1. e4 e5 2. Bc4 Nf6 3. d4 exd4.

3...Nc6 is another good move developing the queenside knight. This often transposes to the Scotch gambit after the normal and common developing move 4. Nf3.
explanations.textZh:
3. Bc4·冯德拉萨策略

白方下注他们的 d4 棋子。在 3...Nf6 或 3...Nc6 之后，这将移至其他空位。

3...Nf6 是黑方最常见的走法，转换为乌鲁索夫策略，这通常从主教的开局中看到，即 1. e4 e5 2. Bc4 Nf6 3. d4 exd4。

3...Nc6 是开发后翼骑士的另一个好动作。这通常在正常和常见的发展着棋 4. Nf3 之后转换为苏格兰策略。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. d4/2...exd4/3. Bc4/3...Nc6
explanations.text:
3...Nc6

Black develops their knight on b8. 4. Nf3 transposes to the Scotch gambit.

4. Nf3 is the most common move, which transposes into the well-known Scotch gambit, more often seen from the move order 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Bc4.
explanations.textEn:
3...Nc6

Black develops their knight on b8. 4. Nf3 transposes to the Scotch gambit.

4. Nf3 is the most common move, which transposes into the well-known Scotch gambit, more often seen from the move order 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Bc4.
explanations.textZh:
3...NC6

黑方在 b8 上发展了他们的马。 4. Nf3 转换为苏格兰策略。

4. Nf3 是最常见的着法，它转换成著名的苏格兰弃兵，更常见的是从着法顺序 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Bc4。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. d4/2...exd4/3. Nf3
explanations.text:
3. Nf3 · Kieseritzky variation

With this move, White brings another attacker to Black's d4 pawn. This often transposes to other openings, though independent lines exist.

3...Nc6 is the most common move, transposing to the Scotch game line, more normally seen from the move order 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 instead.

3...Bc5 is another normal move, developing the bishop. This can go two ways; 4. Nxd4 Nc6 transposes into the Classical Scotch game, while 4. c3 is the Lanc-Arnold gambit, an independent option.
explanations.textEn:
3. Nf3 · Kieseritzky variation

With this move, White brings another attacker to Black's d4 pawn. This often transposes to other openings, though independent lines exist.

3...Nc6 is the most common move, transposing to the Scotch game line, more normally seen from the move order 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 instead.

3...Bc5 is another normal move, developing the bishop. This can go two ways; 4. Nxd4 Nc6 transposes into the Classical Scotch game, while 4. c3 is the Lanc-Arnold gambit, an independent option.
explanations.textZh:
3. Nf3·基塞利茨基变体

通过这一步棋，白棋将另一名攻击者带到了黑棋的 d4 棋子上。尽管存在独立的线路，但这通常会转移到其他空位。

3...Nc6 是最常见的走法，转移到 Scotch 游戏线，更常见的是从走法顺序 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 代替。

3...Bc5 是另一个正常的举动，发展主教。这可以有两种方式： 4. Nxd4 Nc6 转入古典苏格兰游戏，而 4. c3 是 Lanc-Arnold 策略，一个独立的选项。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Ke2
explanations.text:
2. Ke2? · Bongcloud

The so-called "Bongcloud" opening, where White "develops" their king.

This is the second worst possible move after 1. e4 e5 (second only to Ba6, which loses a bishop in one move): White gives up the right to castle unprovoked, misses the opportunity to develop a piece, blocks the lines 1. e4 opened for the queen and bishop, and ignores the centre. The joke rationale for this move is to prepare for the endgame early.

It can be played as an insult, or a gag, or due to the dubiousness of the move, it can be used as a form of a handicap system.

History

In 2008 a Chess.com user by the handle Lenny_Bongcloud came to notoriety for beginning every game with 1.e4 & 2. Ke2 with White, and 1...e5 & 2...Ke7 with Black (and is still doing so as of November 2025). After him, Chess.com users christened 2. Ke2 the "bongcloud", a name, we suppose, that has something to do with drugs, but as good little chess players we wouldn't know anything about that.

In 2010 Andrew Fabbro wrote a tongue-in-cheek book on the opening, Winning with the Bongcloud, dedicated to Lenny_Bongcloud. The book is a parody of overwritten chess opening repertoire literature. Fabbro invented spurious defences with chess jargon names ("...Ke7! This inaugurates the Bongcloud Counter-Gambit, and play often leads to the very sharp Marijanezy Bind, after 3. g4 g5 3. Kf3!") and recommended it for people whose "current repertoire is too drawish" or who "can't afford the full version of ChessBase and want an opening where all known games will fit in ChessBase Light's 32,000-game limit."

Hikaru Nakamura is largely responsible for popularising the joke with a wider audience. In 2020, Nakamura made a new Chess.com account to stream playing the opening exclusively (and, of course, winning with it, because he's a super-GM). In 2021, Magnus Carlsen and Nakamura made headlines when they played the following game: 1. e4 e5 2. Ke2 Ke7 3. Ke1 Ke8 4. Ke2 Ke7 5. Ke1 Ke8 6. Ke2 Ke7 ½-½

所谓的“Bongcloud”开局，白棋“发展”他们的国王。

这是继 1. e4 e5 后第二差的可能棋（仅次于 Ba6，一步失去象）：白方无缘无故地放弃了城堡的权利，错过了发展棋子的机会，封锁了 1. e4 为后和象打开的线，并忽略了中心。此举的笑话理由是尽早为残局做好准备。

它可以被当作一种侮辱，或者一个笑话，或者由于该动作的可疑性，它可以被用作一种障碍系统。

2008 年，一位名为 Lenny_Bongcloud 的 Chess.com 用户因每场比赛都以白棋 1.e4 和 2.Ke2 以及黑棋 1...e5 和 2...Ke7 开始而声名狼藉（截至 2025 年 11 月仍然如此）。在他之后，Chess.com 用户将 2. Ke2 命名为“bongcloud”，我们认为这个名字与毒品有关，但作为优秀的小棋手，我们对此一无所知。

2010 年，Andrew Fabbro 在开幕之际写了一本半开玩笑的书《Winning with the Bongcloud》，专门献给 Lenny_Bongcloud。这本书是对国际象棋开局文献的模仿。 Fabbro 用国际象棋术语名称发明了虚假防御（“...Ke7！这开创了 Bongcloud Counter-Gambit，并且在 3.g4 g5 3.Kf3 之后，游戏通常会导致非常尖锐的 Marijanezy Bind！”），并将其推荐给“当前曲目太吸引人”或“买不起 ChessBase 完整版并希望所有已知游戏都适合 ChessBase 的开局”的人Light 的游戏限制为 32,000 场。”

2...Ke7?

Black plays the worst conceivable response to the worst opening from White, serving to show that they, too, are "in" on the joke.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bb5
explanations.text:
Portuguese Opening: 2. Bb5?!

The Portuguese Opening is a rare opening starting with the moves 1.e4 e5 2.Bb5?!. The bishop is ineffective on the b5 square when there is no black knight on c6. It can be easily attacked by Black's c-pawn with 2...c6. Other moves can result in a Ruy Lopez/Spanish Opening (like 2...Nc6 3.Nf3) or other situations, where Black should be fine.

After 2...c6, the bishop can move to f1 (which makes White just waste 2 tempi), c4 (which allows 3...d5 to come with tempo and gives Black a classical center), d3, e2 (which allow a classical center for Black as well) and a4 (allowing 3...b5 4.Bb3 d5 and Black has a classical center, though engines may prefer 3...Nf6).

On move 2, Black can also play Nf6, develop normally, and exploit the bishop on b5 later. The Portuguese Opening is akin to a Ruy Lopez where White does not play Nf3 and is trying to gain pressure on Black's d-pawn. White may be hoping that Black attacks the bishop too much and weakens their dark squares or overextends.

explanations.textZh:
葡萄牙语开局：2. Bb5？！

葡萄牙开局是一个罕见的开局，以 1.e4 e5 2.Bb5?! 开始。当c6上没有黑骑士时，主教在b5方格上无效。它可以很容易地被黑方的 c 兵用 2...c6 攻击。其他走法可能会导致鲁伊·洛佩兹/西班牙开局（如 2...Nc6 3.Nf3）或其他情况，黑棋应该没问题。

2...c6 之后，主教可以移动到 f1（这使得白方浪费 2 个节奏）、c4（允许 3...d5 带有节奏并为黑方提供古典中心）、d3、e2（也允许黑方使用古典中心）和 a4（允许 3...b5 4.Bb3 d5 和黑方有一个古典中心，尽管引擎可能更喜欢 3...Nf6）。

在第2步，黑方也可以下Nf6，正常发展，并在稍后的b5上利用主教。葡萄牙开局类似于鲁伊·洛佩兹，其中白方不下 Nf3，并试图对黑方的 d 兵施加压力。白方可能希望黑方过多地攻击主教并削弱其暗方或过度延伸。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bb5/2...Bc5/3. b4
explanations.text:
Portuguese Opening, Miguel Gambit

In this line, White attempts to directly challenge Black's control of the center with the sacrifice of the pawn on b4. As in the Evans Gambit, after Black's most obvious move 3...Bxb4, White will play 4. c3 with tempo, a move that will eventually allow him to play d4 and get two pawns in the center.

explanations.textZh:
葡萄牙开局，米格尔·甘比特

在这一行中，白方试图通过牺牲b4上的棋子来直接挑战黑方对中心的控制。正如在埃文斯弃兵中一样，在黑方最明显的走棋 3...Bxb4 之后，白方将按节奏下 4.c3，这一着法最终将允许他下 d4 并在中心获得两个棋子。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bc4
explanations.text:
2. Bc4 · Bishop's opening

With 2. Bc4 White develops their bishop to increase control over d5 and pressure f7, the weakest pawn in Black's position. The Bishop's opening is very transpositional: by not having played Nf3 yet, White retains the option of f4 and may plan to transpose into Vienna or King's gambit lines, or the game can be taken into a Russian or Italian direction.

Compared to 2. Nf3, White has not threatened Black's e5 pawn, so Black is afforded flexibility in their reply. The main moves are 2...Nf6 or 2...Bc5.

2...Nf6 and Black attacks White's e pawn. White may defend it or not. They can defend with 3. Nc3, transposing into a Vienna game, or 3. d3, happy that their king's bishop is already developed outside of the pawn chain. They can leave it undefended to develop 3. Nf3, transposing into a Russian game, or to counterattack with 3. d4 or 3. f4 (the Ponziani and Greco gambits, respectively).

2...Bc5 is the classical response, developing Black's bishop. Transpositions to Vienna or Italian games are possible with 3. Nc3 or 3. Nf3. 3. b4 is a gambit resembling the Evan's gambit. The more original response is 3. c3, supporting an eventual d4 push.

In amateur games, 3. Qh5 or 3. Qf3 may follow, expecting that Black will allow Qxf7#.

Other second moves for Black include

2...Nc6, letting White whether to transpose into the Italian with 3. Nf3 or the Vienna with 3. Nc3, or hold off with 3. d3.

2...f5!?, the Calabrese countergambit, a sharp but not very sound gambit.

2...b5?!, the Anderssen attack, a Romantic but not very sound gambit.

2...c6, the Philidor counterattack, preparing d5, striking in the centre.

2...d5!?, the Khan gambit, to give up a pawn for the bishop pair (if 3. Bxd5 Nf6 4. Nc3 Nxd5 5. exd5) or two pawns for development (if 3. exd5 c6 4. dxc6 Nxc6), or a lead in development (if 3. exd5 Nf6 4. Nc3 Bd6)

2...d6 to transpose to Philidor's Defence.

History

The Bishop's opening was popular in the 18th Century and a favourite of Philidor. His 1790 book, Analysis of the Game of Chess, largely focuses on this opening. In the 1930s, Weaver Adams used to claim it was a "forced win" for White, but it's usually considered that Black can equalise with best play.

Danish Grandmaster Bent Larsen revived the opening in the 1960s at the 1964 Amsterdam Interzonal.

explanations.textZh:
2. Bc4·主教开幕

2. Bc4 白方发展了象，以增强对 d5 的控制，并对黑方最弱的棋子 f7 施加压力。主教的开局非常具有换位性：由于还没有玩过Nf3，白方保留了f4的选择，并可能计划换位为维也纳或国王的弃兵路线，或者游戏可以带入俄罗斯或意大利方向。

与2.Nf3相比，白方没有威胁到黑方的e5兵，因此黑方的应对具有灵活性。主要动作是 2...Nf6 或 2...Bc5。

2...Nf6 和黑方攻击白方的 e 兵。白棋可以防守也可以不防守。他们可以用 3.Nc3（转换为维也纳游戏）或 3.d3 进行防守，很高兴他们的国王的主教已经在典当链之外发展起来。他们可以不设防地发展 3. Nf3，转换成俄罗斯游戏，或者用 3. d4 或 3. f4 进行反击（分别是庞齐亚尼和格雷科的策略）。

2...Bc5 是经典的反应，发展黑方的象。使用 3. Nc3 或 3. Nf3 可以转换为维也纳或意大利游戏。 3. b4 是一种类似于埃文策略的策略。更原始的响应是 3.c3，支持最终的 d4 推送。

在业余对局中，可能会出现 3.Qh5 或 3.Qf3，期望黑方允许 Qxf7#。

黑棋的其他第二步棋包括

2...Nc6，让白方是否用 3. Nf3 转换成意大利语，或者用 3. Nc3 转换成维也纳，或者用 3. d3 推迟。

2...f5!?，卡拉布雷斯反策略，一种尖锐但不太健全的策略。

2...b5？！，安徒生攻击，一个浪漫但不太合理的策略。

2...c6，菲利多反击，准备d5，攻击中路。

2...d5!?，可汗策略，放弃主教对的一个棋子（如果 3. Bxd5 Nf6 4. Nc3 Nxd5 5. exd5）或两个棋子用于发展（如果 3. exd5 c6 4. dxc6 Nxc6），或发展中的领先地位（如果 3. exd5 Nf6 4. Nc3 Bd6）

2...d6 转置为菲利多防御。

历史

主教式开局在 18 世纪很流行，也是菲利多 (Philidor) 的最爱。他 1790 年出版的著作《国际象棋棋局分析》主要关注这一开局。 20世纪30年代，韦弗·亚当斯曾声称这是白棋的“强迫胜利”，但通常认为黑棋可以凭借最佳发挥扳平比分。

丹麦大师本特·拉森 (Bent Larsen) 在 1960 年代于 1964 年阿姆斯特丹洲际赛上恢复了开幕式。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bc4/2...b5
explanations.text:
2...b5?!

This ancient move from the romantic era was Adolf Anderssen’s favourite. Black tries to emulate an Evan’s gambit in reverse, but White can refute the risky gambit by acting early.

White can snap up the pawn 3. Bxb5 and it's not transparent what Black is getting. Anderssen played both 3...f5 and 3...c6:

After 3...f5, the Thorold gambit, either 4. exf5 or 4. d4 seem pleasant for White. With the Bishop on b5, Black can't play Nc6 so there is no tempo gain if Qxd4, hence:

4. exf5 Nf6 5. d4 exd4 6. Qxd4 and Nc6 isn't possible

4. d4 exd4 5. Qxd4 and Nc6 still isn't possible.

If Black meets 4. d4 with 4...fxe4?, then 5. Qh5+ g6 6. Qxe5+ and "Black can put the pieces back in the box."

3...c6, the Anderssen gambit, can be met by 4. Ba4 or 4. Bc4 and the game resumes with Black being down a pawn, and it's up to them to prove an advantage.

explanations.textZh:
2...b5？！

这种来自浪漫主义时代的古老举动是阿道夫·安德森 (Adolf Anderssen) 的最爱。黑棋试图反向模仿埃文的策略，但白棋可以通过尽早行动来反驳这种冒险的策略。

白方可以抢占棋子 3. Bxb5，但黑方得到的东西并不透明。安德森同时演奏了 3...f5 和 3...c6：

在 3...f5 之后，Thorold 策略，无论是 4. exf5 还是 4. d4 似乎对白方来说都是令人愉快的。当主教在 b5 上时，黑方无法下 Nc6，因此如果 Qxd4 则没有速度增益，因此：

4. exf5 Nf6 5. d4 exd4 6. Qxd4 和 Nc6 不可能

4. d4 exd4 5. Qxd4 和 Nc6 仍然不可能。

如果黑方遇到 4. d4 和 4...fxe4？，则 5. Qh5+ g6 6. Qxe5+ 并且“黑方可以将棋子放回盒子中”。

3...c6，安德森策略，可以通过 4. Ba4 或 4. Bc4 来满足，并且游戏将在黑棋落下棋子的情况下继续，并且由他们来证明优势。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bc4/2...b6
explanations.text:
Bishop's Opening - Sideline 2... b6?

2...b6?

The position after the moves 1. e4 e5 2. Bc4 b6? is generally considered weak and slightly unusual as it doesn't immediately help in developing black's minor pieces or controlling the center of the board. The primary weakness this move creates in Black's position is a lack of central control. The traditional moves 2...Nc6 or 2...Nf6! contest the center and allow for quicker development of the pieces, but 2...b6 does not. Furthermore, the move 2...b6 could potentially weaken the c6 square, which could be exploited in the future.

White's plan usually involves a standard development with 3.Nf3! followed by 0-0, d4, and c3. White's plan of rapid development and central control can help to exploit the 2...b6 weaknesses and gain an early advantage. This plan allows White to quickly develop his pieces, aiming to control the center with a pawn at d4, and prepare for a potential pawn storm with c3 and d4. The Knights are well placed on f3 and c3, the Bishop on c4 is eyeing the f7 square, and the King has been tucked away safely by castling. This setup provides a solid foundation for White to launch an attack, putting pressure on Black's position.

Meanwhile, Black's slower development and lack of central control can allow White to seize the initiative early on in the game. The key for White will be to capitalize on these advantages while maintaining a solid position and preparing for any counterattacks that Black might launch.

2...b6？

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bc4/2...d6
explanations.text:
2...d6

A modest move that over-defends the e-pawn at the expense of developing a piece and making it harder to develop the king's bishop.

Black invites White to play 3. Nf3 and transpose into the Philidor defence. This is the most common move. In the Philidor, White typically looks for a pawn break with d4.

3. Nc3 may lead to a more original game. After 3...Nf6 this resembles a Vienna game where Black has played the passive move ...d6. White can play d3, having already developed their bishop outside of the pawn chain, and delaying the move Nf3 allows White to play for a pawn break with f4 instead.

explanations.textZh:
2...d6

这是一个适度的举动，过度保护电子兵，但代价是发展棋子并使发展国王的主教变得更加困难。

黑方邀请白方下3.Nf3并转入菲利多防御。这是最常见的举动。在 Philidor 中，白方通常会用 d4 寻找兵突破。

3. Nc3可能会带来更加原创的游戏。 3...Nf6 之后，这类似于维也纳游戏，黑棋下被动棋...d6。白方可以下 d3，因为他们已经在典当链之外发展了象，并且延迟 Nf3 的走法使得白方可以用 f4 来下棋。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bc4/2...Qg5
explanations.text:
2...Qg5?

A suspicious move. Black threatens White's g2-pawn, thinking to take advantage of the fact that the early development of White's bishop left it undefended.

However, the pawn is poisonous. 3. Nf3 attacks the queen and forces it to move, and if 3...Qxg2? then 4. Rg1 Qh3 5. Bxf7+!. It turns out Black's f7-pawn was hanging, because Black can't afford to take it back. 5...Kxf7?? Ng5+! wins the queen.

Even if White does not spot the Bxf7+ tactic, many turn five moves are good for White because they are ahead in development and can easily gain time by attacking Black's queen and forcing it to move, e.g. 5. Nc3 Nf6 6. Rg3 Qh5 7. Rg5 Qh6 8. Rxe5+ Be7 This illustrates the danger of developing one's queen early, unsupported by the minor pieces.

Nc3 Nf6 6. Rg3 Qh5 7. Rg5 Qh6 8. Rxe5+ Be7 This illustrates the danger of developing one's queen early, unsupported by the minor pieces.
explanations.textZh:
2...Qg5？

可疑的举动。黑方威胁白方的 g2 兵，想利用白方象的早期发展使其处于不设防的事实。

然而，棋子是有毒的。 3. Nf3攻击皇后并迫使其移动，如果3...Qxg2？然后 4.Rg1 Qh3 5.Bxf7+!。事实证明，黑方的 f7 兵悬而未决，因为黑方无力收回它。 5...Kxf7？？ NG5+！赢得女王。

即使白棋没有发现 Bxf7+ 战术，许多第五回合的棋步对白棋来说也是有利的，因为它们在发展上处于领先地位，并且可以通过攻击黑棋的后并迫使其移动来轻松赢得时间，例如5. Nc3 Nf6 6. Rg3 Qh5 7. Rg5 Qh6 8. Rxe5+ Be7 这说明了在没有小棋子支持的情况下过早发展出皇后的危险。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bc4/2...Qh4
explanations.text:
2...Qh4?

Black attempts to play for an immediate mating attack. Essentially they are playing the Parham attack or "wayward queen" attack with colours reversed.

The immediate threat is ...Qxe4+, so White should defend their e-pawn with 3. Nc3. Then, Black may try 3...Bc5, bringing another attacker to f2 and hoping White will blunder and allow ...Qxf2#. 4. g3 prevents the queen from seeing f2, and after 4...Qf6, White plays 5. Nf3 to defend the f2-pawn again.

After all this, what has Black to show for it? In violation of opening principles, they have spent two moves moving their queen around that could have been spent on developing their minor pieces and castling. White is better.

White may try for their own "scholar's mate" with 3. Qf3!?, which also defends e4, but Black can parry this just as easily with 3...Nf6. White has allowed Black to "get away" with violating opening principles, and still has to develop their minor pieces having taken away the f3 square from their knight.

explanations.textZh:
2...Qh4？

黑棋试图立即进行交配攻击。本质上，他们正在玩帕勒姆攻击或颜色反转的“任性女王”攻击。

直接的威胁是...Qxe4+，所以白方应该用 3. Nc3 来保卫他们的电子兵。然后，黑方可能会尝试 3...Bc5，将另一名攻击者带到 f2，并希望白方会犯错并允许 ...Qxf2#。 4. g3 阻止后看到 f2，在 4...Qf6 之后，白方再次下 5. Nf3 来防守 f2 兵。

经历了这一切之后，黑方能拿出什么来呢？他们违反了开局原则，花了两步棋来移动皇后，而这些棋本来可以用来开发小棋子和易位。白色比较好。

白棋可能会尝试使用 3.Qf3!? 来尝试自己的“学者之友”，这也可以防御 e4，但黑棋也可以使用 3...Nf6 轻松招架。白棋允许黑棋“逃脱”违反开局原则的行为，并且仍然必须发展他们的小棋子，从他们的马手中夺走f3方格。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bc4/2...Bc5/3. Qg4
explanations.text:
3. Qg4!?

3. Qg4!? is a rare sideline.

Black's queen threatens to take on g7. If e.g. 3...Nf6? 4. Qxg7 and the two threats are Qxf7# and Qxh8. 4...Rh8 is the only way to defend both. 3...d5?, attacking the bishop on c4 while discovering an attack on the queen, doesn't work as g7 is undefended.

3...Qf6 is Black's best way of defending g7. This also threatens to take on f2 (4. Nc3?? Bxf2+ 6. Kd1). White can play 4. Nf3 to defend the pawn while developing a piece, though the knight is pinned to f2 until White castles, then 4...Nc6 allows Black's rook to see the bishop, so 5...d5! with a discovered attack on White's queen is now a threat.

3...g6 is playable but weakens the dark squares.

explanations.textZh:
3.Qg4！？

3.Qg4！？是难得的副业。

黑后威胁要挑战七国集团。如果例如3...NF6？ 4. Qxg7，两个威胁是Qxf7#和Qxh8。 4...Rh8 是保护两者的唯一方法。 3...d5？，攻击c4上的主教，同时发现对女王的攻击，不起作用，因为g7不设防。

3...Qf6 是黑方防守 g7 的最佳方式。这也有可能挑战f2（4.NC3??Bxf2+ 6.Kd1）。白棋可以下4.Nf3来防守棋子，同时发展棋子，尽管马被固定到f2直到白棋城堡，然后4...Nc6允许黑棋的车看到主教，所以5...d5！随着对白后的攻击被发现，现在成为了威胁。

3...g6 可以玩，但削弱了黑暗方块。

explanations.text:

3. Nf3

White position is quite sharp, an attack on the e5 pawn, a possible break on d4 would gain a tempo on the Black Bishop. Black has one one move to try for equality, that's 3...Nc6 and transpose into the Giuoco Piano.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bc4/2...Be7
explanations.text:
2...Be7?

Perhaps Black is thinking of transposing into the Hungarian variation of the Italian with 3. Nf3!? Nc6, or a Philidor defence with 3. Nf3 d6.

However this move order leaves Black's e-pawn undefended and allows White the tactic 3. Qh5!. Black must respond to the threat of Qxf7#, and can't do that and defend their e-pawn at the same time. 3...g6 4. Qxe5 wins the pawn.
explanations.textEn:

However this move order leaves Black's e-pawn undefended and allows White the tactic 3. Qh5!. Black must respond to the threat of Qxf7#, and can't do that and defend their e-pawn at the same time. 3...g6 4. Qxe5 wins the pawn.
explanations.textZh:
2...Be7？

也许布莱克正在考虑用 3. Nf3! 转换成意大利语的匈牙利变体？ Nc6，或具有 3. Nf3 d6 的 Philidor 防御。

然而，这一走法使得黑方的电子兵处于不设防的状态，并允许白方采用战术 3.Qh5!。黑方必须对 Qxf7# 的威胁做出反应，但不能同时防守自己的 e 兵。 3...g6 4. Qxe5 赢得棋子。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bc4/2...g6
explanations.text:
Bishop's Opening - Sideline 2... g6?

2...g6?

The opening line 1. e4 e5 2. Bc4 g6 is a deviation from standard opening principles in chess. The move 2…g6? is considered weak because it allows White to seize control of the center with 3. d4 quickly. This move attacks the pawn on e5 and prepares to develop the knight to f3.

After 3. d4!, White plans to continue with 4. Nf3, aiming to put more pressure on the central square e5. Black cannot respond with 4... Bg7?? because 5. Nxe5 Bxe5 6. dxe5 would lead to White winning a pawn due to the pin on the e5 pawn.

White could also consider a long-term plan of advancing the pawn on a2 to a5 (via a4) to control the b6 square. This move could potentially limit Black's queenside development and create weaknesses in Black's pawn structure.

Overall, this sideline in the Bishop's Opening leads to a superior position for White due to Black's neglect of central control and weak pawn structure.

The opening line 1. e4 e5 2. Bc4 g6 is a deviation from standard opening principles in chess. The move 2…g6? is considered weak because it allows White to seize control of the center with 3. d4 quickly. This move attacks the pawn on e5 and prepares to develop the knight to f3.

After 3. d4!, White plans to continue with 4. Nf3, aiming to put more pressure on the central square e5. Black cannot respond with 4... Bg7?? because 5. Nxe5 Bxe5 6. dxe5 would lead to White winning a pawn due to the pin on the e5 pawn.

White could also consider a long-term plan of advancing the pawn on a2 to a5 (via a4) to control the b6 square. This move could potentially limit Black's queenside development and create weaknesses in Black's pawn structure.

Overall, this sideline in the Bishop's Opening leads to a superior position for White due to Black's neglect of central control and weak pawn structure.
explanations.textZh:
主教的开局 - 边线 2...g6？

2...g6？

开局线 1. e4 e5 2. Bc4 g6 偏离了国际象棋中的标准开局原则。棋步2…g6？被认为是弱的，因为它允许白方用 3.d4 快速夺取中心的控制权。这一招攻击e5上的棋子，准备将马发展到f3。

3.d4!之后，白方计划继续4.Nf3，旨在对中心方e5施加更多压力。黑方无法回应 4...Bg7？因为 5. Nxe5 Bxe5 6. dxe5 将导致白方因 e5 棋子上的针而赢得棋子。

白棋还可以考虑一个长期计划，将a2上的棋子推进到a5（通过a4）以控制b6方格。这一举动可能会限制黑方后翼的发展并造成黑方兵结构的弱点。

总体而言，由于黑方忽视了中央控制和薄弱的兵结构，主教开局中的这一边线导致了白方处于优势地位。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bc4/2...Ne7
explanations.text:
Bishop's Opening - Sideline 2... Ne7

2...Ne7

The move 2...Ne7 in response to the Bishop's Opening is a less common choice for Black, but it can lead to flexible setups like the Hungarian Defense or transpositions into other openings. Also, it is a passive move to prepare d5 when the classical 2. ..., Nf6! accomplishes the same goal placing it in a better developing and natural square. It aims to avoid exchanges with a move like d3. The knight on e7 is also vulnerable to attacks from the f3 knight and/or the c4 bishop and can be a target for a future Bxf7+ sacrifice.

White Central Control and Space:

Maintain e4 Pawn: White's pawn on e4 remains a central figure in maintaining a spatial advantage and central control. Depending on Black's play, White may opt to support it with d2-d3 or even a timely f2-f4.

Nf3 Development: Developing the knight to f3 not only supports the e5 pawn but also prepares to castle kingside swiftly.

d2-d3 and c2-c3: These pawn moves help support the central pawn structure, allow the bishop on c1 to be developed (often to e3 or g5), and sometimes provide a stepping stone for the d2 pawn to push to d4, striking at the heart of Black's center.

Piece Play and Tactical Ideas:

Bg5 Pin: Depending on how Black develops, the move Bg5 can be a strong pin against the knight on e7, especially if Black has already moved its d7 pawn.

Central Pawn Break: If Black remains passive or overly defensive, White can consider a central pawn break with d4, challenging Black's central pawn on e5.

King's Safety: White should be quick to castle kingside, connecting the rooks and preparing for central or kingside operations.

Flexible Queen's Knight Development: Depending on the situation, White's queen's knight can develop to c3 or d2, with each square having its benefits. Nc3 supports the e4 pawn, while Nd2 can offer added support for a future d3-d4 push or even prepare to reroute to the kingside via f1 and g3.

Longer-term Plans:

Kingside Pawn Storm: If Black castles kingside and White's center is secure, a pawn storm with moves like h2-h4 can become a potent weapon, especially if combined with pieces targeting Black's king.

Positional Pressure: The bishop on c4, combined with a knight on f3 and a rook on e1, can exert significant pressure on the f7 pawn, which is often a vulnerable spot in Black's position.

Control of d5: The d5 square is of particular importance. White's bishop on c4 already eyes this square. If Black ever plays ...c6 and ...d5, White should be ready to challenge or, if appropriate, allow a pawn exchange to open lines of play.

explanations.textZh:
主教的开局 - 边线 2... Ne7

2...Ne7

对于黑棋来说，响应主教开局的 2...Ne7 棋不太常见，但它可以带来灵活的布局，例如匈牙利防御或换位到其他开局。还有，当经典2....，Nf6时准备d5是一个被动的举动！实现了同样的目标，将其置于一个更好的发展和自然广场。它的目的是避免与 d3 这样的棋步进行交换。 e7 上的骑士也容易受到 f3 骑士和/或 c4 主教的攻击，并且可能成为未来 Bxf7+ 牺牲的目标。

白色中央控制和空间：

维持e4兵：白方在e4上的兵仍然是维持空间优势和中央控制的核心人物。根据黑棋的玩法，白棋可能会选择用 d2-d3 甚至及时的 f2-f4 来支援。

Nf3发展：将骑士发展到f3不仅可以支援e5兵，还可以为快速攻占王翼做好准备。

d2-d3 和 c2-c3：这些棋子走法有助于支撑中心棋子结构，使 c1 上的象得以发展（通常发展到 e3 或 g5），有时还为 d2 棋子推向 d4 提供踏脚石，打击黑方中心的核心。

棋子游戏和战术理念：

Bg5 Pin：根据黑方的发展方式，Bg5 走法可以成为对抗 e7 上的马的强有力的钉住点，特别是如果黑方已经移动了其 d7 兵。

中央兵突破：如果黑方仍然被动或过度防守，白方可以考虑使用 d4 进行中央兵突破，挑战黑方 e5 上的中央兵。

国王的安全：白棋应该快速占领王翼，连接车并为中央或王翼行动做好准备。

灵活的后骑士发展：根据情况，白后骑士可以发展到c3或d2，各有其优势。 Nc3 支持 e4 pawn，而 Nd2 可以为未来的 d3-d4 推送提供额外支持，甚至准备通过 f1 和 g3 重新路由到王翼。

长期计划：

王侧兵风暴：如果黑方占据王侧城堡并且白方中心安全，则具有 h2-h4 等走法的兵风暴可以成为有效的武器，尤其是与针对黑方国王的棋子结合使用时。

位置压力：c4 上的象，加上 f3 上的马和 e1 上的车，可以对 f7 兵施加巨大的压力，而 f7 兵通常是黑棋位置上的一个弱点。

d5的控制：d5方块尤为重要。白方c4上的主教已经注视着这个方格。如果黑棋曾经下过...c6 和...d5，白棋应该准备好挑战，或者如果合适的话，允许棋子交换来打开比赛路线。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bc4/2...Nf6
explanations.text:
Bishop's Opening: Berlin Defence

2... Nf6

Black develops the king's knight and in doing so threatens the e4-pawn and makes it possible to play d5. This move also preempts Scholar's Mate by preventing 3. Qh5, and blocking the queen's path in the 3. Qf3 version of the mate.

White's options:

/3. d3/ is the most common continuation.

/3. d4/ can go either to Ponziani-Urusov Gambit or to the Two Knights Defence by transposition.

/3. Nc3/ transposes to the Vienna Game (Falkbeer Defence), with an opportunity to use a center fork trick.

/3. Nf3/ transposes to Petrov's Defence.

/3. f3/ should not be played

/3. f4/ offers a transposition to the King's Gambit after 3...exf4.

主教开场：柏林防御

2...NF6

黑方发展出国王的马，从而威胁到 e4 兵并使得下 d5 成为可能。这一招还可以通过阻止 3.Qh5 来抢先学者的伴侣，并在 3.Qf3 版本的伴侣中阻挡皇后的路径。

白棋的选择：

/3。 d3/ 是最常见的延续。

/3。 d4/ 可以通过换位进入庞齐亚尼-乌鲁索夫策略或双骑士防御。

/3。 Nc3/ 转移到维也纳比赛（法尔克比尔防守），有机会使用中叉技巧。

/3。 Nf3/ 转换为彼得罗夫的防御。

/3。 f3/ 不应该播放

/3。 f4/ 在 3...exf4 之后提供到 King's Gambit 的转换。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bc4/2...Nf6/3. d3
explanations.text:
Bishop's Opening: Berlin Defence

3. d3

Responding to Black's threat on the e4 pawn, White simultaneously defends it and supports their light-squared bishop. The dark-squared bishop is also opened up for future strategic potential.

Black's most common responses are c6 (the Paulsen defense), intending to strike in the centre with d5 and kick White's bishop, as well as Bc5 and Nc6, which both solidify control over the d4 square.

3.d3

黑方最常见的反应是c6（保尔森防守），打算用d5攻击中心并踢白方的主教，以及Bc5和Nc6，它们都巩固了对d4方格的控制。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bc4/2...Nf6/3. d4
explanations.text:
Bishop's Opening: Ponziani-Urusov Gambit

3. d4!?

The Ponziani-Urusov Gambit is a line in which White sacrifices a pawn early in the game. White will occupy the center at the beginning of the game and challenge Black’s central control.

Black's strongest and most natural response is to accept the gambit with 3...exd4. If Black tries to transpose to the Two Knights Defence with 3...Nc6?!, then White will have 4. d5!, which prevents the transposition and will cause Black trouble.

3.d4！？

庞齐亚尼-乌鲁索夫弃兵是白方在游戏早期牺牲一个棋子的路线。白方将在比赛开始时占据中心位置，挑战黑方的中控。

黑方最强烈、最自然的反应是接受 3...exd4 的策略。如果黑方试图用 3...Nc6?! 转为二马防御，那么白方将有 4. d5!，这会阻止转位并给黑方带来麻烦。

3... exd4!

Black's natural and best response is to accept the gambit with 3...exd4.

With accurate play, Black will reach an equal or even slightly better position.

explanations.text:
Can also be reached via 1. e4 e5 2. f3 Nf6 3. Bc4 or 1. f3 Nf6 2. e4 e5 3. Bc4.

Bishop's Opening: Walkerling

3. f3?!

The Walkerling variation of the Bishop's Opening is a chess opening that begins with the moves 1. e4 e5 2. Bc4 Nf6 3. f3!?. This move is considered an obvious error by chess experts, as it weakens White's pawn structure and hinders the development of the king's knight, as well as weakening the kingside.

Black's main options are:

/3...Bc5/ develops the bishop to an active square that attacks f2.

/3...Nc6/ aims to activate both knights to active squares and control the center.

/3...d5/ strikes back in the center and fights for a lead in development, which black already has.

However, Black cannot play 3...Nxe4?, aiming to win a rook with 4...Qh4+, because white simply has 5. Kf1!, simply being up a piece.

1. e4 e5 2. Bc4 Nf6 3. f3?!

主教开场：沃克林

3.f3？！

主教开局的沃克林变体是一种以走棋 1. e4 e5 2. Bc4 Nf6 3. f3!? 开始的国际象棋开局。这一着法被国际象棋专家认为是一个明显的错误，因为它削弱了白棋的兵结构，阻碍了王马的发展，同时也削弱了王翼。

黑棋的主要选择是：

/3...Bc5/ 将主教发展为攻击 f2 的活跃方格。

/3...Nc6/ 旨在激活两个骑士到活动方格并控制中心。

/3...d5/ 在中间反击并争取领先优势，而黑棋已经取得了领先优势。

然而，黑方不能下 3...Nxe4?，旨在以 4...Qh4+ 赢得车，因为白方只有 5.Kf1!，只是领先一子。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bc4/2...Nf6/3. f3/3...d5
explanations.text:
Bishop's Opening: Walkerling

3...d5!

This move is an aggressive response to white's passive 3. f3!? as it strikes in the center and opens up more lines for black's pieces.

White's main options are:

/4. exd5/ is the most popular and best option as it is an equal trade after 4...Nxd5 5. Bxd5 Qxd5.

/4. Bxd5/ usually transposes to the 4. exd5 line, after 4...Nxd5 5. exd5 Qxd5.

/4. Bb3/?! is a dubious option as it does not accept an important pawn trade as 4...dxe4 5. fxe4 and white's kingside is very weak, but this might have something with because after 5. fxe4, white still has a pawn in the center and it opens up f3 for the king's knight.

4. Bb5?! checks the black king, and its purpose is almost the same as 4. Bb3.

白方的主要选择是：

/4。 exd5/ 是最受欢迎和最好的选择，因为它是 4...Nxd5 5. Bxd5 Qxd5 之后的平等交易。

/4。 Bxd5/ 通常转置到 4. exd5 行，位于 4...Nxd5 5. exd5 Qxd5 之后。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bc4/2...Nf6/3. f4
explanations.text:
Bishop's Opening: Berlin Defence, Greco Gambit

3. f4?!

An interesting gambit. White gives up their f-pawn, offering a transposition to the Cozio Defence of the King's Gambit if Black accepts the gambit with 3...exf4. However, Black can choose to take the e-pawn with 3...Nxe4 instead, and White cannot play 4. fxe5?? as 4...Qh4+! starts a powerful attack.

Bishop's Opening: Berlin Defence, Greco Gambit

3. f4?!

An interesting gambit. White gives up their f-pawn, offering a transposition to the Cozio Defence of the King's Gambit if Black accepts the gambit with 3...exf4. explanations.textZh:
主教开局：柏林防守，格雷科开局

3.f4？！

一个有趣的策略。如果黑方接受 3...exf4 的开局，白方放弃他们的 f 兵，提供对国王开局的 Cozio 防御的换位。然而，黑方可以选择用 3...Nxe4 来拿电子兵，而白方不能下 4.fxe5??作为 4...Qh4+！开始强力攻击。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bc4/2...Nf6/3. f4/3...Nxe4
explanations.text:
Bishop's Opening: Berlin Defence, Greco Gambit

3...Nxe4

Black captures the free e-pawn with their knight. White cannot take Black's own e-pawn with 4. fxe5??, as after 4...Qh4+! a powerful attack is launched on White's king. White's best move is 4. d3, attacking the knight, and now 4...Qh4+ comes with less attacking power than if 4. fxe5?? were played.

3...Nxe4

explanations.textZh:
主教开局：柏林防守，格雷科开局

3...Nxe4

黑方用他们的马夺取了自由电子兵。白方不能用 4.fxe5?? 拿走黑方自己的电子兵，如 4...Qh4+ 之后！对白王发起了强大的攻击。白方最好的棋是 4.d3，攻击马，现在 4...Qh4+ 的攻击力比 4.fxe5 低？被演奏了。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bc4/2...Nf6/3. f4/3...Nxe4/4. d3
explanations.text:
Bishop's Opening: Berlin Defence, Greco Gambit

4. d3

White attacks Black's knight and avoids losing material with the tempting 4. fxe5??. Black can choose to retreat it with 4...Nd6, or try the same attacking idea if White played 4. fxe5??, 4...Qh4+. However, unlike the fxe5 version, 4...Qh4+ does not win a rook as after 5. g3! Nxg3 6. Nf3! the queen cannot go to e4 to check the White king and then take the rook on h1 with the knight on g3.
explanations.textEn:
Bishop's Opening: Berlin Defence, Greco Gambit

4. d3

White attacks Black's knight and avoids losing material with the tempting 4. fxe5??. Black can choose to retreat it with 4...Nd6, or try the same attacking idea if White played 4. fxe5??, 4...Qh4+. However, unlike the fxe5 version, 4...Qh4+ does not win a rook as after 5. g3! Nxg3 6. Nf3! the queen cannot go to e4 to check the White king and then take the rook on h1 with the knight on g3.
explanations.textZh:
主教开局：柏林防守，格雷科开局

4.d3

白棋攻击黑棋的马，并用诱人的 4.fxe5?? 避免损失材料。黑方可以选择用4...Nd6撤退，或者如果白方下4.fxe5??、4...Qh4+，则尝试相同的进攻思路。然而，与 fxe5 版本不同的是，4...Qh4+ 不会像 5.g3 之后那样赢得车！ Nxg3 6. Nf3！后不能去e4检查白王，然后在h1上拿车，而马在g3上。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bc4/2...Nf6/3. f4/3...Nxe4/4. fxe5
explanations.text:
Bishop's Opening: Berlin Defence, Greco Gambit

4. fxe5??

White got way too greedy and captured the seemingly free pawn on e5, but at a cost: 4...Qh4+! starts an overwhelming attack on White's king which will either win material or checkmate White.
explanations.textEn:
Bishop's Opening: Berlin Defence, Greco Gambit

4. fxe5??

White got way too greedy and captured the seemingly free pawn on e5, but at a cost: 4...Qh4+! starts an overwhelming attack on White's king which will either win material or checkmate White.
explanations.textZh:
主教开局：柏林防守，格雷科开局

4.fxe5??

白棋太贪心了，在 e5 上吃掉了看似免费的棋子，但付出的代价是：4...Qh4+！对白棋王发起压倒性的攻击，要么赢得材料，要么将死白棋。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bc4/2...Nf6/3. f4/3...Nxe4/4. fxe5/4...Qh4
explanations.text:
Bishop's Opening: Berlin Defence, Greco Gambit

4...Qh4+!

Black punishes White's careless 4. fxe5?? and will now either win material or checkmate the White king. White has three legal moves: 5. Kf1?? gets checkmated immediately to 5...Qf2#, 5. Ke2? leads to a long forced checkmate sequence after 5...Qf2+ 6. Kd3 Nc5+, and 5. g3 is the only non-losing move, but it will still lose a rook after 5...Nxg3 6. Nf3 Qe4+.
explanations.textEn:
Bishop's Opening: Berlin Defence, Greco Gambit

4...Qh4+!

Black punishes White's careless 4. fxe5?? and will now either win material or checkmate the White king. White has three legal moves: 5. Kf1?? gets checkmated immediately to 5...Qf2#, 5. Ke2? leads to a long forced checkmate sequence after 5...Qf2+ 6. Kd3 Nc5+, and 5. g3 is the only non-losing move, but it will still lose a rook after 5...Nxg3 6. Nf3 Qe4+.
explanations.textZh:
主教开局：柏林防守，格雷科开局

4...Qh4+！

黑棋惩罚白棋的粗心 4. fxe5??现在要么赢得材料，要么将死白王。白棋有 3 步合法棋步： 5. Kf1??立即被将死为 5...Qf2#, 5.Ke2?在 5...Qf2+ 6. Kd3 Nc5+ 之后会导致很长的强制将死序列，并且 5. g3 是唯一不输的着法，但在 5...Nxg3 6. Nf3 Qe4+ 之后仍然会失去车。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bc4/2...Nf6/3. f4/3...Nxe4/4. fxe5/4...Qh4/5. Ke2
explanations.text:
Bishop's Opening: Berlin Defence, Greco Gambit

5. Ke2?

White tries to avoid the loss of their rook, but in fact this leads to a long checkmating sequence after 5...Qf2+ 6. Kd3 Nc5+, where Stockfish says that there is a forced mate in 12 after 6...Nc5+.
explanations.textEn:
Bishop's Opening: Berlin Defence, Greco Gambit

5. Ke2?

White tries to avoid the loss of their rook, but in fact this leads to a long checkmating sequence after 5...Qf2+ 6. Kd3 Nc5+, where Stockfish says that there is a forced mate in 12 after 6...Nc5+.
explanations.textZh:
主教开局：柏林防守，格雷科开局

5.Ke2？

白棋试图避免失去车，但事实上这会导致 5...Qf2+ 6. Kd3 Nc5+ 之后的长将死序列，其中 Stockfish 说 6...Nc5+ 之后的 12 中存在强制交配。

explanations.text:
Bishop's Opening: Berlin Defence, Greco Gambit

5. Kf1??

This move may seem safe as it walks the king to a square that looks defended, but in fact it loses to an immediate checkmate, 5...Qf2#.
explanations.textEn:
Bishop's Opening: Berlin Defence, Greco Gambit

5. Kf1??

This move may seem safe as it walks the king to a square that looks defended, but in fact it loses to an immediate checkmate, 5...Qf2#.
explanations.textZh:
主教开局：柏林防守，格雷科开局

5.Kf1??

这一步棋看起来可能很安全，因为它将国王带到了一个看似被防守的方格，但实际上它输给了直接将死者 5...Qf2#。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Bc4/2...Nf6/3. f4/3...Nxe4/4. fxe5/4...Qh4/5. g3
explanations.text:
Bishop's Opening: Berlin Defence, Greco Gambit

5. g3

This move wisely avoids walking the king to e2 or f1 where it gets checkmated by force, and instead blocks the check. However, White will lose their rook after 5...Nxg3 6. Nf3 Qe4+ 7. Be2 Nxh1.
explanations.textEn:
Bishop's Opening: Berlin Defence, Greco Gambit

5. g3

This move wisely avoids walking the king to e2 or f1 where it gets checkmated by force, and instead blocks the check. However, White will lose their rook after 5...Nxg3 6. Nf3 Qe4+ 7. Be2 Nxh1.
explanations.textZh:
主教开局：柏林防守，格雷科开局

5.g3

这一举动明智地避免了将王带到 e2 或 f1 处，在那里它会被武力将死，而是阻止了检查。然而，白方将在 5...Nxg3 6. Nf3 Qe4+ 7. Be2 Nxh1 后失去车。

This rarely played slow move does little to give Black any issues. Black can play 2. ...Nf6 with d5 when the White Bishop is misplaced.

这种很少下的慢棋几乎不会给黑方带来任何问题。当白棋主教放错位置时，黑方可以下 2. ...Nf6 和 d5。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. f4
explanations.text:
2. f4 · King's gambit

White attacks Black's pawn on e5 with the f-pawn, even though that pawn is itself attacked and undefended. White seeks to pry Black's pawn away from control of d4, so that they may place their own pawn there. In addition, White's trying to open the f-file so that once they have castled, their rook is activated on the open file immediately.

The king's gambit is a very aggressive opening that comes with severe trade offs. By moving the f-pawn so early, before they have castled, White has greatly weakened their kingside and exposed their king to danger.

Accept the gambit

2...exf4, accepting the gambit, is the main move. Black grabs the extra pawn. Accepting the gambit and forcing White to justify an advantage is the most testing response. Although White has succeeded in deflecting the pawn, they cannot play 3. d4?! yet because Black threatens 3...Qh4+!.

Usually White controls h4 first with 3. Nf3, sometimes called the king's knight gambit. This leads to a variety of continuations that promise Black a superior position. In most lines, Black will try to hold on to the pawn with ...g5 and exploit the e1-h4 and a7-g1 diagonals with ...Qh4+ and ...Bc5.

3. Bc4, the bishop's gambit, is an alternative: White allows 3...Qh4+ intending Kf1 & Nf3 to gain tempo on the queen. The usual move is 3...Nf6, although 3...d5 and 3...Nc6 have their merits.

Decline the gambit

There are several effective ways Black may decline the gambit instead. The most popular and sound are 2...Bc5 and 2...d5.

It's important to realise two things: Black can't immediately exploit the weakened e1-h4 diagonal (2...Qh4+? 3. g3! and the queen has to go back) but they could were White to move their f-pawn. Therefore, White isn't really threatening fxe5 yet. That is to say, Black doesn't need to defend the e5-pawn directly, (say with 2...d6!?) because if White takes on e5, Black has the reply ...Qh4+!.

For example, 2...Bc5, the classical way to decline the gambit, and if 3. fxe5?? Qh4+! 4. g3 (4. Ke2?? Qxe4#) Qxe4+ picking up the rook on h1. 3. Nf3 is the main move: controlling h4 so that fxe5 (or Nxe5) is now a threat, 3...d6 to defend the pawn then White has a variety of plans including c3 & d4 and building a mammoth three pawn centre. Overall 2...Bc5 gives an even game and avoids the fireworks of the king's gambit accepted, but other than setting a few traps is not as critical of White's play.

2...d5, the Falkbeer countergambit, is the main way of declining the gambit in modern times. 3. exd5 exf4 4. Nf3 Nf6 is the main line: Black still takes the pawn on f4, but rather than holding on to the extra material, they want to trade it for an open position and easy development. With an open position and active pieces, Black expects that, all other things being equal, they must come out on top eventually due to White's king's side weaknesses.

2...Nc6, the queen's knight defence, is the most common way of declining the gambit in amateur games. After 3. Nf3, preventing ...Qh4, 3...d5 4. exd5 Qxd5 5. Nc3 scores tempo on the queen. At higher levels the main idea is 3...f5, the Miles defence.

Unorthodox moves

Other possible approaches, in roughly descending order of legitimacy, are:

2...Nf6, resembling a reversed Latvian gambit, was suggested by Petroff.

2...c5?! is the Mafia defence.

2...f5? is a dubious countergambit sometimes called the Panteldakis countergambit. Black volunteers to sabotage their king's side too, which White gets to exploit e.g. 3. exf5 exf4? 4. Qh5+. In the game Kennaugh vs Shirazi, the game continued 3...e4?! 4. Qh5+ Ke7 5. d3 Nf6! 6. Qg5?!, and Black went on to win a wild game.

2...Qf6?, the Norwalde variation, is playable but at best a mistake of missed opportunity.

2...f6?, bad.

2...g5??, called the Zilbermints double countergambit, is irredeemable.

History

The king's gambit is one of the oldest recorded openings. It was extremely popular during the Romantic era of chess, when attacking, tactical chess was in vogue and it was seen as unsporting to decline a gambit. Open any 19th century book of analysis and you will see it was regarded as one of the main-est of main lines.

This admirable opening, in which is comprehended every variety of the game... gives birth to the most intricate and beautiful combinations of which the chess-men are susceptible―Howard Staunton

In 1851, the opening was played in what would become one of the most famous chess games of all time, the Immortal Game, where Adolf Anderssen as White sacrificed twenty-one points of material and mated their opponent.

Towards the end of the century, the popularity of the gambit declined with improvements in technique for Black and as Steinitz's new "positional" chess began to displace Romantic chess. By the 1930s, Tarrasch wrote that the strength of the defences 2...d5, 2...Bc5, or 2...exf4 3.

Towards the end of the century, the popularity of the gambit declined with improvements in technique for Black and as Steinitz's new "positional" chess began to displace Romantic chess. By the 1930s, Tarrasch wrote that the strength of the defences 2...d5, 2...Bc5, or 2...exf4 3.
explanations.textZh:
2. f4·国王的策略

白方用 f 棋子攻击黑方 e5 上的棋子，即使该棋子本身受到攻击且没有防御。白方试图将黑方的棋子从 d4 的控制中撬开，以便他们可以将自己的棋子放在那里。此外，白方试图打开 f 文件，以便一旦他们出局，他们的车就会立即在打开的文件上激活。

国王的策略是一种非常激进的开局，伴随着严重的权衡。通过在 f 兵尚未攻城之前就移动 f 兵，白方极大地削弱了他们的王翼，并使他们的国王面临危险。

接受策略

2...exf4，接受开局，是主要举措。黑棋夺取多余的棋子。接受这一策略并迫使白棋证明优势是最考验人的反应。虽然白棋已经成功偏转棋子，但他们不能下3.d4？！但因为黑方威胁 3...Qh4+!。

通常白方首先用 3.Nf3 控制 h4，有时称为国王的骑士策略。这导致了一系列的延续，从而保证了黑方的优势地位。在大多数行中，黑方将尝试使用 ...g5 保住棋子，并使用 ...Qh4+ 和 ...Bc5 利用 e1-h4 和 a7-g1 对角线。

3. Bc4，主教的开局，是一种替代方案：白方允许 3...Qh4+ 意图 Kf1 和 Nf3 获得对皇后的节奏。通常的走法是 3...Nf6，尽管 3...d5 和 3...Nc6 有其优点。

拒绝策略

黑棋有几种有效的方法可以拒绝这一策略。最流行、最声音的是 2...Bc5 和 2...d5。

重要的是要认识到两件事：黑方不能立即利用削弱的 e1-h4 对角线（2...Qh4+？3.g3！而后必须后退），但他们可以由白方移动他们的 f 兵。因此，白棋还没有真正威胁到fxe5。也就是说，黑方不需要直接防守 e5 兵（例如 2...d6！？），因为如果白方吃 e5，黑方就会得到答复 ...Qh4+！。

例如，2...Bc5，拒绝策略的经典方法，如果 3.fxe5?? Qh4+！ 4. g3 (4. Ke2?? Qxe4#) Qxe4+ 在 h1 捡起车。 3. Nf3是主要走法：控制h4，使fxe5（或Nxe5）现在成为威胁，3...d6保卫棋子，然后白方有多种计划，包括c3和d4并建立一个庞大的三棋子中心。总体而言，2...Bc5 提供了一场均匀的比赛，并避免了接受的国王弃兵的烟火，但除了设置一些陷阱之外，对白棋的发挥并不那么重要。

2...d5，Falkbeer 反棋，是现代衰落棋的主要方式。 3. exd5 exf4 4. Nf3 Nf6 是主线：黑方仍然在 f4 上拿走棋子，但他们不想保留多余的材料，而是想用它来换取空位和轻松的发展。有了空位和活跃的棋子，黑方预计，在所有其他条件相同的情况下，由于白方国王的弱点，他们最终一定会占据上风。

2...Nc6，女王的骑士防御，是业余游戏中最常见的拒绝策略的方式。 3. Nf3之后，阻止...Qh4，3...d5 4. exd5 Qxd5 5. Nc3对皇后得分。在较高级别，主要思想是 3...f5，即迈尔斯防御。

非正统的举动

其他可能的方法（按合法性大致降序排列）是：

2...Nf6，类似于拉脱维亚的反向策略，是由彼得罗夫建议的。

2...c5？！是黑手党的防御。

2...f5？是一种可疑的反策略，有时称为潘特尔达基斯反策略。黑棋也自愿破坏他们国王的一方，白棋可以利用这一点，例如3. exf5 exf4？ 4.Qh5+。肯诺VS设拉子的比赛中，比赛继续3...e4？！ 4.Qh5+ Ke7 5.d3 Nf6！ 6. Qg5？！，黑棋继续赢得了一场狂野的比赛。

2...Qf6？，Norwalde 变体，可以玩，但充其量是错失机会的错误。

2...f6？，糟糕。

2...g5??，称为 Zilbermints 双反策略，是不可挽回的。

历史

国王的开局是有记录的最古老的开局之一。它在国际象棋的浪漫时代非常流行，当时进攻性、战术性的国际象棋很流行，拒绝下棋被认为是不道德的。打开任何一本 19 世纪的分析书籍，你都会发现它被认为是最重要的主线之一。

这个令人钦佩的开局，其中涵盖了棋局的每一个变化……产生了棋手们容易接受的最复杂和最美丽的组合——霍华德·斯汤顿

1851 年，在后来成为有史以来最著名的国际象棋游戏之一的“不朽棋”中，阿道夫·安德森（Adolf Anderssen）作为白棋牺牲了二十一点棋子，与对手交手。

到了世纪末，随着黑棋技术的进步以及斯坦尼茨新的“位置”国际象棋开始取代浪漫国际象棋，该策略的受欢迎程度下降。到 1930 年代，Tarrasch 写道，防御强度为 2...d5、2...Bc5 或 2...exf4 3。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. f4/2...Nc6
explanations.text:
2...Nc6 · Queen's knight defence

2...Nc6, a way to decline the king's gambit, is much more common in amateur games than in tournament chess. 2...Nc6 develops a piece and prepares to recapture on e5, though Black's pawn was not actually hanging because 3. fxe5?? can be answered with 3...Qh4+!.

3. Nf3 is the main move, as in many king's gambit lines. This controls h4, therefore preventing the riposte ...Qh4+, and White actually threatens fxe5. Though the engine line is 3...d5 4. exd5 Qxd5 5. Nc3 Qe6, Black's usual idea is 3...f5!?, the Miles defence. 3...exf4 4. d4 transposes to the MacLeod defence.

3. Nc3 transposes to the Max Lange defence of the Vienna gambit.

explanations.textZh:
2...NC6 · 女王骑士防御

2...Nc6，一种拒绝国王策略的方法，在业余比赛中比在锦标赛国际象棋中更常见。 2...Nc6 发展出一颗棋子并准备在 e5 上重新夺回，尽管黑棋的棋子实际上并没有挂起来，因为 3. fxe5？可以用 3...Qh4+! 来回答。

3. Nf3 是主要走法，正如许多国王的弃兵路线一样。这控制了 h4，因此阻止了反击...Qh4+，而白方实际上威胁到了 fxe5。尽管引擎线是 3...d5 4. exd5 Qxd5 5. Nc3 Qe6，黑方通常的想法是 3...f5!?，即迈尔斯防御。 3...exf4 4. d4 转置至麦克劳德防守。

3. Nc3 转换为维也纳开局的 Max Lange 防御。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. f4/2...d5
explanations.text:
2...d5 · Falkbeer countergambit

2...d5 is the most common way to decline the king's gambit (at least, for the moment: Black often takes the f-pawn later).

White has the choice of two centre pawns they may take, though 3. fxe5?? is a blunder as 3...Qh4+! 4. g3 Qxe4+ 5. Qe2 Qxh1 is most embarrassing.

3. exd5 is the main move, leading to a scramble for control of the d5, e4, and e5 squares. Black's traditional idea (called the Staunton line) is 3...e4, but more common today is 3...exf4 4. Nf3, transposing into the modern line of the king's gambit accepted, as if they had played 2...exf4 3. Nf3 d5 4. exd5.

3. Nf3, the Blackburne attack, postpones taking in the centre to develop the knight. This controls the h4 square, ending with the threat of ...Qh4+, and if 3...dxe4 (attacking the knight) 4. Nxe5!. After 3...exf4 4. exd4 this transposes. Alternatively, 3...Bg4 4. Be2 exf4 5. exd5 Bxf3 6. Bxf3 Qh4+ 7. Kf1 and Black equalises.

Other lines include:

3. d4?, the Hinrichsen gambit.

3. Nc3?!, the Milner-Barry variation.

History

The earliest recorded appearance of this countergambit comes from the games of 17th century chess player Gioachino Greco, who recorded the following miniature (Greco as White): 3. exd5 Qxd5 4. Nc3 Qe6 5. Nf3 exf4+ 6. Kf2 Bc5+ 7. d4 Bd6?? (...Be7 is better) 8. Bb5+ Kf8 9. Re1 Qf5?? (Black must give up the queen or is lost) 10. Re8# 1-0.

Ernst Falkbeer (1819―1885) was an Austrian chess master who played 2...d5 against Adolf Anderssen in 1851, with the continuation 3. exd5 e4. In 1905, Frank Marshall (1877―1944) introduced the continuation 3...c6.

explanations.textZh:
2...d5 · 福克比尔的对策

2...d5 是拒绝国王弃兵的最常见方法（至少目前是这样：黑方通常会稍后拿走 f 兵）。

白方可以选择他们可以采取的两个中心棋子，尽管 3. fxe5??是一个错误 3...Qh4+！ 4.g3 Qxe4+ 5.Qe2 Qxh1 最尴尬。

3. exd5是主要动作，导致对d5、e4和e5方格控制权的争夺。黑方的传统想法（称为斯汤顿线）是 3...e4，但今天更常见的是 3...exf4 4. Nf3，转换为已接受的国王弃兵的现代路线，就好像他们玩了 2...exf4 3. Nf3 d5 4. exd5。

3. Nf3，布莱克本进攻，推迟中锋发展骑士。它控制 h4 方格，以 ...Qh4+ 的威胁结束，如果 3...dxe4（攻击骑士）4. Nxe5！。在 3...exf4 4. exd4 之后进行转置。或者，3...Bg4 4. Be2 exf4 5. exd5 Bxf3 6. Bxf3 Qh4+ 7. Kf1 和黑棋相等。

其他线路包括：

3. d4？，Hinrichsen 策略。

3. Nc3？！，米尔纳-巴里变体。

历史

这种反棋的最早出现记录来自 17 世纪国际象棋棋手 Gioachino Greco 的棋局，他记录了以下缩影（Greco 为白）： 3. exd5 Qxd5 4. Nc3 Qe6 5. Nf3 exf4+ 6. Kf2 Bc5+ 7. d4 Bd6?? （...Be7 更好） 8. Bb5+ Kf8 9. Re1 Qf5？ （黑必须放弃后，否则就输了） 10. Re8# 1-0。

恩斯特·法尔克比尔（Ernst Falkbeer，1819―1885 年）是一位奥地利国际象棋大师，他于 1851 年与阿道夫·安德森 (Adolf Anderssen) 下棋 2...d5，并延续了 3. exd5 e4。 1905 年，弗兰克·马歇尔（Frank Marshall，1877―1944）推出了延续 3...c6。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. f4/2...d5/3. exd5
explanations.text:
3. exd5 · Falkbeer countergambit accepted

Accepting the d-pawn is the main move. From here, Black has three choices:

3...e4!? is the traditional idea, but it has fallen out of fashion due to 4. d3!, the Charousek gambit. If 4...Qxd5 5. Nc3 (hits queen) Bb4. If 4...Nf6 5. dxe4 with complications that favour White.

3...exf4 is the main move today. 4. Nf3 (to prevent Qh4+) transposes to the modern king's gambit accepted.

3...c6!? is the Nimzowitsch-Marshall countergambit that offers material for development.

3. exd5 · 接受 Falkbeer 对策

接受 d 兵是主要动作。至此，黑方有三种选择：

3...e4！？是传统的想法，但由于 4.d3!，Charousek 策略，它已经过时了。如果 4...Qxd5 5. Nc3（击中皇后）Bb4。如果 4...Nf6 5. dxe4 具有有利于白棋的复杂性。

3...exf4 是今天的主要走势。 4. Nf3（防止Qh4+）转置为已接受的现代国王的策略。

3...c6！？是为发展提供材料的尼姆佐维奇-马歇尔对策。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. f4/2...d5/3. exd5/3...c6
explanations.text:
Falkbeer Countergambit

3...c6!?

An interesting move to sacrifice a pawn for development. Nc3 exf4 Nf3 Bd6 is equal. The greedy dxc6?! is bad, as Black has superior development while White's kingside is weak. Bc5 ideas prevent castling kingside unless White diverts the bishop from the diagonal.

Qe2 cxd5 fxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 leads to equality.

Falkbeer Countergambit

Qe2 cxd5 fxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 leads to equality.
explanations.textZh:
福克比尔反击策略

3...c6！？

为了发展而牺牲棋子的举动很有趣。 Nc3 exf4 Nf3 Bd6 相等。贪婪的dxc6？！情况很糟糕，因为黑方发展优越，而白方王翼较弱。 BC5 的思路是防止王翼易位，除非白方将主教从对角线转移。

Qe2 cxd5 fxe5 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 导致相等。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. f4/2...d5/3. exd5/3...e4
explanations.text:
Falkbeer Countergambit

3...e4

After giving the pawn on d5, the e4 square is now free so Black pushes the e pawn instead of taking on f4. The idea is to ruin White's plan of opening the f file. The e4 pawn will also be quite a nuisance for White as it prevents natural development of the knight on f3. White will thus try to get rid of this pawn as soon as possible.

3...e4

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. f4/2...d6
explanations.text:
King's Gambit Declined

2...d6

This is one way to decline the King's Gambit. This can arise from many different positions, but this transposition to the King's Gambit Declined is most common. This is somewhat sounder than the King's Gambit Declined, Classical Variation, as in the Classical Variation, white can chase the bishop out of c5 and put more pressure on e5, especially with Nf3. Here, on the other hand, if white plays 3. Nf3?!, then black plays 3...exf4! transposing to the King's Gambit Accepted, Fischer Defense. This is similarly true with with 3. Nc3!?, but in this case, white gets a lot more compensation for the pawn compared to 3. Nf3. In fact, the best move here is 3. d3!, defending the pawn on f4 and blocking all transpositions to the King's Gambit Accepted. However, white had to make a concession for this: block his light-squared bishop. Nevertheless, 3.d3 leads to equality with best play. Note: If white plays 3. Bc4 (to not block the bishop), 3...exf4! also works.
