An improved version of 8.Nd4 is 8. O-O, which was played three times in the 2014 world rapid and blitz championships in Dubai. White postpones the decision about what to put on d4. If Black pre-empts Nd4 with ...Qd6, White can switch tack with 9.d4.
explanations.textZh:
8. d4，威胁 e5 兵，是真正控制黑方兵中心的走法 - 考虑到直接 8.Nxe5 是不可能的，因为白后在 8...fxe5 9.Qxe5+ Qe7 之后被钉住。

克鲁姆·格奥尔基耶夫（Krum Georgiev）尝试了 8. Nd4，不是为了炫耀白棋已经钉住了多少黑棋，而是威胁对 h5 进行皇后检查，这将剥夺黑棋的易位权。但这并不是一个威胁，因为...Qd6巩固了c6骑士并为d8上的国王腾出了空间。

8.Nd4的改进版本是8.O-O，在2014年迪拜世界快速和闪电战锦标赛上比赛了3次。白方推迟了 d4 下什么的决定。如果黑棋用...Qd6抢先Nd4，白棋可以用9.d4改变策略。

explanations.text:
8...Bg7 is a deceptive move. Yes, it defends the vulnerable e-pawn - but not by attacking the square it's standing on, which wouldn't actually work because it would still have three attackers and two (non-pinned) defenders. Instead it defends the e-pawn indirectly by allowing ...O-O, which will unpin the c6-knight and, more importantly, allow the king's rook to come to the e-file and make the white king and queen uncomfortable.

8...e4 looks impressive but it just freezes Black's central pawns into a block of ice. White can play around the block of ice with Nh4, Bf4 and Qh5, or can play c4 which hits the block of ice with a hammer.

8...Bg4 is also not as powerful as it looks, because 9.dxe5 fxe5 10.Qxe5+ breaks the pin with check, and 9...Bxf3 10.Qxf3 just gives up the bishop pair for nothing. Possibly less than nothing, as it speeds up the White queen's journey to h5.
explanations.textEn:
8...Bg7 is a deceptive move. Yes, it defends the vulnerable e-pawn - but not by attacking the square it's standing on, which wouldn't actually work because it would still have three attackers and two (non-pinned) defenders. Instead it defends the e-pawn indirectly by allowing ...O-O, which will unpin the c6-knight and, more importantly, allow the king's rook to come to the e-file and make the white king and queen uncomfortable.

8...e4 looks impressive but it just freezes Black's central pawns into a block of ice. White can play around the block of ice with Nh4, Bf4 and Qh5, or can play c4 which hits the block of ice with a hammer.

8...Bg4 is also not as powerful as it looks, because 9.dxe5 fxe5 10.Qxe5+ breaks the pin with check, and 9...Bxf3 10.Qxf3 just gives up the bishop pair for nothing. Possibly less than nothing, as it speeds up the White queen's journey to h5.
explanations.textZh:
8...Bg7 是一个欺骗性的着法。是的，它保护了脆弱的电子棋子 - 但不是通过攻击它所站立的方格，这实际上是行不通的，因为它仍然有三个攻击者和两个（未固定的）防御者。相反，它通过允许 ...O-O 来间接保护 e-pawn，这将取消 c6-knight 的锁定，更重要的是，允许国王的车来到 e-file 并使白国王和王后感到不舒服。

8...e4 看起来令人印象深刻，但它只是将黑方的中央棋子冻结成一块冰。白棋可以用 Nh4、Bf4 和 Qh5 围绕冰块下棋，也可以下 c4，用锤子击打冰块。

8...Bg4 也没有看起来那么强大，因为 9.dxe5 fxe5 10.Qxe5+ 通过检查破坏了引脚，而 9...Bxf3 10.Qxf3 只是白白放弃了主教对。可能比什么都没有好，因为它加速了白皇后到达 h5 的旅程。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...f5/4. Nc3/4...fxe4/5. Nxe4/5...Nf6/6. Nxf6
explanations.text:
6...Qxf6 is a useful developing move - many writers caution against bringing the queen out early, but without the b1-knight on the board she doesn't have to worry about losing tempos to Nb1-c3-d5 or Nb1-c3-e4 ideas. Any opening that features a quick ...e5 and ...f5 (looking at you, Latvian Gambit) will likely involve putting the queen on f6 and castling kingside to bring a rook to f8 and then mating White on the f-file.

6...gxf6 has been played by FM Danko Bokan. You get the same pawn structure as in the 6.Qe2 d5 7.Nxf6+ line but White still has the option of putting her queen on a square other than e2.

6...gxf6 已由 FM Danko Bokan 演奏。您得到与 6.Qe2 d5 7.Nxf6+ 行中相同的棋子结构，但白方仍然可以选择将她的皇后放在 e2 以外的方格上。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...f5/4. Nc3/4...fxe4/5. Nxe4/5...Nf6/6. Nxf6/6...Qxf6
explanations.text:
Having avoided committing the queen to e2 on move 6, White typically puts it there anyway with 7. Qe2. This restricts Black's options, because now ...d5 would self-pin the c6-knight allowing White to capture the e5-pawn for zero compensation.

Viktor Kupreichik mixed things up a couple times with 7. O-O. If Black reacts the same way she would after 7. Qe2, with 7...Be7, White has a huge positive score with the plan of Bxc6 and Qe1. But alert Black players found 7...Nd4! to take advantage of the fact that the e-pawn isn't under any pressure.

explanations.textZh:
在避免在第 6 步将后下到 e2 后，白方通常会用 7.Qe2 将其放在那里。这限制了黑方的选择，因为现在...d5将自行固定c6马，从而允许白方捕获e5兵以获得零补偿。

Viktor Kupreichik 有几次把 7. O-O 搞混了。如果黑棋的反应与 7.Qe2 后的反应相同，则 7...Be7，白棋对 Bxc6 和 Qe1 的计划有巨大的正分。但机警的黑人玩家发现了 7...Nd4！利用电子典当没有任何压力的事实。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...f5/4. Nc3/4...fxe4/5. Nxe4/5...Nf6/6. Nxf6/6...Qxf6/7. Qe2
explanations.text:
Attempting to defend the e-pawn with moves like 7...d6 or 7...Bd6 are ultimately futile. Either 7...d6 8.d4 or 7...Bd6 8.d4 (not allowing Black the trick 8.Bxc6 dxc6 9.d4 Bg4) just win it outright.

So instead Black gambits the pawn with 7...Be7. The compensation will be in the form of open lines for the rooks and an unopposed light-squared bishop.

So instead Black gambits the pawn with 7...Be7. The compensation will be in the form of open lines for the rooks and an unopposed light-squared bishop.
explanations.textZh:
尝试用 7...d6 或 7...Bd6 之类的动作来保卫 e-pawn 最终是徒劳的。 7...d6 8.d4 或 7...Bd6 8.d4（不允许黑棋 8.Bxc6 dxc6 9.d4 Bg4）直接获胜。

因此，黑方用 7...Be7 弃兵。补偿将以车的开放线和无对手的浅方主教的形式进行。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...f5/4. Nc3/4...fxe4/5. Nxe4/5...Nf6/6. Nxf6/6...Qxf6/7. Qe2/7...Be7
explanations.text:
White accepts the gambit with 8. Bxc6, planning to capture on e5 once the guard is removed.

Castling kingside is still sub-optimal due to the ...Nd4 option (compare the position after 6...Qxf6).
explanations.textEn:

explanations.textZh:
白棋接受了 8.Bxc6 的策略，计划在防守被移除后在 e5 上吃掉。

由于 ...Nd4 选项，王翼易位仍然不是最佳（比较 6...Qxf6 之后的位置）。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...f5/4. Nc3/4...fxe4/5. Nxe4/5...Nf6/6. Nxf6/6...Qxf6/7. Qe2/7...Be7/8. Bxc6
explanations.text:
Here's an example of how chess opening theory moves with the times.

8...dxc6 was by far the more common move until the mid-2000s. It seems logical to open a diagonal for the bishop that it can actually use, right? The same exchange in the Exchange Ruy Lopez is always met with dxc6.

But then along came Teimour Radjabov and revived the whole 5...Nf6 line based on the innovation 8...bxc6, and now every top player who tries this line - Zvjagintsev, Timmerman, Fressinet - goes 8...bxc6.

Why 8...bxc6 and not 8...dxc6? The intelligent answer is something to do with capturing towards the centre and pawn islands. The honest answer is that Black players tried 8...dxc6 and laid an egg, so they tried something different.

explanations.textZh:
这是国际象棋开局理论如何与时俱进的一个例子。

8...dxc6 是 2000 年代中期之前最常见的举措。为主教打开一条它实际可以使用的对角线似乎是合乎逻辑的，对吧？在交易所 Ruy Lopez 中的同一交易所总是会遇到 dxc6。

但后来 Teimour Ra​​djabov 出现，并在创新 8...bxc6 的基础上复兴了整个 5...Nf6 系列，现在每个尝试该系列的顶级玩家 - Zvjagintsev、Timmerman、Fressinet - 都选择 8...bxc6。

为什么是 8...bxc6 而不是 8...dxc6？明智的答案与夺取中心和典当岛有关。诚实的答案是，黑人玩家尝试了 8...dxc6 并下了一个蛋，所以他们尝试了不同的东西。

explanations.text:
9. Nxe5 is the main line. White simply captures the free pawn with the nearest piece to hand.

9. Qxe5 has been played by Michael Adams, because being a pawn up and taking the queens off is usually what you want to do, but in this case simplifying hurts White's winning percentage as well as Black's. The queen enjoys being the most mobile piece on the board; if you exchange her off then that title would pass to the Black bishops, and there are two of them.

9. d4 is a fun idea of Swedish GM Emanuel Berg's, taken up by Alexei Shirov. It's not a gambit in that if Black grabs the pawn with 9...exd4, White shoves the queen away with 10.Bg5 and grabs it back. It's a pseudo-gambit in that White had the chance of going 1 pawn up and instead decided to be 0 pawns up.

explanations.textZh:
9、Nxe5为主线。白方只需用手边最近的棋子吃掉自由棋子即可。

9. Qxe5 由迈克尔·亚当斯 (Michael Adams) 扮演，因为作为棋子并拿走皇后通常是您想要做的事情，但在这种情况下，简化会损害白棋和黑棋的胜率。皇后喜欢成为棋盘上最具机动性的棋子；如果你把她交换掉，那么这个头衔就会传给黑人主教，而他们有两个。

9. d4 是瑞典总经理 Emanuel Berg 的一个有趣想法，后来被 Alexei Shirov 采纳。这不是一个策略，因为如果黑方用 9...exd4 抓住棋子，白方用 10.Bg5 将皇后推开并将其夺回来。这是一个伪策略，因为白方本来有机会上 1 兵，但却决定上 0 兵。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...f5/4. Nc3/4...fxe4/5. Nxe4/5...Nf6/6. Nxf6/6...Qxf6/7. Qe2/7...Be7/8. Bxc6/8...bxc6/9. Nxe5
explanations.text:
9...O-O looks like the best developing move Black has, immediately bringing the rook to the open f-file. What could be better than that?

9...Qe6 could be better than that. Catching the opposing king in the centre is half the fun of sacrificing pawns, and here 10.O-O?? would unprotect the White queen and so drop a piece to 10...d6.

10.d4 is surprisingly popular given that it doesn't actually get out of the pin! (It does help develop a piece though.) Black has tried various moves to claim some initiative; Radjabov's choice is 10...Bf6, 10...O-O is also obvious, 10...a5 prepares ...Ba6 hitting the queen, 10...c5 immediately challenges the d-pawn.

Karjakin tried 10.Nf3 against Radjabov, which does get out of the pin. White loses castling privileges after 10...Qxe2 11.Kxe2 but can easily castle by hand with Re1 and Kf1.

Dominguez Perez tried 10.Nc4 against Fressinet, to similar effect.

10.Qe3 is a radical solution tried by Frolyanov and Timofeev. Black has ...Ba6, ...Bf6 and ...c5 options after mutual kingside castling.

explanations.textZh:
9...O-O 看起来是黑棋发展得最好的一步，立即将车带到开放的 f 档。还有什么比这更好的呢？

9...Qe6 可能比这更好。在中心抓住对方的国王是牺牲棋子的一半乐趣，而这里 10.O-O??会取消对白皇后的保护，因此将棋子落到 10...d6。

10.d4 出人意料地受欢迎，因为它实际上并没有摆脱困境！ （不过，这确实有助于发展棋子。）布莱克尝试了各种走法来占据主动权； Radjabov的选择是10...Bf6，10...O-O也很明显，10...a5准备...Ba6击中后，10...c5立即挑战d-兵。

卡尔亚金尝试用 10.Nf3 对抗拉贾博夫，但确实出局了。白方在 10...Qxe2 11.Kxe2 之后失去了易位特权，但可以轻松地用手中的 Re1 和 Kf1 进行易位。

多明戈斯·佩雷斯（Dominguez Perez）尝试对弗雷西内使用 10.Nc4，取得了类似的效果。

10.Qe3是Frolyanov和Timofeev尝试过的激进解决方案。在相互王侧易位后，黑方有 ...Ba6、...Bf6 和 ...c5 选项。

explanations.text:
9. Nxe5 is the main line. White needs to capture the pawn now otherwise Black will play ...Bd6 and ...Bg4 and the window will be shut.

Why is it not a good idea to capture with 9. Qxe5, since White will be a pawn up with the queens off? Because Black doesn't have to obligingly exchange queens on e5. Instead she can play 9...Bg4 to exploit the brittle knight on f3, which won't have any good squares after 10.Qxf6 Bxf6, and if White has to play gxf3 her kingside pawn majority will be nobbled. (10.Qxc7? is suicide with White so under-developed. The simple 10...O-O! gives Black an irresistible attack.)

explanations.textZh:
9、Nxe5为主线。白棋现在需要吃掉棋子，否则黑棋将下...Bd6 和...Bg4 并且窗口将被关闭。

为什么用 9.Qxe5 吃子不是一个好主意，因为白棋在皇后离开的情况下将成为棋子？因为黑方不必在 e5 上主动交换皇后。相反，她可以下 9...Bg4 来利用 f3 上的脆弱骑士，在 10.Qxf6 Bxf6 之后不会有任何好的方格，如果白方必须下 gxf3，她的王翼兵多数将被贵族化。 （10.Qxc7？是白棋不发达的自杀。简单的10...O-O！给黑棋带来了不可抗拒的攻击。）

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...f5/4. Nc3/4...fxe4/5. Nxe4/5...Nf6/6. Nxf6/6...Qxf6/7. Qe2/7...Be7/8. Bxc6/8...dxc6/9. Nxe5
explanations.text:
9...Bf5 is a useful developing move. 9...O-O is also a useful developing move.

Why is ...Bf5 more popular than ...O-O? It comes down to a general principle of opening theory: postpone the hard decisions for as long as you can. Black in this position no longer has to decide where to put the c8-bishop. The White knight is hitting d7 and g4, and on e6 the bishop will be vulnerable to tactics like Nxc6 as soon as White gets a rook to the e-file. So it has to go to f5. That's an easy decision. Whether Black wants to castle queenside or kingside is a hard decision. Make the easy decision first!

为什么...Bf5 比...O-O 更受欢迎？这归结为开放理论的一般原则：尽可能推迟艰难的决定。黑棋在这个位置上不再需要决定将c8象放在哪里。白骑士正在打 d7 和 g4，而在 e6 上，一旦白棋获得了 e 档的车，主教将很容易受到 Nxc6 等战术的影响。所以必须转到f5。这是一个简单的决定。黑棋想要在后侧还是王侧筑垒是一个艰难的决定。首先做出简单的决定！

explanations.text:
What happens next in this position depends more on what Black is planning than on what White's next move is.

Scenario 1: White and Black both castle kingside, Black attacks the e5-knight with ...Bd6, White defends it with d4 and possibly f4 too, Black swaps it off and gets a light-square bind to compensate for White's extra passed pawn.

There are three routes by which Scenario 1 can come about: 10. O-O, 10. d4 and, surprisingly, 10. d3. White loses a tempo in the 10.d3 line by playing d2-d3-d4, but Black also loses a tempo by playing Ra8-e8-d8. It all makes sense - see below!

Scenario 2: White castles kingside, Black castles queenside, Black attacks the e5-knight with ...Rhe8 and ...Bd6, White counter-attacks with Qf2 and claims an advantage based on some devilish tactics along the f-file.

There are two ways of arriving at Scenario 2: 10. O-O and 10. d3. The 10.d4 line diverges if Black goes 10...O-O-O, because the pawn is immediately attacked and White has to take a move to defend it.

In fact, 10.d4 tends to provoke Black into playing 10...O-O-O to exploit the loose pawn - whereas against 10.d3 or 10.O-O, the main line of the 10...O-O-O variation scores extremely well for White. So to maximise the chances of ending up in the 10...O-O lines, White needs to play 10.O-O or 10.d3 here.

What's the difference between 10.O-O and 10.d3? This is a little complicated. 10.O-O means that White retains the option of playing d2-d4 in one move if Black castles kingside - and will usually exercise that option with 10...O-O 11.d4, after which follows 11...Bd6 12.f4 Bxe5 13.dxe5 Qg6 14.Rf2 Rd8. So surely if White goes 10.d3, Black can come out a tempo up by playing 11...Bd6 and 12...Rd8? Sadly for Black, the move ...Re8 turns out to be necessary to force White into playing d4. If Black doesn't bother threatening the e5-knight, White can instead play the manoeuvre Bc1-d2-c3, which would make the queen on f6 feel very uncomfortable.

If Black doesn't bother threatening the e5-knight, White can instead play the manoeuvre Bc1-d2-c3, which would make the queen on f6 feel very uncomfortable.
explanations.textZh:
在这个位置上接下来发生的事情更多地取决于黑方的计划而不是白方的下一步行动。

场景1：白棋和黑棋都在王翼，黑棋用...Bd6攻击e5骑士，白棋用d4和可能的f4防守它，黑棋将其换掉并获得一个浅方束缚以补偿白棋额外通过的棋子。

场景 1 可以通过三种途径实现：10. O-O、10. d4 以及令人惊讶的 10. d3。白方在 10.d3 线上通过 d2-d3-d4 失去了节奏，但黑方通过 Ra8-e8-d8 也失去了节奏。这一切都是有道理的——见下文！

场景2：白方城堡王侧，黑方城堡后侧，黑方用...Rhe8和...Bd6攻击e5骑士，白方用Qf2反击，并基于f线的一些邪恶战术声称优势。

有两种方法可以达到场景 2：10.O-O 和 10.d3。如果黑方走 10...O-O-O，10.d4 线就会发散，因为棋子立即受到攻击，而白方必须采取行动来防御它。

事实上，10.d4 往往会激怒黑棋下 10...O-O-O，以利用松散的兵 - 而对抗 10.d3 或 10.O-O，10...O-O-O 变体的主线对白棋得分非常高。因此，为了最大限度地提高进入 10...O-O 线的机会，白方需要在这里下 10.O-O 或 10.d3。

10.O-O 和 10.d3 有什么区别？这有点复杂。 10.O-O 意味着如果黑方占据王侧，白方保留一步下 d2-d4 的选择权 - 并且通常会使用 10...O-O 11.d4 执行该选择，之后是 11...Bd6 12.f4 Bxe5 13.dxe5 Qg6 14.Rf2 Rd8。那么如果白方走 10.d3，黑方可以通过下 11...Bd6 和 12...Rd8 加快节奏吗？可悲的是，对于黑棋来说，...Re8 棋是迫使白棋下 d4 所必需的。如果黑方不去威胁e5马，白方可以采取Bc1-d2-c3策略，这会让f6的后感到非常不舒服。

explanations.text:
The move 4.d3 defended e4 but also threatened to snaffle the f5-pawn into the bargain, because now Black won't have the instant rejoinder ...e4.

4...fxe4 is the only move to justify the Black pawn thrust.

4.d3 步棋捍卫了 e4，但也威胁要将 f5 兵纳入讨价还价中，因为现在黑棋不会立即反驳 ...e4。

4...fxe4 是证明黑棋推力合理的唯一走法。

explanations.text: 5...Nf6 is the only move. As well as attacking the e4-pawn, it's a case of making the easy decisions first: the g8-knight is the only Black piece that has an obvious square to go to.

explanations.text: There are a few minor moves here, but if White notices that the e-pawn doesn't need to be directly defended, then 6. O-O makes the most sense, avoiding a potential pin or check after 6... Bb4, which would allow Black to develop the dark squared bishop and play d6 more easily. 6... Nxe4? in response would be a tactical error, allowing 7. Re1 or Qe2 with a strong attack along the e file, as 7... d5 allows 8. Nxe5 with the c6 knight pinned.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...f5/4. d3/4...fxe4/5. dxe4/5...Nf6/6. O-O
explanations.text:
Time for Black to develop some more pieces. Spoiler: the pawn currently on d7 isn't going to make it to d5 at this point, because that would leave e5 hanging. So it'll have to go to d6 if the c8-bishop wants to get out.

The immediate 6...d6 would shut in the f8-bishop. That's okay, it's got a perfectly good square on e7.

6...Bc5 makes sure that the bishop doesn't get shut in, but becomes a pawn sacrifice after 7. Bxc6 bxc6 8. Nxe5.

If ...Bc5 is often a luxury Black can't afford in the Ruy Lopez, surely this applies double in the Schliemann Defence where the Black kingside has already been opened up with ...f5? Black's argument is that firstly, the open f-file is an attacking strength as well as a defensive weakness, and allows Black to fantasize about targeting f2 with ...O-O and ...Nxe4/...Ng4 to go with ...Bc5, so that gives White something to worry about. Secondly, the fact that the d-pawn is gone means that White doesn't have the simple plan of c3 and d4 with gain of time against the bishop.

If Black captures on e4 immediately, White has numerous strong options. 7.Nxe5, threatening 8. Qh5+, has to be met with 7...Nxe5, and then 8.Re1 wins the piece straight back with an ongoing attack (8...Nf6? 9.f4!) The immediate 7. Re1 or Qe2 are also strong, as 7... d5 allows 8.Nxe5. Regardless, the e file becomes a huge liability for Black with the king still stuck in the center.

explanations.textZh:
是时候黑棋再开发一些棋子了。剧透：当前位于 d7 的 pawn 此时不会到达 d5，因为这会使 e5 挂起。因此，如果 c8 主教想要退出，就必须进入 d6。

紧接着的 6...d6 将关闭 f8 主教。没关系，e7 上有一个完美的正方形。

6...Bc5 确保主教不会被关在里面，而是在 7. Bxc6 bxc6 8. Nxe5 之后成为典当牺牲品。

如果...Bc5 通常是黑方在鲁伊·洛佩兹 (Ruy Lopez) 中买不起的奢侈品，那么这肯定适用于施利曼防御 (Schliemann Defense)，其中黑方王翼已经用 ...f5 打开了？黑方的论点是，首先，开放的 f 档既是攻击优势，也是防守弱点，并且允许黑方幻想用 ...O-O 和 ...Nxe4/...Ng4 瞄准 f2 来配合 ...Bc5，因此这让白方有一些担心。其次，d兵消失的事实意味着白方没有c3和d4的简单计划来赢得对抗主教的时间。

如果黑方立即吃 e4，白方有许多强有力的选择。 7.Nxe5，威胁8.Qh5+，必须遇到7...Nxe5，然后8.Re1通过持续的攻击直接赢得棋子（8...Nf6？9.f4！）直接的7.Re1或Qe2也很强，因为7...d5允许8.Nxe5。无论如何，e 档对黑棋来说是一个巨大的负担，而王仍然被困在中间。

explanations.text:
Now that Black is no longer vulnerable to Nxe5 tricks, the e4-pawn needs to be defended. The economical-looking 7.Re1, normally a very sensible move in the Ruy Lopez, would be dangerous in the Schliemann because it would weaken f2, the target of Black's future pressure along the f-file.

7. Nc3 develops an undeveloped piece to its natural square. Nothing wrong with that!

7. Qd3 is a move that's recommended against 6...Bc5, because after 6...Bc5 7.Qd3 O-O?? White simply wins a piece with 8.Qc4+, so Black is prevented from castling for a while. However, there's currently no bishop on c5 to win, and if White wants to prevent Black from castling after 7.Nc3 she always has Bc4. White may also lose a tempo if Black's light-squared bishop comes to g4 and swaps itself for the f3-knight, because the queen could have recaptured directly from d1. On the positive side, putting the queen rather than the bishop on c4 has the advantage of maintaining the pin on the c6-knight that Black brought upon herself by playing 6...d6. Results-wise there isn't much to choose between the two moves.

explanations.textZh:
现在黑方不再容易受到 Nxe5 技巧的影响，e4 兵需要防守。看似经济的 7.Re1，通常在鲁伊·洛佩兹 (Ruy Lopez) 中是非常明智的举动，但在施利曼 (Schliemann) 中却是危险的，因为它会削弱 f2，而 f2 是黑方未来沿 f 线施压的目标。

7. Nc3 将未展开的棋子展开至其自然方格。没有什么问题！

7. Qd3 是推荐对抗 6...Bc5 的棋步，因为在 6...Bc5 之后 7.Qd3 O-O??白方只需以 8.Qc4+ 赢得一颗棋子，因此黑方暂时无法进行易位。然而，目前c5上没有主教可以获胜，如果白方想阻止黑方在7.Nc3之后进行易位，她总是有Bc4。如果黑方的光方主教来到g4并将自己换成f3骑士，白方也可能会失去节奏，因为后可以直接从d1夺回。从积极的一面来看，将后而不是主教放在 c4 上有利于保持黑方通过下 6...d6 带来的 c6 马的优势。从结果来看，这两种举措之间没有太多选择。

explanations.text:
Having put the pawn on d6, the only square available for the f8-bishop is e7, so it might as well go there immediately with 7...Be7. The c8-bishop still has options, and the option of breaking the pin on the c6-knight with Bd7 may be particularly useful, so it typically stays put for now.

7...Bg4 is also played, inviting White to transpose to 7.Qd3 lines with 8.Qd3 which gets out of the pin.

explanations.textZh:
将棋子放在 d6 上后，f8 象唯一可用的方格是 e7，因此它最好立即用 7...Be7 去那里。 c8主教仍然有选择，并且用Bd7打破c6骑士上的销钉的选项可能特别有用，所以它通常暂时保留。

7...Bg4 也被打出，邀请白方将 8.Qd3 移调至 7.Qd3 线，而 8.Qd3 则出局。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...f5/4. d4
explanations.text:
This variation counterattacks in the center by challenging the e-pawn, like the Vienna Gambit with 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Nf6 3. f4 d5. Black's best and by far most common option is 4...fxe4.

4. ...fxe4

If Black takes the e-pawn, White's has two main options. 5. Nxe5 wins the pawn back, but runs into complications after 5. ... Nxe5 6. dxe5 c6. Now if the white bishop retreats, Black has 7... Qa5+ winning the e5 pawn and leaving Black better. (Note that in the Deferred Schliemann, because the white bishop is no longer on b5, c6 no longer comes with tempo, so this line is worse for Black. Thus, 5. d4 is the most common response to the Delayed Schliemann.) Thus, the most common line for white is 7. Nc3?!, a piece sacrifice. Play usually follows 7... cxb5 8. Nxe4 d5 9. exd6 Nf6, with an unclear position.

The other option is 5. Bxc6, after which Black enjoys the two bishops in exchange for a worse pawn structure and a white knight on e5 after either recapture on c6. 5... exf3 is less recommended, as after 6. Bxf3 White can quickly castle and place pressure along the e file.

4. ... exd4

If Black takes the d-pawn, White's most common move according to Lichess's Master games explorer is e5, pushing the pawn forward and taking control of the f6 and d6 squares.

4. ... Nxd4

If Black takes the d-pawn with the knight (which resembles the Ruy Lopez Bird Variation), it hits the bishop on b5, so Nxe5 is not an option. 5. Nxd4 is the most common move, followed by 5. ... exd4 6. O-O c6.

4. ... Nf6

If Black plays Nf6, 5. dxe5 is the most common move, followed by 5. ... Nxe4.

explanations.textZh:
这种变化通过挑战 e-pawn 在中心进行反击，就像维也纳开局一样 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Nf6 3. f4 d5。黑方最好且迄今为止最常见的选择是 4...fxe4。

4. ...fxe4

如果黑方拿走电子兵，白方有两个主要选择。 5. Nxe5 赢回棋子，但在 5. ... Nxe5 6. dxe5 c6 之后遇到麻烦。现在，如果白象撤退，黑方有 7...Qa5+ 赢得 e5 兵，让黑方更好。 （请注意，在延迟施利曼中，由于白棋主教不再在b5上，c6不再带有速度，因此这条线对黑棋来说更糟糕。因此，5.d4是延迟施利曼最常见的反应。）因此，白棋最常见的线是7.Nc3？！，棋子牺牲。打法通常遵循7... cxb5 8. Nxe4 d5 9. exd6 Nf6，位置不明确。

另一个选择是 5.Bxc6，之后黑方享受两个象，以换取更差的兵结构和 e5 上的白马，然后在 c6 上重新夺回。 5... exf3 不太推荐，如 6 之后。 Bxf3 白棋可以快速城堡并沿着 e 档施加压力。

4....exd4

如果黑方拿走 d 兵，根据 Lichess 的 Master games explorer，白方最常见的走法是 e5，将棋子向前推并控制 f6 和 d6 方格。

4. ... Nxd4

如果黑方用马拿下 d 兵（类似于鲁伊·洛佩兹伯德变例），它会在 b5 上击中主教，因此 Nxe5 不是一个选择。 5. Nxd4 是最常见的走法，其次是 5. ... exd4 6. O-O c6。

4....NF6

如果黑方下 Nf6，5. dxe5 是最常见的棋步，其次是 5. ... Nxe4。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...f5/4. exf5
explanations.text:
4. exf5!? · Jaenisch gambit accepted

Accepting the "free" pawn is inaccurate, as Black can regain the pawn with extra tempi and space.

After 4...e4, White's knight is kicked and is low on squares: g5 and h4 are controlled by Black'[s queen, while Black's knight controls e4 and d5. (The addition of this knight is the key difference between the Jaenisch and Latvian gambits accepted, 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 f5?! 2. exf5!) Un-developing the knight to g1 would be a big concession to Black.

To make room for the knight to go elsewhere, White has the manoeuvre 5. Qe2, pinning and attacking the e4 pawn, 5...Qe7 un-pins it, 6. Bxc6 with the idea of moving the knight to d4 where it defends the f5-pawn from Black's bishop. 6...dxc6 7. Nd4 . White may followed with Ne6 in some lines, such as after 7...Qe5. After 6...bxc6 7.Nd4, Black will likely play 7...Nf6, and eventually either Qe5 or c5 and then d5 to try to win the pawn back.

5. Bxc6 dxc6 6. Nd5? allows 6...Bxf5 with the threat of ...Qd4. If 6. Qe2 the line can transpose if Black plays 6...Qe7, but better is 6...Bxf5 .

History

Though not now considered an accurate way to refute the gambit, giving Black an even game, 4. exf5!? has been seen occasionally. Capablanca lost in this line to William Pratt in an exhibition simul game in 1909.

Sample game

Paul de Schloezer vs Mikhail Chigorin, 1878

1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 f5 3. exf5 Nc6?! 4. Bb5?

This position is arrived at by transposition from a Latvian gambit. 4. d5 was better: allowing both bishops into the game, White would be able to answer 4...e4 with 5. Ng5! and the knight is defended.

4...Bc5?!

4...e5 is an improvement and the main move today. The text move allows 5. O-O, and due to the open e-file White at the minimum wins the pawn (e.g. 5. O-O, threatens Nxe5 as ...Nxe5 Re1! is a pin, 5...d6? 6. Re1 Nf6 7. d4 Bb6 8. dxe5 Ng4 9. exd6+ Kf8 ).

5. Bxc6 dxc6 6. Nxe5 Bxf5

6...Bxf2+ 7. Kxf2 Qd4+ attacking the knight wins Black a pawn back

7. Qh5+ g6 8. Nxg6??

This appears to be winning material but in fact White's king is too weak.

8...hxg6 9. Qxh8 Qe7+ 10. Kd1 Bxf2

10...Bg4+ would be mate were it not for 11. f3, so Black first eliminates the f-pawn.

11. Qxg8+? Kd7 12. Qc4

Black is down six points of material but has an overwhelming attack on White's king, who is stranded in the middle of the board, and White has only their queen developed. White attempts to stop the bishop from coming to g4.

12...Re8 0-1

Black threatens ...Qe1+ Rxe1 Rxe1#.

Though not now considered an accurate way to refute the gambit, giving Black an even game, 4. exf5!? has been seen occasionally. Capablanca lost in this line to William Pratt in an exhibition simul game in 1909.

Sample game

Paul de Schloezer vs Mikhail Chigorin, 1878

1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 f5 3. exf5 Nc6?! 4. Bb5?

This position is arrived at by transposition from a Latvian gambit. 4. d5 was better: allowing both bishops into the game, White would be able to answer 4...e4 with 5. Ng5! and the knight is defended.

4...Bc5?!

4...e5 is an improvement and the main move today. The text move allows 5. O-O, and due to the open e-file White at the minimum wins the pawn (e.g. 5. O-O, threatens Nxe5 as ...Nxe5 Re1! is a pin, 5...d6? 6. Re1 Nf6 7. d4 Bb6 8. dxe5 Ng4 9. exd6+ Kf8 ).

5. Bxc6 dxc6 6. Nxe5 Bxf5

6...Bxf2+ 7. Kxf2 Qd4+ attacking the knight wins Black a pawn back

7. Qh5+ g6 8. Nxg6??

This appears to be winning material but in fact White's king is too weak.

8...hxg6 9. Qxh8 Qe7+ 10. Kd1 Bxf2

10...Bg4+ would be mate were it not for 11. f3, so Black first eliminates the f-pawn.

11. Qxg8+? Kd7 12. Qc4

Black is down six points of material but has an overwhelming attack on White's king, who is stranded in the middle of the board, and White has only their queen developed. White attempts to stop the bishop from coming to g4.

12...Re8 0-1

Black threatens ...Qe1+ Rxe1 Rxe1#.
explanations.textZh:
4.exf5！？ · Jaenisch 策略被接受

接受“自由”棋子是不准确的，因为黑方可以通过额外的速度和空间重新获得棋子。

4...e4 之后，白方的马被踢出，棋格位置较低：g5 和 h4 由黑方后控制，而黑方的马控制 e4 和 d5。 （增加这个马是 Jaenisch 和拉脱维亚策略之间的主要区别，1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 f5？！ 2. exf5！）不将马发展到 g1 将是对黑方的一个很大让步。

为了给马去其他地方腾出空间，白方采取了策略 5. Qe2，固定并攻击 e4 棋子，5...Qe7 取消固定它，6. Bxc6 的想法是将马移动到 d4，在那里它可以保护 f5 棋子免受黑方象的侵害。 6...dxc6 7. Nd4 。在某些行中，白棋可能会跟 Ne6，例如 7...Qe5 之后。在 6...bxc6 7.Nd4 之后，黑方可能会下 7...Nf6，最终要么 Qe5 要么 c5，然后是 d5，试图赢回棋子。

5.Bxc6 dxc6 6.ND5？允许 6...Bxf5 并威胁 ...Qd4。如果 6.Qe2 如果黑方下 6...Qe7 则该线可以调换，但更好的是 6...Bxf5 。

历史

尽管现在不被认为是反驳该策略的准确方法，但给黑方带来了一场平局，4. exf5！？偶尔也见过。 1909 年，卡帕布兰卡在一场表演赛中输给了威廉·普拉特。

示例游戏

保罗·德·施洛泽 vs 米哈伊尔·奇戈林，1878 年

1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 f5 3. exf5 Nc6？！ 4.Bb5？

这个立场是通过转换拉脱维亚策略得出的。 4. d5 更好：允许两位主教都进入游戏，白方将能够用 5. Ng5 回答 4...e4！骑士受到保护。

4...Bc5？！

4...e5 是一项改进，也是今天的主要举措。文本移动允许 5. O-O，并且由于打开的电子文件，白棋至少赢得棋子（例如 5. O-O，威胁 Nxe5，因为 ...Nxe5 Re1! 是一个 pin，5...d6? 6. Re1 Nf6 7. d4 Bb6 8. dxe5 Ng4 9. exd6+ Kf8 ）。

5.Bxc6 dxc6 6.Nxe5 Bxf5

6...Bxf2+ 7. Kxf2 Qd4+ 攻击马赢得黑棋回兵

7.Qh5+g6 8.Nxg6??

这看似是获胜的材料，但实际上白棋的国王太弱了。

8...hxg6 9.Qxh8 Qe7+ 10.Kd1 Bxf2

如果不是 11.f3，10...Bg4+ 将会成为搭档，因此黑方首先消除 f 兵。

11.Qxg8+？ Kd7 12.Qc4

黑棋落后六分，但对白棋的王有压倒性的攻击，白棋被困在棋盘中间，而白棋只发展了他们的后。白棋试图阻止主教来到g4。

12...Re8 0-1

黑方威胁...Qe1+ Rxe1 Rxe1#。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...f6
explanations.text:
3...f6?! · Nürnberg variation

Black defends their e-pawn with their f-pawn. This is non-standard as it weakens their kingside and prevents the knight coming to f6. It's also unnecessary for Black to defend the e-pawn again: the e5-pawn wasn't hanging because of the tactic Bxc6 dxc6 Nxe5? Qd4!, where Black recovers the material.

One idea Black might have is to bait White into playing 4. Bxc6 dxc6 5. Nxe5??. White may suspect they can sacrifice the knight and recover material using the tactic Qh5+. This is the case in the Damiano defence, 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 f6?, where the refutation is 3. Nxe5 fxe5 4. Qh5+. However, it doesn't work out the same here: Black is better after 5...fxe5 6. Qh5+ Kd7! 7. Qxe5 Qf6! (diagram). White doesn't want to trade queens and be down a bishop for two pawns in the endgame.

Rather than try to exploit the weakened kingside immediately, White should just develop normally and enjoy the more pleasant position. 4. O-O to get the king to safety, then White threatens to open the centre with d4. One line is 4...a6 5. Bc4 Bc5 6. c3 Nge7 7. d4 b5 8. Bb3 exd4 9. cxd4 Bb6 10. Nc3 . White has space and easy development.

explanations.textZh:
3...f6？！ · 纽伦堡变奏

黑棋用 f 棋子保卫 e 棋子。这是不标准的，因为它削弱了他们的王翼并阻止了骑士进入 f6。黑方也没有必要再次防守 e 兵：e5 兵并没有因为 Bxc6 dxc6 Nxe5 战术而挂起？ Qd4！，黑方收回材料。

黑棋可能有的一个想法是引诱白棋下4. Bxc6 dxc6 5. Nxe5??。白棋可能怀疑他们可以使用 Qh5+ 战术牺牲马并恢复材料。这是达米亚诺辩护中的情况，1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 f6？，其中反驳是3. Nxe5 fxe5 4. Qh5+。然而，这里的结果并不相同：黑棋在 5...fxe5 6. Qh5+ Kd7 之后更好！ 7.Qxe5 Qf6！ （图表）。白棋不想在残局中用皇后和主教来换取两个棋子。

白方不应该立即尝试利用弱势的王翼，而应该正常发展并享受更有利的位置。 4. O-O 让国王安全，然后白方用 d4 威胁打开中心。一行是 4...a6 5. Bc4 Bc5 6. c3 Nge7 7. d4 b5 8. Bb3 exd4 9. cxd4 Bb6 10. Nc3 。白色有空间且容易发展。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...f6/4. O-O/4...Bc5/5. c3
explanations.text:
Nürnberg Variation, Main Line

In this line, White castles to protect the king and prepares to play d4 to gain more space in the center. Black develops the bishop to c5, which is a natural square for the bishop and also puts pressure on the f2-pawn. White plays c3 to support the d4-pawn advance.

The Main Line of the Nürnberg Variation is considered to be better for White, as White has more options and flexibility in the position. White can choose to play d4 immediately or delay it and play Re1, h3, or a4 first. White can also exchange the light-squared bishop on b5 with the knight on c6 at any time, creating a weakness in Black’s pawn structure.

Black, on the other hand, has to deal with several problems in the Main Line of the Nürnberg Variation. Black has to find a good square for the knight on g8, which is blocked by the f6-pawn. Black also has to decide whether to castle kingside or queenside, as both sides have their drawbacks. Black’s king is also vulnerable to attacks by White’s pieces, such as Qf3, Qg4 or Qh5.

Therefore, the Main Line of the Nürnberg Variation is not very popular among chess players, as Black has to struggle for equality. Most players prefer to play other variations of the Spanish Game, such as the Berlin Defense, the Marshall Attack, or the Open Variation. These variations do not involve the move f6 and give Black more chances for counterplay.

explanations.textZh:
纽伦堡变例，主线

在这条线上，白方城堡保护王，并准备下d4以在中心获得更多空间。黑方将象发展到c5，这对象来说是一个天然的方格，也给f2兵带来了压力。白方下c3以支持d4兵前进。

纽伦堡变例的主线被认为对白方更好，因为白方在位置上有更多的选择和灵活性。白方可以选择立即下d4，也可以延迟先下Re1、h3或a4。白方还可以随时将 b5 上的光方象与 c6 上的马交换，从而造成黑方兵结构的弱点。

另一方面，黑色必须处理纽伦堡变例主线中的几个问题。黑方必须为 g8 上的马找到一个好的方格，该方格被 f6 兵阻挡。黑方还必须决定是在王翼还是后翼筑垒，因为双方都有各自的缺点。黑方的王也容易受到白方棋子的攻击，例如Qf3、Qg4或Qh5。

因此，纽伦堡变例的主线不太受棋手欢迎，因为黑棋必须争取平等。大多数玩家更喜欢玩西班牙游戏的其他变体，例如柏林防御、马歇尔进攻或开放变体。这些变化不涉及 f6 棋，给了黑棋更多的反击机会。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...Bb4
explanations.text:
3...Bb4!? - Alapin Defence

3...Bb4!?

3...Bb4!? is a very odd response to the Ruy Lopez, named the Alapin Defence. This move copies White's move 3. Bb5 and has no clear idea. Everything that it attacks is defended, and white has two major options against this dubious defence:

4. Bxc6 attempts to ruin Black's pawn structure by forcing them to double their pawns with either 4...bxc6 or 4...dxc6.

4. c3 ignores the idea to double pawns and attacks the Bb4, and prepares to play d4 and rip the center open.

Therefore, the Alapin Defence is a very dubious defence against the Ruy Lopez, and should not be played without proper planning.

explanations.textZh:
3...Bb4！？ - 阿拉平防御

3...Bb4！？

3...Bb4！？这是对鲁伊·洛佩兹（Ruy Lopez）的一个非常奇怪的回应，名为“阿拉平防御”（Alapin Defence）。这手棋抄袭了白棋3.Bb5，没有明确的思路。它所攻击的一切都会受到防御，而白棋有两个主要选择来应对这种可疑的防御：

4. Bxc6 试图通过强迫黑方用 4...bxc6 或 4...dxc6 将其棋子加倍来破坏黑方的棋子结构。

4. c3无视双兵攻击Bb4的想法，准备下d4并撕开中心。

因此，阿拉平防御对于鲁伊·洛佩兹来说是一种非常可疑的防御，在没有适当计划的情况下不应进行。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...Bc5
explanations.text:
3...Bc5 · Classical defence

3...Bc5 is the Classical defence, one of the oldest continuations. Sensing there is no immediate danger to e5, Black brings out their bishop to its most active square. However, this does not address the long-term threat to e5, and while Black's bishop is on c5 it may find itself kicked by White's c3, d4 manoeuvre. Therefore, even though 3...Bc5 appears to be a sensible developing move, it is only a minor sideline today and more common in amateur games.

4. c3, the Central variation, is the sharpest response. White intends to expand in the centre straight away with c3 and d4. Black usually replies 4...Nf6, though they also have the option of the gambit 4...f5.

Alternatively, White may wish to castle first. After 4. O-O they are ready to defend their e4 pawn with their rook. However, White has castled straight into the pin from Black's bishop, and White may need to leave their rook guarding f2.

4. Nxe5!? is a trap line where White goes for a centre fork trick, though in this position it is possible for Black to navigate it safely.

explanations.textZh:
3...Bc5 · 古典防御

3...Bc5 是古典防御，是最古老的延续之一。黑方意识到 e5 没有立即的危险，因此将他们的象带到了最活跃的方格。然而，这并不能解决对 e5 的长期威胁，而且当黑棋的主教在 c5 上时，它可能会发现自己被白棋的 c3、d4 策略踢到。因此，尽管 3...Bc5 看起来是一个明智的发展着法，但如今它只是一个次要的副业，并且在业余游戏中更常见。

4. c3，中心变体，是最尖锐的响应。白方打算立即用c3和d4向中心扩张。黑方通常会回答 4...Nf6，但他们也可以选择开局 4...f5。

或者，白棋可能希望先守堡。 4. O-O 之后，他们准备用车保卫他们的 e4 棋子。然而，白棋已经从黑棋的主教处直接进入了棋盘，而白棋可能需要让他们的车守卫f2。

4.Nxe5！？是一条陷阱线，白方采用中叉技巧，尽管在这个位置黑方可以安全地通过它。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...Bc5/4. c3
explanations.text:
4. c3 · Central variation

4. c3, the Central variation, is the most critical move to the Classical defence in the Spanish game. c3 supports White playing d4, building a big pawn centre and kicking Black's bishop.

In addition, White is now threatening to win the e5 pawn. This is because the c3 pawn takes away the d4 square that Black required to defend the pawn tactically. Now if, say, 4...a6? 5. Bxc6 dxc6 6. Nxe5, Black doesn't have the riposte ...Qd4 to win the pawn back/threaten ...Qxf2#. Black's best attempt is 6...Qe7 7. d4 (kicking the bishop and defending the knight) Bd6 8. O-O (allowing Black to win back the pawn in exchange for development).

4...Nf6 is the most common response. This invites 5. d4, attacking the bishop; or White can castle 5. O-O transposing into the Zukertort gambit.

4...d6? is a common amateur reply, but a mistake. Black pins their own knight, and by preventing the retreat of Black's bishop, it is easy for it to become trapped after 5. d4. (e.g. 5...exd4 6. cxd4 Bb4+ 7. Kf1! Bd7 8. Qa4 a5 9. a3 and Black's bishop is trapped. Or if 5...Bb6 6. d5 Black is losing a knight.)

Gambits

4...f5!? is the Cordel gambit. Black attacks the e4 pawn, though this isn't as sharp as 3...f5, the Schliemann.

4...d5!? is the Konikowski Gambit.

explanations.textZh:
4. c3·中心变体

4. c3，中央变体，是西班牙比赛中古典防守最关键的一步。 c3支持白方下d4，建立一个大的兵中心并踢掉黑方的象。

此外，白方现在威胁要赢得 e5 兵。这是因为 c3 棋子夺走了黑方在战术上保卫棋子所需的 d4 方格。现在，如果说 4...a6？ 5. Bxc6 dxc6 6. Nxe5，黑方没有还击...Qd4 赢回兵/威胁...Qxf2#。黑方的最佳尝试是6...Qe7 7. d4（踢象并保卫马） Bd6 8. O-O（让黑方赢回棋子以换取发展）。

4...Nf6 是最常见的响应。这会邀请5. d4，攻击主教；或白方可以城堡 5。O-O 转换成 Zukertort 策略。

4...d6？这是一个常见的业余回复，但却是一个错误。黑方钉住己方马，阻止黑方象撤退，5.d4后很容易陷入困境。 （例如 5...exd4 6. cxd4 Bb4+ 7. Kf1!Bd7 8. Qa4 a5 9. a3 且黑方的主教被困。或者如果 5...Bb6 6. d5 黑方失去了一名马。）

策略

4...f5！？是 Cordel 策略。黑棋攻击 e4 棋子，尽管这不如 3...f5（即施利曼）那么锋利。

4...d5！？是柯尼科夫斯基策略。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...Bc5/4. c3/4...d5
explanations.text:
4...d5?! · Konikowski gambit

4...d5?! is the Konikowski gambit. Black strikes in the centre. By moving their d-pawn, Black pins their own knight. Thus, Black offers white their choice of central pawns to capture, d5 or e5.

Capture d5

If 5. exd5, Black can recapture 5...Qxd5, taking advantage of the fact that, having played c3, White has taken away that square from their knight and so cannot gain tempo on the queen with Nc3. From this position, Black threatens Bxf2+ with a discovered attack on White's bishop.

6. d4 is playable (though after 6...exd4 7. cxd4?? is a mistake, allowing 7...Bb4+ to win the knight). 6. O-O allows Bxf2+ 7. Rxf2 Qxb5 and Black is up a pawn.

The best continuation however is 6. Qe2, defending the bishop and pinning the e-pawn, threatening to take on e5 with check, e.g. 6...Be6 7. Qxe5 Qxe5+ 8. Nxe5 and White is up a pawn.

Capture e5

5. Nxe5 captures the e5 pawn that Black undefended when they played 4...d5?! and pinned their own knight. This threatens to take the pinned knight and win a pawn (Nxc6 bxc6 Bxc6+).

Black's tricky move 5...Qf6? appears to threaten both White's knight and Qxf2#, and if 6. Nf3? dxe4 recovers the pawn at least. However White has 6. d4, both defending the knight and interposing between the bishop and the f2 square.

A better try for Black is 5...Qg5, forking the knight and the g2 pawn. If 6. Nxc6 Qxg2, Black threatens Qxh1# and Qxe4+. Instead, the best continuation for White is to give up on the knight, knowing that they can recover a bishop by forking on d4: 6. O-O Qxe5 7. d4 Qe6 8. dxc5.

Countergambit

5. d4? offers a countergambit. If 5...dxe4? then 6. Nxe5 is winning. There is no 6...Qg5 in this position because 5. d4 opened up White's queenside bishop, so White is simply going to be up a pawn and the exchange after 6...Bb6 (e.g.) 7. Nxc6 bxc6 8. Bxc6+ Bd7 9. Bxa8 Qxa8.

However, if 5...exd4 then the position is equal.

Declining the gambit

Declining the gambit with e.g. 5. Qe2 or 5. O-O is also fine for White and avoids the sharper lines.

History

The Konikowski gambit is named for Jerzy Konikowski (1947-), Polish-German FM, who played it with some success in the 1960s and 1970s. It is also called the Konikowski-Hardy Gambit for Konikowski and Otto Henry Hardy (1927-2010).

explanations.textZh:
4...d5？！ · 科尼科夫斯基策略

4...d5？！是柯尼科夫斯基策略。黑棋在中间进攻。通过移动他们的 D 兵，黑方固定了他们自己的马。因此，黑方为白方提供了选择的中央棋子来吃掉，d5 或 e5。

捕获d5

如果 5. exd5，黑方可以夺回 5...Qxd5，利用这样一个事实：在下完 c3 后，白方已经从他们的马手中拿走了该方格，因此无法通过 Nc3 获得对后的节奏。从这个位置，黑方通过发现对白方主教的攻击来威胁 Bxf2+。

6. d4 可以玩（尽管在 6...exd4 7.cxd4?? 之后是一个错误，允许 7...Bb4+ 赢得骑士）。 6. O-O 允许 Bxf2+ 7. Rxf2 Qxb5 且黑棋是棋子。

然而，最好的延续是 6. Qe2，保卫主教并钉住 e-pawn，威胁用检查来对抗 e5，例如6...Be6 7. Qxe5 Qxe5+ 8. Nxe5 和白棋是棋子。

捕获e5

5. Nxe5 吃掉黑方在下 4...d5 时不设防的 e5 棋子？！并钉住了自己的骑士。这有可能夺取被钉住的马并赢得一个棋子（Nxc6 bxc6 Bxc6+）。

黑方棘手棋5...Qf6？似乎对白棋的骑士和 Qxf2# 都构成威胁，如果 6. Nf3？ dxe4 至少恢复棋子。然而白方有 6.d4，既可以防守马，又可以介入主教和 f2 方格之间。

黑方更好的尝试是 5...Qg5，将马​​和 g2 兵分开。如果6. Nxc6 Qxg2，黑方威胁Qxh1#和Qxe4+。相反，白棋最好的延续就是放弃马，因为他们知道他们可以通过在 d4 上分叉来恢复主教：6. O-O Qxe5 7. d4 Qe6 8. dxc5。

反策略

5.d4？提供了一个反策略。如果 5...dxe4？那么 6. Nxe5 获胜。这个位置上没有 6...Qg5，因为 5.d4 打开了白方的后翼主教，所以白方只是成为棋子，并在 6...Bb6 之后交换（例如） 7. Nxc6 bxc6 8. Bxc6+ Bd7 9. Bxa8 Qxa8。

但是，如果 5...exd4 则位置相等。

拒绝策略

拒绝策略，例如5. Qe2 或 5. O-O 也适用于白棋并避免较尖锐的线条。

历史

科尼科夫斯基策略以波兰裔德国调频杰西·科尼科夫斯基 (Jerzy Konikowski，1947 年-) 的名字命名，他在 20 世纪 60 年代和 1970 年代运用该策略并取得了一些成功。它也被称为 Konikowski 和 Otto Henry Hardy (1927-2010) 的 Konikowski-Hardy 策略。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...Bc5/4. c3/4...f5
explanations.text:
4...f5 · Cordel gambit

4....f5 is the Cordel gambit. Black offers their f-pawn for White's e-pawn.

This resembles the Schliemann after 3...f5, though it is not as sharp. In this variation, White does not have the option of Nc3 to defend the e pawn, their main response to the Schliemann, but on the other hand Black's bishop on c5 gives White some tempo options they wouldn't otherwise have.

5. exf5, accepting the gambit, allows 5...e4 to hit White's knight. Trying to save it with 6. Nd4 leads to Black recovering the pawn and taking over more space: 6...Nxd4 7. cxd4 Bxd4 8. Be2. Alternatively, White can trade it with 6. d4, but has to accept losing their centre and a poorer pawn structure (6...exf3 7. dxc5 Qe7+ 8. Be3 fxg2 9. Rg1 Nf6, see diagram).

5. d4, declining the gambit, is the stronger riposte. If 5...fxe4 6. dxc5 exf3 7. Qxf3, and White is happy with the open position and the bishop pair (see diagram). If 5...exd4? White must be sure to play 6. e5, moving their e-pawn out of danger, before they recapture on d4.

Since Black has played f5, White might try for an attack on Black's king while it is still in the centre. They have the following tricky alternative with Nxe5:

First White plays 5. Bxc6?! to remove the defender of e5, then 5...dxc6 6. Nxe5 with the idea to allowing the queen out to h5. The natural 6...fxe4?? allows 7. Qh5+ g6 8. Nxg6!. White has a double attack on Black's rook and bishop. 8...hxg6 9. Qxh8 and White is up the exchange.

However, this is dubious for White as Black has 6...Bd6 7. Nc4 fxe4 where it's equal material and Black has the bishop pair, or 6...Qh4, preventing Qh5+.

explanations.textZh:
4...f5 · Cordel 策略

4....f5 是 Cordel 策略。黑棋将其 f 棋子换成白棋的 e 棋子。

这类似于 3...f5 之后的 Schliemann，尽管没有那么锐利。在这个变体中，白方没有 Nc3 来防守 e 兵的选择，这是他们对施利曼的主要反应，但另一方面，黑方 c5 上的主教为白方提供了一些他们原本没有的节奏选择。

5. exf5，接受策略，允许 5...e4 击中白方的马。试图用 6. Nd4 挽救它会导致黑方收回棋子并占据更多空间： 6...Nxd4 7. cxd4 Bxd4 8. Be2。或者，白方可以用 6. d4 进行交易，但必须接受失去中心和较差的棋子结构（6...exf3 7. dxc5 Qe7+ 8. Be3 fxg2 9. Rg1 Nf6，见图）。

5. d4，拒绝策略，是更强的还击。如果 5...fxe4 6. dxc5 exf3 7. Qxf3，白方对开局和象对感到满意（见图）。如果 5...exd4？白方必须确保下 6. e5，将他们的 e 棋子移出危险，然后才能在 d4 上重新夺回。

由于黑方已下f5，白方可能会在黑方王仍在中心时尝试攻击它。他们对 Nxe5 有以下棘手的替代方案：

第一个白方下 5.Bxc6？！移除 e5 的防守者，然后 5...dxc6 6. Nxe5 的想法是让皇后出局到 h5。自然6...fxe4??允许 7.Qh5+ g6 8.Nxg6!。白棋对黑棋的车和象进行双重攻击。 8...hxg6 9. Qxh8 和白方对局。

然而，这对于白棋来说是可疑的，因为黑棋有 6...Bd6 7. Nc4 fxe4，其材料相同，而黑棋有主教对，或 6...Qh4，阻止 Qh5+。

explanations.text:
4...Nf6

4...Nf6 is the most common response to the Central variation.

This invites 5. d4, attacking the bishop. Black can take the pawn, 5...exd4, and after 6. cxd4 Black can get their bishop out of trouble with check and then take the e4 pawn (e.g. 6...Bb4+ 7. Nc3 Nxe4). (6...Bb3+ . However, White has the intermezzo 6. e5!, protecting the e4 pawn and kicking Black's knight.

Alternatively, 5. O-O transposes into the Zukertort gambit. Black can take the e4 pawn but White can recover it after Qe2.

4...NF6

4...Nf6 是对中心变异最常见的反应。

这会邀请5.d4，攻击主教。黑方可以拿走棋子，5...exd4，在 6.cxd4 之后，黑方可以通过过牌让主教摆脱困境，然后拿走 e4 棋子（例如 6...Bb4+ 7.Nc3 Nxe4）。 (6...Bb3+ 。然而，白方有间奏曲 6. e5!，保护 e4 兵并踢黑方的马。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...Bc5/4. O-O
explanations.text:
4. O-O

White castles.

By activating the rook, White renews the threat to win Black's e-pawn, because if e.g. 4...a6 5. Bxc6 dxc6 6. Nxe5, the 6...Qd4 tactic is no longer a threat. If 6...Qd4?, the rook on f1 prevents 7...Qxf2?? from resulting in checkmate, and the apparent fork of the knight and e4 pawn is diffused by 7. Nf3 Qxe4?? 8. Re1! pinning Black's queen on the now open e-file.

4...Nd4 is a common continuation, threatening the Spanish bishop. This is similar to the Bird defence (3...Nd4) but now Black has the option of recapturing with the bishop instead of the pawn: 5. Nxd4 Bxd4. This allows White to get in 6. c3 with tempo, however.

4...Nf6 transposes into the Beverwijk variation of the Berlin defence. This counterattacks e4, so that in the event White chooses Bxc6 dxc6 Nxe5, it is at best a trade of pawns.

4.O-O

白色的城堡。

通过激活车，白方重新发起了赢得黑方电子兵的威胁，因为如果例如4...a6 5. Bxc6 dxc6 6. Nxe5，6...Qd4 战术不再是威胁。如果 6...Qd4?，则 f1 上的车阻止 7...Qxf2??导致将死，并且骑士和 e4 兵的明显分叉被 7 扩散。 Nf3 Qxe4?? 8.Re1！将布莱克后固定在现在打开的电子文件上。

4...Nd4是常见的延续，威胁西班牙主教。这与鸟防御 (3...Nd4) 类似，但现在黑方可以选择用象而不是兵夺回：5. Nxd4 Bxd4。然而，这使得白棋能够以节奏进入 6.c3。

4...Nf6 转换为柏林防御的贝弗韦克变体。这反击了e4，因此如果白方选择Bxc6 dxc6 Nxe5，这充其量只是棋子的交易。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...Bc5/4. Nxe5
explanations.text:
4. Nxe5!? · Centre fork trick

White takes the pawn, apparently blundering their knight but intending to recover it with a central fork trick. Black can equalise in this line, but it is very commonly misplayed.

4...Nxe5, taking back the pawn, is the most common reply in amateur games by far. Then, White intends to fork Black's bishop and knight with 5. d4. Taking the pawn to save the knight, 5...Bxd5?, gives up the bishop pair and gives White a nicely centralised queen.

In the central fork trick as common in the Three knights game (1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Nc3 Bc5? 4. Nxe5! Nxe5 5. d4), Black's best response is to play 5...Bd3 and recapture the pawn after the knight is taken, and at least then material is equal. However, by facing this trick in the Spanish game move order, Black has some additional resources.

Firstly, after 4...Nxe5 5. d4, Black has the tricky move 5...c6, counterattacking White's Spanish bishop. Black would be more than happy to trade bishops, and be up a knight for a pawn (6. dxc5 cxb5 7. Nc3). If White saves the bishop with 6. Ba4, there is the sharp line 6...Qa5+. One continuation is 7. Nc3?? Bb4 8. dxe5 Qxa4 (the knight is pinned).

Most critically, however, Black needn't play 4...Nxe5 at all:

4...Qe7 skewers the knight and pawn. Unlike in the Three knights version of this trick, White's e4 pawn is not guarded. This means after 5. Nxc6 or 5. Nf3, 5...Qxe4+ Black recovers the pawn with an even game.

explanations.textZh:
4.Nxe5！？ · 中心叉技巧

白方拿下了棋子，显然是犯了马的错误，但打算用中央分叉技巧来挽回棋子。黑棋可以在这条线上扳平比分，但很容易出现失误。

4...Nxe5，收回棋子，是迄今为止业余游戏中最常见的回复。然后，白方打算用5.d4叉黑方的象和马。用棋子拯救马，5...Bxd5？，放弃象对，给白方一个很好的集中后。

在三马游戏中常见的中央分叉技巧中（1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Nc3 Bc5？4. Nxe5！Nxe5 5. d4），黑方的最佳反应是下5...Bd3并在马被拿走后重新夺回棋子，并且至少材料是相等的。然而，通过面对西班牙棋步顺序中的这一招，黑方拥有了一些额外的资源。

首先，在4...Nxe5 5.d4之后，黑方有棘手的棋步5...c6，反击白方的西班牙主教。黑方会非常乐意交易主教，并成为马换一个棋子（6. dxc5 cxb5 7. Nc3）。如果白方用 6.Ba4 救了象，则有锐线 6...Qa5+。一个延续是 7.NC3?? Bb4 8. dxe5 Qxa4（骑士被钉住）。

然而，最关键的是，黑方根本不需要下 4...Nxe5：

4...Qe7 串起马和卒。与此技巧的三马版本不同，白方的 e4 棋子没有防守。这意味着在 5.Nxc6 或 5.Nf3 之后，5...Qxe4+ 黑方以平局收回棋子。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...g5
explanations.text:
3...g5? · Brentano gambit

An interesting move where Black threatens ...g4 to push the knight back, and to start a pawn assault if White castles.

4. d4! is the best move. This discovers an attack on g5 with the bishop while attacking the e5 square, the purpose being that now White is threatening 5. Nxg5 to just win the pawn, and if 4...g4? 5. Nxe5 is supported.

4. h3?! is more conservative, preventing ...g4 but is otherwise passive. 4. O-O?! allows 4...g4 5. Ne1 and White's position is far from comfortable.

History

Analysis of the line was published by Franz Brentano in Wiener Schachzeitung in 1900.

3...g5 was tried by Carl Schlechter against Richard Teichmann in 1904. The game went into the line 4. d4 Nxd4 5. Nxd4 exd4 6. Qxd4 Qf6.

explanations.textZh:
3...g5？ · 布伦塔诺策略

这是一个有趣的举动，黑方威胁...g4 将马击退，如果白方城堡，则开始兵攻击。

4.d4！是最好的举动。这发现在攻击 e5 方格时，主教对 g5 进行攻击，目的是现在白方威胁 5.Nxg5 赢得棋子，如果 4...g4？ 5. 支持Nxe5。

4.h3？！更加保守，阻止...g4，但在其他方面是被动的。 4. 哦哦？！允许 4...g4 5。Ne1 和 White 的位置远非舒适。

历史

弗兰茨·布伦塔诺 (Franz Brentano) 于 1900 年在《Wiener Schachzeitung》上发表了对该线路的分析。

1904 年，卡尔·施莱希特 (Carl Schlechter) 与理查德·泰希曼 (Richard Teichmann) 尝试了 3...g5。比赛进入行 4. d4 Nxd4 5. Nxd4 exd4 6. Qxd4 Qf6。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...g6
explanations.text:
Fianchetto Defence

Black allows their Bf8 to go to g7, which would place it on the long diagonal for activity. White can play a few moves, such as 4. Nc3 and 4. O-O as Black's quiet move doesn't interfere with White's development.

explanations.textZh:
菲安凯托防守

黑方允许他们的 Bf8 进入 g7，这会将其放置在长对角线上以进行活动。白棋可以下一些棋，例如 4. Nc3 和 4. O-O，因为黑棋的安静棋步不会干扰白棋的发展。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...Nge7
explanations.text:
3...Nge7 · Cozio defence

The Cozio defence is an unusual but sound sideline that can be used to avoid main line Spanish theory. On e7, Black's knight prevents the development of their king's bishop. Black has two ways to resolve this: one plan is to move the knight again, ...Ng6, the other is to play ...g6 & ...Bg7. The latter option resembles the fianchetto defence, 3...g6.

The immediate utility of 3...Nge7 is that it prepares to recapture on c6 with a knight, Bxc6? Nxc6!, so Black avoids doubling their pawns or dropping e5.

After 4. O-O, the modern main move, Black makes a decision as to their bishop. If Black wants to keep the deterrent of Bxc6? Nxc6!, then they will need to play with 4...g6 and the kingside fianchetto. Otherwise, the line is 4...Ng6, from where the knight defends e5 and the trade on c6 is no longer so useful for White anyway.

4. Nc3, uncommon in the Spanish, is the main sideline, where 4...g6 is the Paulsen variation. There there is 5. d4! exd4, and White's idea is not to recapture immediately but to play 6. Nd5. 6...Bg7 7. Bg5! h6 8. Bf6 Bxf6 9. Nxf6+ Kf8.

4. c3 was one of the main approaches in the 19th century, as recommended by Carl Jaenisch over 4. d4 in 1848, writing that it "affords Black no satisfactory method of developing his game." In 1865, Zukertort scored a win over Anderssen in a twelve move miniature with 4. c3 d6 5. d4 Bd7 6. O-O Ng6 7. Ng5 h6 8. Nxf7 Kxf7 9. Bc4+ Ke7?? (9...Ke8 is better, so that 10. Qh5 can be met with ...Qf6) 10. Qh5 Qe8?? (better was to give up the knight) 11. Qg5+ hxg5 12. Bxg5# 1-0

4. d4 is also playable.

History

Named for Carlo Cozio, 18th century Italian chess master. The line was popular in the 19th century but became unfashionable by the 20th in favour of 3...a6 and 3...Nf6.

It is recommended occasionally as a non-theoretical reply to 3. Bb5: an "Anti-Spanish". Levon Aronian helped to re-popularise it in 2009, playing it exclusively with black against 3...Bb5 in the 2009 World Blitz Championship.

explanations.textZh:
3...Nge7 · 科齐奥防守

科齐奥防守是一种不寻常但健全的边线，可以用来避开西班牙主线理论。在e7上，黑方的骑士阻止了他们国王的主教的发展。黑棋有两种方法解决这个问题：一种是再次移动马，...Ng6，另一种是下...g6 & ...Bg7。后一个选项类似于 fiianchetto 防守，3...g6。

3...Nge7 的直接用途是它准备用骑士 Bxc6 在 c6 上重新夺回？ Nxc6！，因此黑方避免将棋子加倍或放弃 e5。

在 4. O-O（现代主要棋步）之后，黑方决定了他们的象。如果黑方想保持Bxc6的威慑力呢？ Nxc6！，那么他们将需要使用 4...g6 和王翼前卫。否则，这条线是 4...Ng6，从这里骑士防守 e5，而 c6 上的交易对白方来说不再那么有用了。

4. Nc3 在西班牙人中不常见，是主要边线，其中 4...g6 是保尔森变体。还有5.d4！ exd4，白方的想法不是立即夺回而是下6.Nd5。 6...Bg7 7.Bg5！ h6 8.Bf6 Bxf6 9.Nxf6+ Kf8。

4. c3 是 19 世纪的主要方法之一，正如 Carl Jaenisch 在 1848 年对 4. d4 所推荐的那样，他写道，它“无法为布莱克提供令人满意的发展棋局的方法”。 1865 年，Zukertort 在十二步微型棋中以 4. c3 d6 5. d4 Bd7 6. O-O Ng6 7. Ng5 h6 8. Nxf7 Kxf7 9. Bc4+ Ke7?? 战胜了安德森。 （9...Ke8 更好，因此 10.Qh5 可以与 ...Qf6 相遇） 10.Qh5 Qe8?? （最好放弃骑士） 11. Qg5+ hxg5 12. Bxg5# 1-0

4. d4也可以玩。

历史

以 18 世纪意大利国际象棋大师卡洛·科齐奥 (Carlo Cozio) 的名字命名。该系列在 19 世纪很流行，但到了 20 世纪就不再流行，取而代之的是 3...a6 和 3...Nf6。

有时建议将其作为对 3. Bb5：“反西班牙”的非理论答复。莱文·阿罗尼安 (Levon Aronian) 在 2009 年帮助重新普及了这项运动，他在 2009 年世界闪电战锦标赛中仅用黑棋对抗 3...Bb5。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...Nf6
explanations.text:
3...Nf6 · Berlin defence

3...Nf6 is the main sideline to 3...a6. The Berlin defence is known for being solid and is used at the top level of chess as a reliable drawing weapon. The mainline continuation leads to an equal endgame known as the Berlin Wall, where it is difficult for White to achieve better than a draw. Another common variation leads to a quick draw by repetition by turn 14.

3...Nf6 is developing move that controls the centre, attacks e4, and gets Black closer to castling.

The main line 4. O-O allows Black to take the e4 pawn 4...Nxe4. This is a trade because White can recover the material by applying pressure on the e-file (e.g. 5. Re1 skewers e5 through the knight). The main line continues 5. d4 Nd6 and either 6. Bxc6 or 6. dxe5.

6. Bxc6 leads to a queen trade on turn eight and the Berlin Wall endgame;

6. dxe5 often leads to the famous Berlin draw by repetition, employed when it is advantageous for the players to agree a quick draw in tournaments where draws by agreement are otherwise restricted.

4. d3 avoids these main Berlin defence continuations. It defends e4 so defuses the threat of 4...Nxe4, but also reinforces White's threat on e5, as after Bxc6 dxc6 Nxe5, the ...Qd4 tactic no longer forks the pawn. Black may defend it directly (4...d6) or tactically (4...Bc5! sets up the threat of ...Qd4 and ...Qxf2#).

4. Qe2 is a tricky sideline. It, too, defends e4 so avoids the trade of e-pawns, but also defends f2, defusing the ...Bc5 ...Qd4 ...Qxf2# threat (4. Qe2 Bc5 5. Bxc6 dxc6? 6. Nxe5 wins the pawn, as 6...Qd4 7. Nd3 [gains time on the bishop] Bb6 8. f3 [defends pawn]). Compared to 4. d3, White keeps the option of c3 then d4 in one move, but after ...Bc4 Black has too much control of d4 to manage this anyway.

4. Nxe5?? is the so-called Halloween attack. It resembles the well-known Halloween gambit, but worse because Nc3 has been replaced by Bb5, reducing White's space advantage.

History

An early analysis of 3...Nf6 was published by Berliner Baron von der Lasa in Handbuch des Schachspiels (1843). The name "Berlin defence" came into use in German by at least 1848, appearing in Deutsche Schachzeitung which attributed the coining to Carl Jaenisch. In his article for Le Palamède, 1847, Jaenisch wrote that it was "discovered in Berlin (we cannot affirm whether by de Heydebrand [i.e. Baron von der Lasa] or by another)".

The Berlin defence was revived by Vladimir Kramnik who used it to stall out Garry Kasparov's 1. e4 repertoire in their 2000 World Championship match. Try as he might, Kasparov couldn't manage better than a draw in Kramnik's Berlin Wall endgame.

explanations.textZh:
3...Nf6·柏林防御

3...Nf6 是 3...a6 的主要副线。柏林的防守以坚固而闻名，在顶级国际象棋比赛中被用作可靠的绘图武器。主线的延续导致了一场平等的残局，被称为柏林墙，白方很难取得比平局更好的成绩。另一种常见的变化是在第 14 回合时通过重复进行快速平局。

3...Nf6 正在开发控制中心、攻击 e4 并让黑方更接近易位的走法。

主线 4.O-O 允许黑方吃 e4 兵 4...Nxe4。这是一个交易，因为白方可以通过对 e-file 施加压力来恢复材料（例如 5. Re1 通过马串 e5）。主线继续 5. d4 Nd6 和 6. Bxc6 或 6. dxe5。

6. Bxc6 在第八回合导致皇后交易和柏林墙残局；

6. dxe5经常导致著名的柏林重复抽签，当在比赛中同意快速抽签对球员有利时使用，而协议抽签受到其他限制。

4. d3 避免了这些主要的柏林防御延续。它保卫 e4，因此化解了 4...Nxe4 的威胁，但也加强了白方对 e5 的威胁，因为在 Bxc6 dxc6 Nxe5 之后，...Qd4 策略不再分叉兵。黑方可以直接防守（4...d6）或战术性防守（4...Bc5！设置...Qd4 和...Qxf2# 的威胁）。

4. Qe2 是一个棘手的副业。它也保护 e4，从而避免电子棋子的交易，但也保护 f2，化解 ...Bc5 ...Qd4 ...Qxf2# 威胁 (4. Qe2 Bc5 5. Bxc6 dxc6? 6. Nxe5 赢得棋子，因为 6...Qd4 7. Nd3 [在主教上获得时间] Bb6 8. f3 [防御典当]）。与 4.d3 相比，白棋一步保留了 c3 然后 d4 的选择，但在 ...Bc4 之后，黑方对 d4 的控制太多，无论如何都无法做到这一点。

4.Nxe5??就是所谓的万圣节袭击。它类似于众所周知的万圣节策略，但更糟糕的是，因为 Nc3 已被 Bb5 取代，从而减少了白方的空间优势。

历史

Berliner Baron von der Lasa 在 Handbuch des Schachspiels (1843) 中发表了对 3...Nf6 的早期分析。 “柏林防卫”这个名称至少在 1848 年开始在德语中使用，出现在《德国日报》上，并认为这个词是卡尔·雅尼施 (Carl Jaenisch) 创造的。 Jaenisch 在 1847 年为 Le Palamède 发表的文章中写道，它“是在柏林发现的（我们无法确定是由 de Heydebrand [即冯德拉萨男爵]还是其他人发现的）”。

弗拉基米尔·克拉姆尼克 (Vladimir Kramnik) 恢复了柏林的防守，他在 2000 年世界锦标赛比赛中用它拖延了加里·卡斯帕罗夫 (Garry Kasparov) 的 1. e4 技能。尽管卡斯帕罗夫竭尽全力，但他在克拉姆尼克的柏林墙残局中却没有比平局更好的了。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...Nf6/4. d3
explanations.text:
4. d3 · Anti-Berlin

4. d3 defends White's e4 pawn. This avoids the main line of the Berlin defence, 4. O-O, where White temporarily sacrifices the e4 pawn.

Now that White's e4 pawn is protected, this increases the threat to Black's e5 pawn. If for example 4...a6?, White can trade off the defending knight and win the pawn (5. Bxc6 dxc6 6. Nxe5), and Black's usual 6...Qd4? tactic no longer forks anything.

Defend the pawn

Black can choose to defend the pawn directly or tactically:

4...d6, to defend the e5 pawn directly, is playable but relegates the kingside bishop to a supporting role on e7.

4...Bc5 is the main line. This pressures White's f2 pawn and sets up a new tactical riposte: now if White trades off the knight and takes the pawn (5. Bxc6 dxc6 6. Nxe5), then 6...Qd4! forks the knight with the threat of Qxf2#. White's usual response is 5. c3, controlling the d4 square and so preventing Qd4.

Gambit the pawn

4...Ne7, the Mortimer variation, is a sideline. This gambits the e5 pawn, but if White takes it, they fall into the devious Mortimer trap: 5. Nxe5 c6 6. Bc4 Qa5+!, forking the knight with check.

explanations.textZh:
4. d3·反柏林

4. d3 防守白方的 e4 兵。这避开了柏林防御的主线，4.O-O，其中白方暂时牺牲了 e4 棋子。

现在白棋的 e4 棋子受到保护，这增加了对黑棋 e5 棋子的威胁。例如，如果 4...a6？，白棋可以交易防守马并赢得棋子（5. Bxc6 dxc6 6. Nxe5），而黑棋通常是 6...Qd4？策略不再分叉任何东西。

保卫典当

黑方可以选择直接防守或战术防守：

4...d6，直接防守 e5 兵，可以玩，但在 e7 上将王翼主教降级为辅助角色。

4...Bc5为主线。这会给白方的 f2 棋子带来压力，并建立一个新的战术反击：现在如果白方放弃马并拿下棋子（5. Bxc6 dxc6 6. Nxe5），那么 6...Qd4！以Qxf2#的威胁分叉骑士。白棋通常的反应是5.c3，控制d4方格，从而阻止Qd4。

开棋

4...Ne7，莫蒂默变体，是一个副线。这让 e5 兵下注，但如果白方拿下它，他们就会陷入狡猾的莫蒂默陷阱：5. Nxe5 c6 6. Bc4 Qa5+!，用过牌分叉马。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...Nf6/4. d3/4...Ne7
explanations.text:
4...Ne7 · Mortimer variation

4...Ne7 in the Anti-Berlin is the Mortimer variation. On the surface this is a strange move: Black violates principles by moving their knight a second time in the opening, at the same time inhibiting the development of their king-side bishop. Black's idea is to free the c6 square for their pawn, and chase White's bishop away that way.

5. Nxe5? falls into the Mortimer trap. 4...Ne7 appeared to undefend the e5 pawn. As the opening manoeuvres of the Spanish game centre around these e-pawns, White may think to punish Black's passive move by snapping up the e-pawn. But, after 5...c6 6. Bc4 (or Ba4), Black has 6...Qa5+!, forking the knight.

Therefore 5. O-O is the mainline, removing the king from the centre and any ideas of Qa5+. After 5...c6 6. Ba4 Black must defend e5, either with 6...d6 or by moving the knight again, 6...Ng6.

History

The Mortimer variation is named after James Mortimer (1832―1911), who played it at a tournament in London in 1883.

explanations.textZh:
4...Ne7·莫蒂默变体

4...Anti-Berlin 中的 Ne7 是 Mortimer 的变体。从表面上看，这是一个奇怪的举动：黑方违反了原则，在开局中第二次移动了他们的马，同时抑制了他们王方象的发展。黑方的想法是为他们的棋子释放c6方格，并以此方式将白方的主教赶走。

5.Nxe5？落入莫蒂默陷阱。 4...Ne7 似乎无法防御 e5 棋子。由于西班牙棋的开局策略围绕这些电子兵展开，白方可能会考虑通过抢夺电子兵来惩罚黑方的被动走法。但是，在 5...c6 6. Bc4（或 Ba4）之后，黑方有 6...Qa5+!，分叉了马。

因此5.O-O为主线，去掉了中心的王以及Qa5+的任何想法。 5...c6 6. Ba4 黑后必须防守 e5，要么用 6...d6，要么再次移动马，6...Ng6。

历史

莫蒂默变体以詹姆斯·莫蒂默（James Mortimer，1832—1911 年）的名字命名，他于 1883 年在伦敦举行的一场锦标赛上打过该球。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...Nf6/4. d3/4...Ne7/5. Nxe5
explanations.text:
5. Nxe5?

White takes the apparently free e5-pawn, thereby falling into Black's trap.

Black springs the Mortimer trap with 5...c6, kicking away White's bishop but at the same moment giving their queen access to a5. After 6. Bc4? (or 6. Ba4?) Qa5+! 7. Nc3 Black picks up the knight. Black needs to be aware of a couple of alternative sixth moves for White, but while tricky they are not sound.

Any other fifth move for Black (5...Ng6?, 5...a6?) fails to recover the material.

5.Nxe5？

白方拿走了明显自由的 e5 兵，从而落入黑方的陷阱。

黑棋用 5...c6 启动莫蒂默陷阱，踢掉白棋的主教，但同时让他们的后可以下 a5。 6.BC4之后？ （或 6.Ba4？）Qa5+！ 7. Nc3 黑棋拿走马。黑方需要了解白方的几种替代第六步，但虽然很棘手，但它们并不健全。

黑棋的任何其他第五步棋（5...Ng6？、5...a6？）都无法恢复材料。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...Nf6/4. d3/4...Ne7/5. Nxe5/5...c6
explanations.text:
5...c6 · Mortimer trap

Black kicks White's bishop, gaining tempo while opening a line for their queen reach a5.

White has fallen into the Mortimer trap. After 6. Bc4? or 6. Ba4?, 6...Qa5+! 7. Nc3 and Black picks up the knight.

White has some tricky moves of their own, but if Black avoids their traps then they are strictly ahead here.

6. Nc4?!, leaving the bishop to hang, sets Black up for the blunder 6...cxb5?? 7. Nd6#, and Black's king is smothered. Giving the king some space with 6...d6 (Black still wins a minor piece after 7. Ba4 b5!) or 6...d5 is better.

The best move for White is 6. Nxf7. White at least gets another pawn for their knight. The knight attacks Black's queen, but 6...Qa5+? 7. Bd2 Qxb5?? 8. Nd6+ forks the king and queen. 6...Kxf7 7. Bc4+ d5 8. Bb3. is best. Black is ahead material but loses castling rights.

explanations.textZh:
5...c6 · 莫蒂默陷阱

黑方踢了白方的主教，加快了节奏，同时为他们的皇后到达a5打开了一条线。

怀特陷入了莫蒂默陷阱。 6.BC4之后？或 6.Ba4？、6...Qa5+！ 7. Nc3 和黑棋拿下马。

白棋也有一些棘手的棋步，但如果黑棋避开了他们的陷阱，那么他们就绝对领先了。

6. Nc4？！，让主教挂起，让黑方犯下错误 6...cxb5?? 7. Nd6#，黑王被闷。用 6...d6 给国王一些空间（黑棋在 7.Ba4 b5 之后仍然赢得一个小子！）或 6...d5 更好。

白方的最佳棋步是 6. Nxf7。白棋至少为他们的马得到了另一个棋子。马攻击黑方后，但 6...Qa5+？ 7.Bd2 Qxb5?? 8. Nd6+分叉国王和王后。 6...Kxf7 7. Bc4+ d5 8. Bb3。是最好的。黑棋领先，但失去了易位权。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...Nf6/4. d3/4...Bc5
explanations.text:
Black develops their dark-squared bishop to an active square where it controls d4 and is ready to castle. White has a few options here:

5.c3 is the main line. It prepares the d3-d4 push and is now ready to play Bxc6 and Nxe5 since Qd4 no longer works.

5. 0-0 is also an option but is relatively drawish. Black will respond with Nd4, getting equality soon.

5. Bxc6 now is another interesting line and if black does not know how to respond they might get into trouble very soon. Black will likely reposition the f6-knight to d7 and play f6 later to protect the e5 pawn.

explanations.textZh:
黑方将其暗方象发展为活跃方格，控制 d4 并准备城堡。白棋在这里有几个选择：

5.c3为主线。它准备了 d3-d4 推送，现在准备玩 Bxc6 和 Nxe5，因为 Qd4 不再起作用。

5. 0-0也是一种选择，但相对乏味。黑方将用 Nd4 回应，很快就平等。

5. Bxc6 现在是另一条有趣的线，如果黑棋不知道如何应对，他们可能很快就会遇到麻烦。黑方可能会将 f6-马重新定位到 d7，并稍后下 f6 以保护 e5 兵。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...Nf6/4. O-O
explanations.text:
4. O-O · Rio gambit

Castling is the most common continuation in the Berlin defence. This leaves White's e4 pawn undefended, but gives White's rook access to the centre.

If Black accepts the pawn, 4...Nxe4, this is actually a trade because White can take back e5 easily. One line is 5. Re1, bringing another attacker to the e-file and recovering the pawn after the knight is forced to move. One of the reasons this works is because Black's king is still in the centre: 4...Nxe4 5. Re1 Nd6 (threatens to take White's bishop) 6. Nxe5 Nxe5 (Black is not in time to capture the bishop: 6...Nxb5, because the discovered check Nxc6 wins White the queen) 7. Rxe5+ Be7 and White can evacuate the bishop.

5. Re1 is very drawish, and 5. d4 is actually the main line (although as this is the Berlin, 5. d4 is pretty drawish too, and usually leads to the Berlin Wall endgame). 5...exd4? opens the e-file and lets 6. Re1 pin-and-win Black's knight, so the main reply is 5...Nd6.

4...Bc5, the Beverwijk variation, is the main alternative to 4...Nxe4. Black pressures f2 and White's castled king. This is sharp because 5. Re1?! to defend e4 undefends f2 so after 5...Ng4, White finds themselves having to move it back 6. Rf1. (A trap is 6. d4?? Nxd4! 7. Nxd4 Qh4!).

White has the choice to capture e5 (5. Nxe5), due to a tactic that arises from the c5 and e5 squares being forkable. More commonly White plays for c3 and d4 instead.

4...Be7 before taking the pawn shelters Black's king and gets ready to castle. This prevents any mischief around a discovered check. Now the threat of 5...Nxe4 is more severe, as while White can still recover the pawn, they would have to give up the bishop pair to do so (e.g. 5. c3?! Nxe4 6. Re1 Nd6 7. Bxc6 dxc6 8. Nxe5 Bf5). 4...Be7 functionally declines the gambit, as it gives White time to play 5. Re1 and defend the e4 pawn. It is typically a quieter continuation.

4...Ng4?!, the Fishing pole variation, invites White to blunder by accepting a sacrificial knight but opening the h-file and exposing themselves to potential checkmate.

explanations.textZh:
4. O-O·里约开局

易车易位是柏林防御中最常见的延续。这使得白方的 e4 兵不设防，但让白方的车可以进入中心。

如果黑方接受棋子 4...Nxe4，这实际上是一笔交易，因为白方可以轻松拿回 e5。其中一行是 5.Re1，将另一名攻击者带到电子文件中，并在骑士被迫移动后恢复棋子。这样做的原因之一是因为黑方的国王仍然在中间：4...Nxe4 5. Re1 Nd6（威胁夺走白方的象） 6. Nxe5 Nxe5（黑方没有及时捕获象：6...Nxb5，因为发现的检查 Nxc6 赢得白方后） 7. Rxe5+ Be7 和白方可以撤离象。

5.Re1非常画风，而5.d4实际上是主线（尽管这是柏林，5.d4也非常画风，通常会导致柏林墙残局）。 5...exd4？打开电子文件，让 6.Re1 锁定并获胜黑方骑士，所以主要回复是 5...Nd6。

4...Bc5（Beverwijk 变体）是 4...Nxe4 的主要替代品。黑方对f2施压，白方的城堡王。这很尖锐，因为 5.Re1？！防守 e4 不防守 f2，所以在 5...Ng4 之后，白方发现自己必须将其移回 6. Rf1。 （陷阱是 6.d4??Nxd4！7.Nxd4 Qh4！）。

由于c5和e5方格可分叉而产生的策略，白方可以选择吃掉e5（5.Nxe5）。更常见的是白方下 c3 和 d4。

4...Be7 在吃兵之前庇护黑方国王并准备城堡。这可以防止围绕已发现的支票进行任何恶作剧。现在 5...Nxe4 的威胁更加严重，因为虽然白方仍然可以收回棋子，但他们必须放弃主教对才能这样做（例如 5. c3？！ Nxe4 6. Re1 Nd6 7. Bxc6 dxc6 8. Nxe5 Bf5）。 4...Be7 在功能上拒绝了这个策略，因为它给了白方时间来玩 5.Re1 并防守 e4 兵。它通常是一个更安静的延续。

4...Ng4?!，鱼竿变体，让白方犯下错误，接受了一名牺牲的骑士，但打开了 h 档，将自己暴露给了潜在的将死者。

explanations.text:
4...Nxe4 · Open Berlin

Black takes the hanging e4 pawn.

This is a trade more than a gambit as White can recover the pawn easily enough using the semi-open e-file.

One line is 5. Re1, recovering the pawn after the knight is forced to move. One of the reasons this works is because Black's king is still in the centre: 5...Nd6 (threatens to take White's bishop) 6. Nxe5 and Black is not in time to capture the bishop: 6...Nxb5? 7. Nxc6+ discovered check wins White the queen. If 6...Nxe5 7. Rxe5+ Be7 and White can evacuate the bishop. 6...Be7 closes the e-file but gives White time to play 7. Bf1.

5. Re1 is very drawish, and 5. d4 is actually the main line (although as this is the Berlin, 5. d4 is pretty drawish too, and usually leads to the Berlin Wall endgame). 5...exd4? opens the e-file and lets 6. Re1 pin-and-win Black's knight, so the main reply is 5...Nd6.

explanations.textZh:
4...Nxe4 · 柏林公开赛

黑棋拿下悬挂的 e4 棋子。

这不仅仅是一种策略，因为白棋可以使用半开放的电子文件轻松地收回棋子。

一行是5.Re1，在马被迫移动后恢复棋子。这种方法有效的原因之一是因为黑方的国王仍然位于中心：5...Nd6（威胁夺取白方的主教） 6. Nxe5 和黑方没有及时捕获主教：6...Nxb5？ 7. Nxc6+发现检查赢得了白皇后。如果 6...Nxe5 7. Rxe5+ Be7 和白方可以撤离主教。 6...Be7 关闭电子文件，但给白方时间下棋 7. Bf1。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...Nf6/4. O-O/4...Nxe4/5. d4
explanations.text:
5. d4

White is down a pawn, but is on the way to recovering it. They look to open the position and threaten Re1, to shoo the knight away, then Nxe5 comes loaded with a discovered check. While Black's king is still in the centre, White hopes to generate tactics around the e-file, e.g.

5...exd4? is a mistake because it opens the e-file. 6. Re1 pins the knight. 6...f5 7. Nxd4 and f3 is on its way and the knight can't be saved.

5...d6? to defend the pawn lets White bring another attacker. 6. Qe2 (or 6. Re1) Nf6 and Black's game can soon unravel due to e-file pressure, e.g. 6. Qe2 Nf6? 7. dxe5 dxe5?! 8. Nxe5 Be6 9. Rd1 Bd6 10. Nxc6 bxc6 11. Bxc6+ Nd7 12. Bxa8 Qxa8, White is up the exchange.

So Black must figure with threats on the e-file.

5...Be7, the Rio de Janeiro variation, shelters the king and prepares to castle, after which an open centre is less dangerous. The game continues 6. Qe2 Nd6 7. Bxc6 bxc6! 8. dxe5 Nb7 9. Nc3 O-O. This was how this position was played in the 19th century.

More common today is to start with 5...Nd6, L'Hermet variation. Black moves their knight, preventing White from gaining time on it with Re1 or Qe2, while attacking the bishop. If 6. dxe5 this leads to a big trade and the famous Berlin draw, 6...Nxb5 7. a4 Nbd4 8. Nxd4 Nxd4 9. Qxd4 d5 10. exd6 Qxd6. If 6. Bxc6 this leads to the famous Berlin Wall endgame, 6...dxc6 7. dxe5 Nf5 8. Qxd8+ Kxd8.

Alternatively, if Black could play ...d5, they could support their knight in the centre and perhaps keep the e-file closed for now. However, 5...d5? in this position pins Black's knight and allows 6. Nxe5!. Black must prepare it with 5...a6, the Rosenthal Variation, where 6. Ba4 transposes into an Open Spanish and Black gets to play ...d5: 6...b5 7. Bb3 d5.

explanations.textZh:
5.d4

白棋落下棋子，但正在追回棋子的路上。他们希望打开位置并威胁Re1，将骑士赶走，然后Nxe5带着被发现的支票来了。当黑棋的国王仍然处于中心位置时，白棋希望围绕电子文件制定战术，例如

5...exd4？是一个错误，因为它打开了电子文件。 6. Re1压制了骑士。 6...f5 7. Nxd4 和 f3 正在赶来，骑士无法获救。

5...d6？为了保卫棋子，让白方带另一名攻击者。 6. Qe2（或 6. Re1）Nf6 和黑方的棋局很快就会因电子文件压力而瓦解，例如6.Qe2 Nf6？ 7. dxe5 dxe5？！ 8. Nxe5 Be6 9. Rd1 Bd6 10. Nxc6 bxc6 11. Bxc6+ Nd7 12. Bxa8 Qxa8，白棋上调。

因此布莱克必须考虑到电子文件中的威胁。

5...Be7，里约热内卢的变种，庇护国王并准备城堡，之后开放的中心危险性较小。游戏继续 6. Qe2 Nd6 7. Bxc6 bxc6！ 8. dxe5 Nb7 9. Nc3 O-O。这就是19世纪这个职位的扮演方式。

如今更常见的是从 5...Nd6、L'Hermet 变体开始。黑棋移动他们的马，阻止白棋用Re1或Qe2赢得时间，同时攻击主教。如果 6. dxe5 这会导致一笔大交易和著名的柏林平局，6...Nxb5 7. a4 Nbd4 8. Nxd4 Nxd4 9. Qxd4 d5 10. exd6 Qxd6。如果 6. Bxc6 这会导致著名的柏林墙残局，6...dxc6 7. dxe5 Nf5 8. Qxd8+ Kxd8。

或者，如果黑方可以下...d5，他们可以支持中间的马，也许暂时关闭电子文件。然而，5...d5？在此位置固定黑方的马并允许 6. Nxe5!。黑方必须准备 5...a6，即罗森塔尔变例，其中 6. Ba4 转变成公开西班牙语，黑方开始下棋 ...d5: 6...b5 7. Bb3 d5。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...Nf6/4. O-O/4...Nxe4/5. d4/5...a6
explanations.text:
5...a6 · Rosenthal variation

Black now kicks White's bishop. Removing its pressure from Black's knight will allow Black to play ...d5, expanding in the centre and defending the knight on e4, without dropping a pawn due to the pin.

Any retreat along the f1-a6 diagonal the bishop travelled on move 3 constitutes a loss of tempo and allows ...d5. The two serious possibilities are 6. Bxc6 or 6. Ba4.

6. Ba4 is a transposition to the Open Spanish. Reaching the Open Spanish via the Berlin defence is a move order trick that avoids sidelines like the Wormald attack.

But White doesn't have to transpose into an Open Spanish if they do not want to: 6. Bxc6 dxc6 enters something like the Exchange variation, though there really is a threat of Nxe5 this time. Rather than recover the pawn straight away, White's better line is 7. Qe2, pressuring the e-file while unpinning the d-pawn to prevent a queen trade.

5...a6 · 罗森塔尔变体

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...Nf6/4. O-O/4...Nxe4/5. d4/5...Nd6
explanations.text:
5...Nd6 · l'Hermet variation

Black attacks White's bishop. White's choices are between a quick draw or a drawish endgame.

White could take with the bishop first, 6. Bxc6. This leads to the famous Berlin Wall endgame, 6...dxc6 7. dxe5 Nf5 8. Qxd8+ Kxd8 where it is very hard for White to achieve more than a draw.

If White allows Black to take their bishop, 6. dxe5, Black doesn't actually win it and this leads to a big trade. 6...Nxb5 7. a4 Nbd4 8. Nxd4 Nxd4 9. Qxd4 d5. If White takes 10. exd6 e.p. Qxd6= this is the famous Berlin draw: neither side have anything better than to move their queens between the e- and d-files.

White could retreat the bishop, 6. Ba4 the Showalter variation, which allows Black to take the pawn 6...exd4 or push 6...e4 to where their pawn is defended by the knight. The game is thought equal either way.

The intermezzo 6. Bg5!? Be7 7. Bxe7 Qxe7 has been tried to avoid the queen trade after Bxc6 and postpone the endgame.

History

Named after German chess master and composer Rudolf l'Hermet.

explanations.textZh:
5...Nd6 · l'Hermet 变体

黑棋攻击白棋的象。白棋的选择是在快速平局或平局之间进行选择。

白棋可以先拿主教，6. Bxc6。这导致了著名的柏林墙残局，6...dxc6 7. dxe5 Nf5 8. Qxd8+ Kxd8，白方很难取得比平局更多的成绩。

如果白方允许黑方拿走他们的象，6.dxe5，黑方实际上并没有赢得它，这会导致一笔大交易。 6...Nxb5 7.a4 Nbd4 8.Nxd4 Nxd4 9.Qxd4 d5。如果白棋走 10。exd6 e.p. Qxd6= 这就是著名的柏林抽签：双方都没有什么比在 e 档和 d 档之间移动他们的皇后更好的了。

白方可以撤退主教，6。Ba4 Showalter 变体，它允许黑方将棋子 6...exd4 或将 6...e4 推到马防守的棋子处。无论哪种方式，游戏都被认为是平等的。

间奏曲 6. Bg5!? Be7 7. Bxe7 Qxe7 已尝试避免 Bxc6 之后的皇后交易并推迟残局。

历史

以德国国际象棋大师和作曲家鲁道夫·埃尔梅命名。

explanations.text:
Ruy Lopez: Berlin Wall Endgame

After trading off the pawns and minor pieces in the center of the board, both sides find themselves in an undeveloped and rather drawish position. For this reason, it has gained a reputation for being an unexciting opening which has almost always led to draws in games between grandmasters. However, some players have argued that White holds an imbalance with a kingside majority while Black's bishop pair can dominate the board.

GM Vladimir Kramnik was the one who popularized the position among chess players like Magnus Carlsen and Viswanathan Anand.

explanations.textZh:
鲁伊·洛佩兹：柏林墙终局之战

在交换了棋盘中央的棋子和小棋子后，双方发现自己处于一个未开发且相当吸引人的位置。出于这个原因，它被认为是一个平淡的开局，几乎总是导致大师之间的平局。然而，一些棋手认为，白棋在王侧多数方面处于不平衡状态，而黑棋的主教对可以在棋盘上占据主导地位。

总经理弗拉基米尔·克拉姆尼克 (Vladimir Kramnik) 是在马格努斯·卡尔森 (Magnus Carlsen) 和维斯瓦纳坦·阿南德 (Viswanathan Anand) 等国际象棋棋手中推广这一立场的人。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...Nf6/4. O-O/4...Ng4
explanations.text:
4...Ng4?! · Fishing pole variation

Black's knight forays into White's territory. This leads to a trap where Black baits White into opening the h-file.

After 5. h3 h5 sets a trap: the bait is the g4 knight, the h3 pawn is the fish, and the h5 pawn is the hook. Black appears to blunder his knight, but 6. hxg4?? hxg4 opens the h-file onto White's castled king, and attacks the f3 knight. Trying to save the knight leads to forced mate, 7. Nh2?? Qh4!. White's best recourse is to allow the knight to be captured.

White can sidestep the trap by leaving Black's knight on g4 and continuing to develop normally: 6. c3 intending d4, 6. d4, 6. Nc3 are all playable and leave White with the advantage.

The same trap can arise out of the Morphy defence, after 3...a6 4. Ba4 Nf6 5. O-O Ng4.

4...NG4？！ · 鱼竿变异

黑方的马侵入白方的领土。这导致了黑方诱使白方打开 h 文件的陷阱。

5.h3 h5后设置陷阱：诱饵是g4骑士，h3棋子是鱼，h5棋子是鱼钩。黑棋似乎搞错了他的马，但是 6. hxg4?? hxg4 打开 h 文件攻击白方的城堡国王，并攻击 f3 骑士。试图拯救骑士导致被迫交配，7. Nh2?? Qh4！白方最好的办法就是让马被俘获。

白方可以通过将黑方的马留在 g4 上并继续正常发展来避开陷阱：6. c3 打算 d4、6. d4、6. Nc3 都可以下棋，让白方获得优势。

在 3...a6 4. Ba4 Nf6 5. O-O Ng4 之后，Morphy 防守也会出现同样的陷阱。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...Nf6/4. O-O/4...Bc5
explanations.text:
4...Bc5 · Beverwijk variation

A sideline in the Berlin defence where Black has developed their bishop to its most active square.

White can take the pawn, 5. Nxe5. Although the e5 pawn appears to be defended by Black's knight, the position of the bishop on c5 means that it is potentially forkable. Therefore, 5...Nxe5 is met with 6. d4, forking the bishop and knight. Nevertheless, Black can safely navigate this and eventually recover the pawn, though Black needs to be aware of the danger of Re1, exploiting the open e-file while their king is still in the centre (e.g. 6...Nxe4? 7. dxc5 Nxc5 8. Re1!).

5...Nxe4 first is also playable, where 6. Re1? is a mistake allowing 6...Bxf2+ forking the king and rook. After 6. Qe2 instead, leaving the rook to guard f2, one continuation is 6...Nxe5 7. Qxe4 Qe7 8. d4 Nc6 9. Qxe7+ Bxe7.

5. c3 preparing d4, is the most common continuation and more straight-forward than the complicated 5. Nxe5 lines. 5. c3 is called the Zukertort gambit: White is actually offering Black their e-pawn, 5...Nxe4, but they can recover it easily enough after 6. Qe2.

5. Re1?, though it seems natural, is a mistake due to the pressure the bishop is exerting on f2. After 5...Ng4, White will have to move their rook back again. (6. d4 is a nice try but insufficient. At best, 6...Nxd4 7. Be3 Nxe3 8. fxe3 Nxb5, Black is up a bishop and a pawn.)

explanations.textZh:
4...Bc5 · 贝弗韦克变奏

柏林防守中的边线，黑棋将其主教发展到了最活跃的方阵。

白棋可以拿走棋子，5。Nxe5。虽然 e5 棋子看起来是由黑方的马防守的，但 c5 上主教的位置意味着它有可能被分叉。因此，5...Nxe5 与 6.d4 相遇，将主教和马分叉。尽管如此，黑方可以安全地解决这个问题并最终收回棋子，尽管黑方需要意识到Re1的危险，在他们的王仍在中心时利用打开的电子文件（例如6...Nxe4？7.dxc5 Nxc5 8.Re1！）。

5...Nxe4第一个也能玩，6.Re1在哪里？允许 6...Bxf2+ 分叉国王和车是一个错误。 6. Qe2 之后，让车去防守 f2，一连串是 6...Nxe5 7. Qxe4 Qe7 8. d4 Nc6 9. Qxe7+ Bxe7。

5. c3 准备 d4，是最常见的延续，比复杂的 5. Nxe5 行更直接。 5. c3 被称为 Zukertort 策略：白方实际上向黑方提供了他们的电子棋子 5...Nxe4，但他们可以在 6. Qe2 之后轻松恢复它。

5. Re1？虽然看起来很自然，但由于主教对f2施加压力而导致错误。 5...Ng4 之后，白方将不得不再次将车移回原位。 （6. d4 是一个不错的尝试，但还不够。最多，6...Nxd4 7. Be3 Nxe3 8. fxe3 Nxb5，黑棋是一个主教和一个棋子。）

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...Nf6/4. O-O/4...Bc5/5. c3
explanations.text:
5. c3 · Zukertort gambit

White leaves their e4 pawn undefended.

Accepting with 5...Nxe4 increases the pressure on f2. If White plays inaccurately they are in trouble: 6. Re1?? allows either 6...Bxf2+! (7. Kh1 Bxe1 8. Qxe1 Nf6 and Black is up four points of material) or 6...Nxf2! (7. Qa4 Nd3+ 8. Re3 Bxe3+ 9. dxe3 Nxc1). White can try 6. d4 to obstruct the bishop, but their best reply is 6. Qe2, attacking the knight and eventually winning back the pawn or more.

More common is to decline with 5...O-O, avoiding these complications. White continues 6. d4 and achieves a big centre with tempo.

With White having now played c3, 5...a6? is a mistake. White's pawn on c3 now prevents Black's standard exchange Spanish rejoinder Qd4. 5...a6? 6. Bxc6 dxc6 7. Nxe4 and 7...Qd4 is not possible due to the pawn on c3.

explanations.textZh:
5. c3 · Zukertort 策略

白棋让他们的 e4 棋子不设防。

接受 5...Nxe4 会增加 f2 的压力。如果白方下棋不准确，他们就会遇到麻烦： 6. Re1？允许 6...Bxf2+! （7. Kh1 Bxe1 8. Qxe1 Nf6 和黑棋是四点材料）或 6...Nxf2！ (7.Qa4 Nd3+ 8.Re3 Bxe3+ 9.dxe3 Nxc1)。白棋可以尝试6.d4来阻碍象，但他们最好的回应是6.Qe2，攻击马并最终赢回棋子或更多。

更常见的是以 5...O-O 拒绝，避免这些并发症。白棋继续6.d4并以节奏实现大中锋。

现在白棋已经下c3、5...a6？是一个错误。现在，白棋在 c3 上的棋子阻止了黑棋的标准交换西班牙语反驳 Qd4。 5...a6？ 6. Bxc6 dxc6 7. 由于 c3 上的棋子，Nxe4 和 7...Qd4 是不可能的。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bb5/3...h6
explanations.text:
3...h6!? - Sideline

The h6 sideline in the Spanish Game

The h6 sideline in the Ruy Lopez is a rare and provocative move that aims to prevent White from playing Bg5 and pinning the black knight. It also prepares to play g5 and Bg7, creating a kingside fianchetto. However, it also has some drawbacks, such as:

It weakens the g6-square and the dark squares around the black king.

It delays the development of the black pieces and the castling of the black king.

It allows White to play d4 and gain a strong center. The main line after 3…h6 is 4.d4 exd4 5.Nxd4 Nf6 6.Nxc6 bxc6 7.Bd3, where White has a clear advantage in space and development. Black can try to create counterplay on the queenside with moves like d5, Bc5, O-O, and Rb8, but White can maintain the pressure with moves like O-O, Nc3, e5, and Qf3.

Another possible continuation after 3…h6 is 4.O-O g5, where Black goes all-in for a kingside attack. This is very risky and dubious, as White can exploit the weaknesses in Black’s position with moves like d4, Nc3, Nd5, c3, and Be3. For example, after 4.O-O g5 5.d4 exd4 6.Nxd4 Bg7 7.Nf5 Bf6 8.Nc3 Nge7 9.Re1 d6 10.Nd5 Nxd5 11.exd5+ Ne5 12.Nd4 O-O 13.Qh5 Bg7 14.h4 Bg4 15.Bg5 Bxh5 16.Bxd8 Raxd8 17.Nf5 Bg6 18.Ne7+ Kh7 19.hxg5 hxg5 20.Re3 Bxd3 21.Rh3+ Bh6 22.cxd3 f5 23.d4 Ng6 24.Nc6 Rde8 25.Ra3 Nf4 26.Rxa7 Rf7 27.Rb7 Nxd5 28.a4 g4 29.a5 f4 30.a6 g3 31.a7 gxf2+ 32.Kxf2 Nb6 33.Rb8 Rff8 34.Rxe8 Rxe8 35.Nb8 Na8 36.Rc1 Re7 37.Nc6 Re8 38.Rc3 Bg7 39.Rb3 Nb6 40.Rxb6 cxb6 41.Nb8 Bxd4+ 42.Kf3 b5 43.Nc6 Bxa7 44.Nxa7 b4 45.Nc6 b3 46.Nd4 Re3+ 47.Kxf4 Rd3 48.Ke4 Rd2 49.Nxb3 Rxb2 50.Nd4 Rxg2 51.Kd5 Rd2 52.Kc4 Rxd4+ 53.Kxd4 Kg6 54.Kd5 Kf5 55.Kxd6 1/2-1/2, White had a clear advantage throughout the game, but failed to convert it into a win.

explanations.textZh:
3...h6！？ - 边线

西班牙比赛中的h6边线

鲁伊·洛佩兹的 h6 边线是一种罕见且具有挑衅性的举动，旨在阻止白棋下 Bg5 并压制黑马。它还准备演奏 g5 和 Bg7，创建王翼前奏。然而，它也有一些缺点，例如：

它削弱了g6方格和黑王周围的黑暗方格。

它延迟了黑棋的发展和黑王的易位。

它让白方可以下 d4 并获得一个强大的中锋。 3…h6之后的主线是4.d4 exd4 5.Nxd4 Nf6 6.Nxc6 bxc6 7.Bd3，其中白棋在空间和发展上具有明显的优势。黑棋可以尝试用 d5、Bc5、O-O 和 Rb8 等棋子在后翼发起反击，但白棋可以用 O-O、Nc3、e5 和 Qf3 等棋子维持压力。
