explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4
explanations.text:
3. Bc4 · Italian game

White develops the bishop to a good square where it controls a valuable diagonal. From c4 the Bishop controls d5 and pressures Black's f7-pawn, the most vulnerable pawn in Blacks position. Having developed both their kingside minor pieces quickly, White is ready to castle. White's plans include a swift attack on f7 and building a big centre with c3 and d4.

There is no immediate threat to Black's position so they have some flexibility in how to respond. It would be good to develop a piece, and there are several options, the top two being 3...Nf6, the Two Knights, or 3...Bc5, the Giuoco Piano, which is a choice of whether to keep or to release control of g5.

Attack e4

3...Nf6 is the Two Knights defence. This develops a piece and puts pressure on e4.

If White should try to defend it with 4. Nc3, this allows the centre fork trick 4...Nxe4 5. Nxe4 d5 6. Bd3 dxe4 7. Bxe4. Therefore White more usually defends it with 4. d3, which can transpose into the Giuoco Pianissimo (see below), or with 4. Ng5, a sharp move that also attacks f7 and can lead to an aggressive knight sacrifice known as the Fried liver. The Two Knights defence has the reputation for bringing about a tactical and sharp game.

=== Control g5 ===

The most common move (about 53% of games) is 3...Bc5. By developing the kingside bishop before the kingside knight, Black's queen keeps control of the g5 square, then after 4...Nf6, Black is ready to castle 5...O-O.

By developing the kingside in this order, Black avoids the sharper Ng5 lines that follow the Two Knights defence: g5 is controlled by the queen until Black is ready to castle and defend f7 with the rook. Hence this continuation is called the Giuoco Piano (Italian: Quiet game): it avoids the sharp Ng5 continuations in favour of a steadier, more positional game.

Although 3...Nf6 4. Ng5 is not winning by force, avoiding the complications with 3...Bc5 is a bit more common.

After 3...Bc5, White usual plans are to continue with c3 and d4 to build a strong centre, or c3 and d3, the Giuoco Pianissimo (Italian: Very quiet game). Despite the "quiet game" soubriquet, Black may face some aggressive sidelines, including 4. b4, the Evans gambit.

3...h6, called the Anti-Fried Liver, is an amateur attempt to avoid the Ng5 lines. The idea is to allow Black to play 4...Nf6 without giving up control of g5. Though this is a straightforward idea, its drawbacks are that it does not control the centre or develop a piece, and essentially just gives White extra tempo to attack. White can play 4. d4 to bust open the centre, and Black has no time to play 4...Nf6 after all. 4...exd4 5. Nxd4 Nxd4 6. Qxd4. Then, before Black can get their knight out, they must play 6...d6 to prevent e5, letting White get further ahead in development (see diagram). 3...h6 is strictly inferior to 3...Bc5.

3...Be7, the Hungarian defence, is a minor sideline. This is a more conservative developing move to get ready to castle while not giving up control of g5 yet. After 4. d4 d6, a Philidor-style position is reached. This usually leads to the centre opening up and a queen trade. 5. dxe5 dxe5 6. Qxd8+ Bxd8.

3...d6, the Paris defence, is very passive. It avoids developing a piece and restricts Black's kingside bishop to over defend e5, which wasn't at risk anyway. This usually transposes into an Exchange Philidor: 4. d4 exd4 5. Nxd4 Nf6 6. Nc3 and Black's bishop has nowhere better to go than 6...Be7.

Wild gambits

3...Nd4?!, the Blackburne shilling gambit or Kostić gambit, is primarily a psychological try. Black pretends to blunder their e-pawn, but has a crushing response prepared: 4. Nxe5? Qg5! (see diagram). However after 4. Nxd4 exd4 Black is behind in development and cannot find compensation.

3...f5?!, the Rousseau gambit, resembles a Vienna gambit with colours reversed. Black hopes White will take the offered pawn, 4. exf5?, deflecting one of their pawns from the centre and allowing 4...e5, and the only place for the White's knight to go is back to g1. However, White can decline with 4. d3 or countergambit with 4. d4

History

The Italian game is one of the oldest openings in chess.

Early studies of the opening were published in the 17th century by the Italians Giulio Cesare Polerio and Gioachino Greco, the strongest player of his time. 3...Bc5, the Giuoco Piano, was the usual continuation.

In the 18th century it was promoted by the Modenese masters, including Domenico Lorenzo Ponziani. The Modenese school of thought emphasised piece activity and material over pawn structure (in contrast to their contemporary Philidor), and thought that White's bishop was better developed to c4, from where it could attack f7, rather than b5 to pressure the e5 (as in the Spanish game).

In the 19th century, the popularity of the Romantic style of lead to a shift to more tactical lines. 4. b4, the Evans gambit, reinvigorated the Giuoco Piano and became the most common continuation, a favourite of Morphy and the like.

explanations.textZh:
3.BC4·意大利比赛

白方将象发展成一个良好的方格，控制着一条有价值的对角线。从 c4 开始，主教控制 d5 并向黑棋的 f7 棋子施加压力，这是黑棋位置上最脆弱的棋子。在快速开发出王翼的两个小子后，白棋已准备好城堡。白方的计划包括快速进攻f7并与c3和d4建立一个大中锋。

布莱克的位置没有立即受到威胁，因此他们在如何应对方面有一定的灵活性。开发一首曲子就好了，有几个选择，前两个是3...Nf6，两个骑士，或者3...Bc5，Giuoco Piano，这是一个选择是保留还是释放对g5的控制。

攻击e4

3...Nf6 是两骑士防御。这发展了一块，给e4带来了压力。

如果白方应该尝试用 4. Nc3 防守，这将允许中心叉技巧 4...Nxe4 5. Nxe4 d5 6. Bd3 dxe4 7. Bxe4。因此，白棋通常用 4. d3 来防御，它可以转换为 Giuoco Pianissimo（见下文），或者用 4. Ng5，这是一种尖锐的棋步，也可以攻击 f7，并可能导致被称为“炸肝”的侵略性骑士牺牲。两骑士的防守以带来战术性和犀利的比赛而闻名。

===控制g5 ===

最常见的走法（约 53% 的游戏）是 3...Bc5。通过在王边骑士之前发展王边主教，黑方后可以控制 g5 方格，然后在 4...Nf6 之后，黑方准备城堡 5...O-O。

通过按此顺序发展王侧，黑方避免了遵循两骑士防御的更尖锐的 Ng5 线：g5 由后控制，直到黑方准备好用车筑垒并防守 f7。因此，这个延续被称为 Giuoco Piano（意大利语：安静的游戏）：它避免了尖锐的 Ng5 延续，有利于更稳定、更有位置的游戏。

虽然 3...Nf6 4. Ng5 并不是靠武力取胜，但避免 3...Bc5 的并发症更为常见。

3...Bc5 之后，白棋通常的计划是继续使用 c3 和 d4 建立一个强大的中锋，或者 c3 和 d3，Giuoco Pianissimo（意大利语：非常安静的游戏）。尽管有“安静游戏”的绰号，布莱克可能会面临一些激进的边线，包括 4. b4，埃文斯开局。

3...h6，称为反炸肝，是一种避免 Ng5 线的业余尝试。这个想法是让黑棋下4...Nf6而不放弃对g5的控制。虽然这是一个简单的想法，但它的缺点是它不能控制中心或开发棋子，并且本质上只是给白方额外的进攻节奏。白棋可以下4.d4来破坏中心，而黑棋毕竟没有时间下4...Nf6。 4...exd4 5.Nxd4 Nxd4 6.Qxd4。然后，在黑棋出局之前，他们必须下 6...d6 来阻止 e5，让白棋进一步领先（见图）。 3...h6 严格低于 3...Bc5。

3...Be7，匈牙利的防守，是一个次要的边线。这是一个更为保守的发展举措，目的是在不放弃对 g5 控制权的情况下做好城堡准备。 4. d4 d6 之后，达到 Philidor 风格的位置。这通常会导致中心开放和女王交易。 5. dxe5 dxe5 6. Qxd8+ Bxd8。

3...d6，巴黎后防线非常被动。它避免了发展棋子并限制黑方王翼主教过度防守 e5，而 e5 无论如何都没有危险。这通常转变成交换 Philidor： 4. d4 exd4 5. Nxd4 Nf6 6. Nc3 和布莱克的主教没有比 6...Be7 更好的去处。

狂野的策略

3...Nd4？！，布莱克本先令策略或科斯蒂奇策略，主要是一种心理尝试。黑方假装犯了错误，但已经准备好了一个毁灭性的回应： 4. Nxe5？ Qg5！ （见图）。然而4.Nxd4 exd4 Black之后发展落后，无法找到补偿。

3...f5?!，卢梭策略，类似于颜色相反的维也纳策略。黑方希望白方接受所提供的棋子，4. exf5？，将他们的一个棋子从中心偏转并允许 4...e5，而白方的马唯一可以去的地方是回到 g1。然而，白棋可以用 4. d3 下棋，或者用 4. d4 进行反击

历史

意大利棋是国际象棋中最古老的开局之一。

意大利人 Giulio Cesare Polerio 和当时最强大的棋手 Gioachino Greco 在 17 世纪发表了对开局的早期研究。 3...Bc5，Giuoco Piano，是通常的延续。

18世纪，它受到包括多梅尼科·洛伦佐·庞齐亚尼（Domenico Lorenzo Ponziani）在内的摩德纳大师的推动。摩德内斯思想流派强调棋子的活动和材料而不是兵结构（与同时代的 Philidor 形成鲜明对比），并认为白方的主教更好地发展到 c4，从那里它可以攻击 f7，而不是 b5 来压力 e5（如西班牙游戏中）。

19世纪，浪漫主义风格的流行导致了战术路线的转变。 4. b4，Evans 的策略，重振了 Giuoco Piano 的活力，并成为最常见的延续，是 Morphy 等人的最爱。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Nd4
explanations.text:
3...Nd4? · Blackburne shilling gambit

Black violates an opening principle by moving his knight again. Black hopes to tempt White into taking the unprotected e5 pawn.

4. Nxe5?? falls into Black's trap. After 4...Qg5, forking White's knight the g2 pawn, White is in dire trouble. If White attempts to save the knight, (5. Nxf7?? Qxg2) then White has to give up the rook instead. If they try to hold onto their rook, then they must give up their queen or get mated. (6. Rf1 Qxe4+ 7. Qe2 (7. Be2? Nf3#) 7...Nxe2) 5. Bxf7+ is the only way to stay in the game.

The gambit is a one-trick pony: as long as White avoids 4. Nxe5??, they are comfortably ahead. For this reason, Black is supposed to exclaim, "Oh my God!" to sell the illusion that they have blundered a pawn.

Black's knight is misplaced and they are falling behind in development, so White has a lot of good options. White can simply decline the gambit with 4. O-O or kick Black's knight with 4. c3 (both of these usually induce 4...Nxf3 5. Qxf3). The most critical line is 4. Nxd4.

4. Nxd4 exd4 trades knights and dislodges Black's pawn from e5. This opens up a number of tactical opportunities for White. After 4...exd4, White has an idea of playing e5 themself, e.g. 4...exd4 5. O-O Nf6 6. Re1 Bc5? 7. e5! Ng8 (only safe square for the knight). Another idea is that Qh5 can attack f7 while forking anything on the fifth rank, e.g. 4...exd4 5. O-O Bc5? 6. Bxf7+ Kxf7 7. Qh5+ Ke7 8. Qxc5+ d6 9. Qxd4 nets White two pawns.

History

This gambit is named for Joseph Henry Blackburne (1841-1924), who apocryphally used to win shillings (about £3-4 today) from amateurs in coffee shops. It is also called the Kostić gambit after Serbian grandmaster Boris Kostić (1887-1963), who was recorded to have a game in this line in 1912.

Steinitz published an analysis of the gambit in 1895, recommending 4. O-O or 4. Nxd4, but did not associate it with Blackburne.

explanations.textZh:
3...Nd4？ · 布莱克本先令策略

黑棋再次移动他的马，违反了开局原则。黑方希望引诱白方吃掉未受保护的 e5 棋子。

4.Nxe5??落入黑棋的陷阱。 4...Qg5 之后，白棋的马成为 g2 兵，白棋陷入了可怕的麻烦。如果白方试图拯救马，(5. Nxf7?? Qxg2) 那么白方必须放弃车。如果它们试图保住自己的车，那么它们就必须放弃它们的女王或进行交配。 (6. Rf1 Qxe4+ 7. Qe2 (7. Be2? Nf3#) 7...Nxe2) 5. Bxf7+ 是留在游戏中的唯一方法。

策略是一招小马：只要白方避免 4. Nxe5??，他们就轻松领先。因此，布莱克应该惊呼：“天啊！”出售他们误入棋子的错觉。

黑棋的马位置不对，发展落后，所以白棋有很多好的选择。白方可以简单地用 4. O-O 拒绝这一策略，或者用 4. c3 踢黑方的马（这两种通常都会导致 4...Nxf3 5. Qxf3）。最关键的一行是4.Nxd4。

4. Nxd4 exd4 交易马并将黑方棋子从 e5 中移出。这为白棋提供了许多战术机会。在 4...exd4 之后，白方有自己下 e5 的想法，例如4...exd4 5. O-O Nf6 6. Re1 Bc5？ 7.e5！ Ng8（对骑士来说唯一安全的方格）。另一个想法是 Qh5 可以攻击 f7，同时分叉第五级上的任何内容，例如4...exd4 5.O-O Bc5？ 6. Bxf7+ Kxf7 7. Qh5+ Ke7 8. Qxc5+ d6 9. Qxd4 净白棋两子。

历史

这一策略以约瑟夫·亨利·布莱克本 (Joseph Henry Blackburne，1841-1924 年) 的名字命名，据传说，他曾经在咖啡馆从业余爱好者那里赢过先令（今天约为 3-4 英镑）。它也被称为科斯蒂奇弃兵，以塞尔维亚大师鲍里斯·科斯蒂奇（Boris Kostić，1887-1963）的名字命名，据记录，他于 1912 年在该路线上进行过一场比赛。

斯坦尼茨在 1895 年发表了对该策略的分析，推荐 4. O-O 或 4. Nxd4，但没有将其与布莱克本联系起来。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Nd4/4. Nxe5
explanations.text:
4. Nxe5?

This move looks natural, but it is a bad move as there is a strong double attack. It turns out that Black's pawn on e5 wasn't free.

After 4...Qg5!, both e5 and g2 are attacked by the queen. White is in a lot of trouble and has to give up a knight to have a playable game with either 5. Bxf7+ or 5. O-O, both with a better position for Black.

4.Nxe5？

这一招看似理所当然，但却是一个糟糕的招式，因为它有很强的双重攻击。事实证明，黑方在 e5 上的棋子并不是免费的。

4...Qg5!之后，e5和g2都受到了皇后的攻击。白棋陷入了很多麻烦，必须放弃马才能与 5. Bxf7+ 或 5. O-O 进行比赛，这两种棋对黑棋来说都有更好的位置。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Nd4/4. Nxe5/4...Qg5
explanations.text:
4...Qg5!

Accepting the gambit was a mistake, as Black now shows with the accurate 4...Qg5.

Attempting to hold on to the knight with 5. Nxf7?? will result in 5...Qxg2!, in which White will lose either the rook, attempt to hold on to the rook and lose the queen with 6. Rf1 Qxe4+, or get checkmated by attempting to keep both the rook and the queen with 7. Be2 Nf3#.

Better for White is 5. Bxf7+, which loses a piece for two pawns but keeps White in the game.

/5. O-O/ is another possible option. White castles and defends g2 while giving away the e5 knight to try and get development as compensation for the lost knight.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Nd4/4. Nxe5/4...Qg5/5. O-O
explanations.text:
5. O-O

White resists the temptation to take the 'free' pawn on f7 but instead calmly castles, sacrificing their e5 knight while defending g2 and relocating their king to safety.

5...Qxe5 is obviously the best move. Black captures the free knight and is now up 2 points of material, but they are only slightly better as White will get developmental compensation after 6. c3 followed by 7. d4.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Nd4/4. Nxe5/4...Qg5/5. Nxf7/5...Qxg2/6. Rf1
explanations.text:
6. Rf1

Rf1 seems like a defense to the gambit, but Black can play 6...Qxe4+ and White must sacrifice their queen or allow checkmate.

Better was 6. Ng5, which gives away the rook but moves the knight to safety and protects the e4-pawn. After 6...Qxh1+ White can play 7. Bf1.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Nd4/4. Nxe5/4...Qg5/5. Nxf7/5...Qxg2/6. Rf1/6...Qxe4
explanations.text:
6...Qxe4+

White is completely lost. Black plays 6...Qxe4+, which allows for two options.

The worse of the two options doesn't seem the worst, but 7. Be2? allows the smothered mate (7...Nf3#) where the bishop is pinned.

Therefore White must give away the queen with 7. Qe2 and play on without that queen.

6...Qxe4+

白彻底迷失了。黑方下 6...Qxe4+，有两种选择。

3... d6

Similar to the Philidor's Defence, but here the e5-pawn is already defended. Black's kingside bishop is now blocked in behind the pawn chain. White has a spatial advantage.

explanations.text:
Paris Defence

4... Bg4

The White knight is somewhat pinned, however allows for the Legal Trap if White 'sacrifices' their queen with 5. Nxe5.

More sound, however, is first playing 5. h3. If Black mistakenly tries to maintain their pin with 5...Bh5, White can freely attempt Legal's Trap with 6. Nxe5! without worry of being down on material if Black captures their knight.

explanations.text:

5. Nxe5? - Legal Trap

Legal's trap is named after the French player Sire de Legall, one of the best players of the 1700s. Although 5. Nxe5 is a losing move, as it leaves White's knight hanging, a naive opponent might capture White's queen with 5...Bxd1??. This leads to a mate in 2 for White (6. Bxf7+! Ke7 7. Nd5#).

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...f5
explanations.text:
Rousseau Gambit

3...f5

White has two strong choices: The first is to support with 4. d3. This results in a reversed King's Gambit Declined, dangerous for both sides. Black often places their pieces in typical Giuoco Piano fashion and waits for white to castle kingside before pushing f4. Black will attack the kingside and white will attack in the center.

White can also play 4. d4. Black responds by taking one of the pawns. If 4...exd4 then 5. e5 and black will play 5...d5 or 5...d6 allowing the center to open; white quickly castles with a huge initiative. If 4...fxe4 then 5. Nxe5 and white is in an improved version of the main line of the Latvian Gambit.

Taking with 4. exf5? is a common mistake by beginners. After 4...e4, white has to find the piece sacrifice 5. Nd4!, planning to respond to 5...Nxd4?? with Qh5+ and going into massive complications that favor white. But if black plays the correct 5...Nf6 then black already has a small advantage. Attempting to defend the pawn with 4. Nc3?? is a losing blunder.

Key themes for White at this point are to attack Black's kingside using the light bishop and to resist attempts by black to simplify the position via exchanges. Exchanges involving White's light bishop are particularly suspect. The best advice for Black is to not play this gambit, as it's considered to be refuted.

explanations.textZh:
卢梭开局

3...f5

白方有两个强有力的选择：第一个是用 4.d3 来支援。这会导致国王弃兵的逆转，对双方来说都很危险。黑棋经常以典型的 Giuoco Piano 方式放置棋子，并等待白棋占领王翼，然后再推 f4。黑方将攻击王翼，白方将攻击中央。

白棋也可以下4.d4。黑方以拿走其中一颗棋子作为回应。如果 4...exd4 则 5。e5 和黑棋将下 5...d5 或 5...d6，让中心打开；白迅速攻城略地，主动出击。如果 4...fxe4 那么 5。Nxe5 和白色是拉脱维亚开局主线的改进版本。

与 4.exf5 一起服用？是初学者常犯的错误。 4...e4之后，白棋必须找到牺牲5.Nd4！的棋子，计划回应5...Nxd4？与 Qh5+ 并进入有利于白色的大量并发症。但如果黑棋下正确的 5...Nf6，那么黑棋就已经有了一点优势。试图用 4. Nc3 保卫棋子？是一个失败的错误。

此时白棋的关键主题是利用轻主教攻击黑棋的王翼，并抵制黑棋通过交换来简化局面的尝试。涉及怀特之光主教的交易尤其值得怀疑。对黑棋来说最好的建议是不要玩这个策略，因为它被认为是被驳斥的。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5
explanations.text:
3...Bc5 · Giuoco Piano

This is one of the two main branches of the Italian game. Black develops their kingside bishop ahead of the knight: this move order keeps control of g5 until Black is ready to castle. Compared to the Two Knights defence (3...Nf6), where Black develops while making an attack on e4, this is considered the slower and more positional continuation, hence the name which in Italian means "quiet game".

White chooses between two sorts of plans: to get their pawn to d4, or to content themselves with d3 (the hallmark move of the giuoco pianissimo, "very quiet game").

Strike in the centre

Currently Black controls d4 three times and White twice, so White will need to wrestle for control of the square first if they wish to play d4 and keep it there.

4. d4!? immediately is the Italian or Rosentreter gambit. White gambits the pawn and can lose it one of three ways: 4...exd4, 4...Bxd4, or 4...Nxd4. White usually pins their hopes on turning around a quick attack on the weak f7 pawn, e.g. 4...exd4 5. c3 dxc3? 6. Bxf7+! Kxf7 7. Qd5+!--but otherwise the gambit is not quite sound.

4. c3 is the classical variation. This adds control to the d4 square and so prepares for White to occupy it with their d-pawn. After 4...Nf6 5. d4 exd4 6. cxd4 (Black's bishop is attacked) Bb4+ the modern main line is 7. Bd2, and Black chooses between 7...Bxd2+ or 7...Nxe4, the latter of which doesn't really win a pawn on account of a tactical sequence involving Bxf2+: 8. Bxb4 Nxb4 9. Bxf7+ Kxf7 10. Qb3+ Kf8 11. Qxb4+ Qe7 12. Qxe7+ Kxe7.

This endgame might be why the line with 6. cxd4 has fallen out of favor, so more common nowadays is 6. e5, which attacks the knight on f6, and gains space. Black almost responds with 6...d5, in which the game usually continues 7. Bb5 Ne4 8. cxd4 Bb6, with a slight advantage to White.

Alternatively, White may also play 6. b4!?, known as the Dubov Italian, popularized by GM Daniil Dubov. Though this line is considered somewhat dubious, it can serve as a venomous weapon if Black isn't prepared.

Alternatively, c3 can serve as a springboard for b4: 4...Nf6 5. b4!? is called Bird's attack.

4. b4 is the Evan's gambit. This first deflects the bishop to b4, allowing White to play c3 with tempo on the bishop. This line was hugely popular in the 19th century.

Keep the position closed

White doesn't have to push for d4 right away. They may be happy with the solid d3: it supports e4 and is enough to allow the queen's bishop to develop. It also allows White's knight to reach the active c3 square. The key feature of the giuoco pianissimo is d3, whether it is played immediately 4. d3 or after castling 4. O-O Nf6 5. d3 or developing the knight 4. Nc3 Nf6 5. d3, etc.

The most common line today is for White to play with pawns on both c3 and d3 (after 4. d3 Nf6 5. c3 or in the order 4. c3 Nf6 d3) which is the most concrete continuation.

Wild gambits

4. Bxf7+? is the unhinged Jerome gambit. Though a Bxf7+ sacrifice works in many lines in the Italian, this is far too early and it is objectively woeful for White. However, it is sharp enough that White has some success at the club level. The idea is 4...Kxf7 5. Nxe5+ Nxe5 6. Qh5+, and White hopes that between Black's exposed king and the skewering of Black's pieces on the fifth rank they will swindle compensation. e.g. 6. Qh5+ g6 7. Qxe5 d6?? (better is Qe7) 8. Qxh8.

O-O Nf6 5. d3 or developing the knight 4. Nc3 Nf6 5. d3, etc.

The most common line today is for White to play with pawns on both c3 and d3 (after 4. d3 Nf6 5. c3 or in the order 4. c3 Nf6 d3) which is the most concrete continuation.

Wild gambits

4. Bxf7+? is the unhinged Jerome gambit. Though a Bxf7+ sacrifice works in many lines in the Italian, this is far too early and it is objectively woeful for White. However, it is sharp enough that White has some success at the club level. The idea is 4...Kxf7 5. Nxe5+ Nxe5 6. Qh5+, and White hopes that between Black's exposed king and the skewering of Black's pieces on the fifth rank they will swindle compensation. e.g. 6. Qh5+ g6 7. Qxe5 d6?? (better is Qe7) 8. Qxh8.
explanations.textZh:
3...Bc5 · 乔科钢琴

这是意大利足球的两个主要分支之一。黑方在马之前发展了他们的王翼象：此移动顺序保持对 g5 的控制，直到黑方准备好城堡。与黑方一边进攻 e4 一边发展的双马防御 (3...Nf6) 相比，这被认为是更慢、更具位置性的延续，因此得名，在意大利语中意为“安静的游戏”。

白方在两种计划之间进行选择：将棋子放到 d4，或者满足于 d3（giuoco pianissimo 的标志性动作，“非常安静的游戏”）。

攻击中心

目前黑方控制了 d4 3 次，白方控制了 2 次，因此白方如果想下 d4 并将其保留在那里，就需要首先争夺方格的控制权。

4.d4！？立即是意大利或罗森特雷特的策略。白方弃兵并可以通过以下三种方式之一输掉它：4...exd4、4...Bxd4 或 4...Nxd4。白方通常寄希望于扭转对弱f7兵的快速攻击，例如4...exd4 5.c3 dxc3？ 6.Bxf7+！ Kxf7 7. Qd5+！——但除此之外，这个策略并不十分合理。

4. c3 是经典变体。这增加了对 d4 方格的控制，为白方用 d 兵占据它做好准备。 4...Nf6 5. d4 exd4 6. cxd4（黑方的主教受到攻击）Bb4+之后，现代主线是 7. Bd2，黑方在 7...Bxd2+ 或 7...Nxe4 之间进行选择，后者由于涉及 Bxf2+ 的战术顺序并没有真正赢得棋子： 8. Bxb4 Nxb4 9. Bxf7+ Kxf7 10. Qb3+ Kf8 11. Qxb4+ Qe7 12. Qxe7+ Kxe7。

这个残局可能就是为什么 6.cxd4 这条线已经失宠的原因，所以现在更常见的是 6.e5，它攻击 f6 上的骑士，并获得空间。黑方几乎以 6...d5 回应，其中游戏通常继续 7. Bb5 Ne4 8. cxd4 Bb6，白方稍占优势。

或者，白方也可以下 6. b4!?，称为杜博夫意大利式，由 GM 丹尼尔·杜博夫推广。尽管这条线被认为有些可疑，但如果黑方没有做好准备，它可以成为有毒的武器。

或者，c3 可以作为 b4 的跳板：4...Nf6 5. b4！？称为鸟的攻击。

4. b4 是埃文策略。这首先将象转向 b4，允许白方以象的节奏下奏 c3。这条线在 19 世纪非常流行。

保持平仓

白方不必立即下 d4。他们可能对坚实的 d3 感到满意：它支持 e4 并且足以让皇后的主教发展。它还允许白方的马到达活动的 c3 方格。 giuoco pianissimo 的关键特征是 d3，无论是立即演奏 4. d3 还是在易位后演奏 4. O-O Nf6 5. d3 或者发展马 4. Nc3 Nf6 5. d3 等。

今天最常见的路线是白方在 c3 和 d3 上都下棋（在 4. d3 Nf6 5. c3 之后或按照 4. c3 Nf6 d3 的顺序），这是最具体的延续。

狂野的策略

4.Bxf7+？这是杰罗姆的疯狂策略。尽管 Bxf7+ 牺牲在意大利语中的许多行中都起作用，但这还为时过早，客观上对白棋来说是可悲的。然而，它足够敏锐，使得怀特在俱乐部层面取得了一些成功。这个想法是 4...Kxf7 5. Nxe5+ Nxe5 6. Qh5+，白方希望通过黑方暴露的王和黑方第五级棋子的串连来骗取补偿。例如6.Qh5+g6 7.Qxe5d6?? （更好的是Qe7） 8. Qxh8。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. b4
explanations.text:
4. b4 · Evans gambit

White offers a pawn to divert the bishop away from the centre.

White would like to play d4 and put both d and e pawns in the centre. At the moment, Black has too much control over the d4 square for that to be worthwhile. White can prepare d4 with c3, as in 4. c3, the classical variation. However, this gives Black extra time to develop and get ready to castle. The idea of 4. b4 is to achieve c3 and d4 with tempo instead.

If Black accepts the pawn, 4...Bxb4, 5. c3 prepares d4 while also forcing Black's bishop to move again. c3 also gives White's queen access to b3. 5...Ba5 (5...Bc5? and the bishop can be kicked again) 6. d4 and the main reply is 6...d6. 6...exd4 appears to be winning because the c-pawn is pinned to the king, White doesn't have to take back immediately and can unpin first. 7. Qb3 (battery against f7) Qe7 8. O-O (unpins) Bb6 9. cxd4 Nxd4 10. Nxd4 Bxd4, and though Black is up two pawns, White is thought to have compensation.

6. O-O before playing d4, known as the slow variation, avoids the c3 pawn becoming pinned and was popular in the Romantic era.

4...Bb6 declines the gambit and White switches plans to expanding on the queen's side. 5. a4 a6 (to prevent the bishop becoming trapped) 6. Nc3 is the Showalter variation.

History

Welsh sea captain William Davies Evans originated the idea of 4. b4. He first played the idea in the order 4. O-O d6 5. b4 against MacDonnell in 1827. He played 4. b4 a few years later in 1833.

This new gambit received lots of attention, leading to lots of open, tactical games and more importantly opportunities for sacrifices favoured by chess players of the era, who preferred quick, sacrificial games over long positional games. It became featured in many well-known miniatures like the "Evergreen Game" and one of the main lines of the 19th century.

The Evans gambit began to fall out of popularity with the rise of positional play, introduced by Wilhelm Steinitz, which aimed for long term advantages instead of attacking all the time. The coup de grâce came in the 20th century from Emanuel Lasker, who's defence against the gambit was to return the pawn and trade queens, sucking the energy out of the position. This was bad for the gambit player.

Lasker's defence killed the preferred slow variation. The 6. d4 line was briefly revitalised in the interwar period by Savielly Tartakower's attack, 7. Qb3. This turned out to be the best variation.

A later outing for the Evans gambit was in Garry Kasparov versus Vishwanathan Anand, 1995, but otherwise it is now rare at the highest levels of chess.

explanations.textZh:
4. b4·埃文斯策略

白方提供了一个棋子，将主教从中心转移开。

白棋想下 d4，并将 d 和 e 棋子放在中间。目前，黑方对 d4 方格拥有太多控制权，因此不值得这样做。白棋可以用 c3 准备 d4，如 4. c3 中的经典变体。然而，这给了黑方额外的时间来发展和准备城堡。 4.b4的思路是用节奏来实现c3和d4。

如果黑方接受棋子，4...Bxb4, 5。c3 准备 d4，同时也迫使黑方的主教再次移动。 c3 还让白方后能够吃到 b3。 5...Ba5（5...Bc5？并且主教可以再次被踢） 6. d4，主要回复是6...d6。 6...exd4 似乎获胜，因为 c 兵被钉在王上，白方不必立即收回并可以先取消钉住。 7. Qb3（对 f7 的电池） Qe7 8. O-O（取消固定） Bb6 9. cxd4 Nxd4 10. Nxd4 Bxd4，尽管黑方领先两兵，但白方被认为有补偿。

6. 玩 d4 之前的 O-O，称为慢变，避免 c3 棋子被钉住，在浪漫主义时代很流行。

4...Bb6 拒绝了这一策略，白方改变了在后方扩张的计划。 5. a4 a6（防止主教被困） 6. Nc3 是 Showalter 变体。

历史

威尔士船长威廉·戴维斯·埃文斯 (William Davies Evans) 提出了 4. b4 的想法。 1827 年，他在对阵 MacDonnell 的比赛中首次按照 4. O-O d6 5. b4 的顺序使用了这个想法。几年后，即 1833 年，他又使用了 4. b4。

这种新的策略受到了广泛的关注，导致了许多开放的战术游戏，更重要的是，为那个时代的棋手们所青睐的牺牲机会，他们更喜欢快速、牺牲性的游戏，而不是长时间的走位游戏。它出现在许多著名的微缩模型中，如《长青游戏》，并成为 19 世纪的主线之一。

随着威廉·斯坦尼茨（Wilhelm Steinitz）引入的阵地战的兴起，埃文斯策略开始不再流行，阵地战的目标是获得长期优势，而不是一直进攻。二十世纪的致命一击来自伊曼纽尔·拉斯克（Emanuel Lasker），他对这一策略的防御是归还典当和交易皇后，从而吸走该位置的能量。这对开局玩家来说很糟糕。

拉斯克的防守杀死了首选的缓慢变化。 6. d4 线在两次世界大战期间因萨维利·塔塔科维尔 (Savielly Tartakower) 的进攻而短暂恢复活力，7. Qb3.事实证明这是最好的变体。

后来埃文斯的策略出现在 1995 年加里·卡斯帕罗夫 (Garry Kasparov) 对阵维什瓦纳坦·阿南德 (Vishwanathan Anand) 的比赛中，但除此之外，这种策略现在在最高水平的国际象棋比赛中已经很少见了。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. b4/4...Bxb4
explanations.text:
4...Bxb4 · Evans Gambit Accepted

Black accepts the gambit with 4...Bxb4.

White almost exclusively continues with 5. c3, gaining a tempo on the bishop and supporting the ...d4 advance in the future.
explanations.textEn:
4...Bxb4 · Evans Gambit Accepted

Black accepts the gambit with 4...Bxb4.

White almost exclusively continues with 5. c3, gaining a tempo on the bishop and supporting the ...d4 advance in the future.
explanations.textZh:
4...Bxb4 · 埃文斯策略已接受

黑方接受 4...Bxb4 的弃兵。

白方几乎完全继续使用 5.c3，获得主教的节奏并支持未来 ...d4 的推进。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. b4/4...Bxb4/5. c3
explanations.text:
Evans Gambit Accepted

With 5. c3, White attacks the bishop and also supports the d4 advance in the future.

Black must do something about the bishop, and there are 5 safe squares for the bishop.

Rare retreats

5...Bf8?! is the Mayet defence. This undevelops the bishop, and is the worst move of the five, as in order to castle kingside, Black must move it again in addition to the g8-knight. White almost always play 6. d4 in order to punish this move, in which he has gained a comfortable advantage.

5...Bc5?! is the McDonnell Defence. This is usually only played by beginners, thinking this move stops the d4 push, but it actually doesn't, and white can then play 6. d4 which also gains a tempo on the bishop.

5...Bd6!? is the Stone-Ware Defence. Although this blocks the d-pawn, it also adds a defender to the e5-pawn, so when 6. d4 happens, it won't come with an attack on the pawn.

Common retreats

5...Be7 is the Anderssen variation. This is arguably the safest square for the bishop, as it won't be attacked again in the near future, and also protects the g5 square, not allowing a white knight there. In addition, it allows the c6-knight to come to a5 and attack to the bishop, which is not possible in the main line with 5...Ba5. After white's automatic response of 6. d4, Black responds with 6...Na5, which drives the bishop away from the powerful diagonal.

5...Ba5 is the main line. This keeps the bishop on the a5-e1 diagonal, and therefore pins the c3 pawn when 6. d4 occurs, so that when 6...exd4 (Pierce Defence) is played, White can't simply recapture the pawn. However White gains immense attacking chances after either 7. Qb3 or 7. O-O, so Black more often plays 6...d6 (Bronstein Defence), in which he's achieved a solid position, though White still has good attacking chances.

explanations.textZh:
埃文斯策略被接受

白方以5.c3攻击主教，也支持未来的d4推进。

黑方必须对象采取行动，并且有 5 个安全方格可供象使用。

罕见的撤退

5...Bf8？！是梅耶防御。这不利于象的发展，是五步棋中最糟糕的一步，因为为了占据王翼，除了g8马之外，黑方还必须再次移动它。白棋几乎总是下6.d4来惩罚这一步棋，在这步棋中他获得了轻松的优势。

5...Bc5？！是麦克唐纳防御。这通常只有初学者才玩，认为这一步棋会停止 d4 推，但实际上并没有，然后白方可以下 6. d4，这也获得了主教的节奏。

5...Bd6！？是石器防御。虽然这会阻挡 d-pawn，但它也为 e5-pawn 添加了一个防御者，因此当 6.d4 发生时，它不会对 pawn 进行攻击。

常见静修处

5...Be7 是安徒生变体。这对于主教来说可以说是最安全的方格，因为它在不久的将来不会再次受到攻击，并且还保护了g5方格，不允许白骑士出现在那里。此外，它还允许c6骑士来到a5并攻击主教，这在5...Ba5的主线中是不可能的。白方自动回应 6.d4 后，黑方回应 6...Na5，这将象驱离强大的对角线。

5...Ba5为主线。这使主教保持在a5-e1对角线上，因此当6.d4发生时固定c3棋子，这样当玩6...exd4（皮尔斯防御）时，白方不能简单地重新夺回棋子。然而，白棋在 7.Qb3 或 7.O-O 后获得了巨大的进攻机会，因此黑棋更多地采用 6...d6（布朗斯坦防守），在其中他取得了稳固的地位，尽管白棋仍然有很好的进攻机会。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. b4/4...Bxb4/5. c3/5...Ba5
explanations.text:
5...Ba5

5...Ba5 is the main retreat after the Evans Gambit 5. c3, and it is considered the best attempt to "refute the gambit." However, it is not as safe as the retreat 5...Be7. Now, the most aggressive move for White is to play /6. d4/, when Black has four options:

6...exd4

6...d6

6...Nf6

6...b5

explanations.textZh:
5...Ba5

5...Ba5是埃文斯开局5.c3之后的主要撤退，被认为是“反驳开局”的最佳尝试。不过，它并不像撤退5...Be7那么安全。现在，白棋最激进的棋是下/6。 d4/，当黑方有四种选择时：

6...exd4

6...d6

6...NF6

6...b5

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. b4/4...Bxb4/5. c3/5...Ba5/6. d4
explanations.text:
6. d4

White takes the whole center, attacking the pawn on e5 aggressively. Black can choose from four options:

/6...exd4/ is usually played.

/6...d6/ is the most solid move.

/6...b5/ is interesting.

/6...Nf6/ is a mistake.
explanations.textEn:
6. d4

White takes the whole center, attacking the pawn on e5 aggressively. Black can choose from four options:

/6...exd4/ is usually played.

/6...d6/ is the most solid move.

/6...b5/ is interesting.

/6...Nf6/ is a mistake.
explanations.textZh:
6.d4

白棋占据整个中心，积极攻击 e5 上的棋子。黑方有四种选择：

通常播放 /6...exd4/。

/6...d6/ 是最扎实的举动。

/6...b5/ 很有趣。

/6...Nf6/ 是一个错误。

explanations.text:
6...b5?!

An interesting gambit, Black sacrifices their b7 pawn to White's bishop on c4. The idea is that after 7. Bxb5, Black can play 7...Nxd4 where White's c3 pawn is pinned to the king, and unlike 6...Nxd4?, Nxe5 wouldn't be possible as the bishop on b5 is also attacked.
explanations.textEn:
6...b5?!

An interesting gambit, Black sacrifices their b7 pawn to White's bishop on c4. The idea is that after 7. Bxb5, Black can play 7...Nxd4 where White's c3 pawn is pinned to the king, and unlike 6...Nxd4?, Nxe5 wouldn't be possible as the bishop on b5 is also attacked.
explanations.textZh:
6...b5？！

这是一个有趣的策略，黑方将其 b7 棋子牺牲给白方 c4 上的主教。这个想法是，在 7.Bxb5 之后，黑方可以下 7...Nxd4，其中白方的 c3 棋子被固定在王上，并且与 6...Nxd4？不同，Nxe5 是不可能的，因为 b5 上的主教也受到攻击。

explanations.text:
6...Nf6?

Black counterattacks the e4 pawn with their knight, but this is not good. White should play /7. dxe5/ to exploit Black's mistake and set a trap.
explanations.textEn:
6...Nf6?

Black counterattacks the e4 pawn with their knight, but this is not good. White should play /7. dxe5/ to exploit Black's mistake and set a trap.
explanations.textZh:
6...NF6？

黑方用马反击 e4 兵，但这并不好。白棋应该下/7。 dxe5/ 利用黑方的错误设置陷阱。

explanations.text:
7. dxe5!

White exploits Black's mistake by taking the free pawn on e5. This also sets a trap. The most commonly played move is /7...Nxe4/, but that loses the knight to 8. Qd5!. Black should play /7...Ng4/ instead, but Black's position is still inferior.
explanations.textEn:
7. dxe5!

White exploits Black's mistake by taking the free pawn on e5. This also sets a trap. The most commonly played move is /7...Nxe4/, but that loses the knight to 8. Qd5!. Black should play /7...Ng4/ instead, but Black's position is still inferior.
explanations.textZh:
7.DXE5！

白棋利用黑棋的错误，获得了 e5 上的自由棋子。这也设置了一个陷阱。最常用的着法是 /7...Nxe4/，但这会让马输给 8.Qd5!。黑棋应该下/7...Ng4/，但黑棋的位置仍然较差。

explanations.text:
8. Qd5!

White will win Black's knight on e4 as both it and mate on f7 is threatened (for example 8...Nxc3?? 9. Qxf7#). After Black plays 8...O-O or 8...Qe7, White will take the knight on e4.
explanations.textEn:
8. Qd5!

White will win Black's knight on e4 as both it and mate on f7 is threatened (for example 8...Nxc3?? 9. Qxf7#). After Black plays 8...O-O or 8...Qe7, White will take the knight on e4.
explanations.textZh:
8.Qd5！

白棋将在 e4 上赢得黑棋的马，因为它和 f7 上的伙伴都受到威胁（例如 8...Nxc3?? 9. Qxf7#）。黑方下 8...O-O 或 8...Qe7 后，白方将在 e4 上拿下马。

explanations.text:
8. Bg5

White attacks Black's queen. The only good way to block the attack without losing material is /8...f6/. Although 8...Ne7? does not lose material, it unnecessarily cramps Black's position.
explanations.textEn:
8. Bg5

White attacks Black's queen. The only good way to block the attack without losing material is /8...f6/. Although 8...Ne7? does not lose material, it unnecessarily cramps Black's position.
explanations.textZh:
8. 背景5

白棋攻击黑棋后。阻止攻击而不损失材料的唯一好方法是 /8...f6/。虽然8...Ne7？不会损失材料，但会不必要地限制黑棋的位置。

explanations.text:
10. Bh4

White retreats their g5 bishop to h4. White is simply better as Black's kingside pawn structure is ruined and Black's king is weak while material is equal. This is why 6...Nf6? is a mistake.
explanations.textEn:
10. Bh4

White retreats their g5 bishop to h4. White is simply better as Black's kingside pawn structure is ruined and Black's king is weak while material is equal. This is why 6...Nf6? is a mistake.
explanations.textZh:
10.Bh4

白棋将他们的 g5 主教撤退到 h4。白方只是更好，因为黑方的王侧兵结构已被破坏，而黑方的国王在材料相同的情况下很弱。这就是为什么 6...Nf6？是一个错误。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. b4/4...Bxb4/5. c3/5...Bc5
explanations.text:
5...Bc5

Black retreats their bishop to c5. This move is usually played by beginners, who believe this stops d4 when it does not. White should play /6. d4/, gaining tempo on the bishop and contesting Black's center.
explanations.textEn:
5...Bc5

explanations.textZh:
5...Bc5

黑方将其象撤退至 c5。这个动作通常由初学者玩，他们相信这会阻止 d4，但事实并非如此。白棋应该下/6。 d4/，加快主教的节奏并争夺黑方的中锋。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. b4/4...Bxb4/5. c3/5...Bd6
explanations.text:
5...Bd6

Black retreats their bishop to d6, defending the e5 pawn so d4 doesn't come with an attack on the pawn, but at the cost of blocking the d7 pawn. White usually plays /6. d4/ taking the center.
explanations.textEn:
5...Bd6

Black retreats their bishop to d6, defending the e5 pawn so d4 doesn't come with an attack on the pawn, but at the cost of blocking the d7 pawn. White usually plays /6. d4/ taking the center.
explanations.textZh:
5...Bd6

黑方将象撤退到 d6，保护 e5 棋子，因此 d4 不会对棋子进行攻击，但代价是阻挡 d7 棋子。白方通常下/6。 d4/ 取中心。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. b4/4...Bb6
explanations.text:
Evans Gambit Declined

4... Bb6

Black declines the gambit by playing 4... Bb6. Black refuses to give White the opportunity to gain tempo and hangs onto the center. However, White can play /5. a4/ with plans to play 6. a5 later on to trap the bishop. White can also try attacking the c6 knight with /5. b5/, but it is not as accurate.
explanations.textEn:
Evans Gambit Declined

4... Bb6

Black declines the gambit by playing 4... Bb6. Black refuses to give White the opportunity to gain tempo and hangs onto the center. However, White can play /5. a4/ with plans to play 6. a5 later on to trap the bishop. White can also try attacking the c6 knight with /5. b5/, but it is not as accurate.
explanations.textZh:
埃文斯甘比特拒绝

4...Bb6

黑棋拒绝了这一策略，下了 4...Bb6。黑方拒绝给白方获得节奏的机会，并坚守在中心位置。然而，白棋可以下/5。 a4/ 计划稍后打 6.a5 来困住主教。白棋也可以尝试用/5攻击c6马。 b5/，但不太准确。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. b4/4...Bb6/5. b5
explanations.text:
Evans Gambit Declined

5. b5

White pushes their b-pawn forward to attack the black knight on c6, aiming to win the black pawn on e5. This is not as accurate as 5. a4, as Black has /5...Na5/, saving the knight and counterattacking the white bishop on c4. Black may also try to be tricky with /5...Nd4/, encouraging 6. Nxe5??, although 6. Nxd4 would be better.
explanations.textEn:
Evans Gambit Declined

5. b5

White pushes their b-pawn forward to attack the black knight on c6, aiming to win the black pawn on e5. This is not as accurate as 5. a4, as Black has /5...Na5/, saving the knight and counterattacking the white bishop on c4. Black may also try to be tricky with /5...Nd4/, encouraging 6. Nxe5??, although 6. Nxd4 would be better.
explanations.textZh:
埃文斯甘比特拒绝

5.b5

白棋将b兵向前推进，攻击c6上的黑棋，旨在赢得e5上的黑棋。这不像5.a4那么准确，因为黑棋有/5...Na5/，拯救了马并在c4上反击了白棋主教。黑棋也可能尝试用/5...Nd4/进行狡猾，鼓励6.Nxe5??，尽管6.Nxd4会更好。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. b4/4...Bb6/5. b5/5...Na5
explanations.text:
Evans Gambit Declined

5...Na5

Black saves their knight while attacking white's bishop on c4. White's idea with 5. b5 was to lure away the knight from the defence of the e-pawn, so White will often play /6. Nxe5/, taking the free pawn, defending the bishop and attacking f7.
explanations.textEn:
Evans Gambit Declined

5...Na5

Black saves their knight while attacking white's bishop on c4. White's idea with 5. b5 was to lure away the knight from the defence of the e-pawn, so White will often play /6. Nxe5/, taking the free pawn, defending the bishop and attacking f7.
explanations.textZh:
埃文斯甘比特拒绝

5...Na5

黑棋在 c4 上攻击白棋的主教时拯救了他们的马。白方5.b5的想法是引诱马脱离e兵的防守，因此白方经常会下/6。 Nxe5/，拿走自由兵，防守主教，攻击f7。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. b4/4...Bb6/5. b5/5...Na5/6. Nxe5
explanations.text:
Evans Gambit Declined

6. Nxe5

White takes the undefended pawn on e5 while also defending their attacked bishop and threatening Nxf7, which would win Black's rook to a fork. It is true Black could trade with 6...Nxc4, but after the recapture 7. Nxc4, White is a clean pawn up. So Black has two real options: /6...Nh6/, the Lange Variation, defending f7, and /6...Qg5/, the Hirschbach Variation, going on a counterattack instead.
explanations.textEn:
Evans Gambit Declined

6. Nxe5

White takes the undefended pawn on e5 while also defending their attacked bishop and threatening Nxf7, which would win Black's rook to a fork. It is true Black could trade with 6...Nxc4, but after the recapture 7. Nxc4, White is a clean pawn up. So Black has two real options: /6...Nh6/, the Lange Variation, defending f7, and /6...Qg5/, the Hirschbach Variation, going on a counterattack instead.
explanations.textZh:
埃文斯甘比特拒绝

6.NXE5

白棋在 e5 上拿下不设防的棋子，同时也保卫了被攻击的象并威胁 Nxf7，这将赢得黑棋的车到叉子。黑方确实可以用 6...Nxc4 进行交易，但在夺回 7.Nxc4 后，白方就成为了干净的棋子。所以黑方有两个实际选择：/6...Nh6/，兰格变例，防守f7，和/6...Qg5/，赫希巴赫变例，进行反击。

explanations.text:
Evans Gambit Declined: Hirschbach Variation

6...Qg5

Black ignores the threat on f7 and instead counterattacks the knight on e5 and the pawn on g2. White can fork the queen and rook with /7. Nxf7/, but runs into complications after 7...Qxg2!. /7. d4/ saves the knight but doesn't save g2. Instead, the best move for White is /7. Bxf7/+.
explanations.textEn:
Evans Gambit Declined: Hirschbach Variation

6...Qg5

Black ignores the threat on f7 and instead counterattacks the knight on e5 and the pawn on g2. White can fork the queen and rook with /7. Nxf7/, but runs into complications after 7...Qxg2!. /7. d4/ saves the knight but doesn't save g2. Instead, the best move for White is /7. Bxf7/+.
explanations.textZh:
埃文斯弃兵：赫施巴赫变例

6...Qg5

黑方无视f7上的威胁，转而反击e5上的马和g2上的兵。白棋可以用/7 来分叉后和车。 Nxf7/，但在 7...Qxg2! 之后遇到麻烦。 /7。 d4/ 拯救了骑士，但没有拯救 g2。相反，白棋的最佳棋步是/7。 Bxf7/+。

explanations.text:
Evans Gambit Declined: Hirschbach Variation

7. Nxf7?!

White believes they are winning material with a fork on the queen on g5 and the rook on h8, but Black surprises White with 7...Qxg2!.
explanations.textEn:
Evans Gambit Declined: Hirschbach Variation

7. Nxf7?!

White believes they are winning material with a fork on the queen on g5 and the rook on h8, but Black surprises White with 7...Qxg2!.
explanations.textZh:
埃文斯弃兵：赫施巴赫变例

7.Nxf7？！

白方认为他们在 g5 上用叉子叉住后，在 h8 上用叉子赢得了胜利，但黑方以 7...Qxg2! 令白方大吃一惊。

explanations.text:
Evans Gambit Declined: Hirschbach Variation

7...Qxg2!

Black's queen captures the pawn on g2 and attacks the white rook on h1. White will want to save their rook, so they will almost always play /8. Rf1/ (8. Ke2?? allows the queen on d1 to defend the rook but after 8...Qxe4+! White's king is forced to f1 where the queen can no longer see the rook)
explanations.textEn:
Evans Gambit Declined: Hirschbach Variation

7...Qxg2!

Black's queen captures the pawn on g2 and attacks the white rook on h1. White will want to save their rook, so they will almost always play /8. Rf1/ (8. Ke2?? allows the queen on d1 to defend the rook but after 8...Qxe4+! White's king is forced to f1 where the queen can no longer see the rook)
explanations.textZh:
埃文斯弃兵：赫施巴赫变例

7...Qxg2！

黑方后在 g2 上吃掉棋子并在 h1 上攻击白车。白棋会想要拯救他们的车，所以他们几乎总是会下/8。 Rf1/（8.Ke2??允许d1上的皇后防守车，但在8...Qxe4+之后！白棋的国王被迫f1，皇后再也看不到车）

explanations.text:
Evans Gambit Declined: Lange Variation

6...Nh6

Black defends f7 with their knight and potentially preparing to castle. Most often in amateur play White plays /7. d4/, threatening to remove the defender of f7 with Bxh6, however according to Stockfish, /7. Be2/ is the best move.
explanations.textEn:
Evans Gambit Declined: Lange Variation

6...Nh6

Black defends f7 with their knight and potentially preparing to castle. Most often in amateur play White plays /7. d4/, threatening to remove the defender of f7 with Bxh6, however according to Stockfish, /7. Be2/ is the best move.
explanations.textZh:
埃文斯弃兵：兰格变例

6...NH6

黑方用马防守 f7，并可能准备攻城略地。在业余比赛中，白棋最常下/7。 d4/，威胁用 Bxh6 移除 f7 的防守者，然而根据 Stockfish, /7 的说法。 Be2/ 是最好的举动。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. b4/4...d5
explanations.text:
Evans Gambit: Hein Countergambit

4...d5

This very fun counterattacking option against the Evans Gambit is called the Hein Countergambit. Here black attacks both the Bc4 and the pawn e4. White has a couple of moves:

5. exd5

5. bxc5

5. Bxd5

5. c3!?

5. Bb3!?

5.exd5 removes the attacker of the c4 bishop, and counterattacks the knight. Black has two pieces hanging in the middle of the board - however, black can escape with 5...Nxb4, saving the knight and remove the attacker of the C5 bishop. 5. bxc5 opts for a bishop trade, but after the trade, the c4 and C5 pawns are both double and weak, and can be attacked easily. 5. Bxd5 captures a pawn - however black can also capture a pawn like with 5...Bxb4 and material is even. 5. c3!? is a dubious choice against the Hein Countergambit as it doesn't deal with most threats, however it defends the pawn B4 that could have been captured by the Bc5. 5. Bb3!? is another dubious choice against the Hein Countergambit that retreats the bishop to a safe square but it leaves a pawn hanging, but material is eventually equal (5...Bxb4 6. exd5 (6...Qxd5?? is not possible due to 7. Bxd5) or 5...dxe4 6. bxc5 exf3 7. Qxf3).

explanations.textZh:
埃文斯开局：海因反开局

4...d5

这种针对埃文斯开局的非常有趣的反击选项被称为海因反开局。这里黑棋同时攻击 Bc4 和棋子 e4。白棋有几个动作：

5.exd5

5.bxc5

5.Bxd5

5.c3！？

5. BB3！？

5.exd5去除c4主教的攻击者，并反击骑士。黑方有两颗棋子悬在棋盘中央——然而，黑方可以用 5...Nxb4 逃脱，拯救马并消灭 C5 象的攻击者。 5. bxc5选择主教交易，但交易后，c4和C5兵都是双弱的，很容易被攻击。 5. Bxd5 吃掉一个棋子 - 然而黑色也可以像 5...Bxb4 一样吃掉一个棋子并且材质是均匀的。 5.c3！？对于 Hein Countergambit 来说，这是一个可疑的选择，因为它不能处理大多数威胁，但它可以保护可能被 Bc5 捕获的棋子 B4。 5. BB3！？是针对 Hein Countergambit 的另一个可疑选择，它将主教撤退到安全方格，但留下了一个棋子悬而未决，但材料最终是相等的（5...Bxb4 6. exd5 (6...Qxd5?? 是不可能的，因为 7. Bxd5) 或 5...dxe4 6. bxc5 exf3 7. Qxf3）。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. c3
explanations.text:
Giuoco Piano

4. c3

White reinforces the d4 square, and prepares d4 in order to establish two pawns in the centre. It also stops any Nd4 by black, in the future.

White also prepares b4 to try and trap the Black bishop. White's secondary aim is to bring the queen to b3, thus intensifying the pressure on Black's f7-pawn.

A drawback to this move is that the pawn occupies a square that should be reserved for the queen's knight.
explanations.textEn:
Giuoco Piano

4. c3

White reinforces the d4 square, and prepares d4 in order to establish two pawns in the centre. It also stops any Nd4 by black, in the future.

White also prepares b4 to try and trap the Black bishop. White's secondary aim is to bring the queen to b3, thus intensifying the pressure on Black's f7-pawn.

A drawback to this move is that the pawn occupies a square that should be reserved for the queen's knight.
explanations.textZh:
乔科钢琴

4.c3

白方加固 d4 方格，并准备 d4 以便在中心建立两个棋子。将来它还会阻止任何 Nd4 变成黑色。

白方还准备了b4来尝试困住黑方主教。白方的次要目标是将后带到b3，从而加大对黑方f7兵的压力。

这一举动的一个缺点是，棋子占据了一个应该为后的马保留的方格。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. c3/4...Nf6/5. d3
explanations.text:
Giuoco Piano: Giuoco Pianissimo Variation

This is the most popular variation. White opens up the bishop and defends e4. Often the light-squared bishop will move to b3, the knight on b1 to d2, the dark-squared bishop to e3 or g5, and kingside castling. Sometimes a4 and b4 thrusts occur as well.

The most popular continuation, 5...d6, is a common move in the Giuoco Piano, with similar reasons as white's 5. d3. The light-squared bishop often comes to e6 or g4, the dark-squared bishop either stays on c5 or sometimes goes to b6 or a7, and Black castles kingside. If Black attempts h6 and g5, she usually castles queenside. Often a6 is played.

5...a6 is also similar and often transposes to main lines of the Pianissimo. The same goes for 5...O-O and 5...h6.
explanations.textEn:
Giuoco Piano: Giuoco Pianissimo Variation

This is the most popular variation. White opens up the bishop and defends e4. Often the light-squared bishop will move to b3, the knight on b1 to d2, the dark-squared bishop to e3 or g5, and kingside castling. Sometimes a4 and b4 thrusts occur as well.

The most popular continuation, 5...d6, is a common move in the Giuoco Piano, with similar reasons as white's 5. d3. The light-squared bishop often comes to e6 or g4, the dark-squared bishop either stays on c5 or sometimes goes to b6 or a7, and Black castles kingside. If Black attempts h6 and g5, she usually castles queenside. Often a6 is played.

5...a6 is also similar and often transposes to main lines of the Pianissimo. The same goes for 5...O-O and 5...h6.
explanations.textZh:
乔科钢琴：乔科最弱变奏曲

这是最流行的变体。白方打开主教并防守 e4。通常，浅方象会移至 b3，马从 b1 移至 d2，暗方象移至 e3 或 g5，王翼易位。有时也会出现a4 和b4 推力。

最流行的延续 5...d6 是 Giuoco 钢琴中常见的走法，其原因与白棋的 5.d3 类似。浅方象经常来到e6或g4，暗方象要么留在c5，要么有时去b6或a7，黑方城堡王侧。如果黑方尝试 h6 和 g5，她通常会在后侧筑垒。经常演奏a6。

5...a6 也类似，并且经常移调至最弱的主线。 5...O-O 和 5...h6 也是如此。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. c3/4...Nf6/5. d4
explanations.text:
Center Attack

5. d4

White attacks the center with 5. d4, attempting to create a strong pawn center with the d4 and e4 pawns. Black has to respond with exd4, or else surrender the entire center to White.
explanations.textEn:
Center Attack

5. d4

White attacks the center with 5. d4, attempting to create a strong pawn center with the d4 and e4 pawns. Black has to respond with exd4, or else surrender the entire center to White.
explanations.textZh:
中锋进攻

5.d4

白方用 5. d4 攻击中心，试图用 d4 和 e4 棋子创建一个强大的棋子中心。黑方必须用 exd4 回应，否则将整个中心拱手让给白方。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. c3/4...Nf6/5. d4/5...exd4
explanations.text:
Center Attack

5...exd4

Black takes the d4 pawn with the e5 pawn. White will respond by either pushing the e4 pawn forward to e5 attacking the Black knight, or recapturing the pawn with 6. cxd4, or by playing 6. b4!?.
explanations.textEn:
Center Attack

5...exd4

Black takes the d4 pawn with the e5 pawn. White will respond by either pushing the e4 pawn forward to e5 attacking the Black knight, or recapturing the pawn with 6. cxd4, or by playing 6. b4!?.
explanations.textZh:
中锋进攻

5...exd4

黑方拿下 d4 棋子和 e5 棋子。白方将通过将 e4 棋子向前推到 e5 来攻击黑骑士，或者用 6.cxd4 重新捕获棋子，或者通过下 6.b4!? 来做出反应。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. c3/4...Nf6/5. d4/5...exd4/6. b4
explanations.text:
Dubov Gambit

6. b4

White sacrifices the d4 pawn for quick development and an open d file. White also attacks the Black bishop on c5, forcing it to move. Black can play either 6...Bb6 or 6...Be7.

In contrast to the Evans gambit, White doesn't sacrifice the b pawn. Because of this White has the threat of b5, forcing the knight to move to a5 or e7.

The Dubov gambit is named after the Russian GM Daniil Dubov, who used it to great success against Russian GM Sergey Karjakin in 2020 at the Russian Championship in Moscow. Before GM Daniil Dubov popularised 6. b4, it was used very rarely in high level chess except for a 9 year old Dutch NM that used it to defeat Anish Giri in 2009 and Levon Aronian in 2008 but lost to GM Gukesh in 2009. Recently, the Dubov gambit has been used in online games by very strong players including GM Hikaru Nakamura, former world chess champion Ding Liren and GM Daniil Dubov himself.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. c3/4...Nf6/5. d4/5...exd4/6. cxd4/6...Bb4
explanations.text:
Center Attack

6...Bb4+

The bishop must move, and it did. This is actually the only not losing move. White has a couple options here.

7. Bd2 is a natural blocking move. Black can either trade and break the center with 8...d5, or immediately take with 7...Nxe4 which leads to complicated variations and the sacrifice of 8. Bxf7+!

7. Nc3 is a main line that sacrifices the e4 pawn. This is the Greco Gambit, where White then castles and gambits the pawn for development.

7. Nbd2 also exists. It was once very rare but has recently increased in popularity.

7. Kf1, also known as the Cracow Variation, is not usually played, as White can no longer castle and hangs the e4 pawn. For the pawn, White gains initiative and attacks Black who has to find only moves to keep advantage.

6...Bb4+

7. Bd2是一个自然的阻挡动作。黑棋可以交易并用 8...d5 打破中心，或者立即用 7...Nxe4 拿下，这会导致复杂的变化并牺牲 8.Bxf7+！

7. Nc3是牺牲e4棋子的主线。这就是希腊式开局，白方随后将棋子围成城堡并开局以求发展。

7. Nbd2也存在。它曾经非常罕见，但最近越来越受欢迎。

7. Kf1，也称为克拉科夫变例，通常不被使用，因为白方无法再城堡并挂起 e4 兵。对于棋子，白方获得主动权并攻击黑方，黑方必须找到唯一的走法来保持优势。

explanations.text:
Greco’s Gambit

White castles her king. This unpins her knight to her king, causing the black knight on e4 to be hanging. Due to the open e-file creating complications should black retreat her knight, black generally exchanges on c3. While …Nxc3 is appealing to keep the bishop pair, it enters the rabbit hole.

Therefore, Black should play …Bxc3, where after exchanging, there is no hanging piece, giving her time to play …d5

explanations.textZh:
格列柯的策略

白城堡她的国王。这会将她的骑士与她的国王解除固定，导致 e4 上的黑骑士被挂起。由于打开的电子文件会导致黑棋撤退时的情况变得复杂，黑棋通常在c3上进行交换。当…Nxc3 呼吁保留主教对时，它进入了兔子洞。

因此，黑棋应该下…Bxc3，交换后没有挂子，给她时间下…d5

explanations.text:
7. Kf1!? · Cracow Variation

This is a weird-looking move that seemingly doesn't make any sense. White can no longer castle and the e4 pawn is undefended. But the compensation exists. White has got a massive center while Black has none, and White are more prepared to attack than Black. The Cracow Variation a tricky opening, Black has to find the only moves to not to get a bad position. Black has several options:

7...Nxe4. Black has grabbed an actually free pawn. White can strike in the center with 8. d5!, kicking the knight back. After 8...Ne7 White has 9. Qd4, grabbing even more space, or a tricky 9. Bb3 with a threat of 10. Qd4 which is somewhy often unseen.

7...d5!. This is the strongest for Black option. After 8. exd5 Nxd5 9. Nc3 Black has to be careful to not to take the knight with their own knight. There is no reason to trade off a central knight. None. Instead, they should take the knight with the bishop, like in the Greco Gambit.

7...O-O?. After 8. d5! Black has giant problems with space and activity. In case of 8...Ne7 or 8...Nb8 White will go 9. e5!, completely paralysing Black, in case of 8. Na5 there is 9. Bd3 with an unstoppable 10. a3 and 11. b4.

7...d6??. This is a blunder. After 8. d5! Ne7 or 8...Na5 there is 9. Qa4+, winning the bishop on b4.

explanations.textZh:
7.Kf1！？ · 克拉科夫变例

这是一个看似奇怪的举动，似乎没有任何意义。白棋不再能占据城堡，e4 棋子处于不设防状态。但补偿是存在的。白棋有一个巨大的中锋，而黑棋没有，而且白棋比黑棋更有准备进攻。克拉科夫变例是一个棘手的开局，黑方必须找到唯一的走法，以免陷入不利局面。黑方有多种选择：

7...Nxe4。黑方抓住了一颗实际上是空闲的棋子。白棋可以用 8.d5! 攻击中心，将马踢回去。 8 之后...Ne7 白棋有 9. Qd4，抢占更多空间，或者是棘手的 9. Bb3，具有 10. Qd4 的威胁，但不知何故经常看不见。

7...d5！。这是黑方最强的选择。 8. exd5 Nxd5 9. Nc3 后，黑方必须小心，不要将马与自己的马一起拿走。没有理由去交易中央骑士。没有任何。相反，他们应该选择骑士和主教，就像希腊开局一样。

7...O-O？。 8.d5之后！黑色在空间和活动方面存在巨大问题。如果是 8...Ne7 或 8...Nb8 白棋将走 9. e5!，完全瘫痪黑棋，如果是 8. Na5，则有 9. Bd3 以及不可阻挡的 10. a3 和 11. b4。

7...d6??。这是一个错误。 8.d5之后！ Ne7或8...Na5有9.Qa4+，赢得b4上的主教。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. Bxf7
explanations.text:
4. Bxf7+?? · Jerome gambit

4. Bxf7+?? is the unhinged Jerome gambit. Though a Bxf7+ sacrifice works in many lines in the Italian, this is far too early and it is objectively woeful for White. However, it is sharp enough that White has some success at the club level.

The idea is 4...Kxf7 5. Nxe5+ Nxe5 6. Qh5+, and White hopes that between Black's exposed king and the skewering of Black's pieces on the fifth rank they will swindle compensation. e.g. 6. Qh5+ g6 7. Qxe5 d6?? (better is Qe7) 8. Qxh8.

After 4...Kxf7 5. Nxe5+ Nxe5 6. Qh5+ there are several winning approaches for Black. The engine line involves marching their king out to into the middle of the board to guard the bishop: 6...Ke6 7. Qf5+ Kd6 8. f4 Kc6 9. Qxe5 Nf6 etc, and despite the weakness of their enemy's king, White's queen alone can't sustain an attack.

The simplest approach is to just return the bishop, 6...Ng6 7. Qxc6. White has only captured two pawns in exchange for their knight, and the only piece they have developed is their queen. Black can come out swinging.

History

So named for Alonzo Wheeler Jerome, who wheeled it out against William Shinkman in 1874. Joseph Blackburne referred to it as the "Kentucky opening".

explanations.textZh:
4.Bxf7+?? · 杰罗姆·甘比特

4.Bxf7+??这是杰罗姆的疯狂策略。尽管 Bxf7+ 牺牲在意大利语中的许多行中都起作用，但这还为时过早，客观上对白棋来说是可悲的。然而，它足够敏锐，使得怀特在俱乐部层面取得了一些成功。

这个想法是 4...Kxf7 5. Nxe5+ Nxe5 6. Qh5+，白方希望通过黑方暴露的王和黑方第五级棋子的串连来骗取补偿。例如6.Qh5+g6 7.Qxe5d6?? （更好的是Qe7） 8. Qxh8。

4...Kxf7 5. Nxe5+ Nxe5 6. Qh5+ 之后，黑棋有几种获胜方法。引擎线包括将他们的国王推进到棋盘中间以保护主教：6...Ke6 7. Qf5+ Kd6 8. f4 Kc6 9. Qxe5 Nf6 等，尽管敌人的国王很弱，但白棋的皇后无法独自承受攻击。

最简单的方法是只返回主教，6...Ng6 7. Qxc6。白棋只吃掉了两个棋子来换取他们的马，而他们唯一发展的棋子就是他们的皇后。黑色可​​以摇摆出来。

历史

因阿朗佐·惠勒·杰罗姆 (Alonzo Wheeler Jerome) 的名字而得名，他于 1874 年对阵威廉·欣克曼 (William Shinkman)。约瑟夫·布莱克本 (Joseph Blackburne) 将其称为“肯塔基州开局”。

4...Kxf7!

Black has a clear advantage. White will attempt to mate the black king with a series of checks, but with proper play black will come out ahead. His bishop pair and lead in development make it impossible to find enough compensation.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. Bxf7/4...Kxf7/5. Nxe5
explanations.text:
5. Nxe5+

This move sacrifices another piece, but White will soon get it back with d4 or Qh5+. They will have gotten a second pawn for the piece, but would have lost the bishop pair and their own king would not be able to get out of the center. Therefore, the compensation is not nearly enough and Black is close to winning. Do not sacrifice unless you see reason. Here, White didn't have enough development to attack the king successfully.

5.NXE5+

这步棋牺牲了另一子，但白方很快就会用 d4 或 Qh5+ 收回它。他们将获得该棋子的第二个棋子，但会失去主教对，并且他们自己的国王将无法离开中心。因此，补偿还远远不够，黑方已接近获胜。除非你明白原因，否则不要牺牲。在这里，白方没有足够的发展来成功攻击国王。

explanations.text:
Nxe5

This is the obvious response. It seems that black has won 2 pieces, but white will regain one. He will then be a piece down for two pawns with no compensation, however.

Since Black has many replies after 6.d4, all of which retain a winning position, the most popular move is 6.Qh5+.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. Bxf7/4...Kxf7/5. Nxe5/5...Nxe5/6. Qh5
explanations.text:
6.Qh5+

After this, Black has various good replies. 6...g6 and 6...Kf8 are enough to win, but the greedy and probably best 6...Ke6!? shows the unsoundness of White's attack. He simply is not developed enough despite the centralized Black king. He will just be down a piece for a pawn. Lines to avoid are: 6... Kf6?? 7.Qf5+ followed by Qxe5+ and Qxc5 with 2 extra pawns for White, or 6... Ke7?? 7.Qxe5+ with Qxc5 coming next, once again with two extra pawns for White.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. d3
explanations.text:
Giuoco Pianissimo

With 4.d3, White plays the Giuoco Pianissimo (Italian: "very quiet game"). White aims for a slow buildup deferring d4 until it can be prepared. By avoiding an immediate confrontation in the center White prevents the early release of tension through exchanges and enters a positional maneuvering game. If White plays c2-c3, the position can take some characteristics of the Ruy Lopez if his bishop retreats to c2 via Bc4-b3-c2. (The alternative move order 4.c3 Nf6 5.d3 is common in master play.) Despite its drawish reputation, this variation became more popular after being taken up by Anatoly Karpov in the 1978 World Championship. Black may also play the rare /4...f5/ to gambit a pawn and create a more combative game.

乔科·皮尼西莫

在 4.d3 中，怀特演奏 Giuoco Pianissimo（意大利语：“非常安静的游戏”）。白棋的目标是缓慢积累，推迟 d4 直到可以准备好为止。通过避免中间的直接对抗，白方可以防止通过交换而过早释放紧张局势，并进入阵地机动游戏。如果白方下c2-c3，如果他的主教通过Bc4-b3-c2撤退到c2，该位置可以采用Ruy Lopez的一些特征。 （另类走法 4.c3 Nf6 5.d3 在高手对弈中很常见。）尽管这种走法名声不佳，但在 1978 年世界锦标赛上被阿纳托利·卡尔波夫采用后，这种变体变得更受欢迎。黑棋也可以使用罕见的/4...f5/来下棋并创造一个更具战斗性的游戏。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. d3/4...f5
explanations.text:
4...f5 · Lucchini Gambit

With 4...f5!?, Black unleashes the Lucchini Gambit—an aggressive response to the Giuoco Pianissimo that breaks the symmetry and transforms a quiet line into a tactical battlefield. Named after Italian player Marco Lucchini, this gambit challenges White’s center and seeks rapid development at the cost of material.

After 5. exf5 d5, Black aims to blow open the center while White is still underdeveloped. If 6. Bb5 Ne7!, Black keeps the kingside flexible while preparing Bxf5 or even queenside castling in sharper lines. Even if White declines the pawn with 5. Nc3 or 5. O-O, Black can still build strong initiative with Nf6, d6, and Qe7.

Even sharper is 5. Ng5!?, where the game can explode into tactics. In these lines, Black may sacrifice pieces for open lines and an all-out assault, echoing ideas from the King's Gambit and the Traxler Counterattack.

Though not fully sound, the Lucchini is dangerous and practical—especially against opponents who expect a slow positional game and instead find themselves fighting off a storm.

explanations.textZh:
4...f5 · 卢基尼策略

通过 4...f5!?，黑方释放了卢基尼弃兵——这是对 Giuoco Pianissimo 的激进回应，打破了对称性，将一条安静的战线转变为战术战场。这一策略以意大利球员马可·卢基尼的名字命名，挑战怀特的中锋，以牺牲材料为代价寻求快速发展。

5. exf5 d5之后，黑棋的目标是炸开中心，而白棋仍然不发达。如果 6. Bb5 Ne7!，黑方保持王翼灵活，同时准备 Bxf5 甚至后翼易位，形成更锐利的路线。即使白棋用 5.Nc3 或 5.O-O 拒绝棋子，黑棋仍然可以利用 Nf6、d6 和 Qe7 建立强大的主动权。

更犀利的是 5.NG5!?，游戏可以爆发出战术。在这些路线中，黑棋可能会为了开放路线和全面进攻而牺牲棋子，这与国王弃兵和特拉克斯勒反击的想法相呼应。

虽然卢基尼并不完全健全，但它既危险又实用——尤其是面对那些期待缓慢的阵地比赛却发现自己正在对抗风暴的对手。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. d3/4...f5/5. Ng5
explanations.text:
5. Ng5 · Lucchini Gambit

White chooses the aggressive 5. Ng5, eyeing an early attack on f7. This sharpens the game considerably and signals a tactical battle. Black must now decide how to respond to the dual threats of Nf7, forking the queen and rook, as well as Qh5+. If White is able to bring their queen, knight and bishop towards Black's weakened kingside, they'll be in trouble.

However, Black has 5...f4!, cutting off White's dark-squared bishop and threatening Qxg5, effectively inviting White to attack their f7 square.
explanations.textEn:
5. Ng5 · Lucchini Gambit

Black must now decide how to respond to the dual threats of Nf7, forking the queen and rook, as well as Qh5+. If White is able to bring their queen, knight and bishop towards Black's weakened kingside, they'll be in trouble.

However, Black has 5...f4!, cutting off White's dark-squared bishop and threatening Qxg5, effectively inviting White to attack their f7 square.
explanations.textZh:
5.NG5·卢基尼策略

白棋选择了激进的 5.NG5，着眼于对 f7 进行早期攻击。这大大提高了游戏的清晰度，标志着一场战术战斗。黑方现在必须决定如何应对 Nf7 的双重威胁，分叉后和车，以及 Qh5+。如果白方能够将他们的后、马和主教带到黑方被削弱的王翼，他们就会遇到麻烦。

然而，黑方有 5...f4!，切断了白方的暗方象并威胁 Qxg5，有效地邀请白方攻击他们的 f7 方格。

explanations.text:
5...f4 · Lucchini Gambit: Dubois Variation

Black plays 5...f4!, the critical move of the Dubois Variation (named after Serafino Dubois, an 1850s Italian master). Here Black threatens Qxg5. Most often, White will continue to fork Black's queen and rook with 6. Nf7. Otherwise, they will force Black's king to move with 6. Bf7+?, a mistake. White's strongest move here is actually h4! to reinforce their knight and stop Black's queen from moving outwards.
explanations.textEn:
5...f4 · Lucchini Gambit: Dubois Variation

Black plays 5...f4!, the critical move of the Dubois Variation (named after Serafino Dubois, an 1850s Italian master). Here Black threatens Qxg5. Most often, White will continue to fork Black's queen and rook with 6. Nf7. Otherwise, they will force Black's king to move with 6. Bf7+?, a mistake. White's strongest move here is actually h4! to reinforce their knight and stop Black's queen from moving outwards.
explanations.textZh:
5...f4 · 卢基尼开局：杜波依斯变例

黑棋走 5...f4!，这是杜波依斯变例的关键一步（以 1850 年代意大利大师塞拉菲诺·杜波依斯的名字命名）。这里黑棋威胁Qxg5。大多数情况下，白棋会继续用 6. Nf7 分叉黑棋的后和车。否则，他们将迫使黑方王下 6. Bf7+?，这是一个错误。白棋这里最强的棋实际上是h4！来增援他们的马并阻止黑后向外移动。

explanations.text:
6. Bf7+ · Lucchini Gambit: Dubois Variation

After Black calmly sidesteps with 6...Kf8, White’s knight on g5 comes under immediate threat from ...h6, and there’s no safe retreat. For example, 7. h4 h6 8. Bxg8 hxg5 leaves Black with open lines on the kingside and a dangerous initiative down the h-file. Thus, 6. h4 or 6. Nf7 are much better options for White.
explanations.textEn:
6. Bf7+ · Lucchini Gambit: Dubois Variation

After Black calmly sidesteps with 6...Kf8, White’s knight on g5 comes under immediate threat from ...h6, and there’s no safe retreat. For example, 7. h4 h6 8. Bxg8 hxg5 leaves Black with open lines on the kingside and a dangerous initiative down the h-file. Thus, 6. h4 or 6. Nf7 are much better options for White.
explanations.textZh:
6. Bf7+·卢基尼开局：杜波依斯变例

黑方用 6...Kf8 冷静地回避后，白方 g5 的马立即受到 ...h6 的威胁，并且没有安全的撤退。例如，7. h4 h6 8. Bxg8 hxg5 使黑方在王翼留下空位，并在 h 档中形成危险的主动。因此，6.h4 或 6.Nf7 对于白方来说是更好的选择。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. d4
explanations.text:
Italian Gambit

4.d4

White sacrifices the d-pawn in order to open lines for their pieces and develop faster. The gambit is considered unsound but it's not bad. Black has 3 ways to capture the pawn:

4…exd4 transposes into Haxo Gambit (1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Bc4 Bc5).

4…Nxd4 is playable but allows White to play 5. Nxe5 with pressure on f7, or the venomous 5. b4. But, if Black knows what's he doing, this move is surprisingly strong.

4…Bxd4 is the calmest line and probably the strongest one. Play tends to continue 5. Nxd4 Nxd4 6. Be3 Nc6.
explanations.textEn:
Italian Gambit

4.d4

White sacrifices the d-pawn in order to open lines for their pieces and develop faster. The gambit is considered unsound but it's not bad. Black has 3 ways to capture the pawn:

4…exd4 transposes into Haxo Gambit (1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Bc4 Bc5).

4…Nxd4 is playable but allows White to play 5. Nxe5 with pressure on f7, or the venomous 5. b4. But, if Black knows what's he doing, this move is surprisingly strong.

4…Bxd4 is the calmest line and probably the strongest one. Play tends to continue 5. Nxd4 Nxd4 6. Be3 Nc6.
explanations.textZh:
意大利开局

4.d4

白棋牺牲了d兵，以便为他们的棋子打开线路并发展得更快。这种策略被认为是不合理的，但也不错。黑方有 3 种吃子的方法：

4…exd4 转置为 Haxo Gambit (1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. Bc4 Bc5)。

4…Nxd4 可以下，但允许白棋下 5.Nxe5，对 f7 施加压力，或者有毒的 5.b4。但是，如果黑方知道他在做什么，这一步棋就会出人意料地强大。

4…Bxd4 是最平静的路线，也可能是最强的路线。比赛倾向于继续 5. Nxd4 Nxd4 6. Be3 Nc6。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. d4/4...Bxd4
explanations.text: This capture is the best way for Black to proceed without entering the Haxo Gambit. White has nothing better to do than /5. Nxd4/ to open lines for their pieces.
explanations.textEn: This capture is the best way for Black to proceed without entering the Haxo Gambit. White has nothing better to do than /5. Nxd4/ to open lines for their pieces.
explanations.textZh: 这种吃子是黑方在不进入 Haxo 弃兵的情况下继续前进的最佳方式。白棋没有什么比/5更好的事情可做了。 Nxd4/ 为他们的作品打开行。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. d4/4...Nxd4
explanations.text:
Italian Gambit: Knight Capture

4...Nxd4

Even though this move looks very bad, because White can go 5. Nxe5 and it's unclear how to save the f7 pawn and the rook on h8, that's not like that. Yes, after 5. Nxe5 the f7 pawn would be captured in any variant, but black can go 5... Qe7! From now, there are a couple of ways the game can continue:

6. Nxf7!? - the most logical move. It doesn't just capture the pawn, but also trapped the rook in the corner. But this move is awkward because of 6... Qxe4 and after 7. Kf1 Qxc2 the rook will be regained, or a deadly 6... d5! move.

6. Bxf7+! - the best move in this position. Here Black must go 6... Kf8! Now the move 7. Bxg8 is forced because the knight on e5 is attacked. After 7... Kxg8, the knight has to go somewhere, and after 8... Qxe4 black has a better position.

Another option would be to go 5. Be3, avoiding all the stuff with 5. Nxe5. This is the most solid and best by the computer move.
explanations.textEn:
Italian Gambit: Knight Capture

4...Nxd4

Even though this move looks very bad, because White can go 5. Nxe5 and it's unclear how to save the f7 pawn and the rook on h8, that's not like that. Yes, after 5. Nxe5 the f7 pawn would be captured in any variant, but black can go 5... Qe7! From now, there are a couple of ways the game can continue:

6. Nxf7!? - the most logical move. It doesn't just capture the pawn, but also trapped the rook in the corner. But this move is awkward because of 6... Qxe4 and after 7. Kf1 Qxc2 the rook will be regained, or a deadly 6... d5! move.

6. Bxf7+! - the best move in this position. Here Black must go 6... Kf8! Now the move 7. Bxg8 is forced because the knight on e5 is attacked. After 7... Kxg8, the knight has to go somewhere, and after 8... Qxe4 black has a better position.

Another option would be to go 5. Be3, avoiding all the stuff with 5. Nxe5. This is the most solid and best by the computer move.
explanations.textZh:
意大利策略：骑士捕获

4...Nxd4

尽管这步棋看起来很糟糕，因为白棋可以走5.Nxe5，而且不清楚如何拯救h8上的f7兵和车，但事实并非如此。是的，在 5.Nxe5 之后，f7 棋子将在任何变体中被捕获，但黑色可以走 5...Qe7！从现在开始，游戏可以通过以下几种方式继续：

6.NXF7！？ - 最合乎逻辑的举动。它不仅捕获了棋子，还把车困在了角落里。但这招很尴尬，因为6...Qxe4和7.Kf1 Qxc2之后车将被收回，或者致命的6...d5！移动。

6.Bxf7+！ - 这个位置的最佳动作。这里黑方必须走 6...Kf8！现在，7.Bxg8 棋被迫执行，因为 e5 上的马受到攻击。 7...Kxg8之后，骑士必须去某个地方，8...Qxe4黑之后有更好的位置。

另一种选择是选择 5.Be3，避免 5.Nxe5 的所有内容。这是最扎实、最好的电脑动作。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. d4/4...Nxd4/5. Nxe5
explanations.text:
Italian Gambit: Knight Capture

5. Nxe5

White has taken the undefended e5 pawn and now threatning to take a pawn on f7 which cannot be protected by any Black's piece.
explanations.textEn:
Italian Gambit: Knight Capture

5. Nxe5

White has taken the undefended e5 pawn and now threatning to take a pawn on f7 which cannot be protected by any Black's piece.
explanations.textZh:
意大利策略：骑士捕获

5.NXE5

白棋已经拿走了不设防的 e5 棋子，现在威胁要拿走 f7 上的棋子，而 f7 棋子无法受到任何黑棋的保护。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. d4/4...Nxd4/5. Nxe5/5...Qe7/6. Bxf7
explanations.text:
Italian Gambit: Knight Capture

6. Bxf7+!

White didn't take the f7 pawn with the knight but took with the bishop, and they did a right choice. Here the best and the most popular move for Black is 6...Kf8.
explanations.textEn:
Italian Gambit: Knight Capture

6. Bxf7+!

White didn't take the f7 pawn with the knight but took with the bishop, and they did a right choice. Here the best and the most popular move for Black is 6...Kf8.
explanations.textZh:
意大利策略：骑士捕获

6.Bxf7+！

白棋没有拿马的f7兵，而是拿了主教，他们做了正确的选择。这里黑方最好和最受欢迎的棋步是 6...Kf8。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. d4/4...Nxd4/5. Nxe5/5...Qe7/6. Bxf7/6...Kf8
explanations.text:
Italian Gambit: Knight Capture

6... Kf8

Black has moved their king from check. White has the only move 7. Bxg8! because all the other move would lead to either a knight on e5 or a bishop on f7 hanging.
explanations.textEn:
Italian Gambit: Knight Capture

6... Kf8

Black has moved their king from check. White has the only move 7. Bxg8! because all the other move would lead to either a knight on e5 or a bishop on f7 hanging.
explanations.textZh:
意大利策略：骑士捕获

6...Kf8

黑棋已经将他们的王从受制状态中移开。白方唯一的棋步是 7.Bxg8！因为所有其他的举动都会导致 e5 上的马或 f7 上的主教挂起。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. d4/4...Nxd4/5. Nxe5/5...Qe7/6. Nxf7
explanations.text:
Italian Gambit: Knight Capture

6. Nxf7?!

Taking the pawn on f7 with the knight wasn't the best move for White in that position. It would be better to take this pawn with the bishop. From now, there are 2 main lines:

6... Qxe4. Black has just took a hanging pawn. White has the only move 7. Kf1 and after 7... Qxc2 Black in any variation will be a pawn up.

6... d5!. By computer this move is worse than 6... Qxe4, but for White it would be extremely hard to deal with this move. Yes, after 7. Bxd5 Nf6! black sacrifices their rook and 2 pawns, but the compensation will be Black's wild activity against no White's activity.
explanations.textEn:
Italian Gambit: Knight Capture

6. Nxf7?!

Taking the pawn on f7 with the knight wasn't the best move for White in that position. It would be better to take this pawn with the bishop. From now, there are 2 main lines:

6... Qxe4. Black has just took a hanging pawn. White has the only move 7. Kf1 and after 7... Qxc2 Black in any variation will be a pawn up.

6... d5!. By computer this move is worse than 6... Qxe4, but for White it would be extremely hard to deal with this move. Yes, after 7. Bxd5 Nf6! black sacrifices their rook and 2 pawns, but the compensation will be Black's wild activity against no White's activity.
explanations.textZh:
意大利策略：骑士捕获

6.NXF7？！

对于白方来说，在这个位置上用马吃 f7 的兵并不是最好的棋步。最好把这个棋子和主教一起拿走。从现在开始，有2条主线：

6...Qxe4。黑方刚刚拿下了一颗悬棋。白棋有唯一的棋子 7。Kf1 和 7 之后... Qxc2 黑棋在任何变化中都将是棋子。

6...d5！。从计算机上看，这手棋比 6...Qxe4 还要差，但对于白方来说，应对这手棋是极其困难的。是的，7.Bxd5 Nf6之后！黑方牺牲了他们的车和 2 个棋子，但补偿将是黑方的野行为对抗白方的行为。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. e4/1...e5/2. Nf3/2...Nc6/3. Bc4/3...Bc5/4. d4/4...Nxd4/5. Nxe5/5...Qe7/6. Nxf7/6...d5
explanations.text:
Rybasov Gambit

6... d5!

At this moment Black has already sacrificed a pawn and now sacrifices the other pawn and the rook on h8. Here White have only one move to not to lose on spot: 7. Bxd5. Taking the rook isn't the best option as after 7... Qxe4 8. Kf1 dxc4 black has an awesome position because of the trapped knight on h8 and amazing piece activity.

The main ideas for Black in this gambit is to open the e file by capturing the e4 pawn (if Black manages to do it, especially if White didn't castle, no matter of material, Black is victorious) and try to develop as fast as possible and open as much files as possible while attacking opponent's pieces.
explanations.textEn:
Rybasov Gambit

6... d5!

At this moment Black has already sacrificed a pawn and now sacrifices the other pawn and the rook on h8. Here White have only one move to not to lose on spot: 7. Bxd5. Taking the rook isn't the best option as after 7... Qxe4 8. Kf1 dxc4 black has an awesome position because of the trapped knight on h8 and amazing piece activity.

The main ideas for Black in this gambit is to open the e file by capturing the e4 pawn (if Black manages to do it, especially if White didn't castle, no matter of material, Black is victorious) and try to develop as fast as possible and open as much files as possible while attacking opponent's pieces.
explanations.textZh:
雷巴索夫开局

6...d5！

此时黑方已经牺牲了一个棋子，现在又牺牲了 h8 上的另一个棋子和车。这里白棋只有一招可以不当场输：7. Bxd5。拿车并不是最好的选择，因为 7... Qxe4 8. Kf1 dxc4 黑色有一个很棒的位置，因为 h8 上的被困骑士和令人惊叹的棋子活动。

此策略中黑方的主要思路是通过吃掉e4兵来打开e档（如果黑方能做到这一点，特别是如果白方没有城堡，无论材料如何，黑方都是胜利），并在攻击对手棋子的同时尝试尽可能快地发展并打开尽可能多的文件。

explanations.text:
Rybasov Gambit

7... Nf6!

This is the only move for Black in this position. From now, white has 2 main options:

8. Nxh8??. This move looks natural because White had captured the rook that can be saved the next move, but this move is losing. Here Black can go 8... Bg4!. From now there is quite a lot of variations.

8. Bg5!. This move is much better. Now the knight on f6 cannot capture the bishop on d5 because it's pinned to the queen. But Black has a paradoxal move in this position: 8... 0-0! and after 9. Ne5+ Be6 there are also quite a lot of variations and all of them cannot be described in one article.
explanations.textEn:
Rybasov Gambit

7... Nf6!

This is the only move for Black in this position. From now, white has 2 main options:

8. Nxh8??. This move looks natural because White had captured the rook that can be saved the next move, but this move is losing. Here Black can go 8... Bg4!. From now there is quite a lot of variations.

8. Bg5!. This move is much better. Now the knight on f6 cannot capture the bishop on d5 because it's pinned to the queen. But Black has a paradoxal move in this position: 8... 0-0! and after 9. Ne5+ Be6 there are also quite a lot of variations and all of them cannot be described in one article.
explanations.textZh:
雷巴索夫开局

7...NF6！

这是黑方在此位置上唯一的棋步。从现在开始，白棋有两个主要选择：

8.Nxh8??。这手棋看起来很自然，因为白棋已经吃掉了可以挽救下一步棋的车，但是这手棋却输了。这里黑方可以下 8...Bg4！。从现在开始，有很多变化。

8. Bg5！这个动作就好多了。现在，f6 上的马无法捕获 d5 上的主教，因为它已固定在皇后身上。但黑棋在这个位置上有一个矛盾的棋步：8……0-0！而9.Ne5+Be6之后也有相当多的变体，无法在一篇文章中全部描述。

explanations.text:
Rybasov Gambit

9... Be6

Black has covered a check with their bishop. From this position there is a couple of variations:

10. Bxe6+??. This move is the most obvious one and the blunder. After a natural 10... Qxe6 move White don't have any way of defending both the knight on e5 and the pawn on e4.

10. Bxb7?. The fun fact is that after 10... Rb8 the bishop on b7 is dead. Trying to escape the attack by 11. Ba6? move is bad because of 11... Bd5! and black is victorious again because of the same reason as after 10. Bxe6+ move.

10. c3!. Black will go 10... Nc6 and after the only 11. Ng4! move, after a series of trades Black will end up in a more pleasant position.

10.Bxe6??

explanations.text:
Rybasov Gambit

8. Nxh8??

Look at activities of each side. Black already has both knights, a queen and a dark-squared bishop developed, and the light-squared one is ready to join the party. White has only the light-squared bishop developed since they wasted a ton of tempos by capturing material (and also deactivated their knight). Black can go 8...Bg4!, bringing a new piece to the attack. From now, there are a couple of variations:

9. Qd3 - the most natural move. After that White can go 9... Nxd5, and after 10. 0-0 Nb4 11. Qd2 Nbxc2 Black will regain the lost rook with a bonus.

9. Bf7+. White realises that after 9. Qd3 the bishop on d5 will be captured and removes his bishop with check. Here Black has the only move 9... Kf8!. Now White has to go 10. Qd3 but after 10... Be2! 11. Qh3 Qxe4 Black is winning. If White instead of 10. Qd3 decide to go 10. f3??, Black can go 10... Nxe4! with a totally won position.

9. f3?. Here Black can just simply go 9... Nxd5, and if White takes the bishop on g4, after 10... Qxe4 White will lose.

explanations.textZh:

8.Nxh8??

看看双方的活动。黑色已经拥有了两个马、一个皇后和一个深色方形的主教，而浅色方形的主教已经准备好加入队伍。白方只开发了光方主教，因为他们通过捕获材料浪费了大量节奏（并且还停用了他们的马）。黑方可以走 8...Bg4!，为进攻带来新的棋子。从现在开始，有一些变化：

9. Qd3 - 最自然的走法。之后，白棋可以走 9... Nxd5，在 10. 0-0 Nb4 11. Qd2 Nbxc2 后，黑棋将重新获得失去的车并获得奖金。

9.Bf7+。白方意识到在 9.Qd3 之后，d5 上的主教将被捕获，并用过牌移除他的主教。这里黑棋有唯一的棋步 9...Kf8!。现在白方必须走 10.Qd3，但在 10...Be2 之后！ 11. Qh3 Qxe4 黑胜。如果白棋而不是 10.Qd3 决定走 10.f3??，黑棋可以走 10...Nxe4！完全赢得了位置。

9. f3？这里黑方可以简单地走 9...Nxd5，如果白方在 g4 上拿下主教，则在 10...Qxe4 后白方将输。

explanations.text:
Rybasov Gambit

8... Bg4!

Black has attacked White's queen.

9. f3?? isn't the best move for White in this position as Black can safely take the bishop on d5. The bishop on g4 can't be captured because after 10. fxg4?? Black will go 10... Qxe4! with a forced checkmate.

9. Qd3! is a much better option. But after that the bishop on d5 will be captured.

So Black often chooses 9. Bf7! to remove their bishop from the danger with check. Black has to go 9... Kf8! and after 10. Qd3 Be2 11. Qh3 Qxe4 (or 11. Qg3 Nxe4) Black has got an overwhelming position.

8...BG4！

黑棋攻击了白棋的皇后。

9.f3??对于白方来说，在这个位置上并不是最好的棋步，因为黑方可以在 d5 上安全地吃掉主教。 g4上的主教无法被捕获，因为10.fxg4之后？黑方将走 10...Qxe4！与强制将死。

9.Qd3！是一个更好的选择。但之后d5上的主教将被捕获。

所以黑棋经常选择9。Bf7！通过检查将他们的主教从危险中移除。黑棋必须下9...Kf8！ 10.Qd3 Be2 11.Qh3 Qxe4（或11.Qg3 Nxe4）之后，黑方占据压倒性优势。

explanations.text:

9... Nxd5

Black has just captured an undefended bishop on d5. Black's ideas of either 10... Nb4 and 11..Nbxc2 or 10... Be2 and 11... Qxe4 are unstoppable. If White goes 10. Nc3, Black will trade off the knights and then go 11... 0-0-0!.

10. f3??

10.f3??

这步棋看起来很合乎逻辑：它拯救了白棋的后，攻击了g4上的主教并捍卫了e4兵，但黑棋却因为令人震惊的10...Nxe4!而输了。马显然不能被吃掉，但如果白棋吃掉了象，11后...Ng3+白棋就会输。

explanations.text:
Rybasov Gambit

10... Nxe4!

Black bravely sacrifices the bishop on g4 for the e file to be opened. Accepting the sacrifice would be a fatal error because of the move 11... Ng3+! with a forced mate in 6. It's much better to go 11. Be3! and after the same 11... Ng3 either the bishop on e3 or the rook on h1 will be captured the next move.

10...Nxe4！

黑方在g4上勇敢地牺牲了象，使e档得以打开。接受牺牲将是一个致命错误，因为棋步 11...Ng3+！与 6 中的强迫伴侣一起。最好选择 11。Be3！在同样的 11...Ng3 之后，e3 上的象或 h1 上的车将在下一步被捕获。

explanations.text:
Rybasov Gambit

11. Be3!

The best attempt for Black to hold the position. But a simple move 11... Ng3 makes Black's victory inevitable. The knight obviously cannot be captured as after 12... Qxe3+ 13. Kf1 Nxf3+! Black aren't able to defend from the checkmate on f2.

If White try to defend their bishop with the move 12. Qd2, Black wouldn't take the rook on h1 but instead go 12... Nxf3+! 13. gxf3 Bxe3 White are forced to sacrifice their queen as there are no other good moves against 14... Bf4+.

12. Qd3 is another defending option, but after 12... Nxc2+! the knight cannot be captured because the bishop on e3 will be captured. After 13. Kf2 Black will go 13... Nxe3! Kxg3 Bf5 White is lost, after 13. Kd2 Bf5 White is lost as well.

11. Be3！

黑棋守住局面的最佳尝试。但简单的一步 11...Ng3 就使得黑方的胜利不可避免。骑士显然无法被俘获，因为12...Qxe3+ 13.Kf1 Nxf3+！黑方无法防御 f2 上的将死。

如果白方试图用 12.Qd2 来保卫他们的象，黑方不会在 h1 上拿下车，而是走 12...Nxf3+！ 13. gxf3 Bxe3 白方被迫牺牲他们的皇后，因为没有其他好的棋法对抗 14...Bf4+。

12.Qd3是另一个防守选择，但在12之后...Nxc2+！马无法被捕获，因为 e3 上的主教将被捕获。 13 后。Kf2 黑将走 13...Nxe3！ 13 点后，Kxg3 Bf5 白棋输了。Kd2 Bf5 白棋也输了。

explanations.text:
Rybasov Gambit

11. fxg4??

After this move Black's victory is inevitable after the move 11... Ng3+!

12. Kf2 is a worse option as after 12... Ndf5+! White has to sacrifice a queen and the bishop and get checkmated on e3 with the queen.

12. Kd2 is a better option, but it doesn't save the game. Here Black out of nowhere goes 12... Nb3+!!, and after 13. cxb3 (13. axb3 leads to 13... Qe3#) Black is the whole 12 points of material down, but after 13... Rd8+ 14. Kc3 Bb4+ 15. Kc2 Qe4+ 16. Qd3 Qxd3# White loses.

11.fxg4??

12. Kf2 是一个更糟糕的选择，因为 12...Ndf5+ 之后！白棋必须牺牲一个后和主教，并在 e3 上用后将死。

12. Kd2是一个更好的选择，但它并不能拯救比赛。这里黑方突然下12...Nb3+!!，在13.cxb3之后（13.axb3导致13...Qe3#）黑方是整个12点的材料下降，但在13...Rd8+ 14.Kc3 Bb4+ 15.Kc2 Qe4+ 16.Qd3 Qxd3#之后白方输了。
