explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. f3/1...e5/2. Kf2
explanations.text:
The Fried Fox Attack

The move 2.Kf2?! (ECO code A00) is called various things in various parts of the world. Most commonly known as the Fried Fox/Pork Chop Opening but also known throughout much of Europe as the Hammerschlag. In the United States some theory has been published to award-winning praise under the name Schmoe Attack.

On 29 September 2020, the World Chess Champion at the time, Magnus Carlsen, defeated grandmaster Wesley So in the Banter Series with this opening. So described the loss as "humiliating".

In 2001 a "mystery GM" playing at the I.C.C. (Internet Chess Club) was beating all Grandmasters (GMs) and International Masters (IMs) with this opening for several months. GM Nigel Short lost several games to this mystery player using this opening, and he had a theory from chats he and this player had had after their games that this was in fact Bobby Fischer, trying to prove that you can win at the highest levels in chess even with random openings and in this way promoting Fischer Random Chess.

There is a competing rumor told by GM Larry Evans and others in the chess community that someone using a chess interface engine which plays the moves straight to the game instead of the cumbersome process of transferring moves from the chess engine to the online game was playing a trick on the online chess community. Fischer is not on record as having ever commented on the matter.

Positional Ideas: White wants to calmly trade off pieces to lessen the chances of a successful attack against his king. As pieces come off the board white's king will be in a good position to control the center and help in a king and pawn ending.

Psychological Ideas: The shock and awe factor of facing this opening may lead to overconfidence and reckless play from black, in this way the game may reach atypical positions with chances for creative and energetic play.

Opening Ideas: Controlling the center with f3 and often an early pawn advance to c3. An active king who if handled properly can assist in both attack and defense in the late opening and early middle-game.

Fried Fox/Pork Chop Opening Mainline

2...d5 Taking firm control of the center and opening line for the development of black's pieces. In the game between the two masters Williams, Simon Kim (2421) vs. Simons, Martin (2264)11.08.1999 - Chessbase Mega Database 2010 play continued 3.e3 Nf6 4.d4!? Nc6 5.Bb5 Bd6! 6.Ne2 O-O 7.Re1?! e4 8.Ng3 h5!? 9.f4 Bg4 10.Be2 g6?! and white went on to win a wild game.

3.c3 is a trappy move which can assist in taking over the center with a timely pawn advance to d4, it also allows movement of the queen along the deadly d1-a4 diagonal. 3...Nf6 4.Na3!? leads to fun and unexplored positions.

explanations.textZh:
炸狐狸袭击

招式2.Kf2？！ （ECO代码A00）在世界各地有不同的称呼。最常被称为“炸狐狸/猪排开口”，但在欧洲大部分地区也被称为“Hammerschlag”。在美国，一些名为“施莫攻击”的理论已经发表，并获得了赞誉。

2020 年 9 月 29 日，当时的世界国际象棋冠军马格努斯·卡尔森 (Magnus Carlsen) 在戏谑系列赛中击败了大师韦斯利·苏 (Wesley So)。因此将这次损失描述为“耻辱”。

2001 年，一位“神秘总经理”在 I.C.C. 打球。 （互联网国际象棋俱乐部）在几个月内击败了所有特级大师（GM）和国际大师（IM）。总经理奈杰尔·肖特（Nigel Short）利用这个开局输给了这位神秘棋手，他从他和这位棋手在比赛结束后的聊天中得到了一个理论，这实际上是鲍比·费舍尔（Bobby Fischer），试图证明即使在随机开局下你也可以在国际象棋的最高水平上获胜，并通过这种方式推广费舍尔随机象棋。

GM 拉里·埃文斯 (Larry Evans) 和国际象棋社区的其他人告诉我们，有人使用国际象棋界面引擎直接在游戏中下棋，而不是从国际象棋引擎将棋步转移到在线游戏的繁琐过程，这是对在线国际象棋社区的欺骗。菲舍尔没有对此事发表评论的记录。

走位思路：白棋想要冷静地交换棋子，以减少成功攻击王的机会。当棋子离开棋盘时，白方的王将处于控制中心的良好位置，并有助于形成王和兵的结局。

心理想法：面对这个开局的震惊和敬畏因素可能会导致黑色的过度自信和鲁莽的比赛，这样比赛可能会达到非典型的位置，并有机会进行创造性和充满活力的比赛。

开局思路：用 f3 控制中心，通常早期棋子会推进到 c3。活跃的王者如果处理得当，可以在开局后期和中前期起到攻防兼备的作用。

炸狐狸/猪排开场主线

2...d5 牢牢控制中线和开局线，推动黑棋的发展。在两位大师 Williams, Simon Kim (2421) 与 Simons, Martin (2264) 的比赛中 11.08.1999 - Chessbase Mega Database 2010 比赛继续 3.e3 Nf6 4.d4！？ NC6 5.Bb5 Bd6！ 6.Ne2 O-O 7.Re1？！ e4 8.NG3 h5！？ 9.f4 Bg4 10.Be2 g6？！白棋继续赢得了一场狂野的比赛。

3.c3是一个陷阱走法，可以通过及时的棋子推进到d4来帮助占领中心，它还允许皇后沿着致命的d1-a4对角线移动。 3...Nf6 4.Na3！？导致有趣和未探索的位置。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. f3/1...e5/2. g4
explanations.text:
Barnes Opening, Fool's mate

2. g4??

This move is a blunder (as can be seen by the ??), as it allows Black to immediately checkmate with 2...Qh4#. This is known as Fool's Mate. It is the fastest possible checkmate in a chess game.

Popular Moves

2...Qh4# 34%. 2...d5 24%. 2...Nc6 15%. 2...Bc5 8%. All other moves ~15%.

2...Qh4# 34%. 2...d5 24%. 2...Nc6 15%. 2...Bc5 8%. All other moves ~15%.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. f3/1...e5/2. g4/2...Qh4
explanations.text:
Barnes Opening/Fool's Mate

2... Qh4#

White has played a very poor and weakening move and allowed Black the quickest possible checkmate (Fool's Mate) in the opening game of chess: Mate in two moves. The mate almost never occurs in practice but is commonly known among chess players, due to it being the fastest possible checkmate. However, Black was already better.

A variation of this mate occurs when White advances the f-pawn two squares: 1. f4 e6 2. g4?? Qh4#. White can also move their g-pawn before the f-pawn.

巴恩斯开场/傻瓜之友

2...Qh4#

白方下的棋非常糟糕且削弱，并让黑方在国际象棋的首局比赛中以最快的速度将死（愚人之友）：两步棋之内。这种交配在实践中几乎不会出现，但在国际象棋棋手中却广为人知，因为它是最快的将死方式。然而，黑棋已经更好了。

当白方将 f 兵推进两个方格时，就会出现这种配对的变化： 1. f4 e6 2. g4?? Qh4#。白棋也可以在 f 棋子之前移动他们的 g 棋子。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. f4
explanations.text:
1. f4 · Bird's opening

Bird's opening is an aggressive and less common first move. 1. f4 controls e5 from the flank, and means White will be able to soon play Nf3 without it keeping their f-pawn back. A danger in moving their f-pawn so soon is that it weakens White's kingside, and White must be aware of potential attacks on the e1-h4 diagonal.

1...d5, the Dutch variation, is the main line. Black takes space in the centre and controls e4, and the game resembles a Dutch defence in reverse.

Certainly White wishes to play 2. Nf3, developing while controlling h4. Then, a common plan for White is to adopt a reversed Leningrad Dutch set-up: 3. g3, 4. Bg2, and 5. O-O, and Black usually adopts a similar kingside fianchetto position also. White would like to play d3 and c3, or d3 and Qe1 to try for e4. Playing more in the manner of a stonewall Dutch, with 3. e3, 4. Be2, and d3 or d4, is an alternative.

1...Nf6, likewise controlling e5, usually transposes.

1...c5 allows 2. e4, and White reaches a more competitive Sicilian defence position, the McDonnell attack. However, it is more common for White to continue with the same Nf3, g3, Bg2, O-O approach, and only play e4 later if it is still available.

1...e5?!, From's gambit, offers the pawn to open lines of attack. It is an immediate attempt to exploit White's weakened kingside. Some famous "beginner" traps that stem from accepting the gambit include 2. fxe5 Qh4+!? 3. g3 Be7?, where Black sacrifices their queen as 4. gxh4?? Bxh4#; and 2. fxe5 d6 3. exd6 Bxd6 (a more sound way for Black to continue), where e.g. 4. e4?? Qh4+! and 5. g3?? leads to forced mate. White can decline the gambit (e.g. 2. e4, transposing to the king's gambit) but best is to accept it, and as long as White prevents infiltration of their position via h4 (2. fxe5 d6 3. exd6 Bxd6 4. Nf3!), they are better.

Other moves

1...f5, the symmetrical variation, may lead to a number of original gambits.

1...Nh6!? is called the Horsefly Defence.

1...g5?! is called the Hobbs Gambit.

1...h6 2. Nf3 3. g5 is called the Hobbs-Zilbermints Gambit.

History

Bird's opening is named for Henry Bird (1829―1908), who helped to popularise it.

The earliest example of a game beginning 1. f4 was published Gioachino Greco's 1620 treatise. The game continued 1...e5, now known as From's gambit.

It was played occasionally in the first half of the 19th century, including in the 1834 matches between La Bourdonnais and McDonnell (something of a forerunner to the World Chess Championship), where the game transposed to a queen's pawn game. From 1856 Henry Bird began playing 1. f4 near exclusively with White, and had over 100 recorded games with it.

In the 20th century, Bent Larsen was known to play it, and 1. f4 received its highest level outing in Larsen v Fischer in the 1970-2 Candidates. Fischer played 1...c5 and the game transposed into something like the McDonnell attack.

1. f4 doesn't make many appearances in classical tournament chess today, though it is more common as a blitz weapon, played by the aggressive tactician who hopes to avoid theory and succeed by their wits alone.

explanations.textZh:
1. f4·鸟的开场

伯德的开局是一个侵略性的、不太常见的第一步。 1. f4从侧翼控制e5，这意味着白方很快就能下Nf3，而不会让他们的f兵落后。这么快移动他们的 f 兵的一个危险是它会削弱白方的王翼，白方必须意识到 e1-h4 对角线上的潜在攻击。

1...d5（荷兰语变体）是主线。黑棋在中间占据空间并控制e4，比赛类似于荷兰的反向防守。

当然，白棋希望下2. Nf3，在控制h4的同时发展。然后，白棋的常见计划是采用相反的列宁格勒荷兰布局：3. g3、4. Bg2 和 5. O-O，而黑棋通常也采用类似的王翼前卫位置。白棋想下d3和c3，或者d3和Qe1尝试e4。另一种选择是更多地以石墙荷兰人的方式进行演奏，使用 3. e3、4. Be2 和 d3 或 d4。

1...Nf6，同样控制e5，通常转置。

1...c5 允许 2. e4，白方到达更具竞争力的西西里防御位置，即麦克唐纳攻击。然而，白方更常见的是继续使用相同的 Nf3、g3、Bg2、O-O 方法，并且仅在 e4 仍然可用时才下棋。

1...e5?!，From 的策略，提供棋子以打开攻击线。这是利用白棋弱势王翼的直接尝试。一些著名的“初学者”陷阱源于接受这个策略，包括 2. fxe5 Qh4+!? 3. g3 Be7？，黑方牺牲其后为 4. gxh4?? Bxh4#； 2. fxe5 d6 3. exd6 Bxd6（黑棋继续的更合理方式），例如4.e4?? Qh4+！和5.g3??导致强迫交配。白方可以拒绝该策略（例如 2. e4，转换为王的策略），但最好是接受它，并且只要白方通过 h4 阻止其位置渗透（2. fxe5 d6 3. exd6 Bxd6 4. Nf3！），他们就会更好。

其他动作

1...f5，对称变化，可能会导致许多原始策略。

1...NH6！？被称为“马蝇防御”。

1...g5？！称为霍布斯策略。

1...h6 2. Nf3 3. g5 称为 Hobbs-Zilbermints 策略。

历史

伯德的开场以亨利·伯德（Henry Bird，1829—1908 年）的名字命名，他帮助推广了这一开场。

最早的以 1.f4 开头的游戏示例是 Gioachino Greco 于 1620 年发表的论文。游戏继续进行 1...e5，现在称为 From 策略。

这种游戏在 19 世纪上半叶偶尔会进行，包括 1834 年 La Bourdonnais 和 McDonnell 之间的比赛（可以说是世界国际象棋锦标赛的前身），比赛变成了皇后的典当游戏。从 1856 年起，亨利·伯德 (Henry Bird) 开始几乎只与怀特一起玩 1. f4，并记录了超过 100 场比赛。

在 20 世纪，Bent Larsen 因演奏该曲而闻名，1. f4 在 1970-2 候选人赛的 Larsen v Fischer 比赛中获得了最高水平的表现。 Fischer 打出 1...c5，比赛变成了麦克唐纳进攻。

1. 如今，f4 在经典国际象棋锦标赛中出现的次数并不多，尽管它作为一种闪电战武器更为常见，由那些希望避免理论并仅靠智慧取得成功的激进战术家所使用。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. f4/1...d5
explanations.text:
1...d5 · Dutch variation

From here, one possible reply is to treat the position as a Dutch defence reversed. As in the Dutch, White can either fianchetto with 2. g3 (Leningrad Dutch) or go for the Stonewall with 2. e3, soon followed by d4 and c3.

Another possible motive is to go with a uniquely "Bird" strategy of dark-square control. The plan is to develop the King's knight to f3, to fianchetto the dark-square bishop with b3 and Bb2, and to focus in further pressure on the e5 square, sometimes with Qe1 and Qg3. Depending on the position, the light square bishop can go either on e2 or on b5 (with the idea to exchange it for the black knight on c6 and clear the way for the move Nf3-e5). The main problem with the arising positions is where to put the b1 knight. Sometimes c3 or d2 are good squares, but at other times, (especially if Black pushes ...d5, ...c5, ...d4), it may be good to play a4 and put the knight on a3, with increased queenside control and flexible options.

A third strategy is simply to play for the break e4. The logical moves are d3, Nd2, and Qe1. Note that the king's bishop will go to e2 if black plays ...Bg4.

explanations.textZh:
1...d5 · 荷兰语变体

从这里开始，一个可能的答案是将这一立场视为荷兰防守的逆转。与荷兰棋一样，白棋可以用 2. g3（列宁格勒荷兰棋）进行 fianchetto，也可以用 2. e3 下石墙，紧接着是 d4 和 c3。

另一个可能的动机是采用独特的暗方控制“鸟”策略。计划是将国王的骑士发展到f3，用b3和Bb2与暗方主教进行双杀，并集中对e5方进一步施压，有时使用Qe1和Qg3。根据位置的不同，浅色方形主教可以走 e2 或 b5（想法是用它交换 c6 上的黑马，并为 Nf3-e5 的移动扫清道路）。出现的位置的主要问题是b1骑士放在哪里。有时c3或d2是很好的方格，但在其他时候（特别是如果黑方推...d5，...c5，...d4），下a4并将马放在a3上可能会很好，增加后侧控制和灵活的选择。

第三个策略就是为突破e4而战。逻辑动作是 d3、Nd2 和 Qe1。请注意，如果黑方下...Bg4，则国王的主教将进入 e2。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. f4/1...d5/2. e4
explanations.text:
2. e4? · Williams gambit

White offers Black the e-pawn for free. It is very similar to the Englund gambit (1. d4 e5) with colours reversed.

After 2...dxe4 Black has a clear lead, but White has the opportunity to try the same sort of traps seen in the Englund gambit:

3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Qe2 Bf5 (Black looks to hold on to the extra pawn) 5. Qb5+ Bd7 6. Qxb7?! where 6...Bc6?? is a game losing blunder to 7. Bb5!, pinning the bishop to the king. Rather 6...Nc6 followed by 7...Rb8 is winning for Black. (Compare the Englund gambit main line, 1. d4 e5? 2. dxe5 Nc6 3. Nf3 Qe7 4. Bf4 Qb4+ 5. Bd2 Qxb2?!.)

3. Bc4 Nf6 4. d3 exd3 5. Ne2!? (White appears to blunder the knight, as if a pre-move mistake) dxe2?? 6. Bxf7+ (removes defender of queen) Kxf7 7. Qxd8. (Compare the Wu trap in the England gambit, 1. d4 e5 2. dxe5 Bc5 3. Nf3 d6 4. exd6 Ne7!? 5. dxe7?? Bxf2+ 6. Kxf2 Qxd1.)

Simplest for Black is just to give the pawn back, and convert the tempo White spends on recovering the pawn into developing moves.

History

The identity of the "Williams" behind this gambit is a little uncertain.

The second edition of the Oxford Companion attributes it to Elijah Williams, a nineteenth century chess player. However, this is probably incorrect: no games where Elijah Williams played this line are cited by the book or are otherwise attested in databases.

A 1997 monograph on the gambit written by a William L. Williams disputed the Oxford Companions account. Williams asserted they originated the gambit in 1975. Twelve of their games from 1975 onwards appeared in one database attributed to a "W. Williams", however in some versions of the database this was given as Walford Hall Williams.

Sample game

"Williams, W." versus Cranford, W., 1982

1. f4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Qe2

White is threatening e4, but Black would like to keep the extra material.

4...Qd4!?

Better perhaps is a normal developing move, 4...Bf5 (defending the pawn) or 4...Bg4 (attacking the queen). White may continue with the reversed Englund gambit line, 5. Qb5+, but as long as Black avoids the trap of 5...Bd7 6. Qxb7?! Bc6?? there is no danger.

After the text move, 5. Qb5+ is still possible where 5...Bd7?? falls into the trap but 5...Nc6 defuses it.

5. h3

Not strictly necessary. White prevents 5...Bg4 but even if 5. g3 Bg4? is a mistake. 6. Qb5+! and White is winning at least a pawn: 6...Nbd7 7. Qxb7 Rb8 8. Qxc7. 6...Nc6 loses a knight: the difference between this position and that after 4...Bg4 5. Qb5+ is that Black's queen is not on the back rank to defend the rook.

5...a6 6. g4 g6 7. Bg2

Black cannot now bring another defender to the pawn.

7...Nc6 8. Nxe4 h6??

8...Nxe4 was necessary to save the game. With their queen on e2 and the e-file half-open, White can exploit Black's uncastled king.

9. c3 Qd8?? 10. Nxf6# 1-0

9. c3 drives the queen away from controlling f6, allowing White to take the knight and Black cannot take back due to the pin on the e-file. Black's knight is lost regardless, but 9...Qd8?? was the worst place to move the queen, as it takes away the king's escape square and 10. Nxf6# is checkmate.

explanations.textZh:
2.e4？ · 威廉姆斯策略

白方免费向黑方提供电子棋子。它与英格伦德策略（1.d4 e5）非常相似，只是颜色相反。

2...dxe4 后，黑方明显领先，但白方有机会尝试英格兰开局中出现的相同类型的陷阱：

3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Qe2 Bf5（黑方看起来会保留多余的棋子） 5. Qb5+ Bd7 6. Qxb7？！ 6...Bc6 在哪里？这是一场以 7. Bb5! 输掉比赛的错误，将主教钉在了国王身上。相反，6...Nc6 紧随其后的是 7...Rb8，黑棋获胜。 （比较英格伦德弃兵主线，1. d4 e5？2. dxe5 Nc6 3. Nf3 Qe7 4. Bf4 Qb4+ 5. Bd2 Qxb2？！。）

3.BC4 Nf6 4.d3 exd3 5.Ne2！？ （白棋似乎使马犯了错误，就好像棋前的错误一样）dxe2？ 6. Bxf7+（移除后的防守者）Kxf7 7. Qxd8。 （对比英格兰棋局中的吴陷阱，1. d4 e5 2. dxe5 Bc5 3. Nf3 d6 4. exd6 Ne7！？ 5. dxe7?? Bxf2+ 6. Kxf2 Qxd1。）

对于黑方来说，最简单的就是将棋子还给棋子，然后将棋子白棋收回棋子的节奏转变为发展步法。

历史

这一策略背后的“威廉姆斯”的身份有点不确定。

《牛津指南》第二版将其归功于 19 世纪国际象棋棋手伊利亚·威廉姆斯 (Elijah Williams)。然而，这可能是不正确的：本书没有引用伊利亚·威廉姆斯玩过这句台词的游戏，也没有在数据库中得到证实。

1997 年，威廉·L·威廉姆斯 (William L. Williams) 撰写的一本关于这一策略的专着对《牛津同伴》的说法提出了质疑。威廉姆斯声称他们在 1975 年发起了这一策略。从 1975 年起，他们的 12 场比赛出现在一个数据库中，归属于“W. Williams”，但在该数据库的某些版本中，该数据库被指定为 Walford Hall Williams。

示例游戏

“威廉姆斯，W。”与克兰福德，W.，1982 年

1. f4 d5 2. e4 dxe4 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. Qe2

白方威胁 e4，但黑方希望保留多余的材料。

4...Qd4！？

更好的也许是正常的发展动作，4...Bf5（保卫兵）或4...Bg4（攻击皇后）。白方可能会继续反向英格伦德策略线，5. Qb5+，但只要黑方避免陷入 5...Bd7 6. Qxb7 的陷阱？！ BC6？？没有危险。

文本移动后，5.Qb5+ 仍然可能，其中 5...Bd7??落入陷阱，但 5...Nc6 化解了它。

5.h3

并非绝对必要。白棋可以防止 5...Bg4 但即使 5.g3 Bg4？是一个错误。 6.Qb5+！白方至少赢得一个棋子：6...Nbd7 7. Qxb7 Rb8 8. Qxc7。 6...Nc6 失去一个马：这个位置与 4...Bg4 5.Qb5+ 之后的位置之间的区别是黑方后不在后排防守车。

5...a6 6.g4 g6 7.Bg2

黑方现在无法将另一名防守者带入棋子。

7...Nc6 8.Nxe4 h6??

8...Nxe4 是保存游戏所必需的。由于他们的皇后在 e2 上并且电子文件半打开，白方可以利用黑方未城堡的国王。

9. c3 Qd8?? 10. Nxf6# 1-0

9. c3 驱使后脱离对 f6 的控制，让白棋拿走马，而黑棋由于电子文件上的 pin 而无法收回。无论如何，黑方的马都输了，但是9...Qd8？是移动后最糟糕的地方，因为它夺走了国王的逃生方格和 10。Nxf6# 将死。

2. g4??

This move blunders a pawn for no apparent reason, while severely weakening the kingside. Black can play 2...e5!, threatening checkmate and therefore winning a pawn. Or Black could just take the pawn with 2...Bxg4.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. f4/1...e5
explanations.text:
Bird's Opening: From's Gambit

1...e5

Here black enters the From Gambit. White's choices are either taking the pawn, or moving to e4, entering the King's Gambit. The From's main line is with 2.fxe5 d6 3.exd6 Bxd6, usually followed by a vicious kingside assault with g5, or a more strategical Nc6.

White can also decline the second pawn with the line 1.f4 e5 2.fxe5 d6 3.Nf3 dxe5 4.e4, where White's missing f-pawn can be a king safety issue, or an attacking asset after he castles due to the open f-file. The trade of the f-pawn for the d-pawn can also give white additional center control.
explanations.textEn:
Bird's Opening: From's Gambit

1...e5

Here black enters the From Gambit. White's choices are either taking the pawn, or moving to e4, entering the King's Gambit. The From's main line is with 2.fxe5 d6 3.exd6 Bxd6, usually followed by a vicious kingside assault with g5, or a more strategical Nc6.

White can also decline the second pawn with the line 1.f4 e5 2.fxe5 d6 3.Nf3 dxe5 4.e4, where White's missing f-pawn can be a king safety issue, or an attacking asset after he castles due to the open f-file. The trade of the f-pawn for the d-pawn can also give white additional center control.
explanations.textZh:
Bird 的开局：From 的开局

1...e5

这里黑棋进入起始弃兵。白方的选择是要么吃卒，要么移动到e4，进入国王的弃兵。 From的主线是2.fxe5 d6 3.exd6 Bxd6，通常紧随其后的是g5的恶毒王翼攻击，或者更具战略性的Nc6。

白方还可以使用 1.f4 e5 2.fxe5 d6 3.Nf3 dxe5 4.e4 行拒绝第二个棋子，其中白方缺少的 f 棋子可能会成为国王的安全问题，或者由于打开的 f 线而在城堡后成为攻击资产。将 f 棋子换成 d 棋子也可以为白方提供额外的中心控制权。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. f4/1...e5/2. fxe5
explanations.text:
From's Gambit Accepted

This wins a pawn, but creates more kingside weaknesses. Now white will have to be careful to not allow a quick knockout in the opening, after d6 exd6 Bxd6. For example: 4.Nc3?? Qh4+ g3 Qxg3+!! hxg3 Bxg3# is a slam dunk finish.

Practically taking the pawn is the best move, since Black gambits are rarely sound due to White's first move. That way, Black's compensation is minimized compared to White's gambits.

White is better, but he will defend for a long time and it is not easy. If White knows what he is doing, he should be better. At club level, it is popular as amateurs know less about the From's Gambit and there are many traps.

Black will typically plan to attack the weakened white kingside. He is threatening Qh4+ and a sacrifice on g3 followed by mate after d6 exd6 Bxd6.

Black will typically plan to attack the weakened white kingside. He is threatening Qh4+ and a sacrifice on g3 followed by mate after d6 exd6 Bxd6.
explanations.textZh:
已接受发件人的策略

这赢得了一个棋子，但造成了更多的王翼弱点。现在白方必须小心，不要在 d6 exd6 Bxd6 之后在开局中快速击倒对手。例如：4.NC3?? Qh4+ g3 Qxg3+!! hxg3 Bxg3# 是灌篮终结。

实际上，吃卒是最好的棋步，因为由于白棋的第一步，黑方的策略很少是合理的。这样，与白棋的策略相比，黑方的补偿被最小化。

白棋更好，但他要防守很长时间，并不容易。如果怀特知道自己在做什么，他应该会做得更好。在俱乐部层面，它很受欢迎，因为业余爱好者对From's Gambit知之甚少，而且陷阱也很多。

黑棋通常会计划攻击被削弱的白棋王翼。他威胁 Qh4+ 并在 g3 上做出牺牲，然后在 d6 exd6 Bxd6 后进行 mate。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. f4/1...e5/2. fxe5/2...Nc6/3. Nf3/3...g5
explanations.text:
3...g5!?

This is a committing and demented-looking move. But it is the a standard move in the From's Gambit. The point of 3...g5 to to play ...g4 and kick the f3-knight away, and to discourage kingside castling by White. However, it is certainly not without consequence.
explanations.textEn:
3...g5!?

This is a committing and demented-looking move. But it is the a standard move in the From's Gambit. The point of 3...g5 to to play ...g4 and kick the f3-knight away, and to discourage kingside castling by White. However, it is certainly not without consequence.
explanations.textZh:
3...g5！？

这是一个坚定而疯狂的举动。但这是From 策略中的标准动作。 3...g5 的要点是玩 ...g4 并将 f3 骑士踢开，并阻止怀特王翼易位。然而，这肯定不是没有后果的。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. f4/1...e5/2. fxe5/2...Nc6/3. Nf3/3...g5/4. d4
explanations.text:
== 4.d4 ==

This is a common move in the From's Gambit for White, defending e5 and attacking g5 at the same time. 4.h3 was weakening, but also playable. However, it was not in the spirit of the From's Gambit.

Black can now continue his plan with 4...g4.
explanations.textEn:
== 4.d4 ==

This is a common move in the From's Gambit for White, defending e5 and attacking g5 at the same time. 4.h3 was weakening, but also playable. However, it was not in the spirit of the From's Gambit.

Black can now continue his plan with 4...g4.
explanations.textZh:
== 4.d4 ==

这是白棋From 开局中的常见棋法，同时防守e5 并进攻g5。 4.h3被削弱了，但还能玩。然而，这并不符合From的策略的精神。

黑方现在可以用 4...g4 继续他的计划。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. f4/1...e5/2. fxe5/2...Nc6/3. Nf3/3...g5/4. d4/4...g4
explanations.text:
4...g4

This move continues the plan of Black's 3...g5. He is kicking the f3-knight away. Houdini recommends the passive-looking Ng1 d6 e4!, giving back the pawn. After dxe5 d5 Nce7 Nc3 f5 (Otherwise white gets a bind on the f-file), Bg5 h6 Bh4 Bg7 Bb5+ Kf7 Bc4 Qd6 and both exf5 and Bb5 are good for white.
explanations.textEn:
4...g4

This move continues the plan of Black's 3...g5. He is kicking the f3-knight away. Houdini recommends the passive-looking Ng1 d6 e4!, giving back the pawn. After dxe5 d5 Nce7 Nc3 f5 (Otherwise white gets a bind on the f-file), Bg5 h6 Bh4 Bg7 Bb5+ Kf7 Bc4 Qd6 and both exf5 and Bb5 are good for white.
explanations.textZh:
4...g4

这一步棋延续了黑棋 3...g5 的计划。他正在把f3骑士踢开。 Houdini 推荐看起来被动的 Ng1 d6 e4!，还给棋子。在 dxe5 d5 Nce7 Nc3 f5（否则白色会在 f 文件上绑定）之后，Bg5 h6 Bh4 Bg7 Bb5+ Kf7 Bc4 Qd6 以及 exf5 和 Bb5 都适合白色。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. f4/1...e5/2. fxe5/2...d6/3. exd6
explanations.text:
3.exd6

After this, Black's only sensible move is Bxd6, developing with a threat. However, Nf6, the Langheld Gambit has also been tried with similar ideas to the mainline but with a Queen on c7 instead of a pawn.
explanations.textEn:
3.exd6

After this, Black's only sensible move is Bxd6, developing with a threat. However, Nf6, the Langheld Gambit has also been tried with similar ideas to the mainline but with a Queen on c7 instead of a pawn.
explanations.textZh:
3.exd6

此后，黑方唯一明智的棋步是Bxd6，以威胁的方式发展。然而，Nf6，朗格德开局也曾尝试过与主线类似的想法，但在 c7 上使用皇后而不是棋子。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. f4/1...e5/2. fxe5/2...d6/3. exd6/3...Bxd6
explanations.text:
3...Bxd6

This move develops with a threat. There are three sane ways to stop Qh4+. The first one, Nf3, is the best move. The second one, g3?!, runs into a rapid drill attack after 3...h5. A sample line: Nf3 h4! Nxh4? (gxh4 is better, but black has good compensation for the pawn after the simple 5...Bg4) Rxh4! gxh4 Qxh4# The third one, 4.h4??, runs into Bg3 mate! Also, one more trap is Nh3?? Bxh3 and Qh4 mate to follow.
explanations.textEn:
3...Bxd6

This move develops with a threat. There are three sane ways to stop Qh4+. The first one, Nf3, is the best move. The second one, g3?!, runs into a rapid drill attack after 3...h5. A sample line: Nf3 h4! Nxh4? (gxh4 is better, but black has good compensation for the pawn after the simple 5...Bg4) Rxh4! gxh4 Qxh4# The third one, 4.h4??, runs into Bg3 mate! Also, one more trap is Nh3?? Bxh3 and Qh4 mate to follow.
explanations.textZh:
3...Bxd6

这一举动充满了威胁。有三种明智的方法可以阻止 Qh4+。第一个，Nf3，是最好的举动。第二个，g3？！，在 3...h5 后遇到快速演习攻击。示例行：Nf3 h4！ Nxh4？ （gxh4 更好，但黑棋对简单 5...Bg4 之后的棋子有很好的补偿） Rxh4！ gxh4 Qxh4# 第三个，4.h4??，遇到了 Bg3 伙伴！另外，还有一个陷阱是NH3？？ Bxh3 和 Qh4 紧随其后进行交配。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. f4/1...e5/2. fxe5/2...d6/3. exd6/3...Bxd6/4. Nf3/4...g5
explanations.text:
4...g5

This is the Lasker variation, the most aggressive and double edged line. Black now threatens g4 followed by Qh4+, Bxg3+, and mate to follow. The most common move, and, according to Lakdawala, "Our only hope of wresting the advantage". The game now turns into a full-blown firefight.
explanations.textEn:
4...g5

This is the Lasker variation, the most aggressive and double edged line. Black now threatens g4 followed by Qh4+, Bxg3+, and mate to follow. The most common move, and, according to Lakdawala, "Our only hope of wresting the advantage". The game now turns into a full-blown firefight.
explanations.textZh:
4...g5

这是拉斯克变体，最具侵略性和双刃剑的路线。黑方现在威胁 g4，随后是 Qh4+、Bxg3+，然后是大副。根据拉克达瓦拉的说法，这是最常见的举动，也是“我们夺取优势的唯一希望”。比赛现在变成了一场全面的交火。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. f4/1...e5/2. fxe5/2...d6/3. exd6/3...Bxd6/4. Nf3/4...g5/5. h3
explanations.text:
5.h3??

This unfortunate move caused the loss of three white players in Lakdawala's database. While white has stopped g4, the price is far too high, he just allowed Bg3 mate!
explanations.textEn:
5.h3??

This unfortunate move caused the loss of three white players in Lakdawala's database. While white has stopped g4, the price is far too high, he just allowed Bg3 mate!
explanations.textZh:
5.h3??

这一不幸的举动导致拉克达瓦拉数据库中失去了三名白人球员。虽然白棋已经阻止了g4，但代价太高了，他只让Bg3搭档！

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. f4/1...e5/2. fxe5/2...d6/3. exd6/3...Nf6
explanations.text:
3...Nf6

This is the Langheld Gambit, a dubious pawn sacrifice to create lots of unknown traps and trick the white players to fall for them. The opening reached small amounts of popularity in recent years due to FM William Graifs advocacy for its playability, its often only played in blitz, or bullet; but to a high level still!
explanations.textEn:
3...Nf6

This is the Langheld Gambit, a dubious pawn sacrifice to create lots of unknown traps and trick the white players to fall for them. The opening reached small amounts of popularity in recent years due to FM William Graifs advocacy for its playability, its often only played in blitz, or bullet; but to a high level still!
explanations.textZh:
3...NF6

这就是朗海尔德策略，一种可疑的棋子牺牲，目的是制造许多未知的陷阱并欺骗白人玩家上当。由于 FM William Graifs 对其可玩性的宣传，该开场近年来小幅流行，通常只以闪电战或子弹形式播放；但仍达到高水平！

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. f4/1...e5/2. fxe5/2...d6/3. Nf3/3...dxe5/4. Nxe5
explanations.text:
4. Nxe5

This move is the From's Gambit accepted. The only way to get compensation for the lost pawn and transpose back into mainline theory is 4...Bd6.
explanations.textEn:
4. Nxe5

This move is the From's Gambit accepted. The only way to get compensation for the lost pawn and transpose back into mainline theory is 4...Bd6.
explanations.textZh:
4.NXE5

这一招被From的策略所接受。获得损失棋子补偿并转回主线理论的唯一方法是 4...Bd6。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. f4/1...e5/2. fxe5/2...d6/3. Nf3/3...dxe5/4. Nxe5/4...Bd6
explanations.text:
4...Bd6

This attacks the knight. Since 5. d4? Bxe5 6. dxe5 Qxd1+ is uncomfortable for White, taking on double isolated e-pawns and forfeiting castling rights, while 5. Nc4?? Qh4+! 6. g3 Qxg3+!! 7. hxg3 Bxg3# is lost, and 5. Nd3? Qh4+ 6. Nf2 Bxh2 is equal, White is well advised to transpose to mainline theory with /5. Nf3/.
explanations.textEn:
4...Bd6

This attacks the knight. Since 5. d4? Bxe5 6. dxe5 Qxd1+ is uncomfortable for White, taking on double isolated e-pawns and forfeiting castling rights, while 5. Nc4?? Qh4+! 6. g3 Qxg3+!! 7. hxg3 Bxg3# is lost, and 5. Nd3? Qh4+ 6. Nf2 Bxh2 is equal, White is well advised to transpose to mainline theory with /5. Nf3/.
explanations.textZh:
4...Bd6

这会攻击骑士。从 5.d4 开始？ Bxe5 6. dxe5 Qxd1+ 对白方来说是不舒服的，接受双孤立电子兵并丧失易位权，而 5. Nc4?? Qh4+！ 6.g3 Qxg3+！！ 7. hxg3 Bxg3#丢失，5. Nd3？ Qh4+ 6. Nf2 Bxh2 相等，建议白方用 /5 转置到主线理论。 NF3/。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. f4/1...e5/2. g4/2...Qh4
explanations.text:
Bird's Opening/Fool's Mate

2...Qh4#

White has played a very poor move and allowed Black the quickest possible checkmate in the opening game of chess. Mate in two moves.

The mate almost never occurs in practice but is commonly known among chess players because it is the fastest possible.
explanations.textEn:
Bird's Opening/Fool's Mate

2...Qh4#

White has played a very poor move and allowed Black the quickest possible checkmate in the opening game of chess. Mate in two moves.

The mate almost never occurs in practice but is commonly known among chess players because it is the fastest possible.
explanations.textZh:
鸟的开口/愚人的伴侣

2...Qh4#

白棋的棋步非常糟糕，让黑棋在国际象棋的首局比赛中以最快的速度被将死。两步交配。

交配在实践中几乎不会出现，但在国际象棋棋手中广为人知，因为它是最快的。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. f4/1...e6
explanations.text:
1...e6

This move takes advantage of White's exposed f4-pawn.

Also, if White blunders with 2. g4??, Black may apply Fool's mate with 2...Qh4#.

The most common move in this position is /2. Nf3/.
explanations.textEn:
1...e6

This move takes advantage of White's exposed f4-pawn.

Also, if White blunders with 2. g4??, Black may apply Fool's mate with 2...Qh4#.

The most common move in this position is /2. Nf3/.
explanations.textZh:
1...e6

此步棋利用了白方暴露的 f4 兵。

另外，如果白方在 2.g4?? 上犯了错误，黑方可能会用 2...Qh4# 来应用愚人的配合。

这个位置最常见的移动是/2。 NF3/。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. f4/1...f5
explanations.text:
The Symmetrical Variation

This is not a very popular line for Black because it can lead to a closed and relatively uneventful game if Black copies White's moves. This opening has only 40 games played by masters in the Lichess Master Database. There are two ways of playing this opening: 1. immediately disrupting the closeness with 2.e4, or 2. playing solidly and developing quietly.

Of note here is the Double Duck Formation, which is when White plays d4 and Black responds with d5.

Statistics

Approximate Chances

White wins 25%, Draws 43%, Loses 33%

对称变化

对于黑棋来说，这不是一条非常受欢迎的路线，因为如果黑棋复制白棋的走法，它可能会导致一场封闭且相对平静的比赛。巫妖大师数据库中只有 40 场高手玩过的比赛。打这个开局的方法有两种：1.立即用2.e4打乱封闭性，或者2.扎实地打，安静地发展。

这里值得注意的是双鸭阵，即白棋下 d4，黑棋响应 d5。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. f4/1...Nh6
explanations.text:
Bird's Opening: Horsefly Defence

1...Nh6!?

This move looks odd, as it develops a knight to a really odd square and to the edge, but it has some benefits:

Psychological Advantage

This move puts opponents out of their comfort zone and they may get confused and make a mistake and a blunder and fall into a trap.

Controls the f5, g4, and f7 squares

This move controls the f5 square, which white may use to start a kingside attack with the f-pawn, the g4 square, also if white is going for a kingside attack or an aggressive plan (such as putting the queen on g4 to attack the g7 pawn which attacks the rook that might be trapped), and the f7 square, safeguarding the king.

"Develops" a piece

It doesn't look like 1...Nh6 actually develops a piece, however it can get closer to the center with Nf7, Nf5, Ng4, and sometimes even Ng8 to reroute the knight to f6 or e7.

1.f4 Nh6!?

explanations.textZh:
鸟的开局：马蝇防御

1...NH6！？

这一举动看起来很奇怪，因为它将骑士发展到一个非常奇怪的方格和边缘，但它有一些好处：

心理优势

这一举动让对手脱离了他们的舒适区，他们可能会感到困惑，犯下错误和大错，落入陷阱。

控制 f5、g4 和 f7 方块

此步控制f5方格，白棋可以使用f5方格与f兵发起王侧攻击，g4方格，也可以用于白方进行王方攻击或进攻计划（例如将后放在g4上攻击g7棋子，g7兵攻击可能被困的车），以及f7方格，保护王。

“开发”一块

它看起来并不像 1...Nh6 实际上开发了一个棋子，但是它可以通过 Nf7、Nf5、Ng4 甚至 Ng8 更接近中心，将马重新路由到 f6 或 e7。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nf3
explanations.text:
1. Nf3 · Zukertort opening

1. Nf3 is the third most popular initial move. It is highly flexible and often transposes into lines better known through other move orders, though some independent lines are possible. White reckons that Nf3 will almost certainly be a useful move sooner or later, whereas every pawn move is an irrevocable commitment, so 1. Nf3 keeps White's options open.

This means it is a useful transpositional tool. White can feel out how Black wishes to play then transpose into their preferred line. For example, a player who hates facing the queen's gambit declined, but doesn't mind the Dutch defence might play 1. Nf3 and only follow with 2. d4 if Black plays 1...f5.

Because 1. Nf3 controls the e5 square, 1...e5? would be quite bad. Therefore White can use this move order to avoid certain continuations with ...e5: if they wish to play the classical Nimzo-Larsen attack (1. b3 d5) but avoid the modern line (1. b3 e5); or a symmetrical English (1. c4 c5) but not a reversed Sicilian (1. c4 e5); they may choose to start with 1. Nf3.

Black's main way to play is to deny White 2. e4 with either 1...Nf6 or 1...d5. This leads to a number of transpositions and some more independent lines.

1...d5 takes space in the centre and prevents White from playing 2. e4?. The main replies are:

2. d4, which often leads to the Colle system or the queen's gambit by transposition;

2. g3, the king's Indian attack, otherwise seen in the French defence;

2. c4, the Réti, one of the most "independent" lines after 1. Nf3;

2. b3, the classical variation of the Nimzo-Larsen.

2. d3, with the idea of Nbd2 and e4, the old Indian attack.

If 2. e4? is played anyway, this is the Tennison gambit, otherwise reached from the Scandinavian defence 1. e4 d5 2. Nf3?.

1...Nf6 is the most common reply in high-level chess. Black also avoids making a committing pawn move. Chief replies are:

2. d4, often transposing either to an Indian defence or to a 1. d4 d5 opening.

2. c4, transposing into the English opening,

2. g3, again with the idea of Bg2 and the king's Indian attack.

1...c5 looks to prevent 2. d4 instead. This invites White to transpose into the Sicilian defence with 2. e4, or the symmetrical English with 2. c4.

1...e5? has a name, the Ross gambit, but just loses a pawn immediately. If played anyway, it's sometimes with the idea of 2. Nxe5 Nc6?! 3. Nxc6 dxc6, called (for whatever reason) the Walrus.

1...Nc6, called the black mustang defence, invites White to transpose to normality with 2. e4 e5. However, it doesn't prevent 2. d4 because the d4 square will immediately be protected by White's queen.

1...g6 is the Kingside Fianchetto. Black decides to fianchetto their kingside bishop on g7, which has ideas of transposing into a Modern Defence after 2. e4 Bg7 3. d4, or White can copy with 2. g3.

1...e6 is the Queen's Gambit Invitation. If 2. d4 or 2. c4 is played, it could transpose to a Queen's Gambit Declined. 2. e4 transposes to the Knight Variation of the French Defence.

1...d6 is the Pirc Invitation which may transpose into a 2. Nf3 Pirc Defence after 2. e4 or an Indian Defence after 2. d4 Nf6. A unique option after 2. d4 is 2...e5?, the dubious Vos Gambit.

1...c6 is the Slav Invitation. Although more passive than other responses to 1. Nf3, this is nonetheless playable and relatively good and can transpose into a Slav after 2. d4 d5 3. c4.

Rarer moves include:

1...b6, the Queenside Fianchetto Variation trying to fianchetto on b7.

1...f6?, the Arctic Defence, preparing e5, although 1...d6 is a better way of doing so.

1...a6?!, the St. George Defence, playing in the style of the St. George that is 1. e4 a6.

1...a5?!, the Ware Defence, does nothing to help Black's position.

1...h6?!, the Basman Defence, prepares g5.

1...g5?, the Herrstrom Gambit, an unsound gambit with the idea of kicking the knight around after 2. Nxg5 e5.

1...b5?!, the Polish Defence, playing a Polish/Orangutan Opening with colors reversed.

History

When Indian chess master Moheschunder Bannerjee's games with John Cochrane were published in the 1850s in Britain, they introduced ideas on flank and fianchetto openings from Indian chess (such as the "Indian defence") to European chess, and included the earliest games with 1. Nf3.

Johannes Zukertort (1842―1888) was a master chess player, known for competing against Wilhelm Steinitz in 1886 in what is considered to be the first "official" World Chess Championship. He employed 1. Nf3 in some of his games in his 1880 match against Samuel Rosenthal and used it intermittently from then on.

Depending on who you ask, 1. Nf3 is the Zukertort and the continuation 1...d5 2. c4 is the Réti, for Richard Réti, or 1. Nf3 is the Réti and 1. Nf3 d5 2. c4 is the Réti gambit.

explanations.textZh:
1. Nf3·Zukertort开场

1. Nf3 是第三受欢迎的起始动作。它非常灵活，通常可以通过其他移动指令转换成更熟悉的线路，尽管一些独立的线路也是可能的。白方认为 Nf3 几乎肯定迟早会是一个有用的棋步，而每一步兵棋都是不可撤销的承诺，因此 1. Nf3 使白方有选择余地。

这意味着它是一个有用的换位工具。白方可以感觉到黑方希望如何下棋，然后转换成他们喜欢的路线。例如，一个讨厌面对后弃兵策略的玩家会拒绝，但不介意荷兰防守可能会下1. Nf3，并且如果黑方下1...f5，则只接着下2. d4。

因为1. Nf3控制e5方格，1...e5？会很糟糕。因此，白方可以使用此走棋顺序来避免...e5的某些延续：如果他们希望发挥经典的尼姆佐-拉森攻击（1. b3 d5）但避免现代路线（1. b3 e5）；或对称的英语 (1. c4 c5)，但不是颠倒的西西里语 (1. c4 e5)；他们可能会选择从 1. Nf3 开始。

黑棋的主要玩法是用 1...Nf6 或 1...d5 来否定白棋 2. e4。这导致了许多换位和一些更独立的线路。

1...d5 占用中间空间并阻止白棋下 2. e4?。主要回复有：

2. d4，经常通过换位导致Colle系统或后弃兵；

2. g3，国王的印度进攻，否则见于法国防守；

2. c4，Réti，1. Nf3之后最“独立”的品系之一；

2. b3，Nimzo-Larsen 的经典变体。

2. d3，带有Nbd2和e4的思路，老印度攻击。

如果2.e4？无论如何，这是网球策略，否则从斯堪的纳维亚防御 1. e4 d5 2. Nf3? 到达。

1...Nf6 是高级国际象棋中最常见的答复。黑方也避免走棋。主要答复是：

2. d4，通常转移到印度防守或 1. d4 d5 空位。

2. c4，移调为英文开头，

2. g3，同样是Bg2的思路和王印的进攻。

1...c5 看起来是为了防止 2.d4 代替。这邀请白方用 2. e4 转入西西里防御，或者用 2. c4 转入对称的英式防守。

1...e5？有一个名字，罗斯策略，但立即失去了一个棋子。如果无论如何玩的话，有时会想到2. Nxe5 Nc6？！ 3. Nxc6 dxc6，被称为（无论出于何种原因）海象。

1...Nc6，称为黑野马防御，邀请白方用 2. e4 e5 转置为常态。然而，它并不能阻止 2. d4，因为 d4 方格将立即受到白后的保护。

1...g6 是王翼 Fianchetto。黑方决定在 g7 上向王翼主教发起攻击，其想法是在 2. e4 Bg7 3. d4 之后转换为现代防御，或者白方可以用 2. g3 进行复制。

1...e6 是后弃兵邀请。如果使用 2.d4 或 2.c4，它可能会转换为拒绝后弃兵。 2. e4 转置为法国防御的骑士​​变奏。

1...d6 是 Pirc 邀请，可在 2. e4 后转换为 2. Nf3 Pirc 防御或 2. d4 Nf6 后印度防御。 2.d4 之后的一个独特选项是 2...e5?，这是可疑的 Vos 策略。

1...c6 是斯拉夫邀请。虽然比其他对 1. Nf3 的反应更被动，但这仍然是可玩的并且相对较好，并且可以在 2. d4 d5 3. c4 之后转换为斯拉夫语。

较罕见的动作包括：

1...b6，后翼 Fianchetto 变奏尝试在 b7 上进行 fianchetto。

1...f6？，北极防御，正在准备 e5，尽管 1...d6 是更好的方法。

1...a6?!，圣乔治防守队，以圣乔治队的风格进行比赛，即 1. e4 a6。

1...a5？！，Ware Defence，对黑方的位置没有任何帮助。

1...h6？！，巴斯曼防御，准备g5。

1...g5？，Herrstrom 策略，一种不健全的策略，其想法是在 2. Nxg5 e5 之后踢马。

1...b5?!，波兰防守队，以颜色反转的波兰/猩猩开局。

历史

当印度国际象棋大师 Moheschunder Bannerjee 与 John Cochrane 的对弈于 1850 年代在英国出版时，他们将印度国际象棋（例如“印度防御”）的侧翼和前腰开局思想引入欧洲国际象棋，并收录了最早的对弈 1. Nf3。

约翰内斯·祖克托特（Johannes Zukertort，1842―1888 年）是一位国际象棋大师，因在 1886 年与威廉·斯坦尼茨 (Wilhelm Steinitz) 参加被认为是首届“官方”世界国际象棋锦标赛的比赛而闻名。在 1880 年对阵塞缪尔·罗森塔尔的比赛中，他在一些比赛中使用了 1. Nf3，从那时起就断断续续地使用它。

根据您问的人，1. Nf3 是 Zukertort，延续 1...d5 2. c4 是 Réti，对于 Richard Réti，或者 1. Nf3 是 Réti，1. Nf3 d5 2. c4 是 Réti 策略。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nf3/1...c5
explanations.text:
Sicilian Invitation (Réti Opening)

1...c5

Black invites White to transpose into the Sicilian Defence with /2. e4/

White has a number of other choices here. /2. c4/ transposes into a Symmetrical English. Many other moves are possible—the position is still very flexible for both sides.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nf3/1...d5
explanations.text:
1.Nf3 Opening

1...d5

Black stakes a claim to the center. White has many options now and as so often with 1.Nf3 many transpositions. 2. g3, 2. d4, 2. c4 (Réti), 2. d3, 2. b3, 2. e3, and even 2. b4!? are sensible moves.

White can also try the Tennison Gambit with 2. e4?!, usually reached with 1. e4 d5 2. Nf3?!, but it's considered dubious with best play.

1.Nf3 Opening

White can also try the Tennison Gambit with 2. e4?!, usually reached with 1. e4 d5 2. Nf3?!, but it's considered dubious with best play.
explanations.textZh:
1.Nf3开局

1...d5

黑棋占据中心位置。白棋现在有很多选择，1.Nf3 也有很多换位。 2.g3、2.d4、2.c4（Réti）、2.d3、2.b3、2.e3，甚至2.b4！？都是明智之举。

白方也可以尝试使用 2. e4?! 进行网球开局，通常使用 1. e4 d5 2. Nf3?! 达到目标，但最佳玩法被认为是可疑的。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nf3/1...d5/2. c4
explanations.text:
__NOTOC__

2. c4 - Réti Opening

This opening is a hypermodern opening, which invites white's minor pieces to control the centre rather than their pawns. Here black has 4 options:

Defending the Pawn

This can be done with moves such as 2... c6, or 2... e6, both of which generally transpose to the Queen's Gambit Declined or Slav Defense. However, white can deviate with 3. g3, leading the positions that resemble the Catalan Opening (or even transposing to the Catalan Opening, normally reached with 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. g3), or even 3. b3!?

Advancing the Pawn

This gives black a spatial advantage in the center and a quite annoying pawn on d4 that controls c3 and e3, squares where the bishop and knight could have originally been developed to. From here, white challenges the pawn with e3, a3 (followed by b4), and b4, while black tries to hold onto the pawn with Nc6 and c5.

The most critical line in this variation is known as the Reversed Blumenfeld Gambit (similar to the Blumenfeld Countergambit played as black), going 3. e3 c5 4. b4 dxe3 5. fxe3 cxb4 6. d4, where black is up a pawn, but it's a weak pawn on b4, and white has central control and development to compensate for that. White is generally considered to get enough compensation for the pawn in this line and gets a ~52% score from it.

White can also choose to avoid this line and go for 3. g3, which leads to positions resembling the Alekhine Defense, where black has a huge spatial advantage in the center after 3... Nc6 4. Bg2 e5 5. O-O e4 6. Ne1, but the pawns are weak and white can attack them with moves like d3. This is best for people who want to follow the "hypermodern" opening ideal, where black follows the classical opening ideas, but white controls the center with pieces and targets the central pawns that black has.

Capturing the Pawn

Capturing the pawn with 2... dxc4 isn't considered the best, but theory and practice has shown that black does just fine. This usually transposes into a Queen's Gambit Accepted line, which is usually fine for both sides. A sample line would be 3. e3 e6 4. Bxc4 c5 5. d4 Nf6, transposing to the Classical Defense of the Queen's Gambit Accepted.

Ignoring the threat

Black can choose to ignore white's threat since black's Queen is defending the pawn and instead to develop a piece. The correct response is to capture black's pawn on d5. When black captures back with their Queen, white can develop their knight to c3 with tempo.

Defending the Pawn

This can be done with moves such as 2... c6, or 2... e6, both of which generally transpose to the Queen's Gambit Declined or Slav Defense. However, white can deviate with 3. g3, leading the positions that resemble the Catalan Opening (or even transposing to the Catalan Opening, normally reached with 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. g3), or even 3. b3!?

Advancing the Pawn

This gives black a spatial advantage in the center and a quite annoying pawn on d4 that controls c3 and e3, squares where the bishop and knight could have originally been developed to. From here, white challenges the pawn with e3, a3 (followed by b4), and b4, while black tries to hold onto the pawn with Nc6 and c5.

The most critical line in this variation is known as the Reversed Blumenfeld Gambit (similar to the Blumenfeld Countergambit played as black), going 3. e3 c5 4. b4 dxe3 5. fxe3 cxb4 6. d4, where black is up a pawn, but it's a weak pawn on b4, and white has central control and development to compensate for that. White is generally considered to get enough compensation for the pawn in this line and gets a ~52% score from it.

White can also choose to avoid this line and go for 3. g3, which leads to positions resembling the Alekhine Defense, where black has a huge spatial advantage in the center after 3... Nc6 4. Bg2 e5 5. O-O e4 6. Ne1, but the pawns are weak and white can attack them with moves like d3. This is best for people who want to follow the "hypermodern" opening ideal, where black follows the classical opening ideas, but white controls the center with pieces and targets the central pawns that black has.

Capturing the Pawn

Capturing the pawn with 2... dxc4 isn't considered the best, but theory and practice has shown that black does just fine. This usually transposes into a Queen's Gambit Accepted line, which is usually fine for both sides. A sample line would be 3. e3 e6 4. Bxc4 c5 5. d4 Nf6, transposing to the Classical Defense of the Queen's Gambit Accepted.

Ignoring the threat

Black can choose to ignore white's threat since black's Queen is defending the pawn and instead to develop a piece. The correct response is to capture black's pawn on d5. When black captures back with their Queen, white can develop their knight to c3 with tempo.
explanations.textZh:
__NOTOC__

2. c4 - 雷蒂开局

这个开局是一个超现代的开局，它邀请白棋的小子控制中心而不是他们的棋子。这里黑色有 4 个选择：

保卫典当

这可以通过 2...c6 或 2...e6 等动作来完成，这两种动作通常都转换为后弃兵或斯拉夫防御。然而，白棋可能会偏离 3. g3，领先类似于加泰罗尼亚开局的位置（甚至转移到加泰罗尼亚开局，通常通过 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. g3 达到），甚至 3. b3！？

推进典当

这给了黑方在中心的空间优势，以及控制 c3 和 e3 的 d4 上相当烦人的棋子，这些方格原本是象和马发展到的地方。从这里开始，白棋用 e3、a3（随后是 b4）和 b4 挑战棋子，而黑棋则试图用 Nc6 和 c5 保住棋子。

这种变体中最关键的路线被称为反向布卢门菲尔德弃兵（类似于黑色的布卢门菲尔德反策略），走3. e3 c5 4. b4 dxe3 5. fxe3 cxb4 6. d4，其中黑色是棋子，但它是b4上的弱棋子，而白色有中央控制和发展来弥补这一点。白方通常被认为对该行中的棋子获得了足够的补偿，并从中获得了约 52% 的分数。

白棋也可以选择避开这条线，走3. g3，这会导致类似于阿廖欣防御的局面，黑棋在3... Nc6 4. Bg2 e5 5. O-O e4 6. Ne1之后在中心拥有巨大的空间优势，但棋子较弱，白棋可以用d3等棋子攻击他们。这对于想要遵循“超现代”开局理想的人来说是最好的，其中黑色遵循经典的开局思想，但白色用棋子控制中心并瞄准黑色拥有的中心棋子。

捕获典当

用 2...dxc4 吃掉棋子并不被认为是最好的，但理论和实践表明黑色做得很好。这通常会转换为后弃兵接受线，这通常对双方都很好。示例行为 3. e3 e6 4. Bxc4 c5 5. d4 Nf6，转换为接受后弃兵的古典防御。

无视威胁

黑方可以选择忽略白方的威胁，因为黑方的后正在保卫棋子，而是发展一颗棋子。正确的反应是吃掉 d5 上的黑棋。当黑色用他们的皇后夺回时，白色可以将他们的骑士以节奏发展到c3。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nf3/1...d5/2. g3/2...c5/3. Bg2/3...Nc6/4. d4
explanations.text:
With 4. d4, White enters the reversed Grünfeld where play can be very sharp. The d-pawn immediately confronts Black's centre and forces a response.

Black may respond with /4...cxd4/, entering a reversed exchange Grünfeld. However, they may also respond with /4...e6/, discovering the f8-bishop's defense of the c4-pawn. The most common response is /4...Nf6/.

通过 4. d4，白方进入反转的格林菲尔德，那里的比赛可能会非常激烈。 d 兵立即对抗黑方中心并迫使其做出反应。

黑棋可能会用 /4...cxd4/ 响应，进入反向交换格伦菲尔德。然而，他们也可能用 /4...e6/ 进行响应，发现 f8-主教对 c4-pawn 的防御。最常见的响应是 /4...Nf6/。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nf3/1...e5
explanations.text:
Zukertort Opening: Ross Gambit

1...e5?

The move 1...e5? by black, also known as the Ross Gambit, is a dubious pawn sacrifice for black to try and kick the knight as much as possible and potentially even trap it if white's not careful. This gambit can be accepted by playing the move 2. Nxe5, however white can also decline the gambit with 2. e4 transposing to the King's Knight Opening, 2. d3 stopping ...e4, or 2. d4 attacking the pawn on e5, however allowing ...e4.

1. Nf3 e5?

Zukertort 开局：罗斯·甘比特

1...e5？

棋步 1...e5？黑棋，也称为罗斯弃兵，是一种可疑的棋子牺牲，黑棋试图尽可能多地踢马，如果白棋不小心，甚至可能困住它。这个策略可以通过下棋 2.Nxe5 来接受，但是白棋也可以通过 2.e4 转换到国王骑士开局来拒绝该策略，2.d3 停止 ...e4，或 2.d4 攻击 e5 上的棋子，但允许 ...e4。

1.NF3 e5？

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nf3/1...f5
explanations.text:
Dutch Defence

1...f5

Black's opening move aims to transpose into a Dutch Defence. 2.d4 gives a main-line Dutch, while 2.c4 and 2.g3 reserve options.

A major independent option is 2.e4. The sacrifice of White's e-pawn is borrowed from the Staunton Gambit, but the positional themes are very different since here White's king's knight can reach g5.

2.d3 is a way of preparing e4.
explanations.textEn:
Dutch Defence

1...f5

Black's opening move aims to transpose into a Dutch Defence. 2.d4 gives a main-line Dutch, while 2.c4 and 2.g3 reserve options.

A major independent option is 2.e4. The sacrifice of White's e-pawn is borrowed from the Staunton Gambit, but the positional themes are very different since here White's king's knight can reach g5.

2.d3 is a way of preparing e4.
explanations.textZh:
荷兰国防

1...f5

布莱克的开局旨在转变为荷兰防守。 2.d4 提供主线荷兰语，而 2.c4 和 2.g3 保留选项。

一个主要的独立选项是 2.e4。白方电子兵的牺牲是从斯汤顿弃兵中借用的，但位置主题非常不同，因为这里白方的国王骑士可以达到g5。

2.d3是准备e4的一种方法。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nf3/1...f5/2. e4
explanations.text:
Lisitsin Gambit

2. e4 is a very counter-intuitive move, as after the pawn is captured White does not get to make a developing move but must move an already developed piece again. However, practice has shown that the knight landing on g5 is hard to chase away and creates certain tactical threats (more than simply Nxe4!) that compensate for the lost pawn. This gambit contains various traps that black must be careful not to fall into, but will lead to approximate equality if black knows what they're doing.

2...fxe4 is the only way to challenge White's idea.

"The way to refute a gambit is to accept it." - Wilhelm Steinitz

2...e5 transposes to the notorious Latvian Gambit. This may actually be a good practical choice for someone who knows nothing about the Lisitsyn, as it gives Black a greater initiative, but if white knows the theory in this line as well, black doesn't get much out of it.
explanations.textEn:
Lisitsin Gambit

2. e4 is a very counter-intuitive move, as after the pawn is captured White does not get to make a developing move but must move an already developed piece again. However, practice has shown that the knight landing on g5 is hard to chase away and creates certain tactical threats (more than simply Nxe4!) that compensate for the lost pawn. This gambit contains various traps that black must be careful not to fall into, but will lead to approximate equality if black knows what they're doing.

2...fxe4 is the only way to challenge White's idea.

"The way to refute a gambit is to accept it." - Wilhelm Steinitz

2...e5 transposes to the notorious Latvian Gambit. This may actually be a good practical choice for someone who knows nothing about the Lisitsyn, as it gives Black a greater initiative, but if white knows the theory in this line as well, black doesn't get much out of it.
explanations.textZh:
利西辛·甘比特

2. e4 是一个非常反直觉的走法，因为在吃掉棋子后，白方不能再走发展棋，而必须再次移动已经发展的棋子。然而，实践表明，落在 g5 上的马很难被赶走，并且会产生一定的战术威胁（不仅仅是 Nxe4！）来弥补损失的棋子。这个策略包含各种陷阱，黑方必须小心不要陷入其中，但如果黑方知道自己在做什么，就会导致近似平等。

2...fxe4是挑战白棋想法的唯一方法。

“反驳策略的方法就是接受它。” ——威廉·斯坦尼茨

2...e5 转置为臭名昭著的拉脱维亚开局。对于对利西琴一无所知的人来说，这实际上可能是一个很好的实际选择，因为它给了黑棋更大的主动权，但如果白棋也知道这行理论，黑棋就不会从中得到太多好处。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nf3/1...f5/2. e4/2...fxe4
explanations.text:
Lisitsin Gambit

Black logically accepted White's gambit and is now attacking White's f3-knight. By far the best move to save it is 3. Ng5. On d4 or e5 it can be kicked by pawns, on h4 it does nothing (as long as Black is wary of a Qh5 check) but on g5 it forces Black to defend her e4-pawn.
explanations.textEn:
Lisitsin Gambit

Black logically accepted White's gambit and is now attacking White's f3-knight. By far the best move to save it is 3. Ng5. On d4 or e5 it can be kicked by pawns, on h4 it does nothing (as long as Black is wary of a Qh5 check) but on g5 it forces Black to defend her e4-pawn.
explanations.textZh:
利西辛·甘比特

黑方逻辑上接受了白方的策略，现在正在攻击白方的f3马。到目前为止，挽救它的最佳举措是 3. Ng5。在 d4 或 e5 上，它可以被棋子踢，在 h4 上，它什么也不做（只要黑方警惕 Qh5 检查），但在 g5 上，它迫使黑方保卫她的 e4 棋子。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nf3/1...f5/2. g3
explanations.text:
2. g3

This is a principled move similar to the King's Indian Attack that allows White to fianchetto a bishop next move. Black's most popular response is /2...Nf6/ followed by 3...g6 3...d6, or 3...e6 to protect the f-pawn but Black could also prepare 3...e5 with /2...d6/ to take the center.
explanations.textEn:
2. g3

This is a principled move similar to the King's Indian Attack that allows White to fianchetto a bishop next move. Black's most popular response is /2...Nf6/ followed by 3...g6 3...d6, or 3...e6 to protect the f-pawn but Black could also prepare 3...e5 with /2...d6/ to take the center.
explanations.textZh:
2.g3

这是一个原则性的举动，类似于国王的印度攻击，允许白棋下一步行动向主教发起攻击。黑方最受欢迎的反应是/2...Nf6/，然后是3...g6 3...d6，或3...e6来保护f兵，但黑方也可以准备3...e5和/2...d6/来占据中心。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nf3/1...Nf6
explanations.text:
1.Nf3

1...Nf6

1...Nf6, keeping the position symmetrical, is the most flexible reply to 1.Nf3. At Grandmaster level this is a very popular move and has been the preferred response of both Anand and Kasparov.

From here, the game can go in a number of directions and there are plenty of transpositional possibilities into 1.d4 and 1.c4 openings.
explanations.textEn:
1.Nf3

1...Nf6

1...Nf6, keeping the position symmetrical, is the most flexible reply to 1.Nf3. At Grandmaster level this is a very popular move and has been the preferred response of both Anand and Kasparov.

From here, the game can go in a number of directions and there are plenty of transpositional possibilities into 1.d4 and 1.c4 openings.
explanations.textZh:
1.Nf3

1...NF6

1...Nf6，保持位置对称，是对1.Nf3最灵活的回复。在大师级别，这是一个非常受欢迎的举动，也是阿南德和卡斯帕罗夫的首选回应。

从这里开始，游戏可以向多个方向发展，并且有大量的转换可能性进入 1.d4 和 1.c4 开局。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nf3/1...Nf6/2. c4
explanations.text:
English Opening, Anglo-Indian Defense, King's Knight Variation

2.c4

2.c4 is a very common move in the Zukertort Opening, competing for the d5 square. It is also very flexible, allowing white to transpose into Queen's Pawn openings with a later d4 move or various lines in the English Opening (1.c4).

This position is also often reached with the move order 1.c4 Nf6 2.Nf3.
explanations.textEn:
English Opening, Anglo-Indian Defense, King's Knight Variation

2.c4

2.c4 is a very common move in the Zukertort Opening, competing for the d5 square. It is also very flexible, allowing white to transpose into Queen's Pawn openings with a later d4 move or various lines in the English Opening (1.c4).

This position is also often reached with the move order 1.c4 Nf6 2.Nf3.
explanations.textZh:
英国开局、英印防御、国王骑士变例

2.c4

2.c4是Zukertort开局中非常常见的一步，争夺d5方。它也非常灵活，允许白棋通过随后的 d4 走法或英式开局 (1.c4) 中的各种线转入后兵开局。

该位置也经常通过移动顺序 1.c4 Nf6 2.Nf3 到达。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nf3/1...Nf6/2. g3
explanations.text:
King's Indian Attack

2. g3

A sound, but very unambitious opening move where white almost certainly intends to fianchetto his bishop and enable castling. Black has the choice to continue to mirror white's move once more with g6 or begin a more aggressive attempt to control the center.
explanations.textEn:
King's Indian Attack

2. g3

A sound, but very unambitious opening move where white almost certainly intends to fianchetto his bishop and enable castling. Black has the choice to continue to mirror white's move once more with g6 or begin a more aggressive attempt to control the center.
explanations.textZh:
国王对印第安人的攻击

2.g3

这是一个合理但非常不雄心勃勃的开局棋，白棋几乎肯定是打算先擒杀他的主教并进行易位。黑方可以选择继续用 g6 模仿白方的走法，或者开始更加激进地尝试控制中心。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nh3
explanations.text:
__NOTOC__

1. Nh3?! · Ammonia Opening

The Ammonia opening is based on the chemical formula of ammonia (NH3) and the fact that ammonia, like this opening, 'stinks'. Other titles for this opening include; the Amar Opening, the Paris Opening, and Drunken Knight Opening. Chess author Tim Harding has jokingly suggested that "Amar" is an acronym for "Absolutely mad and ridiculous"; that sums up this move!

Jokes aside, this move isn’t actually bad, it just does not improve White's position. White has made an odd decision to develop the knight to a square where it has very little influence on the game (knights generally hate the edge of the board, and love the centre). As such, Black can fairly easily get an edge.

Black's responses

White’s choice has effectively surrendered the first move to Black. Any one of White's opening moves may be employed by Black (except, of course, 1... g5??, which loses a pawn and weakens the kingside).

1... e5

1... d5

All possible Black's moves

explanations.textZh:
__NOTOC__

1.NH3？！ · 氨开口

氨开口是基于氨 (NH3) 的化学式以及氨与此开口一样“有臭味”的事实。本次空缺的其他标题包括：阿马尔公开赛、巴黎公开赛和醉骑士公开赛。国际象棋作家蒂姆·哈丁开玩笑地表示，“Amar”是“绝对疯狂和荒谬”的缩写；这总结了这一举动！

抛开笑话不谈，这一步棋实际上并不坏，只是没有改善白棋的局面。白方做出了一个奇怪的决定，将马发展到一个对棋局几乎没有影响的方格（马通常讨厌棋盘的边缘，而喜欢中心）。因此，黑棋可以很容易地获得优势。

黑方的回应

白棋的选择实际上将先手棋让给了黑棋。白棋的任何一手开局棋都可以被黑棋使用（当然，除了 1...g5??，它会失去一个棋子并削弱王翼）。

1...e5

1...d5

黑方所有可能的走法

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nh3/1...d5
explanations.text:
__NOTOC__

1…d5 - Amar Opening

This move takes space in the centre, and threatens to damage White's already vulnerable kingside pawn structure with 2...Bxh3 3. gxh3. White may put off Black’s threats or even encourage them, either in search of outrageous activity of their king’s rook, or a more subtle approach with 2. g3 (with perhaps f3 and Nf2 to follow). It should also be noted that 2. g3 e5 3. f4 Bxh3 4. Bxh3 exf4 is known as the Amar Gambit, which severely weakens White’s king and sacrifices a pawn for a kingside initiative. This line is considered dubious, and gives Black at least a slightly better chance. It could be said that 1... d5 falls into the trap laid by 1. Nh3.
explanations.textEn:
__NOTOC__

1…d5 - Amar Opening

This move takes space in the centre, and threatens to damage White's already vulnerable kingside pawn structure with 2...Bxh3 3. gxh3. White may put off Black’s threats or even encourage them, either in search of outrageous activity of their king’s rook, or a more subtle approach with 2. g3 (with perhaps f3 and Nf2 to follow). It should also be noted that 2. g3 e5 3. f4 Bxh3 4. Bxh3 exf4 is known as the Amar Gambit, which severely weakens White’s king and sacrifices a pawn for a kingside initiative. This line is considered dubious, and gives Black at least a slightly better chance. It could be said that 1... d5 falls into the trap laid by 1. Nh3.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nh3/1...e5
explanations.text:

1... e5 - Amar Opening

Black takes space in the centre, but refuses to threaten the knight, thus calling White's bluff. A different way of doing so, emphasizing the correct placement of one's own Knight, might be 1... Nc6. Then, 2. d4 is the Mozarabic Opening — trying to put Black's riposte in the wrong just the same. In any case, Black can get a very solid game.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. Nh3/1...Nh6
explanations.text:
__NOTOC__

1...Nh6!? - Ammonia Opening

1...Nh6!?

A really odd move. It is almost never seen as it does not help black exploit white's mistake. White can continue with moves such as:

2. e4 controls the center and fixes the mistake that white made on move 1, while exploiting black's own mistake of putting the knight on h6.

2. d4 controls the center and fixes the mistake that white made on move 1, while exploiting black's own mistake of butting the knight on h6 by attacking it with the bishop and threatening to double their pawn structure.

2. g3 'justifies' 1. Nh3 as it prepares to put the bishop on g2 and allows white to castle safely.

2. f3!? tries to prepare g4 threatening to attack the knight on h6, but black can play 2...e5! and is now threatening 3...Qh4+.

2. g4!? immediately tries to threaten the knight on h6, however black can just take the g4 pawn and then white can choose between 3. f3 and 3. Bg2. 3. Bg2 is better because it prepares to castle, and develops a piece on the long diagonal, and tries to compensate for the pawn. 3. f3 attacking the knight immediately is bad because black can play 3... e5!! and white cannot take due to ...Qh4+.

2. Nc3 is a passive option that develops a knight to a natural square but doesn't take advantage of black's mistake of putting the knight on h6.

1.Nh3 Nh6!?

__NOTOC__

1...NH6！？ - 氨开口

1...NH6！？

一个非常奇怪的举动。它几乎从未见过，因为它无助于黑棋利用白棋的错误。白棋可以继续下棋，例如：

2. e4控制中心并修复白棋在第1步中所犯的错误，同时利用黑棋自己将马放在h6上的错误。

2. d4 控制中心并修复白棋在第 1 步中所犯的错误，同时利用黑棋自己在 h6 上顶撞马的错误，通过象攻击它并威胁将其兵结构加倍。

2. g3“证明”1. Nh3，因为它准备将主教放在g2上并允许白棋安全地城堡。

2.f3！？尝试准备 g4 威胁攻击 h6 上的马，但黑棋可以下 2...e5！现在威胁 3...Qh4+。

2.g4！？立即尝试在 h6 上威胁马，但是黑方可以拿走 g4 兵，然后白方可以在 3. f3 和 3. Bg2 之间进行选择。 3. Bg2 更好，因为它准备城堡，并在长对角线上发展一个棋子，并尝试补偿兵。 3. f3 立即攻击马是不好的，因为黑棋可以下 3...e5！由于...Qh4+，白棋不能吃。

2. Nc3 是一个被动选项，将马发展到自然方格，但没有利用黑方将马放在 h6 上的错误。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. g3
explanations.text:
1. g3 · Hungarian Opening

1. g3, the Hungarian Opening (also known as the Benko's Opening and the King's Fianchetto Opening) is the 5th most popular initial move. It is highly transpositional, and can lead to many other mainstream openings. This move doesn't immediately influence the center, but White prepares to fianchetto the Bishop to g2, which does. The hypermodern school of opening theory, most influential in the 1920s and 1930s, was all about controlling the center from a distance with pieces rather than occupying it with pawns. Hypermodernists claimed that while a large center could very well be a boon, it could also end up being a target that would need the rest of White’s forces to babysit it. The move 1. g3 has many long term prospects of applying pressure on the center and Black's queenside. The ease with which White can castle Kingside often aids White's position. When playing this opening, White will often adopt the King’s Indian Attack (or Barcza System), with a Bishop on g2, a Knight on f3, and kingside castling. Black can mirror White's move with 1…g6, thus entering the hypermodern Fianchetto. Analysis shows that, as with most openings, the positions arising from the Hungarian Opening are equal, or perhaps just a little bit more comfortable for White. Black has plenty of responses, the most popular of which being moves like 1…d5 or 1…e5, which place a pawn in the center and gain space. Nevertheless, even responses such as the bizarre 1…h5?! (known as the Lasker Simul Special) have been tried before, surprisingly only giving White a slight edge.

Statistics

explanations.textZh:
1. g3·匈牙利公开赛

1. g3，匈牙利开局（也称为 Benko 开局和 King's Fianchetto 开局）是第五大最受欢迎的开局。它具有高度的换位性，可以导致许多其他主流的空缺。这一着棋并不会立即影响到中路，但白方准备将主教劈向 g2，这确实影响到了中路。超现代的开局理论学派在 20 年代和 1930 年代最具影响力，其核心是用棋子从远处控制中心，而不是用棋子占领中心。超现代主义者声称，虽然一个大型中心很可能是一个福音，但它最终也可能成为一个目标，需要怀特的其他部队来照顾它。棋步 1. g3 有许多长期前景可以对中路和黑方后翼施加压力。白棋能够轻松地占领王翼，这通常有助于白棋的位置。在下这种开局时，白方通常会采用国王的印度进攻（或Barcza系统），主教在g2上，马在f3上，王翼易车。黑棋可以用 1…g6 模仿白棋的走法，从而进入超现代的 Fianchetto。分析表明，与大多数开局一样，匈牙利开局产生的局面是相同的，或者可能只是让白棋更舒服一些。黑方有很多应对措施，其中最受欢迎的是 1…d5 或 1…e5 等走法，这些走法将棋子放在中心并获得空间。然而，即使是诸如奇怪的 1…h5？！ （被称为拉斯克模拟特殊）以前已经尝试过，令人惊讶的是只给白方带来了轻微的优势。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. g3/1...b6
explanations.text:
Benko Opening

1...b6

With this rather rare choice, Black is trying to put their queen’s bishop on the very same diagonal that White is trying to control with Bg2. Of course, 2. Bg2 Bb7?? is out of the question since White can respond simply with 3. Bxb7, winning a free bishop (and rook!). However, with a move like 2…Nc6, Black can safely fianchetto the bishop. A thematic struggle on the a8-h1 diagonal is to be expected.

explanations.textZh:
本科开场

1...b6

通过这个相当罕见的选择，黑方试图将他们的后主教放在白方试图用 Bg2 控制的同一对角线上。当然，2.Bg2 Bb7??这是不可能的，因为白方可以简单地用 3. Bxb7 做出回应，赢得一个免费的主教（和车！）。然而，通过像 2…Nc6 这样的棋步，黑方可以安全地先杀主教。 a8-h1 对角线上的主题斗争是可以预料的。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. g3/1...b6/2. Bg2
explanations.text:
Benko Opening

2. Bg2

This is the expected continuation. White has fianchettoed their king’s bishop, and Black is practically forced to either play the logical 2…Nc6 (preparing …Bb7), or a move like 2…d5, which takes up the centre and protects the threatened rook, but reduces the scope of Black’s bishop. Of course, 2…c6 is playable but very passive, and all other moves are blunders that fail to 3. Bxa8.

2.背景2

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. g3/1...d5
explanations.text:
Benko Opening

1...d5

This is Black’s most common reply. By placing a pawn in the centre, White must react fast so as to not surrender the whole centre to Black. Moves like 2. Bg2 or 2. Nf3, continuing on with the hypermodern theme, or 2. d4, striking back in the centre, are all seen and considered viable.

explanations.text:
1...e5 · Hungarian Opening

1...e5

Black has placed a pawn in the centre of the board, gaining space and taking over the d4- and f4-squares. Black also discourages the natural 2. Nf3, as Black will simply kick the knight with a further pawn advance. 1. g3 e5 2. Nf3 is still sometimes seen anyway, and is known as the Reversed Alekhine, as the strategy from this opening is similar to Alekhine’s Defense but with the colours reversed. More commonly, White will either continue developing with Bg2, Nf3, O-O, etc. and adopt a King’s Indian Attack setup, or will strike back in the centre immediately.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. g3/1...g6
explanations.text:
Benko Opening

1...g6

Black mirrors White’s move, and prepares to fianchetto their own king’s bishop with an eventual …Bg7 in order to control part of the centre and place pressure on White’s queenside. Play could now continue in a symmetrical vein with 2. Bg2 Bg7, or could transpose into more well-known lines if White tries a flexible move like 2. Nf3. A transposition to a sideline of the English Opening is also possible via 2. c4.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. g4
explanations.text:
__NOTOC__

1. g4? · Grob's Attack

Grob's Attack is generally considered to be one of the worst starting moves, and is possibly the single worst starting move, for White. However, if White knows enough theory and Black is caught by surprise, this opening can be playable even at relatively high levels. An unprepared player with Black can be led into dangerous territory, especially if they fixate on attempting to win the g4-pawn early.

It is named after Swiss IM Henry Grob (1904-1971) who analysed it in great depth and played hundreds of correspondence games with it.

With decent play from Black and slight inaccuracies by White, Black can establish a relatively large or even decisive advantage. White’s move significantly compromises their kingside's pawn structure, and places the g-pawn on an unusual square that is difficult to defend without giving Black the initiative and compromising the kingside further, as well as making kingside castling severely disadvantageous. Some players argue that, as compensation, White influences more kingside space and can fianchetto the kingside bishop, contributing to influence across the board, as well as discouraging ... Nf6 due to g5 kick. The general plan and idea is similar to the Polish Opening mirrored horizontally. But, kingside space is usually completely ignored since f5, g5, and h5 are rarely played by Black, and Black may just develop the kingside knight to e7, avoiding the kick threat. Also, Black can occupy and take control of the centre, and continually threaten the pawn, gaining initiative.

After the most common 1...d5, 2. h3, e3, g5, and c4 are notable continuations.

Grob's Attack can often lead to 'meme' openings, such as a series of increasingly bold gambits named after fizzy drinks following on from the Double Grob 1...g5

After the most common 1...d5, 2. h3, e3, g5, and c4 are notable continuations.

Grob's Attack can often lead to 'meme' openings, such as a series of increasingly bold gambits named after fizzy drinks following on from the Double Grob 1...g5
explanations.textZh:
__NOTOC__

1.g4？ · 格罗布的攻击

格罗布的攻击通常被认为是白方最差的开局棋之一，也可能是最差的开局棋。然而，如果白方了解足够的理论并且黑方措手不及，那么即使在相对较高的水平上，这个开局也可以发挥作用。毫无准备的黑棋玩家可能会陷入危险的境地，特别是如果他们一心想尽早赢得 g4 兵。

它以瑞士人 IM Henry Grob（1904-1971）的名字命名，他对它进行了深入的分析，并用它玩了数百次通信游戏。

由于黑方下得不错，白方略有失误，黑方可以建立较大甚至决定性的优势。白方的这一步棋极大地损害了王侧的兵结构，并将g兵放置在一个不寻常的方格上，如果不给予黑方主动权并进一步损害王侧，则很难防守，并且使王侧易位变得非常不利。一些玩家认为，作为补偿，怀特影响了更多的王翼空间，并且可以向王翼主教发起进攻，从而有助于全面影响，并且由于 g5 踢球而阻止... Nf6。总体规划和想法类似于水平镜像的波兰开口。但是，王翼空间通常被完全忽略，因为黑方很少下f5、g5和h5，而黑方可能只是将王翼骑士发展到e7，从而避免了踢威胁。另外，黑方可以占领并控制中心，不断威胁棋子，取得主动。

在最常见的 1...d5 之后，2. h3、e3、g5 和 c4 是值得注意的延续。

Grob 的攻击通常会导致“模因”开局，例如继 Double Grob 1...g5 之后一系列以碳酸饮料命名的越来越大胆的策略

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. g4/1...Na6
explanations.text:
1...Na6?!

This move doesn't do anything to help Black's position, but rather hurts it. The knight on a6 is not doing anything important or attacking White's weak kingside. White can develop with /2. Nf3/, /2. Bg2/, or take the center with /2. d4/, /2. e4/.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. g4/1...d5
explanations.text:
Grob's Attack

1...d5

Black responds by taking up central space as well as threatening capture on g4. This is a sound response to 1. g4, as opposed to the more instinctual 1...e5. Although White’s g4 pawn is at risk, they can also just sacrifice it, in return receiving an improvement in their position through development, though Black will still be in a much better position. As a result, 2. Bg2 is commonly played, to which Black most commonly responds 2...c6, protecting the d5-pawn although it it is already protected by Black's queen, or 2...Bxg4, gaining the pawn at the cost of a slight loss of time as well as developing the queenside bishop.

Statistics

No stats as 1. g4 occurs rarely among serious chess players.

格罗布的攻击

1...d5

黑棋的回应是占据中央空间并威胁吃掉 g4。这是对 1.g4 的合理反应，而不是更本能的 1...e5。虽然白棋的 g4 棋子面临风险，但他们也可以牺牲它，作为回报，通过发展获得自己位置的改善，尽管黑棋仍然处于更好的位置。因此，通常会下 2.Bg2，黑方最常响应 2...c6，保护 d5 兵，尽管它已经受到黑方后的保护，或者 2...Bxg4，以稍微损失时间为代价获得棋子并发展后侧主教。

统计数据

没有统计数据为 1。g4 在严肃的国际象棋棋手中很少出现。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. g4/1...d5/2. Bg2
explanations.text:
2. Bg2

White fianchettos the bishop, gambiting the pawn on g4 as there's no actual way to defend it. In exchange they have a few tricks up their sleeve. Black usually accepts the gambit by taking the free pawn with /2...Bxg4/.
explanations.textEn:
2. Bg2

explanations.textZh:
2.背景2

白棋成为主教，将棋子押在 g4 上，因为没有实际的方法来防御它。作为交换，他们有一些锦囊妙计。黑方通常接受该策略，用 /2...Bxg4/ 拿走空闲棋子。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. g4/1...d5/2. Bg2/2...c6
explanations.text:
Grob's Gambit Declined

Black plays c6, declines the gambit in order to avoid tricky situations and defends d4. The position for black looks like Caro-Kann Defense. White still can continue with c4 idea, but then they should play Qa4 after dxc4.

explanations.textZh:
格罗布的策略被拒绝

黑方下c6，为了避免棘手的情况而拒绝开局并防守d4。黑棋的位置看起来像卡罗-卡恩防守。白方仍然可以继续c4想法，但他们应该在dxc4之后下Qa4。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. g4/1...d5/2. Bg2/2...Bxg4
explanations.text:
Grob's Gambit Accepted

Black "accepts" the gambit by just taking a pawn. White usually continues with two moves:

3. c4

c4, the Fritz Gambit is another move where white gambits a pawn. However it's tricky - after dxc4 white can play Bxb7 and take the rook in future. But this is risky situation, because you don't really have a continuation after fourth move.

3. c3

This is more solid move. It doesn't create any attacks but helps to develop and play d4 in future in order to create a good pawn structure to complete development later. But don't forget that your kingside is damaged.

格罗布的策略被接受

黑方仅拿走棋子就“接受”了这一策略。白方通常会继续走两步棋：

3.c4

c4，弗里茨弃兵是白方弃兵的另一步棋。然而这很棘手——在dxc4之后，白方可以下Bxb7并在未来拿走车。但这是有风险的情况，因为第四步之后你并没有真正的延续。

3.c3

这是更扎实的举动。它不会产生任何攻击，但有助于将来开发和玩 d4，以便创建一个良好的棋子结构以完成以后的开发。但不要忘记你的主翼已损坏。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. g4/1...d6
explanations.text:
1...d6

Black attacks the g4-pawn with the bishop. White should ignore the attack and play /2. Bg2/, because after 2... Bxg4?! 3. Bxb7 Nd7 4. Bxa8 Qxa8 White is up one point of material but Black has their queen on an active square and is threatening to capture White's rook on h1.

Protecting the pawn with /2. h3/ is another good choice.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. g4/1...e5
explanations.text:
Grob's Attack

1. g4 e5

This move is interesting not because it is a commonly-played move, nor because it gives an advantage to either player (though Black should still be far better), but because White has not one, but two moves that lead to an early checkmate for Black. 2. f4?? transposes to the From Gambit of the Bird’s Opening, but this matters little because black can easily mate. 2. f3?? leads to the same early demise for white, this time transposing to the Barnes Opening. Both these blunders are called Fool's Mate, and tie for the fastest possible checkmate for black.

Although Grob's Attack is itself rarely used among serious players, 2. d3 is a more serious alternative. White will still be objectively worse, but can put up a good fight in spite of their weak kingside, and lack of resistance in the centre.

There is also 2. Bg2 which attempts to get into a psuedo-King's Indian with the g pawn able to kick out a potential f6 knight.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. g4/1...e5/2. d3
explanations.text:
Grob's Attack

1. g4 e5 2. d3

d3 aims to open up the queen side bishop to attack Black's kingside, as well as support a future e4 for control of the center as well. It is basically trying to do two things at once, being hyper-modern as well as classic. Due to this as well as a weak kingside due to the advanced g pawn, White is at a disadvantage, being a jack of all trades, but a master of none.

With good play however, White can establish a mimicry of the King's Indian Attack, with the g pawn able to disrupt the king side knight if it ever comes to f6, meaning Black would have to play h6 to secure it, losing a tempo. Some common moves of this caliber for White include Nf3, Bg2, or the eventual e5, as well as the unique move of g5 common in many games of this opening to prevent Black's knight from moving there.

The main continuation for Black is to play d5, opening up the bishop to attack the g4 pawn, leading to g5. There is also the developing move of Nc6, which defends the e5 pawn and controls d4 along with said pawn.

格罗布的攻击

1.g4 e5 2.d3

d3的目标是打开后侧主教来攻击黑方的王侧，并支持未来的e4来控制中心。它基本上试图同时做两件事：超现代和经典。由于这一点以及由于先进的 g 兵而导致王翼较弱，白方处于劣势，他是万事通，但一无是处。

然而，如果发挥出色，白方可以模仿国王的印第安攻击，如果国王方的骑士出现 f6，g 兵就可以扰乱国王方的骑士，这意味着黑方必须下 h6 才能确保其安全，从而失去节奏。白方这种级别的一些常见走法包括 Nf3、Bg2 或最终的 e5，以及此开局的许多游戏中常见的独特走法 g5，以阻止黑方的马移动到那里。

黑方的主要延续是下d5，让象攻击g4兵，导致g5。还有 Nc6 的发展走法，它保卫 e5 棋子并控制 d4 以及该棋子。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. g4/1...e5/2. f3/2...Qh4
explanations.text:
Fool's Mate

2...Qh4#

White has played a very poor move and allowed Black the quickest possible checkmate in the opening game of chess. Mate in two moves.

The mate almost never occurs in practice but is commonly known among chess players because it is the fastest possible.

傻瓜的伴侣

2...Qh4#

白棋的棋步非常糟糕，让黑棋在国际象棋的首局比赛中以最快的速度被将死。两步交配。

交配在实践中几乎不会出现，但在国际象棋棋手中广为人知，因为它是最快的。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. g4/1...f5
explanations.text:
1...f5 · Alessi Gambit

This offbeat, dubious gambit attacks the g4 pawn immediately, but allows White to take the pawn with 2. gxf5.

Advantages of 1...f5:

Puts opponent off their comfort zone.

Unknown, relatively surprising.

Confuses lots of players.

Can be tricky.

Goes out of known theory.

Disadvantages of 1...f5:

Weakens kingside.

Sacrifices pawn for no apparent reason.

White can get a good position if they know that they are doing.

Does not contribute to development.

Even if we develop (Nf6, Bg7, Qe7, O-O, Bf5, Nc6, O-O-O), White can keep up and consolidate their one pawn advantage.

这种另类的、可疑的策略立即攻击 g4 棋子，但允许白方用 2.gxf5 拿下棋子。

1...f5 的优点：

让对手离开他们的舒适区。

即使我们发展（Nf6，Bg7，Qe7，O-O，Bf5，Nc6，O-O-O），白方也可以跟上并巩固他们的一兵优势。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. g4/1...g5
explanations.text:
Grob's Opening, Symmetrical Variation

Alternatively known as the Double Grob.

1...g5!?

The Symmetrical Variation is a rare response to Grob's Opening (1. g4), due to the fact that it copies White's moves and gets a draw more often instead of capitalising on White's structural disadvantages, and that most players view g4 (g5 for Black) as detrimental due to losing the ability to castle kingside safely. But, this opening may be well-known because of the Coca-Cola Gambit which comes after 2. f4.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. g4/1...g5/2. f4
explanations.text:
2...f4? · Coca-Cola Gambit

The Coca-Cola gambit is a highly unorthodox and aggressive "meme" chess opening

After 2...gxf4 some theory has been developed⸺3.d4 e5 4.h4 d6 5. dxe5 dxe5 6. Qxd8+ Kxd8 7. g5 h6 8. Bg2 Nc6 9. e3 Bg4 10. c3 hxg5 11. hxg5 Rxh1 12. Bxh1 Nge7 13. exf4 Ng6 14. fxe5 Bc5 15. Kf1 is the so-called "main line".

2...f5?! continues the chaos with the Pepsi Countergambit.

History

The origins of the name "Coca-Cola Gambit" are uncertain, with the first known online references to its name being a German forum post from 2008 by user Latvian Gambit and a chess.com forum post from September 2008.

It has featured in numerous Youtube videos, such as as Anish Giri's 2020 video "They made me play the worst gambit ever" and Fischy Stream's "Weirdest Chess Openings Explained", which gained over 600,000 views

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. g4/1...g5/2. f4/2...f5
explanations.text:
Pepsi Countergambit

This Pepsi Countergambit is a rare "meme" opening which mirrors its parent, the Coca-Cola Gambit, in it's boldness and aggression:

1.g4 g5 2.f4? f5?

Although it's technical value is dubious at best and it hasn't been seen in any formal 'over the board' high level tournaments, it has been played online, with it's popularity highest in bullet chess.

It's doubled mirrored pawn structure is similar to the Beyer Gambit of the Centre Game or the Austrian Defence to the Queen's Gambit.

History

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. g4/1...Nf6
explanations.text:
1...Nf6

This move develops a knight and attacks the defenseless g-pawn. The problem with this move is that White can play /2. g5/ to attack the knight, which does not have a good square to retreat besides h5 and its starting square. The move 2...Ng4 is particularly bad as the knight gets trapped after 3. d4.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. h3
explanations.text:
1. h3 · Clemenz Opening

This opening move achieves nothing in terms of development or control of the center. However, this can actually be used as an effective waiting move, though 1. Nf3 is clearly better. Also, if White knows a lot of theory for both sides, this can be useful. 1. h3 also blocks a possible …Bg4 by Black. This may be quite a playable opening despite being inferior to many other openings (like 1. e4, 1. d4, etc). Because it is inferior, and most players want to exploit their first move advantage, however small it may be, as White, this is rarely played. Transpositions are possible, albeit not usual. Black can now exploit the fact that White has wasted time by playing in the centre, or by gaining a slight lead in development.

Black's responses

1... e5 is a solid, sensible move, which places pressure on d4 and f4. Now the strange 2. a3?! is called the Global variation, and if 2... d5 is played after that, it transposes to the "creepy-crawly" formation of the Anderssen opening (1. a3). However, the best follow-up for White after 1... e5 is 2. c4, transposing into the King's English Variation of the English opening. 2. d4 can be tried too, transposing into a "reversed" Scandinavian defence, also playable.

1... d5 is another fine move, with similar ideas to the previous one. This is best followed by 2. d4, 2. f4, or 2. c4, all moves that give White a portion of the centre. 2. b4 is unusual but interesting. Another interesting (though inferior) option is 2. g4?.

1... f5 is not recommended, as White can play 2. d4, transposing into the Korchnoi attack of the Dutch defence (another way to try to exploit kingside weaknesses created by Black, but Black has enough resources to withstand it after 3. g4 [the original plan after h3, especially after 3... d5. Black gets at least their fair share of the chances, so White has to exploit the weaknesses later on in the game]). Nevertheless, it is playable as long as Black is careful.

1... c5 is an unexplored option. It would lead to uncharted territory in the Sicilian defence after 2. e4.

1... Nf6 is a good response. If White plays 2. d4 or 2. c4, the game could take upon a character typical of the King's Indian defence.

1... Nc6 is an interesting option, simply developing a piece. This is probably playable as well.

explanations.textZh:
1. h3·克莱门茨开局

这一开放举措在发展或控制中心方面没有取得任何成果。然而，这实际上可以用作有效的等待着法，尽管 1. Nf3 显然更好。此外，如果白方了解双方的很多理论，这可能会有用。 1. h3 还阻止了黑棋可能出现的…Bg4。尽管不如许多其他开局（如 1.e4、1.d4 等），但这可能是一个相当可玩的开局。因为它是劣等的，而且大多数棋手都想利用他们的先手优势，无论这种优势有多小，就像白棋一样，很少有人会这样玩。换位是可能的，尽管并不常见。黑棋现在可以利用白棋浪费时间的事实，即在中间下棋，或者在发展中取得轻微领先。

黑方的回应

1...e5是一个坚实、明智的举动，它给d4和f4带来了压力。现在奇怪的2.a3？！被称为全局变体，如果此后播放 2...d5，它会转换为安德森开场的“令人毛骨悚然的”形式（1.a3）。然而，白方在 1... e5 之后最好的后续棋是 2. c4，转换为英语开局的国王英语变体。 2. d4也可以尝试，转换成“反向”斯堪的纳维亚防御，也可以玩。

1...d5 是另一个很好的举动，与上一个想法类似。接下来最好是 2. d4、2. f4 或 2. c4，所有这些棋步都为白方提供了中心的一部分。 2. b4 不寻常但很有趣。另一个有趣的（虽然较差）选项是 2.g4?。

1...f5 不推荐，因为白棋可以下 2.d4，转入荷兰防守的 Korchnoi 进攻（另一种尝试利用黑方创造的王翼弱点的方法，但黑方在 3.g4 之后有足够的资源来承受它[h3 之后的原始计划，特别是在 3...d5 之后。黑棋至少获得了公平份额的机会，因此白棋必须在游戏后期利用弱点]）。不过，只要黑方小心，它还是可以下的。

1...c5 是一个未经探索的选项。 2.e4之后，这将导致西西里防御中的未知领域。

1...Nf6 是一个很好的回应。如果白棋下 2.d4 或 2.c4，则棋局可能会呈现出国王印度防守的典型特征。

1...NC6 是一个有趣的选择，只需开发一个片段即可。这个应该也是可以玩的。

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. h4
explanations.text:
__NOTOC__

1. h4?! · Desprez Opening

The Desprez Opening (or Kádas Opening) is a rare kingside flank opening. It does little for development, does not fight for control of the center, and weakens White's kingside. It frees the rook, but the rook normally does not go to h3. It could be said that White has made their position worse, as castling kingside is now less attractive. Due to the near-uselessness of this opening, it is rarely seen among serious chess players. However, it could be used to throw off the opponent.

No top masters have ever used this opening in professional play, although some, most notably Magnus Carlsen and Hikaru Nakamura, play it during blitz. Magnus Carlsen played it in the November 2023 "Titled Tuesday" online tournament, where he successfully defeated strong grandmasters, including Alireza Firouzja.

Black's responses

Black has many decent replies.

1...d5, staking a claim to the centre and simultaneously making 2. Rh3?? impossible.

1... e5, also staking a claim in the center and freeing Black's queen and dark-squared bishop.

1... g6?! is rarely played, as it justifies the move 1. h4. White can play 2. h5 to attack Black's kingside.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. h4/1...d5
explanations.text:
Kadas Opening

1...d5

Black takes the center and opens the diagonal for the light-squared bishop, preventing White's kingside rook from coming out with 2. Rh3??, to which Black will respond with Bxh3. White may try to rectify this with 3. h5?!, but this allows Black to take the full center with 3... e5! not allowing the rook to come to h4 either.

Responses

White may respond to the move d5 with:

/2. h5/, allowing Black to take the full center with 2...e5,

/2. d4/, which is more principled, and White will always play d4 in this opening so why not?

or 2. Nf3, controlling the center with a knight and either going into a King's Indian-like defense, playing classically, or just transposing into the d4 line.

explanations.pageTitle: Chess Opening Theory/1. h4/1...d5/2. h5/2...e5/3. h6
explanations.text:
Kadas Opening: Croon's Gambit

3. h6

The Croon's Gambit is an ambitious attempt to ruin Black's kingside at the cost of a pawn. The main plan of this opening is to open up White's rook file or have a thorn pawn on h6, then strike at the center with d4 and c4 afterwards. Sometimes if Black takes the pawn, White can take back with Bxh6 after d4. White will always play d4 in every line.

3.h6

A very unsound wing gambit that is arguably the worst possible response to 1. h4, usually played as a joke. After 2. hxg5, possibly the only idea is 2...h6 3. gxh6 Bxh6, a type of wing gambit.
